# Bhavisya-purana 1

## Chapter 0

## \|\| 1.0.1 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam \|*  
*devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva tato jayamudīrayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. After offering salutation to lord Narayana, Narottama — the best among the humans and the goddess Sarasvati — the deity of speech, the scriptures like Mahabharata and the Puranas should be recited.

## \|\| 1.0.2 \|\|

*jayati parāśarasūnuḥ satyavatīhṛdayanandano vyāsaḥ \|*  
*yasyāsyakamalagalitaṃ vāṅmayamamṛtaṃ jagatpibati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Victory to the sage Vyasa, who delights the heart of Satyavati, from whose mouth the words appear like the nectar, which are heard by the whole of the universe.

## \|\| 1.0.3 \|\|

*mūkaṅkaroti vācālaṃ paṅgu laṅghayate girim \|*  
*yatkṛpā tamahaṃ vande paramānandamādhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I bow in reverence to blissful lord Krishna, by whose grace, the dumb person becomes an orator and the handicap lame person crosses the mountain. I offer my salutation to the blissful Madhava also known as Shri Krishna.

## \|\| 1.0.4 \|\|

*pārāśaryavacaḥ sarojamamalaṃ gītārthagandhotkaṭaṃ \|*  
*nānākhyānakakesaraṃ harikathāsambodhanābodhitam \|*  
*loke sajjanaṣaṭpadairaharahaḥ pepīyamānaṃ mudā \|*  
*bhūyādbhāratapaṅkajaṃ kalimalapradhvaṃsi naḥ śreyase \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Let the lotus like Mahabharata which destroys all the sins of the universe, bestow welfare on us, which had grown from the lotus-lake in the form of the speech of the sage Vyasa — the son of Parashara. The poetry of the scripture of Jaya is quite spotless clean. It has been developed with the deep expressions of Bhagavadgita having excellent fragrance, besides various types of stories and the events relating to the life of Lord Krishna. The noble souls consume the nectar from the same like blackwasps who fly over the flowers issuing hissing sound.

## \|\| 1.0.5 \|\|

*yo gośataṃ kanakaśṛṅgamayaṃ dadāti \|*  
*viprāya vedaviduṣe ca bahuśrutāya \|*  
*puṇyāṃ bhaviṣyasukathāṃ śṛṇuyātsamagrāṃ \|*  
*puṇyaṃ samaṃ bhavati tasya ca tasya caiva \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A person, who gives away in charity a cow with her horns covered with gold to a learned Brahmana, and a person, who instead, listens to the recitation of the Bhavishya Purana from beginning to the end, both of them earn equal merits.

## \|\| 1.0.6 \|\|

*kṛtvā purāṇāni parāśarātmajaḥ sarvāṇyanekāni sukhāvahāni \|*  
*tatrātmasaukhyāya bhaviṣyadharmān kalau yuge bhāvi lilekha sarvam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The sage Vyasa — the son of Parashara, composed Puranas of blissful stories. Thereafter, for his self delight, has included description of all the religions of the Kali Age in the Bhavishya Purana.

## \|\| 1.0.7 \|\|

*tatrāpi sarvarṣivarapramukhyaiḥ parāśarādyairmunibhiḥ praṇītān \|*  
*smṛtyuktadharmāgamasaṃhitārthān vyāsaḥ samāsādavadadbhaviṣyam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The creations of all the eminent Rishi including Parashara, in the form of Smritis, and the faiths included in Samhitas, the Vedas and Samhitas, have been included by Vyasa in brief.

## \|\| 1.0.8 \|\|

*alpāyuṣo lokajanānsamīkṣya vidyāvihīnānpaśuvatsuceṣṭān \|*  
*teṣāṃ sukhārthaṃ pratibodhanāya vyāsaḥ purāṇaṃ prathitaṃ cakāra \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The sage Vyasa has composed the popular Bhavishya Purana to awaken the ephemeral, illiterate people and those who work like animals.

## Chapter 1. Description of the Purana

## \|\| 1.1.1 \|\|

*jayati bhuvanadīpo bhāskaro lokakarttā \|*  
*jayati ca śitidehaḥ śārṅgaḥdhanvā murāriḥ \|*  
*jayati ca śaśimaulī rudranāmābhidheyo \|*  
*jayati ca sa tu devo bhānumāṃścitrabhānuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Victory to the Sun-god, who illumines the entire universe, of which he happens to be a creator. Let Murari (Vishnu) having dark complexion, charming body, carrying the bow of a horn, be victorious. Let Rudra, decorating his head with a crescent moon, also known as Shiva, be victorious. Let the Fire-god with many flames be victorious.

## \|\| 1.1.2-5 \|\|

*śriyāvṛtaṃ tu rājānaṃ śatānīkaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*abhijagmurmahātmānaḥ sarve draṣṭuṃ maharṣayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhṛguratrirvasiṣṭhaśca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|*  
*parāśarastathā vyāsaḥ sumanturjaiministathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*muniḥ pailo yājñavalkyo gautamastu mahātapāḥ \|*  
*bhāradvājo munirdhīmāṃstathā nāradaparvatau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vaiśampāyano mahātmā śaunakaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*dakṣo'ṅgirāstathā gargo gālavaśca mahātapāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Once all the Maharishis went to meet the valorous, glorious and virtuous king Shatanika, including Bhrigu, Atri, Vasishtha, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Parashara, Vyasa, Sumantu, Jaimini, Paila, the sage Yajnavalkya, the great ascetic Gautama, Bharadvaja, the intelligent Narada, Parvata, Vaishampayana, Shaunaka — the great ascetic, Daksha, Angiras, Garga and the great ascetic Galava.

## \|\| 1.1.6 \|\|

*tānāgatānṛṣīndṛṣṭvā śatānīko mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*vidhivatpūjayāmāsa abhigamya mahāmatiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the arrival of such a large number of Maharishis, the great king Shatanika welcomed them adoring them at the same time.

## \|\| 1.1.7 \|\|

*purohitaṃ puraskṛtya ardhyaṃ gāṃ svāgatena ca \|*  
*pūjayitvā tataḥ sarvānpraṇamya śirasā bhṛśam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Making his priest to lead him, he received them all quite gracefully and after worshipping them, the king offered his salutation to them again and again.

## \|\| 1.1.8 \|\|

*sukhāsīnāṃstato rājā nirātaṅkān gataklamān \|*  
*uvāca praṇato bhūtvā bāhumuddhṛtya dakṣiṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After the Rishis took their seat quite comfortably getting relieved of the fatigue of the journey, then the king Shatanika humbly addressed them raising his right hand.

## \|\| 1.1.9 \|\|

*idānīṃ saphalaṃ janma manye'haṃ bhuvi sattamāḥ \|*  
*ātmano dvijaśārdūlā tathā kīrtiryaśo balam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O noble and excellent Maharishis, now I feel that my birth on earth is successful. O group of excellent Brahmanas! Both my prowess and the yajnas have became successful.

## \|\| 1.1.10 \|\|

*dhanyo'haṃ puṇyakarmā ca yato māṃ draṣṭumāgatāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ smaraṇamātreṇa yuṣmākaṃ pūyate naraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I practically consider myself to be fortunate and beholder because of the arrival of all of you to meet me here. You are the divine souls, with the mere remembering of whose names, a person gets purified.

## \|\| 1.1.11 \|\|

*śrotumicchāmyahaṃ kiñciddharmaśāstramanuttamam \|*  
*ānṛśaṃsyaṃ samāśritya kathayadhvam mahābalāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All of you possess great prowess. I am therefore desirous of listening to the discourse on some religious scriptures. You therefore speak on the subject.

## \|\| 1.1.12 \|\|

*yenāhaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ tu śrutvā gacche parāṃ gatim \|*  
*yathāgato mama pitā śrutvā vai bhārataṃ purā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With the listening of the auspicious stories, let me achieve the final beatitude, as has been achieved by my adorable father in earlier times the auspicious recitation of the Mahabharata.

## \|\| 1.1.13 \|\|

*tathoktāstena rājñā vai brāhmaṇāste samantataḥ \|*  
*samāgamya mithaste tu vimṛśya ca 1 bhṛśam tadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When thus requested by the king Shatanika, the Brahmanas made intensive consultations among themselves. Thereafter, the sage Vyasa spoke to the king.

## \|\| 1.1.14 \|\|

*pūjayitvā tato vyāsamidaṃ vacanamabruvan \|*  
*vyāsaṃ prasādaya vibho eṣa te kathayiṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O all powerful monarch! You should please the sage Vyasa alone here, who alone would narrate to you the stories from the Dharmashastras.

## \|\| 1.1.15 \|\|

*tiṣṭhatyasminmahābāho vayaṃ vaktuṃ na śaknumaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhamāne gurau śiṣyaḥ kathaṃ vakti mahāmate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O long-armed one, in his presence, we people are unable to speak out everything. O intelligent one! How can a disciple speak in the presence of the preceptor?

## \|\| 1.1.16 \|\|

*2 ayaṃ guruḥ sadāsmākaṃ sākṣānnārāyaṇastathā \|*  
*kṛpāluśca tathā cāyaṃ tathā divyavidhānavit \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He has always functioned as our preceptor and happens to be the incarnation of Narayana. He is quite benevolent too. He is also well versed in the divine predications.

## \|\| 1.1.17 \|\|

*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ pāvanāya mahātmanām \|*  
*dharmaśāstramanenoktaṃ dharmādyaiḥ susamanvitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. It is he who has narrated the story of the composite Dharmashastras in order to purify the influented four varnas.

## \|\| 1.1.18 \|\|

*bibheti gahanācchāstrālloko vyādhirivauṣadhāt \|*  
*bhāratasya ca vistāro muninā vyāhṛtaḥ svayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The people are afraid of the provisions of the difficult Shastras, like the sour medicines. Because of the same reason, the great sage Vyasa composed the comprehensive Mahabharata epic.

## \|\| 1.1.19 \|\|

*yathā svādu ca pathyaṃ ca dadyāstvaṃ bhiṣagauṣadham \|*  
*tathā ramyaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca bhārataṃ kṛtavānmuniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. As a physician prefers to serve a tasteful medicine himself, similarly, the sage has composed the pleasant Mahabharata dealing with the scriptural subjects.

## \|\| 1.1.20 \|\|

*āstikyārohasopānametadbhāratamucyate \|*  
*tacchrutvā svarganarakau lokaḥ sākṣādavekṣate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This Mahabharata is considered to be a step for climbing over the feeling of faithfulness. By listening to it, the people come face to face with the hell and the heaven.

## \|\| 1.1.21 \|\|

*devatātīrthatapasāṃ bhāratādeva niścayaḥ \|*  
*na janyate nāstikatā tasya mīmāṃsakairapi \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It is the Mahabharata which provides a decisive view of the tapas, the gods and the holy shrines. Those who listen to the same, cannot divert their minds towards Mimamsa philosophy or atheism.

## \|\| 1.1.22 \|\|

*viṣṇau 1 deveṣu vedeṣu guruṣu brāhmaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*bhaktirbhavati kalyāṇī bhāratādeva dhīmatām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With the listening to the recitation of the epic of Mahabharata, one develops beneficial devotion in lord Vishnu and other gods, the preceptors, the Vedas and the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.1.23-26 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ bharatātsiddhireva hi \|*  
*ajihmo bhārataḥ panthā nirvāṇapadagāminām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mokṣadharmārthakāmānāṃ prapañco bhārate kṛtaḥ \|*  
*anityatāpasantaptā bhavanti tasya muktaye \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vipattiṃ bhāratācchrutvā vṛṣṇipāṇḍavasampadām \|*  
*duḥkhāvasānādrājendra puṇyaṃ ca saṃśrayedbudhaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*evaṃvidhaṃ bhārataṃ vai proktaṃ yena mahātmanā \|*  
*so'yaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣāt vyāsarūpī mahāmuniḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. The epic of Mahabharata also bestows dharma, artha, kama and moksha. For the achieving of the final beatitude, the Mahabharata happens to be the straight and the simple path, because all the elements like the dharma, artha, kama and moksha which are difficult to be achieved, have been extensively discussed in this epic. The people suffering from transient pain, are sure provided relief by the Mahabharata. Listening to the extreme glory of Yadu race and Pandavas, besides their misfortunes, a person is relieved of his enormous misfortunes. Therefore, the learned people should earn merit from this epic. The great personality who composed this epic, the same great sage in the form of Narayana and Vyasa, is present here.

## \|\| 1.1.27 \|\|

*sa teṣāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā pratāpī yo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*prasādayāmāsa muniṃ vyāsaṃ śāstraviśāradam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On hearing the words of the sages, the glorious monarch — Shatanika then pleased the sage Vyasa, who was well-versed in all the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.1.28 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*añjaliḥ śirasā brahman kṛto'yaṃ pādayostava \|*  
*brūhi me dharmaśāstraṃ 5 tu yenā pūtatāṃ vraje \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Shatanika said — “O Brahman, I am offering my salutation to you folding both my hands over my head. You kindly narrate the Dharmashastras to me, to enable me to get purified.”

## \|\| 1.1.29 \|\|

*samuddhara bhavādasmātkīrtayitvā kathāṃ śubhām \|*  
*yathā mama pitā pūrvaṃ kīrtayitvā tu bhāratam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By delivering auspicious discourse highlighting the beneficial religious stories, you let me cross over the ocean of the universe as you had redeemed my father in earlier times by narrating the stories of the Mahabharata.

## \|\| 1.1.30 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*tasyaitadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyāso vacanamabravīt \|*  
*eṣa śiṣyaḥ sumanturme kathayiṣyati te prabho \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Vyasa said — On hearing the speech of the king, the sage Vyasa said — “This is my disciple Sumantu, who would narrate all the auspicious stories to you.”

## \|\| 1.1.31-32 \|\|

*yadicchasi mahābāho prītidaṃ cādbhutaṃ śubham \|*  
*śravyaṃ bharataśārdūla sarvapāpabhayāpaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yathā vaiśampāyanena purā proktaṃ pitustava \|*  
*mahābhāratavyākhyānaṃ brahmahatyāvyapohanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. O long armed one, O best of those belonging to the Bharata dynasty, in case you are interested in listening to the loveable events of the Mahabharata, which is astonishingly great, bestow welfare, remove the fear and the sins, then the way Vaishampayana had narrated it to your father, for the removal of his Brahmahatya and other sins, he would narrate the same to you in the similar way.

## \|\| 1.1.33-34 \|\|

*atha tamṛṣayaḥ sarve rājānamidamabruvan \|*  
*sādhu proktaṃ mahābāho vyāsenāmitabuddhinā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sumantuṃ pṛccha rājarṣe sarvaśāstraviśāradam \|*  
*asmākamapi rājendra śravaṇe jāyate matiḥ \|*  
*atha vyāso mahātejāḥ sumantumṛṣimabravīt \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. At this speech of the sage Vyasa, all other Rishis also advised the king saying — “O large armed king, the immensely wise Vyasadeva has spoken correctly. O Rajarishi, you can now request the sage Sumantu to narrate all the relevant stories. O king, all of us are also feeling interested in hearing about it.”

## \|\| 1.1.35 \|\|

*kathayāsmai kathāstāta yāḥ śrutvā modate nṛpaḥ \|*  
*bhāratādikathānāṃ tu yatrāsya ramate manaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thereafter, the immensely illustrious Vyasa spoke to the sage Sumantu — “O Excellent one, you narrate the stories to the king, listening to which he will feel happy. In fact, his mind is more attracted towards the events of the Mahabharata.

## \|\| 1.1.36-38 \|\|

*asāvapi mahātejāḥ śrutvā bhāvaṃ mahāmateḥ \|*  
*vyāsasya dvijaśārdūla ṛṣīṇāṃ cāpi sarvaśaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*cakāra vaktuṃ sa manastasmai rājñe mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*vyāsasya śāsanādvipra ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*atha rājā mahātejā ājamīḍho dvijottamam \|*  
*praṇamya śirasātyarthaṃ pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. O lion among the Brahmanas, the illustrious Sumantu, well understanding the mind of the illustrious Vyasa, as well as the desire of the sages present there, then thought of narrating the auspicious stories. O Brahmanas! I have been commanded by the great sage Vyasa as well as the Rishis present here, therefore the Shatanika — the son of Ajamidha, initially offered his salutation to the excellent sage Sumantu.

## \|\| 1.1.39 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*puṇyākhyānaṃ mama brahman pāvanāya prakīrtaya \|*  
*śrutvā yadbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭha mucye'haṃ sarvapātakāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Shatanika said — O Brahmana! You kindly narrate the auspicious stories, in order to purify me, by listening to which, I could be relieved of al! my sins.

## \|\| 1.1.40 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇi santi puṣpāni bhārata \|*  
*yāni śrutvā naro rājan mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Sumantu said — O monarch born in the race of Bharata, there are a large number of the auspicious scriptures, by hearing which, a person is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.1.41 \|\|

*kimicchasi mahābāho śrotuṃ yattvāṃ bravīmi vai \|*  
*bhāratādikathānāṃ tu yāsu dharmādayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O long armed one, in the stories of the Mahabharata highlight of the aspects of dharma, which one of them would you like to listen, and should be related by me?

## \|\| 1.1.42 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*matāni kāni viprendra 1 dharmaśāstrāṇi suvrata \|*  
*yāni śrutvā naro vipra mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Shatanika said — O excellent Brahmana and performer of the best of the vratas, which are the Dharmashastras, by listening to which, a person is relieved of all his sins?

## \|\| 1.1.43-45 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śrūyantāṃ dharmaśāstrāṇi manurviṣṇuryamo'ṅgirāḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhadakṣasaṃvartaśātātapaparāśarāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*āpastambo'tha uśanā kātyāyanabṛhaspatī \|*  
*gautamaḥśaṅkhalikhitau hārīto'trirathāpi vā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*etāni dharmaśāstrāṇi śrutvā jñātvā ca bhārata \|*  
*vṛndārakapuraṃ gatvā modate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Sumantu said — O Monarch, listen about the Dharmashastras, which were composed by Manu, Vishnu, Yama, Angira, Vasishtha, Daksha, Samvarta, Shatatapa, Parashara, Apastamba, Ushna, Katyayana, Brihaspati, Gautama, Shamkha, Likhita, Harita, Atri and others. O king, born of the race of Bharata, listening to all these Dharmashastras and by well understanding them, a person reaches the abode of the gods and feels blissful. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.1.46 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*yānyetāni tvayoktāni dharmaśāstrāṇi suvrata \|*  
*necchāmi śrotuṃ viprendra 3 śrutānyetāni hi dvija \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Shatanika said — O sage of excellent Vrata and Indra among the sages, the Dharmashastras which have just been listed by you have already been heard by me and do not intend to listen them again.

## \|\| 1.1.47 \|\|

*trayāṇāmapi varṇānāṃ proktānāmapi paṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*śreyase na tu śūdrāṇāṃ tatra me vacanaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The learned sages have described them to be beneficial for three castes only. There is no mention of the benefit for the Shudras. You kindly listen to my prayer in this connection.

## \|\| 1.1.48-50 \|\|

*caturṇāmiha varṇānāṃ śreyase yāni suvrata \|*  
*bhavanti dvijaśārdūla śrutāni bhuvanatraye \|\| 48 \|\|*

*viśeṣataścaturthasya varṇasya dvijasattama \|\| 49 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇādiṣu varṇeṣu triṣu vedāḥ prakalpitāḥ \|*  
*manvādīni ca śāstrāṇi tathāṅgāni samantataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. O best of the Brahmanas! I would like to listen to such of the Shastras which are beneficial to all the four varnas, particularly the Madras. There are the scriptures for the benefit of all the varnas, which include the Vedas, Vedangas and the Dharmashastras composed by Manu. O excellent sage, the condition of the shudras is miserable apparently.

## \|\| 1.1.51-52 \|\|

*śūdrāścaiva bhṛśaṃ dīnāḥ pratibhānti dvijaprabho \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣasya śastāḥ syuravane katham \|\| 51 \|\|*

*āgamena vihīnā hi aho kaṣṭaṃ mataṃ mam \|*  
*kaścaiṣāmāgamaḥ proktaḥ purā dvijamanīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*trivargaprāptaye brahmañchreyase ca tathobhayoḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. How could they protect and preserve dharma, artha, kama and moksha? The Shudras are deprived of the Agamas and this situation is painful for my mind, which one of the Agamas has been created by the learned people for their benefit in the past which could be beneficial to the shudras for their dharma, artha and kama?

## \|\| 1.1.53 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhu sādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ yāni proktāni śreyase \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Sumantu said — O valorous one, you have asked a very correct question. You listen to my words, which are said to be beneficial for all the four varnas.

## \|\| 1.1.54 \|\|

*dharmaśāstrāṇi 1 rājendra śṛṇu tāni nṛpottama \|*  
*viśeṣataśca śūdrāṇāṃ pāvanāni manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Indra among the monarchs, O best of the rulers! You listen to the Dharmashastras, which have been created particularly for the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.1.55 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni caritaṃ rāghavasya ca \|*  
*rāmasya kuruśārdūla dharmakāmārthasiddhaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O best of the Kurus, the life sketch of Shri Rama of the race of Raghu has been included in the eighteen Puranas, for the benefit of the people and for achieving of the dharma, artha, kama.

## \|\| 1.1.56 \|\|

*tathoktaṃ bhārataṃ vīra pārāśaryeṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*vedārthasakalaṃ yojya3 dharmaśāstrāṇi ca prabho \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O valorous one, in this way, the extremely intelligent Vyasa, the son of Parashara has put the essence of all the Dharmashastras in the epic of the Mahabharata.

## \|\| 1.1.57-58 \|\|

*kṛpālunā kṛtaṃ śāstraṃ caturṇāmiha śreyase \|*  
*varṇānāṃ bhavamagnānāṃ kṛtaṃ poto hyanuttamam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni aṣṭau vyākaraṇāni ca \|*  
*jñātvā satyavatīsūnuścakre bhāratasaṃhitām \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. The compassionate Vyasa, for the benefit of all the four varnas and to redeem them from the ocean of the universe, composed Mahabharata besides the eighteen Puranas and eight Vyakaranas to serve as a boat, and should be learnt by heart.

## \|\| 1.1.59 \|\|

*yāṃ śrutvā puruṣo rājan mucyate brahmahatyayā \|*  
*prathamaṃ procyate brāhmaṃ dvitīyaṃ caindramucyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O king, listening to it, a person is freed from the sin of killing a Brahmana. The first is known as the Brahma Purana and the second is called Aindra.

## \|\| 1.1.60 \|\|

*yāmyaṃ proktaṃ tato raudraṃ vāyavyaṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*sāvitraṃ ca tathā proktamaṣṭamaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thereafter, there are the Yamya, Raudra, Vayavya, Varuna, Savitra and Vaishnava — the eighth Puranas.

## \|\| 1.1.61-66 \|\|

*etāni vyākaraṇāni purāṇāni nibodha me \|*  
*brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tathānyannāradīyaṃ ca mārkaṇḍeyaṃ ca saptamam \|*  
*āgneyamaṣṭamaṃ vīra bhaviṣyaṃ navamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*daśamaṃ brahmavaivarttaṃ laiṅgamekādaśaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*vārāhaṃ dvādaśaṃ proktaṃ skāndaṃ caiva trayodaśam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*caturdaśaṃ vāmanaṃ ca kaurmaṃ pañcadaśaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*mātsyaṃ ca gāruḍaṃ caiva brahmāṇḍaṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 64 \|\|*

*etāni kuruśārdūla dharmaśāstrāṇi paṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*sādhāraṇāni proktāni varṇānāṃ śreyase sadā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*caturṇāmiha rājendra śrotumarhāṇi suvrata \|*  
*kimicchasi mahābāho śrotumeṣāṃ nṛpottama \|\| 66 \|\|*

61-66. These eight Puranas are known as Vyakarana, I am also narrating the details of the eighteen Puranas, which may be listened by you. These are known as Brahma, Padma, Vaishnava, Shaiva, Bhagavata, Naradiya, Markandeya, Agneya, Bhavishya, Brahma-vaivarta, Lainga, Varaha, Skanda, Kaurma, Matsya, Garuda and Brahmanda. O lion of the Kuru race, the learned Brahmanas have ordinarily composed these Puranas for the benefit of the people of all the varnas. All the Puranas can be listened by all the four varnas. O best of the rulers, O valorous one, which one of these Puranas would you like to listen?

## \|\| 1.1.67 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*bhārataṃ tu śrutaṃ vipra tātasyāṅkagatena tu \|*  
*rāmasya caritaṃ cāpi śrutaṃ brahmansamantataḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Shatanika said — O Brahmana, I have already lead the narration of the auspicious Mahabharata by sitting in the lap of my father, besides the story of lord Rama from the beginning to the end.

## \|\| 1.1.68 \|\|

*purāṇāni ca viprendra bhaviṣyaṃ na tu suvrata \|*  
*purāṇaṃ vada viprendra bhaviṣyaṃ kautukaṃ hi me \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O best of the Brahmanas, similarly I have listened to the recitation of the rest of the Puranas. But I have not yet listened to the Bhavishya Purana so far. Therefore, O excellent Brahmana, you kindly narrate the story of the Bhavishya Purana to me. I am quite anxious to know about the same.

## \|\| 1.1.69 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhu sādhu mahābāho sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi 4 mānada \|*  
*śṛṇu me vadato rājan purāṇaṃ navamaṃ mahat \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Sumantu said — O great human and the valorous one, you have spoken excellently. O king, the Bhavishya Purana which is the ninth in the serial order, is being narrated by me, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.1.70 \|\|

*yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate mānavo nṛpa \|*  
*aśvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya gacched bhānau na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. This is the best of the Dharmashastra which was narrated initially by Brahma himself and by listening to it, a person is relieved of all the sins. The listener of the Bhavishya Purana achieves the merit of the performing of the Ashvamedha sacrifice and ultimately achieves the solar region or Suryaloka. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.1.71 \|\|

*idaṃ tu brahmaṇā proktaṃ dharmaśāstramanuttamam \|*  
*viduṣā brāhmaṇenedamadhyetavyaṃ prayatnataḥ 5 \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. This excellent Dharmashastra was narrated by Brahma himself. The learned Brahmanas should recite the same, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.1.72 \|\|

*śiṣyebhyaścaiva vaktavyaṃ cāturvarṇyebhya eva hi \|*  
*adhyetavyaṃ na cānyena brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vinā \|*  
*śrotavyameva śūdreṇa nādhyetavyaṃ kadācana 6 \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The same should be taught to the pupils of all the varnas. But, except the Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, it should not be studied by anyone else. The Shudras should only listen to the same.

## \|\| 1.1.73 \|\|

*devārcāṃ purataḥ 1 kṛtvā brāhmaṇaiśca nṛpottama \|*  
*śrotavyameva śūdraiśca tathānyaiśca dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O best of the rulers, initially after worshipping the gods and the Brahmanas, it should be listened to by the people. Similarly, the Shudras can listen to the same from the two castes (Brahmanas and Kshatriyas).

## \|\| 1.1.74 \|\|

*śrautaṃ smārtaṃ hi vai dharmaṃ proktamasminnṛpottama \|*  
*tasmācchūdrairvinā viprānna śrotavyaṃ kathañcana \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O best of the kings, all the Shrauta-Smarta Dharmas have been recited in this Purana, Therefore, the Shudras should listen to its narration from the Brahmanas and not from others.

## \|\| 1.1.75 \|\|

*idaṃ śāstramadhīyāno brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ \|*  
*manovāgdehajairnityaṃ karmadoṣairna limpate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A Brahmana who observes the discipline as well as the vratas can study this Purana and can get himself relieved from all the mental spoken and the bodily sins forever.

## \|\| 1.1.76 \|\|

*śṛṇvanti cāpi ye rājan bhaktyā vai brāhmaṇādayaḥ \|*  
*mucyante pātakaiḥ sarvairgacchanti ca divaṃ prabho \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Such of the people, who having been born in the family of Brahmanas listen to it with devotion, they also achieve the heaven getting relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.1.77 \|\|

*śrāvayeccāpi yo vipraḥ sarvānvarṇānnṛpottama \|*  
*sa guruḥ procyate tāta varṇānāmiha sarvaśaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O excellent monarch, a Brahmana who recites this Purana to the people of all the castes, he is turned to be the preceptor of all the varnas.

## \|\| 1.1.78 \|\|

*sa pūjyaḥ sarvakāleṣu sarvairvarṇairnarādhipa \|*  
*pṛthivīṃ ca tathaivemāṃ kṛtsnāmeko'pi so'rhati \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O excellent king, such a Brahmana becomes adorable from the people of all the varnas. He alone becomes competent for the whole of this earth.

## \|\| 1.1.79 \|\|

*idaṃ svastyayanaṃ śreṣṭhamidaṃ buddhivivardhanam \|*  
*idaṃ yaśasyaṃ satatamidaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ param \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. This is extremely beneficial, excellent and enhances the wisdom. It bestows immense and everlasting glory.

## \|\| 1.1.80 \|\|

*asmindharmo'khilenokto guṇadoṣau ca karmaṇām \|*  
*caturṇāmapi varṇānāmācāraścāpi śāśvataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The provisions of all the dharmas are enshrined therein. The good and evil effects of the karmas (deeds) have been discussed therein. The conduct and performances of the people of all the four varnas have been specified.

## \|\| 1.1.81 \|\|

*ācāraḥ prathamo dharmaḥ śrutyuktaśca narottama \|*  
*tasmādasminsamāyukto nityaṃ syādātmavāndvijaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. O best of kings, the conduct is considered to be the foremost of all the varnas, which has been highlighted in the Shrutis. This is the reason that the Brahmana having his faith in this Purana, can exercise his control over his mind.

## \|\| 1.1.82 \|\|

*ācārādvicyuto vipro na vedaphalamaśnute \|*  
*ācāreṇa ca saṃyuktaḥ sampūrṇaphalabhāksmṛtaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. A Brahmana, who falls from his good conduct cannot enjoy the fruits of the Vedas and due to his noble conduct enjoys the benefit of all the fruits.

## \|\| 1.1.83 \|\|

*evamācārato dṛṣṭvā dharmasya munayo gatim \|*  
*sarvasya tapaso mūlamācāraṃ jagṛhuḥ param \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The sages, having observed the movements of dharmas with the conduct and come to the conclusion that the conduct alone is the root of all the tapas.

## \|\| 1.1.84 \|\|

*anye ca mānavā rājannācāraṃ saṃśritā sadā \|*  
*evamasminpurāṇe tu ācārasya tu kīrtanam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O king, because of this reason, the humans also take refuge under the noble conduct as well. In this Purana, emphasis has been laid over the observing of the good conduct.

## \|\| 1.1.85 \|\|

*vṛttāntāni ca rājendra tathā coktāni paṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*trilokyāstu samutpattiḥ saṃskāravidhiruttamaḥ \|*  
*śravaṇaṃ cetihāsasya vidhānaṃ kathyate nṛpa \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Besides these, the learned ascetics have also discussed in this Purana, several of the events, stories and the episodes. There is the mention about the creation of the three worlds. The method of performing the best of samskaras have been discussed in detail. The predication of history have been discussed, besides the glory for listening to the same.

## \|\| 1.1.86-87 \|\|

*tathāsminkathyate rājanmāhātmyaṃ vācakasya tu \|*  
*vratacaryāśramācārāḥ snātakasya paro vidhiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*dārādigamanaṃ caiva vivāhānāṃ ca lakṣaṇam \|*  
*puṃsāṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ rājanyoṣitāṃ cātra kathyate \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. O king, besides this, the glory of the orators or the speakers has been discussed. The methods of performing the various types of vratas, the conduct of ashramas, the activities of the graduates, sex with women, symptoms of marriage, the symptoms of men and the women have been discussed.

## \|\| 1.1.88-90 \|\|

*mahāyajñavidhānaṃ ca śāstrakalpaṃ ca śāśvatam \|*  
*pṛthivyā lakṣaṇaṃ tāta devārcāyāḥ sulakṣaṇam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*vṛttīnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ caiva snātakasya vratāni ca \|*  
*bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ śuddhireva ca \|\| 89 \|\|*

*strīdharmayogastāpasyaṃ mokṣaḥ saṃnyāsa eva ca \|*  
*rājñaśca dharmo hyakhilaḥ kāryāṇāṃ ca vinirṇayaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. O excellent one, the method of performing the great yajnas, the eternal Shastra-cakra or kalpa, the symptoms of the earth, the method of the worship of the gods, symptoms of livelihood, rules for the students, the eatable and non-eatable food, means of cleanliness, purification of the materials, the dharma of the ladies, tapas and the yogic practices, moksha (salvation) and Sannyasa, all the royal dharmas and the method of their taking decisions have been discussed therein.

## \|\| 1.1.91-92 \|\|

*māhātmyaṃ savituścātra tīrthānāṃ ca viśāmpate \|*  
*nārāyaṇasya māhātmyaṃ tathā rudrasya kathyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

*mahābhāgyaṃ ca viprāṇāṃ māhātmyaṃ pustakasya ca \|*  
*durgādevyāstathā coktaṃ satyasya ca mahāmate \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. O king, besides the above, the glory of the sun, the glory of the holy places, glory of Narayana, the glory of the Brahmanas, glory of the book, besides O immensely intelligent one, the glory of the goddess Durga and the glory of truth has been discussed therein.

## \|\| 1.1.93-98 \|\|

*saṃkṣiptaṃ 1 saṃvidhānaṃ ca dharmaṃ strīpuṃsayorapi \|*  
*vibhāgaṃ dharmadyūtaṃ ca kathakānāṃ ca śodhanam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*vaiśyaśūdropacāraṃ ca saṃkīrṇānāṃ ca saṃbhavam \|*  
*āpaddharmaṃ ca varṇānāṃ prāyaścittavidhiṃ tathā \|\| 94 \|\|*

*saṃdhyāvidhiṃ pretaśuddhiṃ snānatarpaṇayorvidhim \|*  
*vaiśvadevavidhiṃ cāpi tathā bhojyavidhiṃ nṛpa \|\| 95 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇaṃ dantakāṣṭhasya caraṇavyūhamuttamam \|*  
*saṃsāragamanaṃ caiva trividhaṃ karmasambhavam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*naiḥśreyasaṃ karmaṇāṃ ca guṇadoṣaparīkṣaṇam \|*  
*dārāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ tathā pātraparīkṣaṇam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*prasūtiṃ cāpi garbhasya tathā karmaphalaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*jātidharmānkuladharmānvedadharmāṃśca 1 pārthiva \|\| 98 \|\|*

93-98. The dharmas of men and women, the methods in brief, spiritual gamble and its divisions, correction of old stories, performance of Vaishyas and the Shudras, birth of the hybrid castes, dharmas at the birth of all the varnas, repentance for the sins performed, method of performing Sandhya, purification of a goblin, method of taking bath and performing of oblation, method of performing Vaishvadeva rites, method of taking food, symptoms of Dantakashtha (tooth stick), to have birth in the world due to different deeds and the related stories, receiving of the glory according to deeds, analysis of the good and evil deeds, the symptoms of foe women, test of the performers, description of the effect of the karmas and the narration of the fruit of the deeds at the time of birth, have been described in this The discussion of the dharmas of a caste, race and the Vedic dharmas have been discussed therein.

## \|\| 1.1.99 \|\|

*vaitānavratikānāṃ ca tathāsau proktavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*brahmā kurukulaśreṣṭha śaṃkarāya mahātmane \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O best king of the race of Kuru, lord Brahma had narrated the glory of the vratas of Vaitanika type to lord Shiva.

## \|\| 1.1.100-102 \|\|

*śaṃkareṇa tathā viṣṇoḥ kathitaṃ kurunandana \|*  
*viṣṇunāpi punaḥ proktaṃ nāradāya mahīpate \|\| 100 \|\|*

*nāradātprāptavāñchakraḥ śakrādapi parāśaraḥ \|*  
*parāśarāttato vyāso vyāsādapi mayā vibho \|\| 101 \|\|*

*evaṃ paramparāprāptaṃ purāṇamidamuttamam \|*  
*śṛṇu tvamapi rājendra matsakāśātparaṃ hitam \|\| 102 \|\|*

100-102. O son of Kuru race, thereafter lord Shiva repeated it to lord Vishnu. O lord of earth, again lord Vishnu repeated the same to Narada who in turn revealed the same to Indra. Parashara passed it on to the sage Vyasa. I however received the same from Vyasadeva. I achieved this Purana as per the appraisal tradition. O great king, you also listen from me the beneficial and the excellent Purana.

## \|\| 1.1.103-104 \|\|

*sarvāṇyeva purāṇāni saṃjñeyāni nararṣabha \|*  
*dvādaśaiva sahasrāṇi proktānīha manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*punarvṛddhiṃ gatānīha ākhyānairvividhairvṛṣa \|*  
*yathā skāndaṃ tathā cedaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ kurunandana \|\| 104 \|\|*

103-104. O best of humans, the people of wisdom count the number of verses as twelve thousand. But with the subsequent addition of other stories in it, the number of its verses has been immensely increased.

## \|\| 1.1.105 \|\|

*skāndaṃ śatasahasraṃ tu lokānāṃ jñātameva hi \|*  
*bhaviṣyametadṛṣiṇā lakṣārddhaṃ saṃkhyayā kṛtam 2 \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The number of the verses in Skanda Purana is one lakh, which is well known to everyone. The number of the verses of this Purana has been given as fifty thousand.

## \|\| 1.1.106 \|\|

*tacchrutvā puruṣo bhaktyā idaṃ phalamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*ṛddhirvṛddhistathā śrīśca bhavanti tasya niścitam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. By listening to Bhavishya Purana with devotion, one achieves all types of success, besides the riches are surely achieved by a person.

## Chapter 2. Creation of the universe and reciting of the Vedas from the five months of Brahma

## \|\| 1.2.1 \|\|

*vājapeyo'tirātraśca āptoryāmeti vai smṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O valorous king, you listen to the Bhavishya Purana with its five characteristics, hearing which a person is released of the sin of Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 1.2.2 \|\|

*tāsāṃ guṇo raso jñeyaḥ sarvalokasya bhāvanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Svayambhu has mentioned about five parvas in it. Brahma-parva is the first one, while the second one is Vaishnava.

## \|\| 1.2.3 \|\|

*tṛtīyaṃ śaivamākhyātaṃ caturthaṃ tvāṣṭramucyate \|*  
*pañcamaṃ pratisargākhyaṃ sarvalokaiḥ supūjitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The third one is Shaiva and the fourth one is Tvashtra. The fifth one is known as Pratisarga.

## \|\| 1.2.4-5 \|\|

*etāni tāta parvāṇi lakṣaṇāni nibodha me \|*  
*sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam \|*  
*caturdaśabhirvidyābhirbhūṣitaṃ kurunandana \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Which is adored by all. Thus, there are five sargas of the Bhavishya Purana. Now you listen to their characteristics. Sarga (creation of the universe), Pratisarga (creation of Daksha and other Prajapatis under Svayambhuva), Vamsha (dynasties) and Manvantaras. In fact, the seventy one divine yugas make a Manvantara, and deals with the stories of the kings coming under each dynasty. These are the five characters of the Puranas which are well established. O king of the Kuru race, this Purana is decorated with the fourteen lores.

## \|\| 1.2.6 \|\|

*aṅgāni caturo vedā mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ \|*  
*purāṇaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca vidyā hyetāścaturdaśa \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The fourteen lores include all the four Vedas, six angas of the Vedas, Mimamsa (one of the six systems of Hindu philosophy), comprehensive logic, Purana and Dharmashastras are the fourteen lores.

## \|\| 1.2.7 \|\|

*āyurvedo dhanurvedo gāndharvaścaiva te trayaḥ \|*  
*arthaśāstraṃ caturthaṃ tu vidyā hyaṣṭādaśaiva tāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Ayurveda (the science of medicines), Dhanurveda (archery), Gandharvaveda (science of dance and music) and Arthashastra when added to the above said lores, their number reaches eighteen.

## \|\| 1.2.8 \|\|

*prathamaṃ kathyate sargo bhūtānāmiha sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*yacchrutvā pāpanirmukto yāti śāntimanuttamām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Initially, there is a mention of the creation of the universe in this Purana, listening to which a person is relieved of all the sins and achieves peace.

## \|\| 1.2.9 \|\|

*jagadāsītpurā tāta tamobhūtamalakṣaṇam \|*  
*avijñeyamatarkyaṃ ca prasuptamiva sarvaśaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent one, the world had initially plunged in darkness, have no characteristic at all. It could not be known by any means. It was beyond reasoning and looked like the one under deep sleep.

## \|\| 1.2.10-11 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhagavānīśo hyavyakto vyañjayannidam \|*  
*mahābhūtāni vṛttaujāḥ protthitastamanāśanaḥ 1 \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yo'sāvatīndriyo'grāhyaḥ sūkṣmo'vyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*sarvabhūtamayo'cintyaḥ sa eṣa svayamutthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Thereafter, the supreme lord turned the invisible world as visible, produced the five elements, viz. the earth, fire, water, wind and the sky, destroying the heap of darkness. The one who is beyond the sense organs, beyond absorption, is gross as well as subtle, eternal, who always remains in the same form, pervades in all the jivas and is beyond comprehension, He rises up at the same time.

## \|\| 1.2.12 \|\|

*yo'sau ṣaḍviṃśako loke tathā yaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*bhāskaraśca mahābāho paraṃ brahma ca kathyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He is known as the thirty-sixth padartha (element) of the universe. It is he who is well-known as Purushottama. O valorous one, he is also known as Bhaskara as well as the supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 1.2.13 \|\|

*so'bhidhyāya śarīrātsvātsisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*ata eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryamavāsṛjat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The same lord, with the desire of creating various types of subjects, started thinking. Then he created water first of all and drops his semen in the same.

## \|\| 1.2.14 \|\|

*yasmādutpadyate sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*bījaṃ śukraṃ tathā reta ugraṃ vīryaṃ ca kathyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The whole universe including the gods, asuras, humans are born. It is also called the seed, semen, mercury etc.

## \|\| 1.2.15 \|\|

*vīryasyaitāni nāmāni kathitāni svayambhuvā \|*  
*tadaṇḍamabhavaddhaimaṃ jvālāmālākulaṃ vibho \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Svayambhu has mentioned various names of semen. O lord, the said semen was turned into the form of a resplendent golden egg.

## \|\| 1.2.16-17 \|\|

*yasmiñjajñe svayaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*surajyeṣṭhaścaturvaktraḥ parameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṣetrajñaḥ puruṣo vedhāḥ śambhurnārāyaṇastathā \|*  
*paryāyavācakaiḥ śabdaireva brahmā prakīrtyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Out of this Brahma — the grandsire of all, was born by himself. Brahma — the grandsire, was the best of all the gods, having four faces, Paramesthi, Kshetrajna, Purusha, Vedha, Shambhu and Narayana. He is known by these synonymous names as well.

## \|\| 1.2.18 \|\|

*āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O excellent one, he is also called as Viranchi, Kanjaja and other names as well. He is also known by the name of Narayana. The reason behind it is that the word ‘nara’ is used for the water as well as the son of Nara.

## \|\| 1.2.19 \|\|

*tā yadasyāyanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*aramityeva śīghrāya niyatāḥ kavibhiḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Initially he dwelt in the water itself. Therefore, he is known by the name of Narayana as well. The poets also use the word ‘aram’ for the formation of the word Narayana.

## \|\| 1.2.20-22 \|\|

*āpa 3 evārṇavībhūtvā suśīghrāstena tā narāḥ \|*  
*yattatkāraṇamavyaktaṃ nityaṃ sadasadātmakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tadvisṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣo loke brahmeti kīrttyate \|*  
*evaṃ sa bhagavānaṇḍe tattvameva nirūpya vai \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dhyānamāsthāya rājendra tadaṇḍamakaroddvidhā \|*  
*śakalābhyāṃ ca rājendra divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca nirmame \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The water turning itself into an ocean flows swiftly, therefore it is called Nara. The one who is the cause of the creation of all is infallible, eternal, truth, non-existent. Having been born out of him, the universe has been known by the name of Brahma. Thus with firm resolve for starting the creation, the lord, inserted in the golden egg, all the tattvas in the golden egg, having been reminded of the earlier creation, divided the golden egg into two parts. O great king, both the sky and the earth were created with both the parts of the golden egg.

## \|\| 1.2.23 \|\|

*antarvyoma diśaścāṣṭau vāruṇaṃ sthānameva hi \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ mahāngato rājan samantāllokabhūtaye \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereafter, the sky, the eight directions, besides all the oceans were created. O king, thus, for the benefit of the universe, raising himself up, he built all of them.

## \|\| 1.2.24 \|\|

*mahataścāpyahaṃkārastasmācca triguṇā api \|*  
*triguṇā atisūkṣmāstu buddhigamyā hi bhārata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Out of grandeur emerged the arrogance, and three gunas — sattva, rajas and tamas emerged out of it. O Bharatas, all the three gunas are quite subtle and can be known with the use of intelligence.

## \|\| 1.2.25 \|\|

*utpattihetubhūtā vai bhūtānāṃ mahatāṃ nṛpa \|*  
*teṣāmeva gṛhītāni śanaiḥ pañcendriyāṇi tu \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O king, all the three gunas (sattva, rajas and tamas) are the cause for the creation of all the elements in the world. All the five sense organs were slowly created due to them.

## \|\| 1.2.26-27 \|\|

*tathaivāvayavāḥ sūkṣmāḥ ṣaṇṇāmapyamitaujasām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saṃniveśyātmamātrāsu sa rājanbhagavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*bhūtāni nirmame tāta sarvāṇi vidhipūrvakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The limbs of all the six of them are also subtle like themselves. O king, the illustrious lord, by entering into the soul, created all the elements appropriately by entering into them.

## \|\| 1.2.28 \|\|

*yanmūrtyavayavāḥ sūkṣmāstasyemānyāśrayāṇi ṣaṭ \|*  
*tasmāccharīramityāhustasya mūrtiṃ manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The subtle limbs of the body are said to be the six abodes for him. The images made by him are known to the people as the human bodies.

## \|\| 1.2.29-32 \|\|

*mahānti tāni bhūtāni āviśanti tato vibhum \|*  
*karmaṇā saha rājendra saguṇāścāpi vai guṇāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*teṣāmidaṃ tu saptānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ mahaujasām \|*  
*sūkṣmābhyo mūrtimātrābhyaḥ sambhavatyavyayādvayam 1 \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhūtādimahatastāta yena vyāptamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*tasmādapi mahābāho puruṣāḥ pañca eva hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kecidevaṃ parāṃ tāta sṛṣṭimicchanti paṇḍitāḥ \|*  
*anye'pyevaṃ mahābāho pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. O excellent king, because of the merits of the earlier births, the other elements also enter the body with the three gunas. The perishable universe emerges out of the image of the seven Purushas with matras. O excellent one, several elements pervade the universe. O valorous one, out of which the five Purushas alone are born. O excellent one, some learned people desire for the creation of the universe like this. This is also claimed by other people of wisdom.

## \|\| 1.2.33 \|\|

*yo'sāvātmā parastāta kalpādau sṛjate tanum \|*  
*prajanaśca mahābāho sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The one which is known as the supreme soul, they themselves, taking themselves to the human forms and create the people of the universe at the time of its origin. They themselves take to human forms, create different types of subjects in the whole world.

## \|\| 1.2.34 \|\|

*tena sṛṣṭaḥ pudgalastu pradhānaṃ viśate nṛpa \|*  
*pradhānaṃ kṣobhitaṃ tena vikārānyujate bahūn \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O king, the atoms created by them enter the Prakriti and by getting disturbed by them, Pradhana creates several types of creations.

## \|\| 1.2.35 \|\|

*utpadyate mahāṃstasmāttato bhūtādireva hi \|*  
*utpadyate viśālaṃ ca bhūtādeḥ kurunandana \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. It gives birth to Mahat and from the Mahal the Bhutas (the demons) are born. O son of the Kuru race, out of those Bhutas, the gigantic is produced.

## \|\| 1.2.36 \|\|

*viśālācca haristāta hareścāpi vṛkāstathā \|*  
*vṛkairmuṣṇanti ca budhāstasmātsarvaṃ bhavennṛpa \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Hari emerges out of the gigantic one and a Vrika or Hari is born. The Vrika then conceal the people with intelligence. O king, the entire universe emerges out of the same.

## \|\| 1.2.37 \|\|

*tathaiṣāmeva rājendra prādurbhavati vegataḥ \|*  
*mātrāṇāṃ kuruśārdūla vibodhastadanantaram 1 \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Rajendra, O lion among the Kurus, with the force of the same, the matras are known.

## \|\| 1.2.38 \|\|

*tasmādapi hṛṣīkāṇi vividhāni nṛpottama \|*  
*tatheyaṃ sṛṣṭirākhyātā'rādhyataḥ kurunandana \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O best of the rulers, the various types of sense organs emerge out of the same. O son of the race of Kurus, the universe is created with such a type of creation, it is said.

## \|\| 1.2.39 \|\|

*bhūyo nibodha rājendra bhūtānāmiha vistaram \|*  
*guṇādhikāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni pṛthivīpate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O great king, you listen again on the topic of the expansion of the Bhutas. O lord of the earth, in all the Bhutas some of the gunas are found in excess.

## \|\| 1.2.40 \|\|

*ākāśamāditaḥ kṛtvā uttarottarameva hi \|*  
*ekaṃ dvau ca tathā trīṇi catvāraścāpi pañca ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Initially, after creating the sky, progressively one, two, three, four and five Bhutas are formed.

## \|\| 1.2.41 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhagavānbrahmā padmāsanagataḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ tu sa nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thereafter, the lord Brahma seated in padmasana declare the names of everyone and the duties allotted to each one of them, individually.

## \|\| 1.2.42 \|\|

*vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthaksaṃsthāśca nirmame \|*  
*karmodbhavānāṃ devānāṃ so'sṛjaddehināṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. With the word Veda, the existence of all is known. The lord, then created the Devas on the basis of the deeds performed by them in the earlier birth.

## \|\| 1.2.43-45 \|\|

*tuṣitānāṃ gaṇaṃ rājanyajñaṃ caiva sanātanam \|*  
*dattvā 2 vīra samānebhyo guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dudoha yajñasiddhayarthamṛgyajuḥ sāmalakṣaṇam \|*  
*kālaṃ kālavibhaktīśca 3 grahānṛtūṃstathā nṛpa \|\| 44 \|\|*

*saritaḥ sāgarāñchailānsamāni viṣamāṇi ca \|*  
*kāmaṃ krodhaṃ tathā vācaṃ ratiṃ cāpi kurudvaha \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. The origin of Tushita gods is thus attributed. Thereafter, the yajnas which always remained in vogue, were created. Then all the people of the universe possessing equal powers, were bestowed with the extremely secret knowledge of Brahman. Then for the achieving of the successful knowledge of the yajnas, the Vedas known as Rik, Yajuh and Sama were milked Then followed the creation of time, different parts of time, besides the planets, seasons, rivers, oceans, the plain, even and uneven lands, the mountains like high lands, kama (desire), krodha (anger), speed, love, etc. were created.

## \|\| 1.2.46 \|\|

*sṛṣṭiṃ sasarja rājendra sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*dharmādharmau vivekāya karmaṇāṃ ca tathāsṛjat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Rajendra, similarly with the desire of creating several types of creatures or people, the deeds were created for differentiating between dharma and adharma (righteousness and evil).

## \|\| 1.2.47-52 \|\|

*sukhaduḥkhādibhirdvandvaiḥ prajāścemā nyayojayat \|*  
*aṇvyo mātrāvināśinyo daśārdhānāṃ tu yāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tābhiḥ sarvamidaṃ vīra sambhavatyanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*yatkṛtaṃ tu purā karma sanniyuktena vai nṛpa \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sa tadeva svayaṃ bheje sṛjyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharme ṛtānṛte \|\| 49 \|\|*

*yadyathāsyābhavatsarge tattasya svayamāviśat \|*  
*yathā ca liṅgānyṛtavaḥ svayamevānuparyaye \|\| 50 \|\|*

*svāni svānyabhipadyante tathā karmāṇi dehinaḥ \|*  
*lokasyeha vivṛddhyarthaṃ mukhabāhūrupādataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*brahma kṣatraṃ tathā cobhau vaiśyaśūdrau nṛpottama \|*  
*mukhāni yāni catvāri tebhyo vedā viniḥsṛtāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

47-52. Thereafter, the people were entangled in the conflicts of pleasure and pain, which are known as Panchamatras and which are indestructible. O valorous one, with all these elements stated above, the world develops gradually. O king, whatever task is initially performed by a person, having been influenced by the will of the Almighty, the same is received by him again and again which ever activities like violence or non-violence, pleasant or cruel, righteous or unrighteous, true or false a person accumulate, in the same type of activities he is involved in the world. O monarch, as the seasons automatically achieve the symptoms of their respective time, similarly the souls with bodies, automatically achieve the reward of their order deeds. O best of monarchs, for the expansion of the universe, from the face, arms, thighs and the feet, there emerged Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and the Shudras. From the four faces of Brahma, the Vedas were created.

## \|\| 1.2.53 \|\|

*ṛgvedasahitā tāta vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā \|*  
*pūrvānmukhānmahābāho dakṣiṇāccāpi vai śṛṇu \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O excellent one, in earlier time, sage Vasishtha received Rigveda Samhita from eastern face. From the right face, the Veda which emerges is going to be told by me.

## \|\| 1.2.54-55 \|\|

*yajurvedo mahārāja yājñavalkyena vai saha \|*  
*sāmāni paścimāttāta gautamaśca mahānṛṣiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*atharvavedo rājendra mukhāccāpyuttarānnṛpa \|*  
*ṛṣiścāpi tathā rājañchaunako lokapūjitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. From the right face, Rishi Yajnavalkya received the Yajurveda, O excellent one, similarly from the western face the Rishi Gautama received Samaveda from Brahma. O Rajendra, from the northern face of Brahma, Rishi Shaunaka who is revered over the entire world, received Atharvaveda.

## \|\| 1.2.56-59 \|\|

*yattanmukhaṃ mahābāho pañcamaṃ lokaviśrutam \|*  
*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni setihāsāni bhārata \|\| 56 \|\|*

*nirgatāni tatastasmānmukhātkurukulodvaha \|*  
*tathānyāḥ smṛtayaścāpi yamādyā lokapūjitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa bhagavāndevo dvidhā dehamakārayat \|*  
*dvidhā kṛtvātmano dehamardhena puruṣo'bhavat \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ardhena nārī tasyāṃ ca virājamasṛjatprabhuḥ \|*  
*tapastaptvāsṛjadyaṃ tu sa svayaṃ puruṣo virāṭ \|\| 59 \|\|*

56-59. O long armed one, O Bharata, the famous fifth face of Brahma revealed besides the history, the eighteen Puranas. O son of Kuru race, similarly the fifth face of Brahma spoke the five world revered Shrutis as well as the Dharmashastras. Thereafter, lord Brahma divided his body into two parts, viz., male and a female. O Rajendra, the lord resorted to the gigantic creation out of the female part of his body. The figure which was created by him, was none else than Virata Purusha himself.

## \|\| 1.2.60 \|\|

*sa cakāra tapo rājansisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*patīnprajānāmasṛjanmaharṣīnādito daśa \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O monarch, with the desire of creating various types of people, he performed tapas. Initially, ten Rishis known as Prajapatis were created by him.

## \|\| 1.2.61-62 \|\|

*nāradaṃ ca bhṛguṃ tāta kaṃ pracetasameva hi \|*  
*pulahaṃ kratuṃ pulastyaṃ ca atrimaṅgirasaṃ tathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*marīciṃ cāpi rājendra yo'sāvādyaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*etāṃścānyāṃśca rājendra asṛjad bhūritejasaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. They came to be known by the names of Narada, Vasishtha, Pracheta, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri, Angiras and Maricha. O Rajendra, Maricha was the foremost of all the Prajapatis. The aforesaid Prajapati Rishis as well as several other Rishis were created by Brahma who were quite illustrious.

## \|\| 1.2.63-64 \|\|

*atha devānṛṣīndaityānso'sṛjatkurunandana \|*  
*yakṣarakṣaḥ piśācāṃśca gandharvāpsaraso'surān \|\| 63 \|\|*

*manuṣyāṇāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ caiva bhārata \|*  
*nāgānāṃ ca mahābāho sasarja vividhāngaṇān \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. O son of the race of Kuru, similarly the Gods, Daityas and other Rishis were created. O Bharata, O long armed one, thereafter, the yajnas, Rakshasas, Pishachas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, Asuras, the humans, Pitris, serpents, Nagas and several types of ganas were created.

## \|\| 1.2.65 \|\|

*kṣaṇaruco'śanigaṇānrohitendradhanūṃṣi ca \|*  
*dhūmaketūṃstathā colkā niryātāñjyotiṣāṃ gaṇān \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Similarly were created the lightenings which disappear in a moment after issuing lustre, rainbows, comets, besides the astrological chakras devoid of wind.

## \|\| 1.2.66-67 \|\|

*manuṣyānkinnarānmatsyānvarāhāṃśca vihaṅgamān \|*  
*gajānaśvānatha paśūnmṛgānvyālāṃśca bhārata \|\| 66 \|\|*

*kṛmikīṭapataṅgāṃśca yūkālikṣakamatkuṇān \|*  
*sarvaṃ ca daṃśamaśakaṃ sthāvaraṃ1 ca pṛthagvidham \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. O son of the Kuru race, in this way, the lord created the humans, Kinnaras, fish, the birds, elephants, horses, animals, deer, serpents, insects, worms, flies, lies, louse, bugs, mosquitoes, biting insects and various types of immobiles.

## \|\| 1.2.68-70 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhāskaro devaḥ sasarja bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*yeṣāṃ tu yādṛśaṃ karma bhūtānāmiha kīrtitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kathayiṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ kramayogaṃ ca janmani \|*  
*gajā vyālā mṛgāstāta paśavaśca pṛthagvidhāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*piśācā mānuṣāstāta rakṣāṃsi ca jarāyujāḥ \|*  
*dvijāstu aṇḍajāḥ sarpā nakrā matsyāḥ sakacchapāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. Thus the lord Bhaskara created the three types of Bhuvanas. Whatever of performance of the respected Bhutas, is being related by me in a chronological order. O excellent one, creation of the elephants, serpents, deer and various species of the animals is being narrated by me. O excellent one, now I am going to speak about the herds of elephants, serpents, deer and animals of other species. The Pishachas and the creatures which are born of membrane, besides humans, Rakshasas, serpents, crocodiles, fish, tortoise, the birds of all species who are bare of eggs, their performance is also being narrated.

## \|\| 1.2.71-72 \|\|

*evaṃvidhāni yānīha sthalajānyaudakāni ca \|*  
*svedajaṃ daṃśamaśakaṃ yūkālikṣakamatkuṇāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*ūṣmaṇā copajāyante yaccānyatkiñcidīdṛśam \|*  
*udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ sarve bījakāṇḍaprarohiṇaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Similarly, the biting insects like mosquitoes which are born in water or ground, including biting insects, mosquitoes, lies etc., the bugs besides those which are born of sweating, are all born of the heat. Then the creatures which are born of seeds and sugarcane, come under the category of vegetation.

## \|\| 1.2.73 \|\|

*oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntā nānāvidhaphalopagāḥ \|*  
*apuṣpāḥ phalavanto ye te vanaspatayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The several types of herbs with their fruits remain alive till the fruits get ripe or in other words the herbs are dried up after the fruits growing thereon are ripened. Such of the growth which is without flowers, but bear fruits is called the vegetation.

## \|\| 1.2.74 \|\|

*puṣpiṇaḥ phalinaścaiva vṛkṣāstūbhayataḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*gucchagulmaṃ tu vividhaṃ tathaiva tṛṇajātayaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The growth which flowers and bears fruit, are known as trees. There are several types of bunches and shrubs. Similarly, there are various varieties of the grass.

## \|\| 1.2.75 \|\|

*bījakāṇḍaruhāṇyeva pratānā 1 vallya eva ca \|*  
*tamasā bahurūpeṇa veṣṭitāḥ karmahetunā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Growing from the seeds as well as the canes, the creepers climb over the trees and are known as climbers. Because of their relationship with the deeds of the earlier births, they are surrounded by different types of darkness.

## \|\| 1.2.76 \|\|

*antaḥsaṃjñā bhavantyete sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*etāvatyastu gatayaḥ prodbhūtāḥ kurunandana \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They are quite conscious inwardly and they also feel the pleasure and the pain. O son of Kura’s race, these movements of the creatures are quite apparent.

## \|\| 1.2.77 \|\|

*tasmāddevāddīptimanto bhāskarācya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ghore'smiṃstāta saṃsāre nityaṃ satatayāyini \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O excellent one, the extremely lustrous Sun-god moves the entire universe with his brilliance, every moment.

## \|\| 1.2.78 \|\|

*evaṃ sarvaṃ sa sṛṣṭvedaṃ rājaṃllokaguruṃ param \|*  
*tirobhūtaḥ sa bhūtātmā kālaṃ kālena pīḍayan \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O king, the supreme soul, after causing pain to Kala, by the time happens to be the soul of all the creatures, besides being the preceptor of all, disappears after the creation comes into effect.

## \|\| 1.2.79 \|\|

*yadā sa devo jāgarti tadedaṃ ceṣṭate jagat \|*  
*yadā svapiti śāntātmā tadā sarvaṃ nimīlati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. At the awakening of the lord, the entire universe becomes active and when the peaceful soul intends to go to sleep, then the whole universe is absorbed in him.

## \|\| 1.2.80 \|\|

*tasminsvapiti rājendra jantavaḥ karmabandhanāḥ \|*  
*svakarmabhyo nivartante manaśca glānimṛcchati \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O Rajendra, the Jivas are captive of their deeds, are absolved of their activities, when the lord goes to sleep. Their minds feel weariness.

## \|\| 1.2.81 \|\|

*yugapattu pralīyante yadā tasminmahātmani \|*  
*tadāyaṃ sarvabhūtātmā sukhaṃ svapiti bhārata \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. O Bharata, all are absorbed in the great soul together. At that point of time, the lord, who happens to be the soul of all the creatures, as a result of which, the lord sleeps with comfort.

## \|\| 1.2.82 \|\|

*tamo yadā samāśritya ciraṃ tiṣṭhati sendriyaḥ \|*  
*na navaṃ kurute karma tadotkrāmati mūrtitaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Taking refuge with tamoguna, when he squeezing all his sense organs, remains in that condition for long and does not indulge in any new activity, at that point of time, he emerges out of the image.

## \|\| 1.2.83 \|\|

*yadāhaṃmātriko bhūtvā bījaṃ sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca \|*  
*samāviśati saṃsṛṣṭastadā mūtiṃ vimuñcati \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. When he enters in the seeds of all the mobiles and immobiles, then he imprecates their, leaving his amsha in all of them.

## \|\| 1.2.84 \|\|

*evaṃ sa jāgratsvapnābhyāmidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatprabhuḥ \|*  
*saṃjīvayati cājasraṃ pramāpayati cāvyayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The influential and everlasting lord, in his sleeping as well as the awakening positions, enlivens and causes limitation to the entire Universe.

## \|\| 1.2.85 \|\|

*kalpādau sṛjate tāta ante kalpasya saṃharet \|*  
*dinaṃ tasyeha yattāta kalpāntamiti kathyate \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. O excellent one, at the start of the Kalpa, the universe is created and destroys it at the end of the Kalpa. The time of his awakening is known to be the end of the Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.2.86 \|\|

*kālasaṃkhyāṃ tatastasya 1 kalpasya śṛṇu bhārata \|*  
*nimeṣā daśa cāṣṭau ca akṣṇaḥ kāṣṭhā nigadyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O Bharata, you listen about the length of the Kalpa, which is going to be revealed by me. The time one takes in the winking of an eye, is called as nimesha. Eighteen such nimeshas make one Kashtha.

## \|\| 1.2.87 \|\|

*triṃśatkāṣṭhāḥ kalāmāhuḥ kṣaṇastriṃśatkalāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*muhūrtamatha mauhūrtā vadanti dvādaśa kṣaṇam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. A kala comprises of thirty kashthas. A kshana comprising of thirty kalas. The learned people well-versed in Muhurtas declare a Muhurta to be of twelve kshanas.

## \|\| 1.2.88 \|\|

*triṃśanmuhūrtamuddiṣṭamahorātraṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*māsastriṃśadahorātraṃ dvau dvau māsāvṛtuḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The people with intelligence have decided a day to be of thirty Muhurtas. A month comprises of thirty days and a season comprises of two months.

## \|\| 1.2.89 \|\|

*ṛtutrayamapyayanamayane dve tu vatsaraḥ \|*  
*ahorātre vibhajate sūryo mānuṣadaivike \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. An Ayana is formed of three seasons, while a year has two Ayanas (or twelve months). The days and nights of both humans and the gods are divided by the sun.

## \|\| 1.2.90 \|\|

*rātriḥ svapnāya bhūtānāṃ ceṣṭāyai karmaṇāmahaḥ \|*  
*pitrye rātryahanī māsaḥ pravibhāgastu pakṣayoḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The nights are meant for the sleeping of the bhutas and the day is meant for the continuation of the activities. A day and night of the pitris comprises of a month of the humans.

## \|\| 1.2.91 \|\|

*karma ceṣṭāsvahaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ muktaḥ svapnāya śarvarī \|*  
*daive rātryahanī varṣaṃ pravibhāgastayoḥ punaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. A human fortnight is a day for them and another fortnight is the night for them. For the carrying on of the activities, the bright human fortnight is meant for them, while the dark fortnight is meant for their rest. An year of the gods is a day and night for the humans.

## \|\| 1.2.92-93 \|\|

*ahastatrodagayanaṃ rātriḥ syāddakṣiṇāyanam \|*  
*brāhmasya tu kṣapāhasya yatpramāṇaṃ mahīpate \|\| 92 \|\|*

*ekaikaśo yugānāṃ tu kramaśastantibodha me \|*  
*catvāryāhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tatkṛtaṃ yugam \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. The day and night is divided by them, Uttarayana is the day for the gods and Dakshinayana is the night for them. The measure of the day and night for Brahma is going to be related by me according to the sequence of each yuga. You please listen. It is believed that Satyayuga comprises of four thousand years.

## \|\| 1.2.94 \|\|

*tasya tāvacchatī sandhyā sandhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ \|*  
*tretā trīṇi sahasrāṇi varṣāṇi ca vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Their Shandilya (evening) as well as Sandhyamsha comprises of four hundred years. The length of Sandhya has been stated to be this. The learned people believe that Tretayuga comprises of three thousand years.

## \|\| 1.2.95 \|\|

*śatāni ṣaṭ ca rājendra sandhyāsandhyāṃśayoḥ pṛthak \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ dve sahasre tu dvāpare parikīrtite \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. O Rajendra, the length of Sandhya as well Sandhyamsha is six hundred years each. The length of Dvapara yuga is said to be of two thousand years.

## \|\| 1.2.96 \|\|

*catvāri ca śatānyāhuḥ sandhyāsandhyāṃśayorbudhaḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ kathitaṃ tiṣye śatadvayasamanvitam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The learned people conceive the length of Sandhya and Sandhyamsha as four hundred years. O best of the humans, the length of Kali age is a thousand years, while the length of its Sandhya and Sandhyamsha is two hundred years.

## \|\| 1.2.97-99 \|\|

*eṣā caturyugasyāpi saṃkhyā proktā nṛpottama \|*  
*yadetatparisaṃkhyā tamādāveva caturyugam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*etaddvādaśasāhasraṃ devānāṃ yugamucyate \|*  
*daivikānāṃ yugānāṃ tu sahasraparisaṃkhyayā \|\| 98 \|\|*

*brāhmamekamaharjñeyaṃ tāvatī rātrirucyate \|*  
*etadyugasahasrāntaṃ brāhmaṃ puṇyamaharviduḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

97-99. O best of the humans, the number of all the four yugas (eons) has been described above. The length of four yugas which I have just told you, the same is said to be the yuga of the gods which comprises of twelve thousand years. A thousand yugas of the gods form a day of Brahma and his night is of the same length. Thus, the learned people say that at the end of a thousand yugas of the gods, an auspicious day of Brahma lapses.

## \|\| 1.2.100 \|\|

*rātriṃ ca tāvatīmeva te'horātravido janāḥ \|*  
*tato'sau yugaparyante prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The night of Brahma is said to be of the same length. On the expiry of this night, thousand yugas of the gods are spent. The lord getting free of his sleep, wakes up.

## \|\| 1.2.101 \|\|

*pratibuddhastu sṛjati manaḥ sadasadātmakam \|*  
*manaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute codyamānaṃ 1 sisṛkṣayā \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Then with a firm mind, he creates his Sat and Asat worlds. Influence with the desire to expand the creation, he resorts to the mental creation.

## \|\| 1.2.102-104 \|\|

*vipulaṃ jāyate tasmāttasya śabdaṃ guṇaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*vipulāttu vikurvāṇātsarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*balavāñjāyate vāyuḥ sa vai sparśaguṇo mataḥ \|*  
*vāyorapi vikurvāṇādvirociṣṇu tamonudam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*utpadyate vicitrāṃśustasya rūpaṃ guṇaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*tasmādapi vikurvāṇādāpo jātāḥ smṛtā budhaiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-104. The vast sky is created out of him. The qualities of the sky are ‘being stated, with the perversion of the sky the wind is formed. Thereafter with the perverted wind, the fragrant air, which carries the fragrance being powerful, auspicious and various in touch, is formed, which remains the darkness. Its qualities are being described. With the same wind getting disturbed again, the water is created. This is what the learned people believe.

## \|\| 1.2.105 \|\|

*adbhyo gandhaguṇā bhūmirityeṣā sṛṣṭirāditaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Essence is the quality of the water, which bestows life in all the creatures of the world. The earth came into existence out of the water, with fragrance as its special quality. This is the eternal sequence of the creation.

## \|\| 1.2.106 \|\|

*yatprāgdvādaśasāhasramuktaṃ saumanasaṃ yugam \|*  
*tadekasaptatiguṇaṃ manvantaramihocyate \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. A Manvantara comprises of seventy one times of a yuga which comprises of twelve thousands of the gods.

## \|\| 1.2.107 \|\|

*manvantarāṇyasaṃkhyāni sargaḥ saṃhāra eva ca \|*  
*tathāpyahe sadā brāhme manavastu caturdaśa \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Though the number of such Manvantaras cannot be ascertained and there are no limits prescribed for dissolution as well, it is said that still the working period of fourteen Manus expires in a single day of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.2.108-110 \|\|

*kathyante kuruśārdūla 3 saṃkhyayā paṇḍitaiḥ sadā \|*  
*manoḥ svāyambhuvasyeha ṣaḍvaṃśyā 4 manavo'pare \|\| 108 \|\|*

*sṛṣṭavantaḥ prajāḥ svāḥsvāḥ mahātmāno mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*sāvarṇeyastathā pañcabhautyo raucyastathāparaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*ete bhaviṣyā manavaḥ sapta proktā nṛpottama \|*  
*svasve'ntare sarvamidaṃ pālayanti carācaram \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. O lion of the race of Kuru, the learned people take a decision always on the basis of the numbers. In the dynasty of the Svayambhuva Manu, six other Manus are said to have been born, who possessed enormous fortunes, besides being immensely illustrious. They created their own subjects in the ancient times. O best of humans, Savarneya, Panchabhautya and upto Rauchya, seven Manus shall be born in future. All of them shall create their respective subjects during their respective times and maintain their mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 1.2.111 \|\|

*evaṃvidhaṃ dinaṃ tasya viriñcestu mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tasyānte kurute sargaṃ yathedaṃ kathitaṃ tava \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. A day of Brahma — the great soul, has been defined like this. During the conclusion of his time, he completes the business of the creation accordingly, as has been described by me recently.

## \|\| 1.2.112 \|\|

*krīḍannivaitatkurute parameṣṭhī narādhipa \|*  
*catuṣpātsakalo dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiva kṛte yuge \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. O lord of the humans, the Parameshthi creates the entire mobile and immobile beings quite playfully as has been just described by me. During Satyayuga, all the dharmas stand on their four legs.

## \|\| 1.2.113-115 \|\|

*nādharmeṇāgamaḥ kaścinmanuṣyāṇāṃ pravartate \|*  
*itareṣvāgamāstāta dharmaśca kurunandana \|\| 113 \|\|*

*cauryāccāpyanṛtādrājanmāyābhiramitadyute \|\| 114 \|\|*

*pādena hīyate dharmastretādiṣu yugeṣu vai \|*  
*arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāścaturvarṣaśatāyuṣaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

113-115. The nature of the people of that period has no leanings towards the sinful ways. O son of Kuru’s race, during the other yugas, the ways in which the nature and dharma of the people decline, have been described by Manu thus described. O Monarch, by indulging in theft and resorting to falsehood and by creating of confusion and resorting to other sins by the humans, the dharma stands just on three legs. During the Satyayuga, the people are free from ailments and have their desires fulfilled, getting all the Siddhis. All the people have the age of four hundred years and they live comfortably.

## \|\| 1.2.116-117 \|\|

*kṛtatretādiṣu tveṣāṃ vayo hrasati pādaśaḥ \|*  
*vedoktamāyurāśīśca martyānāṃ kurunandana \|\| 116 \|\|*

*karmaṇāṃ tu phalaṃ tāta phalatyanuyugaṃ sadā \|*  
*prabhāvaśca tathā loke phalatyeva śarīriṇām \|\| 117 \|\|*

116-117. During Treta and other yugas, the dharma goes on decline by one leg in each one of the yugas. The people enjoy life, welfare speeches and good and evil results of one’s deeds are achieved by them according to the provision of the Vedas. The influence of the human beings is also exercised or rewarded according to the yugas.

## \|\| 1.2.118 \|\|

*anye kṛtayuge dharmāstretāyāṃ dvāpare pare \|*  
*anye kaliyuge nṛṇāṃ yugadharmānurūpataḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Dharma had a different form during Satyayuga, another in Dvapara, and entirely different in the age of Kali. In other words, the dharmas of the human beings undergo a change in each one of the yugas.

## \|\| 1.2.119 \|\|

*tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānamucyate \|*  
*dvāpare yajñamityāhurdānamekaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The performing of tapas is the supreme dharma of Satyayuga. During the Tretayuga, the achieving of knowledge is the highest dharma. During the age of Dvapara, the performing of the yajnas comes into prominence. In the age of Kali, the giving of charities predominate, which constitute the best of dharma.

## \|\| 1.2.120 \|\|

*sarvasya rājansargasya guptyarthaṃ ca mahādyute \|*  
*mukhabāhūrupādānāṃ pṛthakkarmāṇyakalpayat \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. O extremely illustrious king, the lord has distributed the duties to all those who emerged out of his face, arms, legs and the feet.

## \|\| 1.2.121 \|\|

*adhyāpanamadhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tathā \|*  
*dānaṃ pratigrahaṃ caiva brāhmaṇānāmakalpayat \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. The teaching, studies, gratification and performance of yajnas, giving and taking of charities are the activities which are supposed to be carried out by the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.2.122 \|\|

*prajānāṃ pālanaṃ rājandānamadhyayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*viṣayeṣu prasaktiṃ ca tathejyāṃ kṣatriyasya tu \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Similarly, the duties of maintenance and upkeep of the populace, charities, studies or gaining of knowledge, enjoyment of the worldly pleasures besides the performing of the yajnas are supposed to be carried out by the Kshatriyas.

## \|\| 1.2.123 \|\|

*paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānamijyādhyayanameva ca \|*  
*vaṇikpathaṃ 1 kusīdaṃ ca vaiśyasya kṛṣireva ca \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. The duties of the Vaishyas comprise of protecting the cattle, giving of charities, performing of yajnas, studies, trade and commerce, money lending on interest, and irrigation are all assigned to the Vaishyas.

## \|\| 1.2.124 \|\|

*ekameva tu śūdrasya karma loke prakīrtitam \|*  
*eteṣāmeva varṇānāṃ śuśrūṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. The Shudras in the world have only one duty to perform, which is to serve all the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas respectively.

## \|\| 1.2.125-126 \|\|

*puruṣasya sadā śreṣṭhaṃ nābherūrdhvaṃ nṛpottama \|*  
*tasmādapi śucitaraṃ mukhaṃ tāta svayambhuvaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

*tasmānmukhāddvijo jāta itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|*  
*sarvasyaivāsya dharmasya dharmato brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

125-126. O best of humans, in the human body, that part of the body which abodes above the navel, is considered to be the best always and therefore, the face is considered to be the auspicious one. Out of the auspicious face of lord Manu, there emerged the Brahmanas. This is also the voice of the Vedas, The Brahmanas, because of their dharma, are required to preside in all the religious functions.

## \|\| 1.2.127 \|\|

*sa sṛṣṭo brahmaṇā pūrvaṃ tapastaptvā kurūdvaha \|*  
*havyānāmiva kavyānāṃ sarvasyāpi ca guptaye \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. O best of the race of Kuru! Brahma, after performing severe tapas, had produced the Brahmanas for the protection of all like havya and kavya. The gods consume the havya and havya through mouths of the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.2.128 \|\|

*aśnanti ca mukhenāsya havyāni tridivaukasaḥ \|*  
*kavyāni caiva pitaraḥ kimbhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. The gods also consume havya through the mouths of the Brahmanas. Besides the pitris or the manes also consume havya through the mouths of the Brahmanas. What else could be beyond that?

## \|\| 1.2.129 \|\|

*bhūtānāṃ prāṇinaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prāṇināṃ buddhijīvinaḥ \|*  
*buddhimatsu narāḥ śreṣṭhā nareṣu brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Of all the bhutas, those having life are considered to be the best. They happen to be the best of all the living beings. The one among the living beings is the best who possesses intelligence. Out of those possessing intelligence, the humans are the best. Out of the humans, the Brahmanas are the best.

## \|\| 1.2.130 \|\|

*brāhmaṇeṣu ca vidvāṃso vidvatsu kṛtabuddhayaḥ \|*  
*kṛtabuddhiṣu kartāraḥ kartṛṣu brahmavedinaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Out of the Brahmanas, the learned Brahmana is the best. Out of the intelligent Brahmanas, the one having the firm intelligence is the best. Among them, that one is the best who performs excellently. But out of these who perform excellently, a person is the best who is aware of the Brahman.

## \|\| 1.2.131 \|\|

*janma viprasya rājendra dhamārthamiha kathyate \|*  
*utpannaḥ sarvasiddhayarthaṃ4 yāti brahmasado nṛpa \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. O king, the Brahmanas were born for the performing of dharma. It is believed that he has been born on earth for achieving of all the siddhis. He shall achieve Brahmaloka ultimately.

## \|\| 1.2.132 \|\|

*sa cāpi jāyamānastu pṛthivyāmiha jāyate \|*  
*bhūtānāṃ prabhavāyaiva dharmakośasya guptaye \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. After having been born on earth, he is required to exercise the spiritual control over the people and for the protection of the dharma.

## \|\| 1.2.133 \|\|

*sarvaṃ hi brāhmaṇasyedaṃ yatkiñcitpṛthivīgatam \|*  
*janmanā cottamenedaṃ sarvaṃ vai brāhmaṇo'rhati \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Everything on earth belongs to the Brahmanas. Because of his excellent birth, he has to receive everything.

## \|\| 1.2.134 \|\|

*svakīyaṃ brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte vidadhāti ca suvrata \|*  
*karuṇāṃ kurvatastasya bhuñjantī hetare janāḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. O Suvrata, a Brahmana takes his own food and still makes all the efforts for the welfare of the world, the benefit of which are enjoyed by the people.

## \|\| 1.2.135 \|\|

*trayāṇāmiha varṇānāṃ bhāvābhāvāya vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*bhavedrājanna sandehastuṣṭo bhāvāya vai dvijaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. O king, a Brahmana is competent enough to bestow welfare or otherwise of the three varnas of the world. There is no doubt in the fact, that a Brahmana bestows welfare on others, only after getting pleased.

## \|\| 1.2.136 \|\|

*abhāvāya bhavetkruddhastasmātpūjyatamo hi saḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇe sati nānyasya prabhutvaṃ vidyate nṛpa \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. After getting enraged, he resorts of having as well, therefore, he is adorable by all. O king, when a Brahmana is present, people of other varnas have no importance.

## \|\| 1.2.137 \|\|

*kāmātkarotyasau karma kāmagaśca nṛpottama \|*  
*tasmādvṛndārakapurī tasmādapi mahaḥ punaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. O best of the rulers, a Brahmana performs according to his own will. He achieves Devaloka from this Loka, and there also enjoys stays in the palaces.

## \|\| 1.2.138 \|\|

*maharlokājjanolokaṃ brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*brahmatvaṃ ca mahābāho yāti vipro na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. From Maharloka he proceeds to Janaloka and from there, he goes on to Brahmaloka. O long armed one, there is no doubt in the statement that a Brahmana achieves Brahmaloka ultimately.

## \|\| 1.2.139 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*brahmatvaṃ nāma duṣprāpaṃ brahmalokeṣu suvrata \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Shatanika said — O Suvrata, it is quite difficult to achieve Brahmatva or the true knowledge of the supreme self.

## \|\| 1.2.140 \|\|

*brahmatvaṃ kīdṛśaṃ vipro brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*nāmamātro'tha kiṃ vipro brahmatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sadā \|*  
*yāti brahmanguṇāḥ ke syurbrahmaprāptau mamocyatām \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. How does a Brahmana achieves the Brahmatva and Brahmaloka? Does a Brahmana achieves Brahmapada for the name sake only? O Brahmana, what are the qualities of a Brahmana to achieve the position of the Brahman? O Brahmana, what are the means to achieve the position of Brahmapada? You kindly enlighten me on this.

## \|\| 1.2.141 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. Sumantu said — O long armed one, you are extremely praiseworthy. Listen to my excellent words.

## \|\| 1.2.142-143 \|\|

*ye proktā vedaśāstreṣu saṃskārā brāhmaṇasya tu \|*  
*garbhādhānādayo ye ca 1 saṃskārā yasya pārthiva \|\| 142 \|\|*

*saṃskārāḥ sarvathā heturbrahmatve nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. These are two religious rites, prescribed for a Brahmana in his life. O Parthiva, the conception and other forty-eight rites are ordained in the religious scriptures. If all these rites are properly performed for a Brahmana in accordance with the scriptures, he achieves the position of Brahmanhood. These rites are instrumental in the achieving of the Brahmanhood by a Brahmana. Only these rites are instrumental in the achieving of Brahmanhood by a Brahmana, there is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.2.144 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*saṃskārāḥ ke matā brahmanbrahmatve brāhmaṇasya tu \|*  
*śaṃsa me dvijaśārdūlaṃ kautukaṃ hi mahanmama \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Shatanika said — O lion among the Brahmanas, which one of the religious rites are instrumental in achieving of Brahmanhood by a Brahmana? I am quite anxious to know about them. You kindly speak out the same to me.

## \|\| 1.2.145 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*ye proktā vedaśāstreṣu saṃskārā brāhmaṇasya tu \|*  
*manīṣibhirmahābāho śṛṇu sarvānaśeṣataḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Sumantu said — O valorous one, you are really praiseworthy. You listen to my excellent words. The religious rites which have been prescribed in the religious scriptures besides the Vedas and the Shastras are being related by me.

## \|\| 1.2.146-147 \|\|

*garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*jātakarmānnāśanaṃ ca cūḍopanayanaṃ 2 nṛpa \|\| 146 \|\|*

*brahmavratāni catvāri snānaṃ ca tadanantaram \|*  
*sadharmacāriṇīyogo yajñānāṃ 3 karma mānada \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. O king, the first one is the rite of conception, ceremony on the birth of the child, tasting of food, tonsure ceremony, thread ceremony, vratas of four types of Brahmacharya and baths, the marriage and the performing of beneficial yajnas. These ceremonies are considered extremely beneficial for the welfare of the self.

## \|\| 1.2.148-153 \|\|

*pañcānāṃ kāryamityāhurātmanaḥ śreyase nṛpa \|*  
*devapitṛmanuṣyāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ brāhmaṇastathā \|\| 148 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ cāṣṭakākarma pārvaṇaśrāddhameva hi \|*  
*śrāvaṇī cāgrahāyaṇī caitrī cāśvayujī tathā \|\| 149 \|\|*

*pākayajñāstathā sapta agnyādhānaṃ ca satkriyā \|*  
*agnihotraṃ tathā rājandarśaṃ ca vidhusañkṣaye \|\| 150 \|\|*

*paurṇamāsaṃ ca rājendra cāturmāsyāni cāpi hi \|*  
*nirūpaṇaṃ 5 paśuvadhaṃ tathā sautrāmaṇīti ca \|\| 151 \|\|*

*haviryajñāstathā sapta teṣāṃ cāpi hi satkriyā \|*  
*agniṣṭomo'tyagniṣṭomastathokthyaḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ viduḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*saṃskāreṣu sthitāḥ sapta somāḥ kurukulodvaha \|\| 153 \|\|*

148-153. The performance of religious ceremonies on the eighth day of the moon in order to please the gods, the manes, the humans, bhutas and Brahman are known as the Ashtakarma.
