These ceremonies are performed on full moon days in the months Shravana, Margashirsha, Chaitra on the full moon days, besides the seven Paka-yajnas, consecration of fire, Satkriya, Homa, Darsha Shraddha on Amavasya or the moonless night, festivities of four months, killing of animals, Sautramani-yajna, Havir-yajna of seven types known as Satkriya, Agnistoma, Ukthya, Shodashi, Vajapeya, Atira and Aptoryama, are all known as the holy rites. O best of the Kurus, the seven Somayajnas are also included in the holy rites.

## \|\| 1.2.154 \|\|

*ityete dvijasaṃskārāścatvāriṃśannṛpottama \|*  
*aṣṭau cātmaguṇāstāta śṛṇu tānapi bhārata \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. O best of the humans, these forty rites are known as the rites for the Brahmanas. O Bharata, they have eight natural qualities, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.2.155-156 \|\|

*anasūyā dayā kṣāntiranāyāsaṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*akārpaṇyaṃ tathā śaucamaspṛhā ca kurūdvaha \|\| 155 \|\|*

*ya ete'ṣṭaguṇāstāta kīrtyante vai manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vīra śṛṇu sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

155-156. Non-jealousy, compassion, forgiveness, without difficulty, welfare, lack of miserliness, purity and lack of desire are the eight natural qualities of the Brahmanas which have been prescribed by the learned people. O valorous one, I shall now speak out the natural symptoms of these natural qualities, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.2.157 \|\|

*na guṇānguṇino hanti na stautyātmaguṇānapi \|*  
*prahaṣyante nānyadoṣairanasūyā prakīrtitā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. A person who does not mitigate the virtues of others and does not highlight his own virtues, besides does not highlight the shortcomings of others, he is known as Anasuya or a person devoid of jealousy.

## \|\| 1.2.158 \|\|

*apare bandhuvarge vā mitre dveṣṭari vā sadā \|*  
*ātmavadvartanaṃ yatsyātsā dayā parikīrtitā \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. A person who treats the friends and the foes equally is known as the compassionate one.

## \|\| 1.2.159 \|\|

*vācā manasi kāye ca duḥkhenotpāditena ca \|*  
*na kupyati na cāprītiḥ sā kṣamā parikīrtitā \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. A person who does not utter harsh words which cause pain to the body or the mind, is known as the one who excels in forgiveness.

## \|\| 1.2.160 \|\|

*abhakṣyaparihāraśca saṃsargaścāpyaninditaiḥ \|*  
*ācāre ca vyavasthānaṃ śaucametatprakīrtitam \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Those who discard the food unfit for eating, developing contact with the praiseworthy people, and those who lead the life of purity and good conduct are known as having been purified.

## \|\| 1.2.161 \|\|

*śarīraṃ pīḍyate yena śubhenāpi ca karmaṇā \|*  
*atyantaṃ tanna kurvīta anāyāsaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. A noble cause which extends torture to the body, such a practice should be totally discarded. The discarding of such a type is known as automatic.

## \|\| 1.2.162 \|\|

*praśastācaraṇaṃ nityamapraśastavivarjanam \|*  
*etaddhi maṅgalaṃ proktaṃ munibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. By performing of the noble deeds and discarding the evil path, is known as welfare for the Brahmavadin sages.

## \|\| 1.2.163 \|\|

*stokādapi pradātavyamadīnenāntarātmanā \|*  
*ahanyahani yatkiṃcidakārpaṇyaṃ taducyate \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. A person who with a delightful mind gives charity even of small quantity, it is known as the lack of miserliness.

## \|\| 1.2.164 \|\|

*yathotpannena santuṣṭaḥ svalpenāpyatha vastunā \|*  
*ahiṃsayā parasveṣu 3 sā'spṛhā parikīrtitā \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. A person who feels contented even after receiving a small quantity of something and feeling a sense of non-violence for the riches of others, it is called as lack of jealousy.

## \|\| 1.2.165 \|\|

*vapuryasya tu ityetaiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*brahmatvamiha samprāpya brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. O Brahmana, a person who owns these qualities, achieves the form of Brahman in this world, and he finally achieves Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.2.166 \|\|

*vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyairniṣekādyairdvijanmanām \|*  
*kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. In order to make this as well as the future world a success, all the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas should purify their bodies by following the dharma and performing the prescribed Vedic deeds. The body having been thus civilized, should be purified.

## \|\| 1.2.167 \|\|

*garbhaśuddhiṃ tataḥ prāpya dharmaṃ cāśramalakṣaṇam \|*  
*yāti muktiṃ na sandehaḥ purāṇe'sminnṛpottama \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. When the body is thus purified, the conception is also purified and a person following the dharma of his respective ashrama, achieves salvation or beatitude as prescribed in the Puranas. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.2.168 \|\|

*uśanti kuruśārdūla brāhmaṇā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*1 āśritānāṃ viśeṣeṇa ye nityaṃ svastivādinaḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. O best monarch of the Kuru race, a Brahmana who performs welfare mantras for the people dependent on him, always remains delightful. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.2.169-170 \|\|

*nikaṭasthāndvijānhitvā yo'nyānpūjayati dvijān \|*  
*siddhaṃ pāpaṃ tadapamānāttadvaktuṃ naiva śakyate \|\| 169 \|\|*

*tasmātsadā samīpasthaḥ sampūjyo vidhivannṛpa \|*  
*pūjayedatithīṃstadvadannapānādidānataḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

169-170. Neglecting the Brahmanas who are found nearby and adores other Brahmanas, he surely earns sin by humiliating the Brahmana in the vicinity. The extent of the relative sin is beyond measure. Therefore, a Brahmana in the vicinity should always be adored.

## \|\| 1.2.171-173 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhastathottamaḥ \|*  
*evamasminpurāṇe tu saṃskārānbrāhmaṇasya tu \|\| 171 \|\|*

*śṛṇoti yaśca jānāti yaścāpi paṭhate sadā \|*  
*ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā kīrtiṃ prāpyeha śriyamuttamām \|\| 172 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ yaśaścāpi putrānbandhūnsurūpatām \|*  
*sāvitraṃ lokamāsādya brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 173 \|\|*

171-173. A Brahmana is senior, the best and excellent of all the varnas. Thus, the rites of the Brahmanas as prescribed in the Purana when listened and followed by a person, he surely achieves all the Riddhis (prosperity), Vriddha (development), Kirti (glory), the best of fortunes, wealth, cereals, grace, sons, relatives and the health with beauty, and thus proceeds to the region of the sun and from these, he achieves Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 3. Brief description of the rites starting from conception etc.

## \|\| 1.3.1 \|\|

*jānvantare mahābāho brahmasūtrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O best of the Brahmanas, you kindly speak out the ceremonies relating to the birth of a child and thereafter in all the ashramas (including Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa etc.) in a chronological order.

## \|\| 1.3.2-4 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*jātakarmānnaprāśaśca cūḍāmauñjīnibandhanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*baijikaṃ gārbhikaṃ caino dvijānāmapamṛjyate \|*  
*svādhyāyena vratairhomaistraividyenejyayā śrutaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mahāyajñaiśca brāhmīyaṃ yajñaiśca kriyate tanuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājanyathā sā kriyate tanuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Sumantu said — O king, the conception, ceremony of the third month of conception, ceremony performed during the birth or eighth month of the pregnant, ceremony of the tasting of food by the infant, tonsure ceremony and thread ceremony of the Dvijas, by performing these ceremonies all the defects of the birth as well as the seed are removed. The body is infused by divine glory with the study of the Vedas, performing of vratas, study of the three Vedas, besides the performing of the small or the great yajnas. O king, listen to me with a concentrated mind, as to how a body is infused with the divine glory.

## \|\| 1.3.5 \|\|

*prāṅnābhikartanātpuṃso jātakarma vidhīyate \|*  
*mantravatprāśanaṃ cāsya hiraṇyamadhusarpiṣām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Before the cutting of the cord of the child at the birth, the birth ceremony is performed. Then reciting the Vedic hymns, the infant is made to lick the gold, honey and ghi (clarified butter).

## \|\| 1.3.6 \|\|

*apūjitaṃ tu tadbhuktamubhayaṃ nāśayedidam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Parthiva, O monarch, some of the Acharyas perform the name giving ceremony on the tenth day after the birth of the infant. Some people do it on the twelfth day, while others do so on the completion of a month of the birth of the child.

## \|\| 1.3.7-8 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśe'hani tathā'nye vadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*puṇye tithau muhūrte ca nakṣatre ca guṇānvite \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maṅgalyaṃ tāta viprasya śivaśarmeti pārthiva \|*  
*rājanyasya viśiṣṭaṃ 1 tu induvarmeti kathyate 2 \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Some of the learned Brahmanas perform this ceremony on the eighteenth day after the birth. On an auspicious tithi (day), auspicious constellation, auspicious muhurta and when all the gunas are favourable, the name like Shiva Sharma should be given to the Brahmana boy with grace. The Kshatriyas should be called by the name like Indra Varma. Such types of special names should be given to the child.

## \|\| 1.3.9 \|\|

*vaiśyasya dhanasaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya ca jugupsitam \|*  
*dhanavardhaneti vaiśyasya sarvadāseti hīnaje \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A Vaishya child should be given a name with combination of riches. A Shudra should have a reproached name. As for example, a Vaishya child should have a name like Dhanavaradhana, while a Shudra child should have the name like Sarvadasha.

## \|\| 1.3.10-12 \|\|

*manunā ca tathā proktaṃ nāmno lakṣaṇamuttamam \|*  
*śarmavadbrāhmaṇasya syādrājño rakṣāsamanvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vaiśyasya puṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya preṣyasaṃyutam \|*  
*strīṇāṃ sukhodyamakrūraṃ vispaṣṭārthamanoramam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*maṅgalyaṃ dīrghavarṇāntamāśīrvādābhidhānavat \|*  
*dvādaśe'hani rājendra śiśorniṣkamaṇaṃ gṛhāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Manu has prescribed these excellent symbols of the giving of names. The title of Sharma should be added to the name of a Brahmana, Varma should be added to the name of a Kshatriya. A supportive title should be added to the name of a Vaishya and the name of a Shudra should project a spirit of service. The name of the ladies should be soft, comfortable, simple, clear, pleasant and sound the well-being, with a dirgha-varna at the end, displaying blessings. O Rajendra, on the twelfth day, the child can be taken out of the house. In case, the ceremony for the tasting of food for an infant is performed in the sixth month of the birth, then the family meets with welfare.

## \|\| 1.3.13 \|\|

*caturthe māsi karttavyaṃ tathānyeṣāṃ mataṃ vibho \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhe'nnaprāśanaṃ māsi yatheṣṭaṃ maṅgalaṃ kule \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O magnanimous one, some other Acharyas hold the view that the infant should be taken out in the fourth month out of the house.

## \|\| 1.3.14 \|\|

*cūḍākarma dvijātīnāṃ sarveṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*prathame'bde tṛtīye vā kartavyaṃ kurunandana \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O son of Kuru race, the tonsure ceremony of all the children of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas should be performed during the first or the third year of his birth.

## \|\| 1.3.15 \|\|

*garbhāṣṭame'bde kurvīta brāhmaṇasyopanāyanam \|*  
*garbhādekādaśe rājankṣatriyasya vinirdiśet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The thread ceremony of a Brahmana boy should be performed in the eighth year of his birth. The thread ceremony of a Kshatriya should be done before the eleventh year of the birth.

## \|\| 1.3.16 \|\|

*dvādaśe'bde'pi garbhāttu vaiśyasya vratamādiśet \|*  
*brahmavarcasakāmena kāryaṃ viprasya pañcame \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This vrata for the Vaishyas has been prescribed in the twelfth year. But in case excessive glory of Brahman is desired, then the thread ceremony of a Brahmana boy should be performed in the fifth year itself.

## \|\| 1.3.17 \|\|

*balārthinā tathā rājñaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'bde kāryameva hi \|*  
*arthakāmena vaiśyasya aṣṭame kurunandana \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The thread ceremony of the princes of the kings should be performed during the sixth year of their birth. Similarly, the thread ceremony of a Vaishya boy should be performed during the eighth year, because he has to be engaged in the earning of the wealth.

## \|\| 1.3.18 \|\|

*āṣoḍaśādbrāhmaṇasya sāvitrī nātivartate \|*  
*dvāviṃśateḥ kṣatrabandhorācaturviṃśaterviśaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The thread ceremony of the Brahmana boys can be performed upto the age of sixteen years after birth. Similarly, the thread ceremony of the Kshatriyas can be performed before the age of twenty two years and those of the Vaishyas upto twenty four years.

## \|\| 1.3.19 \|\|

*ata ūrdhvaṃ tu ye rājanyathākālamasaṃskṛtāḥ \|*  
*sāvitrīpatitā vrātyā vrātyastomādṛte 3 kratoḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In case the thread ceremony of the boys is not performed according to the above time schedule, he remains uncivilized. With the fall of Savitri, they become vratyas or outcasts and nothing can be done in a yajna by outcasts.

## \|\| 1.3.20 \|\|

*na cāpyebhirapūtaistu āpadyapi hi karhicit \|*  
*brāhmaṃ yaunaṃ ca sambandhamācaredbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With such an inauspicious person, there should be no contact even in emergency, including studies, teaching or sexual relations, by a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.3.21 \|\|

*bhavanti rājaṃścarmāṇi vratināṃ trividhāni ca \|*  
*kārṣṇarauravavāstāni brahmakṣatraviśāṃ nṛpa \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O king, for those who perform the vrata of the thread ceremony, three types of hide is to be used by them. For the Brahmanas, the hide of black buck is required, for a Kshatriya it should be of a musk deer, while for the Vaishyas the skin of a goat is required.

## \|\| 1.3.22 \|\|

*vaśīraṃścānupūrvyeṇa vastrāṇi vividhāni tu \|*  
*brahmakṣatraviśo rājañchāṇakṣaumādikāni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O king, similarly, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas can make use of the silken garments of different types.

## \|\| 1.3.23 \|\|

*mauñjī trivṛtsamā ślakṣṇā kāryā viprasya mekhalā \|*  
*kṣatriyasya ca maurvījyā vaiśyasya śaṇatāntavī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. During the performing of the thread ceremony, the girdle of a Brahmana is required to be made of munja grass, with three strings and should not be quite slippery. The girdle of a Kshatriya should be of a medicinal plant and for the use of a Vaishya, it should be made of jute.

## \|\| 1.3.24 \|\|

*muñjālābhe tu kartavyā kuśāśmantakabalvajaiḥ \|*  
*trivṛttā granthinaikena tribhiḥ pañcabhireva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In case the munja is not available, then in that case the kusha grass can be used by the Brahmanas or alternatively, the Ashmantaka grass or Balvaja plant could be used for the purpose. It should be tied in a knot with three strings or alternatively three, five or eight knots should be bound in the same.

## \|\| 1.3.25 \|\|

*kārpāsamupavītaṃ syādviprasyordhvavṛtaṃ trivṛt \|*  
*śaṇasūtramayaṃ rājño vaiśyasyāvikasautrikam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The upavita of the Brahmana should be made of cotton, having three threads. The upavita of the kings or the Kshatriyas should be made of jute fibres, while the one of Vaishyas should be made of the sheep’s wool.

## \|\| 1.3.26 \|\|

*puṣkarāṇi tathā caiṣāṃ bhavanti trividhāni tu \|*  
*brahmaṇo bailvapālāśau tṛtīyaṃ plakṣajaṃ nṛpa \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Among all the three varnas, the dandas of the Brahmacharis should also be of three types. O king, the Brahmana should had a danda of wood apple tree, palasha tree or of plaksha tree.

## \|\| 1.3.27 \|\|

*vāṭakhādirau kṣatriyastu tathānyaṃ vetasodbhavam \|*  
*pailavodumbarau vaiśyastathāśvatthajameva hi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A Kshatriya’s danda should be of a banyan tree, khadira tree or of the cane. The Vaishya should have the danda of paila — an autumn tree, wild fig tree, or of a pippala tree.

## \|\| 1.3.28 \|\|

*daṇḍānetānmahābāho dharmato'rhanti dhāritum \|*  
*keśāntiko brāhmaṇasya daṇḍaḥ kāryaḥ pramāṇataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O valorous one, the danda should be held during the thread ceremony religiously. The length of the danda should be upto the length of his hair.

## \|\| 1.3.29-33 \|\|

*lalāṭasammito rājñaḥ syāttu nāsāntiko viśaḥ \|*  
*ṛjavaste tū sarve syurbrāhmaṇāḥ saumyadarśanāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*anudvegakarā nṝṇāṃ satvaco nāgnidūṣitāḥ \|*  
*pragṛhya cepsitaṃ daṇḍamupasthāya ca bhāskaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*samyagguruṃ tathā pūjya caredbhaikṣyaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*bhavatpūrvaṃ caredbhaikṣyamupanīto dvijottamaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhavanmadhyaṃ tu rājanyo vaiśyasya bhavaduttaram \|*  
*mātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vā māturvā bhaginīṃ nijām \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bhikṣeta bhaikṣyaṃ prathamaṃ yā cainaṃ nāvamānayet \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ cānnaṃ sā pātre'sya vinirdiśet \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. The danda of the rulers should have the length upto their head, and the danda of Vaishya should reach upto the nose. These dandas should be beautiful and straight and should not create disturbance in the minds of the people who look at them. They should be covered by the beautiful bark and should have no sign of having been burnt by the fire. Thus holding the danda as per one’s desire, the sun should be worshipped. Thereafter, the preceptor should be appropriately adored and then Brahmachari should resort to go for begging. A Kshatriya should use the word Bhavat in his utterances, while Vaishya should use the same word at the end of the sentence. One should beg from the mother, sister, or mother’s sister, in the first instance, who should not disappoint the Brahmachari. The giver should place the food in the plate of gold or silver, and should be given to Brahmachari. This has been ordained in the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.3.34 \|\|

*samāhṛtya tato bhaikṣyaṃ yāvadarthamamāyayā \|*  
*nivedya gurave'śnīyādācamya prāṅmukhaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus after begging in this way, the Brahmachari, after getting relieved of the confusion, should offer the earnings by begging to the preceptor with dedication. Then sipping the water with pure mind, he should take his food sitting facing east.

## \|\| 1.3.35 \|\|

*āyuṣyaṃ prāṅmukho bhuṅkte yaśasyaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ \|*  
*śriyaṃ pratyaṅmukho bhuṅkte ṛtaṃ 1 bhuṅkte udaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By taking food facing east, one earns long life. Taking food facing south, one achieves glory. By taking food facing west, one achieves riches and while facing north while eating, one achieves Brahman.

## \|\| 1.3.36 \|\|

*upaspṛśya dvijo rājannannamadyātsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā copaspṛśetsamyagadbhiḥ khāni ca saṃspṛśet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O king, the Brahmana while concentrating his mind, should rinse his mouth appropriately and then take the food. After finishing the food, one should again rinse his mouth appropriately. Then he should touch all his sense organs.

## \|\| 1.3.37 \|\|

*tathānnaṃ pūjayennityamadyāccaitadakutsayan \|*  
*darśanāttasya haṣyedvai prasīdeccāpi bhārata \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The food should always be adored and while looking at the food, one should praise it and then consume it. This has been ordained by Manu that one should discard the evil thoughts, and then the food should be taken. He should feel happy by looking at the food.

## \|\| 1.3.38 \|\|

*abhinandya tato'śnīyādityevaṃ manurabravīt \|*  
*pūjitaṃ tvaśanaṃ nityaṃ balamojaśca yacchati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Alternately, at the end, food should be taken after praising it. The food which is taken after its adoration, always increases strength.

## \|\| 1.3.39 \|\|

*nocchiṣṭaṃ kasyaciddadyānnādyāccaitattathāntarā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In case the unadored food is taken, it becomes cause of destruction both for the one who serves and the other who eats. One’s own left over should not be given to anyone, nor should the leftover of others be taken by anyone.

## \|\| 1.3.40 \|\|

*yastvannamantarā kṛtvā lobhādatti nṛpottama \|*  
*vināśaṃ yāti sa nara iha loke paratra ca \|*  
*yathābhavatpurā vaiśyo dhanavarddhanasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Similarly, one should not consume his own left over again. O king, out of greed, in case a person consumes his own left over a second time, he faces destruction in both the worlds as the rich Vaishya was destroyed in earlier times.

## \|\| 1.3.41 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*sa kathamantaraṃ pūrvamannasya dvijasattama \|*  
*kimantaraṃ tathānnasya kathaṃ vā tatkṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Shatanika said — O excellent Brahmana, how was he before taking food and what happened to him after taking it?

## \|\| 1.3.42 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*purā kṛtayuge rājanvaiśyo vasati puṣkare \|*  
*dhanavardhananāmā vai samṛddhau dhanadhānyataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Sumantu said — O king, long time ago, during the Satyayuga, in the city of Pushkara, there lived a Vaishya known by the name of Dhanavaradhana. He had enough of riches and food grains.

## \|\| 1.3.43-44 \|\|

*nidāghakāle rājendra sa kṛtvā vaiśvadevikam \|*  
*saputrabhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ tathā vai mitrabandhubhiḥ \|*  
*āhāraṃ kurute rājanbhakṣyabhojyasamanvitam 1 \|\| 43 \|\|*

*atha tadbhuñjatastasya 2 annaṃ śabdo mahānabhūt \|*  
*karuṇaḥ kuruśārdūla atha taṃ sa pradhāvitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. O Rajendra, once during the summer season, he together with his relatives and friends performed the festivities of Vaishvadeva, after which he was consuming the food appropriately. In the meantime, he heard the word of food and at once, he rushed towards that direction.

## \|\| 1.3.45 \|\|

*tyaktvā sa bhojanaṃ yāvanniṣkrānto gṛhabāhyataḥ \|*  
*atha śabdastirobhūtaḥ sa bhūyo gṛhamāgataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By the time leaving his food he rushed outside, that the word that had been heard by him disappeared. Thereafter, he returned to his home.

## \|\| 1.3.46 \|\|

*tameva bhājanaṃ gṛhya 3 āhāraṃ kṛtavānnṛpa \|*  
*bhuktaśeṣaṃ mahābāho āhāraṃ sa tu bhuktavān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After returning home, he took up the same vase and started eating. He consumed the food left over by him.

## \|\| 1.3.47 \|\|

*bhuktvā sa śatadhā jātastasminneva kṣaṇe nṛpa \|*  
*tasmādannaṃ na rājendra aśnīyādantarā kvacit \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Soon after that, he was torn into a hundred pieces. O Rajendra, therefore the food should not be left half eaten.

## \|\| 1.3.48 \|\|

*na caivātyaśanaṃ kuryānna cocchiṣṭaḥ kvacidvrajet \|*  
*raso bhavatyatyaśanādrasādrogaḥ pravartate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, one should not take excess of food and one should not go without rinsing the food, nor should be glut the food, because by so doing, the juice in the body increases, as a result of which a person attract ailments.

## \|\| 1.3.49 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevābhipūjanam \|*  
*na bhavanti rase jāte narāṇāṃ bharatarṣabha \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O great king of Bharata’s race, with the increase of the juice in the body, one is unable to bath, perform charities, homa recitation besides adoration of the gods as well as the manes.

## \|\| 1.3.50 \|\|

*anārogyamanāyuṣyamasvargyaṃ cātibhojanam \|*  
*apuṇyaṃ lokavidviṣṭaṃ tasmāttatparivarjayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The excessive eating reduces health, length of life and chances of achieving heaven. By so doing, the virtuous face decline and the jealousy in the world increases. Therefore, a person should avoid the excessive eating.

## \|\| 1.3.51 \|\|

*yakṣabhūtapiśācānāṃ rakṣasāṃ ca nṛpottama \|*  
*4 gamyo bhavati vai vipra ucchiṣṭo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A Brahmana who consumes the left over, becomes prey to the yakshas, goblins, Pishachas, and Rakshasas. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.3.52 \|\|

*śucitvamāśrayettasmācchucitvānmodate diti \|*  
*sukhena ceha ramate itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Therefore, sanctity should be patronized, Diti is pleased with purity and by so doing, a person lives here with comfort. This is what has been ordained in the parts (angas) of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.3.53 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*śucitāmiyātkathaṃ vipraḥ kathaṃ cāśucitāmiyāt \|*  
*etanme ihi viprendra kautukaṃ paramaṃ mama \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Shatanika said — O best of the Brahmanas, how can a Brahmana achieve purity and how does he attract impurity? You please tell me. My mind is quite anxious to know about the same.

## \|\| 1.3.54 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*upaspṛśya śucirvipro bhavate bharatarṣabha \|*  
*vidhivatkuruśārdūla bhavedvidhiparo hyataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Sumantu said — O lion of the Kuru race, a Brahmana gets purified by merely taking a bath. By taking an auspicious bath, he becomes well-versed in all the procedures.

## \|\| 1.3.55 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*upasparśavidhiṃ vipra kathaya tvaṃ mamākhilam \|*  
*śucitvamāpnuyādyena ācānto brāhmaṇo dvijaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Shatanika said — You kindly speak out to me the complete method of having an auspicious bath, by following which the Acharya — Brahmana, besides the Dvijas achieve purification.

## \|\| 1.3.56 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra śṛṇu vipro yathā bhavet \|*  
*śucirbharataśārdūla vidhinā yena vā vibho \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Sumantu said — O lion of the Bharata’s race and beset of the rulers, you have put an appropriate question, the way a Brahmana gets purified.

## \|\| 1.3.57-61 \|\|

*prakṣālya hastau pādau ca prāṅmukhodaṅmukho'pi vā \|*  
*upaviśya śucau deśe bāhuṃ kṛtvā ca dakṣiṇam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*susamau caraṇau kṛtvā tathā baddhaśikho nṛpa \|\| 58 \|\|*

*na tiṣṭhanna ca saṃjalpaṃstathā cānavalokayan \|*  
*na tvarankupito vāpi tyaktvā rājansudūrataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*prasannābhistathādbhistu ācāntaḥ śucitāmiyāt \|*  
*noṣṇābhirna saphenābhiryuktābhiḥ kaluṣeṇa ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

*varṇena rasagandhābhyāṃ hīnābhirna ca bhārata \|*  
*sabudbudābhiśca tathā nācāmetpaṇḍito nṛpa \|\| 61 \|\|*

57-61. Washing one’s hands and feet, one should face east or the north and should get himself at an auspicious place. He should extend the right arm towards the south and then place the sacred thread over the shoulder. Then placing the feet in a similar position, the tuft should be bound. He should neither be seated nor talking, nor looking aside, nor discarding anything from a distance. Using the spotless and clean water, one should perform sipping. O monarch of the Bharata race, a Brahmana gets purified in this manner. O king, Brahmana should not use the hot water, water with foam or contaminated water, colourless or the water devoid of fragrance or the boiling water should not be used by a learned person for the purpose of sipping.

## \|\| 1.3.62-64 \|\|

*pañcatīrthāni viprasya śrūyante dakṣiṇe kare \|*  
*devatīrthaṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ brahmatīrthaṃ ca mānada \|\| 62 \|\|*

*prājāpatyaṃ tathā cānyattathānyatsaumyamucyate \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhamūlottarato yeyaṃ rekhā mahīpate \|\| 63 \|\|*

*brāhmaṃ tīrthaṃ vadantyetadvasiṣṭhādyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kāyaṃ kaniṣṭhikāmūle aṅgulyagre tu daivatam \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. O respectable monarch, it is heard that a Brahmana have five holy spots over his right-hand. These holy spots are known as — Devatirtha, Brahmatirtha, Prajapatya tirtha, Pitritirtha and Saumyatirtha. At the root of the thumb, there starts a line which is known as Vasishtha or the Brahma tirtha, which is the best in a Brahmana. Near the line at the root of the little finger exists the Prajapatya tirtha and at the fore part of the other fingers is known as Devatirtha.

## \|\| 1.3.65 \|\|

*tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayorantaḥ pitryaṃ tīrthamudāhṛtam \|*  
*karamadhye sthitaṃ saumyaṃ praśastaṃ devakarmaṇi \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. In the space between the forefinger and the thumb, is known as Pitri-tirtha. The middle part of the hand is known as Saumya-tirtha, which is used for the purpose of the gods.

## \|\| 1.3.66 \|\|

*devārcābaliharaṇaṃ pravikṣapaṇameva ca \|*  
*etāni devatīrthena kuryātkurukulodvaha \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O king born in the Kuru race, worshipping the god, carrying of the offerings and then dropping it etc. are performed through the Devatirtha.

## \|\| 1.3.67 \|\|

*annanirvapaṇaṃ rājaṃstathā sapavanaṃ 1 nṛpa \|*  
*lājāhomaṃ tathā saumyaṃ prājāpatyena kārayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Offering of the foods, collection and offering of the fried paddy, are known as Saumya activities and should be performed through Prajapatya tirtha.

## \|\| 1.3.68 \|\|

*kamaṇḍalūpasparśanaṃ dadhiprāśanameva ca \|*  
*saumyatīrthena rājendra sadā kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O Indra among the rulers, the carrying of the kamandalu and the consuming of the curd should always be resorted to by Saumya tirtha.

## \|\| 1.3.69 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ pitṛtīrthena dhīmatā \|*  
*brāhmeṇa cāpi tīrthena sadoṣasparśanaṃ param \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A person with wisdom should offer oblation to pitris or offering of pindas and the other rites of the manes, should be performed through Saumya-tirtha. All other types of oblations should be performed through Brahma-tirtha.

## \|\| 1.3.70-72 \|\|

*2 ghanāṅgulikaraṃ kṛtvā ekāgraḥ sumanā dvijaḥ \|*  
*triḥ kṛtvā yaḥ pibedāpo mukhaśabdavivarjitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*śṛṇu yatphalamāpnoti prīṇāti ca yathā surān \|*  
*prathamaṃ yatpibedāpa ṛgvedastena tṛpyati \|\| 71 \|\|*

*yaddvitīyaṃ yajurvedastena prīṇāti bhārata \|*  
*yattṛtīyaṃ sāmavedastena prīṇāti bhārata \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. For performing achamana, uniting the fingers, a Brahmana should thrice sip water without creating any sound to receive the fruit of the same and the way in which he pleases the gods, you please listen to the same. With his first sipping of the water, Rigveda is pleased; with the sipping of the water a second time, Yajurveda is pleased. His third sipping pleases the Samaveda.

## \|\| 1.3.73 \|\|

*prathamaṃ yanmṛjedāsyaṃ dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhamūlataḥ \|*  
*atharvavedaḥ prīṇāti tena rājannasaṃśayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Initially, when he cleans the face with root of the right thumb, it surely pleases the Atharvaveda.

## \|\| 1.3.74-75 \|\|

*itihāsapurāṇāni yaddvitīyaṃ pramārjati \|*  
*yanmūrdhānaṃ hi rājendra abhiṣiñcati vai dvijaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tena prīṇāti vai rudraṃ śikhāmālabhya vai ṛṣīn \|*  
*yadakṣiṇī cālabhate raviḥ prīṇāti tena vai \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. With the sprinkling which is done twice, he pleases the Itihasas (history) as well as the Puranas. O king! A Brahmana, by touching his head and tuft and by so doing, he please Rudra and the Rishis. When he touches his eyes, he pleases the Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.3.76 \|\|

*nāsikālambhanādvāyuṃ prīṇātyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yacchrotramālabhedvipro diśaḥ prīṇāti tena vai \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. With the touching of his nose by him, the Wind-god is surely pleased. A Brahmana who touches his ears, he pleases all the directions by so doing.

## \|\| 1.3.77 \|\|

*yamaṃ kuberaṃ varuṇaṃ vāsavaṃ cāgnimeva ca \|*  
*yadbāhumanvālabhate etānprīṇāti tena 1 vai \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The gods like Yama, Kubera, Vasus, Varuna and Agni get pleased, with his touching of his arms.

## \|\| 1.3.78 \|\|

*yannābhimanvālabhate prāṇānāṃ granthimeva ca \|*  
*tena prīṇāti rājendra itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. With the touch of his navel which is the knot of life, he pleases Indra. This has been revealed in the Vedic literature.

## \|\| 1.3.79-81 \|\|

*abhiṣiñcati yatpādau viṣṇuṃ prīṇāti tena vai \|*  
*yadbhūmyācchādakaṃ vāri visarjayati mānada \|\| 79 \|\|*

*vāsukipramukhānnāgāṃstena prīṇāti bhārata \|*  
*yadbindavo'ntare bhūmau patantīha narādhipa \|\| 80 \|\|*

*bhūtagrāmaṃ tatastastu prīṇantīha caturvidham \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhena pradeśinyā labheta cākṣiṇī nṛpa \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-81. When one decorates his feet, he actually pleases Vishnu. O respectable one, when he discharges the water, which has covered the earth from all the sides, it pleases the Sun-god and Vasuki. When the water drops in the inner parts of the earth, they please all types of bhutas (elements). O king, the eyes should be touched with the thumb and forefinger.

## \|\| 1.3.82 \|\|

*anāmikāṅguṣṭhikābhyāṃ nāsikāmālabhennṛpa \|*  
*madhyamāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ mukhaṃ saṃspṛśedbharatarṣabha \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. O monarch, the nose should be touched with the thumb and the ring finger. The mouth should be touched with the thumb and the middle finger.

## \|\| 1.3.83 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhikāṅguṣṭhakābhyāṃ karṇamālabhate nṛpa \|*  
*aṅgulībhistathā bāhumaṅguṣṭhena tu maṅgalam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The ears should be touched with the thumb and the little finger. The hand should be touched with a finger, while the rest of the body should be touched with the thumb.

## \|\| 1.3.84-85 \|\|

*nābhiṃ kurukulaśreṣṭha śiraḥ sarvābhireva ca \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhoganarmahābāho prokto vāyuḥ pradeśinī \|\| 84 \|\|*

*anābhikā tathā sūryaḥ kaniṣṭhā māghavā vibho \|*  
*prajāpatirmadhyamā jñeyā tasmāddharatasattama \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. The navel and the head should be touched with all of fingers collectively. O excellent valorous king of the Kuru race, it is said that the thumb represents the Fire-god, while the little finger represents the Wind-god. The ring finger represents the Sun, while the little finger represents Indra. The middle finger represents Prajapati.

## \|\| 1.3.86 \|\|

*evamācamya viprastu prīṇāti satataṃ jagat \|*  
*sarvāṅca devatāstāta lokaracāpi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O brothers! By performing the sipping in this way, a Brahmana surely pleases all the gods. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.3.87-88 \|\|

*tasmātūjyaḥ sadā vipraḥ sarvadevamayo hi saḥ \|*  
*brāhyeṇa vipratīrthena nityakālamuspṛśet \|\| 87 \|\|*

*-kāyavaraideśikābhyāṃ vā na pitreṇa kadācana \|*  
*hṛdgābhiḥ pūyate vipraḥ kaṇṭhagābhistu bhūmipaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. Because of these provisions of the scriptures, a Brahmana is always adorable. The outward tirtha known as Brahmana, should always be touched daily and not by the ancestral body and mind. A Brahmana gets pleased with eulogy or praise. With the praise or songs which are stored in the throat, the king gets purified.

## \|\| 1.3.89 \|\|

*vaiśyoddhiḥ prāśitābhistu śūdraḥ syṛṣṭābhirantataḥ \|*  
*uddhate dakṣiṇe pāṇāvupavītyucyate vudhaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Vaishya is purified with water and shudra is purified with the clear and liberated water. With the raising of the right hand, it becomes the condition of one wearing a yajnopavita.

## \|\| 1.3.90-93 \|\|

*savyena prācīnāvītī nivītī kaṇṭhasaṃñite \|*  
*mekhalāmajinaṃ daṇḍamupavītaṃ kamaṇḍalum \|\| 90 \|\|*

*agu prāsya vinaṣṭāni gṛhītānyāni manravit \|*  
*upavītyācameniityamantarajānu mahīpate \|\| 91 \|\|*

*evam tu vipro hacantah sucitam yati bharata \|*  
*yastvetah karamadhye tu rekha viprasya bharata \|\| 92 \|\|*

*gaṅgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvā jñeyā bhāratasattaya \|*  
*yānyaṅguliṣu parvāṇi girayastāni viddhi vai \|\| 93 \|\|*

90-93. In the opposite position, because of the placing of the yajnopavita on the right or hanging in the neck, it is called niviti. In the absence of the girdle, dear skin, danda or the sacred thread and kamandalu one should sip water, reciting the mantras in order to gain purity. O king, the sacred thread should be placed over the left shoulder, then placing the right hand in the middle of the two thighs, when a Brahmana performs the sipping, he achieves purity. O lion of the Bharata’s race, the lines found in the hands of a Brahmana should be taken to the auspicious rivers like Ganga and others. The lines of the finger represent the auspicious mountains.

## \|\| 1.3.94 \|\|

*sarvadevamayo rājankaro viprasya daśṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*hasto pasparśanavidhistavākhyāto mahīpate \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Thus the right hand of a Brahmana is said to be representing all the gods. O lord of the earth, I have already narrated the method of performing sipping of water with the hand.

## \|\| 1.3.95 \|\|

*esu sarveṣu lokaṣu yenācānto divaṃ brajet \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. In this way performing the sipping in a proper way, one achieves the heaven found in all the lokas.

## Chapter 4. Meaning of Pranava, glory of Savitri and method of wearing Yajnopavita

## \|\| 1.4.1 \|\|

*ta eva hi trayo lokāsta eva traya āśramāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O king, the tonsure ceremony of the Brahmana is performed during the sixteenth year of his age. For Kshatriya, it is performed during the twenty second year and of the Vaishyas during the twenty third year.

## \|\| 1.4.2 \|\|

*amantrikā sadā kāryā strīṇāṃ cūḍā mahīpate \|*  
*saṃskārahetoḥ kāyasya yathākālaṃ vibhāgaśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lord of the Earth, the tonsure ceremony of the ladies should be performed without reciting of the mantras. The Samskaras of the women have been prescribed distributing them according to the time or the age of a woman.

## \|\| 1.4.3 \|\|

*nātikramedgṛhāsīnaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ viprakarmaṇi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Only the marriage ceremony has been prescribed for the women in the Vedas. Before the performing of the thread ceremony, a Brahmachari should stay in the abode of the preceptor or should continue the studies at his own house.

## \|\| 1.4.4 \|\|

*eṣa te kathito rājannaupanāyaniko vidhiḥ \|*  
*dvijātīnāṃ mahābāho utpattivyañjakaḥ paraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O king, I have already described the method of the thread ceremony of the Brahmana and others. O valorous one, the thread ceremony is the distinguishing mark for the future generations of the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas.

## \|\| 1.4.5 \|\|

*karmayogamidānīṃ te kathayāmi mahābala \|*  
*upanīya guruḥ śiṣyaṃ prathamaṃ śaucamādiśet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O valorous one, now I shall speak to you on Karmayoga or the religious performance for the purification of the mind. After performing the thread ceremony, initially the disciple should be made to purify himself.

## \|\| 1.4.6 \|\|

*ācāramagnikāryaṃ ca sandhyopāsanameva ca \|*  
*adhyāpayettu sacchiṣyānsadācānta udaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereafter, he should be adversed on the performing of Sandhya, the fire ceremony and the sipping, facing north. The preceptor should then teach the competent disciples.

## \|\| 1.4.7 \|\|

*brahmāñjalikaro nityamadhyāpyo vijitendriyaḥ \|*  
*laghuvāsāstathaikāgraḥ sumanā supratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The disciple should completely control his sense organs, and forming the Brahmanjali engage himself in studies. He should have scanty clothes with concentrated mind and should always remain delightful.

## \|\| 1.4.8 \|\|

*brahmārambhe'vasāne ca pādau pūjyau guroḥ sadā \|*  
*saṃhatya hastāvadhyeyaṃ sa hi brahmāñjaliḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should remain firm. At the start and the end of the Vedic studies, a disciple should always adore the feet of the preceptor. Folding both the hands is called Brahmanjali.

## \|\| 1.4.9 \|\|

*vyatyastapāṇinā kāryamupasaṅgrahaṇaṃ guroḥ \|*  
*savyena savyaḥ spraṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena tu dakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The disciple should touch the feet of his preceptor with both his hands or in other words, he should touch the right foot of the preceptor with his right hand and the left foot with his left hand.

## \|\| 1.4.10 \|\|

*adhyeṣyamāṇaṃ tu gururnityakālamatandritaḥ \|*  
*adhīṣva bho iti brūyādvirāmo'stviti vārayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Without laziness, the preceptor should command his disciple to start the studies, and at the end the disciple should be commanded to stop it.

## \|\| 1.4.11 \|\|

*brahmaṇaḥ praṇavaṃ kuryādādāvante ca sarvadā \|*  
*sravatyanoṅkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ parastācca viśīryate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. During the study of the Vedas, the Pranava should be uttered at the beginning as well as at the end. This is necessary because in case the Pranava or Omkara is not recited at the beginning and at the end of the recitation, the entire exercise becomes useless.

## \|\| 1.4.12-13 \|\|

*śrūyatāṃ cāpi rājendra yathoṅkāraṃ dvijo'rhati \|*  
*prākkūlānparyupāsīnaḥ pavitraiścaiva pāvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prāṇāyāmaistribhiḥ pūtastatastvoṅkāramarhati \|*  
*oṃkāralakṣaṇaṃ cāpi śṛṇuṣva kurunandana \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. O Rajendra, you listen to my words. I am going to reveal about the necessity of uttering of Pranava by a Brahmana. Sitting in meditation over the bank of a lake or a river, in case the pranayama is performed thrice with devotion, a person gets purified. This is the reason why it is so important for a Brahmana to recite Pranava. O son of the race of Kuru, now I shall reveal the symptoms of Omkara, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.4.14-16 \|\|

*akāraṃ cāpyukāraṃ ca makāraṃ ca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vedatrayāttu nirgṛhya bhūrbhuvaḥ svaritīti ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tribhya eva tu vedebhyaḥ pādaṃpādamadūduhat \|*  
*tadityṛco'syāḥ sāvitryāḥ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*etadakṣarametāṃ ca japanvyāhṛtipūrvikām \|*  
*sandhyayorubhayorvipro veda puṇyena yujyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. The Akara A, Ukara U and Makara М (of the word Omkara) represents the three Vedas viz., Bhu, Bhuvah and Svah. The Prajapati has milked one pada each from each one of the three Vedas. Savitri possesses all the then fads. A person, who recites this mystic word during the mornings and evenings, earns the merit of studying the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.4.17 \|\|

*sahasrakṛtvastvabhyasya bahiretattrikaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*mahato'pyenaso māsāttvacevāhirvimucyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A Brahmana who recites the Trika (triad) with Pranava at a lonely place a thousand times for a month, he is relieved of the gravest sin in the same way as the serpent discards its slough.

## \|\| 1.4.18 \|\|

*etayarcā visaṃyuktaḥ kāle ca kriyayā svayā \|*  
*viprakṣatriyaviḍyonirgarhaṇāṃ yāti sādhuṣu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Discarding the Rea, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas who are deprived of their religious duties, earn the denounce from the learned people.

## \|\| 1.4.19-21 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājanparamaṃ brahmaṇo mukham \|*  
*oṃkārapūrvikāstisro mahāvyāhṛtayo'vyayāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tripadā caiva sāvitrī vijñeyā brahmaṇo mukham \|*  
*yo'dhīte'hanyahanyetāṃ trīṇi varṣāṇyatandritaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sa brahma paramabhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān \|*  
*ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaḥ parantapa \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. O king, you listen to it again with a concentrated mind. These eternal and great mystic words viz., Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svah represent the excellent faces of Brahma. Savitri, with three padas, should be considered to be the face of Brahma. A Brahmana, who shedding away laziness, studies it without interruption for three years, he, like the sky, taking to the form of the wind, gets absorbed in supreme Brahman. Omkara is the form of the supreme Brahman. The Pranayama is of greater importance as compared to all the tapas.

## \|\| 1.4.22-23 \|\|

*sāvitryāstu paraṃ nāsti maunātsatyaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*tapaḥ kiyā homakriyā tathā dānakriyā nṛpa \|\| 22 \|\|*

*akṣayāntāḥ sadā rājanyathāha bhagavānmanuḥ \|*  
*avaraṃ svakṣaraṃ jñeyaṃ brahma caiva prajāpatiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The single letter Omkara is the form of Brahman. No one else has the glory comparable to Savitri. The speaking of the truth is more important than keeping silent. O king, Manu has ordained that the activities like tapas, performing of homa and charities are surely fruitful. Besides them, the everlasting Pranava of a single letter is also fruitful. One should take it to be the form of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.4.24-26 \|\|

*vidhiyajñātsadā rājañjapayajño viśiṣyate \|*  
*nānāvidhairguṇoddeśaiḥ sūkṣmākhyātairnṛpottama \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pāṃśuḥ syāllakṣaguṇaḥ sahasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ye pākayajñāścatvāro vidhiyajñena cānvitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarve te japayajñasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*japādeva tu saṃsidhyeddbrāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. O best of the humans, the Japa-yajna is more important than the yajna which is performed with all the due rites. The Upamshu japam is a lakh of times more fruitful as compared to the reciting of the different types of name of the lord, or the short time recitations. The mental recitation is thousand times more rewarding. The mixed or coordinated cannot be compared with one-sixteenth part of the performing of the Japa-yajna. A Brahmana achieves success only with the performing of the Japa-yajna. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.4.27-31 \|\|

*kuryādanyanna vā kuryānmaitro brāhmaṇa ucyate \|*  
*pūrvāṃ sandhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhetsāvitrīmārkadarśanāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*paścimāṃ tu samāsīnaḥ samyagṛkṣavibhāvanāt \|*  
*dinasyādau bhavetpūrvā śarvaryādau tathā parā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sanakṣatrā parā jñeyā aparā sadivākarā \|*  
*japaṃstiṣṭhanparāṃ sandhyāṃ naiśameno vyapohati \|\| 29 \|\|*

*aparāṃ tu samāsīno malaṃ hanti divākṛtam \|*  
*nopatiṣṭhati yaḥ pūrvāṃ nopāste paścimāṃ nṛpa \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sa śūdravadbahiṣkāryaḥ sarvasmāddvijakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*apāṃ samīpe niyato naityakaṃ vidhimāsthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

27-31. Irrespective of his indulging in any other activity, a Brahmana should perform the Japa-yajna. In the early morning, one should recite the Gayatri mantra after looking at the Sun. Similarly, in the evening, one should perform the japam till the constellations and stars rise up in the sky properly. Sandhya appears at the start and at the close of the day. The morning Sandhya is known as Divakara sandhya while the evening sandhya is known as Para sandhya. In the early morning, the Gayatri mantra should be recited while standing and during the evening, the Sandhya should be performed while seated. With the performing of the Para sandhya, the sins of the night are removed, while with the performing of Apara sandhya, the sins of the day are removed. A Brahmana who does not perform the Para and Apara Sandhya, he is fit to be driven out of the Brahmana caste. The Sandhya should be performed quite appropriately controlling the sense organs and near a lake, regularly in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 1.4.32-33 \|\|

*sāvitrīmapyadhīyīta gatyā'raṇyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*vedopakaraṇe rājansvādhyāye caiva naityake \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nātra doṣostyanadhyāye homamantreṣu vā vibho \|*  
*naityake nāstvanadhyāyo brahmasatraṃ hi tatkṛtam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Alternatively, one should do so by going to a forest and perform japam with a concentrated mind. O king, with the performing of the naityika studies and homa as ordained in the Vedas, and reciting the Vedic hymn, one does not attract the intermission sin, because all of them are called the Brahmasutras.

## \|\| 1.4.34-37 \|\|

*brahmāhutihutaṃ puṣyamanadhyāyavaṣaṭkṛtam \|*  
*ṛgekāṃ yastvadhīyīta vidhinā niyato dvijaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasya nityaṃ kṣaratyeṣā payo medhyaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu \|*  
*agniśuśrūṣaṇaṃ bhaikṣamadhaḥ śayyāṃ gurorhitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*āsamāvartanātkuryātkṛtopanayano dvijaḥ \|*  
*ācāryaputraśuśrūṣāṃ jñānado dhārmikaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*āptaḥ śaktonnadaḥ sādhuḥ svādhyāpyā daśa dharmataḥ \|*  
*nāpṛṣṭaḥ kasyacidbrūyānna cānyāyena pṛcchataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-37. The reciting of the Vedic hymns, pouring of the offering with the reciting of the Vedic hymns, keeping in mind the intermission and the performing of Vasatkara is quite auspicious. A Brahmana who appropriately studies with the Richas, he is bestowed with the auspicious milk, ghi and honey. A Brahmana, after his thread ceremony, to the time of his departure from the place of the preceptor and after completing his studies, should adore the fire, begging, sleeping on the ground and serve the preceptor. He should advocate the son of the Acharya, the servants, the teacher, the religious-minded people, the auspicious orator, the competent person and bestower of food. These are the ten type of people with noble temperament. He should not speak anything to anyone unless asked for and should speak only when he is specifically asked to do so.

## \|\| 1.4.38-39 \|\|

*jānannapi hi medhāvī jaḍavalloka ācaret \|*  
*adharmeṇa ca yaḥ prāha yaścādharmeṇa pṛcchati \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tayoranyataraḥ praiti vidveṣaṃ vā nigacchati \|*  
*dharmārthau yatra na syātāṃ śuśrūṣā cāpi tadvidhā \|*  
*na tatra vidyā vaptavyā śubhaṃ bījamivoṣare \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. (When confronted with injustice), he should keep quiet inspite of his being illustrious, because the one who speak falsely or asks some one to speak falsely, either of the two surely dies, or earns the enmity of others. A disciple by teaching whom the preceptor does not receive due service, artha or dharma in that case, the seed should not be sown like the barren land.

## \|\| 1.4.40 \|\|

*vidyayaiva samaṃ kāmaṃ martavyaṃ brahmavādinā \|*  
*āpadyapi hi ghorāyāṃ na tvenāmīriṇe vapet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. A preceptor should never import knowledge to an inappropriate disciple, even when he has to the carrying the knowledge with him.

## \|\| 1.4.41 \|\|

*vidyā brāhmaṇamityāha śevadhiste'smi rakṣa mām \|*  
*asūyakāya mā prādāstathā syāṃ vīryavattamā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Vidya — the goddess, once went to a Brahmana and asked — “You must protect me, because I happen to be your treasure. Do not give me to a person, who finds fault with the virtues. In case you act accordingly, then I shall prove quite forceful to you.”

## \|\| 1.4.42 \|\|

*śevaṃ sukhamuśantīha kecijjñānaṃ pracakṣate \|*  
*tau dhārayati vai yasmācchevadhistena socyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Some people interpret the word Seva as comfort, while others interpret it as knowledge. Therefore, she is well known by Shevadhi or one of the nine treasures of Kubera.

## \|\| 1.4.43 \|\|

*yameva tu śuciṃ vidyānniyataṃ brahmacāriṇam \|*  
*tasmai māṃ brūhi viprāya nidhipāyāpramādine \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Vidya further addressed the Brahmana — “Whosoever a Brahmachari possesses the good and auspicious conduct besides being well behaved, you should entrust my care as a trust to the careful, conscious and the one who can protect me carefully.

## \|\| 1.4.44-45 \|\|

*brahma yastvananujñātamadhīyānādavāpnuyāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

*laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vāpi tathādhyātmikameva ca \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ rauravaṃ bhīmadarśanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. A person, who while studying the Vedas, achieves the knowledge of Vedas without his permission or achieves the worldly, Vedic or the spiritual knowledge, (without his knowledge), he falls in the terrific hell.

## \|\| 1.4.46 \|\|

*aṇumātrātmakaṃ dehaṃ ṣoḍaśārdhamiti smṛtam \|*  
*ādadīta yato jñānaṃ taṃ pūrvamabhivādayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It is said that the subtle body is made of eight tattvas or elements. A person who receives knowledge from a particular person, he should initially get up and welcome him.

## \|\| 1.4.47 \|\|

*sāvitrīsāramātro'pi varo vipraḥ suyantritaḥ \|*  
*nāyantritastrivedo'pi sarvāśī sarvavikrayī \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A Brahmana who is well-versed in Savitri, having controlled all his sense organs, but has no control over his mind, besides being valorous and consumes everything, is better than a Brahmana who is well-versed in the three Vedas.

## \|\| 1.4.48 \|\|

*śayyāsanedhyācarite śreyasā na samāviśet \|*  
*śayyāsanasthaścaivenaṃ pratyutthāyābhivādayet \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. A person who carries studies in front of the preceptor sitting over the bed, does not meet with welfare. Even when he be seated over the bed, he should at once get up and welcome the preceptor on his arrival.

## \|\| 1.4.49 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hyutkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āgate \|*  
*pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastānpratipadyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On the arrival of the old people as well as the preceptors, the pupils become nervous but by welcoming the elders, they regain their lost confidence.

## \|\| 1.4.50 \|\|

*abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ \|*  
*catvāri samyagvardhante āyuḥ prajñā yaśo balam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A person, who is always engaged in service of the preceptors as well as the elderly people and the one who respects and welcomes them, achieves long life, intelligence, glory and strength.

## \|\| 1.4.51 \|\|

*abhivādaparo vipro jyāyāṃsamabhivādayet \|*  
*asau nāmāhamasmīti svanāma parikīrtayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. By extending respect and salutation to elders, saying that “I am such and such person”, thus reveal his introduction.

## \|\| 1.4.52 \|\|

*nāmadheyasya ye kecidabhivādaṃ na jānate \|*  
*tānprājño'hamiti brūyātstriyaḥ sarvāstathaiva ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The people who out of ignorance, do not understand the meaning of importance of introducing themselves, revealing their own introduction, he should welcome them saying, “I am such and such person.” All the ladies should also conduct themselves accordingly.

## \|\| 1.4.53 \|\|

*bhoḥ śabdaṃ kīrtayedante svasya nāmnobhivādane \|*  
*nāmnaḥ svarūpabhāvo hi bho bhāva ṛṣibhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Revealing one’s name, while offering his salutation, he should reveal his name, last of all. This has been prescribed by the Rishis or the ascetics.

## \|\| 1.4.54 \|\|

*āyuṣmānbhava saumyeti vācyo vipro'bhivādane \|*  
*akāraścāsya nāmno'nte vācyaḥ pūrvākṣaraḥ plutaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After a welcome, a Brahmana should be thus addressed — “O pleasant one, let you enjoy a long life.” He should thus be blessed. At the end of his name, Akara should be added. The first letter of the name should be protracted.

## \|\| 1.4.55 \|\|

*yo na vettyabhivādasya vipraḥ pratyabhivādanam \|*  
*nābhivādyaḥ sa viduṣā yathā śūdrastathaiva saḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A Brahmana, who after having been welcomed does not know how to respond, the learned person should not welcome him, because such a person is equated with a low grade person.

## \|\| 1.4.56 \|\|

*abhivāde kṛte yastu na karotyabhivādanam \|*  
*āśīrvā kuruśārdūla sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A Brahmana who after the welcoming him by others does not reciprocate, or does not bless the other party, O son of the Kuru dynasty, such a person surely goes to the hell.

## \|\| 1.4.57 \|\|

*abhīti bhagavānviṣṇuाrvādayāmīti śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*dvāveva pūjitau tena yaḥ karotyabhivādanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A person who welcomes others saying abhivddayami, in the word ‘abhi’ represent lord Vishnu while ‘vadayami’ stands for lord Shiva, with the reciting of the said passage, both the gods are adored by the person who welcomes the elderly people.

## \|\| 1.4.58 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchetkṣatrabandhumanāmayam \|*  
*vaiśyaṃ kṣemaṃ samāgamya śūdramārogyameva tu \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After welcoming a Brahmana, one should enquire about his welfare. The Kshatriyas should enquire about the welfare. The Vaishya should be enquire about kshema (wealth or happiness), while a Shudra should be enquired about his health.

## \|\| 1.4.59 \|\|

*na vācyo dīkṣito nāmnā yavīyānapi yo bhavet \|*  
*bho bhavatpūrvakatvena iti svāyambhuvo'bravīt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A person who is junior in age but has been initiated, he should not be addressed by calling his name. But while calling him, he should be addressed with respect. This has been ordained by Svayambhuva Manu.

## \|\| 1.4.60 \|\|

*parapatnī tu yā rājannasambaddhā tu yonitaḥ \|*  
*vaktavyā bhavatītyevaṃ subhage bhaganīti ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O monarch! The other’s wife with whom one has no sexual relationship, should be addressed as a goddess, fortunate one or a sister.

## \|\| 1.4.61 \|\|

*pitṛvyānmātulānrājañchvaśurānṛtvijo gurūn \|*  
*asāvahamiti brūyātpratyutthāya jaghanyajaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O king! One’s uncle, maternal uncle, father-in-law, the priest and the preceptor should be addressed with respect, revealing one’s own name at the same time offering his salutation to him, because the person so addressing then happens to be younger to them in age.

## \|\| 1.4.62 \|\|

*mātṛṣvasā mātulānī śvaśrūratha pitṛṣvasā \|*  
*sampūjyā gurupatnī ca samāstā gurubhāryayā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The sister of the mother, wife of the maternal uncle, mother-in-law, husband of one’s father’s sister and the wife of the preceptor, are alt adorable like the wife of the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.4.63 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasya bhrāturyā bhāryā savarṇāhanyahanyapi \|*  
*2 pūjayanprayato vipro yāti viṣṇusado nṛpa \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O monarch, the wife of the elder brother belonging to the same caste, is adorable daily. A person or a Brahmana, who controlling all his sense organs, conducts himself accordingly, surely goes to Vishnuloka.

## \|\| 1.4.64-65 \|\|

*pravāsādetya sampūjyā jñātisambandhiyoṣitaḥ \|*  
*pituryā bhaginī rājanmātuścāpi viśāmpate \|\| 64 \|\|*

*ātmano bhaginī yā ca jyeṣṭhā kurukulodvaha \|*  
*sadā svamātṛvaddhṛttimātiṣṭhedbhāratottama \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. After returning from some other country, the women of one’s own caste should also be respected and adored. O monarch, O best of the race of Bharata, O son of the race of Kuru, one’s own elder sister, the sister of one’s own father, the sister of one’s own mother, should be treated like one’s own mother.

## \|\| 1.4.66 \|\|

*garīyasī tatastābhyo mātā jñeyā narādhipa \|*  
*putramitrabhāgineyā draṣṭavyā hyātmanā samāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. But one’s own mother is far better than all of them. This should always be kept in mind. O excellent person, one should consider his own son, friend and sister’s son, like himself always.

## \|\| 1.4.67 \|\|

*daśābdākhyaṃ paurasakhyaṃ pañcābdākhyaṃ kalābhṛtām \|*  
*abdapūrvaṃ śrotriyāṇāṃ svalpenāpi svayoniṣu \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A person who lives in the same village develops friendship in ten years time and the artists or those who earn their livelihood, making use of their artistic skill» become friends after their association for five years. Those who are well-versed in the Vedas become friendly after three years. But those who belong to one’s own race or caste become friendly in short period of two years only.

## \|\| 1.4.68-69 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ daśavarṣaṃ ca śatavarṣaṃ ca bhūmipam \|*  
*pitāputrau vijānīyādbrāhmaṇastu tayoḥ pitā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ kṣatriyapitā vaiśyasyāpi pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*prapitāmahaśca śūdrasya prokto vipro manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. A Brahmana of the age of ten years and a Kshatriya of a hundred years old should be treated as the father and the son. Out of these two, the status of a father for Kshatriya and a grandfather for a Vaishya, besides being, the great grandfather for a Shudra. The people of high learnings have ordained ini this connection like this.

## \|\| 1.4.70 \|\|

*vittaṃ bandhurvayaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī \|*  
*etāni mānyasthānāni garīyo yadyaduttaram \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The wealth, relationship or, brotherhood, age, activity or profession, besides the education are all respectable. Out of these five, one is much better than the other.

## \|\| 1.4.71 \|\|

*pañcānāṃ triṣu vargeṣu bhūyāṃsi guṇavanti ca \|*  
*yasya syuḥ so'tra mānārhaḥ śūdro'pi daśamīṃ gataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Out of the three high castes, whosoever possesses these five qualities in, excessive quantity, he is considered to be more respectable, Even Shudra, when in the tenth stage, or has grown too o№, becomes respectable.

## \|\| 1.4.72 \|\|

*cakriṇo daśamīsthasya rogiṇo bhāriṇaḥ 1 striyāḥ \|*  
*snātakasya tu rājñaśca panthā deyo varasya ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. An old person who is ailing but drives a chariot, carrier of burden, a woman, a person who has been initiated and the groom forgoing to perform a marriage, should out of respect, be given the way for passage on the road.

## \|\| 1.4.73 \|\|

*eṣāṃ samāgame tāta pūjyau snātakapārthivau \|*  
*ābhyāṃ samāgame rājansnātako nṛpamānabhāk \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O king, when all of them collect at a particular place, the Brahmachari and the king, both are adorable. Out of these two, the Brahmachari is more adorable than the king.

## \|\| 1.4.74 \|\|

*adhyāpayedyastu śiṣyaṃ kṛtvopanayanaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*sarahasyaṃ sakalpaṃ ca vedaṃ bharatasattama \|*  
*tamācāryaṃ mahābāho pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. A Brahmana, who after completing of the thread ceremony of his disciple, educates the disciple in all the Vedas with kalpas, O valorous one, he is known as the Acharya by the people of learning.

## \|\| 1.4.75 \|\|

*ekadeśaṃ tu vedasya vedāṅgānyapi vā punaḥ \|*  
*yo'dhyāpayati vṛttyarthamupādhyāyaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A Brahmana who learns a part of the Vedas for making his own living, he is known as the Upadhyaya.

## \|\| 1.4.76 \|\|

*niṣekādīni kāryāṇi yaḥ karoti nṛpottama \|*  
*adhyāpayati cānyena sa vipro gururucyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O best of the humans, one who performs the ceremony of conception and educates the pupils by serving them with food etc., such a Brahmana is called the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.4.77 \|\|

*agnyādheyaṃ pākayajñānagniṣṭomādikānmakhān \|*  
*yaḥ karoti vṛto yasya sa tasyartvigihocyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. A Brahmana, who accepting the responsibility of the performing of sacrificial fire, Agnishtoma homa, Pakayajna and other yajnas, and gets them completed properly, he is called Ritvika.

## \|\| 1.4.78 \|\|

*ya āvṛṇotyavitathaṃ brahmaṇā śravaṇāvubhau \|*  
*sa mātā sa pitā jñeyastaṃ na druhyetkathañcana 1 \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. One who teaches the hymns by reciting them loudly to his disciples, he should be treated as the parent or the teacher. One should not pick up ill will or hatred with him.

## \|\| 1.4.79 \|\|

*upādhyāyāndaśācāryaṃ ācāryāṇāṃ śataṃ pitā \|*  
*sahasreṇa piturmātā gauraveṇātiricyate \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The Acharya commands ten times more respect than are Upadhyaya. The father is a hundred times more respectable than the Acharya. The mother is thousand times more respectable than the father.

## \|\| 1.4.80 \|\|

*utpādakabrahmadātrorgarīyānbrahmadaḥ pitā \|*  
*brahmajanma hi viprasya pretya ceha ca śāśvatam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Out of the father and the one who imparts; the knowledge of Brahmajnana, the latter is more respectable because for a Brahmana, the latter performs the samskara which bestows welfare in this as well as the future world.

## \|\| 1.4.81 \|\|

*kāmānmātā pitā cainaṃ yadutpādayato mithaḥ \|*  
*sambhūtiṃ tasya tāṃ vidyādyadyonāvabhijāyate \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. One is born out of the desire of his patents. Through his father, one enters the womb of his mother and then-takes the human form.

## \|\| 1.4.82 \|\|

*ācāryastasya tāṃ jātiṃ vidhidvedapāragaḥ \|*  
*utpādayati sāvitryā sā satyā sā'jarāmarā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Then an Acharya, giving away Savitri in charity to him, produces in him the caste; This truth is eternal.

## \|\| 1.4.83 \|\|

*upādhyāyamāditaḥ kṛtvā ye pūjyāḥ kathitāstava \|*  
*mahāgururmahābāho sarveṣāmadhikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O valorous one, I have already discussed about the people of the adorable class like, Upadhyaya and other Mahagurus or great preceptors who are considered to be the best.

## \|\| 1.4.84 \|\|

*sahasraśatasaṃkhyo'sāvācāryāṇāmidaṃ matam \|*  
*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ sa mahāgururucyate \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The Acharyas who possess a lakh of excellent merits, hold this opinion. These Mahagurus are meant for all the classes or castes of the people.

## \|\| 1.4.85 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*ya ete bhavatā proktā upādhyāyamukhā dvijāḥ \|*  
*viditā eva me sarve na mahāgurureva hi \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Shatanika said — The Brahmanas, right from Upadhyayas and others about whom you have just discussed, are known to me already, but I am totally ignorant about the Mahagurus.

## \|\| 1.4.86-88 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*jayopajīvī yo vipraḥ sa mahāgururucyate \|*  
*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni rāmasya caritaṃ tathā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*viṣṇudharmādayo dharmāḥ śivadharmāśca bhārata \|*  
*kārṣṇaṃ vedaṃ pañcamaṃ tu yanmahābhārataṃ smṛtam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*śrautā 1 dharmāśca rājendra nāradoktā mahīpate \|*  
*jayeti nāma eteṣāṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

86-88. Sumantu said — O Monarch, a Brahmana, who earns his living with the reciting of Jaya, he is known as Mahaguru. Now you listen to the interpretation of the word Mahaguru. The person who is; aware of all the eighteen Puranas, the Ramayana containing the auspicious story of lord Rama, the dharmas relating to the Vaishnava and Shaiva sects, Mahabharata — the fifth Veda composed by Krishnadvaipayana — Vyasa, besides the Shrauta and Dharma sutras combined together, are known by the name of Jaya.

## \|\| 1.4.89-90 \|\|

*evaṃ viprakadambasya dhārakaḥ2 pravaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yastvetāni samastāni purāṇānīha vindati \|\| 89 \|\|*

*bhārataṃ ca mahābāho sa sarvajño mato nṛṇām \|*  
*tasmātsa pūjyo rājendra varṇairviprādibhiḥ sadā \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. A person who gains mastery over all the Puranas, the Mahabharata, he becomes the leader of the Brahmanas and the best of all. O valorous one, he is considered as the best educated among the humans. O Rajendra, because of this reason, such a Brahmana becomes adorable among all the varnas and castes.

## \|\| 1.4.91 \|\|

*kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ vākyaṃ yadāha bhagavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*alpaṃ vā bahu vā yasya śrutasyopakaroti yaḥ \|*  
*tamapīha guruṃ vidyācchrutopakriyayā tayā3 \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Have you heard the words himself spoken by the extremely glorious lord? A person who attains even the little knowledge of the Vedas, should be treated as a preceptor or the Guru.

## \|\| 1.4.92 \|\|

*brāhmasya janmanaḥ kartā svadharmasya ca śāsitā \|*  
*bālo'pi vipro vṛddhasya pitā bhavati dharmataḥ 4 \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A Brahmana boy who can impart the knowledge of the Vedas, is considered to be the father by dharma.

## \|\| 1.4.93 \|\|

*adhyāpayāmāsa pitṝñchiśurāṅgirasaḥ kaviḥ \|*  
*putrakā iti hovāca jñānena parigṛhya tām \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Kavi — the son of Angiras, during his childhood had delivered discourse to his pitris or manes, knowing fully well that they were his ancestors. He addressed them as sons.

## \|\| 1.4.94 \|\|

*te tamarthamapṛcchanta devānāgatamanyavaḥ \|*  
*devāścaitānsametyocurnyāyyaṃ vai śiśuruktavān \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The manes got enraged with the conduct of Kavi and questioned the gods on the subject, the gods collected them all and then told them that the child had addressed you properly.

## \|\| 1.4.95-96 \|\|

*ajño bhavati vai bālaḥ pitā bhavati mantradaḥ \|*  
*ajñaṃ hi bālamityāhuḥ pitetyeva tu mantradam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*pitāmaheti jayadamityūcuste divaukasaḥ \|*  
*jayo mantrāstathā vedā dehamekaṃ tridhā kṛtam \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. Because an ignorant person is a child, but a person who teaches the mantras, he becomes the father. The people call the ignorant as the child and the father, who bestows the mantras, while the one who bestows Jaya (i.e., Mahabharata, Puranas, Ramayana etc.), he is called the grandsire. These were the words spoken by the gods to the manes. Jaya, mantra and the Vedas are the three parts of one and the same body.

## \|\| 1.4.97 \|\|

*nahāyanairna palitairna mitreṇa na bandhubhiḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayaścakrire dharmaṃ yo'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The Rishis while creating discipline in dharma spent many years, which made their hair grey. They did not so perform because of their being a friend or a relative or a brother. But a person who is the fluent orator of the Vedas with its six angas, he has surely been treated to be great.

## \|\| 1.4.98 \|\|

*brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca viśāṃpate \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaṃ vandanti rājendra sandehaṃ śṛṇu vai yathā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. O Indra among the rulers, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and the Shudras call some one great in their respective castes, which I am going to tell you. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.4.99 \|\|

*jñānato vīryato rājandhanato janmatastathā \|*  
*śīlatastu pradhānā ye te pradhānā matā mama \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O monarch, the Brahmanas become foremost by their knowledge, the Kshatriyas become foremost because of their prowess, the Vaishyas become foremost because of their wealth. The Shudras become foremost because of their humility since birth. This is our considered opinion.

## \|\| 1.4.100 \|\|

*na tena sthaviro bhavati yenāsya palitaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*yo vai yuvāpyadhīyānastaṃ devāḥ sthaviraṃ viduḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. In case the hair of someone’s head grow grey, he does not become old by that. The one who is quite young and studies the Vedas with its six parts, he is to be taken as aged. Because the gods consider him to be the aged one.

## \|\| 1.4.101 \|\|

*yathā kāṣṭhamayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ \|*  
*yaśca vipro'nadhīyānastrayaste nāma 1 bibhrati \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. A denounced Brahmana is like a wooden elephant or a deer made of skin, are taken as such for the name sake. Similarly, a Brahmana without studies is a Brahmana for name sake only. All the three are known as such for the name sake only.

## \|\| 1.4.102 \|\|

*yathā yoṣā'phalā strīṣu yathā gaurgavi cāphalā \|*  
*yathā cājñe'phalaṃ dānaṃ yathā vipro'nṛco'phalaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. As a woman is useless with barren woman and in herd of cows the dry cow is of no use, similarly, giving away of the charity to a foolish Brahmana is of no use.

## \|\| 1.4.103 \|\|

*vaiśvadevena ye hīnā ātithyena vivarjitāḥ \|*  
*sarve tu vṛṣalā jñeyāḥ prāptavedā api dvijāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. But such of the Brahmanas, having full knowledge of the Vedas, are considered to be the Shudras who do not welcome the guests and are averse to the performing of the Balivishvedeva.

## \|\| 1.4.104 \|\|

*nānṛgbrāhmaṇo bhavati na vaṇiṅna kuśīlavaḥ \|*  
*na śūdraḥ preṣaṇaṃ kurvannasteno na cikitsakaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. A person who is engaged in trade, or is attracted in dance and music for his livelihood, or the one who serves others or the one who otherwise performs the work of a Shudra, the one who is engaged in stealing others riches or the one who functions as a physician, cannot be considered like a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.4.105 \|\|

*avratā hyanadhīyānā yatra bhaikṣacarā dvijāḥ \|*  
*taṃ grāmaṃ daṇḍayedrājā corabhaktaprado hi saḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The place where such Brahmanas are found who are not performing vratas, are illiterate, are earning on begging, such a village should be punished by the king, because the activities of such people encourage stealing.

## \|\| 1.4.106 \|\|

*santuṣṭo yatra vai vipraḥ sāgnikaḥ kurunandana \|*  
*yāti sāphalyatāṃ vedairdevairevaṃ hi bhāṣitam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. O son of the race of Kuru, the village in which the Brahmanas are happy, that place should be treated as the yajna-bhumi because its success is attributed to the Vedas. This has been ordained by the gods.

## \|\| 1.4.107 \|\|

*vedairuktaṃ yathā vīra surajyeṣṭhamupetya vai \|*  
*vepante brāhmaṇā bhūmāvabhyasyanti hyanagnikāḥ \|*  
*kliśyante te kimarthaṃ hi mūḍhā vai phalakāmyayā \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. O valorous one, once the Vedas went to Brahma and prayed to him thus, “O lord, the Brahmanas feel uncomfortable on earth because these related to the fire or the yajnas, practice the Vedas. The fools expect reward by reciting of the Vedas and feel painful, uselessly.

## \|\| 1.4.108 \|\|

*anuṣṭhānavihīnānāmasmānabhyasatāṃ bhuvi \|*  
*kleśo hi kevalaṃ deva nāsmadabhyasane phalam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Having been deprived of the systematic approach by practicing the Vedas, one feels painful only.

## \|\| 1.4.109 \|\|

*anuṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ devamasmatsvabhyasanātsadā \|*  
*ityevaṃ rājaśārdūla vedā ūcurhi vedhasam \|*  
*tasmācca vedābhyasanādanuṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ matam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. The systematic approach is better than the reciting of the Vedas. O lion among the rulers, the Vedas spoke such things to Brahma. Therefore, the performing of yajna is better than the mere reciting of the Vedas. This is our opinion as well.

## \|\| 1.4.110 \|\|

*catvāro vā trayo vāpi yadbrūyurvedapāragāḥ \|*  
*sa dharma iti vijñeyo netareṣāṃ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The learned people who are well-versed in the Vedas, could be three or four only, but whatever is done by them it would be quite religious. Similarly, thousands of people are not entitled to possess the Vedas. In case the things are disciplined it does not amount to dharma.

## \|\| 1.4.111 \|\|

*tatpāpaṃ śatadhā bhūtvā vaktṝnevānugacchati \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The foolish people who are unaware of the glory of dharma and indulge in practices prohibited in the Vedas and whatever irrelevant ideas about dharma they spread in the public, the same ideas follow them in the form of sins in hundreds.

## \|\| 1.4.112 \|\|

*śaucahīne vratabhraṣṭe vipre vedavivarjite \|*  
*dīyamānaṃ rudatyannaṃ ki mayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The food which is given to the Brahmana who are devoid of vratas, unclear, fallen from the vratas cries, as to what sin did if commit that it fell in the hands of the sinful person?

## \|\| 1.4.113 \|\|

*japopajīvine dattaṃ yadātmānaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*nṛtyati sma tadā rājankarāvuddhṛtya bhārata \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. O best of the race of Bharata, a person who earns his living with the performing of japam and is given the food in charity, such food finding when offered to such a person, then it dances with joy, raising both the hands.

## \|\| 1.4.114 \|\|

*vidyātapobhyāṃ sampanne brāhmaṇe gṛhamāgate \|*  
*krīḍantyauṣadhayaḥ sarvā yāsyāmaḥ paramāṃ gatim \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. When such a Brahmana carries the food to his house and on reaching there, the food and the aushadhis dance in delight that would achieves the best end.

## \|\| 1.4.115 \|\|

*1 avratānāmamantrāṇāmajapānāṃ ca bhārata \|*  
*pratigraho na dātavyo na śilā tārayecchilām \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. O Bharata, those who are ignorant of vratas etc., besides being unaware of the mantras or the japam, charities should never be given to such people because a stone cannot make another stone to float on water.

## \|\| 1.4.116 \|\|

*śrotriyāyaiva deyāni havyakavyāni nityaśaḥ \|*  
*aśrotriyāya dattāni na pitṝnnāpi 2 devatāḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. The havya and kavya should always be given to a Shrotriya Brahmana, because the giving of such offerings to non-Shrotriya Brahmanas does not reach the gods or the pitris.

## \|\| 1.4.117 \|\|

*yasya caiva gṛhe mūrkho dūre cāpi bahuśrutaḥ \|*  
*bahuśrutāya dātavyaṃ nāsti mūrkhavyatikramaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. A person in whose house there are the fool Brahmanas, he should also invite the well-known Brahmanas from a distance and give away the charities. By so doing, no disturbance is created and one should not think about the disgrace of a food.

## \|\| 1.4.118 \|\|

*brāhmaṇātikramo nāsti mūrkhe japavivarjite \|*  
*jvalantamagnimutsṛjya na hi bhasmani hūyate \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. There is no sin involved by neglecting a foolish Brahmana in any religious exercise in the same way as the offering is not made in the ashes leaving the burning flames.

## \|\| 1.4.119 \|\|

*na caitadeva manyante . pitaro devatāstathā \|*  
*saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ vāpi brāhmaṇaṃ daivataṃ param \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The gods and the pitris do not appreciate such type of donations. Irrespective of a Brahmana being virtuous or non-virtuous, he is treated to be the supreme god.

## \|\| 1.4.120 \|\|

*atikramanmahābāho rauravaṃ yāti bhārata \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. In the yajna or other religious ceremonies performed in a household, a Brahmana living in the house should not be neglected. O valorous one, a person who neglects such a Brahmana, he falls in the terrific hell.

## \|\| 1.4.121 \|\|

*gāyatrīmātrasāro'pi brāhmaṇaḥ pūjyatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*gṛhāsanno viśeṣeṇa na bhavetpatitastu saḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Even a Brahmana who simply knows Gayatri should be adorable. When he remains in the house, he is surely adorable.

## \|\| 1.4.122 \|\|

*dhānyaśūnyo yathā grāmo yathā kūpaśca nirjalaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaścānadhīyānastrayaste nāmadhārakāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. A village without the cereals, a dry well, a Brahmana without the knowledge of the Vedas - all the three are for name sake only.

## \|\| 1.4.123 \|\|

*yastvekapaṅktyāṃ viṣamaṃ dadāti snehādbhayādvā yadi vārthahetoḥ \|*  
*vedeṣu dṛṣṭamṛṣibhiśca gītaṃ tāṃ brahmahatyāṃ munayo vadanti \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. A person, who out of selfish motive or fear or out of affection, discriminate in the persons seated in one line, earns the sin of the killing of a Brahmana. This is the rule found in the Vedas. The Rishis and the Munis have made this arrangement.

## \|\| 1.4.124 \|\|

*ahiṃsayaiva bhūtānāṃ kāryaṃ śreyo'nuśāsanam \|*  
*vākcaiva madhurā ślakṣṇā prayojyā dharmamīpsatā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Those who are desirous of dharma should have the feeling of compassion and nonviolence for all the jivas and should use sweet and soft words for them.

## \|\| 1.4.125 \|\|

*yasya vāṅmanasī śuddhe satyagupte ca bhārata \|*  
*sa vai sarvamavāpnoti vedāntopagataṃ phalam \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. O Bharata, a person whose mind and speech is truthful and well controlled, he achieves all the fruits prescribed in Vedanta.

## \|\| 1.4.126 \|\|

*nāruntudaḥ syādārto'pi na paradrohakarmadhīḥ \|*  
*yayāsyo dvijate loko na tāṃ vācamudīrayet \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Even when aggrieved, one should not hurt the feelings of others and should not develop hatred for others. One should not speak such words, which agitate others.

## \|\| 1.4.127 \|\|

*yatkaroti śubhaṃ vācā 1 procyamānā manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ kuruśārdūla sadā cāpi tathocyatām \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. O lion of the Kuru race, those who complete the auspicious task speaking sweet words to the sacred people, one should listen and follow them.

## \|\| 1.4.128 \|\|

*na tathā śaśī na salilaṃ na candanaraso na śītalacchāyā \|*  
*prahlādayati ca puruṣaṃ yathā madhurabhāṣiṇī vāṇī \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. The moon, the water, sandal paste, the cool and comfortable shade, does not delight a person so much as the sweet words of a person.

## \|\| 1.4.129 \|\|

*arhaṇādbrāhmaṇo nityamudvijeta viṣādiva \|*  
*amṛtasyeva cākāṃkṣedapamānasya sarvadā \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. A Brahmana should keep himself away from honour and glory. He should aspect humiliation like the nectar.

## \|\| 1.4.130 \|\|

*sukhaṃ hyavamataḥ śete sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate \|*  
*sukhaṃ carati lokesminnavamantā vinaśyati \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Because the one who is humiliated, he sleeps with comfort, remains awake with comfort, and performs his duties with comfort. But a person who showers disgrace on others, gets destroyed in the world.

## \|\| 1.4.131 \|\|

*anena vidhinā rājansaṃskṛtātmā dvijaḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*gurau vasansecinuyādbrahmādhigamidaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. O king, in this way, a disciple getting purified gradually, should stay in the hermitage of the preceptor and collect tapas to achieve Brahman.

## \|\| 1.4.132 \|\|

*tapoviśeṣairvividhairvrataiśca vividhoditaiḥ \|*  
*vedaḥ kṛtsnodhigantavyaḥ sarahasyo dvijanmanā \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The people of the three varnas should study the Vedas performing various types of vratas and engage themselves in deep study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.4.133 \|\|

*vedamevābhyasennityaṃ tapastapyaṃ dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vedābhyāso hi viprasya tapaḥ paramihocyate \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. The excellent dvijas should always perform the tapas appropriately and engage themselves in the study of the Vedas. For a Brahmana in this world, the study of Vedas has been prescribed to be the best of tapas.

## \|\| 1.4.134 \|\|

*āhaiva sa nakhāgrebhyaḥ paramaṃ tapyate tapaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ supto'pi dvijo'dhīte svādhyāyaṃ śaktito'nvaham \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. A Brahmana, who according to his strength, daily devotes himself to the Vedas even in sleep, it amounts to his performing the tapas upto the nails of his body.

## \|\| 1.4.135 \|\|

*yo'nadhītya dvijo vedamanyatra kurute śramam \|*  
*sa jīvanneva śūdratvamāśu gacchati sānvayaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. A Brahmana who after the study of the Vedas takes up some attire profession, he, while being alive, achieves the status of a Shudra with his family.

## \|\| 1.4.136 \|\|

*na yasya vedo na japo na vidyāśca viśāmpate \|*  
*sa śūdra eva mantavya ityāha bhagavānvibhuḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. O king, a Brahmana who does not possess the Vedas, nor the japam or knowledge, he should be treated as Shudra. This has been ordained by the lord himself.

## \|\| 1.4.137 \|\|

*māturagre ca jananaṃ dvitīyo mauñjibandhanam \|*  
*tṛtīyo yajñadīkṣāyāṃ dvijasya vidhirīritaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The Brahmana takes his initial birth from the womb of his mother and the second birth is after the performing of the yajnopavita ceremony. He achieves the third birth after his initiation of the yajna.

## \|\| 1.4.138-139 \|\|

*tatra yadbrahma janmāsya mauñjībandhanacihnitam \|\| 138 \|\|*

*tatrāsya mātā sāvitrī pitā tvācārya ucyate \|*  
*vedapradānāttvācāryaṃ pitaraṃ manurabravīt \|\| 139 \|\|*
