138-139. During the yajnopavita ceremony, representing his birth being more important, when Savitri becomes his mother and the Acharya becomes his father. Manu has described Acharya to be father for him since he bestows the knowledge of the Vedas on his pupil.

## \|\| 1.4.140 \|\|

*na hyasya vidyate karma kiñcidāmauñjibandhanāt \|*  
*nābhivyāhārayedbrahama svadhāninayanādṛte 1 \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Before the thread ceremony, no activity has been prescribed for a Brahmana. Besides the Shraddha mantra, the Vedas should not be recited (in an usual) manner.

## \|\| 1.4.141 \|\|

*śūdreṇa tu samaṃ tāvadyāvadvede na jāyate \|*  
*kṛtopanayanasyāsya vratādeśanamiṣyate \|*  
*brahmaṇo grahaṇaṃ caiva krameṇa vidhipūrvakam \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. Unless a Brahmana achieves authority on the Vedas, he is to be treated like a Shudra. After the thread ceremony, he is authorized to perform the religious activities. Thereafter, the study of the Vedas should be started appropriately.

## \|\| 1.4.142 \|\|

*yatsūtraṃ cāpi yaccarma yā yā cāsya ca mekhalā \|*  
*vasanaṃ cāpi yo daṇḍastadvai tasya vrateṣvapi \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. The possession of a Brahmachari, viz. sutra, dharma, girdle, cloth and danda should be carried by him during the study of the Vedas as well.

## \|\| 1.4.143 \|\|

*sevetemāṃstu niyamānbrahmacārī gurau vasan \|*  
*sanniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ tapovṛddhyarthamātmanaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. A Brahmachari, while living with his preceptors, should observe all the rules. He should well control all his sense organs in order to increase his strength in the performing of the tapas.

## \|\| 1.4.144 \|\|

*vṛndārakarṣipitṝṇāṃ kuryāttarpaṇameva hi \|*  
*narāṇāṃ ca mahābāho nityaṃ snātvā prayatnataḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. O valorous one, after taking the bath properly, one should offer oblation always to the gods, rishis, manes as well as the humans.

## \|\| 1.4.145 \|\|

*puṣpaṃ toyaṃ phalaṃ cāpi samidādhānameva 3 ca \|*  
*nānāvidhāni kāṣṭhāni mṛttikāṃ ca tathā kuśān \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. One should collect the flowers, water, fruits, twigs, wood of different kinds, earth and kusha grass.

## \|\| 1.4.146 \|\|

*varjayenmadhu māṃsaṃ ca gandhamālyarathānstriyaḥ \|*  
*śuklāni caiva sarvāṇi prāṇināṃ 1 caiva hiṃsanam \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. During the period of observing Brahmacharya, the Brahmachari should discard meat, honey, sandal paste, rosary, vehicles, women, all types of white things as well as the killing of animals.

## \|\| 1.4.147-148 \|\|

*abhyaṅgamañjanaṃ cākṣṇorupānacchatradhāraṇam \|*  
*saṃkalpaṃ kāmajaṃ krodhaṃ lobhaṃ gītaṃ ca vādanam \|\| 147 \|\|*

*nartanaṃ ca tathā dyūtaṃ janavādaṃ tathānṛtam \|*  
*parivādaṃ cāpi vibho dūrataḥ parivarjayet \|\| 148 \|\|*

147-148. O excellent one, besides the above, the use of collyrium in the eyes, applying of paste over the body, use of footwear, umbrella, passionate feelings, anger, greed, singing and playing on musical instruments, dancing and gambling, speaking of falsehood and the denouncing of others, should also be discarded by a Brahmachari from a distance.

## \|\| 1.4.149 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ ca prekṣaṇālambo rapavītaṃ2 parasya ca \|*  
*puṃścalībhistathā saṅgaṃ na kuryātkurunandana \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. O son of Kuru race, a Brahmachari should not look passionately towards the women and should discard embracing of women or to do evil for others or keep company of a fallen women.

## \|\| 1.4.150 \|\|

*ekaḥ śayīta sarvatra na retaḥ skandayetkvacit \|*  
*kāmāddhi skandayanreto hinasti vratameva tu \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. He should always sleep alone at all the places, because the semen is not to be dropped. In case his semen falls due to passion, he destroys his own vrata by doing so.

## \|\| 1.4.151 \|\|

*suptaḥ kṣaranbrahmacārī dvijaḥ śukramakāmataḥ \|*  
*snātvārkamarcayitvā tu punarmāmityṛcaṃ japet \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. A Brahmachari, while sleeping, if drops the semen without the rising of passion, then he should adore the Sun after taking his bath, reciting the Red of Punarmam, thrice.

## \|\| 1.4.152 \|\|

*manorapi tathā cātra śrūyate paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*udakumbhaṃ sumanaso gośakṛnmṛttikāṃ kuśān \|*  
*āharedyāvadarthānhi bhaikṣaṃ cāpi hi nityaśaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. Manu has also prescribed in his valuable words, the duties of a Brahmachari. According to his words, a Brahmachari should daily collect water pots, flowers, cow-dung, earth, kusha etc. according to his strength and should live on begging.

## \|\| 1.4.153 \|\|

*gṛheṣu yeṣāṃ kartavyaṃ tāñchṛṇuṣva nṛpottama \|*  
*svakarmasu ratā ye vai tathā vedeṣu ye ratāḥ \|*  
*yajñeṣu cāpi rājendra ye ca śraddhāsamāśritāḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. O best of rulers, the houses from which the aims have to be collected daily have also been prescribed, which you please listen. O Rajendra, a Brahmachari should collect alms from the householders, who are devoted to their profession and believe in the Vedas, have a devoted mind and regularly perform the homas. A Brahmacharin should collect alms from the house of such people regularly.

## \|\| 1.4.154 \|\|

*brahmacāryā haredbhaikṣaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ prayato'nvaham \|*  
*guroḥ kule na bhikṣet svajñātikulabandhuṣu \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. He should beg alms from the abodes of the householders, controlling their mind and the sense organs. He should not collect alms from the house of his preceptor or his relatives.

## \|\| 1.4.155 \|\|

*alābhe tvanyagotrāṇāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*sarvaṃ cāpi caredgrāmaṃ pūrvoktānāmasambhave \|*  
*antyavarjaṃ mahābāho ityāha bhagavānvibhuḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. In case he does not get alms from anywhere, then leaving the aforesaid houses, he should collect alms from the other houses and get it from the last mentioned people. In case getting of alms become impossible from other places, then one should resort to begging from the entire village, leaving the houses of the Shudras. This has been ordained by the lord himself.

## \|\| 1.4.156 \|\|

*vācaṃ niyamya prayatastvagniṃ śastraṃ ca varjayet \|*  
*cāturvarṇyaṃ caredbhaikṣamalābhe kurunandana \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. A Brahmachari has not only to control, his mind as well as the sense organs, but has also; to control his speech. He should not make use of the fire as well weapons for his own; purpose or selfish motive. O son of Kuru race, in case it is totally impossible, then a Brahmachari should beg from the people of all: the classes.

## \|\| 1.4.157 \|\|

*ārādāhṛtya samidhaḥ. sannidadhyād gṛhopari \|*  
*sāyaṃprātastu juhuyāttābhiragnimatandritaḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. He should bring twigs from the far off forest and place them over his cottage. Shedding laziness, he should use these twigs during the morning as well as the evening for performing the homa.

## \|\| 1.4.158 \|\|

*bhaikṣācaraṇamakṛtvā na tamagniṃ samidhya vai \|*  
*anāturaḥ saptarātramavakīrṇivrataṃ caret \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. In case a Brahmachari does not perform homa during the morning and evening, he should^ perform repentance in a spread out manner.

## \|\| 1.4.159-160 \|\|

*vartanaṃ cāsya bhaikṣeṇa pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbhaikṣeṇa vai nityaṃ naikānnādī bhavedyatī \|\| 159 \|\|*

*bhaikṣeṇa vratino vṛttirupavāsasamā smṛtā \|*  
*daivatye vratavadrājanpitrye karmaṇyatharṣivat \|*  
*kāmamabhyarthito'śnīyādvratamasya na lupyate \|\| 160 \|\|*

159-160. A person who consumes food of a single person, cannot be called as a vrati. The food of a Brahmachari who lives on begging is comparable with the fasting. O monarch, one should conduct himself as a Rishi in the performing of the pitri ceremonies and like a vrati in the ceremonies of the gods. In case someone insists to take food, one should not hesitate to do so and by so doing his vrata is not wasted.

## \|\| 1.4.161 \|\|

*brāhmaṇasya mahābāho karma yatsamudāhṛtam \|*  
*rājanyavaiśyayornaitatpaṇḍitaiḥ kurunandana \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. O son of Kuru race, O valorous one! I have spoken the duties of a Brahmana Brahmachari. The learned Brahmanas have prescribed different procedures to be adopted by Kshatriya as well as the Vaishya Brahmacharis.

## \|\| 1.4.162 \|\|

*codito'codito 1 vāpi guruṇā nityameva hi \|*  
*kuryādadhyayane yogamācāryasya hiteṣu ca \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. Irrespective of the inspiration extended by the preceptor or otherwise, one should always devote his mind towards studies. The pupil should always think of the welfare of his preceptor as Well.

## \|\| 1.4.163 \|\|

*buddhīndriyāṇi manasā śarīraṃ vācameva hi \|*  
*niyamya prāñjalistiṣṭhedvīkṣamāṇo gurormukham \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. The disciple, controlling his mind, wisdom, sense organs, body and speech, should look at the face of the preceptor and should remain in attention with his hands folded.

## \|\| 1.4.164 \|\|

*nityamuddhṛtapāṇiḥ syātsādhvācārastu saṃyataḥ \|*  
*āsyatāmiti coktaḥ sannāsītābhimukhaṃ guroḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. The disciple should always keep his right arm out of the upper garment and should always conduct himself as a noble person. He should cover the body with the costumes properly. When he is asked to take his seat by the preceptor, he should do so facing him.

## \|\| 1.4.165 \|\|

*vastraveṣaistathānnaistu hīnaḥ syādgurusannidhau \|*  
*uttiṣṭhetprathamaṃ cāsya jaghanyaṃ cāpi saṃviśet \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. In the presence of the preceptor, a disciple should take simple food and should wear simple clothes. He should get up before the preceptor does so and should take his seat after his preceptor does so.

## \|\| 1.4.166 \|\|

*pratiśravaṇasambhāṣe talpastho na samācaret \|*  
*na cāsīno na bhuñjāno na tiṣṭhanna parāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. While listening to the discourse of the preceptor or during his speech, he should not make use of the bed. Similarly, while taking food in seated position or while standing or’ turning his face, a disciple should not talk to the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.4.167 \|\|

*āsīnasya sthitaḥ kuryādabhigacchaṃśca tiṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*pratyudgantā tu vrajataḥ paścāddhāvaṃśca dhāvataḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. When the preceptor is seated and the disciple wants to talk to him, he should do so while himself rising in a standing position. Ы case the preceptor is standing, the disciple then should receive instructions of the preceptor by walking a few steps and should then talk to’ him. On his arrival, he should present himself before him and receive his instructions.

## \|\| 1.4.168 \|\|

*parāṅmukhasyābhimukho dūrasthasyaitya cāntikam \|*  
*namaskṛtya śayānasya nideśe tiṣṭhetsarvadā \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. In case the preceptor is looking on the other side, then the disciple should present himself before him. In case he is standing at a distance, the disciple should himself go to him and himself start the talk. At the time of preceptor’s going to bed, the disciple should offer his salutation to him and should always obey his command.

## \|\| 1.4.169 \|\|

*nīcaṃ śayyāsanaṃ cāsya sarvadā gurusannidhau \|*  
*gurośca cakṣurviṣaye na yatheṣṭāsano bhavet \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. A disciple should place his bed close to that of the preceptor, at a lower level. Upto the distance to which the sight of the preceptor can reach, the disciple should not sit stretching his legs.

## \|\| 1.4.170 \|\|

*nāmoccāraṇamevāsya parokṣamapi suvrata \|*  
*na cainamanukurvīta gatibhāṣaṇaceṣṭitaiḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. O Suvrata, one should not speak out the name of the Guru even in an examination. One should not imitate the walking, speech and performance.

## \|\| 1.4.171 \|\|

*parīvādastathā nindā guroryatra pravartate \|*  
*karṇau tatra pidhātavyo gantavyaṃ vā tato'nyataḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. A disciple should leave the place where the preceptor is being denounced. Listening to the denouncing of the preceptor, one should shut his ears with both the bands and leave the place.

## \|\| 1.4.172 \|\|

*parīvādādrāsabhaḥ syātsārameyastu nindakaḥ \|*  
*paribhoktā kṛmirbhavati kīṭo bhavati matsarī \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. In case a person listens to the denouncement of the preceptor, he is reborn as a donkey while the one who denounces is reborn as a dog. Similarly, the one who consumes the food of the preceptor (stealthily) he is reborn as a worm. The one who displays arrogance before the preceptor, he is reborn as an insect.

## \|\| 1.4.173 \|\|

*dūrastho nārcayedenaṃ na kruddho nāntike striyāḥ \|*  
*yānāsanagato rājannavaruhyābhivādayet \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. The preceptor should not be adored from a distance. He should also not be adored in anger or among the women. O king, similarly, the preceptor should be adored after descending from the seat or the chariot.

## \|\| 1.4.174 \|\|

*pratikūle samāne tu nāsīta guruṇā saha \|*  
*aśṛṇvaṃti gurau rājanna kiñcidapi kīrtayet \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. A disciple should not disturb the preceptor when he is engaged in talking with others or is engaged in some other business or activity.

## \|\| 1.4.175 \|\|

*gośvoṣṭrayānaprāsādaprastareṣu kaṭeṣu ca \|*  
*āsīta guruṇā sārdhaṃ śilāphalaka nauṣu ca \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. One can sit with the preceptor in a bullock cart, camel cart, stone seat of a canopy, a mat, stone slab or in a boat.

## \|\| 1.4.176 \|\|

*gurorgurau sannihite guruvadvṛttimācaret \|*  
*guruputreṣu cāryeṣu guroścaiva svabandhuṣu \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. In case, the preceptor of the preceptor is alive, the disciple should extend the same respect to his grand preceptor as extending to his own guru.

## \|\| 1.4.177 \|\|

*bālaḥ samānajanmā vā viśiṣṭo yajñakarmaṇi \|*  
*adhyāpayangurusuto guruvanmānamarhati \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. In case the son of the preceptor be a child, or be of the same age as that of the disciple, even then a special treatment has to be extended to him. In case the son of the preceptor is engaged in teaching, then he is respectable as the preceptor himself.

## \|\| 1.4.178 \|\|

*utsādanamathāṅgānāṃ snāpanocchiṣṭabhojane \|*  
*pādayornejana rājanguruputreṣu varjayet \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. O king, (while behaving with the son of the preceptor), the activities like the application of paste over his body, giving him a bath, to serve the left over food and washing of the feet, should never be extended to him.

## \|\| 1.4.179 \|\|

*guruvatpratipūjyāstu savarṇā guruyoṣitaḥ \|*  
*asavarṇāstu sampūjyāḥ pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. In case the wife of the preceptor belongs to the same caste, then she is adorable like the preceptor himself. In case she does not belong to his own caste, then she should be welcomed by getting up.

## \|\| 1.4.180 \|\|

*abhyañjanaṃ sa snapanaṃ gātrotsādanameva ca \|*  
*gurupatnyā na kāryāṇi keśānāṃ ca prasādhanam \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. The preceptor should not indulge in the application of oil over the limbs of her body, pressing of her limbs, helping her in taking bath, application of the paste over the body, combing of hair and other such activities.

## \|\| 1.4.181-182 \|\|

*gurupatnīṃ tu yuvatīṃ nābhivādeta pādayoḥ \|*  
*pūrṇaviṃśativarṣeṇa guṇadoṣau vijānatā \|\| 181 \|\|*

*svabhāva eva nārīṇāṃ narāṇāmiha dūṣaṇam \|*  
*atorthānna pramādyanti pratipādya vipaścitaḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

181-182. In case the wife of the preceptor be youthful, then the disciple of twenty years of age, being aware of the merits and demerits of the world, should not welcome her or touching her feet, because there is evil in the natural tendency of a man and a woman on earth. A person who is quite prudent and wise, he does not become careless towards the women.

## \|\| 1.4.183 \|\|

*avidvāṃsamalaṃ loke vidvāṃsamapi vā punaḥ \|*  
*pramadā hyutpathaṃ netuṃ kāmakrodhavaśānugam \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. The women getting overpowered with the lust and anger, are competent enough to lead a learned person or a fool to the evil path.

## \|\| 1.4.184 \|\|

*mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā na viviktāsano bhavet \|*  
*balavānindriyagrāmo vidvāṃsamapi karṣati \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. One should not sit in seclusion with his own mother, sister or a daughter, because the sense organs are quite powerful and can drag immensely learned people towards themselves.

## \|\| 1.4.185 \|\|

*rājendra gurupatnīnāṃ yuvatīnāṃ yuvā bhuvi \|*  
*vidhivadvandanaṃ kuryādasāvahamiti bruvan \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Therefore, the youthful disciples on the earth, should keep themselves away from the youthful wives of the preceptors. They should offer salutation to them speaking out their names.

## \|\| 1.4.186 \|\|

*vipro'sya pādagrahaṇamanvahaṃ cābhivādanam \|*  
*gurudāreṣu kurvīta satāṃ dharmamanusmaran \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. After his return from the foreign land, the disciples, recalling the dharma initiated by the noble people, should touch the feet of preceptor’s wife, welcoming her.

## \|\| 1.4.187 \|\|

*yathā khanankhanitreṇa jalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*tathā gurugatāṃ vidyāṃ śuśrūṣuradhigacchati \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. As a person digging constantly with a pick axe ultimately reaches the water of the ground, similarly, a disciple, who is engaged in the service of a preceptor, achieves all the knowledge or lores of the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.4.188 \|\|

*muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā syādatha vā syācchikhī jaṭī \|*  
*nainaṃ grāme'bhinimlocedarko nābhyudiyātkvacit \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. Irrespective of a Brahmachari being with a shaven head or the locks of hair over the head, he, while his stay in a village, should not observe the rising and setting of the sun.

## \|\| 1.4.189 \|\|

*taṃ cedabhyudiyātsūryaḥ śayānaṃ kāmakārataḥ \|*  
*nimlocedvāpyabhijñānājjapannupavaseddinam \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. Inspite of being aware of this rule, in case the sun rises or sets or rises while he is asleep, then he should keep a fast for the whole day performing japam at the same time.

## \|\| 1.4.190 \|\|

*sūryeṇa hyabhinirmuktaḥ śayānobhyuditaśca yaḥ \|*  
*prāyaścittamakurvāṇo yuktaḥ syānmahatainasā \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. A Brahmachari who does not perform repentance as detailed above, sleeping at sun rise or sun set, he attract the grave sin.

## \|\| 1.4.191 \|\|

*upaspṛśya mahārāja ubhe sandhye samāhitaḥ \|*  
*śucau deśe japañjapyamupāsīta yathāvidhi \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. O great ruler, with a peaceful mind, in the morning as well as in the evening, seated at an auspicious place, one should appropriately perform sipping and should resort to adoration and japam.

## \|\| 1.4.192 \|\|

*yadi strī yadyavarajaḥ śreyaḥ kiñcitsamācaret \|*  
*tatsarvamācaredyukto yatra vā ramate manaḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. In case the auspicious ceremonies are performed by women or the Shudra, then one should perform these ceremonies himself or one should engage himself to the task well suited to his temperament.

## \|\| 1.4.193 \|\|

*dharmārthāvucyate śreyaḥ kāmārthau dharmameva ca \|*  
*artha eveha vā śreyastrivarga iti saṃsthitiḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

193\. Some people prefer dharma as well artha, while others kama and artha. While still others on the earth, prefer artha alone. All the three are called Trivarga or three human pursuits.

## \|\| 1.4.194 \|\|

*pitā mātā tathā bhrātā ācāryāḥ kurunandana \|*  
*nārtenāpyavamantavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. O son of the race of Kuru, the father, the mother, the brother and Acharya should not be disgraced even in the worst circumstances. This rule should be followed by the Brahmanas particularly.

## \|\| 1.4.195 \|\|

*ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*mātāpyathāditermūrtirbhrātā syānmūrtirātmanaḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Acharya is the form of Brahma, the father represents the image of Prajapati, while mother stand for Aditi and the brother is of one’s own form.

## \|\| 1.4.196 \|\|

*yanmātā pitarau kleśaṃ sahete sambhave nṛṇām \|*  
*na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. The pains which the parents have to bear at the birth of a child, one cannot repay its reward in hundreds of years.

## \|\| 1.4.197 \|\|

*tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryādācāryasya ca bhārata \|*  
*teṣu hi triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ sarvaṃ samāpyate \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. O Bharata, therefore, a person should work for his welfare as well as the teacher or Acharya. By pleasing all the three, all the problems get automatically solved.

## \|\| 1.4.198 \|\|

*teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate \|*  
*na tairanabhyanujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācaret \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. By serving all the three, it amounts to the performing of the great tap as. Without there permission, no other dharma should be patronised.

## \|\| 1.4.199 \|\|

*ta eva ca trayo vedāsta evoktāstrayo'gnayaḥ \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. All the three of them, represent the three lokas, the three Vedas, three ashramas and the three fires.

## \|\| 1.4.200 \|\|

*mātā vai gārhapatyāgniḥ pitā vai dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*gururāhavanīyaśca sāgnitretā garīyasī \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. The mother represents the household fire, the father represents the southern fire, while the Acharya represents the fire which is invoked. All the three fires are of extremely glorious types.

## \|\| 1.4.201 \|\|

*triṣu tuṣṭeṣu caiteṣu trīṃllokāñjayate gṛhī \|*  
*dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā devavaddivi modate \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. In case a householder is able to please three fires, then he can conquer the three worlds. He, possessing the divine glory of his body, enjoys all the comforts in the heaven resembling the gods.

## \|\| 1.4.202 \|\|

*imaṃ lokaṃ pitṛbhaktyā mātṛbhaktyā tu madhyamam \|*  
*guruśuśrūṣayā caiva gacchecchakrasalokatām \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. By adoring one’s own father, one achieves Pitriloka, Madhyaloka by adoring the mother, while the devotion towards a preceptor leads one to Indraloka.

## \|\| 1.4.203 \|\|

*sarve tenādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ \|*  
*anādṛtāstu yenaite sarvāstasyāphalāḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. A person who has respected these three, he has respected all the dharmas and the one who disgraces these three, all his activities become fruitless.

## \|\| 1.4.204 \|\|

*yāvattrayaste jīveyustāvannānyatsamācaret \|*  
*teṣveva nityaṃ śuśrūṣāṃ kuryātpriyahite rataḥ \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. Till such time these three remain alive, one should not follow any other dharma and should engage himself into the activities which please them. Getting engaged in the welfare activities, a person should serve his parents and the preceptor.

## \|\| 1.4.205 \|\|

*teṣāmanuparodhena pārthakyaṃ 2 yadyadācaret \|*  
*tattannivedayettebhyo manovacanakarmabhiḥ \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. In case when a person has to perform something with their permission, even then, one should keep them informed of all the activities performed by him by his action, thought and behaviour.

## \|\| 1.4.206 \|\|

*triṣveteṣviti kṛtyaṃ hi puruṣasya samāpyate \|*  
*eṣa dharmaḥ paraḥ sākṣādupadharmo'nya ucyate \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. All the duties, activities and responsibilities of these three are the same. This is known as dharma and besides them all others are of lower grade.

## \|\| 1.4.207 \|\|

*śraddhadhānaḥ śubhāṃ vidyāmādadītāvarādapi \|*  
*antyādapi paraṃ dharmaṃ strīratnaṃ duṣkulādapi \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. The lore speaking to welfare, should be received gracefully even from a person of a low caste, with devotion. Even if a Shudra possesses an excellent knowledge, one should receive it as well. Similarly, the gem of a woman should be accepted from the family of the wicked people.

## \|\| 1.4.208 \|\|

*viṣādapyamṛtaṃ grāhyaṃ bālādapi subhāṣitam \|*  
*amitrādapi sadvṛttamamedhyādapi kāñcanam \|\| 208 \|\|*

208\. The nectar should be extracted even from the person. The truthful and decent words spoken even by a child should be accepted. Thus the words of welfare should also be learnt even from an enemy, while the gold can be picked up from a dirty place.

## \|\| 1.4.209 \|\|

*striyo ratnaṃ nayo vidyā dharmaḥ śaucaṃ subhāṣitam \|*  
*vividhāni ca śilpāni samādeyāni sarvaśaḥ \|\| 209 \|\|*

209\. A noble lady, precious gem, good policy, precious lore, auspiciousness, dharma, eloquent words, and various types of arts should be accepted from the even places.

## \|\| 1.4.210 \|\|

*abrāhmaṇādadhyayanamāpatkāle vidhīyate \|*  
*anuvrajyā ca śuśrūṣā yāvadadhyayanaṃ guroḥ \|\| 210 \|\|*

210\. It has been provided that one should receive education even from the non Brahmanas. When a person receive education from a non-Brahmana, he should serve him as well.

## \|\| 1.4.211 \|\|

*nābrāhmaṇe gurau śiṣyo vāsamātyantikaṃ vaset \|*  
*brāhmaṇe cānanūcāne kāñkṣangatimanuttamām \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. ## \|\| 1.4.213-214 \|\|

## \|\| 1.4.218 \|\|

52\. O group of Brahmanas, the women who have tender nails without any holes over beautiful fingers, such women enjoy enormous riches. To the contrary, the women who have uneven, dry or shattered hands, they are quarrelsome and suffer during the life.

## \|\| 1.5.53 \|\|

*samarekhā yavā yāsāṅguṣṭhāṅguliparvasu \|*  
*tāsāṃ hi vipulaṃ saukhyaṃ dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā'kṣayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The ladies who have parallel lines besides the line in the thumb of the type of barley, such ladies enjoy enormous pleasures, riches and cereals.

## \|\| 1.5.54 \|\|

*maṇibandho'vyavacchinno rekhātrayavibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*dadāti na cirādeva bhogamāyustathākṣayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A lady whose wrist is decorated with three long lines thereon, she enjoys the everlasting bliss, riches, fortunes and long life.

## \|\| 1.5.55-56 \|\|

*śrīvatsadhvajapadmākṣagajavājiniveśanaiḥ \|*  
*cakrasvastikavajrāsipūrṇakumbhanibhāṅkuśaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*prāsādacchatramukuṭairhārakeyūrakuṇḍalaiḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhatoraṇanirvyūhairhastanyastairnṛpastriyaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. The ladies possessing the symbols of Shrivatsa, flag, lotus, eye or a rosary, elephant, horse, palace, cakra or wheel, Svastika, vajra, sword, pitcher of water, royal palace, umbrella, crown, garland, bracelet, ear-ring, conch, arched gateway and vyuha, such ladies become the queens of the kings.

## \|\| 1.5.57 \|\|

*yasyāḥ pāṇitale raktā yūpakumbhāśca kuṇḍikāḥ \|*  
*dṛśyante caraṇe yasyā yajñapalī bhavatyasau \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A woman in whose hand there is red pillar, a pitcher or a pot in the soles of the feet, such a woman becomes the wife of the performer of yajna.

## \|\| 1.5.58 \|\|

*vīthyāpaṇatulāmānaistathā mudrādibhiḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*bhavanti vaṇijāṃ patnyo ratnakāñcanaśālinām \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The ladies who have the marks of streets, market, a balance and coins embossed in their hands, they become the wives of the wealth traders or goldsmiths.

## \|\| 1.5.59 \|\|

*dātrayoktrayugābandhaphalolūkhalalāṅgalaiḥ \|*  
*bhavanti dhanadhānyāḍhyā kṛṣīvalajanāṅganāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The weapon for cutting, the rope of yoke, yoke, ploughshare, mortar and plough are the symbols on the bodies of the women, who usually become the wives of farmers.

## \|\| 1.5.60 \|\|

*anunnataśirāsandhi pīnaṃ romavivarjitam \|*  
*gopucchākṛti nārīṇāṃ bhujayoryugulaṃ śubham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The arms of the women which are without knots and not much fleshy, developed and without the hair and resemble the cow’s tail are quite beneficial for the ladies.

## \|\| 1.5.61 \|\|

*nigūḍhagranthayo yasyāḥ kūrparau romavarjitau \|*  
*bāhū vai lalitau yasyāḥ praśastau vṛttakomalau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A woman, knot of whose elbow is fleshy, without the hair, besides being round, charming and soft arms, such woman is quite praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.5.62 \|\|

*unnatāvanatau caiva nātisthūlau na romaśau \|*  
*sukhadau tu sadā strīṇāṃ saubhāgyārogyavardhanau \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. When the arms of a woman are developed at appropriate points and unraised, free from fatness and hair, they are indicative of fortunes and add to the good health besides being always comfortable.

## \|\| 1.5.63 \|\|

*sthūle skandhe vahedbhāraṃ romaśe vyādhitā bhavet \|*  
*vakraskandhe bhavedvandhyā kulaṭā connatānane \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. When both the shoulders of a woman are quite thick, she serves as the carrier of the load. A woman having hair over the shoulders attracts ailments. The one with the curved shoulders is found to be barren, and the woman with bent shoulders is an unchaste woman.

## \|\| 1.5.64 \|\|

*spaṣṭaṃ rekhātrayaṃ yasyā grīvāyāṃ caturaṅgulam \|*  
*maṇikāñcanamuktāḍhyaṃ sā dadhāti vibhūṣaṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. A woman having three clear lines of four finger’s length over the neck, wears the gem studded gold ornaments.

## \|\| 1.5.65 \|\|

*adhanā strī kṛśagrīvā dīrghagrīvā ca . bandhakī \|*  
*hasvagrīvā mṛtāpatyā sthūlagrīvā ca duḥkhitā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. A woman who has a thin neck, she remains poor. A woman with a long neck is a harlot. A woman with a small neck cannot have children. Similarly, a woman with a thick neck suffers always.

## \|\| 1.5.66 \|\|

*anunnatā samāṃsā ca samā yasyāḥ kṛkāṭikā \|*  
*sudīrghamāyustvasyāstu ciraṃ bhartā ca jīvati \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A woman, whose upper portion of the vertebral column reaching the neck is not found raised besides being fleshy and leveled, she enjoys long life and her husband too has a long life.

## \|\| 1.5.67 \|\|

*nirmāṃsā bahumāṃsā ca śirālā romaśā tathā \|*  
*kuṭilā vikaṭā caiva vistīrṇā na ca śasyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. In case the said knot is fleshy or without much of flesh and covered with the veins and hair, besides being curved and vast, it is not considered to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.5.68 \|\|

*na sthūlo na kṛśo'tyarthaṃ na vakro na ca romaśaḥ \|*  
*hanurevaṃvidhaḥ śreyāṃstato'nyo na praśasyate \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. When the chin of a woman is neither thick nor thin or curved and without facial hair, such a chin is quite fortunate for the ladies. In case the chin has contrary symptoms, it is not considered to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.5.69 \|\|

*caturasramukhī dhūrtā maṇḍalāsyā śivā 1 bhavet \|*  
*aprajā vājivakrā strī mahāvakrā ca durbhagā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The woman with a square face is of a cunning nature. A woman with round face bestows welfare. A woman with her face resembling a horse has no children (or remains barren), while the one with long face has misfortune to her credit.

## \|\| 1.5.70 \|\|

*śvavarāhavṛkolūkamarkaṭāsyāśca yāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*kūrāstāḥ pāpakarmiṇyaḥ prajābāndhavavarjitāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Similarly, the women having the faces resembling a dog, a pig, a wolf, owl and monkey are of cruel temperament, besides being devoid of children and other relatives.

## \|\| 1.5.71 \|\|

*mālatībakulāmbhojanīlotpalasugandhi yat \|*  
*vadanaṃ mucyate naitatpānatāmbūlabhojanaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The women whose bodies issue the fragrance of jasmine, bakula (mimusops elengi) red lotus, blue lotus, flowers, get enough of best of herbs, drinks and tasteful betels.

## \|\| 1.5.72 \|\|

*tāmrābhaḥ kiñcidālambhaḥ sthaulyakārśyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*adharo yadi tuṅgaśca nārīṇāṃ bhojadaḥ sadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. When the lips of the women are thick, raised upwards, have reddish colour, stiff and without thinness, such women enjoy comforts always.

## \|\| 1.5.73 \|\|

*sthūle kalahaśīlā syādvivarṇe cātiduḥkhitā \|*  
*uttaroṣṭhena tīkṣṇena vanitā cātikopanā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The ladies with stiff lips are always quarrelsome. Those with discoloured lips are unfortunate and suffer always. In case the upper lip of a woman is very thin, she is always of an angry nature.

## \|\| 1.5.74 \|\|

*jihvā tanutarā vakrā tāmrā dīrghā ca śasyate \|*  
*sthūlā hrasvā vivarṇā yā vakrā bhinnā ca ninditā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. When the tongue of a woman is quite thin, curved, long and of reddish colour, it is treated to be praiseworthy for the females. To the contrary, in case the tongue is thick, small, discoloured, curved and looks as if separate one, has not been considered to be praiseworthy for the women.

## \|\| 1.5.75 \|\|

*śaṅkhakundendudhavalaṃ snigdhaistuṅgairasandhibhiḥ \|*  
*miṣṭānnapānamāpnoti dantairebhiranunnataiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. When the teeth of the women are white like the conch, kunda flowers or the moon, besides being glossy, raised without cavity, well developed, such women enjoy tasteful beverages, besides sweets.

## \|\| 1.5.76 \|\|

*sūkṣmairatikṛśairhrasvaiḥ sphuṭitairviralaistathā \|*  
*rūkṣaśca duḥkhitā nityaṃ vikaṭairbhāminī bhavet \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. To the contrary, in case their teeth are too small, weak, cracking, loose, intricate, such women always suffer in their life.

## \|\| 1.5.77 \|\|

*sumṛṣṭadarpaṇāmbhojapūrṇabimbendusannibham \|*  
*vadanaṃ varanārīṇāmabhīṣṭaphaladaṃ smṛtam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. When the face of a woman is quite beautiful, charming, resembling a mirror, lotus full moon and attractive, she enjoys all the pleasures in her life.

## \|\| 1.5.78 \|\|

*na sthūlā na kṛśā vakrā nātidīrghā samunnatā \|*  
*īdṛśī nāsikā yasyāḥ sā dhanyā tu śubhaṅkarī \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. When the nose of a woman is neither two small, nor too big or thick, besides being well developed, such a lady is considered to be quite graceful.

## \|\| 1.5.79 \|\|

*unnatā mṛdulā yā ca rekhā śuddhā na saṅgantā \|*  
*bhrūrvakratulyā sūkṣmā ca yoṣitāṃ sā sukhāvahā \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The raised, tender and auspicious eye brows, appearing like the drawn lines, bestow all types of comforts to the ladies.

## \|\| 1.5.80 \|\|

*1 dhanustulyābhiḥ saubhāgyaṃ vandhyā syāddīrgharomabhiḥ \|*  
*piṅgalāsaṅgatā hrasvā dāridryāya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The eye brows which are curved like a bow bestow fortunes. The eye brows with long line of hair, reveal the barrenness of the women. Similarly, the eyebrows of tawny colour, which are disarranged or of small in size, are indicative of sure poverty.

## \|\| 1.5.81 \|\|

*nīlotpaladalaprakhyairātāmraiścārupakṣmabhiḥ \|*  
*vanitā nayanairebhirbhogasaubhāgyabhāginī \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The women with pleasant eyebrows resembling the blue lotus flowers, somewhat reddish in appearance and pleasant eyes, enjoy great pleasures besides the riches.

## \|\| 1.5.82 \|\|

*khañjanākṣī mṛgākṣī ca varāhākṣī varāṅganā \|*  
*yatrayatra samutpannā mahāntaṃ bhogamaśnute \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The beautiful woman, having the eyes resembling the wagtail, deer or pig having been born here and there, enjoy all the pleasures.

## \|\| 1.5.83 \|\|

*agambhīrairasaṃśliṣṭairbahurekhāvibhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*rājapantyo bhavantīha nayanairmadhupiṅgalaiḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The women with eyes devoid of seriousness, unmixed up eyes, decorated with many lines, having red complexion resembling the honey, enjoy the position of queens in this world.

## \|\| 1.5.84 \|\|

*vāyasākṛtinetrāṇi dīrghāpāṅgāni yoṣitām \|*  
*anāvilāni cārūṇi bhavanti hi vibhūtaye \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The ladies having the long eyes resembling those of the crows, are indicative of their wealth and riches.

## \|\| 1.5.85 \|\|

*gambhīraiḥ piṅgalaiścaiva duḥkhitāḥ syuścirāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*vayomadhye tyajetprāṇānunnatākṣī tu2 yāṅganā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The women having the dark yellow eyes enjoy long life, but have to face misery. The women having the developed eyes, they meet with their death, when quite young.

## \|\| 1.5.86 \|\|

*raktākṣī viṣamākṣī ca 3 dhūmrākṣī pretalocanā \|*  
*varjanīyā sadā nārī śvanetrā caiva dūrataḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. A woman with red, uneven, dusty eyes resembling the goblins, have always to be discarded. Similarly, a woman, having the eyes resembling those of a dog, should be discarded from a distance.

## \|\| 1.5.87 \|\|

*udbhrāntakaiḥ karaiścitrairnayanastvaṃganāstviha \|*  
*madyamāṃsapriyā nityaṃ capalāścaiva sarvataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Then women with wavering eyes, or the eyes with surprising colours, like the meat and drinks, they remain unstable always.

## \|\| 1.5.88 \|\|

*karālākṛtayaḥ karṇā nabhaḥśabdāstu saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*vahanti vikasatkāntiṃ hemaratnavibhūṣaṇam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The women having lofty and long ears, earn pleasant glory with beautiful ear-rings.

## \|\| 1.5.89 \|\|

*kharoṣṭranakulolūkakapilaśravaṇāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvanti mahadduḥkhaṃ prāyaśaḥ pravrajanti ca \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The women having the ears resembling those of a donkey, camel, mongoose and owl, with white colour, have to suffer enormously. They usually wander here and there.

## \|\| 1.5.90 \|\|

*īṣadāpāṇḍugaṇḍā yā suvṛttā parvaṇi tviha \|*  
*praśastā ninditā tvanyā romakūpakadūṣitā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The round cheeks of pale yellow colour, have been considered as praiseworthy. On the contrary, the cheeks with hair and deep hair pits are termed as degraded ones.

## \|\| 1.5.91 \|\|

*ardhendupratimābhogamaroma tu samāhitama \|*  
*bhogārogyakaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ lalāṭaṃ varayoṣitām \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The crescent like forehead of a woman, which is free from the hair, is indicative of her healthy body, which increases the enjoyment of pleasures.

## \|\| 1.5.92 \|\|

*dviguṇaṃ pariṇāhena lalāṭaṃ vihitaṃ ca yat \|*  
*śiraḥ praśastaṃ nārīṇāmadhanyā hastimastakā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The type of the forehead that has been described, the head for such woman has been believed to be doubly praiseworthy. A woman having a head resembling that of an elephant is not considered to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.5.93 \|\|

*sūkṣmāḥ kṛṣṇā mṛdusnigdhāḥ kuñjitāgrāḥ śiroruhāḥ \|*  
*bhavanti śreyase strīṇāmanye syuḥ kleśaśokadāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The curly, thin or subtle, tender, slipper, curly in the front and in the head are meant for the welfare of the ladies. The hair to the contrary are considered to bestow grief and sufferings.

## \|\| 1.5.94 \|\|

*haṃsakokilavīṇāliśikhiveṇusvarāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvanti bahūnbhogānbhṛtyānājñāpayanti ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The women having their sound or voice resembling the swan, cuckoo, vina, wasp, peacock and venu, enjoy enormous pleasures and wealth. They exercise their control over servants.

## \|\| 1.5.95 \|\|

*bhinnakāṃsyasvarā nārī kharakākasvarā ca yā \|*  
*rogaṃ vyādhiṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ dāridryaṃ cādhigacchati \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. A woman, whose voice resembles that of the broken vase of bell metal, or that of a donkey or a crow, she has to face disease, grief, danger and poverty.

## \|\| 1.5.96 \|\|

*haṃsagovṛṣacakrāhvamattamātaṅgagāminī \|*  
*svakulaṃ dyotayennārī mahiṣī pārthivasya ca \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. A woman who walks like a swan, a cow, a bull, ruddy-goose or an intoxicated elephant, she illuminates her race and becomes a queen of a king.

## \|\| 1.5.97 \|\|

*śvaśṛgālagatirnindyā yā ca vāyasavadvrajet \|*  
*dāsī mṛgagatirnārī drutagāmī ca bandhakī \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. A woman who walks like a jackal or a dog, is denounced. Similarly, a woman who walks like a crow is also deplorable. A woman who moves like a deer, becomes the slave of others. While the one who walks swiftly, becomes a fallen woman.

## \|\| 1.5.98 \|\|

*phalinī rocanā hemakuṅkumaprabha eva ca \|*  
*varṇaḥ śubhakaraḥ strīṇāṃ yaśca dūrvāṅkuropamaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. When a woman has the colour of body resembling the turmeric, gorochana, saffron, gold or champa flower, it is considered beneficial for her.

## \|\| 1.5.99 \|\|

*mṛdūni mṛduromāṇi nātyantasvedakāni ca \|*  
*surabhīṇi ca gātrāṇi yāsāṃ tāḥ pūjitāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Similarly, the colour like the tender shorts of durva grass is also considered beneficial for the ladies. Such of the ladies who have the soft and tender hair, which does not sweat profusely, gets adorable.

## \|\| 1.5.100 \|\|

*nodvahetkapilāṃ kanyāṃ nādhikāṅgīṃ na rogiṇīm \|*  
*nālomikāṃ nātihrasvāṃ na vācāṭāṃ na piṅgalām \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. A girl with brown colour, should not be married. Similarly, the ailing girl, having excessive limbs, devoid of hair, dwarfish, talkative and a girl of tawny or yellow colour, should not be married.

## \|\| 1.5.101 \|\|

*narkṣavṛkṣanadīnāmnīṃ nāntyaparvatanāmikām \|*  
*na pakṣyahipreṣyanāmnīṃ na ca bhīṣaṇanāmikām \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The girls whose names are based on the names of the rivers, trees, constellations, mountains, birds, serpents, slaves or those, whose names reflect the names of slaves, or the horrible names, should not be married by a person.

## \|\| 1.5.102 \|\|

*avyaṅgāṅgīṃ saumyanāmnīṃ haṃsavāraṇagāminīm \|*  
*tanulomakeśadaśanāṃ mṛdaṅgīmudvahetstriyam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. A girl with pleasant limbs of the body, with beautiful name and who walks like a swan or an elephant, the one having subtle hair, subtle teeth, having soft limbs, should be married.

## \|\| 1.5.103 \|\|

*mahāntyapi samṛddhāni gojāvidhanadhānyataḥ \|*  
*strīsambandhe daśaitāni kulāni parivarjayet \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Inspite of a woman belonging to rich family, with enormous fortunes, with plenty of cows, goats, sheep, milking animals in abundance, but still the women of the races (as detailed below) should be discarded.

## \|\| 1.5.104 \|\|

*hīnakriyaṃ niṣpuruṣaṃ niśchandoromaśārśasam \|*  
*kṣayāmayāvyapasmāriśvitrakuṣṭhikulāni ca \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The women belonging to the families who are inactive, devoid of prowess, devoid of the study of the Vedas, having enough of hair over the body, suffering from the ailment of piles, consumption, epilepsy, always suffering from one ailment or the other, white spots, leprosy, should not be married.

## \|\| 1.5.105 \|\|

*pādau sugulphau prathamaṃ pratiṣṭhau jaṅghe dvitīyaṃ ca sujānucakre \|*  
*meḍhroruguhyaṃ ca tatastṛtīyaṃ nābhiḥ kaṭiśceti caturthamāhuḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Both the feet and the colour of the woman are considered to be praiseworthy. Thereafter, the sacred place is for the thighs, and knees are also praiseworthy. Then comes the pelvic region, rectum etc., the waist, the pelvic region and the navel have the fourth place.

## \|\| 1.5.106 \|\|

*udaraṃ kathayanti pañcamaṃ hṛdayaṃ ṣaṣṭhamatha stanānvitam \|*  
*atha saptamamaṃsajatruṇī kathayantyaṣṭamamoṣṭhakandhare \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. The belly has the fifth place in beauty. The breast with heart have the sixth place. The shoulders and their joints have the seventh place in beauty. Both the lips have the eighth place in beauty.

## \|\| 1.5.107 \|\|

*navamaṃ nayane ca sabhruṇī salalāṭaṃ daśamaṃ śirastathā \|*  
*aśubheṣvaśubhaṃ daśāphalaṃ caraṇaṃ caraṇādyaśubheṣu śobhanam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. The beautiful eyebrows with charming eyes have the ninth place, while the tenth place goes to the beautiful head as well as the forehead. When the limbs are like the feet and others one has to face the auspicious reward and when they are inauspicious, one has to face the evil reward.

## \|\| 1.5.108 \|\|

*idaṃ mahātmā sa mahānubhāvaḥ śacīnimittaṃ gururabravīddvijāḥ \|*  
*śakreṇa pṛṣṭaḥ saviśeṣamuttamaṃ saṃlakṣyamuktaṃ varayoṣalakṣaṇam 1 \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. O Brahmanas, when Indra asked the glorious Brihaspati about the auspicious symbols of the women, in relation to Shachi, all the symptoms of the ladies were specifically told by the former to the latter.

## \|\| 1.5.109 \|\|

*matsakāśātpunaḥ śrutvā lakṣaṇaṃ puruṣasya ca \|*  
*yathādhunā bhavadbhistu śrutaṃ matto dvijottamāḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. O Brahmanas, as you have heard about the auspicious or inauspicious symbols of the women, similarly, you acquaint yourself about the good or bad symbols of men, on listening them from me.

## \|\| 1.5.110 \|\|

*lakṣaṇebhyaḥ praśastaṃ tu strīṇāṃ sadvṛttamucyate \|*  
*sadvṛttamuktvā yā strī sā praśastā na ca lakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The auspicious and inauspicious symbols of the ladies have been discussed by me earlier. But more than that, I have emphasized about the noble character of the ladies. In case a woman with noble symptoms is deprived of nobility, then she is not at all praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.5.111 \|\|

*īdṛglakṣaṇasampannāṃ sukanyāmudvahettu yaḥ \|*  
*ṛddhirvṛddhistathā kīrtistatra tiṣṭhati nityaśaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. A person who marries a girl with the noble symptoms as stated above, his household always remains filled with prosperity, wealth and glory.

## Chapter 6. Development of relationship with people of higher or lower status

## \|\| 1.6.1 \|\|

*śatānīkauvāca \|*  
*sadvṛttaṃ śrotumicchāmi devastrīṇāṃ suvistarāt \|*  
*uttamādhamamadhyaṃ ca sambandhe strīkṛte yathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O great sage, I would now like to learn about the divine women and their righteousness in detail. I would like to know about the women who are graded in the first, second and third place or the best, middle ones and the degraded ones.

## \|\| 1.6.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śatānīka mahābāho brahmaloke pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*uktvā sa lakṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ sadvṛttaṃ coktavānpunaḥ 1 \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O valorous Shatanika! After narrating the symptoms of the women, the father of the Brahmaloka again spoke on the characteristics or righteousness of the women.

## \|\| 1.6.3 \|\|

*yathoktaṃ brahmaṇāṃ teṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ kurunandana \|*  
*sa preyo vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā vacanamabravīt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O son of the race of Kuru, as had been stated to the Brahmanas and Rishis about the righteousness of the women, listening to those words of welfare, Brahma said.

## \|\| 1.6.4 \|\|

*śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijaśārdūlāḥ strīṇāṃ sadvṛttamāditaḥ \|*  
*vakṣye yuṣmānaśeṣaṃ vai lokānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O best of the lion among the Brahmanas, you listen from me, about the righteousness of the ladies from the beginning. I am revealing the behaviour of righteousness of all the women.

## \|\| 1.6.5 \|\|

*trivargaprāptaye vakṣye strīvṛttaṃ gṛhamedhinām \|*  
*prāgvidyādīnupādāya tairarthāṃśca yathākramam \|*  
*vindeta sadṛśīṃ bhāryāṃ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I am going to reveal the conduct of righteousness among the women, so that a householder could become aware of the auspicious religious activities. The first duty of a person is to achieve Vidya (lore) and making use of the same to earn riches, as ordained in the scriptures. Then he should marry a girl who is quite well suited for him.

## \|\| 1.6.6 \|\|

*gṛhāśramo hi niḥsvānāṃ mahatyeṣā viḍambanā \|*  
*tasmātpūrvamupādeyaṃ vittameva gṛhaiṣiṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. For poor people also, the household is a huge obstruction and a mockery, besides being painful. Therefore, a person desirous of entering the life of a householder, should initially earn riches.

## \|\| 1.6.7 \|\|

*varaṃ soḍhā manuṣyeṇa tīvrā narakavedanā \|*  
*na tveva ca gṛhe dṛṣṭaṃ putradārakṣudhārditam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It would be better for a person to bear the acute dramatic pain, but it would not be proper for him to witness the hungry wife and children in his house.

## \|\| 1.6.8 \|\|

*asambhave śiśuṃ dṛṣṭvā rudantaṃ prārthanāparam \|*  
*vajrasāramayaṃ manye hadayaṃ yanna dīryate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In case a child cries having been unable to get his requirement and in such a situation if the heart of a householder does not break, then it appears that the heart had been made of vajra.

## \|\| 1.6.9 \|\|

*sādhvīṃ bhāryāṃ priyāṃ dṛṣṭvā kucailāṃ kṣutkṛśīkṛtām \|*  
*asya duḥkhasya tannāsti sukhaṃ yatsamatāṃ vrajet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is no situation more painful than the one, when a person finds his beloved clad in dirty clothes, starving with hunger. There could be no ugly situation comparable with this.

## \|\| 1.6.10 \|\|

*rūkṣānvivarṇānkṣudhitānbhūmiprastaraśāyinaḥ \|*  
*putradārānnijāndṛṣṭvā kimakāryaṃ bhavennṛṇām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There is no deed which could not be performed in anguish by a person, when he finds his wife and children suffering from hunger, lying over the floor.

## \|\| 1.6.11 \|\|

*bāhūttarīyaṃ kṣutkṣāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā dīnamukhaṃ sutam \|*  
*mṛtyurevotsavaḥ puṃsāṃ vyasanaṃ jīvitaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Brahmanas, it is better for a person to meet with his end than to find his wife and children without robes and suffering from hunger. Such a life indeed is a fallacy.

## \|\| 1.6.12 \|\|

*parisīdatsvapatyeṣu dṛṣṭvā dīnamukho priyām \|*  
*vajrakāryaśarīrāste ye na yānti sahasradhā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Finding the children suffering from hunger, when his beloved felt extremely painful, the body which does not shatter into thousands of pieces, would be the body of vajra.

## \|\| 1.6.13 \|\|

*tasmādarthavihīnasya puṃso dāraparigrahāt \|*  
*kutastrivarga saṃsiddhiryātanaiva hi tasya sā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Therefore, how can a poor person having no wealth, earns dharma, artha and kama. Therefore, a wife in such a case could only cause pain to a person.

## \|\| 1.6.14 \|\|

*abhāryasyādhikāro'sti na dvitīyāśrame yathā \|*  
*tadvadarthavihīnānāṃ sarvatra nādhikaritā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. As a person without a wife has no right to enter the state of a householder, similarly a person devoid of riches has no right to perform any deed.

## \|\| 1.6.15 \|\|

*kecittvapatyamevāhustrivargāvāptisādhanam \|*  
*puṃsāmarthaḥ kalatraṃ ca ye'nye nītivido viduḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Some people consider the children alone as the means to achieve three human purities i.e., dharma, artha and kama.

## \|\| 1.6.16 \|\|

*dharmo'pi dvividho yasmādiṣṭāpūrtakriyātmakaḥ \|*  
*sa ca dārātmakaḥ sarvaṃ jñeyamarthaikasādhanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On the other hand, dharma can also not be performed without a wife, which includes fire sacrifice, tapas, truth, yajna, charities, protection of the Vedas, welcome of guests, offering of bali-vaishvadeva, meditation and other allied activities, like construction of step-wells, wells, tanks, temples of gods, orchards, etc. But the money is the main source of carrying out such works. Therefore, riches are the main source of both the activities.

## \|\| 1.6.17 \|\|

*nijenāpi 1 daridreṇa loko lajjati bandhunā \|*  
*paro'pi hi manuṣyāṇāmaiśvaryātsvajanāyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The people feel ashamed of their own brothers who are poor. On the other hand, they have cordial relations with the people, who are in no way related with them. They treat such persons like their own kiths and kins.

## \|\| 1.6.18 \|\|

*na daridraṃ samīpe'pi sthitavantaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*dūrasthamapi vittāḍhyamādarādbhajate janaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The people fail to recognise the other people in their own neighbourhood if they be poor. To the contrary, they serve faithfully a rich man, though he might be living at a distances.

## \|\| 1.6.19 \|\|

*tasmātprayatnataḥ pūrvamarthameva prasādhayeta \|*  
*sa hi mūlaṃ trivargasya guṇānāṃ gauravasya ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Keeping all these facts in view, a person making all the efforts, should collect wealth, because it is the only means for performing trivarga (dharma, artha and kama). Not only that, the wealth is the foundation of the glory and all the virtues.

## \|\| 1.6.20 \|\|

*sarve'pi hi guṇā vidyākulaśīlādayo nṛṇām \|*  
*santi tasminnasanto'pi santi santo'pi nāsati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Even in the absence of virtuous and other merits in the wealthy people, they are still supposed to be professed by them. But to the contrary, even when all the virtues are possessed by the poor people, for them these virtues are of no consequence.

## \|\| 1.6.21 \|\|

*śāstraṃ śilpaṃ kalāḥ karma yaccānyadapi ceṣṭitam \|*  
*sādhanaṃ sarvamarthānāmarthā dharmādisādhanāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The literature, art, crafts and other activities of the world, besides trade are the means for earning the wealth. The wealth is the source for performing the dharma.

## \|\| 1.6.22 \|\|

*sādhanānāṃ trivargo'sti taṃ vinā kevalaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*ajāgalastanasyeva nidhanāyaiva saṃbhavaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Therefore, the riches are the only source of the trivarga activities. Without wealth, the birth of a human being is of no consequence like the udder hanging in the neck of a goat, which is meant for death alone.

## \|\| 1.6.23 \|\|

*prākpuṇyairvipulā sampaddharmakāmādihetujā \|*  
*bhūyo dharmeṇa sāmutra tayā3 tāviti 4 ca kramaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With the enormous auspicious deeds performed in earlier births, one earns enormous riches which are useful for the performing of the noble deeds. Similarly, both the types of riches are interdependent on wealth.

## \|\| 1.6.24-25 \|\|

*ekacakrakametaddhi proktamanyonyahetukam \|*  
*pūrvapaścimabāhubhyāmuttarādharamadhyamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vijñāya matimānevaṃ yastrivargaṃ niṣevate \|*  
*saṃkhyāśatasamāyuktairavāpnotyuttarottaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Both of them are treated to be the limbs of the same wheel. Both of them are mutually inter-related. With the arms of east and west, one knows about the north and the middle. In other words, one comes to know about both the wheels of the chariot, its front, middle and rear. Therefore, a person who earns the knowledge of trivarga, he enjoying the complete age of a hundred years, experiences comfort, delight and welfare.

## \|\| 1.6.26 \|\|

*nābhāryasyādhikāro'sti trivarge nirdhanasya vā \|*  
*nā bhāryāyāmataḥ pūrvamarthamaiva prasādhayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. But a person without a wife or riches, has no part to play in trivarga. At the same time, a person with no money has no right to have a wife ever. Therefore, a person should first of all earn the wealth.

## \|\| 1.6.27 \|\|

*tasmātkramāgatairartheḥ svayaṃ vādhigatairyutaḥ \|*  
*kriyāyogyaiḥ samarthaśca kuryāddāraparigraham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Therefore, the wealth should be earned gradually. In case the wealth is achieved without making much efforts, it should be collected and when a person does so and becomes competent to perform all the activities, he should marry a woman.

## \|\| 1.6.28 \|\|

*anurūpe kule jātāṃ śrutavittakriyādibhiḥ \|*  
*labhetāninditāṃ kanyāṃ manojñāṃ dharmasādhanām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person should marry a girl of comparable status in studies, wealth, and born in respectably family, who is praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.6.29 \|\|

*pumānardhapumāṃstāvadyāvadbhāryāṃ na vidanti \|*  
*tasmādyathākramaṃ kāle kuryāddāraparigraham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A person remains incomplete, till such time he gets a girl as his wife; therefore, he should gradually at the appropriate time, find a suitable wife.

## \|\| 1.6.30 \|\|

*ekacakro ratho yadvadekapakṣo yathā khagaḥ \|*  
*abhāryo'pi 1 narastadvadayogyaḥ sarvakarmasu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. As a chariot with a single wheel or a bird with a single wing cannot move and becomes useless, similarly a person without a wife, is of no use in all the activities.

## \|\| 1.6.31 \|\|

*patnīparigrahāddharmastathārtho bahulābhataḥ \|*  
*satprītiyogātkāmo'pi trayamasyāṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With the accepting of a wife, several types of benefits are gained in the religious field. With the true mutual love, one achieves kama as well. Similarly, the learned people claim that with the marriage of a girl, a person earns three types of vargas.

## \|\| 1.6.32 \|\|

*tridhā vivāhasambandho hīnatulyādhikaiḥ saha \|*  
*tulyaiḥ saha samasteṣāmitarau nīcamadhyamau \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The performing of the marriage is of three types viz., lower, equal and high. When the marriage is performed between the people of equal status, it is termed as equal. The rest are treated as lower or the middle one.

## \|\| 1.6.33 \|\|

*asamairnindyate sadbhiruttamaiḥ paribhūyate \|*  
*tulyaiḥ praśasyate yasmāttasmātsādhutamo mataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A marriage performed in family of lower status is said to be deplorable. In case the marriage is performed in high status, one gets disgraced. Therefore, the marriage with people of equal status is considered to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.6.34 \|\|

*kṛtvaivādhikasambandhamapamānaṃ samaśnute \|*  
*na caiṣāmānatiṃ gacchennaiva nīcaiḥ saheṣyate2 \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When marriage is performed in the family of higher status, one has to face humiliation all the time. Therefore, a person should not perch insult from such people. Similarly, a person should not aspire to marry in the family of the people with lower status.

## \|\| 1.6.35 \|\|

*uttamo'pi ca sambandho nīcaistatsamatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*atastaṃ varjayeddhīmānninditaṃ sadṛśottamaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. As the relationship with high ups is prohibited, similarly if a person of high rank has relationship with a person of lower rank, he has to act like the people of the lower rank. Realising this, a wise person should avoid relationship with a person of lower rank as well as with the people of higher rank.

## \|\| 1.6.36 \|\|

*vijātīyaiśca sambandhaṃ sahecchanti na sūrayaḥ \|*  
*ubhayorbhraśyate tena yathā kokilayā śukaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The learned people do not desire to marry in the other castes, because by so doing, both the families are considered to be fallen; as the marriage of a cuckoo with a parrot.

## \|\| 1.6.37 \|\|

*tadbhāti kulabāhyatvādavaśyaṃ cāvamānataḥ \|*  
*pratipatteraśakyatvāccottamo'pi na śasyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The people of the lower family look grateful by developing relationship with the people of higher race, but because of the disgrace and incompetence involved, one has to face ugly situations. Therefore in such situations, the person of higher race does not feel praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.6.38 \|\|

*eke'pi parihartavyā anye pariharantyuta \|*  
*tasmāddvāvapi naiveṣṭau sambandhāvadhamottamau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Inspite of being one, the marriage in higher or the lower family is prohibited. Therefore, the marriage in the higher or the lower families are both prohibited.

## \|\| 1.6.39 \|\|

*ekapātrādibhiryeṣāmupacāraiḥ parasparam \|*  
*pratyahaṃ vardhate snehaḥ sambandhaḥ so'bhidhīyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The true relationship is said to be the one when the love goes on increasing gradually.

## \|\| 1.6.40 \|\|

*yatrāvāhavivāhādāvanyo'nyāḥ pratipattayaḥ \|*  
*spardhayaiva pravardhante taṃ sambandhaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The learned people call it as the true relationship, when there develops a mutual effort to enhance the glory of the other party mutually.

## \|\| 1.6.41 \|\|

*yyasane'bhyudaye vāpi yeṣāṃ prāṇairdhanairapi \|*  
*sahaikapratipattitvaṃ sambandhānāṃ sa uttamaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Only that relationship is considered to be the best, when there is a mutual help from both sides.

## \|\| 1.6.42 \|\|

*snehavyaktau manuṣyāṇāṃ dvāveva nikaṣopalau \|*  
*tathā kṛtajñatāyāṃ ca vyasanābhyudayāgamau \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In order to expose the love and regard mutually, this should be the touch stone during the prosperity and the evil times.

## \|\| 1.6.43 \|\|

*sa ca sneho nṛṇāṃ prāyaḥ sameṣveva1 hi dṛśyate \|*  
*sāmyaṃ cāpyupagantavyaṃ vittaśīlakulādibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Such type of relationship is usually noticed in the people with equal status. Therefore, one should develop relationship with the people of comparable status and wealth.

## \|\| 1.6.44 \|\|

*tasmādvivāhasambandhaṃ saṃkhyamekāntakāriṇām \|*  
*sadṛśaireva kurvīta nottamenāpyanuttamaiḥ2 \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Keeping all these facts in view, the people of wisdom should develop friendship and marriage relations only with the people of equal status and not with those of higher or the lower status.

## Chapter 7. Performance of marriage

## \|\| 1.7.1 \|\|

*sarasvatīdṛṣadvatyordevanadyoryadantaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — Leaving aside the girls of the seven generations of the mother of a person and those of the same gotra (or caste group) of one’s father, to perform marriage with other girls is said to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.7.2 \|\|

*sahajo na bhavedyasyā na ca vijñāyate pitā \|*  
*nopayaccheta tāṃ prājñaḥ putrikādharmaśaṅkayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A girl having no real brother and when the name of a girl’s father is unknown, a wise man should not marry such a girl, which will result in apprehensive sins of putrika (or that her son shall have to perform the last rites of the maternal grandparents).

## \|\| 1.7.3 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāṃ praśastā syātsavarṇā dārakarmaṇi \|*  
*kāmaśastu pravṛttānāmimāḥ syuḥ kramaśo'varāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The marriage of a Brahmana is considered to be praiseworthy in the Brahmana family. Out of passion, he can marry the girls of other three castes as well. But such women are termed as degraded.

## \|\| 1.7.4 \|\|

*kṣatrasyāpi savarṇā syātprathamā dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*dve cāvare tathā prokte kāmatastu na dharmataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Dvijas, similarly, according to dharma it would be appropriate to marry a Kshatriya girl. Out of passion, a Kshatriya is also allowed to marry a Vaishya or a Shudra girl, but such a marriage shall not be treated strictly according to dharma.

## \|\| 1.7.5 \|\|

*vaiśyasyaikā varā proktā savarṇā caiva dharmataḥ \|*  
*tathāvarā kāmatastu dvitīyā na tu dharmataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is prescribed for a Vaishya to marry a girl of his own community. A Kshatriya is also permitted to many only a Shudra girl under passion compulsion, but it is not supported by dharma.

## \|\| 1.7.6 \|\|

*śūdraiva bhāryā śūdrasya dharmato manurabravīt \|*  
*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ pariṇetā dvijottamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A Shudra should have a wife from Shudra caste alone; this has been ordained by Manu. The excellent Brahmana has a right to marry a girl of any of the four varnas.

## \|\| 1.7.7 \|\|

*na brāhmaṇakṣatriyayorāpadyapi hi tiṣṭhatoḥ \|*  
*kasmiṃścidapi vṛtānte śūdrā bhāryopadiśyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. But even under the pressing circumstances, a Brahmana or a Kshatriya should not marry a Shudra girl.

## \|\| 1.7.8 \|\|

*hīnajātistriyaṃ mohādudvahanto dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*kulānyeva nayantyāśu sasantānāni śūdratām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A person of high caste (Brahmana, Kshatriya or a Vaishya), out of ignorance, by marrying a woman of the lower caste, makes his own children as well his own family to become Shudras.

## \|\| 1.7.9 \|\|

*śūdramāropya vedyāṃ tu patitotrirbabhūva ha \|*  
*utathyaḥ putrajananātpatitatvamavāptavān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It is said that the sage Atri had fallen from his position by installing a Shudra over his seat He was fallen by producing his son named Utathya.

## \|\| 1.7.10 \|\|

*śūdrasya putramāsādya śaunakaḥ śūdratāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*bhṛgvādayopyevameva patitatvamavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The sage Shaunaka by getting a Shudra son was himself turned as Shudra. Similarly, Bhrigu and other sages also had fallen from their exalted positions.

## \|\| 1.7.11 \|\|

*śūdrāṃ śayanamāropya brāhmaṇo yātyadhogatim \|*  
*janayitvā sutaṃ tasyāṃ brāhmaṇyādeva hīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By enjoying a Sandra woman in his bed, a Brahmana achieves the degraded position and by producing a son only of a Shudra woman, he is deprived of Brahma-tejas or the divine lustre.

## \|\| 1.7.12 \|\|

*devapitryātitheyāni tatpradhānāni yasya tu \|*  
*nādanti pitaro devāḥ sa ca svargaṃ na gacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Such of the people who welcome the gods or the manes, in the company of the Shudra, the gods and the manes do not accept the food so offered by them. They themselves are also barred from entry into the heaven.

## \|\| 1.7.13 \|\|

*vṛṣalīphenapītasya niḥśvāsopahatasya ca \|*  
*tasyāṃ caiva prasūtasya niṣkṛtirna vidhīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. With the consuming of the foam of a Shudra woman and to breath so produced, one does not get redeemed.

## \|\| 1.7.14 \|\|

*caturṇāmapi viprendrāḥ pretyeha ca hitāhitam \|*  
*samāsato bravīmyeṣa vivāhāṣṭakamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O group of Brahmanas, I shall now describe the eight types of marriages which are considered to be good or evil in both the lokas for the people of all the four varnas. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.7.15 \|\|

*kālo daivastathā cārṣaḥ prājāpatyastathāsuraḥ \|*  
*gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva paiśācaścāṣṭamo'dhamaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There are eight types of the marriages known in the world, viz. Brahma, Daiva, Arsha, Prajapatya, Asura, Gandharva, Rakshasa and Pishacha which is the most degraded one. These are the eight types of marriages.

## \|\| 1.7.16 \|\|

*ye yasya dharmā varṇasya guṇadoṣau ca yasya yau \|*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ taddvijaśreṣṭhāḥ prasave ca guṇāguṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The marriage which is prescribed for a particular varna you listen to the blemishes of their generations.

## \|\| 1.7.17 \|\|

*viprasya 1 caturaḥ pūrvānkṣatrasya caturo'varān \|*  
*viṭśūdrayostu trīneva vidyāddharmānarākṣasān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. For Brahmanas, the first four types of marriages are said to be praiseworthy (they are Brahma, Daiva, Arsha and Prajapatya). For Kshatriya, the later four types of marriage are said to be praiseworthy which are Asura, Gandharva, Rakshasa and Pishacha. For Vaishya and Shudra, only three out of the last four types of marriages are said to be suitable.

## \|\| 1.7.18 \|\|

*caturo brāhmaṇasyādyānpraśastānkavayo viduḥ \|*  
*rākṣasaṃ kṣatriyasyaikamāsuraṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The learned people have declared the earlier four types of marriages to be beneficial for the Brahmanas. The Rakshasa type of marriage has been considered to be suitable for the Kshatriyas alone. The Asura type of marriage is suitable for the Vaishyas as well as the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.7.19 \|\|

*kṣatriyāṇāṃ trayo dharmyā dvāvadharmyau2 smṛtāviha \|*  
*paiśācaścāsuraścaiva na karttavyau kathañcana \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the present world, three types of marriages are considered to be quite suitable for the Kshatriyas, but Pishacha and Asura types of marriage for them are termed as irreligious. Therefore, they should under no circumstances patronize these types of marriages.

## \|\| 1.7.20 \|\|

*pṛthakpṛthagvā miśrau vā vivāhau pūrvacoditau \|*  
*gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva dharmyau kṣatrasya tau smṛtau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The combination of the aforesaid two types of marriages could be performed or they could be performed separately as well. The Gandharva and Rakshasa type of marriages have been prescribed to be quite religious for the Kshatriyas.

## \|\| 1.7.21 \|\|

*ācchādya cārcayitvā tu śrutaśīlavate svayam \|*  
*āhūya dānaṃ kanyāyā bāhyo dharmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When a well-read Brahmana is called in one’s house being a humble and able groom who is invited in one’s own house, and is worshipped with honour offering costumes etc., and then giving away the girl in marriage is known as Brahma dharma marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.22 \|\|

*vitate cāpi yajñe tu karma kurvati cārtviji \|*  
*alaṅkṛtya sutādānaṃ daivo dharma udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. While performing the yajna for marriage, when the priest performing all the due rites, and when the girl decorated with all the ornaments and clad in the best of costumes, is given to the groom, it is called the Deva dharma marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.23 \|\|

*ekaṃ gomithunaṃ dve vā varādādāya dharmataḥ \|*  
*kanyāpradānaṃ vidhivadārṣīyo dharma ucyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When the girl is given away after accepting a couple of cows appropriately, this is called the Arsha marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.24 \|\|

*sahobhau carataṃ dharmamiti vācānubhāṣya tu \|*  
*kanyāpradānamabhyarca prājāpatyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When a boy and a girl are allowed to live together, making them aware of all the rules of marriage in an appropriate manner, it is treated as the Prajapatya marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.25 \|\|

*jñātibhyo draviṇaṃ dattvā kanyāyāścaiva śaktitaḥ \|*  
*kanyāpradānaṃ svacchandādāsuro dharma ucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the groom’s side take the girl, after payment of suitable riches to parents or the relatives of the girl. Such a type of marriage is called the Asuri marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.26 \|\|

*icchayānyo'nyasaṃyogaḥ kanyāyāśca varasya ca \|*  
*gāndharvaḥ sa vidhirjñeyo maithunyaḥ kāmasambhavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When the boy and the girl get united out of lust or passion, it is known as the Gandharva type of marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.27 \|\|

*hatvā chittvā ca bhittvā ca krośantīṃ rudatīṃ gṛhāt \|*  
*prasahya kanyāharaṇaṃ rākṣaso vidhirucyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When a girl is abducted from the parent’s house forcibly while crying breaking all the bondages, it is known as the Rakshasa marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.28 \|\|

*suptāṃ mattāṃ pramattāṃ ca raho yatropagacchati \|*  
*sa pāpiṣṭho vivāhānāṃ paiśācaḥ kathito'ṣṭamaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When the girl is sleeping alone and a person forcibly unites with her stealthily, it is sinful and known as the Pishacha marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.29 \|\|

*jalapūrvaṃ dvijāgryāṇāṃ kanyādānaṃ praśasyate \|*  
*itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāmitaretarakāmyayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When the kanyadana is performed by a Brahmana with water, it is considered as praiseworthy. This ceremony can be performed by the people of the other varnas with something else.

## \|\| 1.7.30 \|\|

*yo yasyaiṣāṃ vivāhānāṃ vibhūnāṃ kīrtito guṇaḥ \|*  
*taṃ nibodhata vai viprāḥ samyaktakīrtayato mama \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Brahmanas, whatever the merit has been prescribed for each one of the aforesaid marriages, I am going to speak out the same to you. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.7.31 \|\|

*kulāni daśa pūrvāṇi tathānyāni daśaiva tu \|*  
*sa hi tānyātmanā caivaṃ mocayatyenaso dhruvam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A noble son born after the marriage of Brahma type redeems his past as well as the future ten generations from their sins. You must take it for granted.

## \|\| 1.7.32 \|\|

*brāhmīputraḥ sukṛtakṛddaivoḍhājaṃ sutaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*daivoḍhājaḥ suto viprāḥ sapta sapta parāvarān \|*  
*ārṣoḍhājaḥ sutaḥ strīṇāṃ puruṣāṃstārayeddvijāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Now listen about the son born out of the Daiva marriage. O group of Brahmanas, when a religious minded son is born out of Daiva type of marriage, he redeems the seven past as well as the future generations. O group of Brahmanas, similarly when a son is born to the woman married as per the Arsha rites, he redeems the seven past and seven future generations. Such sons have the equal merits as compared with sons produced out of the Brahma marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.33-34 \|\|

*brahmādiṣu vivāheṣu caturṣvevānupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*brahmavarcasvinaḥ putrā jāyante śiṣṭasammatāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rūpasattvaguṇopetā dhanavanto yaśasvinaḥ \|*  
*putravanto'tha dharmiṣṭhā jīvanti ca śataṃ samāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The sons who are born in the four types of Brahma and other marriages possess the virtues like the Brahma-tejas, politeness, beauty, prowess, wealth, glory, religious minded and have sons. They have the life of a hundred years each.

## \|\| 1.7.35 \|\|

*itareṣu nibodhadhvaṃ nṛśaṃsānṛtavādinaḥ \|*  
*jāyante durvivāheṣu brahmadharmadviṣaḥ 1 sutāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Now you listen to the sons produced after the performing of four other types of marriages. The sons born out of the blemished marriages, become the false Brahmanas besides being envious of dharma.

## \|\| 1.7.36 \|\|

*aninditaiḥ strīvivāhairanindyā bhavati prajā \|*  
*ninditairniṃditā nṛṇāṃ tasmānnidyānvivarjayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The women who are married in the unblemished way, produce unblemished progeny. Similarly, the women who are married in a blemished way, they have the blemished progeny. Therefore, the people with wisdom should keep themselves away from the blemished marriage.

## \|\| 1.7.37 \|\|

*karagrahaṇasaṃskārāḥ savarṇāsu bhavanti vai \|*  
*asavarṇāsvayaṃ jñeyā vidhirudvāhakarmaṇi \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is sure that the marriage is performed with due rituals among the same colour or caste, but when the marriage is performed with a woman of another caste, the same process is followed.

## \|\| 1.7.38 \|\|

*bāṇaḥ kṣatriyayā grāhyaḥ pratodo vaiśyakanyayā \|*  
*vasanasya daśā grāhyā śūdrayotkṛṣṭavedane \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. At the time of marriage of an outcaste, a Kshatriya girl should hold an arrow, a Vaishya girl should hold a whip. Similarly, a Shudra girl while marrying a boy of a higher caste, should hold the end of a costume.

## \|\| 1.7.39 \|\|

*na kanyāyāḥ pitā vidvāngṛhṇīyācchulkamaṇvapi \|*  
*gṛhṇanhi śulkaṃ lobhena syānnaro'patyavikrayī \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A wise father should not accept even the slightest obligation or fee from his son-in-law, because in case he out of greed or otherwise, if accepts even the slightest obligation of fee it would amount to the selling of the daughter.

## \|\| 1.7.40 \|\|

*strīdhanāni tu ye mohādupajīvanti bāndhavāḥ \|*  
*nārīyānāni vastraṃ vā te pāpā yāntyadhogatim \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The father or other relatives, out of ignorance or otherwise if accept any obligation or fee or riches or make use of the costumes brought (from the girl’s side), such sinful people fall in the lowest position.

## \|\| 1.7.41 \|\|

*ārṣe gomithunaṃ śulkaṃ kecidāhurmṛṣaiva 1 tat \|*  
*alpo vāpi mahānvāpi vikrayastāvadeva saḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The practice of giving a couple of cows to the bride’s side as has been stated by some people, is false. Irrespective of such payment being small or big, it surely amounts to sale.

## \|\| 1.7.42 \|\|

*yāsāṃ nādadate śulkaṃ jñātayo na sa vikrayaḥ \|*  
*arhaṇaṃ tatkumārīṇāmānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca kevalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. When some presents or riches are given to the bride by the people of groom’s side, they cannot be taken as a sale, because it amounts to the respect of the girl It amounts to the compassion or the grace for her.

## \|\| 1.7.43 \|\|

*itthaṃ dārānsamāsādya deśamagryaṃ samāvaset \|*  
*brāhmaṇo dvijaśārdūla ya icchedvipulaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O lion among the Brahmanas, in this way when a Brahmana is desirous of the great glory, after accepting a woman with the methods detailed above, he should live in some good place or country.

## \|\| 1.7.44 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ko deśaḥ paramo brahmankaśca puṇyo matastava \|*  
*pravasanyatra viprendra yaśaḥ prāpnoti kañjaja \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Rishis said — O lord born of lotus, O Brahmana, which are the countries considered to be most auspicious and living there one earns great glory?

## \|\| 1.7.45 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*na hīyate yatra dharmaścatuṣpātsa kalo dvijāḥ \|*  
*sa deśaḥ paramo viprāḥ sa ca puṇyo mato mama \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Brahma said — O group of Brahmanas, the place where the dharma is not deprived of its all the four feet or the languages, that place is considered to be quite auspicious and beneficial.

## \|\| 1.7.46 \|\|

*vidvadbhiḥ sevito dharmo yasmindeśe pravartate \|*  
*śāstroktaścāpi viprendrāḥ sa deśaḥ paramo mataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O group of Brahmanas, the sacred country in which the dharma as ordained by the learned Brahmanas remains in vogue, it is considered to be the best.

## \|\| 1.7.47 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcū \|*  
*vidvadbhiḥ sevitaṃ dharmaṃ śāstroktaṃ ca surottama \|*  
*vadāsmāsu suraśreṣṭha kautukaṃ paramaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Rishis said — O best of the gods, O lord of all the gods, we are anxious to listen to the dharma that has been prescribed by the Brahmanas based on the scriptures. You kindly narrate the same.

## \|\| 1.7.48 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vidvadbhiḥ sevitaḥ sadbhirnityamadveṣarāgibhiḥ \|*  
*hṛdayenābhyanujñāto yo dharmastaṃ nibodhata \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Brahma said — O crowd of Rishis, the dharma which has been prescribed by the learned Rishis is going to be spoken by me, which you kindly listen with attention.

## \|\| 1.7.49 \|\|

*kāmātmatā na praśastā na vehāsyāpyakāmatā \|*  
*kāmyo hi vedādhigamaḥ karmayogaśca vaidikaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The methods for performing deeds with the sole purpose of enjoying the related benefits during the present birth alone, are not considered to be praiseworthy. The deeds performed with expectation have also the sanction of the Vedas, while the deeds performed without expecting any reward have also the support of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.7.50 \|\|

*saṅkalpājjāyate kāmo yajñādyāni ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*vratāḥ niyamadharmāśca sarve saṅkalpajāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Taking a vow to perform something gives rise to the desire. The activities like the performance of the yajnas etc., are all based on the vow or a samkalpa. Not only that, the performance of vratas and other religious activities emanate from the vows or the samkalpa.

## \|\| 1.7.51 \|\|

*kāmādṛte kriyākārī dṛśyate neha karhicit \|*  
*yadyaddhi kurute kaścittattatkāmasya ceṣṭitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Nowhere in this world one can find a person who may perform anything without a desire. Whatever tasks are performed by a person, it is the result of the inner urge or desire.

## \|\| 1.7.52-53 \|\|

*nigamo 1 dharmamūlaṃ syātsmṛtiśīle tathaiva ca \|*  
*tathācāraśca sādhūnāmātmanastuṣṭireva ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ tu samavekṣeta niścayaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā \|*  
*śrutiprādhānyato vidvānsvadharme nivaseta vai \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. The Vedas are the roots of all the Dharmas, besides the Smritis. The existence of dharma is decided on the basis of the discipline prescribed by the nobility which bestows eternal relief to the soul. By well visualising such deeds with the eyes of knowledge, the character of dharma is decided. Keeping all these facts in view, a learned person, giving due importance to the Vedas and Shrutis, should have his full faith in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.7.54 \|\|

*śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmamanutiṣṭhansadā naraḥ \|*  
*prāpya ceha parāṃ kīrtiṃ yāti śakrasalokatām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The dharma which is based on or supported by the Shrutis, should always be followed and by so doing a person earning enough of glory in this world, ultimately achieves Indraloka.

## \|\| 1.7.55 \|\|

*śrutistu vedo 4 vijñeyo dharmaśāstraṃ tu vai smṛtiḥ \|*  
*te sarvārtheṣu mīmāṃsye tābhyāṃ dharmo hi nirbabhau \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Vedas represent while Dharmashastra stand for the Smritis. In all the dharmas, one should investigate from this point of view, because all the religious activities look graceful with both of these (Shrutis and Smritis).

## \|\| 1.7.56 \|\|

*yo'vamanyeta te cobhe hetuśāstrāśrayāddvijaḥ \|*  
*sa sādhubhirbahiṣkāryo nāstiko vedanindakaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A Brahmana, who resorting to controversies, neglects the Vedas and the Smritis, he should be driven out from the society by the people of wisdom, because he happens to be an atheist and denouncer of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.7.57 \|\|

*vedaḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāraḥ svasya ca priyamātmanaḥ \|*  
*etaccaturvidhaṃ viprāḥ sākṣāddharmasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The apparent symptoms of dharma have been said to be the Vedas, Smritis, noble conduct and to follow nobility performing deeds which suite one’s soul.

## \|\| 1.7.58 \|\|

*dharmajñānaṃ bhavedviprā arthakāmeṣvasajjatām \|*  
*dharmaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ pramāṇānnaigamaṃ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those who are not involved in the collection of riches and lust, they, while engaging themselves in search of the true dharma, succeed in receiving the true form of dharma. For such people, out of all the evidences, the evidence of the Vedas is the best of all and has been admitted as such.

## \|\| 1.7.59 \|\|

*niṣekādiśmaśānānto mantrairyasyodito vidhiḥ \|*  
*adhikāro bhavettasya vedeṣu ca japeṣu ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Right from the time of conception to the last funeral rites which are to be performed with the reciting of the related mantras, have been prescribed. Those have been ordained m the Vedas as well as in the recitations.

## \|\| 1.7.60 \|\|

*tadeva nirmitaṃ deśaṃ brahmāvartaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The divine rivers like Drishadvati and Sarasvati and the land in between the two rivers is known as Brahmavarta and is considered to be quite auspicious.

## \|\| 1.7.61 \|\|

*yasmin deśe ya ācāraḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ \|*  
*varṇānāṃ sāntarālānāṃ sa sadācāra ucyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The human thoughts and the conduct which continue form ancient times and are still in vogue, they are to be followed by the people of the four varnas, besides the people of the mixed races.

## \|\| 1.7.62 \|\|

*kurukṣetraṃ ca matsyāśca pañcālāḥ śūrasenayaḥ \|*  
*eṣa brahmarṣideśo vai brahmāvartādanantaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After Brahmavarta, Kurukshetra, Matsya, Panchala and Shurasena are said to be the places meant for the Rishis.

## \|\| 1.7.63 \|\|

*etaddeśaprasūtasya sakāśādagrajanmanaḥ \|*  
*svaṃ svaṃ caritraṃ śikṣanti pṛthivyāṃ sarvamānavāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The Brahmanas who are born in these places, serves as teachers to all the Brahmanas of other regions, who arrive here to prosecute their studies.

## \|\| 1.7.64 \|\|

*himavadvindhyayormadhye yatprāgvinaśanādapi \|*  
*pratyageva prayāgācca madhyadeśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The land between the Himalaya and Vindhyachala mountains i.e., the land between eastern Kurukshetra and western Prayaga is known as Madhyadesa.

## \|\| 1.7.65 \|\|

*ā samudrāttu vai pūrvādāsamudrāttu paścimāt \|*  
*tayorevāntaraṃ giryorāryāvarttaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*
