## \|\| 1.22.48 \|\|

*mayā prasannena tava guhyametadudāhṛtam \|*  
*kathitaṃ tithisaṃyoge vināyakakathāmṛtam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I have narrated secret story of Vinayaka feeling extremely pleased in the context of the glory of the tithis.

## \|\| 1.22.49-50 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śrāvayedvidvānbrāhmaṇānvedapāragān \|*  
*kṣatriyāṃśca svavṛttisthānviṭśūdrāṃśca guṇānvitān \|\| 49 \|\|*

*na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcidiha cāmutra vidyate \|*  
*na ca durgatimāpnoti na ca yāti parābhavam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. When a learned person narrates this auspicious story to the Brahmanas well versed in the Vedas, besides the Kshatriyas, virtuous Vaishyas and Shudras following the duties of their varnas, there is nothing beyond his reach in this as well as the future world. He never faces misfortunes nor a defeat.

## \|\| 1.22.51 \|\|

*nirvighnaṃ sarvakāryāṇi sādhayennātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ cāpi vindeta bharatottama \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There is no doubt that he establishes all his tasks without any destruction, O best of the race of Bharata, such a learned person achieves all the success, prosperity and riches quite easily.

## Chapter 23. The story of Vighna Vinayaka

## \|\| 1.23.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*kenāyaṃ bhīmajo vipra pramathādhipatiḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhartṛtve cāpi vighnānāmadhikārī kathaṃ babhau \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O excellent Brahmana, how could Vinayaka — the son of Bhima, be the foremost of all the Shiva ganas? How was he established over the position of the chief of obstructions?

## \|\| 1.23.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra yadayaṃ vighnakārakaḥ \|*  
*yairvāpi vighnakaraṇairniryukto'pi vināyakaḥ \|*  
*tatte vacmi mahābāho śṛṇuṣvaikamanādhunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O Rajendra, you have broached an excellent subject, I am now going to speak out the reason for which Vinayaka was given the name of creator of the obstructions and by creating which set of obstructions^ he earned the position of Vinayaka. O long armed one, when I am going to reveal before you all the cause thereof, you listen to me with a concentrated mind.

## \|\| 1.23.3 \|\|

*ādye kṛtayuge vīra prajāsargamavāpa ha \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā karmāṇi siddhāni vinā vighnena bhārata \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O valorous one, O Bharata, in the earlier Satyayuga when the creation of the people had already started, then all their tasks were accomplished without any obstruction.

## \|\| 1.23.4-5 \|\|

*agatakleśāṃ prajāṃ dṛṣṭvā garvitāṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa \|*  
*bahuśaścintayityā tu idaṃ karma mahīpate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vināyakaḥ samṛddhyarthaṃ prajānāṃ viniyojitaḥ \|*  
*gaṇānāṃ cādhipatye ca bhīmaḥ kañjajasāttvataiḥ \|*  
*tatopasṛṣṭo yastasya lakṣaṇāni nibodha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. O Bharata, because of the performing of their tasks without any obstruction, the people were free of troubles, and had the arrogant temperament. Then Brahma thought over the matter and then established Vinayaka for the prosperity of the people. Thereafter, Brahma having born of lotus, established Vinayaka as the lord of Pramathas. Thereafter, Vinayaka created obstructions for them, which you please listen from me.

## \|\| 1.23.6-8 \|\|

*svapnevagāhate'tyarthaṃ jalaṃ muṇḍāṃśca paśyati \|*  
*kāṣāyavāsasaścaiva kravyādāṃścādhirohati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*antyajairgardabhairuṣṭraiḥ sahaikatrāvatiṣṭhate \|*  
*vrajamānastathātmānaṃ manyate'nugataṃ paraiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdatyanimittataḥ \|*  
*karaṭārūḍhamātmānamambhasontaragaṃ tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. A person, who in a dream, bathes in excess of water or oil, views a person with a shaven head and a person wearing the ochre coloured costumes, mounts the animals who consume the raw meat, and then lives with the discarded donkeys or camels at one and the same place in a dream, finds many people following him. Not only this, he always remains absent minded, starts useless works and suffers pain without any cause. O lion of the race of Kuru, O king, when a person is under the shadow of Vinayaka, he find himself mounted over the head of an elephant and finds exposed naked in the water.

## \|\| 1.23.9 \|\|

*pattibhiścāvṛtaṃ yāntaṃ saṅgamanāntikaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*paśyate kuruśārdūla svapnānte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Similarly, the king finds himself surrounded by the foot soldiers of the enemy or travelling in a far off country at the end of a dream. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.23.10 \|\|

*cittaṃ ca vikṛtākāraṃ karavīravibhūṣitam \|*  
*tenopasṛṣṭo labhate na rājyaṃ paurvasaṃbhavam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. His mind remains disturbed and he finds himself adorned with the flowers of oleander. Thus the king, under the spell of Vinayaka, cannot inherit the ancestral kingdom of his father.

## \|\| 1.23.11 \|\|

*kumārī na ca bhartāramapatyaṃ garbhiṇī tathā \|*  
*ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaśca śiṣyāścādhyayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*vaṇiglābhaṃ ca nāpnoti kṛṣiṃ caiva kṛṣīvalaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A maiden cannot get a husband and the pregnant woman is unable to give birth to a child. A Shrotriya fails to become an Acharya and a student is unable to prosecute his studies. Similarly, the traders are unable to gain profit in the trade and the farmers fail in their farming activity.

## \|\| 1.23.12 \|\|

*snapanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ puṇye'hani mahīpate \|*  
*gaurasarṣapakalkena sājyenotsāditena tu \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O king, such a person should take his bath on some auspicious day appropriately with the water mixed with mustard oil, ghi and fragrant material.

## \|\| 1.23.13 \|\|

*śuklapakṣe caturthyāṃ tu vāsare dhiṣaṇasya ca \|*  
*tiṣye ca vīranakṣatre tasyaiva purato nṛpa \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O king, on the fourth day of the bright fortnight on Thursday in the Pushya constellation, he should perform this in his presence.

## \|\| 1.23.14 \|\|

*sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhairviliptaśirasastathā \|*  
*bhadrāsanopaviṣṭasya svasti vācya dvijāñchubhān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The powder of all the fragrant materials and all the aushadhis should be plastered over the head, one should be seated over an auspicious seat and make the Brahmanas of auspicious race and noble thoughts to recite the welfare mantra.

## \|\| 1.23.15-16 \|\|

*vyomakeśaṃ tu sampūjya pārvatīṃ bhīmajaṃ tathā \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ sapitaraṃ tāta pavamānaṃ sitaṃ tathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dhiṣaṇaṃ cenduputraṃ ca koṇaṃ ketuṃ ca 3 bhārata \|*  
*vidhuntudaṃ bāhuleyaṃ nandakasya ca dhāriṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. O adorable one, initially, Shiva, Parvati and Ganesha should be worshipped. Thereafter, lord Krishna, Vayu, manes, Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, Ketu, Karttikeya, and Rahu holding a sword, should be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.23.17-18 \|\|

*aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkātsaṅgamādhradāt \|*  
*mṛttikāṃ rocanāṃ gandhānguggulaṃ cāpsu nikṣipet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yadāhṛtaṃ hyekavarṇaiścaturbhiḥ kalaśairhradāt \|*  
*carmaṇyānaḍuhe rakte sthāpyaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The four pitchers of same colour should be filled with water. Then the dust from elephant and horse stables, dust from white anthill, the earth from land of the confluence, earth from tanks, yellow pigment vomited by cows, sandal paste, guggulu, and other fragrant should be dropped in the pitchers. Then Ganesha should be bathed with that water and then made to sit over the skin of the red bull. He should then again be made to take a bath.

## \|\| 1.23.19 \|\|

*sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ 1 pāvanaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānyaḥ punantu te \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then the Brahmanas, using the water, which is sanctified by the Rishis with the reciting of the mantras, pouring the water with a thousand streams, should utter — “I am pouring this sanctified water on you, which should purify you.

## \|\| 1.23.20 \|\|

*bhagaṃ te varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*bhagamindraśca vāyuśca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Let all the gods like Varuna, Surya, Brihaspati, Indra, Vayu, all the seven Rishis viz., Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasishtha bestow all the fortunes on you.

## \|\| 1.23.21 \|\|

*yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani \|*  
*lalāṭe karṇayorakṣṇorāpastad ghnantu te sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Similarly, let the sanctified water remove the misfortunes from your head, hair, forehead, ears and eyes.”

## \|\| 1.23.22 \|\|

*snātasya sārṣapaṃ tailaṃ suveṇaudumbareṇa tu \|*  
*juhuyānmūrdhani kuśānsavyena parigṛhya tu \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He should thus be bathed, thereafter the rapeseed oil should be poured over his head with the ladle of wild fig tree and the kusha grass should be held in left hand.

## \|\| 1.23.23 \|\|

*mitaśca sammitaścaiva tathā ca śālakaṃṭakaḥ \|*  
*kūṣmāṇḍo rājaśreṣṭhāste'gnayaḥ svāhāsamanvitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then he should say, let Mita, Sammita, Shalakantaka, Kusmanda and other evil planets should bestow welfare to you combined with Rajasreshtha and Svaha.

## \|\| 1.23.24-26 \|\|

*nāmabhirbalimantraiśca namaskārasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*dadyāccatuṣpathe śūrpe kuśānāstīrya sarvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kṛtākṛtāṃstaṇḍulāṃśca palalaudanameva ca \|*  
*matsyānpakvāṃstathaivāmānmāṃsametāvadeva tu \|\| 25 \|\|*

*puṣpaṃ citraṃ sagandhaṃ ca surāṃ ca trividhāmapi \|*  
*mūlakaṃ pūrikāḥ pūpāṃstathaivoṇḍerikāsrajam \|*  
*dadhipāyasamannaṃ ca guḍaveṣṭānsamodakān \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Thereafter, spreading kusha at the crossings, a winnowing basket should be placed over it. Then the half cooked rice, meat, fish, several types of flowers, three types of wines, radish, scent, fried cakes, garland of flowers, curd, payasam, food and cakes of sugarcane juice, should also be placed there. Then uttering the names of different gods, offering should be made reciting the mantras and then offer the same with salutation.

## \|\| 1.23.27 \|\|

*vināyakasya jananīmupatiṣṭhettato'mbikām \|*  
*dūrvāsarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ dattvā puṣpāñjalitrayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter, placing durva grass, flowers, and rapeseeds, uttering the names of different gods, Ganesha and goddess Ambika should be adored with the offering the flowers in hand cups thrice. Then the mantra should be uttered.

## \|\| 1.23.28 \|\|

*rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi bhagaṃ bhagavati dehi me \|*  
*putrāndehi dhanaṃ dehi sarvānkāmāṃśca dehi me \|*  
*acalāṃ buddhiṃ me dehi dharāyāṃ khyātimeva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He should then pray — “O Bhagavati, bestow charming beauty on me besides glory, fortunes, wealth, son and fulfilling all my desires, bestow excellent wisdom on me and so grace on me that my glory spreads throughout the world.”

## \|\| 1.23.29 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ \|*  
*bhojayed brāhmaṇāndadyādvastrayugmaṃ gurorapi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thereafter, getting clad in white garments, garlands and getting decorated with sandal paste, food should be offered to the Brahmanas. Every Brahmana should be given food, besides a bed sheet and a white dhoti. Similarly, the food should also be offered to the preceptor and two costumes should also be offered to him.

## \|\| 1.23.30 \|\|

*evaṃ vināyakaṃ pūjya grahāṃścaiva vidhānataḥ \|*  
*karmaṇāṃ phalamāpnoti śriyaṃ prāpnotyanuttamām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By thus adoring Ganesha and other planets appropriately, the task is established without obstruction and one achieves the best of riches.

## \|\| 1.23.31 \|\|

*ādityasya sadā pūjāṃ tilakaṃ svāminastathā \|*  
*vināyakapateścaiva sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Therefore, for the fulfillment of all the desires, the sun, Karttikeya and Ganesha should be worshipped.

## Chapter 24. Symptoms of men

## \|\| 1.24.1-3 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*narāṇāṃ yoṣitāṃ caiva lakṣaṇāni mahāmate \|*  
*proktāni yāni viprendra vyomakeśasya sūnunā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kruddhena yāni kṣiptāni īśvareṇa mahodadhau \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya vacanād bhūyaḥ samudreṇārpitāni vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

*arpitāni tatastasya tena prāptāni vai kathan \|*  
*bāhuleyena viprendra tāni me vada suvrata \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Shatanika said — O excellent one, Karttikeya — the son of Parvati, had spoken about the symptoms of men and women. Lord Shiva getting annoyed with the same had thrown them in the ocean, O excellent Brahmana, but at the command of lord Krishna, they were redeemed from the ocean and returned to Karttikeya. Then how did Karttikeya get them back. You kindly narrate the relevant story.

## \|\| 1.24.4 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*yathā guhena rājendra strīpuṃsāṃ lakṣaṇāni vai \|*  
*proktāni kuruśārdūla tathā te kathayāmi vai \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Sumantu said — I am going to narrate the story concerning the symptoms of men and women.

## \|\| 1.24.5 \|\|

*śaktipātāddhate krauñce vyomakeśasya sūnunā \|*  
*brahmā tuṣṭo'bravīdenaṃ varaṃ varaya me'nagha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the time when Karttikeya, the son of Vyomakesha had tom out the Krauncha mountain, Brahma got pleased with him and he said to him with delight — “O auspicious soul, I am extremely pleased with your effort, Therefore you ask for a boon from me.”

## \|\| 1.24.6 \|\|

*asāvapi mahātejāḥ praṇamya śirasā vibhum \|*  
*pitāmahaṃ babhāṣedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi me vibho \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing this, the illustrious Svami Karttikeya, lowering his head in reverence, said to Brahma — “You kindly tell me the symptoms of men and women.”

## \|\| 1.24.7-8 \|\|

*narāṇāṃ yuvatīnāṃ ca kautukaṃ paramaṃ mama \|*  
*yanmayoktaṃ purā deva prakṣiptaṃ lavaṇārṇave \|\| 7 \|\|*

*matpitrā devadeveśa sakrodhena purā tathā \|*  
*prāptaṃ ca vismṛtaṃ bhūyastanme brūhi hyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. I had spoken about the symptoms of men and women (which were written down) but were thrown into the ocean in anger by lord Shiva, my great father. I have got it back, the same has been lost from my memory. Therefore, you kindly enlighten me on the subject comprehensively, because I am quite anxious to learn about the same. You kindly narrate the same to me in detail.

## \|\| 1.24.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi deveśa bhīmasyānandavardhana \|*  
*lakṣaṇāni nibodha tvaṃ puruṣāṇāmaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*adhamottamamadhyāni yāni prāpa payonidhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Brahma said — O lord of the Devas, you enhance the delight of Bhima, you have put in an excellent question. I shall narrate the best, medium and bad symptoms of the men which were received by the ocean, to you.

## \|\| 1.24.10-11 \|\|

*śive'hani sunakṣatre grahe saumye śubhe ravau \|*  
*pūrvāhṇe maṅgalairyukte parīkṣeta vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pramāṇaṃ saṃhatiṃ chāyāṃ gatiṃ sarvāṅgalakṣaṇam \|*  
*dantakeśanakhaśmaśru etatsarvaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The auspicious constellation, favourable planets and when the sun is lodged in the auspicious place, on some auspicious day, a learned person should study about the length, movements, teeth, hair, nails, beard and all the symptoms of the body.

## \|\| 1.24.12 \|\|

*pūrvamāyuḥ parīkṣeta paścāllakṣaṇamādiśet \|*  
*kṣīṇe hyāyuṣi martyānāṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ kiṃ prayojanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. While conducting the study, first of all one should study about the age, the other symptoms should be examined subsequently. Because in case the concerned person has a short life, then the study of the symptoms would be fruitless.

## \|\| 1.24.13-14 \|\|

*jaghanyo navatiḥ prokto madhyamastu śatāḍgulaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ yasya uttamaṃ tasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ samudreṇa śubhāśubham \|*  
*yanme purā devavara mayā vai kathitaṃ tava \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dehāvayavalakṣaṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. A person, who according to his own finger has the height of a hundred and eight fingers, or hundred or ninety fingers he should be treated as the one having the best, medium and degraded symptoms respectively. O excellent god, these auspicious or inauspicious symptoms were revealed before me by the ocean itself. Thereafter, the symptoms of the other parts of the body are being narrated by me.

## \|\| 1.24.15 \|\|

*pādaiḥ samāṃsakaiḥ 2 snigdhai raktaṃ saumyaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ \|*  
*unnataiḥ svedarahitaiḥ śirāhīnaiśca pārthivaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A person whose feet are fleshy with red complexion, pleasant, slippery, attractive, raised, free from sweating and in which the veins are not visible, he becomes a monarch.

## \|\| 1.24.16 \|\|

*yasya pādatale rekhā sāṃkuśeva prakāśate \|*  
*satataṃ hi sukhaṃ tasya puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The foot in the sole of whom has the lines resembling a goad, he always remains delightful.

## \|\| 1.24.17-18 \|\|

*asvedanau mṛdutalau kamalodarasannibhau \|*  
*śliṣṭāṅgulī 1 tāmranakhau supārṣṇī vyomakeśaja \|\| 17 \|\|*

*uṣṇau śirāvirahitau gūḍhagulphau ca bhīmaja \|*  
*kūrmonnatau ca caraṇau prakhyātau pārthivasya tu \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. O Karttikeya, a person whose soles of the feet are free from perspiration, soft, beautiful like the lotus, with joined toes, nails with red colour, beautiful heel, without veins, with hot and tick ankle, curved like the tortoise, he surely becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.24.19-20 \|\|

*śūrpākṛtī mahābāho rūkṣau śvetanakhau tathā \|*  
*vakrau śirāsantatau ca saṃśuṣkau viralāṅgulī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dāridryaduḥkhadau jñeyau caraṇau bhīmanandana \|*  
*brahmaghnau devaśārdūla 3 pakvamṛtsadṛśau padau \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. O son of Bhima, with long arms, the feet with the lines resembling the winnowing baskets, the nails of white colour, uneven nails, covered with veins, with separated dry toes, belong to the unfortunate and poverty stricken persons. O lion among the gods, a person having the feet like the baked clay, is the killer of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.24.21-22 \|\|

*pītāvagamyāniratau kṛṣṇau pānaratau sadā \|*  
*abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe śvetau jñeyau senādhipottama \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aṅguṣṭhau pṛthulau yeṣāṃ te narā bhāgyavarjitāḥ \|*  
*kliśyante vikṛtāṅguṣṭhāste narāḥ pādagāminaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Similarly, a person whose feet are of yellow colour, he unites with the discarded woman. In case the feet are of black colour, he becomes a drunkard, and when they are of white colour, the concerned person consumes the forbidden food.

## \|\| 1.24.23 \|\|

*cipiṭairvikṛtairbhagnairaṅguṣṭhairatininditāḥ \|*  
*vakrairbhagnaistathā hrasvairaṅguṣṭhaiḥ kleśabhāginaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When the thumb of a foot is quite thick, he becomes unfortunate and when there is a defect in one’s thumb of the foot, he walks with bare feet and always remain miserable.

## \|\| 1.24.24 \|\|

*śūrpākāraiśca vikṛtairbhagnarvakraiḥ śirātataiḥ \|*  
*sasvedaiḥ pāṇḍurūkṣaiśca caraṇairatininditāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Because those possessing feet resembling the winnowing basket, defective, disorderly feet, filled with veins and perspiration, besides the feet with yellow colour or the dry feet, should be known as deplorable.

## \|\| 1.24.25 \|\|

*yasya pradeśinī dīrghā aṅguṣṭhaṃ yā atikramet \|*  
*strībhogaṃ labhate nityaṃ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kaniṣṭhāyāṃ tu dīrghāyāṃ suvarṇasya tu bhāginaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The foot having the forefinger of the toe bigger in size than that of the foot thumb, he surely enjoys all the pleasures with his wife. In case the little two is bigger in size than the thumb, he surely gains gold (and other riches).

## \|\| 1.24.26 \|\|

*cipiṭā viralāḥ śuṣkā yasyāṅgulyo bhavanti vai \|*  
*sa bhavedduḥkhito nityaṃ dhanahīnaśca vai 4 guha \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Guha, a person whose toes, of the feet are flat, loose and dry, he is always penniless and faces misery.

## \|\| 1.24.27 \|\|

*śvetairnakhairvirūkṣaiśca puruṣā duḥkhajīvinaḥ \|*  
*kuśīlāḥ kunakhairjñeyāḥ kāmabhogavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*vikṛtaiḥ sphuṭitairūkṣairnakhairdāridryabhāginaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A person whose nails of the toes are whitish, extremely dry, besides being defective, he is devoid of humility, and is unable to enjoy the worldly pleasures. In case a person has expanded or dry feet, he remains a pauper.

## \|\| 1.24.28 \|\|

*brahmahatyāṃ ca kurvanti puruṣā haritairnakhaiḥ \|*  
*bandhubhiśca viyujyante kulakṣayakarāśca te \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person with green nails of the toes, indulges in the killing of a Brahmana, and remains separate from his brothers besides being the destroyer of his whole family.

## \|\| 1.24.29 \|\|

*indragopakasaṃkāśairnakhairnṛpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhāvartapratīkāśairnakhairbhavati pārthivaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The feet with nails resembling lady bird of red colour, and nails curved like the conch, always belong to the rulers.

## \|\| 1.24.30 \|\|

*tāmrairnakhaistathaiśvaryaṃ dhanyāḥ padmanakhā narāḥ \|*  
*raktairnakhaistathaiśvaryaṃ puṣpitaiḥ subhago bhavet \|*  
*sūkṣmairupacitaistāmrairnakhairnṛpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The people with the nails of copper colour possess enormous fortunes and those having the nails resembling the lotus flowers, are graceful. The people with red nails of the feet are also said to be possessing high fortunes. The people with the developed toes of the feet remain beautiful. Those having subtle and developed nails of copper colour become the kings.

## \|\| 1.24.31 \|\|

*romaśābhyāṃ ca jaṅghābhyāṃ duḥkhadāridryabhāginaḥ \|*  
*bandhanaṃ hrasvajaṅghānāmaiśvaryaṃ caiva nirdiśet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A person with hair in the thighs, he remains painful and poor. Those having small thighs, have to face bondages besides fortunes.

## \|\| 1.24.32-34 \|\|

*1 mṛgajaṅghāśca rājāno jāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*dīrghajaṅghāḥ sthūlajaṅghā nityaṃ bhāgyavivarjitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śṛgālajaṅghāḥ puruṣā nityaṃ bhāgyavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*kākajaṃghā narā ye tu bhaveyurduḥkhabhāginaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*2 pīnajaṅghāstathaiśvaryaṃ prāpnuvanti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*siṃhavyāghrasamā jaṅghā dhaninaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Those having the thighs resembling those of a deer, undoubtedly become the kings. Those having long, thick thighs resembling those of a jackal or a crow, always remain miserable and unfortunate. The persons with thick thighs always remain miserable, devoid of fortunes. Those having the thighs resembling the kin or a tiger, remain always wealthy.

## \|\| 1.24.35-36 \|\|

*pārthivānāṃ bhavedroma caikaikaṃ romakūpake \|*  
*paṃḍitaśrotriyāṇāṃ ca dvedve jñeye mahāmate \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tribhistribhistathā niḥsvā mānavā duḥkhabhāginaḥ \|*  
*keśāścaiva mahābāho ninditā pūjitāstathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. In case there is a single hair in each one of the skin pores, he becomes a king. In case there are two of them in one pore, he becomes a Vedic scholar and in case there are three hair in each pore, he becomes quite poor. O long armed one, thus the good and bad symptoms of hair and hair on the body should be understood accordingly.

## \|\| 1.24.37 \|\|

*nirmāṃsajānurmriyate pravāse śivanandana 3 \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O son of Shiva, a person whose knees are not fleshy, he dies in foreign land.

## \|\| 1.24.38 \|\|

*saubhāgyamalpai kathitaṃ dāridryaṃ vikaṭaistathā \|*  
*nimnaiḥ svastrījitā jñeyāḥ samāṃsai rājyabhāginaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Similarly, the one who has small knees, he becomes fortunate. In case the knees are obscure, he faces poverty; when they are bent downwards, he faces defeat from his wife, while the thick knee bestows the kingship.

## \|\| 1.24.39 \|\|

*4 haṃsabhāsaśukānāṃ ca tulyā yasya gatirbhavet \|*  
*sa bhavetpārthivaḥ pūjyaḥ samudravacanaṃ yathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One who walks like the swan, peacock, or parrot, he is adored as a king, as has been revealed by the ocean.

## \|\| 1.24.40 \|\|

*anyeṣāmapi śastānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ ca śubhā gatiḥ \|*  
*vṛṣasiṃhagajendrāṇāṃ 6 gatirbhogavivardhinī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the walk resembles those of other auspicious birds, it is also treated as good. When one walks like the lion or an elephant, he enjoys life.

## \|\| 1.24.41 \|\|

*jalormisadṛśī yā ca kākolūkasamā ca yā \|*  
*gatirdravyavihīnānāṃ duḥkhaśokabhayaṅkarā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those who walk like the waves of the water or like the crow, owl etc., they face misfortunes in their life.

## \|\| 1.24.42 \|\|

*śvānoṣṭmahiṣāṇāṃ 1 kharasūkarayostathā \|*  
*gatirmeṣasamā yeṣāṃ te narā bhāgyavarjitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Similarly, those who walk resembling the walking of a dog, camel, he buffalo, donkey, pig, and the sheep, it is indication of misfortune.

## Chapter 25. Symptoms of men

## \|\| 1.25.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣiṇāvartaliṅgaśca naro vai putramānbhavet \|*  
*vāmāvarte tathā liṅge naraḥ kanyāṃ prasūyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — A person whose phallus leans towards the right side, then he gives birth to a son and in case it is leaning to the left, he gives birth to daughters.

## \|\| 1.25.2 \|\|

*yasya pāṇitale rekhā kaniṣṭhāmūlamutthitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The phallus with thick veins is indicative of poverty. In case, it is straight or round, it is indicative of producing sons.

## \|\| 1.25.3 \|\|

*nimnapādopaviṣṭasya bhūmiṃ spṛśati mehanaḥ \|*  
*duḥkhitaṃ taṃ vijānīyātpuruṣaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. While seated on his feet in case the phallus of a person touches the earth, he surely becomes miserable.

## \|\| 1.25.4 \|\|

*bhūmau pādopaviṣṭasya gulphau spṛśati mehanaḥ \|*  
*īśvaraṃ taṃ vijānīyātpramadānāṃ ca vallabham2 \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Similarly, when seated on feet if the phallus touches the heels, he becomes beloved of the women, besides being a king.

## \|\| 1.25.5 \|\|

*siṃhavyāghrasamo yasya hrasvau bhavati mehanaḥ \|*  
*bhogavānsa tu vijñeyo'śeṣabhogasamanvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A person having a phallus of small size resembling that of a lion or a tiger, he enjoys all the pleasures in the world.

## \|\| 1.25.6 \|\|

*rekhākṛtirmaṇiryasya mehane hi virājate \|*  
*pārthivaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ samudravacanaṃ yathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. According to the words of the ocean, a person whose forepart of the phallus resembles a line, he becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.25.7 \|\|

*suvarṇarajataprakhyairmaṇimuktāsamaprabhaiḥ \|*  
*pravālasadṛśaiḥ snigdhairmaṇibhiḥ pārthivo bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly, when the phallus has the complexion of gold, silver, gems, beads or paddy straw, besides being greasy, it is indicative of a person becoming a king.

## \|\| 1.25.8-10 \|\|

*pāṇḍurairmalinai rūkṣairdīrghavyāsairdiśo vrajet \|*  
*samaistathonnataiścāpi susnigdhairmaṇibhirgṛhī \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dhanarakṣāstathā strīṇāṃ bhoktāraste bhavanti hi \|*  
*maṇibhirmadhyanimnaistu pitaraste bhavanti hi \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yuvatīnāṃ mahābāho niḥsvāścāpi bhavanti te \|*  
*nolbaṇaiścāpi dhanino narā vīrā bhavanti hi \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. A person whose phallus is white or of yellow colour or dry and dirty, he represents a person who roams about in all the directions. When the forepart of a phallus is even, raised and slippery, the person is like by the woman and preserves the wealth. In case the middle of the forepart is lowered, then he becomes father of daughters alone besides being poor. O valorous one, when it is unclear or hazy, the person becomes wealthy.

## \|\| 1.25.11 \|\|

*mūtradhārā patedekā valitā dakṣiṇā yadi \|*  
*sa bhavetpārthivaḥ pṛthvyāḥ samudravacanaṃ yathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In case one’s urine falls in two streams towards the right then he according to the ocean, becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.25.12 \|\|

*dve dhāre ca tathā snigdhe dhanavānbhogavānsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*bahudhārāstathā rūkṣāḥ saśabdāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In case the urine falls in two streams being slippery, he becomes rich enjoying all the pleasures. The urine of a degraded person is dry and falls creating sound.

## \|\| 1.25.13 \|\|

*mīnagandhi bhavedreto dhanavānputravānbhavet \|*  
*havigandhi bhavedyasya dhanāḍhyaḥ śrotriyaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person who has the fishlike smell in his semen, he possesses sons and riches. In case the related smell resembles the one from the fire of homa, he becomes rich besides a Vedic scholar.

## \|\| 1.25.14 \|\|

*1 mūṣagandhirbhavetputrī padmagandhirnṛpaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*lākṣāgandhirbhavedyaśca bahukanyaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*madyagandhirbhavedyoddhā kṣāragandhirdaridrakaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the semen of a person smells like the sheep, he gets sons and the one whose semen smells like lotus, he becomes a king. In case the semen smells like shellac, then he gets more of daughters and when the smell resembles wine, he becomes a warrior and in case it is saltish, the concerned person becomes poor.

## \|\| 1.25.15 \|\|

*śīghramaithunagāmī yaḥ sa dīrghāyurato'nyathā \|*  
*alpāyurdevaśārdūla vijñeyo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The one who cohabits quickly, enjoys long life. O lion among the gods, a person with the contrary symptoms, shall have a short life.

## \|\| 1.25.16 \|\|

*tanuśukraḥ strījanako māṃsagandhī ca bhogavān \|*  
*padmavarṇaṃ bhavedraktaṃ sa naro dhanavānbhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A person having lesser semen gets daughters only. In case the semen smells like the flesh, he enjoys all the pleasures. A person having the blood resembling the red lotus, he becomes rich.

## \|\| 1.25.17 \|\|

*kiñcidraktaṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ bhavedyasya tu śoṇitam \|*  
*adhamaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ sadā duḥkhaikabhājanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The one having short of blood of black colour, he should be considered as degraded and miserable.

## \|\| 1.25.18 \|\|

*pravālasadṛśaṃ snigdhaṃ bhavedyasya ca śoṇitam \|*  
*rājānaṃ taṃ vijānīyātsaptadvīpādhipaṃ guha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O Guha, a person whose blood has the colour of coral and greasy, he becomes the ruler of seven continents.

## \|\| 1.25.19 \|\|

*vistīrṇā māṃsalā snigdhā vastiḥ puṃsāṃ praśasyate \|*  
*nirmāṃsā vikaṭā rūkṣā bastiryeṣāṃ na te śubhāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In case the lower region below the navel is fleshy, broad besides being greasy, then it is considered as auspicious. In case it is deformed and dry, then it is inauspicious.

## \|\| 1.25.20 \|\|

*gomāyusadṛśī yasya śvānoṣṭramahiṣasya ca \|*  
*sa bhavedduḥkhito nityaṃ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A person whose bladder resembles a male jackal, a dog, a camel and the he-buffalos, he always has to face miseries.

## \|\| 1.25.21 \|\|

*yaścaikavṛṣaṇastāta jale prāṇānvimuñjati \|*  
*strīcañcalastu viṣamaiḥ samai rājyaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O excellent owl, a person having a single testicle, he dies in water, In case they are of unequal size, such a person is immoral and a person having testicles of equal size, he enjoys the position of a king.

## \|\| 1.25.22 \|\|

*ūrdhvagaiścāpi hrasvāyuḥ śatañjīvī pralambadhṛk \|*  
*mānavāścāpi raktaistu dhanavanto bhavanti vai \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In case it is raised up, then the person has a short life and in case it is extraordinarily big, the person has a long life of a hundred years. In case the testicles are of red colour, the concerned person becomes quite rich.

## \|\| 1.25.23-24 \|\|

*sthūlasphigbhavati kṣemī dravyayuktaḥ samāṃsadhṛk \|*  
*vyāghrasphiṅmaṇḍalo rājā maṇḍūkasphiṅnarādhipaḥ \|*  
*dvimaṇḍalo mahābāho siṃhasphiksārvabhaumatā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*uṣṭravānarayoryastu dhārayetsphiṅmahāmate \|*  
*dhanadhānyavihīno'sau vijñeyo bhīmanandana \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. In case the part of the body below the waist is stiff, then it is beneficial. In case that part is fleshy, the person gets rich, in case it resembles that of a tiger, he becomes the king of rulers. In case it resembles one with a frog, the person becomes the king, and in case it resembles that of a lion, such a person becomes the king of two countries. O immensely intelligent one, in case it resembles that of a camel or a monkey, it brings poverty to a person.

## \|\| 1.25.25 \|\|

*pumānmṛgodaro dhanyo mayūrodara eva ca \|*  
*vyāghrodaro narapatī rājā siṃhodaro bhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A person whose belly resembles that of a deer or a peacock, he is considered to be the best of the person. In case it resembles that of a tiger, he becomes the lord of rulers and in case it is like that of a lion, he becomes a ruler.

## \|\| 1.25.26 \|\|

*maṇḍūkasadṛśaṃ yasya puruṣasyodaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*sa bhavetpārthivaḥ puṣṭyā samudravacanaṃ yathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A person having the belly like a frog, he according to the words of the ocean, becomes the lord of earth.

## \|\| 1.25.27-28 \|\|

*māṃsalairṛjubhirvṛttaiḥ pārśvairnṛpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*īśvaro vyāghrapṛṣṭhastu senāyāścaiva nāyakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*siṃhapṛṣṭho naro yastu bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet \|*  
*kūrmapṛṣṭhāstu rājāno dhanasaubhāgyabhāginaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. A person whose back is fleshy, straight and circular, he becomes the lord of the kings. A person whose back is comparable with that of a tiger, he becomes the chief commander of the army. In case it resembles the one of a lion, he becomes a prisoner and whose back resembles the one of a tortoise, he becomes a king, who enjoys all the pleasures.

## \|\| 1.25.29 \|\|

*vistīrṇaṃ hadayaṃ yeṣāṃ māṃsalomacitaṃ samam \|*  
*śatāyuṣo vijānīyādbhogabhājo mahādhanān \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A person having a large heart, covered hair besides being fleshy, he lives for a hundred years, possessing enormous riches.

## \|\| 1.25.30 \|\|

*viralāḥ śuṣkāstathā rūkṣā dṛśyante'ṅgulayaḥ kare \|*  
*sa bhaved duḥkhito nityaṃ naro dāridryabhājanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In case the hand fingers of a person are loose, dry and rough, he always remain miserable overpowered with poverty.

## \|\| 1.25.31 \|\|

*yasya mīnasamā rekhā karmasiddhibhra tasya tu \|*  
*dhanavānsa tu vijñeyo bahuputraśca mānavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When a person has the lines in the hand resembling a fish, he meets with success in all his efforts, besides having enormous riches and sons.

## \|\| 1.25.32 \|\|

*tulā yasya tu vedī vā karamadhye tu dṛśyate \|*  
*tasya sidhyati vāṇijyaṃ puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In case a person has lines in his hands resembling a scale or a pedestal, then there would be no doubt in the success of his trade and business.

## \|\| 1.25.33 \|\|

*saumye pāṇitale yasya dvijasya tu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yajñayājī bhavennityaṃ bahuvittaśca mānavaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When the hand of a person and particularly that of a Brahmana is quite beautiful, be becomes quite rich, performing the yajnas,

## \|\| 1.25.34 \|\|

*śailaṃ vāpyatha vā vṛkṣaḥ karamadhye tu dṛśyate \|*  
*acalāṃ śriyamāpnoti bahubhṛtyasamanvitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In case the lines of a person resemble those of a tree or a hill, he becomes owner of enormous riches and others fortunes.

## \|\| 1.25.35 \|\|

*śaktitomarabāṇāsirekhā 1 cāpopamā tathā \|*  
*yasya haste mahābāho sa jayedvigrahe ripūn \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O long armed one, when the lines on the hands of a person resemble a Shakti, a club, arrow sword and the bow, he achieves victory over his enemies.

## \|\| 1.25.36 \|\|

*dhvajabhrāpyatha vā śaṃkhaḥ karamadhye tu dṛśyate \|*  
*samudrayāyī sa bhaveddhanī ca satataṃ guha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Guha, in case in the centre of the palm, there are lines resembling the flag or a conch, he always remains rich and travels abroad.

## \|\| 1.25.37 \|\|

*śrīvatsamatha vā padmaṃ vajraṃ vā cakameva ca \|*  
*ratho vāpyatha vā kumbho yasya haste prakāśate \|*  
*rājānaṃ taṃ vijānīyātparasainyavidāraṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A person whose hand is decorated with the lines resembling the symbols of Shrivatsa, lotus, vajra, cakra, chariot or a pitcher, he becomes the destroyer of the enemy army.

## \|\| 1.25.38 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe tu karāṅguṣṭhe yavo yasya tu dṛśyate \|*  
*sarvavidyāpravaktā ca bhavedvai nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. When the right hand thumb of a person has the symbol of barley, he surely attains all the lores, besides being an excellent orator. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.25.39 \|\|

*gatā madhyaṃ pradeśinyāḥ sa jīveccharadaḥ śatam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When the line in the hand of a person, starts from the root of the little finger and reaches the middle of the forefinger, he surely enjoys the long life of a hundred years.

## Chapter 26. Symptoms of men

## \|\| 1.26.1 \|\|

*nirmāṃsau yasya vai karṇau saṃgrāmānnāśamṛcchati \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — A person having the even belly enjoys all the pleasures, the one having the uneven belly cheats people, indulging in fraudulent ways.

## \|\| 1.26.2 \|\|

*rājā syānnimnakukṣistu sārvabhaumo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sarpodarā daridrāḥ syurbahubhakṣāśca suvrata \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O person with excellent vratas! Similarly, a person with low belly is a valorous king. The one having the belly resembling that of a serpent becomes a pauper, besides being a glutton.

## \|\| 1.26.3 \|\|

*vistīrṇābhirmaṇḍalābhirunnatābhiśca nābhibhiḥ \|*  
*bhavanti sukhino vīrā dhanadhānyasamanvitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A person with broad, round and raised navel always remains rich and comfortable, besides possessing enough of food grains etc.

## \|\| 1.26.4 \|\|

*nimnābhiratha svalpābhiḥ kleśabhājo bhavanti hi \|*  
*valirmadhyaṅgatā vīrā viṣamā ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dhanahāniṃ tathā śūlaṃ nityaṃ janayate vibho \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A person with low and small navel always remains miserable. In case the navel passes through the three lines of the belly, causes the loss of wealth and constant pain in stomach.

## \|\| 1.26.5 \|\|

*vāmāvārtā sadā śāntiṃ karotīti vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*karoti medhāṃ dakṣiṇena saṃpravṛttā divaspate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Similarly, the navel which is turned to the left bestows peace and this is well known to the learned people.

## \|\| 1.26.6 \|\|

*pārśvāyatā dīrghamāyuraiśvaryamūrdhvataḥ smṛtam \|*  
*gavāḍhyatāmadhastāttu karotīti vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When the upper part of the navel of a person is quite vast, he enjoys a long life. In case it is raised upwards, then he enjoys all the riches and in case it is turned towards the lower side, then he has enough of cows, which is well known to the learned people.

## \|\| 1.26.7 \|\|

*śatapatrakarṇikābhā nābhiryasya mahāmate \|*  
*bhūpatvaṃ kurute sā tu puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly, when the navel of a person resembles a lotus, he undoubtedly becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.26.8 \|\|

*samodaro bhavedbhogī nisvaḥ syādviṣamodaraḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmodaro bhavedvāgmī bahusampatsamanvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A person with even belly enjoys all the pleasures, the one having an uneven belly becomes poor, and the one with squeezed belly becomes a warrior, an orator or a rich person.

## \|\| 1.26.9 \|\|

*śastreṇāntaṃ vrajedvīra strībhogaṃ cāpnuyāttathā \|*  
*ācāryo bahuputraśca yathāsaṅkhyaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In case of a person having a single line in the belly, he meets with his death with a weapon. The one having two lines enjoys all the pleasures, and with three lines he becomes an Acharya with many sons.

## \|\| 1.26.10 \|\|

*valibhirdevaśārdūla ityāha sa payonidhiḥ \|*  
*agamyāgāmino jñeyā viṣamābhirna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O lion among the gods, this is what has been told by the ocean, that when a person has an uneven line over the belly, then it is certain that he has relations with a fallen or unchaste woman.

## \|\| 1.26.11 \|\|

*ṛjubhirvasubhogī syātparadāravinindakaḥ \|*  
*māṃsalairmṛdubhiḥ pārśvai rājā syānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When the line is quite straight, the concerned person enjoys the wealth, while denouncing the wives of others. In case the lines are fleshy on both the sides, then he undoubtedly becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.26.12 \|\|

*anūrdhvacibukā ye tu subhagāste bhavanti vai \|*  
*nirdhanā viṣamairdīrghairbhavantīha suvīraja \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The chin which is not raised upwards is certainly auspicious. O son of Suvira, similarly the uneven and long chin is indicative of poverty.

## \|\| 1.26.13 \|\|

*pīnaiścopacitairnimnaiḥ 1 skandhairbhīmāṅgasambhava \|*  
*rājānaḥ sukhinaścāpi bhavantīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Similarly, the thick, raised as well as the low shoulder makes one comfortable and even a king. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.26.14 \|\|

*samonnataṃ tu hṛdayaṃ samaṃ ca pṛthu caiva hi \|*  
*avepanaṃ māṃsalaṃ ca pārthivānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The event, raised or little thick shoulder when filled with stable and fleshy formation, belongs to the kings.

## \|\| 1.26.15 \|\|

*khararomacitaṃ vīraśirālaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*adhanānāṃ bhavedeva hṛdayaṃ ṛbhavottama \|*  
*samavakṣaso'rthayutāḥ pīnaiḥ śūrāḥ smṛtā budhaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O best of the Devas, the chest with hard hair and projecting the veins, belongs to the people who are power stricken. A person with even chest represents fortune and when it is thick, it stands for valorous people. This has been testified by the learned people.

## \|\| 1.26.16 \|\|

*tanubhirdravyahīnāḥ syurasamaiścāpyakiñcanāḥ \|*  
*vadhyante cāpi śastreṇa nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In case it is small, it is meant for poor people and when it is uneven, the concerned person meets with his end, with the striking of a weapon. This is sure without controversy.

## \|\| 1.26.17 \|\|

*hanubhirviṣamairvīra janmahīno bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*yasyonnato bhaveddhanuḥ sa bhogī syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A person having an uneven chin has a short life. A person with a low chin undoubtedly enjoys all the pleasures.

## \|\| 1.26.18 \|\|

*nirmāṃsairviṣamairvīra niḥsvo nimnaiḥ pracakṣyate \|*  
*dhanavāṃśca bhavetpīnaiḥ sukhabhogasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*viṣamairarthahīnaḥ syādduḥkhabhāgī sadā naraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When the chin is devoid of flesh, uneven and low, the concerned person is certainly poor. When the chin of a person is thick, he becomes rich, comfortable and enjoys all the pleasures. Similarly, a person with uneven chin is devoid of riches and always remains miserable.

## \|\| 1.26.19-20 \|\|

*cipiṭagrīvako duṣṭo mato loke sa vai guha \|*  
*śūraḥ syānmahiṣagrīvo mṛgagrīvo bhayāturaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kambugrīvo bhavedrājā lambakaṇṭho'gralakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*hrasvagrīvastu dhanavānsusukhī bhogavāṃstathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. O Guha, a person whose neck is flat, he is said to be a wicked person on earth, similarly a person having a neck resembling the one of a buffalo, becomes a warrior. One having the neck resembling that of a deer is always fearful, the one having the neck resembling a conch becomes a king, besides a person with a long neck possesses all the auspicious symptoms, while the person with a short neck possesses riches besides being comfortable and enjoys all the pleasures.

## \|\| 1.26.21 \|\|

*nimāṃsau romaśau bhagnāvalpau vāpi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*nirdhanasyedṛśāvaṃsau prakhyātau vyomakeśaja \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O son of Shiva, a curved shoulder, besides being fleshy, short one, is meant for the poor people.

## \|\| 1.26.22 \|\|

*bhavedaromaśaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ dhanināṃ bhīmasambhava \|*  
*salomaśaṃ tathā vakraṃ nirdhanānāṃ balādhipa \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O chief commander! Similarly, the back without the hair, is possessed by the rich people, while the curved back full of hair belongs to the poor people.

## \|\| 1.26.23 \|\|

*asvedanāvunnatau ca tathā pīnau ṣaḍānana \|*  
*samaromasugandhau ca kakṣau jñeyau dhanānvitau \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The armpit free from heaviness, thick, raised one, and fragrant without hair, is possessed by the rich people.

## \|\| 1.26.24 \|\|

*avyucchinnau tathā śliṣṭau vipulau ca surādhipa \|*  
*śūrāṇāmīdṛśāvaṃsau nagajānandavardhana \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O lord of gods! An even, broad and a thick shoulder belongs only to the immensely valorous people.

## \|\| 1.26.25 \|\|

*udvṛddhabāhuko yastu vadhabandhanamāpnuyāt \|*  
*dīrghabāhurbhavedrājā samudravacanaṃ yathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A person who arms are stretched upwards, such a person meets with his end in bondage. According to the words of ocean, a person with long arms becomes the king.

## \|\| 1.26.26 \|\|

*pralambabāhurvijñeyo naraḥ sarvaguṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*hrasvabāhurbhaveddāsaḥ parapreṣyakaro'pi vā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A person with exceedingly long arms possesses enormous virtues. It should be well understood. A person with short arms becomes a messenger or a slave.

## \|\| 1.26.27 \|\|

*vāmāvartabhujā ye tu dīrghāyatabhujāśca ye \|*  
*sampūrṇabāhū rājā syādityāha sa payonidhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A person with full arms those turned to the left, or the one with full arms, becomes a king. This is what has been spoken by the ocean.

## \|\| 1.26.28 \|\|

*grīvā ca 1 vartulākārā kamburekhāsamāvṛtā \|*  
*sa bhavetpārthivo bhūmau sarvaduṣṭanibarhaṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person with a round neck resembling a conch in lines, destroys all the wicked people of the earth, becoming a king.

## \|\| 1.26.29 \|\|

*dīrghagrīvā bakagrīvā śukagrīvāśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*uṣṭragrīvāḥ karigrīvāḥ sarve te nirdhanāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When a person has a neck which is quite long resembling that of skylark, parrot, camel and elephant, he becomes a poor.

## \|\| 1.26.30 \|\|

*ibhāṅgasadṛśau2 vṛttau samau pīnau ca suvrata \|*  
*ājānulambinau bāhū pārthivānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Suvrata, the arms resembling the elephant trunk, thick and circular falling upto the knees, surely belong to the kings.

## \|\| 1.26.31 \|\|

*daridrāṇāṃ lomaśau hrasvau bāhū jñeyau surottama \|*  
*taskarāṇāṃ ca viṣamau sthūlau sūkṣmau ca suvrata \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O best of the gods, the short arms covered with hair are possessed by the poor people. Besides the above, the arms which are raised or lowered, thick as well as the thin, belong to the thieves.

## \|\| 1.26.32 \|\|

*nimnaṃ karatalaṃ yasya pitṛvittaṃ na tasya vai \|*  
*bhavedārbhavaśārdūla tathā bhīruśca mānavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A person having the deep palm of the hand, can never inherit the ancestral property or riches. He also becomes a coward.

## \|\| 1.26.33 \|\|

*suvṛttatanunimnena dhanavānkaratalena tu \|*  
*uttānakaratalo dātā bhavatīti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A person with a beautiful, round, thin and deep hand palm, becomes rich, while the one with raised palm becomes a donor.

## \|\| 1.26.34 \|\|

*viṣamā bhavanti viṣamairnimnāścāpi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*karatalairdevaśārdūla lākṣābhairīśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The one having the uneven and usually deep palm is not considered to be auspicious. O Deva! A person having the hand palm resembling the colour of lac, becomes rich.

## \|\| 1.26.35 \|\|

*agamyāgamanaṃ pītai rūkṣairnirdhanatā smṛtā \|*  
*apeyapānaṃ kurvanti nīlakṛṣṇaiḥ sadaiva hi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A person with yellow palm has sexual relationship with an unchaste woman. The one with a dry palm becomes pauper, the one with blue and black palm, always consumes the prohibited beverages.

## \|\| 1.26.36 \|\|

*nimnāḥ snigdhā bhavennṛṇāṃ rekhā karatale guha \|*  
*dhanināṃ na daridrāṇāmityāha sa payonidhiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The lower and greasy lines are found in the hands of rich people and not with the poor people. This has been told by the ocean.

## \|\| 1.26.37 \|\|

*viralāṅgulayo ye tu te daridrāḥ pracakṣate \|*  
*dhaninastu mahābāho ye ghanāṅgulayo narāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When the fingers of the hands of a person are sparse, he becomes a pauper, according to the ocean. The person whose fingers are stick close to one another, he becomes wealthy.

## \|\| 1.26.38 \|\|

*vadanaṃ maṇḍalaṃ yasya dharmaśīlaṃ tamādiśet \|*  
*śuṇḍavaktrā narā ye tu durbhagāste na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A person with a round face becomes religious minded. A person having the face resembling the trunk of an elephant, undoubtedly becomes unfortunate.

## \|\| 1.26.39-40 \|\|

*harivaktrā jihmavaktrā vikṛtāsyāstathā narāḥ \|*  
*bhagnavatrāḥ karālāsyā sarve te taskarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sampūrṇavaktrā rājāno gajasiṃhānanāstathā \|*  
*chāgavānaravaktrāśca dhaninaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The people having the deformed faces like the lions are unfortunate. The beautiful face is possessed by the rulers. The people possessing the faces resembling those of an elephant, lion, male goat and monkey, are always rich and wealthy.

## \|\| 1.26.41 \|\|

*yasya gaṇḍau susampūrṇau padmapatrasamaprabhau \|*  
*kṛṣibhāgī bhavennityaṃ bahuvittaśca mānavaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A person whose cheeks are charming like the lotus leaf, he is always interested in fanning.

## \|\| 1.26.42 \|\|

*siṃhavyāghragajendrāṇāṃ kapolaḥ sadṛśo yadi \|*  
*mahābhogī sa vijñeyaḥ senāyāścaiva nāyakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A person having the cheeks resembling the lion, tiger or elephant, enjoys all the worldly pleasures, besides being the chief of the army.

## \|\| 1.26.43 \|\|

*vadanaṃ tu samaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ saumyaṃ saṃvṛtameva hi \|*  
*pārthivānāṃ mahābāho viparītantu duḥkhadam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The event, greasy, round and beautiful face is possessed by the kings. O long armed one, the faces which are otherwise, are of miserable people.

## \|\| 1.26.44 \|\|

*mahāmukhaṃ tu deveśa durbhagatvaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*strīmukhaṃ putranāśāya maṇḍalaṃ sukhitāṃ vrajet \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O lord of gods, the broad face is indicative of unfortunate people. A person when possesses a woman like face, it is indicative of the looks of his son. But the round face is indicative of comfort.

## \|\| 1.26.45 \|\|

*dravyanāśāya vai dīrghaṃ pāpadaṃ bhayadaṃ tathā \|*  
*dhūrtānāṃ caturasraṃ syātputrahānikaraṃ śṛṇu \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The broad face is indicative of loss of wealth, besides being sinful and dangerous. Similarly, the face of the wicked people is square like. O Deva, I am now talking about the faces, which result in the loss of the son.

## \|\| 1.26.46 \|\|

*nimnavaktraṃ ca devendra putrahānikaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*hrasvaṃ bhatati kīnāśe pūrṇakāntaṃ ca bhoginām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The low face of a son is indicative of loss. A person with a small face is a degraded one. The people who enjoy all the pleasures, are always beautiful.

## \|\| 1.26.47 \|\|

*raktādharo narapatirdhanavānkamalādharaḥ \|*  
*sthūloṣṭhā hanumūlāśca śuṣkaistīkṣṇaiśca duḥkhitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A person with red lips becomes the lord of the people, while the one possessing the face lips resembling the lotus flowers, enjoys all the riches. A person with thick, big, dry and protruding lips always remains miserable.

## \|\| 1.26.48 \|\|

*asphoṭitāgraṃ snigdhaṃ ca nataṃ mṛdu tathā guha \|*  
*sampūrṇaṃ ca sadā śastaṃ śmaśru bhūmipaterguha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O Guha, the beard which is not tom out in the front, besides being greasy, bending downwards, soft and full of hair, is usually possessed by the kings.

## \|\| 1.26.49 \|\|

*raktaiścālpaistathā rūkṣaiḥ śmaśrubhirbhīmanandana \|*  
*narāścaurā bhavantyeva paradāraratāstathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O son of Bhima! Similarly, the real beard which is a little dry, is either of thieves or evil in character.

## \|\| 1.26.50-51 \|\|

*cipiṭābhyāṃ bhavedrogī hrasvau ca kṛpaṇasya ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śaṅkukarṇaśca bhūnāthaḥ sarvaśatrubhayaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyū romaśābhyāṃ tu vipulābhyāṃ narādhipaḥ \|*  
*bhogī ca sa bhavennityaṃ devabrāhmaṇapūjakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. A person whose ears are not fleshy, they meet with their end in war. A person with flat ears enjoys all the pleasures, while a person with small ears is a miserly one. A person with conical ears becomes the destroyer of all the enemies, terrific and happens to be the lord of earth. A person whose ears are full of the hair growth, he enjoys long life, while the one with big ears enjoys all the pleasures besides being the worshipper of the Brahmanas and the gods, becoming a king.

## \|\| 1.26.52 \|\|

*śirāvabaddhau krūrasya vyālambau ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*māṃsalau sukhadau jñeyau śravaṇau vyomakeśaja \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The merciless people have the ears Ml of veins. O son of Shiva, when the long ears are quite fleshy, they bestow comfort to the person.

## \|\| 1.26.53 \|\|

*bhogī syānnigaṇḍo vai mantrī sampūrṇagaṇḍakaḥ \|*  
*śubhabhākchukanāsastu cirajīvī śuṣkanāsikaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The cheeks bending downwards makes a man to enjoy all the pleasures and a person with beautiful cheeks becomes a minister. A person with a parrot like nose is quite fortunate, while the one with a dry nose has a long life.

## \|\| 1.26.54 \|\|

*kundakuṇḍalasaṅkāśaiḥ prakāśairdaśanairnṛpaḥ \|*  
*ṛkṣavānaradantāśca nityaṃ kṣutparipīḍitāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The teeth shining like the bud of the kunda flowers belong to a king. The people having the teeth resembling those of the bears and the monkeys, have always to suffer from hunger.

## \|\| 1.26.55 \|\|

*hastidantāḥ kharadantāḥ snigdhadantā guṇānvitāḥ \|*  
*karālairviralai rūkṣairdaśanairduḥkhajīvinaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The virtuous people have their greasy teeth resembling those of the elephants and donkeys. The terrific and spacious teeth or dry ones are possessed by the miserable people.

## \|\| 1.26.56-58 \|\|

*dvātriṃśaddantā rājāna ekatriṃśacca bhogavān \|*  
*triṃśaddantā narā nityaṃ sukhaduḥkhitvabhāgina \|*  
*ūnatriṃśacya daśanaiḥ puruṣāḥ duḥkhabhāginaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇajihvo bhavetpreṣyaḥ savalayā tu jihvayā \|*  
*bhavetkopasya kartā vai sthūlarūkṣaśca jihvayā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*śvetajihvā narā jñeyāḥ śaucācārasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*padmapatrasamā jihvā sūkṣmā dīrghā suśobhanā \|*  
*sthūlā ca na ca vistīrṇā yeṣāṃ te manujādhipāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. Those possessing thirty two teeth become the kings. Those possessing thirty one teeth enjoy all the pleasures. Those having thirty teeth have to face pleasure and the pain at the same time. A person with twenty nine teeth always remains miserable. When the tongue is of black or of an astonishing colour, such a person serves as a servant. A person with a thick and dry tongue is filled with anger. A person with white tongue possesses a good moral conduct. The tongue which resembles the lotus leaf besides being thin, is considered to be quite auspicious. A person whose tongue is neither too small, neither thick nor fat, he becomes a ruler.

## \|\| 1.26.59 \|\|

*nimnā snigdhā ca hrasvā ca raktāgrā rasanā yadi \|*  
*sarvavidyāpravaktāraste bhavanti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In case the tongue happens to be of lower type, greasy, small besides being of red colour, then the persons who possess such type of tongues, are surely well read in all the lores.

## \|\| 1.26.60 \|\|

*kṛṣṇatālurnaro yastu sa bhavetkulanāśanaḥ \|*  
*sukhabhāgī duḥkhabhāgī pītatālurnarādhipaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A person with a palate of black colour surely destroys the race. The one having a palate of yellow colour faces the pleasures and the pains equally becoming a king.

## \|\| 1.26.61 \|\|

*vikṛtaṃ sphuṭitaṃ rūkṣaṃ tālukaṃ na praśasyate \|*  
*siṃhatālurnarapatirgajatālustathaiva ca \|*  
*padmatālurbhavedrājā śvetatālurdhaneśvaraḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The defective, tom out, dry palate is not considered to be quite auspicious. The people possessing the palate resembling those of a lion, elephant and lotus become rulers and those having the white palate, become wealthy.

## \|\| 1.26.62 \|\|

*haṃsasvarā narā dhanyā meghagambhīraniḥsvanāḥ \|*  
*krauṃcasvanāśca rājāno bhogavanto mahādhanāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The people having the voice resembling a swan earn praise. Those having the voice resembling the clouds, heron, enjoy all the pleasures, with enormous wealth and ultimately become the kings.

## \|\| 1.26.63 \|\|

*cakravākasvanā dhanyā rājāno dharmavatsalāḥ \|*  
*kumbhasvano narapatirdundubhisvana eva ca \|*  
*rūkṣadīrghasvarāḥ krūrāḥ paśūnāṃ sadṛśā na tu \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The people having the voice resembling ruddy goose, earn glory and ultimately become the rulers of religious nature. Those having the sound of a pitcher or a big drum, turn as kings. The dry and the forceful voice, not resembling with those of the animals makes such people cruel.

## \|\| 1.26.64 \|\|

*2 gurgurasvarasaṃyuktāḥ puruṣāḥ kleśabhāginaḥ \|*  
*cāṣasvanā bhāgyayutā bhinnakāṃsyasvarāśca ye \|*  
*kṣīṇabhinnasvarā ye syuradhamāste prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The people with gurgling sound or speech feel miserable. Those having the speech resembling a magpie are considered to be quite fortunate and those having the shattered speech resembling the bell metal, are considered to be degraded ones.

## \|\| 1.26.65 \|\|

*pārthivāstanunāsāśca dīrghanāsāśca bhoginaḥ \|*  
*hrasvanāsā narā ye tu dharmaśīlāstu te matāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The people with thin noses becomes rulers, those with long and flat nose enjoy all the pleasures, and those with small nose are religious minded.

## \|\| 1.26.66 \|\|

*hastyaśvasiṃhanāsāśca sūcīnāsāśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sidhyati vāṇijyaṃ hayānāṃ caiva vikrayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Those having the noses resembling those of an elephant, horse, lion and a needle, are successful traders and also trade in horses.

## \|\| 1.26.67 \|\|

*vikṛtā nāsikā yasya 3 sthūlāgrā rūpavarjitā \|*  
*pāpakarmā sa vijñeyaḥ sāmudravacanaṃ yathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The persons having a defective nose, or with a big tip besides being ugly, they according to the ocean, are sinful.

## \|\| 1.26.68 \|\|

*dāḍimīpuṣpasaṃkāśe bhavetāṃ yasya locane \|*  
*4 bhūpatiḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ saptadvīpādhipo guha \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O Guha! A person having the eyes resembling the flowers of pomegranate, he becomes the ruler of seven continents.

## \|\| 1.26.69 \|\|

*vyāghrākṣāḥ kopanā jñeyāḥ ka5 rkaṭākṣāḥ kalipriyāḥ \|*  
*biḍālahaṃsanetrāśca bhavanti puruṣādhamāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Those having the eyes of a tiger, they are filled with rage. The one having the eyes of a crab is quarrelsome, and the one having the eyes of a cat or a swan, is a degraded one.

## \|\| 1.26.70 \|\|

*mapūranakulākṣāśca narāste madhyamāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*na 1 śrīstyajati sarvajña puruṣaṃ madhupiṅgalam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A person having the eyes resembling those of a peacock or a mangoose, becomes a degraded one. A person having the reddish eyes resembling the honey or of yellow colour, is not discarded even by Lakshmi.

## \|\| 1.26.71 \|\|

*āpiṅgalākṣā rājānaḥ sarvabhogasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*rocanā haritālākṣā guñjāpiṅgā dhaneśvarāḥ \|*  
*balasattvaguṇopetāḥ pṛthivīcakravartinaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A person having totally red or yellow eyes, becomes a king enjoying all the pleasures. The people having the eyes of the colour of gorochana (yellow orpiment), the berry of shrub Arbus precatoriua, are noble hearted and become emperors.

## \|\| 1.26.72 \|\|

*dvimātrāvīkṣaṇā nityaṃ jīvanti paramāśritāḥ \|*  
*trimātrāsyandino jñeyāḥ puruṣāḥ sukhabhāginaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A person who does not wink the eyes for two seconds at a time, he remains under the shelter of a big personality. A person who winks the eyes with an interval of three seconds, he lives quite comfortably.

## \|\| 1.26.73 \|\|

*caturmātrānimeṣaiśca nayanairīśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyuṣo dharmaratāḥ pañcamātrānimeṣiṇaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. A person who winks his eyes after four seconds becomes the lord and the one who winks the eyes after five seconds enjoys a long life besides being a religious minded one.

## \|\| 1.26.74 \|\|

*hrasvakarṇā mahābhāgā mahākarṇāśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*āvartakarṇā dhaninaḥ snigdhakarṇāstathaiva ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. A person having small but vast ears becomes auspicious soul. Those having the black or whirlpool, are always rich.

## \|\| 1.26.75 \|\|

*dīrghāyuṣaḥ śuktikarṇāḥ śaṅkhakarṇā mahādhanāḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyuṣo dīrghakarṇā lambakarṇāstapasvinaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Those having the ears resembling the mother of pearls, enjoy long life, while those having conch like ears are immensely wealthy.

## \|\| 1.26.76 \|\|

*lalāṭenārdhacandreṇa bhavanti pṛthivīśvarāḥ \|*  
*vipulena lalāṭena mahādhanapatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*svalpena tu lalāṭena naro dharmarataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Those having the forehead resembling a crescent are the lords of earth; those having a broad forehead are immensely wealthy, and those having the small foreheads, are quite religious in their outlook.

## \|\| 1.26.77 \|\|

*rekhā pañca lalāṭe tu striyā vā puruṣasya vā \|*  
*śataṃ jīvati varṣāṇāmaiśvaryaṃ cādhigacchati \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. In case, there be five lines in the forehead of a man or a woman, then they enjoy luxurious life for a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.26.78 \|\|

*catūrekhāmaśītiṃ tu tribhiḥ saptatimeva ca \|*  
*dvābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ tu rekhābhyāṃ catvāriṃśattathaikayā \|*  
*arekhena lalāṭena vijñeyā pañcaviṃśatiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. A person with four lines over the forehead, lives for eighty years, those with a single line live for forty years, and those having no lines over the forehead, live for twenty five years.

## \|\| 1.26.79 \|\|

*rekhācchedaistu vijñeyā hīnamadhyottamā narāḥ \|*  
*alpāyuṣastathālpābhirvyādhibhiḥ paripīḍitāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. With the division of the lines of the forehead, the age of a person should be taken to be the best, mediocre and short. The people with short age always suffer from one ailment or the other.

## \|\| 1.26.80 \|\|

*triśūlaṃ paṭṭiśaṃ vāpi lalāṭe yasya dṛśyate \|*  
*īśvaraṃ taṃ vijānīyādbhoginaṃ kīrtimāśritam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. A person having a trident or vajra mark over his forehead becomes a great leader with immense grace.

## \|\| 1.26.81 \|\|

*utkrāntanimnaṃ tu śiraḥ svalpopahatameva ca \|*  
*candrākāraṃ1 narendrāṇāṃ gavāḍhyaṃ maṅgalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The heads having high and low or pressed positions or a crescent head, are considered to be quite auspicious and the possessor of such head becomes the donor of excessive number of cows.

## \|\| 1.26.82 \|\|

*viṣamaṃ tu daridrāṇāṃ śiro dīrghaṃ tu duḥkhinām \|*  
*nāgakumbhanibhaṃ rājñaḥ samaṃ sarvatra bhoginaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The head of a poor people is either high or low. Those in miserable state have long head. The head of the king resembles the head of the elephant. The one who enjoys all the pleasures, has an even head.

## \|\| 1.26.83 \|\|

*kapilaḥ sphuṭitai rūkṣaiḥ sthūlaiśva śikhareśayaiḥ \|*  
*duḥkhitā puruṣā jñeyā romaśmaśrubhireva ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. If the head is broken with dry and thick hair, then the person should be considered as having been overpowered with miseries.

## \|\| 1.26.84 \|\|

*rūkṣā vivarṇā nistejāḥ kharāḥ sthūlāśca mūrdhajāḥ \|*  
*nātistokā na bahuśo mūrdhajā duḥkhabhāginaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. When the hair is dry, lusterless, shineless, pointed and neither very short nor very long, the condition of such a person should be taken to be miserable.

## \|\| 1.26.85 \|\|

*viralāśca mṛdusnigdhā bhramarāñjanasaprabhāḥ \|*  
*kacā yasya tu dṛśyante sa bhavetpṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. When the hair grown over the head of a person have gaps, besides being soft, greasy, black like the beer, he becomes the lord of earth.

## Chapter 27. Symptoms of men

## \|\| 1.27.1 \|\|

*kārtikeya uvāca \|*  
*saṃkṣepato mama vibho lakṣaṇāni nṛpasya tu \|*  
*śubhāni cāṅgajātāni brūhi me vadatāṃ vara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Karttikeya said — O best of orators and the lord, now you tell me the auspicious symbols of the king and the auspiciousness of the limbs of their bodies.

## \|\| 1.27.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vakṣyeṅgajātāni pārthivasya śubhāni ca \|*  
*pārthivo jñāyate yaistu narāṇāṃ madhyabhāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Brahma said — I am narrating such auspicious symbols of the kings, observing which one could recognize a king among the crowds of the people.

## \|\| 1.27.3-6 \|\|

*trīṇi yasya mahābāho vipulāni narasya tu \|*  
*udyatāni tathā ṣaḍ vai gambhīrāṇi ca trīṇi vai \|\| 3 \|\|*

*catvāri cāpi hrasvāni sapta raktāni vā vibho \|*  
*dīrghāṇi cāpi sūkṣmāṇi bhavanti yasya pañca vā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nābhiḥ saṃdhiḥ svanaśceti gambhīrāṇi ca trīṇi vai \|*  
*vadanaṃ ca lalāṭaṃ ca dantottama urastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vistīrṇametastritayaṃ vīra yasya narasya tu \|*  
*sa rājā nātra sandehaḥ śṛṇuṣvevonnatāni ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. O valorous one, a person whose three limbs are big, six are high, three are deep, four small, seven red, five long, five are thin (he is to be treated as a king). As for example, a person whose navel, joint and the speech are quite deep, then o Deva, when the face, forehead and the chest are broad, he surely happens to be a king. Similarly, I am talking about the raised limbs, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.27.7 \|\|

*kṛkāṭikā tadhā cāsyaṃ nakhā vakṣo'tha nāsikā \|*  
*kakṣe cāpi mahābāho ṣaḍetāni vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The glottis of the throat, the face, nails, the thighs, nose and armpit should be raised (for a king), according to the learned people.

## \|\| 1.27.8 \|\|

*liṅgaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ tathā grīvā jaṅghā hrasvāni suvrata \|*  
*netrānte hastapādau tu tālvoṣṭhau ca surottama \|*  
*jihvā raktā nakhāścaiva saptaitāni mahāmate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Suvrata, the phallus, back, throat and the thighs are short, the outer end of the eyes, the hands, feet, palate, lips, tongue and the nails — all the seven should be of red colour.

## \|\| 1.27.9 \|\|

*tvacaḥ kararuhāḥ keśā daśanā ṛbhavottama \|*  
*sūkṣmāṇyetāni ca guha pañca cāpi vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent god, similarly, the joints of the fingers, the upper skin of the body, nails, hair and the teeth should be thin (for the kings) as per the wisdom of the learned people.

## \|\| 1.27.10 \|\|

*nāsikālocane bāhū stanayorantaraṃ hanuḥ \|*  
*iti dīrghamidaṃ proktaṃ pañcakaṃ bhūbhujāṃ nṛpa \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The limbs like nose, eyes, arms, chest and the chin should be expanded as possessed by the king.

## \|\| 1.27.11 \|\|

*kṣutaṃ rājñāṃ sakṛddvistrirnāditaṃ hrāditaṃ tathā \|*  
*dīrghāyuṣāṃ prayuktaṃ te hasitaṃ ca vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Similarly, the sneeze of a king has a peculiar sound. In case one sneezes sweetly twice or thrice, he must be having a long life. This is what has been spoken by the learned people.

## \|\| 1.27.12 \|\|

*padmapatranibhe netre dhanināṃ śivanandana \|*  
*bhārgavīmāpnuyātso'pi raktānte yasya locane \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O son of lord Shiva, when the eyes resemble the lotus leaf, such a person must be rich. When the outer comers of the eyes are of red colour, he gains land.

## \|\| 1.27.13 \|\|

*madhupiṅgairmahātmāno narā jñeyāḥ surādhipa \|*  
*bhīravo hi kṛśākṣāstu caurā maṇḍalacakrakaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The people having the eyes of tawny or yellow colour are surely the great souls. O lord of the Devas, the people having thin or small eyes are cowards, and those having the circular eyes resembling a wheel, are thieves.

## \|\| 1.27.14 \|\|

*hayaḥ kekaranetrāstu gambhīrairarthasampadaḥ \|*  
*nīlotpalābhairvedavido bhṛśaṃ kṛṣṇaistathārthitā \|*  
*mantritvaṃ sthūlasudṛśo vadanti bhuvi tadvidaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. An eye of dark brown colour belongs to the cruel people, k while the deep eyes are possessed by the wealthy people. Those having the blue eyes resembling the blue lotus, become the Vedic scholars. Those with black eyes are also wealthy people. The experts have prescribed that a person having beautiful eyes, becomes a minister.

## \|\| 1.27.15 \|\|

*śyāmākṣāḥ subhagā jñeyā dīnākṣaibhra daridratā \|*  
*vistīrṇairbhogino śreyā vipulaiśca tathā guha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The dark coloured eyes are possessed by the people with great fortunes and a person with miserable eyes becomes a pauper. O Guha, similarly the one having big and wide eyes, enjoys all the pleasures on earth.

## \|\| 1.27.16 \|\|

*abhyunnatābhirhrasvāyurviśālābhiḥ sukhī bhavet \|*  
*daridro viṣamābhistu tato jñeyaḥ surottama \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O best of the Devas, when the eye of a person is raised from all the sides, he has a short life. A person with vast eyes always remains comfortable and the one with uneven eyes remains miserable.

## \|\| 1.27.17-19 \|\|

*bhruvo bālendusadṛśā dhanināmārbhavottama \|*  
*dīrghābhirnirdhano jñeyaḥ saṃsaktābhistu suvrata \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kṣīṇābhirarthahīnāḥ syurnarā jñeyāḥ surottama \|*  
*madhye natabhruvo ye ca paradāraratāstu te \|\| 18 \|\|*

*viralairunnataiḥ śaṃkhairdhanyāḥ1 syurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nimnaiḥ stutyarthasaṃsaktā2 unnataiśca janādhipāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. The eyebrows of the rich people resemble the new moon. O Suvrata, the eyebrows which are thin and joining each other, make a person quite poor. A person the centre of whose eyebrows is lower, he becomes an adulterer. The one whose eyebrows resemble the conch, besides being sparse, he is surely well established. The lower type of eyebrows always earns praise for a person and the one with the raised eyebrows, becomes the lord of the people.

## \|\| 1.27.20 \|\|

*viṣamalalāṭā vidhanāḥ sadā syurdevasattama \|*  
*ācāryāḥ śuktisadṛśairnarāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O best of Devas, the people with uneven forehead are always poor and the people whose forehead resembles a shell or the mother of pearls, he undoubtedly becomes an Acharya.

## \|\| 1.27.21 \|\|

*unnataśirobhirāḍhyā narā jñeyāḥ sadā guha \|*  
*vadhabandhabhāgino vīrā narā ninnalalāṭinaḥ \|*  
*bhṛśamunnataiśca mūrkhāśca kṛpaṇāśca tathā nataiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O Guha, a person with a raised head is always found to be sick, while those with low forehead remain always in bondages and are ultimately killed. The people with high forehead are always fools and those with the bent forehead are always misers.

## \|\| 1.27.22 \|\|

*śubhāvahaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vadanaṃ syādyathā śṛṇu \|*  
*adīnamānanaṃ snigdhaṃ sasmitaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O son, I am now revealing about the auspicious faces of the people, which you please listen. The benevolent lustrous face with a serene smile is indeed the best.

## \|\| 1.27.23 \|\|

*sāśrudīnaṃ tathā rūkṣamasnigdhaṃ ninditaṃ4 guha \|*  
*asambhāvyaṃ mukhaṃ jñeyaṃ narāṇāṃ nagadāraṇa \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Guha, the one having the lusterless face with tears and which is miserable and dry, is considered to be inauspicious. Such a face should always be taken as unbeneficial.

## \|\| 1.27.24 \|\|

*akampaṃ gubhadaṃ jñeyaṃ narāṇāṃ hasitaṃ guha \|*  
*nimīlitākṣaṃ pāpasya hasitaṃ cārbhavottama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Guha, the faultless cheeks of a person is always auspicious. O best of Devas, the sinful people laugh closing their eyes.

## \|\| 1.27.25 \|\|

*āmaṇḍalaṃ śiro yasya sa gavāḍhyo naro bhavet \|*  
*chatrākṛti śiro yasya sa bhavennṛpatirnaraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A person who has a round head, he owns a large herd of cows. A person having the head resembling a bee-hive, he becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.27.26 \|\|

*cipiṭākāritaśirā hanyādvai pitarau naraḥ \|*  
*ghaṇṭākṛti śirodhvānamasakṛtsevate naraḥ \|*  
*nimnaṃ śironarthadaṃ syānnarāṇāmarbhavottama \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A person with a flat head becomes the killer of his parents. A person with a head resembling a bell is always on his heels, being a traveler. O best of the Devas, the lowered head of a person makes him face loss.

## \|\| 1.27.27 \|\|

*guḍaiḥ snigdhaistathā kṛṣṇairabhinnāgraistathaiva hi \|*  
*keśairna cātibahulairmṛdubhiḥ pārthivo bhavet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A person having black, round, greasy hair, the tips of which are not broken, is soft and it is most likely that the person with such type of hair becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.27.28-29 \|\|

*bahulāḥ kapilāḥ sthūlā viṣamāḥ sphuṭitāstathā \|*  
*paruṣā hrasvātikuṭilā daridrāṇāṃ kacāḥ ghanāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ityuktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nṝṇāṃ śubhaṃ vāśubhameva ca \|*  
*yoṣitāṃ tadidānīṃ te lakṣaṇaṃ vacmi bhīmaja \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The hair of brown colour, uneven with broken tips, besides being hard and short, extremely curved and thick hair are with the poor people. Now I shall speak about the good or the bad symptoms of the women folk.

## Chapter 28. Symptoms of women

## \|\| 1.28.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇvidānīṃ mahābāho strīlakṣaṇamanuttamam \|*  
*yanmayoktaṃ purā vīra nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — O valorous one, presently, I am repeating the same symptoms of women, which I had earlier spoken to Narada.

## \|\| 1.28.2 \|\|

*tattvaṃ vijñāyate yena śubhāśubhamavasthitam \|*  
*ninditaṃ ca praśastaṃ ca strīṇāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I am going to speak out the good and bad symptoms of the women.

## \|\| 1.28.3 \|\|

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva bhrātaraṃ mātulaṃ tathā \|*  
*dvau tu bimbau parīkṣeta samudrasya vaco yathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The parents, brother and the maternal uncle should be examined according to the words of the ocean.

## \|\| 1.28.4 \|\|

*muhūrte tithisampanne nakṣatre cābhipūjite \|*  
*dvijaistu saha vāgamya kanyāṃ vīkṣeta śāstravit \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One should go in an auspicious time, tithi or a lunar day and the auspicious constellation, accompanied with a person well-versed in the knowledge of symptoms, besides a Brahmana should go for the selection of a bride.

## \|\| 1.28.5-7 \|\|

*hastau pādau parīkṣeta aṅgulīrnakhameva ca \|*  
*1 pāṇimeva ca jaṅghe ca kaṭināsoru eva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jaghanodarapṛṣṭhaṃ ca stanau karṇau bhujau tathā \|*  
*jihvāṃ coṣṭhau ca dantāśca kapolaṃ galakaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cakṣurnāsā lalāṭaṃ ca śiraḥ keśāṃstathaiva ca \|*  
*romarājiṃ1 svaraṃ varṇamāvartāni tu vā punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Thereafter, the hands, feet, fingers, nails, palms, thighs, waist, nose, knees, belly, back, breasts, arms, tongue, lips, cheeks, neck, forehead, head, hair, hair on the body, complexion, and the navel should be examined.

## \|\| 1.28.8 \|\|

*yasyāstu rekhāgrīvāyāṃ yā2 ca raktāntalocanā \|*  
*yasya sā gṛhamāgacchettadgṛhaṃ sukhamedhate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The one having a line on the throat and the reddish face around the eyes, such a woman, in whichever house she goes, there is the gradual increase in the fortunes of that family.

## \|\| 1.28.9 \|\|

*lalāṭe dṛśyate yasyāstriśūlaṃ devanirmitam \|*  
*bahūnāṃ strīsahasrāṇāṃ svāminīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The woman with a trident mark over her forehead, rules thousands of women.

## \|\| 1.28.10 \|\|

*rājahaṃsagatiryasyā mṛgākṣī mṛgavarṇikā \|*  
*samaśuklāgradantā ca kanyāṃ tāmuttamāṃ viduḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One who walks like a royal goose, the complexion and eyes are like the deer, besides the glittering teeth, she is believed to be the best girl.

## \|\| 1.28.11 \|\|

*maṇḍūkakukṣī yā kanyā nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalā \|*  
*ekaṃ janayate putraṃ so'pi rājā bhaviṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A girl having the armpit resembling a frog and circular like the banyan tree, she gives birth to a son alone, who becomes a king.

## \|\| 1.28.12 \|\|

*haṃsasvarā mṛduvacā yā kanyā madhupiṅgalā \|*  
*aṣṭau janayate putrāndhanadhānyavivardhinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A girl who has a voice resembling a goose, is soft spoken and has the complexion resembling the honey, she increases the wealth and cereals, and gives birth to eight sons.

## \|\| 1.28.13 \|\|

*āyatau śravaṇau yasyāḥ surūpā cāpi nāsikā \|*  
*bhruvau cendrāyudhākārau sātyantaṃ sukhabhāginī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A girl having long ears, beautiful nose and the eyebrows like the rainbow, she enjoys enormous comforts.

## \|\| 1.28.14 \|\|

*tanvī śyāmā tathā kṛṣṇā snigdhāṅgī mṛdubhāṣiṇī \|*  
*śaṅkhakundendudaśanā bhavedaiśvaryabhāginī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A girl having a thin body, dark complexion, lustrous and shining limbs, and who is soft spoken and the teeth resembling conch, lotus and moon, such a girl enjoys all the pleasures.

## \|\| 1.28.15 \|\|

*vistīrṇaṃ jaghanaṃ yasyā vedimadhyā tu yā bhavet \|*  
*āyate vipule netre rājapatnī tu sā bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The one with broad thighs, thin waist resembling a pedestal, broad and long eyes, she becomes a queen.

## \|\| 1.28.16 \|\|

*yasyāḥ payodhare vāme hastekarṇe gale'pi vā \|*  
*maśakaṃ tilakaṃ vāpi sā pūrvaṃ janayetsutam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When there is a mole on the left breast, hand, ear and in the neck, she gives birth to a son first.

## \|\| 1.28.17 \|\|

*gūḍhagulphāṅguliśirā alpapārṣṇiḥ sumadhyamā \|*  
*raktākṣī raktacaraṇā sātyantaṃ sukhabhāginī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A girl whose heels, the ankle and the veins are fleshy, the toes are set together, the heel is small, the waist is charming, nails are broad, uneven nails, lustreless soles of the feet besides being red, she enjoys all the comforts.

## \|\| 1.28.18 \|\|

*kūrmapṛṣṭhāyatanakhau snigdhabhāvavivarjitau \|*  
*vakrāṅgulitalau pādau kanyāṃ tāṃ parivarjayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A girl having the nails of the toes resembling the back of the tortoise, with curved toes and lustreless feet, one should not marry such a girl.

## \|\| 1.28.19 \|\|

*yena kenacidaṃśena māṃsaṃ yasyā vivardhate \|*  
*rāsabhīṃ tādṛśīṃ vidyānna sā kalyāṇamarhati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When a limb of a girl becomes fleshy, she should be treated as useless for welfare work.

## \|\| 1.28.20 \|\|

*pāde pradeśinī yasyā aṅguṣṭhaṃ samatikramet \|*  
*duḥśīlā durbhagā jñeyā kanyāṃ tāṃ parivarjayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A woman whose toe is placed over the big toe, she should be discarded as unfortunate and unchaste woman.

## \|\| 1.28.21 \|\|

*pāde madhyamikā yasyāḥ kṣitiṃ na spṛśate yadi \|*  
*ramate sā na kaumāre svacchandā1 kāmacāriṇī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A woman, the middle toe of whose foot does not touch the earth, she does not enjoy sex and in due course of time she behaves as an unchaste woman.

## \|\| 1.28.22 \|\|

*pāde anāmikā yasyāḥ kṣitiṃ na spṛśate yadi \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ puruṣaṃ hatvā tṛtīye sā pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In case the middle toe of a woman does not touch the earth, then killing the second husband, she

## \|\| 1.28.23 \|\|

*pāde kaniṣṭhā yasyāstu kṣitiṃ na spṛśate yadi \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ puruṣaṃ hatvā tṛtīye sā pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The woman, whose ring toe does not touch the earth, she also killing her second husband, lives with the third one.

## \|\| 1.28.24 \|\|

*na devikā na dhanikā na dhānyapratināmikā \|*  
*gulmavṛkṣasanāmnī ca kanyāṃ tāṃ parivarjayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A girl having the name based on a goddess or on wealth or cereals or the elephants, horse, straw or a creeper or a tree, should not be married by a person.

## \|\| 1.28.25 \|\|

*indracandrādipuruṣasanāmnī ca yadā bhavet \|*  
*naitāḥ patiṣu rajyante yāśca nakṣatranāmikāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The woman whose name is based on Indra, moon, a man and the constellations, do not love their husbands.

## \|\| 1.28.26 \|\|

*āvartaḥ pṛṣṭhato yasyā nābhiṃ samanuvindati \|*  
*tadapatyaṃ bhaved dhrasvaṃ hrasvāyuśca vinirdiśet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A woman having a bee mark over her back or the navel, her children are small in size or with short life.

## \|\| 1.28.27 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhāvartā patiṃ hanti nābhyāvartā pativratā \|*  
*kaṭyāvartā tu svacchandā na kadācidvirajyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In case there is a bee mark at the back, she becomes the destroyer of her husband. In case it is in the navel, then her children are of small size with short life. She is head strong and never becomes unattached.

## \|\| 1.28.28 \|\|

*yasyāstu hasamānāyā gaṇḍe jāyet kūpakam \|*  
*ramate sā na kaumāre svacchandā kāryakāriṇī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A woman, in whose cheeks pits are formed when laughing, she does not have sex when unmarried, but in due course becomes headstrong and moves as per her own will.

## \|\| 1.28.29 \|\|

*yasyāstu gacchamānāyāṣṭiṭṭīkāyati jaṅghikā \|*  
*putraṃ vyavasyetsā kartuṃ patitve nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A woman who while walking produces some sound from the thigh or the ankle bone, she becomes such an unchaste woman who could make use of even her son as a husband.

## \|\| 1.28.30 \|\|

*sthūlapādā ca yā kanyā sarvāṃgeṣu ca lomaśā \|*  
*sthūlahastā ca yā syādvai dāsīṃ tāṃ nirdiśedbudhaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A girl with thick feet, having hair over the entire body, with thick hands, people say that she could be a maid servant.

## \|\| 1.28.31 \|\|

*yasyāścotkaṭakau2 pādau mukhaṃ ca vikṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*uttaroṣṭhe ca romāṇi sā kṣipraṃ bhakṣayetpatim \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A woman, the upper part of whose feet are roundish, a deformity in the mouth, with hair over the upper lip, she has her husband destroyed soon.

## \|\| 1.28.32 \|\|

*trīṇi yasyāḥ pralambante lalāṭamudaraṃ sphicau \|*  
*trīṇi bhakṣayate sā tu devaraṃ śvasuraṃ patim \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The one whose forehead, belly, waist and the back are excessively large, she destroys the husband’s younger brother, father-in-law and the husband soon.

## \|\| 1.28.33 \|\|

*samudbhūṣitacāritrā gurubhaktā pativratā \|*  
*devabrāhmaṇabhaktā ca mānuṣīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 33 \|\|*
