33\. The woman who has the good conduct is devoted to the preceptor and the husband besides the Brahmanas and the gods, and is known as Maranushi.

## \|\| 1.28.34 \|\|

*nityaṃ snātā sugandhā ca nityaṃ ca priyavādinī \|*  
*alpāśinyalparoṣā ca devatāṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Similarly, a woman who takes her bath daily, applies fragrance over her body, is sweet tongued, takes little food and becomes hardly angry, such a woman is considered to be divinity.

## \|\| 1.28.35 \|\|

*pracchannaṃ kurute pāpamapavādaṃ ca rakṣati \|*  
*hadayaṃ syācca durgrāhyaṃ mārjārī tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The one who commits the sins, secretly indulges in evil deeds and then covers them and whose inner feelings are difficult to be known, she is known to be as a cat like woman.

## \|\| 1.28.36 \|\|

*hasate krīḍate caiva kruddhā caiva prasīdati \|*  
*nīceṣu ramate nityaṃ rāsabhī tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A woman who while laughing as well as during sports, becomes angry as well as delighted and loves always the degraded people, she is known as donkey like woman.

## \|\| 1.28.37 \|\|

*pratikūlakarī nityaṃ bandhūnāṃ bhartureva ca \|*  
*svacchande lalitāṃ caiva āsurīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One who always acts against her brothers, is quite headstrong in her behavior, is known as Asuri or demoness like one.

## \|\| 1.28.38 \|\|

*1 bahvāśī bahuvākyā ca nityaṃ cāpriyavādinī \|*  
*hinasti svapatiṃ yā tu rākṣasīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. One who is like a glutton and always talks foul and who kills her own husband, is known as Rakshasi.

## \|\| 1.28.39 \|\|

*śaucācāraparibhraṣṭā rūpabhraṣṭā bhayaṅkarā \|*  
*prasvedamalapaṅkā ca piśācīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A woman who has fallen from the outer purity and good conduct is ugly, and the one with terrific temperament, covered with perspiration, filth and mud is known as Pishachi.

## \|\| 1.28.40 \|\|

*nityaṃ snātāṃ sugandhāṃ ca māṃsamadyapriyādinīm \|*  
*vṛkṣodyānaprasaktā ca gāndharvīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One applies fragrance over the body after taking bath daily, consuming the meat, wine as her favourites, roaming about in the orchard, is known as Gandharvi.

## \|\| 1.28.41 \|\|

*capalā cañcalā caiva nityaṃ paśyeddiśastathā \|*  
*calasvabhāvā lubdhā ca vānarīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A woman who herself is too talkative with rolling eyes, who is always on the lookout, besides being of unstable mind and greedy, she is known as a female monkey.

## \|\| 1.28.42 \|\|

*candrānanāṃ śubhāṅgīṃ tu mattavāraṇagāminīm \|*  
*āraktanakhahastāṃ tu vidyādvidyādharīṃ budhaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A woman having the face like a moon, the body with auspicious symbols and walking like the intoxicated elephant, having the nails and the hands of red colour, such a woman is known by the learned people as Vidyadhari.

## \|\| 1.28.43 \|\|

*vīṇāvāditraśabdena vaṃśagītaraveṇa ca \|*  
*puṣpadhūpaprasaktāṃ ca gāndharvīṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who remains absorbed in the sound of Vina, cymbals, flute, flowers and the sunshine is known as Gandharvi.

## \|\| 1.28.44 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*ityevamuktvā sa mahānubhāvo jagāma vedhā nijamandiraṃ vai \|*  
*strīṇāṃ tathā puṃstvavatāṃ ca vīra yallakṣaṇaṃ pārthiva lokapūjyam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Sumantu said — Thus lord Brahma, then speaking on the symptoms of the women and the men, which are liked by the people, left for his abode.

## Chapter 29. Description of Ganapati kalpa

## \|\| 1.29.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*gakārākṣaradevasya gaṇeśasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ārādhanavidhiṃ brūhi sāṅgaṃ mantrasamanvitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — You kindly enlighten us on the method of the worship of Ganesha, whose name starts with the letter ‘Ga’ in which the limbs of the body are touched with hands.

## \|\| 1.29.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*na tithirna ca nakṣatraṃ nopavāso vidhīyate \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ1 ceṣṭataḥ siddhiḥ sadā bhavati kāmikā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — It is a type of Siddhi which accomplishes all the tasks, conceived by a person on any particular moon-day, constellation and on fasting.

## \|\| 1.29.3 \|\|

*śvetārkamūlaṃ saṅgṛhya kuryādgaṇapatiṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ tu padmāsanagataṃ tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. An image of Ganesha of thumb size of the root of the swallow grass should be made, which should be lodged over a lotus leaf by the learned people.

## \|\| 1.29.4 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ trinetraṃ ca sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*nāgayajñopavītāṅgaṃ śaśāṅkakṛtaśekharam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It should have four arms, three eyes and adored with all the ornaments. The serpent should serve as the sacred thread, while the crescent should be lodged over the forehead.

## \|\| 1.29.5 \|\|

*dantaṃ savye kare dadyāddvitīye cākṣasūtrakam \|*  
*tṛtīye paraśuṃ dadyāccaturthe modakaṃ nyaset \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The left hands should hold a tusk and the rosary of Rudraksha beads. The third hand should hold an axe, while the fourth hand should hold the sweet balls.

## \|\| 1.29.6-7 \|\|

*kuṅkumaṃ candanaṃ cāpi samālambhanamucyate \|*  
*vāsobhirbhūṣaṇai raktairmālyaiścārādhayedgaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dhūpena ca sugandhena modakaiścāpi pūjayet \|*  
*evaṃ pūjyāgratastasya bhojayedbrāhmaṇaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Thereafter, Ganapati should be carefully worshipped offering to him the sandal paste, saffron, costumes, ornaments, besides a garland of red flowers. The incense fragrance material and the sweet balls should also be placed before Ganesha while worshipping him. Thereafter, food should be offered to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.29.8 \|\|

*vāmanaṃ kubjakaṃ cāpi bhojayetpurato dvijam \|*  
*āśīrvādaṃ tatastasmātprāpya siddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At that point of time, the dwarfish and hunch back Brahmanas should also be served food in his presence. When they pronounce blessings, one surely achieves success.

## \|\| 1.29.9 \|\|

*bhaktyā kurukulaśreṣṭha 1 śṛṇu mantrapadāni vai \|*  
*gaṃ svāhā mūlamantro'yaṃ praṇavena samanvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O best of the race of the Kurus, now you listen to the process of the mantras with devotion, which is going to be revealed by me. The mula mantra comprises of Omkara or Pranava combined with gam svaha.

## \|\| 1.29.10-11 \|\|

*gāṃ namo hadayaṃ jñeyaṃ gīṃ śiraḥ parikīrtitam \|*  
*śikhā ca gūṃ namo jñeyo gaiṃ namaḥ kavacaṃ smṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gauṃ namo netramuddiṣṭaṃ gaḥ phaṭ kāmāstramucyate \|*  
*āgaccholkāmukhāyeti mantra āvāhane hyayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then speaking gam namah, one should touch his heart. Then uttering gim namah, one should touch the head, then uttering gum namah one should touch the tuft. Then one should touch the kavaca, uttering gaum namah one should touch the eyes. He should again utter gah phat and then utter the kamastra. Then speaking ulkamukhaya namah, the deity should be invoked.

## \|\| 1.29.12-13 \|\|

*gaṃ gaṇeśāya namo gandhamantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*puṣpolkāya namaḥ puṣpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dhūpolkāya namo dhūpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*dīpolkāya namo dīpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Thereafter, fragrance should be offered uttering gam ganeshaya namah. Then uttering pushpolkaya namah flowers should be offered. Then uttering dhupolkaya namah the incense should be offered and uttering dipolkaya namah the lamp should be offered.

## \|\| 1.29.14 \|\|

*oṃ gaṃ maholkāya namo balimantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*oṃ saṃsiddholkāya namo mantraścāyaṃ visarjane \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, one should utter Maholkaya namah and the offering should be made. Completing all these, he should send off the deity uttering Samsiddholkaya namah.

## \|\| 1.29.15-18 \|\|

*oṃ mahākarṇāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi \|*  
*tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt gāyatrī japaḥ pūrvataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mahāgaṇapataye vīra1 svāhā dakṣiṇataḥ sadā \|*  
*maholkāya paścimataḥ kūśmāṇḍāyottareṇa tu \|*  
*ekadantatripurāntakāya āgneyyāṃ vīra nirdiśet \|\| 16 \|\|*

*oṃ śivadatta vikaṭaharahāsa prāṇāya svā nairṛtyām \|*  
*2 tulambanātyacaladantakāya svāhā vāyavyām \|\| 17 \|\|*

*padmadaṃṣṭrāya narāyeti aiśānyāṃ homayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*huṃ phaṭ huṃ phaṭ hastatāladhvanirhasanakūrdanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. The sending off should be done towards the south, uttering om mahakarnaya combined with the Gayatri mantra. Then towards the east, uttering Mahaganapataye svaha, the send off should be towards the south and uttering Maholkaya namah the send off should be towards the west; Kushmandaya towards the north, Ekadanta Tripurantakaya in the south-east quarters, uttering om Shivadatta....svaha in the south-western quarter, uttering Tulamba... . svaha towards the northwest and Padmadanshtraya etc. towards the north-east quarters and the homa should be performed thereafter. Performing the puja and homa, uttering hum phat hum phat and clapping the hands, one should dance with ecstasy.

## \|\| 1.29.19 \|\|

*mṛdanartanagaṇapatirdevasya mudrāṃ tato homaṃ samācaret \|*  
*na yadā vaśyā bhavati \|*  
*kṛṣṇatilāhutimaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāttrirātreṇa rājā vaśyo bhavati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then forming the mudra of a Deva, the homa should then be started. In case it is not possible, then one should make the offering of the black sesame seeds eight thousand times in seven nights and by so doing, even the king gets subjugated.

## \|\| 1.29.20 \|\|

*tilayavahomena sarve janapadā vaśyā bhavanti \|*  
*ati rūpavatī kanyā gacchantamanu cchati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By performing the homa offering the sesame seeds and barley, all the people come under control. The extremely beautiful girls simply follow such a person.

## \|\| 1.29.21 \|\|

*caṇatandulahomenājito bhavet \|*  
*nimbapatrasamaistailairvidveṣaṇaṃ karoti \|*  
*somagrahaṇe udakamadhye avatīrya aṣṭasahasraṃ japet \|*  
*saṅgrāme aparājito bhavati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By performing homa with the gram and rice, a person becomes invincible. By performing homa with leaves of nima tree and oil, the enmity with an enemy is decreased. A person during it at the time of lunar eclipse should repeat the mantra eight thousand times standing in water as a result of which he would never be defeated by the enemy.

## \|\| 1.29.22 \|\|

*ādityābhimukho bhūtvā aṣṭasahasraṃ japet \|*  
*ādityo varado bhavati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. One who utters Lambarajna namah and recites this mantra eight thousand times facing towards the sun, then the Sun-god getting pleased with him, bestows boons to him.

## \|\| 1.29.23 \|\|

*śuklacaturthyāmupoṣya gandhapuṣpādibhirarcanaṃ kṛtvā tilatandulāñjuhuyāt \|*  
*śirasā dhārayaṃstairaparājito bhavati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On the fourth bright moon day, when a person, performing the fast, worships with fragrant flowers and performs homa of sesame and rice, placing it over the head, he becomes invincible.

## \|\| 1.29.24 \|\|

*apāmārgasamidbhiragniṃ prajvālya ekaviṃśatyāhutīryo juhuyāt \|*  
*trirātrācchatruṃ vyāpādayati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person who burning the wood of a medicinal plant (apamarga) makes twenty one offerings for three days continuously, all his enemies get destroyed.

## \|\| 1.29.25 \|\|

*athottareṇa mantraṃ vyākhyāsye \|*  
*vṛkṣamūle kajjalaṃ saṅgṛhya saptabhirmantritaṃ kṛtvā netrāṇyañjayedyaṃ paśyati sa vaśī bhavati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I am now explaining about the mantra. A person who making the collyrium of the root of a tree applies it in his eyes seven times, he is able to overpower any person over whom he casts his glance.

## \|\| 1.29.26 \|\|

*puṣpaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ cāṣṭasahasrābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā yasmai dadāti sa vaśyo bhavati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By sanctifying the fruit, flowers and the roots eight thousand times, when given to a person, he becomes under control of the giver.

## \|\| 1.29.27-30 \|\|

*yatkiñcinmūlamantreṇa karoti tatsidhyati \|*  
*sarve grahāḥ suprītā bhavanti \|*  
*nagaradvāraṃ gatvā aṣṭasahasraṃ dvāraṃ nirūpayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

*puraṃ dvāreṇa gṛhyate prāṅmukho yajati sa uccāṭayati \|*  
*sammukho japati corānvidrāvayati \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tṛṇāni lūnayati \|*  
*kāṣṭhāni cchedayati \|\| 29 \|\|*

*1 gajarājena yuddhayati \|*  
*jalamadhye saptarātraṃ japet \|*  
*akāle varṣayati \|*  
*kūpataḍāgāñchoṣayati \|*  
*pratimāṃ nṛtyayati \|*  
*ākarṣayati \|*  
*stambhayati \|*  
*yojanaśatātstrīpuruṣānākarṣayati \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. Whatever is done uttering this basic mantra, it meets with success. All the planets get pleased. A person, who going at the city gate, performs japam of the mantra eight thousand times facing east, he uprooting the enemy, destroys the thieves, while cutting off straw, makes hole in the wood besides making the elephants to fight. By performing japam in water for seven nights, he makes the untimely rain to fall, besides drying up of a tank or a well. He makes the image to dance, attracting people irrespective of being men or women from hundreds of yojanas.

## \|\| 1.29.31 \|\|

*gorocanāṃ ca sahasrābhimantritāṃ kṛtvā haste baddhvā yojanaśatasahasraṃ gatvā punarāgacchati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After initiating gorochana a thousand times, when bowed in a hand, the person returns (safely) after travelling thousands of yojanas.

## \|\| 1.29.32 \|\|

*atha mārayitukāmaḥ khadirakīlakaṃ kṛtvā strīpuruṣaṃ vicintya hadaye nikhanayet \|*  
*kṣaṇādeva mriyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In case a person desires to kill someone, may be a man or a woman, when inserts a nail of the wood of Acacia catechu in the heart of the image of that man or a woman, the same person dies at once.

## \|\| 1.29.33 \|\|

*sarvapātakavimukto bhavati \|*  
*agnitejāḥ sarvebhyo'parājito bhavati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus with the performing of the worship of Ganapati, a person is relieved of all the sins, besides becoming illustrious like the fire.

## \|\| 1.29.34 \|\|

*oṃ vakatuṇḍāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ ekadaṃṣṭrāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ kṛtakṛṣṇāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ gajakarṇāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ lambodarāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ vikaṭāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ dhūmravarṇāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ gaganakūjāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ vināyakāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ gaṇapataye svāhā \|*  
*oṃ hastimukhāya svāhā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Reciting the above mantra vakratunda etc., the homa should be performed.

## Chapter 30. Method of the worship of Vinayaka

## \|\| 1.30.1 \|\|

*sumantaruvāca \|*  
*nimbamayamaṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā nityadhūpagandhādibhirarcayitvā pracchannaṃ śirasi baddhvā gacchet \|*  
*sarvajanapriyo bhavati \|*  
*śvetārkamūlāṅguṣṭhamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā dhūpādibhirarcayitvā sarvānvarṇānvaśamānayati \|*  
*śvetacandanamaṅguṣṭhamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā puṣpagandhādibhirarcayitvā śuklacaturthyāmaṣṭamyāṃ vā baliṃ kuryādaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāddadhnā pāyasena rājānaṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*raktacandanamayaṃ gaṇapatimaṅguṣṭhamātraṃ kṛtvā bhautikaṃ baliṃ dadyāddadhimadhughṛtāhutīnāṃ gaṇapatimaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyādātmaprāpikāṃ prajāṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*raktakaravīramūlāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet \|*  
*raktapuṣpagandhopahārairbaliṃ dadyāt \|*  
*tilalavaṇaghṛtenāṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāt \|*  
*daśagrāmānvaśamānayati \|*  
*śvetakaravīrāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā tilapiṣṭadadhighṛtakṣīraharidrāmiśreṇāṣṭasahasraṃ \|*  
*juhuyādveśyāṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*aśvatthamūlāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpabaliṃ dattvā śataṃ juhuyācchatruṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*arkamūlāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpabalīn dadyāt \|*  
*tindukāṣṭaśataṃ juhuyācchatruṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*bilvamūlamayamaṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpārcitaṃ kṛtvā trimadhvaktānāmaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyādrājāmātyānvaśamānayati \|*  
*śirasi dhūpāndhṛtvā gacchedrājadvāraṃ vigrahe jayo bhavati \|*  
*hastidantamṛttikāmayamaṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet \|*  
*gandhapuṣpadhūpārcitaṃ kṛtvā. kṛṣṇacaturthyāṃ nagno bhūtvābhyarcayet \|*  
*sapta vārāñjapennityaṃ 1 nārīṇāṃ subhago bhavati \|*  
*vṛṣabhaśṛṅgamṛttikāṅguṣṭhamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet \|*  
*gandhapuṣpārcitaṃ kṛtvā gugguludhūpaṃ dadyādghoṣapatiṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*atha vā valmīkamṛttikāṃguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet \|*  
*kaṭukatailena pratimāṃ lepayet \|*  
*unmattakakāṣṭhenāgniṃ prajvālyāhutīnāmaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāttilasarṣapamiśreṇa sarvadhūpaṃ dadyāttrikaṭukena lepayet \|*  
*agarudhūpaṃ dadyādrājānaṃ vaśamānayati \|*  
*pareṣāṃ ca vallabho bhavati \|*  
*raktacandanenātmānaṃ dhūpayetsubhago bhavati \|*  
*oṃ gaṇapataye vakratuṇḍāya gajadantāya gulaguletininādāya2 caturbhujāya trinetrāya muśalapāśavajrahastāya sarvabhūtadamanāya sarvalokavaśaṃkarāya sarvaduṣṭopaghātajananāya sarvaśatruvimardanāya sarvarājyasamīhanāya rājānamiha vaśamānaya hana hana paca paca vajrāṅkuśena gaṇeśa phaṭ svāhā \|*  
*oṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ svāhā namaḥ hadayaṃ mūlamantrasya \|*  
*oṃ kaḥ śiraḥ oṃ khaḥ śikhā oṃ gaḥ hadayam oṃ guḥ vaktraṃ oṃ gaiṃ netram \|*  
*oṃ ghaḥ kavacam oṃ ṅa āvāhanaṃ hadayasya āvāhanāṅgāni bhavanti oṃ namaḥ hadayaṃ mūlamantrasya oṃ gāḥ śiraḥ oṃ gaiḥ namaḥ śikhā oṃ gauḥ namaḥ kavacam oṃ gaṃ namaḥ netre oṃ gaḥ phaṭ astram \|*  
*oṃ aṅguṣṭholkāya svāhā āvāhanaṃ hadayasya svāhā visarjanaṃ hadayasya oṃ gandholkāya svāhā \|*  
*gandhamantraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — A small wooden image of Ganesha of the size of a thumb should be made and placing it secretly on his head, wherever the person goes, he is liked by all the people. Making a tiny figure of Ganesha of wood, offering incense etc., it should be adored and by so doing, people of all the castes are overpowered by him. On the fourth or eighth moon day of the bright fortnight, the image of Ganapati of the same size should be made, and should be worshipped with flowers. Then pouring eight offerings of curd and payasam in fire and when bali is so offered, even the king comes under the influence of the performer. Similarly, after making a small figure of Ganapati in red sandal, and after worshipping it the curd and honey is poured with ghi in the burning flames eight thousand times as the offering and giving away the bali to the bhutas, the entire populace comes under the influence of the king. When a tiny image of Ganesha is made in the red oleander of the size of a thumb and worshipped with fragrant red flowers, and offering should then be made of sesame, salt and ghi eight thousand times, then the people of all the ten villages come under the influence of the performer. Making a thumb size figure of Ganesha in white caper bush one should worship it and when the offering of sesame, curd, ghi and milk is offered mixed with turmeric powder eight thousand times, then even a harlot comes under the influence of the performer. Similarly, by making the thumb size image of Ganapati one should adore it with fragrant incense, flowers a hundred times, and then even the enemy comes under the influence of the performer. When the thumb size figure of Ganesha is made of swallow-wort, and offering of fragrant flowers and incense made to it, then burning the husk and wood, a hundred offerings should be made in it and by so doing even the enemy is overpowered. Making a thumb size figure of Ganesha from the root of wood apple tree, it should be worshipped with fragrant flowers and incense, and dipping it thrice in honey, one should make eight thousand offerings in the fire flames and by so doing, the minister of the king is brought under the influence of the performer. Then again offering incense to the head, one should go to the king and by so doing one becomes victorious in the war. On the fourth moon day of the dark fortnight, one should dig out the earth with the tusk of the elephant and then make a tiny figure of Ganesha in clay. Worshipping the same image with fragrant flowers, one should adore it for seven nights continuously. By so doing one becomes favourite of the ladies. Then making an image of clay digging the earth with the horn of a bull, ii should be worshipped with guggulu and incense, then the masters of the milkmen and cows get overpowered. By making the thumb size tiny figure of Ganesha with the earth of white ant’s hill, the linseed oil should be applied over it, and then burning the wood of thorn apple plant, eight thousand offerings should be made of sesame besides incense made of all the herbs. Then plastering it with ginger and pepper, incense of aguru should be burnt and by so doing, even the king gets influenced with the performer who also becomes favourite of others. In case he applies the red sandal paste over his body, he himself becomes beautiful. The relevant mantra is as follows: “Om Ganapataye Vakratundaya Gajadantdya Gulaguletinindddya Catur-bhujaya Trinetraya Musalapdtiavajrahastdya Sarvabhutddamandya Sarvalokavasamkaraya Sarvadushtopaghdtajananaya, Sarvashatru-vimardandya, Sarvarajyasamlhandya Rajanamiha Vasamanaya Han Han Paca Paca Vajrahkusena Ganesha Phat Svaha.” “Om gam gim gum gaim gaum gab svaha namah” — this is the heart of the basic mantra. Then invocation of head should be made uttering om kah for head, om khah for tuft, om gah for heart, om guh for the face, om gaim for eyes, om ghah for the kavaca, om ha for the heart, om namah is the heart of the basic mantra. Then om gab stands for head, om gaih namah stands for tuft, om gauh namah for kavaca, om gam namah for eyes, om gah phat astram. Om angustholkaya svaha invokes the heart and then send off. Then the flowers etc. should be offered uttering Dharmabhutolkaya svaha and fragrance should be offered. Then with om Durjayaya flowers should be offered towards east; with om Dhurjataya towards the south; with Lambodaraya towards the west; with om Ganapataye towards the north; with Ganadhipataye towards thee north-east quarters; with om Mahaganapataye towards the south-east quarters; with Kushmandaya towards the south-west quarters; and with Ekadanta Tripuraghatine Trinetraya towards north-west quarters, the flowers should be offered. Thereafter, the mantras like Ganadhipataye and Gayatri mantra should be recited. Then he should display padma, damshtra, mala, prakarsani, parashu, ankusha, pada and pataha mudras and then start with work. By pouring eight thousand offerings of black sesamum seeds, the king is influenced. Thereafter, all the eleven hand symbols or mudras and Avahana to Naivedya should be displayed. The adoration of three-eyed Ganesha should be performed in the same way as the worship of Trinetra Shiva is performed.

## \|\| 1.30.2 \|\|

*tadeva maṇḍalaṃ cāsya aṅganyāsastathaiva ca \|*  
*ṛte mantrapadānīha samānaṃ sarvameva hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Except the mantra, the mandala is the same, Anganyasa is the same and all other formalities are similar.

## \|\| 1.30.3 \|\|

*pūjayedyastu vighneśamekadantamumāsutam \|*  
*naśyanti tasya vighnāni na cāriṣṭaṃ kadācana \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Thus a person who worships Ganesha — the son of Uma in this way, all his obstructions are removed and he never faces any misfortunes.

## \|\| 1.30.4 \|\|

*yaścopavāsaṃ kṛtvā tu caturthyāṃ pūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*sarve tasya samārambhāḥ sidhyeyurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A person, who fasting on the fourth moon day adores Ganapati, all the tasks which had started earlier are successfully accomplished undoubtedly.

## \|\| 1.30.5-7 \|\|

*yasyānukūlo vighneśaḥ śivayoḥ kulanandana \|*  
*tasyānukūlaṃ sarvaṃ syājjagadvai sarvakarmasu \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasmādārādhayedenaṃ bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*kuṅkumāgurudhūpena tathaivoṇḍīrakasrajā \|*  
*3 palalollāpikābhiśca jātikonmattakaistathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śuklapakṣe caturthyāṃ tu vidhinānena pūjayet \|*  
*tasya sidhyati nirvighnaṃ sarvakarma na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. O son of the Kuru race, when Ganesha — the son of Uma and Maheshvara is favourable towards anyone, the entire world is helpful in his tasks. Therefore, a person making canopies and arches with decoration, with a devoted mind, over the bright fourth moon day, should appropriately worship Ganapati offering saffron, guggulu, incense, lotus flower garland, powdered sesamum seeds, jasmine and thorn apple fruits. When it is so performed, all the tasks of the performer are well established without any obstruction.

## \|\| 1.30.8 \|\|

*ekadante jagannāthe gaṇeśe tuṣṭimāgate \|*  
*pitṛdevamanuṣyādyāḥ sarve tuṣyanti bhārata \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Bharata, O king, when Ganesha with a single tusk and the lord of the universe is pleased, all the manes, the gods and the humans also get pleased.

## \|\| 1.30.9 \|\|

*tasmādārādhayedenaṃ sadā bhaktipuraḥsaram \|*  
*karṇalepaistuṇḍikābhirmodakaiśca1 mahīpate \|*  
*pūjayetsatataṃ devaṃ vighnavināśāya dantinam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Therefore, for the destruction of all the obstructions, one should please the lord with a single .tusk, offering sandalpaste, lotus flowers, sweet balls and other things in a proper manner.

## Chapter 31. Worship of Shiva on the fourth moon day

## \|\| 1.31.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śivā śāntā sukhā rājaṃścaturthī trividhā smṛtā \|*  
*māsi bhādrapade śuklā śivā lokeṣu pūjitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O king, the fourth moon day of Shiva is of three types, viz. Shiva, Santa and Sukha. The fourth moon day falling in the month of Bhadrapada is known by the name of Shiva, which is honoured by all the people.

## \|\| 1.31.2 \|\|

*tasyāṃ snānaṃ tathā dānamupavāso japastathā \|*  
*kriyamāṇaṃ śataguṇaṃ prasādāddantino nṛpa \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O ruler, a bath taken during this moon day, besides the charities given, the fast observed and the recitation performed, is multiplied a hundred times by the grace of Ganesha.

## \|\| 1.31.3 \|\|

*guḍalavaṇaghṛtānāṃ tu dānaṃ śubhakaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*guḍāpūpaistathā vīra puṇyaṃ brāhmaṇabhojanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The giving away of salt and ghi during this period is particularly considered to be quite auspicious. O valorous one, during the worship of Ganesha, the fired cakes made in sugarcane balls when served to Brahmanas, is considered to be more meritorious.

## \|\| 1.31.4-5 \|\|

*yāstasyāṃ naraśārdūla pūjayanti sadā striyaḥ \|*  
*guḍalavaṇapūpaiśca śvaśrūṃ śvasurameva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tāḥ sarvāḥ subhagāḥ syurve1 vighreśasyānumodanāt \|*  
*kanyakā tu viśeṣeṇa vidhinānena pūjayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. O lion among the humans, during the particular day, the women who offer the fried cakes with sweet and saltish dishes to their parents in-law, with the pleasure of Ganapati, they all become virtuous enjoying all the fortunes. The girls particularly should adore lord Ganesha appropriately. Here ends Shiva-kalpah.

## \|\| 1.31.6 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*māghe māsi tathā śuklā yā caturthī mahīpate \|*  
*sā śāntā śāntidā nityaṃ śāntiṃ kuryātsadaiva hi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Sumantu said — O lord of earth, the bright fourth moon day of the month of Magha is known as the bestower of peace and as such it is known by the name of Santa and always bestows peace.

## \|\| 1.31.7 \|\|

*snānadānādikaṃ karma sarvamasyāṃ kṛtaṃ vibho \|*  
*bhavetsahasraguṇitaṃ prasādāttasya2 dantinaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O excellent one, all the deeds like bathing, giving of charities etc., during that particular day, by the grace of Ganesha are a thousand times more productive.

## \|\| 1.31.8 \|\|

*kṛtopavāso yastasyāṃ pūjayedvi ghnanāyakam \|*  
*tasya homādikaṃ karma bhavetsāhasrikaṃ nṛpa \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A person who fasting on that particular day worships Ganesha, the homas and other religious activities yield him a thousand times more merits.

## \|\| 1.31.9 \|\|

*lavaṇaṃ ca guḍaṃ śākaṃ guḍapūpāṃśca bhārata \|*  
*dattvā bhaktyā tu viprebhyaḥ phalaṃ sāhasrikaṃ bhajet3 \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Therefore, one should avail a thousand times more merit by giving away in charity to the Brahmanas the salt, jaggery, vegetables and sweet cakes.

## \|\| 1.31.10 \|\|

*viśeṣataḥ striyo rājanpūjayanto guruṃ nṛpa \|*  
*guḍalavaṇaghṛtairvīra sadā syurbhāgyasaṃyutāḥ4 \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O monarch, especially the women should give away in charity jaggery, salt and clarified butter to the preceptors, adoring them by offering saltish and sweet dishes. By so doing, they would earn great fortunes. Here ends Shanta-kalpah.

## \|\| 1.31.11-13 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sukhāvahā ca susukhā saubhāgyakaraṇī param \|\| 11 \|\|*

*caturthī kuruśārdūla rūpasaubhāgyadā śubhā \|*  
*sukhāvrataṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ rūpadaṃ bhāgyadaṃ tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*susūkṣmaṃ sukaraṃ dhanyamiha puṇyasukhāvaham \|*  
*paratra phaladaṃ vīra divyarūpapradāyakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Sumantu said — O lion among the Kuru race, this fourth moon day is the bestower of enormous pleasures, is extremely fortunate, bestows welfare and great beauty. O valorous one, this is known as Sukha fourth moon day. It is said to be extremely auspicious, bestows beauty and the merits. It is extremely subtle, simple and bestows all the worldly pleasures, glory and heavenly bliss, besides the comforts of heaven. It also bestows the divine beauty.

## \|\| 1.31.14 \|\|

*hasitaṃ lalitaṃ coktaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ ca sukhāvaham \|*  
*savilāsabhujakṣepaścaṃkramaśceṣṭitaṃ śubham \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The activities like laughing, sporting, making efforts to express oneself with the movement of hands, walking etc., are considered to be quite auspicious.

## \|\| 1.31.15 \|\|

*sukhāvratena sarveṣāṃ sukhaṃ kurukulodvaha \|*  
*kṛtyena pūjite ceśe vighreśe śivayoḥ sute \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O leader of the race of Kuru, a person who performs the worship of Ganesha — the son of Shiva and Parvati, in an appropriate manner, he enjoys all the bliss.

## \|\| 1.31.16 \|\|

*yadā śuklacaturthyāṃ tu vāro bhaumasya vai bhavet \|*  
*tadā sā sukhadā jñeyā caturthī vai sukheti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A Tuesday in a bright fortnight and on the fourth moon day is known as Sukha.

## \|\| 1.31.17 \|\|

*purā maithunamāśritya sthitābhyāṃ tu himācale \|*  
*bhīmomābhyāṃ mahābāho raktabinduścyutaḥ kṣitau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O large armed one, in earlier times, when Shiva and Parvati were enjoying conjugal pleasures over the mountain Himalaya, a drop of blood fell on the earth.

## \|\| 1.31.18 \|\|

*medinyāṃ sa prayatnena sukhe vidhṛto'nayā \|*  
*jātosyāḥ sa kujo vīra rakto raktasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. It was preserved by earth with comfort, making all the efforts. The same drop of blood produced Bhauma (Mangala or Mars) having red complexions.

## \|\| 1.31.19 \|\|

*mamāṅgato yathotpannastasmādaṅgārako hyayam \|*  
*aṅgadoṅgopakāraśca aṅgānāṃ tu prado nṛṇām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He is also known as Angaraka since he was born of my limbs. He is the one who bestows the limbs, makes them strong. He bestows limbs to the humans.

## \|\| 1.31.20-22 \|\|

*saubhāgyādikaro yasmāttasmādaṅgārako mataḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā caturthyāṃ naktena yo vai śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*upavatsyati nā rājannārī vā nānyamānasā \|*  
*pūjayecca kujaṃ bhaktayā raktapuṣpavilepanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gaṇeśaṃ prathamaṃ bhaktyā yojayecchaddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*yasya tuṣṭaḥ prayacchetsa saubhāgyaṃ rūpasampadam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Since he also bestows fortunes, he is also known as Angaraka. Therefore, O king, a woman or a man, who with faith and devotion, if fasts on the fourth moon day and adores initially Ganesha and then Mars during the night applying red sandal paste with a concentrated mind, the deities getting pleased with him or her, bestow beauty and fortunes on him or her.

## \|\| 1.31.23-29 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ ca kṛtasaṅkalpaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*gṛhītvā mṛttikāṃ vandenmantreṇānena bhārata \|\| 23 \|\|*

*iha tvaṃ vanditā pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇenoddharatā kila \|*  
*tasmānme daha pāpmānaṃ yanmayā pūrvasañcitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra ādityāya pradarśayet \|*  
*ādityaraśmisampūtāṃ gaṅgājalakaṇokṣitām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dattvā mṛdaṃ śirasi tāṃ sarvāṅgeṣu ca yojayet \|*  
*tataḥ snānaṃ prakurvīta mantrayeta jalaṃ punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tvamāpo yoniḥ sarveṣāṃ daityadānavadyaukasām \|*  
*svedāṇḍajodbhidāṃ caiva rasānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*snāto'haṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvaprasravaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*taḍāgeṣu ca sarveṣu mānasādisaraḥsu ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nadīṣu devakhāteṣu sutīrtheṣu hradeṣu vai \|*  
*dhyāyanyaṭhannimaṃ mantraṃ tataḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 29 \|\|*

23-29. O mother, initially samkalpa should be performed. One should take his bath appropriately. While so doing, he should pick up some dust and then reciting the mantra “Iha tvam vandita”, while adoring him, the dust should be soaked with the sacred water of the Ganga, and he should apply it over his head and then apply it over the entire body. Thereafter, reciting the mantra “tvamapo yonih sarvesham”, the water should be sanctified with the waters collected from sacred rivers and various holy places. Then he should take his bath.

## \|\| 1.31.30 \|\|

*tataḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā gṛhamāgatya vai spṛśet \|*  
*dūrvāśvatthau śamīṃ spṛṣṭvā gāṃ ca mantreṇa mantravit \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereafter, the person well-versed in the mantras purify himself after the bath. Then doing homa, he should touch Durva grass, Pippala tree and Shami bush.

## \|\| 1.31.31-37 \|\|

*dūrvā namasya mantreṇa śucau bhūmau samutthitām \|*  
*tvaṃ dūrve'mṛtanāmāsi sarvadevaistu vanditā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vanditā daha tatsarvaṃ duritaṃ yanmayā1 kṛtam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śamīmantraṃ pravakṣyāmi tannibodha mahīpate \|*  
*pavitrāṇāṃ pavitrāṃ tvaṃ kāśyapī prathitā śrutau \|*  
*śamī śamaya me pāpaṃ nūnaṃ vetsi dharādharān \|\| 33 \|\|*

*aśvatthālambhane vīra mantrametaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*netraspandādijaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥsvapnaṃ durvicintanam \|*  
*śaktānāṃ ca samudyogamaśvattha tvaṃ kṣamasva me \|\| 34 \|\|*

*imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra kuryādvai sparśanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*tato devyai tu gāṃ dadyādvīraṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*samālabhya tu hastena tato mantramudīrayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sarvadevamayī devi munibhistu supūjitā \|*  
*tasmātspṛśāmi vande tvāṃ vanditā pāpahā bhava \|\| 36 \|\|*

*imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādarjunaṃ kurunandana \|*  
*pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena pṛthivī syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

31-37. O lord of earth, with the durva grass used in the bath, one should adore the Sami bush. I am going to speak out the relevant mantras as well. You please listen, the mantra is; “pavitranam pavitra tvam etc” By reciting the mantra “netra-spandadijam etc.” one should touch ashvattha tree. Then performing the circumambulation and uttering the mantra “sarvadevamayi Devi”, one should touch a cow. Then the cow should be given in charity. O son of the race of Kuru, one who reciting this mantra goes round the Arjuna tree, it would surely be equated in merit of going round the earth.

## \|\| 1.31.38-44 \|\|

*evaṃ maunena cāgatya tato vahnigṛhaṃ vrajet \|*  
*prakṣālya ca mṛdā pādāvācāntognigṛhaṃ viśet \|*  
*homaṃ tatra prakurvīta ebhirmantrapadairvaraiḥ3 \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śarvāya śarvaputrāya kṣoṇyutsaṅgabhavāya ca \|*  
*kujāya lalitāṅgāya lohitāṅgāya vai tathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*oṃkārapūrvakairmantraiḥ svāhākārasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭottaraśataṃ vīra ardhārdhamardhameva ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

*etairmantrapadairbhaktyā śaktyā vā kāmato nṛpa \|*  
*khādiraiḥ susamidbhistu cājyadugdhairyavaistilaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*bhakṣyairnānāvidhaiścānyaiḥ śaktyā bhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*hutvāhutīstato4 vīra devaṃ saṃsthāpayetkṣitau \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi śaktyā dārumayaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*devadārumayaṃ vāpi śrīkhaṇḍacandanairapi \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tāmre pātre raupyamaye cājyakuṅkumakesaraiḥ \|*  
*anyairvā lohitairvāpi puṣpaiḥ patraiḥ phalairapi \|*  
*raktaiśca vividhairvīra atha vā śaktito'rcayet1 \|\| 44 \|\|*

38-44. Then keeping silence, he should arrive at the fire altar. Reaching there, he should purify his feet with dust and perform sipping of water and then entering the chamber of homa, reciting the mantra “Om Sarvaya Sarvaputraya etc.”, he should pour offerings of various types of eatables in the fire flames. A hundred and eight offerings of catechu wood, clarified butter, milk, barley and sesamum or half of it, or still half of it, i.e. twenty seven times, should be made. O monarch, this should be done as per the means of a person, with devotion and as per one’s desire. O valorous one, after performing the homa, one should give away a figure made of gold, silver, devadaru, or some other wood or of sandalwood, and placing it in the vase of silver or copper, should establish it on earth. Thereafter, vermilion, saffron, red flowers, fruits and the leaves should be offered to the deity as per one’s capacity while worshipping it.

## \|\| 1.31.45 \|\|

*varadvisṛjate vittaṃ vittavānvīra bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvivardhate puṇyaṃ dātuṃ śatasahasrikam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O great warrior, whatever is spent by a rich person in such cases he earns the merit thousand times more than that.

## \|\| 1.31.46-47 \|\|

*anye tāmramaye pātre vaṃśaje mṛnmaye'pi vā \|*  
*pūjayanti narāḥ śaktyā kṛtvā kuṅkumakeśaraiḥ \|*  
*puruṣākṛtikṛtaṃ pātra imaṃ mantraiḥ samarcayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

*agrirmūrdheti mantreṇa gandhapuṣpādibhistathā \|*  
*dhūpairabhyarcya vidhivadbrāhmaṇāya pradīyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The people worship the deity placing him in the copper, bamboo and earthen vases, and offering vermilion and saffron. Therefore, making an image resembling a human and reciting the Agni-murdha mantra appropriately, offer the deity incense, flowers, fragrance and then donate it to a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.31.48 \|\|

*guḍaudanaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ godhūmāñchālitaṇḍulān \|*  
*avekṣya śaktiṃ dadyādvai daridro vittavāṃstathā \|\| 48\|\|*

48\. Thereafter, irrespective of one’s being a rich or a poor person, according to one’s own capacity, one should offer to a Brahmana sweet rice, clarified butter, milk, wheat and excellent rice.

## \|\| 1.31.49 \|\|

*vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kartavyaṃ vidyamāne dhane nṛpa \|*  
*vittaśāṭhyaṃ hi kurvāṇo nāmutra balabhāgbhavet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O monarch, one should not behave miserly inspite of being rich because one who behaves miserly in giving away charity, he does not earn the divine reward.

## \|\| 1.31.50 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*aṅgārakeṇa saṃyuktā caturthī naktabhojanaiḥ \|*  
*upoṣyā katimātrā tu utāho sakṛdeva tu2 \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Shatanika said — After observing the fast for Bhauma’s fourth moon day, the food is taken in the night. How many times should it be taken? Or has it to be taken only once?

## \|\| 1.31.51 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*caturthī sā caturthī sā yadāṅgārakasaṃyutā \|*  
*upoṣyā tatra tatraiva pradeyo vidhivadguḍaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Sumantu said — The fourth moon day of Angaraka (or Mars) is called Chautha. In due course of time, whenever it arrives, then fasting during that period jaggery should be offered in charity.

## \|\| 1.31.52 \|\|

*upoṣya naktena vibho catasraḥ kujasaṃyutā \|*  
*caturthyāṃ ca caturthyāṃ ca vidhānaṃ śṛṇu yādṛśam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O excellent one, it has been ordained that the fourth moon day of Mars should be observed four times. You listen, I shall speak out whatever has been prescribed about it in the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.31.53-57 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ tu kujaṃ kṛtvā savināyakamādarāt \|*  
*daśasauvarṇikaṃ mukhyaṃ daśārdhamardhameva ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sauvarṇapātre raupye vā bhaktyā tāmramaye'pi vā \|*  
*viṃśatpalāni pātrāṇi viṃśatyardhapalāni vā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*viṃśatkarṣāṇi vā vīra viṃśadardhārdhameva vā \|*  
*raupyasaṅkhyaṃ palaṃ kāryaṃ palārdhamardhameva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śaktyā vittaiśca bhaktyā ca pātre tāmramaye'pi tu \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya graheśaṃ vai vastraiḥ sampariveṣṭitam \|*  
*vividhaiḥ sādhakai raktaiḥ puṣpai raktaiḥ samanvitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇāya sadā dadyāddakṣiṇāsahitaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*vācakāya mahābāho guṇine śreyase nṛpa \|\| 57 \|\|*

53-57. A figure of Ganesha and Mars should be made in dashaphala (a weight) or the half of it or a quarter of it, of gold. The figure should be covered with cloth and kept in a vase of gold, silver or copper vase which should be of twenty or ten palas or alternatively of twenty, ten or five karshas of gold. Similarly, the vase of copper should also be made according to one’s financial position. O valorous one, thereafter, other materials for worship should be collected and should be offered with devotion and dakshina to a Brahmana who performs the religious rites as well as the recitation.

## \|\| 1.31.58-60 \|\|

*iti te kathitā puṇyā tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naro rūpaṃ divyamāpnoti bhārata \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kāntyātreyasamaṃ vīraṃ tejasā ravisannibham \|*  
*prabhayā ravikalpaṃ ca samīrabalasaṃśritam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*īdṛgrūpaṃ samāpyeha yāti bhaumasado nṛpa \|*  
*prasādādvighnanāthasya tathā gaṇapaternṛpa \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. O Bharata, thus I have described the glory of the auspicious moon day Chaturthi which is quite meritorious and is best of all the moon days and by performing whose vrata, a person attains the divine form. As a result of this, one attains the lustre of the moon, the shine of the sun and the strength of the wind by the grace of Vighneshvara Ganapati and finally achieves the place of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.31.61 \|\|

*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ rājankurvatāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyādipāpāni kṣīyante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā lakṣmīṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. By reading this episode or by listening to the same and particularly the one who performs the vrata, all his sins including those like the killing of a Brahmana, are removed undoubtedly. He achieves all the success, prosperity and the riches.

## Chapter 32. Worship of Naga-panchami

## \|\| 1.32.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*pañcamī dayitā rājannāgānāṃ nandivardhinī \|*  
*pañcamyāṃ kila nāgānāṃ bhavatītyutsavo mahān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O king, the fifth moon day (of a fortnight) enhances the delight of the Nagas (serpents) and is quite dear to them. Because of this, a great festival is observed on the fifth moon day for the Nagas.

## \|\| 1.32.2 \|\|

*vāsukistakṣakaścaiva kāliyo maṇibhadrakaḥ \|*  
*airāvato dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ1 karkoṭakadhanañjayau \|*  
*ete prayacchantyabhayaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇajīvitām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Nagas like Vasuki, Takshaka, Kaliyanaga, Manibhadra, Airavata, Dhritarashtra, Karkotaka and Dhananjaya besides others, bestow amnesty to the people.

## \|\| 1.32.3 \|\|

*tathā gandhaiśca dhūpaiśca pūjya pañcakamuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Therefore, the people who offer milk to the serpents or bathe them with the same, their families are always protected from the snake bite.

## \|\| 1.32.4-5 \|\|

*śaptā nāgā yadā mātrā dahyamānā divāniśam \|*  
*nirvāpayanti snapanairgavāṃ3 kṣīreṇa miśritaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ye snapayanti vai nāgānbhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitā \|*  
*teṣāṃ kule sarpabhayaṃ na bhavediti niścayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Therefore, on the same day, the serpents who suffer day and night because of their own mother, a person who offers the cow’s milk to the Nagas with devotion or bathes them, surely he earns protection from the snake bite for his family.

## \|\| 1.32.6 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*mātrā śaptāḥ kathaṃ nāgāḥ kiṃ samuddiśya kāraṇam \|*  
*kathaṃ cānandakaraṇaṃ kasya vā samprasādajam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Shatanika said — Why did the mother curse the Nagas? What was the aim behind it? By whose grace the fifth moon day becomes delightful for them?

## \|\| 1.32.7-8 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*uccaiḥśravā aśvaratnaṃ śveto jāto'mṛtodbhavaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā cābravītkadrūrnāgānāṃ jananī svasām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*aśvaratnamidaṃ śvetaṃ samprekṣe'mṛtasambhavam \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśca vīkṣase bālānsarvaṃ śvetamutāmbare \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Sumantu said — At the time of churning of the ocean, the divine horse Ucchaishrava emerged out of the nectar of the ocean. It was of white colour and was as precious like the other gems. On breezing the divine horse, Kadru — the mother of the Nagas, spoke to her sister Vinata— “I am observing this horse who has emerged out of the nectar of the ocean, resembling the white gem. But it is black as well. Do you find the white hair of the horse or the black part of it?”

## \|\| 1.32.9 \|\|

*vinatovāca \|*  
*sarvaśveto hayavaro nāsya kṛṣṇo na lohitaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ paśyasi kṛṣṇaṃ tvaṃ vinatovāca tāṃ svasām4 \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vinata said — “The excellent horse is all white. It’s hair is neither black nor red. How do you find it black?”

## \|\| 1.32.10 \|\|

*kadrūruvāca \|*  
*vīkṣe'hamekanayanā kṛṣṇabālasamanvitam \|*  
*dvinetrā tvaṃ tu vinate na paśyasi paṇaṃ kuru \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Kadru said — “O Vinata, I have a single eye, but I find the horse with black hair. But you have two eyes, still you cannot look at the horse properly. Then let us have a stake.”

## \|\| 1.32.11 \|\|

*vinatovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ dāsī bhavitrī te kṛṣṇe keśe pradarśite \|*  
*na ceddarśayase kadru mama dāsī bhaviṣyasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Vinata said — “In case you can show me the black hair of the horse, then I shall be your slave for life or otherwise you will serve me as my slave.”

## \|\| 1.32.12 \|\|

*evaṃ te vipaṇaṃ kṛtvā gate krodhasamanvite \|*  
*vinatā śayane suptā kadrūrjihmamacintayat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus, both of them getting enraged, put a wager. When Vinata went to her bedroom for sleep, then Kadru thought of playing a trick.

## \|\| 1.32.13 \|\|

*āhūya putrānprovāca bālā bhūtvā hayottame \|*  
*tiṣṭhadhvaṃ vipaṇe jeṣye vinatāṃ jayagarddhinīm \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. She called for all the serpents and asked them to stick to the body of the horse like the black hair to enable her to win the wager from Vinata.

## \|\| 1.32.14 \|\|

*procuste jihmabuddhiṃ tāṃ nāgā mātāṃ1 vigṛhya tu \|*  
*adharmyametanmātaste na kariṣyāma te vacaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On hearing this, the serpents spoke to their mother, who was about to play a trick to defeat Vinata. They said — “O mother, this is degraded and irreligious thought. We shall not agree to these words spoken by you.”

## \|\| 1.32.15-16 \|\|

*tāñśaśāpa ruṣā kadrūḥ pāvako vaḥ pradhakṣyati \|*  
*gate bahutithe kāle pāṇḍavo janamejayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sarpasatraṃ sa kartā vai bhuvi hyanyaiḥ suduṣkaram \|*  
*tasminsatre sa tigmāṃśuḥ pāvako vaḥ pradhakṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Thereafter, Kadru getting enraged, pronounced a curse to her sons — the serpents, thus — “Let you be burnt by fire. After a long time, Janmejaya — the son of the Pandavas, will perform a serpent yajna on earth which would be difficult for anyone else to perform. The terrific fire flames of the fire altar will bum you out.”

## \|\| 1.32.17 \|\|

*evaṃ śaptvā ruṣā kadrūḥ kiñcinnoktavatī tu sā \|*  
*mātrā śaptāstathā nāgāḥ kartavyaṃ nānvapatsata \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Getting immensely enraged, Kadru pronounced the terrific curse on the serpents, and said nothing further. The serpents then, having been so cursed by their own mother, could not be conscious of their deity at that point of time.

## \|\| 1.32.18 \|\|

*vāsukiṃ duḥkhitaṃ jñātvā brahmā provāca sāntvayan \|*  
*mā śuco vāsuke'tyarthaṃ śṛṇu madvacana param \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Finding Vasuki in miserable state, lord Brahma said to him — “O Vasuki, don’t feel agitated too much. Listen to my excellent words.

## \|\| 1.32.19 \|\|

*yāyāvarakule jāto jaratkārūriti dvijaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati mahātejāstasminkāle taponidhiḥ 1 \|*  
*\|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. At the same time, an immensely illustrious son named Jaratkaru would be born in Yayavara race.

## \|\| 1.32.20 \|\|

*bhaginīṃ ca jaratkāruṃ tasmai tvaṃ pratidāsyasi \|*  
*bhavitā tasya putro'sāvāstīka iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You would offer him in marriage your sister named Jaratkaru. A son named Astika would be born to her. This is what has been heard by me.

## \|\| 1.32.21 \|\|

*sa tatsatraṃ pravṛddhaṃ vai nāgānāṃ bhayadaṃ mahat \|*  
*niṣedhetsumatirvāgbhiragryābhistaṃ naviṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter, an intelligent Brahmana shall pray with his excellent speech to stop the horrible yajna which had been started for the destruction of the serpents.

## \|\| 1.32.22 \|\|

*tadimāṃ bhaginīṃ rājaṃstasya tvaṃ pratidāsyasi \|*  
*jaratkāruṃ jaratkāroḥ pradadyā avicārayan \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Therefore, you must give away in marriage your sister to the said Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.32.23 \|\|

*yadāsau prārthate'raṇye yatkiñciddhi vadiṣyati \|*  
*tatkartavyamaśaṅkena yadīccheḥ śreya ātmanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In case you are desirous of your own welfare, whatever the said Brahmana desires in the forest, you must fulfil his desires without any doubt.”

## \|\| 1.32.24 \|\|

*pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā vāsukiḥ praṇipatya ca \|*  
*tathākarodyathā coktaṃ yatnaṃ ca paramāsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus listening to the words of Brahma — the grandsire, the serpent Vasuki offered his salutation to him and took vow to perform accordingly, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.32.25 \|\|

*tacchrutvā pannagāḥ sarve praharṣotphullalocanāḥ \|*  
*punarjātamivātmānaṃ menire bhujagottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hearing the words of Brahma, the eyes of all the serpents started beaming and they thought themselves as having been reborn.

## \|\| 1.32.26 \|\|

*tatra satraṃ mahābāho1 tava pitrā pravartitam \|*  
*ṛtvigbhiḥ sa hi teneha sarvalokeṣu duṣkaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O valorous one, your father started the difficult yajna through the Brahmanas who acted as the performers of the same, which was beyond the capacity of anyone else.

## \|\| 1.32.27 \|\|

*proktaṃ ca viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ dharmaputrasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*avaśyaṃ tasya bhavitā nāgānāṃ bhayakārakam3 \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Lord Krishna had informed the intelligent Yudhishthira earlier that the yajna for the destruction of the serpents would surely be performed.

## \|\| 1.32.28 \|\|

*tasmātkālāntarādrājansāgre varṣaśate gate \|*  
*tatsatraṃ bhavitā ghoraṃ nāgānāṃ kṣayakārakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After the lapse of the period of a hundred years, the terrific yajna for the destruction of the serpents would be surely performed.

## \|\| 1.32.29 \|\|

*yāsyantyadharmabharitā dandaśūkā viṣolbaṇāḥ \|*  
*koṭisaṅkhyā mahārāja nipatiṣyantyaharniśam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O great ruler, the poisonous serpents would also be sinful and shall fall (in the fire altar) in millions throughout the day and night.

## \|\| 1.32.30 \|\|

*apūrve tu nimagnānāṃ ghore raudrāgnisāgare \|*  
*āstīkastatra bhavitā teṣāṃ naurvahnisāgare \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. But in order to save the serpents from the horrible, unprecedented flames of fire, a sage named Astika would arrive like a boat in the ocean of the disturbed waters.

## \|\| 1.32.31 \|\|

*śrutvā sa cāgniṃ rājānamṛtvijastadanantaram \|*  
*nivartayiṣyate yāgaṃ nāgānāṃ mohanaṃ param \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Hearing about the start of the serpent yajna, (the Brahmana) would stop the fire, the king as well as the performers of yajna.

## \|\| 1.32.32 \|\|

*pañcamyāṃ tatra bhavitā brahmā provāca lelihān \|*  
*tasmādiyaṃ mahābāho pañcamī dayitā sadā \|*  
*nāgānāmānandakarī dattā vai brahmaṇā purā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Brahma had informed the serpents that the task of their protection would be performed on the fifth moon-day. O valorous one, because of this, the fifth moon day is the favourite of the serpents. Brahma have bestowed a boon on the serpents on the same day, delighting them at the same time.

## \|\| 1.32.33-35 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu bhojanaṃ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu kāmataḥ \|*  
*visṛjya nāgāḥ prīyantāṃ ye kecitpṛthivītale \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ye ca helimarīcisthā ye'ntare divi saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*ye nadīṣu mahānāgā ye sarasvatigāminaḥ \|*  
*ye ca vāpītaḍāgeṣu teṣu sarveṣu vai namaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nāgānviprāṃśca sampūjya visṛjya ca yathārthataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ paścāttu bhuñjīta saha bhṛtyairnarādhipa \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Therefore, on that particular day, after well feeding the Brahmanas, the rite of sending off the serpents should be performed. Thereafter, he should offer salutation to serpents living on the earth, the female friend, catechu tree, seven Rishis, the sky, Sarasvati, a river bed, step well, tanks etc. Thus, the serpents and the Brahmanas should be sent off, adoring them. Thereafter, he should take return with the servants.

## \|\| 1.32.36 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ madhuramaśnīyāttato bhuñjīta kāmataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ niyamayuktasya yatphalaṃ tannibodha me \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At that point of time, the sweet dishes should be taken initially. Thereafter, one can take anything as per his liking. When he performs the vrata appropriately, the fruit he achieves for the same is being revealed by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.32.37 \|\|

*mṛto nāgapuraṃ yāti pūjyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*vimānavaramārūḍho ramate kālamīpsitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After meeting with his end, the person initially reaches the abode of serpents, where he is served by the fairy maidens. He then mounting the excellent plane, sports with them upto the time of his liking.

## \|\| 1.32.38 \|\|

*iha cāgatya rājāsāvayutānāṃ1 varo bhavet \|*  
*sarvaratnasamṛddhaḥ syādvāhanāḍhyaśca jāyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thereafter, he arrives in this world at sometime and becomes a king, who becoming the lord of the world possesses enough of gems, vehicles besides other riches.

## \|\| 1.32.39 \|\|

*pañca janmānyasau rājā dvāpare dvāpare bhavet \|*  
*ādhivyādhivinirmuktaḥ patnīputrasahāyavān \|*  
*tasmātpūjyāśca pālyāśca2 ghṛtapāyasaguggulaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, he in Dvapara and other yugas enjoys the position of a king in five births, who is always free from the mental and bodily ailments. His wives and sons always remain in attention to serve him. Therefore, on that particular day, the serpent should be worshipped offering ghi, payasam and guggulu.

## \|\| 1.32.40 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*daśanti ye naraṃ vipra nāgāḥ krodhasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*bhavetkiṃ tasya daṣṭasya vistarād brūhi me dvija \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Shatanika said — O Brahmana, getting enraged when a serpent bites someone, what type of a condition does he face? You kindly tell me in detail.

## \|\| 1.32.41 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*nāgadaṣṭo naro rājanprāpya mṛtyuṃ vrajatyadhaḥ \|*  
*adho gatyā bhavetsarpo nirviṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Sumantu said — O king, when a serpent bites someone, the concerned person meets with his death and reaches the nether world, where he is surely freed from venom.

## \|\| 1.32.42 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*nāgadaṣṭaḥ pitā yasya bhrātā vā duhitāpi vā \|*  
*mātā putro'tha vā bhāryā kiṃ kartavyaṃ vadasva me \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Shatanika said — O chief among the rulers, a person whose father, brother, daughter, mother, the son or the wife is bitten by a snake, what is the duty of that person towards them? You please tell me.

## \|\| 1.32.43 \|\|

*mokṣāya tasya viprendra dānaṃ vratamupoṣaṇam \|*  
*brūhi taddvijaśārdūla yena tadvai karomyaham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. What is to be done to get the person bitten by sake redeemed from the snake bite? Otherwise, you enlighten as to what is required to be done in such cases? I shall surely do so.

## \|\| 1.32.44-45 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*upoṣyā pañcamī rājannāgānāṃ puṣṭivardhinī \|*  
*tvamevamekaṃ rājendra vidhānaṃ śṛṇu bhārata \|\| 44 \|\|*

*māsi bhādrapade yā tu kṛṣṇapakṣe1 mahīpate \|*  
*mahāpuṇyā tu sā proktā grāhyāpi ca mahīpate \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Sumantu said — O king, for the sake of the person bitten by a snake, one should perform the vrata on the fifth moon day, which makes the people strong. O Bharata, I am going to reveal the method for the same. O lord of the earth, the fifth moon day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada is said to be more auspicious. Therefore, it should be patronised for the performing of the vrata.

## \|\| 1.32.46-47 \|\|

*jñeyā dvādaśa ṣañcamyo hāyane bharatarṣabha \|*  
*cartuthyāṃ tvekabhaktaṃ tu tasyāṃ naktaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*bhuvi citramayānnāgānatha vā kaladhautakān \|*  
*kṛtvā dārumayānvāpi atha vā mṛnmayānnṛpa \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. O best of the race of Bharata, there are twelve (dark) fifth moon days in a year and accordingly, on the night of the fourth moon day, taking of food once a day has been prescribed. Because of that, on the fifth moon day, a figure of a serpent in gold, wood or clay should be made and should be worshipped with devotion.

## \|\| 1.32.48-49 \|\|

*pañcamyāmarcayedbhaktyā nāgānāṃ pañcakaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*karavīraiḥ śatapatrairjātīpuṣpaiśca suvrata \|\| 48 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayetpaścād ghṛtapāyasamodakaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. O Suvrata, the flowers of lotus, jasmine etc. should be offered besides fragrance of incense on the fifth moon day. Thereafter, the Brahmanas should be served with payasam with ghi and sweet balls.

## \|\| 1.32.50-51 \|\|

*ananto vāsukiḥ śaṅkhaḥ padmaḥ kambala eva ca \|*  
*tathā karkoṭako nāgo nāgo hyaśvataro nṛpa \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ śaṅkhapālaḥ kāliyastakṣakastathā \|*  
*piṅgalaśca tathā nāgo māsi māsi prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. O king, accordingly the worship of twelve serpents has been prescribed for the twelve months of the year, which includes: Ananta, Vasuki, Shankha, Padma, Kambala, Karkotaka, Asvatara, Dhritarashtra, Shamkhapala, Kaliya, Takshaka and Pingala.

## \|\| 1.32.52 \|\|

*vatsarānte pāraṇaṃ syādbrāhmaṇānbhojayedbahūn \|*  
*itihāsavide nāgaṃ gairikeṇa kṛtaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tathārcanā pradātavyā vācakāya mahīpate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After completion of the year, the fast may be concluded after offering food to served Brahmanas. The figure of gold should be handed over to the reciter of the scriptures who is also well-versed in the Puranas.

## \|\| 1.32.53 \|\|

*eṣa vai nāgapañcamyā5 vidhiḥ proktā budhairnṛpa \|*  
*tava pitrā kṛtaścaiva piturmokṣāya bhārata \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O king, the prescribed process for the Naga-panchami as prescribed by the learned Brahmanas, was performed by your father for the redemption of his own father.

## \|\| 1.32.54-56 \|\|

*tvamekamekaṃ vai vīra pañcamyāṃ bharatarṣabha \|*  
*suvarṇabhāraniṣpannaṃ nāgaṃ dattvā tathā ca gām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vyāsāya kuruśārdūla piturānṛṇyamāpnuyāḥ \|*  
*tava pitrā kṛtā hyevaṃ pañcamyupāsanā nṛpa \|\| 55 \|\|*

*utsṛjya nāgatāṃ vīra tava pūrvapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*puṣpottaraṃ sado gatvā tathā puṣpasado nṛpa \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. Therefore, you also, in each one of the Panchami vrata, give away the figure of each one of the serpents made in gold, with a cow to the narrator of scriptures and get yourself free from the debt of your parents who are manes at present. This is because your father also worshipped in the same way with varied flowers on panchami.

## \|\| 1.32.57 \|\|

*sunāsīrasado gatvā tadā bhargasado gataḥ \|*  
*svabhūsadastato gatvā kañjajasya sado gataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O king, your great grandfather, discarding his serpent body, had respectively achieved the places of Kubera, Indra, Brahma and Vishnu.

## \|\| 1.32.58 \|\|

*anye'pi ye kariṣyanti idaṃ vratamanuttamam \|*  
*daṣṭako mokṣyate teṣāṃ śubhaṃ sthānamavāpsyati \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Similarly, such of the people, who will perform this vrata in future, after having been bitten by snakes, they would surely achieve the best of place.

## \|\| 1.32.59 \|\|

*yaścedaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ naraḥ1 śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*kule tasya na nāgebhyo bhayaṃ bhavati kutracit \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A person who listens with devotion this episode, there remains no danger of a snake bite in his family.

## Chapter 33. Divisions of serpents

## \|\| 1.33.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*sarpāṇāṃ kati rūpāṇi ke varṇāḥ kiṃ ca lakṣaṇam \|*  
*kā jātistu bhavetteṣāṃ keṣu yonikuleṣu vā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — What is number of the varieties of the serpents, what is the number of their colours? How many types they have and what are their symptoms and in which category do they fall? You kindly let me know.

## \|\| 1.33.2-3 \|\|

*mayūrānmānuṣādvāpi cakorādgokhurāttathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sarpāṇāṃ kati rūpāṇi kiṃ cihnaṃ kiṃ ca lakṣaṇam \|*  
*jātiṃ kulaṃ tadhā varṇānbrūhi sarvaṃ prajāpate \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Sumantu said — Once in earlier times, over the beautiful Meru mountain, Gautama offered his salutation with utmost devotion to the sage Kashyapa who was the incarnation of tapas, lowering his head and said — “O lord Prajapati, how many forms of serpents are there? What are their symptoms, types, races and the colours? You kindly enlighten me about all of them.

## \|\| 1.33.4-6 \|\|

*kathaṃ vā jāyate sarpaḥ kadhaṃ muñcedviṣaṃ prabho \|*  
*viṣavegāḥ kati proktāḥ katyeva viṣanāḍikāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrāḥ katividhāḥ proktāḥ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ viṣāgame \|*  
*gṛhṇīte tu kadā garbhaṃ kathaṃ ceha prasūyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kīdṛśī strī pumāṃścaiva kīdṛśaśca napuṃsakaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ nāma daśanaṃ caiva etatkathaya suvrata \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. How are the serpents born? How do they bite emitting the venom? What is the force of the venom? What is the number of veins in the venom? What are the varieties of teeth of the serpents? What is the proof of their being poisonous? When do they become pregnant and how are their young one born? How are the males, females and the eunuchs divided among them? What is the snake bite? O Suvrata, you kindly enlighten me on all these points.”

## \|\| 1.33.7-8 \|\|

*tasya1 tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kaśyapaḥ pratyabhāṣata \|*  
*śṛṇu gautama tattvena sarpāṇāmiha lakṣaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*māsyāṣāḍhe tathā jyeṣṭhe pramādyanti bhujaṅgamāḥ \|*  
*tato nāgo'tha nāgī ca maithune samprapadyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Listening to the words of Gautama, Kashyapa said — “O Gautama, you listen to me attentively, I am going to speak about the symptoms of the serpents. During the months of Ashadha and Jyestha, the serpents get intoxicated, when №gas and Nagins unite.

## \|\| 1.33.9 \|\|

*caturo vārṣikānmāsānnāgī garbhamadhārayat \|*  
*tataḥ kārttikamāse tu aṇḍakāni prasūyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The female serpent remains pregnant during four months of the rainy season and in the month of Karttika, she lays down the eggs.

## \|\| 1.33.10 \|\|

*aṇḍakānāṃ tu vijñeye dveśate dve ca viṃśatī \|*  
*tānyeva bhakṣayetsā tu bhogaikaṃ ghṛṇayā tyajet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The number of the eggs laid at a time is two hundred and forty. Soon after laying the eggs, the female serpent starts eating them and out of contempt, she leaves one fourth of them.

## \|\| 1.33.11 \|\|

*svarṇārkavarṇādvai tasmātpumānsañjāyate'ṇḍakāt \|*  
*tānyeva khādate sarpa ahorātrāṇi viṃśatim \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The eggs which shine like the sun rays or the gold produce the male serpents. The serpent swallows them for twenty days.

## \|\| 1.33.12-14 \|\|

*svarṇaketakavarṇābhāddīrgharājīvasannibhāt \|*  
*tasmādutpadyate strī vai aṇḍādbrāhmaṇasattama \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śirīṣapuṣpavarṇābhādaṇḍakātsyānnapuṃsakaḥ \|*  
*tato bhinatti cāṇḍāni ṣaṇmāsena tu gautama \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tataste prītisambandhātsnehaṃ badhnanti bālakāḥ \|*  
*tato'sau saptarātreṇa kṛṣṇo bhavati pannagaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. O best of Brahmanas, similarly, out of the eggs which resemble the golden ketaki flowers or the long lotus flowers, female serpents emerge, while the eggs resembling the flowers of acacia tree produce the eunuch serpents. O Gautama, the eggs get hatched during the sixth month, when the motherly affection is aroused in the mother serpent, which turn black in a week’s time.

## \|\| 1.33.15 \|\|

*āyuḥpramāṇaṃ sarpāṇāṃ śataṃ viṃśottaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*mṛtyuścāṣṭavidho jñeyaḥ śṛṇuṣvātra yathākramam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The serpents remain alive for a hundred and twenty years. They have to face eight types of death, which I am going to tell you. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.33.16-17 \|\|

*biḍālānnakulāccaiva varāhādvṛścikāttathā \|*  
*eteṣāṃ yadi mucyeta jīvedviṃśottaraṃ śatam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*saptāhe tu tataḥ pūrṇe daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ cādhirohaṇam \|*  
*viṣasyāgamanaṃ tatra nikṣipecca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. In case a serpent could be able to save itself from the attack of peacock, cow’s hoofs, cat, mongoose, pigs and scorpion, then it can live for a hundred and twenty years. After birth of the young one of a serpent, its teeth are grown after a week and the venom starts infusing in them.

## \|\| 1.33.18 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā tu tattvena viṣakarmmārabheta vai \|*  
*ekaviṃśatirātreṇa viṣadaṃṣṭrā sujāyate \|*  
*nāgīpārśvasamāvartī bālasarpaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Well realizing about the same, they start biting. The poisonous teeth of the serpent are firmly in position after twenty one days. A serpent keeping company of a female serpent is known as a bala serpent.

## \|\| 1.33.19 \|\|

*pañcaviṃśatirātrastu sadyaḥ prāṇaharo bhavet \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsājjātamātrastu kañcukaṃ vai pramuñcati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus a serpent which, after birth, completes living on earth for twenty five days, kills a person soon after biting him. A snake removes the skin after six months.

## \|\| 1.33.20 \|\|

*pādānāṃ cāpi vijñeye dve śate dve ca viṃśatī \|*  
*golomasadṛśāḥ pādāḥ praviśanti kramanti ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They have two hundred and forty feet resembling the hair of the cow, which emerge at the time of crawling and otherwise remain concealed in the body.

## \|\| 1.33.21 \|\|

*sandhīnāṃ cāsya vijñeye dveśate viṃśatī tathā \|*  
*aṃgulyaścāpi vijñeyā dve śate viṃśatī tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There are two hundred and twenty joints in the body of each serpent. Similar are the number of their fingers.

## \|\| 1.33.22 \|\|

*akālajātā ye sarpā nirviṣāste prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*pañcasaptativarṣāṇi āyusteṣāṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The serpents which do not have a timely birth, they are devoid of venom and live the life of seventy five years each.

## \|\| 1.33.23 \|\|

*raktapītaśukladantā anīlā mandaveginaḥ \|*  
*ete alpāyuṣo jñeyo anye ca bhīravaḥ smṛtā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The serpents other than those with teeth of red, yellow, white or blue colours, crawl slowly and are short lived besides being fearful.

## \|\| 1.33.24 \|\|

*ekaṃ cāsya bhavedvaktraṃ dve jihve ca prakīrtite \|*  
*dvātriṃśaddaśanāḥ proktāḥ pannāgānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The serpents have a single mouth, two tongues and thirty two teeth. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.33.25-27 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhye catasrastu daṃṣṭrā yāḥ suviṣāvahāḥ \|*  
*makarī karālī kālarātrī yamadūtī tathaiva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarvāsāṃ caiva daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*prathamā brahmadevatyā dvitīyā viṣṇudevatā \|*  
*tṛtīyā rudradevatyā caturthī yamadevatā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*hīnā pramāṇataḥ sā tu vāmanetraṃ samāśritā \|*  
*nāsyāṃ mantrāḥ prayoktavyā nauṣadhaṃ naiva bheṣajam \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Out of them, the four teeth are extremely venomous. They have four jaws each, known by the names of Makari, Karali, Kalaratri and Yamaduti and their respective gods are said to be Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra and Yama. The jaw known by the name of Yamaduti is the smallest of all and is lodged over the left eye. After a person is bitten with this jaw, no mantra, medicine or any other treatment works.

## \|\| 1.33.28 \|\|

*vaidyaḥ parāṅmukho yāti mṛtyustasyā vilekhanāt \|*  
*cikitsā na budhaiḥ kāryā tadantaṃ tasya jīvitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Because the death in such a case is certain, the physician gets defeated in such a case. Therefore, it has to be taken for granted that the life of the person (who is so bitten) has come to an end. Thus realizing, the wise Brahmanas should not extend any treatment to him.

## \|\| 1.33.29 \|\|

*makarīṃ māsikāṃ vidyātkarālī ca dvimāsikā \|*  
*kālarātrī bhavettrīṇi caturo yamadūtikā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The jaw named Makari is grown in a month, Karali in two months, Kalaratri in three months and Yamaduti in four months.

## \|\| 1.33.30 \|\|

*makarīṃ guḍaudanaṃ1 dadyātkaṣāyānnaṃ karālikām \|*  
*kālarātrīṃ kaṭuyutaṃ dūtīṃ vai sānnipātikam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. For Makari, jaggery and rice should be offered; for Karali, anything of the taste of cotton; for Kalaratri anything bitter; and for Yamaduti all the things combined should be given.

## \|\| 1.33.31-32 \|\|

*makarī śastrakaṃ vidyātkarālī kākapādikā \|*  
*karākṛtiḥ kālarātriryāmyā kūrmākṛtiḥ smṛtā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*makarī vātulā jñeyā karālī paittikī smṛtā \|*  
*kaphātmikā kālarātrī yamadūtī sānnipātakī \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Makari resembles a weapon, Karali resembles the claws of a crow, Kalaratri resembles a hand, while Yamaduti resembles a tortoise. In Makari, the wind is in excess; Karali has bilious in excess; cough is in excess in Kalaratri, while in Yamaduti all the three are in excess.

## \|\| 1.33.33 \|\|

*śuklā tu makarī jñeyā karālī raktasannibhā \|*  
*kālarātrī bhavetpītā kṛṣṇā ca yamadūtikā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Makari is of white colour, Karali is of red colour, Kalaratri is of yellow colour, while Yamaduti is of black colour.

## \|\| 1.33.34 \|\|

*vāmā śuklā ca kṛṣṇā ca raktā pītā ca dakṣiṇā \|*  
*samāsena tu vakṣyāmi yathaitā varṇataḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The jaws of the left side are white and black, while those of the right side are red and yellow. Now I am speaking about their colour as well.

## \|\| 1.33.35 \|\|

*śuklā tu brāhmaṇī jñeyā raktā tu kṣatriyā smṛtā \|*  
*vaiśyā tu pītikā jñeyā kṛṣṇā śūdrā tu kathyate \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ viṣalakṣaṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The white jaw is Brahmani by nature, the red one is of Kshatriya nature, the yellow one is of Vaishya nature and the black jaw is of Shudra nature. Now I am speaking as to how the venom is infused in the teeth.

## \|\| 1.33.36 \|\|

*daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ tu viṣaṃ nāsti nityameva bhujaṅgame \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ netramāsādya viṣaṃ sarpasya tiṣṭhati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The venom is not always found in the teeth of the serpents. On the other hand, the venom is stored near the right eye.

## \|\| 1.33.37-40 \|\|

*saṅkuddhasyeha sarpasya viṣaṃ gacchati mastake \|*  
*mastakāddhamanīṃ yāti tato nāḍīṣu gacchati \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nāḍībhyaḥ padyate daṃṣṭrāṃ viṣaṃ tatra pravartate \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*aṣṭabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarpo daśate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ākrānto daśate pūrvaṃ dvitīyaṃ pūrvavairiṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaṃ daśate bhītaścaturthaṃ madadarpitaḥ \|*  
*pañcamaṃ tu kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ ceha viṣolbaṇaḥ \|*  
*saptamaṃ purarakṣārthamaṣṭamaṃ kālacoditaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. When the snake is angry, the venom reaches the head. From there, through the arterial vein, it is spread in all the blood vessels and then it reaches the teeth. The snakes surely bite anyone due to eight reasons. First of all when they are pressed; secondly to an earlier enemy; thirdly getting frightened; fourthly getting intoxicated; fifthly getting upset with hunger; then with the heat of the venom; seventhly for the protection of the young one and lastly due to the move of the destiny.

## \|\| 1.33.41 \|\|

*yastu sarpo daśitvā3 tu udaraṃ parivartayet \|*  
*balabhugnākṛtiṃ daṃṣṭrāmākrāntaṃ taṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In case a serpent takes a turn after a bite and curves the fang, it amounts to biting under pressure.

## \|\| 1.33.42 \|\|

*yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya gabhīraṃ dṛśyate vraṇam \|*  
*vairadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In case a deep wound is caused with the snake bite, according to Kashyapa it should be considered to have been caused due to enmity.

## \|\| 1.33.43 \|\|

*ekaṃ daṃṣṭrāpadaṃ yasya avyaktaṃ na ca kalpitam \|*  
*bhītadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyādyathovāca prajāpatiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When there is the mark of only one tooth at the spot of bite, but does not look like an artificial one, then according to Prajapati the serpent must have bitten out of panic.

## \|\| 1.33.44 \|\|

*yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya rekhā dantasya jāyate \|*  
*madadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. When a line appears after the snake bite, then according to Kashyapa, one should understand that an intoxicated serpent has bitten.

## \|\| 1.33.45-46 \|\|

*dve ca daṃṣṭrāpade yasya dṛśyante ca mahākṣatam \|*  
*kṣudhāviṣṭaṃ vijānīyādyathovāca prajāpatiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dve daṃṣṭre yasya dṛśyete kvacidrudhirasaṅkule \|*  
*viṣolbaṇaṃ vijānīyāddaṃśaṃ taṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. When the biting spot has marks of two teeth with deep wound, then according to Prajapati it should be taken for granted that the serpent has bitten out of hunger. When there is the mark of two teeth filled with blood, then surely the serpent has bitten because of the head of the venom.

## \|\| 1.33.47-48 \|\|

*apatyarakṣaṇārthāya jānīyāttaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yattu kākapadākāraṃ tribhirdantaistu lakṣitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*mahānāga iti proktaṃ kāladaṇḍaṃ vinirdiśet \|*  
*trividhaṃ daṣṭajātaistu lakṣaṇaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. This could also be for the protection of the young ones of the snakes. When there is the mark of three teeth resembling the talons of a crow, then it can be surmised that the snake has bitten due to the move of the destiny.

## \|\| 1.33.49-51 \|\|

*daṣṭānupītaṃ vijñeyaṃ kaśyapasya vaco yathā \|*  
*viṣabhāgāttu sarpasya tribhāgastatra saṃkramet \|\| 49 \|\|*

*udaraṃ darśayedyastu uddhataṃ taṃ vinirdiśet \|*  
*charditaṃ viṣavegena nirviṣaḥ pannago bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

*asādhyaścāpi vijñeyaścaturdaṃṣṭrābhipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*grīvābhaṅgo bhavetkiñcitsandaṣṭo viṣayogataḥ \|*  
*ito daṃśastataḥ śuddho vyantaraḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. It According to the words of Kashyapa, the surmise of the snake bite has been known as symptoms or lakshana. When three parts of the venom by chance reaches the body of a person when a serpent takes a turn after the bite, it should be taken as having been intoxicated. When the spot after the snake bite is found rubbed, then the serpent should be taken as devoid of venom. A person when bitten with all the four teeth, he becomes incurable and no treatment can make the patient survive. A serpent, which after its bite, turns the hood, it should be taken that the bite is infused with venom. Thus after the snake bite, one should make all the efforts to get relieved of the effect of the snake bite.

## Chapter 34. Symptoms of victim bitten by Kala

## \|\| 1.34.1 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kāladaṣṭasya lakṣaṇam \|*  
*śṛṇu gautama tattvena yādṛśo bhavate naraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Kashyapa said — O Gautama, I am now revealing to you the condition of the victim of the snake bite or Kola. You should listen to me attentively.

## \|\| 1.34.2 \|\|

*jihrābhaṅgo'tha hṛcchūlaṃ cakṣurbhyāṃ ca na paśyati \|*  
*daṃśaṃ ca dagdhasaṃkāśaṃ pakvajambūphalopamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After the biting of a person by Kala, the tongue is shattered and there is the severe pain in the heart. The eyesight is lost. The spot which is bitten by the snake resembles the one which is burnt by fire or turns red like the ripe rose-apple fruit.

## \|\| 1.34.3 \|\|

*vaivarṇyaṃ caiva dantānāṃ śyāvo bhavati varṇataḥ \|*  
*sarveṣvaṅgeṣu śaithilyaṃ purīṣasya ca bhedanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The face gets faded out and the teeth are turned like of the mixed red and yellow colour. All the limbs of the body become inactive and the anus is burnt out.

## \|\| 1.34.4 \|\|

*bhagnaskandhakaṭigrīva ūrdhvadṛṣṭiradhomukhaḥ \|*  
*dahyate vepate caiva svapate ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The shoulders, neck and waist get deformed, the eyes become drowsy, the face is fallen, the entire body has the burning sensation and one faints repeatedly.

## \|\| 1.34.5 \|\|

*śastreṇa cchidyamānasya rudhiraṃ na pravartate \|*  
*daṇḍena tāḍyamānasya daṇḍarājī na jāyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. No blood flows from the body even after cutting it with a weapon. No mark is left over the body even when the victim be beaten by a stick.

## \|\| 1.34.6 \|\|

*daṃśe kākapadaṃ sunīlamasakṛjjambūphalābhaṃ ghanamucchūnaṃ rudhirārdrasekabahulaṃ kṛcchrānnirodho bhavet \|*  
*hikkāśvāsagalagrahaśca sumahānpāṇḍustvacā dṛśyate śuṣkāṅgaḥ pravadanti śāstranipuṇāstatkāladaṣṭaṃ viduḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the part of the body bitten by the snake when a sign of crow’s talon is developed» which turns dark blue resembling the rose — apple tree, then develops swelling and the wound starts bleeding, which could be stopped with great difficulty. The victim has to face hiccup again and again. There is an obstruction in breathing, the complexion of the body turns pale and the limbs are dried up. When such symptoms appear, the experts in the field describe the victim as having been bitten by Kala.

## \|\| 1.34.7 \|\|

*daṃśe yasyātha śothaḥ pracalitavalitaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vā sunīlaṃ prasvedo gātra bhedaḥ sravati ca rudhiraṃ sānunāsaṃ ca jalpet \|*  
*dantoṣṭhābhyāṃ viyogo bhramati ca hṛdayaṃ sannirodhaśca tīvro divyānāmeṣa daṃśaḥ sthalavipulamayo viddhi taṃ kāladaṣṭam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The spot bitten by a snake develops? swelling or it gets deformed or round, black spot, perspiration, tearing out of some limb, continuous flow of blood, sound through the nose, separation of teeth and lips, palpitation in heart and then sudden stoppage of the same, and when the sign of snake bite further spreads, then it should be taken to have been bitten by Kala.

## \|\| 1.34.8 \|\|

*dantairdantānspṛśati bahuśo dṛṣṭirāyāsakhinnā sthūlo daṃśaḥ sravati rudhiraṃ kekaraṃ cakṣurekam \|*  
*pratyādiṣṭaḥ śvasiti satataṃ sānunāsaṃ ca bhāṣetpāpaṃ brūte sakalagaditaṃ kāladaṇḍaṃ tamāhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the victim grinds the teeth repeatedly, the eyes get fatigued, the spot of snake bite when becomes stiff and blood oozes out of it, the victim’s eyes flicker, quick breathing, while making sound through the nose — these are the symptoms for the person bitten by Kala.

## \|\| 1.34.9 \|\|

*vepate vedanā tīvrā raktanetraśca jāyate \|*  
*grīvābhaṅgaścalā nābhiḥ kāladaṣṭaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When the victim feels extremely painful in the body, the throat becomes stuffy, flickering of the navel are the symptoms of the one who is bitten by snake.

## \|\| 1.34.10 \|\|

*darpaṇe salile vāpi ātmacchāyāṃ na paśyati \|*  
*mandaraśmiṃ tathā tīvraṃ tejohīnaṃ divākaram1 \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then a person is unable to see his reflection in water or in a mirror, while the sun and the moon appear to him without shine.

## \|\| 1.34.11 \|\|

*vepate vedanātrasto raktanetraśca jāyate \|*  
*sa yāti nidhanaṃ jantuḥ kāladaṇḍaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The body keeps on shaking with pain and the eyes become red, then he meets with his death. Such a person should be treated to have been bitten by Kala.

## \|\| 1.34.12 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca navamyāṃ ca kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm \|*  
*nāgapañcamīdaṣṭānāṃ jīvitasya ca saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When a person is bitten by a snake during the eighth, ninth besides fourteenth black moon day or Naga-Panchami day, his remaining alive becomes doubtful.

## \|\| 1.34.13 \|\|

*ārdrāśleṣāmaghābharaṇīkṛttikāsu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*viśākhāṃ triṣu pūrvāsu mūlasvātīśatātmake \|*  
*sarpadaṣṭā na jīvanti viṣaṃ pītaṃ ca yaistathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person who is bitten by snake during Ardra, Shlesha, Magha, Bharani, Krittika, Vishakha, all the three Purvas, Mula and Svati besides Shatabhisha constellations or the one who consumes poison during these constellations, he cannot remain alive.

## \|\| 1.34.14 \|\|

*śūnyāgāre śmaśāne ca śuṣkavṛkṣe tathaiva ca \|*  
*na jīvanti narā daṣṭā nakṣatre tithisaṃyute \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A person also does not remain alive in the deserted house, the cremation ground and near dry tree on the lower moon days.

## \|\| 1.34.15-17 \|\|

*aṣṭottaraṃ marma śataṃ prāṇināṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye tu marmāṇi daśa dve cāpi kīrtite \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śaṅkhe netre bhruvormadhye bastibhyāṃ vṛṣaṇottare \|*  
*kakṣe skandhe hadi madhye tāluke cibuke gude \|\| 16 \|\|*

*eṣu dvādaśamarmeṣu2 daṃśaiḥ śastreṇa vā hataḥ \|*  
*na jīvati naro loke kāladaṇḍaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The scriptures have mentioned a hundred and eight sensitive spots in the body. But the skull bone, the centre of the eyebrows, both sides below the navel, the testicles, armpits, shoulders, heart, waist, palate, chin and anus are the spots, which are when bitten by the snake, then the person cannot remain alive and should be treated to have been bitten by the snake.

## \|\| 1.34.18 \|\|

*akacaṭatapayaśāṃ vadanti proktā jīvanti na tatra hi \|*  
*gataṃ brūyādyadi skhalati śirastasya samprāptakālaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*
