18\. When a person bitten by a snake is asked to repeat the letter a, ka, ca, ta, ta, pa, besides ya and sha, then the victim remains alive. In case he utters the last letter or something irrelevant, then it should be taken for granted that the god of death has arrived for him.

## \|\| 1.34.19 \|\|

*bhavati ca yadi dūto hyuttamasyādhamo vā yadi bhavati ca dūta uttamo vādhamasya \|*  
*ādau daṣṭasya nāma yadi vadati kvacidvakti tasyātha paścāttaṃ varṇabhedo yadi bhavati samaḥ prāpta kālasya dūtaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When there is the first messenger of the high caste or the best messenger of a low caste person speaks out the name of the victim or talks to someone else, then no difference of castes remains. Then he should be treated as the messenger of death and not of a physician.

## \|\| 1.34.20 \|\|

*dūto vā daṇḍahasto bhavati ca yugalaṃ pāśahastastathā vā raktavastraṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ mukhaśirasi gatamekavastraśca dūtaḥ \|*  
*tailābhyaktaśca tadvadyadi tvaritagatirmuktakeśaśca yāti yaḥ kuryādghoraśabdaṃ karacaraṇayugaiḥ prāptakālasya dūtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Similarly, where there are two persons carrying sticks in their hands, with their heads covered with the red or black clothes, clad in similar clothes, with oil applied over their bodies, talking rapidly, with disheveled heads, creating horrible sounds from their hands and feet, they should be treated as the messengers of death.

## \|\| 1.34.21-23 \|\|

*nāgodayaṃ pravakṣyāmi īśānena tu bhāṣitam \|*  
*brahmaṇā tu purā sṛṣṭā grahā nāgāstvanekaśaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*anantaṃ bhāskaraṃ vidyātsomaṃ vidyāttu vāsukim \|*  
*takṣakaṃ bhūmiputraṃ tu karkoṭaṃ ca budhaṃ viduḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*padmaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vidyānmahāpadmaṃ ca bhārgavam \|*  
*kulikaḥ śaṃkhapālaśca dvāvetau tu śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. I am now narrating about the rise of the serpent, as had been revealed by lord Shiva in earlier times. Brahma initially created the nagas and the planets. The serpent Ananta represents the sun, Vasuki represents the moon, Takshaka represents Mars, Karkotaka represents Mercury, Padma represents Brihaspati, Mahapadma represents Venus, Kulika and Shankhapala represent Saturn.

## \|\| 1.34.24-29 \|\|

*pūrvapādaḥ śaṃkhapālo dvitīyaḥ kulikastathā \|*  
*nityaṃ bhāge yathoddiṣṭe dinarātrī tathaiva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śukrasomau ca madhyāhne udaye tu kṣamāsutaḥ \|*  
*śaniḥ prāgaṣṭame bhāge divārātre tvihocyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*grahāśca bhuñjate caiva śeṣaṃ bhāgasya lakṣaṇam \|*  
*ravivāre sadā jñeyau pādau daśa caturdaśa \|\| 26 \|\|*

*aṣṭa dvādaśa vai candre daśa ṣaṣṭhe kuje tathā \|*  
*budhasya navame pāde rāhau ca divasasya ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*gurordvitīyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaśca ṣoḍaśasya tu varjayet \|*  
*bhāskarasya dine prokte caturthe daśameṣṭame \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śanaiścaradine pādaṃ tyajeccaiva sudāruṇam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ dvādaśaṃ caiva ṣoḍaśasya tu varjayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

24-29. Like the day and night, Shankhapala is the master of first half and Kulika is the master of second half. The morning is enjoyed by Mars, noon time by Venus and the Moon. The first eight parts of the day and night are enjoyed by Saturn. Out of the rest, the tenth and fourteenth parts of Sunday, the eighth and twelfth parts of Monday, the sixth and tenth (parts of Tuesday, the ninth parts of Wednesday, the second and sixth parts of Thursday, eight and tenth parts of Saturday, are quite horrible and are therefore to be discarded. In other words, it means that in case there is a snake bite during these times, the victim cannot remain alive.

## \|\| 1.34.30 \|\|

*muhūrtaghaṭikādūrddhvaṃ ghaṭikā caturthaṃ bhāgaṃ viṃśatiśca \|*  
*kuhūsutaṃ budbudaṃ nimeṣametatkālasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The fourth and twentieth parts of the ghati are also to be discarded, which is known by the names of Bumdabuda — the son of Kuhu. Thus I have narrated the condemned period of Kala as well.

## Chapter 35. Symptoms of Yamaduti

## \|\| 1.35.1 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*saviṣā daṃṣṭrayormadhye yamadūtī tu vai bhavet \|*  
*na cikitsā budhaiḥ kāryā taṃ gatāsuṃ virnidaśet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Kashyapa said — Of the various jaws of the serpents, there is a jaw named Yamaduti. When the snake bites with that jaw, no treatment would be effective in that case and the victim who is bitten by the serpent, he is sure to meet with his death.

## \|\| 1.35.2-3 \|\|

*bṛhatī vṛścikā kālī indra vāruṇimūlakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nāgodayo yamuddiśya hato viddho vidāritaḥ \|*  
*kāladaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Similarly, both during the day and the night, in a prahara or a half of it, the serpents have to suffer for the second or the sixteenth part of the same. Therefore, the victim who has been bitten or tom out by the serpent, then according to the words of Kashyapa, one should take it to have been bitten by Kala.

## \|\| 1.35.4-6 \|\|

*yanmātraṃ patate bindurvālāgraṃ saliloddhṛtam \|*  
*tanmātraṃ sravate daṃṣṭrā viṣaṃ sarpasya dāruṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nāḍīśate tu sampūrṇe dehe saṅkramate viṣam \|*  
*yāvatsaṅkrāmayedbāhuṃ kuñcitaṃ vā prasārayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*anena kṣaṇamātreṇa viṣaṃ gacchati mastake \|*  
*vepate viṣavege tu śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The extent of the drop of water which falls over the tip of a hair, the venom of the same quantity is emitted by the serpent from its fangs and the time one takes in spreading or folding an area, in the same time the venom reaches in all the veins of the body of the victim. The venom also reaches in the head at the same time. Because of the severity of the venom, the victim is shaken a hundred or a thousand times.

## \|\| 1.35.7-8 \|\|

*vardhate raktamāsādya tato vātaiḥ śikhī yathā \|*  
*tailabindurjalaṃ prāpya yathā vegena vardhate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śikhaṇḍī āśrayaṃ prāpya mārutena samīritaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sthānaśataṃ prāpya tvacāsthānaṃ viceṣṭitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Thereafter, the venom mixes with the blood and spread with the wind like the fire. As the drop of oil rapidly spreads in the water, similarly, the venom reaching at the appropriate spot in the body, gets expanded with the air, and then spreads quickly like the spread of the fire.

## \|\| 1.35.9-10 \|\|

*tvacāsu dviguṇaṃ vidyācchoṇiteṣu caturguṇam \|*  
*pitte tu triguṇaṃ yāti śleṣme vai ṣoḍaśaṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vāyau triṃśadguṇaṃ caiva majjāṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*prāṇe caikārṇavībhūte sarvagātrāṇi sandhayet1 \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Similarly, reaching at several spots, it spreads deeply in the skin, four times in the blood, three times in bile, sixteen times in cough, thirty times in wind and sixty times in marrow. Then it mixes up with breath and spreads in the entire body.

## \|\| 1.35.11 \|\|

*śrotre nirudhyamāne ca yāti daṣṭastvasādhyatām \|*  
*tato'sau mriyate janturniḥśvāsocchvāsavarjitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When a patient is unable to listen from the ears, then it becomes an incurable disease. Therefore, with the stoppage of the breathing, a person meets with his end.

## \|\| 1.35.12 \|\|

*niṣkrānte tu tato jīve bhūte pañcatvamāgate \|*  
*tāni bhūtāni gacchanti yasya yasya yathātatham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After the exhausting of the life breath, all the five bhutas like earth, fire, water, wind and sky off merge themselves in the respective bhutas from where they had emerged.

## \|\| 1.35.13 \|\|

*pṛthivyāpastathā tejo vāyurākāśameva ca \|*  
*ityeṣāmeva saṅghātaḥ śarīramabhidhīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Because the body comprises of the earth, fire, water, wind and sky.

## \|\| 1.35.14-16 \|\|

*pṛthivī pṛthivīṃ yāti toyaṃ toyeṣu līyate \|*  
*tejo gacchati cādityaṃ māruto mārutaṃ vrajet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ākāśaṃ caivamākāśe saha tenaiva gacchati \|*  
*svasthānaṃ te prapadyante parasparaniyojitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*na jīvedāgataḥ kaścidiha janmani suvrata \|*  
*viṣārtaṃ na upekṣeta tvaritaṃ tu cikitsayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Therefore, after the death, the part of earth is absorbed in the earth, the water content merges in water, the lustre is absorbed in the sun, the wind in wind, while the part of the sky merges in the sky. With leaving of the life breath from the body, they all reach their respective places. O Suvrata, by taking the birth on the earth, none can remain alive always. Therefore, the victim of the snake bite should not be neglected at all, but should be treated at once.

## \|\| 1.35.17 \|\|

*ekamasti viṣaṃ loke dvitīyaṃ copapadyate \|*  
*yathā nānāvidhaṃ caiva sthāvaraṃ tu tathaiva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. As the poison is one and it turns into several types, it becomes visible in the world in several forms. Its results are also seen differently. Therefore, the solid poisons should also be treated similarly.

## \|\| 1.35.18-20 \|\|

*prathame viṣavege tu romaharṣo'bhijāyate \|*  
*dvitīye viṣavege tu svedo gātreṣu jāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tṛtīye viṣavege tu kampo gātreṣu jāyate \|*  
*caturthe viṣavege tu śrotrāntaranirodhakṛt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pañcame viṣavege tu hikkā gātreṣu jāyate \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhe ca viṣavege tu prāṇebhyo'pi pramucyate \|*  
*saptadhātuvahā hyete vainateyena bhāṣitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. When the poison enters the body, at once the person feels sensation, then the body perspires, shivers, at the fourth stage internal membrane is closed, at the fifth stage starts the hiccup, and at the sixth stage the person departs. According to the words of Garuda, the poison reaches in all the seven limbs.

## \|\| 1.35.21 \|\|

*tvacaḥ sthāne viṣe prāpte tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu \|*  
*aṅgāni timirāyante tapante ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When the poison reaches the skin, the condition of the victim is being defined by me, which you please listen. On reaching of the poison in the body, darkness spreads over all the limbs of the body, which starts twisting with burning sensation.

## \|\| 1.35.22-23 \|\|

*etāni yasya cihnāni tasya tvaci gataṃ viṣam \|*  
*tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham \|\| 22 \|\|*

*arkamūlamapāmārgaṃ priyaṅguṃ tagaraṃ2 tathā \|*  
*etadāloḍya dātavyaṃ tataḥ sampadyate sukham \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. With these symptoms, it should be believed that the poison has reached the skin level. I am now speaking about the medicine to be used at that time. It’s use makes the victim comfortable. The root of swallow-wort (calotrapis gigantean), dhak tree (butea (rondosa), panic seed (panicum italicum) or black mustard seeds and tagara tree (tabarnasmontana coronaria), all these should be powdered together and given to the victim, which makes him comfortable.

## \|\| 1.35.24 \|\|

*tatastasmitkṛte vipra na nivarteta cedviṣam \|*  
*tvacaḥ sthānaṃ tato bhittvā raktasthānaṃ pradhāvati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In case the venom is not removed with the application of the above medicine, then it should be believed that the poison has reached beyond the skin.

## \|\| 1.35.25 \|\|

*viṣe ca raktaṃ saṃprāpte tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu \|*  
*dahyate muhyate1 caiva śītalaṃ bahu manyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The condition which a patient has to face when the poison mixes up with the blood is being spoken by me, which you please listen. There is the burning sensation in the body and the patient faints, feeling cold.

## \|\| 1.35.26 \|\|

*etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya raktagataṃ viṣam \|*  
*tatrāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When such a condition develops in a patient, it should be presumed that the poison has reached the blood. I am now speaking for the remedy for the same, by which the patient feels relieved.

## \|\| 1.35.27 \|\|

*uśīraṃ candanaṃ kuṣṭhamutpalaṃ tagaraṃ tathā \|*  
*mahākālasya mūlāni sinduvāranagasya ca \|*  
*hiṅgulaṃ maricaṃ caiva pūrvavege tu dāpeyat \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Ushira or fragrant root of the grass anaropagon nuricatum, sandalwood, kushtha (caslus speciousus), blue lotus, tagara tree (tabarnasmontana coroneria), mahakala — a type of creeper, root of sinduvara — a medicinal plant, sulphate of mercury and black pepper should be powdered and given to the patient at the first stage of the entering of poison in the body of the patient.

## \|\| 1.35.28 \|\|

*saptagandhaghṛtaṃ caiva dvitīye parikīrtitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. During the second stage, gorse, Nettlewort, colocynth or a wield bitten gourd, and the seven scents mixed with ghi have been prescribed for the treatment of the patient.

## \|\| 1.35.29 \|\|

*sinduvāraṃ tathā hiṅguṃ tṛtīye kārayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*tasya pānaṃ ca kurvīta añjanaṃ lepanaṃ tathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In the third attack, Nettlewort, Asafetida (hinga) should be used as a paste for applying over the body as well in the eyes.

## \|\| 1.35.30 \|\|

*etenaivopacāreṇa tataḥ sampadyate sukham \|*  
*raktasthānaṃ tato gatvā pittasthānaṃ pradhāvati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With the extending of the aforesaid type of treatment, the patient shall feel at ease. After the blood, the venom reaches the bile.

## \|\| 1.35.31-32 \|\|

*pittasthānagate vipra viṣarūpāṇi me śṛṇu \|*  
*uttiṣṭhate nipatate dahyate muhyate tathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*gātrataḥ pītakaḥ syādvai diśaḥ paśyati pītikā \|*  
*prabalā ca bhavanmūrcchā na cātmānaṃ vijānate \|*  
*viṣakriyāṃ tasya kuryādyathā sampadyate sukham \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. O Brahmana! When the venom reaches the bile, the form of the body it takes is being spoken by me, which you please, listen. The patient tries to get up again and again, but falls down. He feels burning sensation in the body, besides fainting. The body turns pale. The patient finds everything yellow and he faints for long and he forgets himself. Therefore, he should be treated in such a way by which he gets quick relief.

## \|\| 1.35.33 \|\|

*pittasthānamatikramya śleṣmasthānaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After the bilious spot, the venom reaches the phlegm mucus.

## \|\| 1.35.34-35 \|\|

*pippalyo madhukaṃ caiva madhu khaṇḍaṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā \|*  
*madhusāramalābūṃ ca jātiṃ śaṅkaravālukām \|*  
*indravāruṇikāmūlaṃ gavāṃ mūtreṇa peṣayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nasyaṃ tasya prayuñjīta pānamālepanāñjanam \|*  
*etenaivopacāreṇa tataḥ sampadyate sukham \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Collecting the herbs like holy fig tree, bassia lafitatia, honey, sugar, ghi, wine of bassia latifoha, gourd, jasmine, sankara-valuka and root of bitter gourd should be collected and a paste of all of them should be made using the cow’s urine. The patient should be made to smell it with the nose or should consume the same or should use it as eye drops to be poured in the eyes. By extending this treatment, the patient would surely have relief.

## \|\| 1.35.36 \|\|

*śleṣmasthānaṃ tataḥ prāpte tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu \|*  
*gātrāṇi1 tasya rudhyante niḥśvāsaśca na jāyate \|*  
*lālā ca sravate tasya kaṇṭho ghurughurāyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With the reaching of the venom in the cough, the painful situation which a person has to face is going to be related by me. You please listen. The patient becomes deaf, the breathing is stopped, saliva drops from the mouth and the throat becomes sour.

## \|\| 1.35.37-39 \|\|

*etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya śleṣmagataṃ viṣam \|*  
*tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham \|\| 37 \|\|*

*trikuṭakī śleṣmātako lodhrañca madhusārakam \|*  
*etāni samabhāgāni gavāṃ mūtreṇa peṣayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasya pānaṃ ca kurvīta añjanaṃ lepanaṃ tathā \|*  
*etenaivopacāreṇa tataḥ sampadyate sukham \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Under such a situation, one should believe that the venom had reached the cough. Now I am speaking about its cure, which makes the patient quite comfortable. Ginger, pepper, bug pepper, cardymyxa, symploce recemoze, wine of mahuva tree, should all the taken together and powdered in the urine of a cow. The paste so prepared should be used as an eye ointment and plaster. With the use of this medicine, the patient world relief.

## \|\| 1.35.40-41 \|\|

*śleṣmasthānamatikramya vāyusthānaṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*tatra rūpāṇi vakṣyāmi vāyusthānagate viṣe \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ādhmāyate ca jaṭharaṃ bāndhavāṃśca na paśyati \|*  
*īdṛśaṃ kurute rūpaṃ vṛṣṭibhaṅgaśca jāyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. After reaching the cough, the venom reaches in the air and with its touching the wind, the condition of the victim is being defined by me. The belly fattens and he is unable to see his kiths and kins. His eye sight is lost under these conditions when the air in his body is infested with the venom.

## \|\| 1.35.42-44 \|\|

*etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya vāyugataṃ viṣam \|*  
*tasyāgadaṃ prakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham \|\| 42 \|\|*

*śoṇāmūlaṃ priyālaṃ ca raktaṃ ca gajapippalīm \|*  
*bhārṅgīṃ vacāṃ pippalīṃ ca devadāruṃ madhūkakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*madhūkasāraṃ sahasinduvāraṃ hiṅguṃ ca piṣṭā guṭikāṃ ca kuryāt \|*  
*dadyācca tasyāñjanalepanādi eṣo'gadaḥ sarpaviṣāṇi hanyāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. I am now speaking about the medicine which could cure him. Shonamula’s chironji sapida and its edible nuts, gajapippali — a plant whose twigs are used as medicine, red gajapipala, the medicinal shrub edipta prastrata, acorns calamus, fig tree, pine or ceder tree, mahuva, madhuka juice, sinduvara — a medicinal plant and asafetida, should be collected and powdered together and turned into pills. With the use of the said powder in the form of the pills, the paste or the ointment, the snake venom is removed.

## \|\| 1.35.45 \|\|

*añjanaṃ caiva nasyaṃ ca kṣipraṃ dadyādviṣānvite \|*  
*vāyusthānaṃ tato muktvā majjāsthānaṃ pradhāvati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The eye ointment should be applied in the eyes as well as smelt by the nose at once. Thereafter, the venom reaches the marrow.

## \|\| 1.35.46 \|\|

*viṣe majjāgate vipra tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu \|*  
*dṛṣṭiśca hīyate tasya bhṛśamaṅgāni muñcati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Brahmana. I am going to speak out the condition of the victim of the snake bite on reaching of the venom in the marrow. His vision is blurred, and the patient feels as if all the limbs of the body have been separated from him.

## \|\| 1.35.47 \|\|

*etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya majjāgataṃ viṣam \|*  
*tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Under the condition when the venom reaches the brain, I am now speaking about the medicine which can cure him, when taken by the patient.

## \|\| 1.35.48-49 \|\|

*ghṛtamadhuśarkarānvitamuśīraṃ caṃdanaṃ tathā \|*  
*etadāloḍya dātavyaṃ pānaṃ nasyaṃ ca suvrata \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tataḥ praṇaśyate duḥkhaṃ tataḥ saṃpadyate sukham \|*  
*atha tasminkṛte yoge viṣaṃ tasya nivartate \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Mixing up ghi, honey and sugar, the resultant should be powered with the root of mushira and the sandalpaste. The patient should be then asked to consume it or smell it through the nose. O Suvrata, by so doing, the patient is relieved of the pain and he feels comfortable.

## \|\| 1.35.50 \|\|

*majjāsthānaṃ tato gatvā marmasthānaṃ pradhāvati \|*  
*viṣe tu marma saṃprāpte śṛṇu rūpaṃ yathā bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. From marrow, the venom reach the sensitive spots, and the condition of the patient at that point of time is being narrated by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.35.51 \|\|

*niśceṣṭaḥ patate bhūmau karṇābhyāṃ badhiro bhavet \|*  
*vāriṇā sicyamānasya romaharṣo na jāyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The patient faints and falls down on the ground. He becomes deaf of ears and he does not feel thrilled even when bathed with water.

## \|\| 1.35.52 \|\|

*daṃḍena hanyamānasya daṃḍarājī na jāyate \|*  
*śastreṇa cchidyamānasya rudhiraṃ na pravartate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. When beaten by a rod, no trace is left on the body for such a strike and in case his body is cut by a weapon, the blood does not ooze.

## \|\| 1.35.53 \|\|

*keśeṣu lucyamāneṣu naiva keśānpravedate \|*  
*yasya karṇau ca pārśve ca hastapādaṃ ca saṃdhayaḥ \|*  
*śithilāni bhavaṃtīha sa gatāsuriti śrutiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In case his hair are pulled, he does not feel any sensation. Similarly, when the ear, both the armpits, hands and the feet are faded out at the roots, he should be taken as dead.

## \|\| 1.35.54-55 \|\|

*etāni yasya rūpāṇi viparītāni gautama \|*  
*mṛtaṃ tu na vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vaidyāstasya na paśyaṃti ye bhavaṃti kuśikṣitāḥ \|*  
*vicakṣaṇāstu paśyaṃti maṃtrauṣadhisamanvitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. To the contrary, when the condition of the patient is reverse of the same, he should not be taken as dead according to the words of Kashyapa and he should be treated well by a competent physician, because such symptoms would not be truly known to an unqualified physicians. Only the competent physicians are aware of the correct treatment and the mantras applicable in such cases.

## \|\| 1.35.56-59 \|\|

*tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi svayaṃ rudreṇa bhāṣitam \|*  
*mayūrapittaṃ mārjārapittaṃ gandhanāḍīmūlameva ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kuṃkumaṃ tagaraṃ kuṣṭhaṃ kāsamardatvacaṃ tathā \|*  
*utpalasya ca kiṃjalkaṃ padmasya kumudasya ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

*etāni samabhāgāni gomūtreṇa tu peṣayet \|*  
*eṣo'gado yasya haste daṣṭo na mriyate sa vai \|*  
*kālāhināpi daṣṭena kṣipraṃ bhavati nirviṣaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kṣiprameva pradā tavyaṃ mṛtasaṃjīvanauṣadham \|*  
*aṃjanaṃ caiva nasyaṃ ca kṣipraṃ dadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

56-59. The treatment of such a patient has been narrated by lord Rudra, and is being revealed by me. The gall-bladder of a cat and a peacock, the sandalpaste, gandha durva (a kind of grass), vermilion, tabernasmontana coronaria, castus speciouses, skin of Kasamarda tree, blue lotus, lotus and lily or red lotus and the flower dust, should be collected in equal weight and their paste may be made with the urine of the cow. It should be used as an eye ointment and also should be smelt through the nose. In case this medicine is available, he cannot die with the snake bite and has rightly been declared as the one which can bring back the dead to life. Because even when a person is bitten by the Kala serpent, he regains his life with the use of this medicine.

## Chapter 36. Description of Naga-Panchami

## \|\| 1.36.1-2 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*kīdṛśaṃ sarpadaṣṭasya sarpiṇyāḥ kīdṛśaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kumāradaṣṭaḥ kīdṛksyātsūtikādaṃśitasya ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rūpaṃ napuṃsakeneha vyaṃtareṇa ca kīdṛśam \|*  
*etadākhyāhi me sarvamebhirdaṣṭasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Gautama said — The serpents, the female serpents, their young ones, pregnant and eunuch serpents when bite a person, what type of conditions a person has to face? You kindly speak out the relative symptoms in detail.

## \|\| 1.36.3 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi nāgānāṃ rūpalakṣaṇam \|*  
*sarpadaṣṭasya ca tathā samāsāddvijapuṃgava \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Kashyapa said — Now I shall speak about the biting of a person by the huge Nagas as well as the serpents, their forms and the symptoms in brief.

## \|\| 1.36.4-5 \|\|

*atha sarpeṇa daṣṭasya ūrdhva dṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*sarpīdaṣṭasya ca tathā adhodṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kanyādaṣṭasya vāmā syādṛṣṭirdvijavarottama \|*  
*kumāreṇāpi daṣṭasya dakṣiṇā eva jāyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. With the snake bite, the eyelids of the victim are turned upwards. Similarly, when a person is bitten by a female snake, the eyelids of a person are downcast. In case a person is bitten by a maid serpent, they turn to the left and when bitten by bachelor serpent, the eyelids turn to the right.

## \|\| 1.36.6 \|\|

*garbhiṇyā vātha daṣṭasya tathā svedaśca jāyate \|*  
*romāṃcaḥ sūtikāyāstu vepathuścāpi jāyate \|*  
*napuṃsakena daṣṭasya aṃgamardaḥ prajāyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When a person is bitten by a pregnant serpent, the victim perspires. When a person is bitten by a female serpent who has just delivered one, he feels thrilled and shivering. When bitten by an eunuch serpent, the limbs of the victim have the sensation as if breading.

## \|\| 1.36.7 \|\|

*pannagyaḥ prabhavo rātrau divā sarpo viṣādhikaḥ \|*  
*napuṃsakastu saṃdhyāyāṃ kaśyapena tu bhāṣitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Kashyapa says that the effect of the snake bite is much more when a person is bitten by a female serpent at night, by a male serpent during the day and by the eunuch snake during the evening.

## \|\| 1.36.8 \|\|

*aṃdhakāre tu daṣṭo ya udake gahane vane \|*  
*supto vā cetpramatto vā yadi sarpaṃ na paśyati \|*  
*daṣṭarūpāṇyajānanvai kathaṃ vaidyacikitsitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Therefore, during the darkness, in the water or in the thick forest, in case a person is bitten by the serpent and unless the victim had seen the serpent, how could physician be able to provide treatment to the victim of the snake bite?

## \|\| 1.36.9 \|\|

*caturvidhā iha proktāḥ pannagāstu mahātmanā \|*  
*darvīkarā maṃḍalino rājilā vyaṃtarāstathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The serpents are said to be of four types viz., with expanded hoods, mandali, rajila and vyantara (or flying snake).

## \|\| 1.36.10 \|\|

*darvīkarā vātaviṣā maṃḍalā paittikāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*śleṣmalā rājilrā jñeyā vyaṃtarāḥ sānnipātikāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The venom of the serpent Darvikara has the force of wind, the venom of the serpent Mandali has the force of bile, while that of serpent Rajila has the force of cough. The venom of Vyamtara serpent has the force of delirium.

## \|\| 1.36.11-12 \|\|

*raktaṃ parīkṣayedeṣāṃ sarpāṇāṃ tu pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ darvīkarāṇāṃ tu jāyate nālpamulbaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*raktaṃ ghanaṃ ca bahuśaḥ śoṇitaṃ maṃḍalī kṛtam \|*  
*picchilaṃ rājile svalpaṃ tadvadvyaṃtarake tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The blood of these snakes should be tested separately, because the blood of serpent Darvikara is black, and is excessively hot. The blood of Mandali serpent is red and thick, which resembles the mud and appears in small quantity. The blood of the serpent Rajila and Vyamtara is also red.

## \|\| 1.36.13 \|\|

*sarpā jñeyāstu catvāraḥ paṃcamo nopalabhyate \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra ścaiva caturthakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras are also of four varnas. The fifth one is not found anywhere.

## \|\| 1.36.14 \|\|

*brāhmaṇe madhuraṃ dadyāttiktaṃ dadyāttathottare \|*  
*vaiśye karṣaphalaṃ dadyācchūdre tristhūṇameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Brahmana should be given the sweet fruit, the sharp one to a Kshatriya and Vaishya should be given Karshaphala. Shudra should be given a bitter fruit.

## \|\| 1.36.15 \|\|

*brāhmaṇena tu daṣṭasya dāho gātreṣu jāyate \|*  
*mūrcchā ca prabalā syādvai nātmānamabhijānate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the Brahmana is bitten by a he feels burning sensation in the body and he faints so deeply that he loses all his senses completely.

## \|\| 1.36.16 \|\|

*śyāmavarṇaṃ mukhaṃ ca syānmajjāstaṃbhaśca jāyate \|*  
*tasya kuryātpratīkāraṃ yena saṃpadyate sukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. His face is turned black and the marrow starts flickering. Therefore, he should be cured by means of mantras, which could bring relief to him.

## \|\| 1.36.17-18 \|\|

*aśvagaṃdhāpyapāmārgaḥ siṃduvāraṃ surāmayam \|*  
*etatsarpiḥ samāyuktaṃ pāne nasye ca dāpayet \|*  
*etenaivopacāreṇa sukhī bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kṣatriyeṇa tu daṣṭasya kaṃpo gātreṣu jāyate \|*  
*mūrchā mohastathā syādvai nātmānamabhivetti saḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The plant ashvagandha, apamarga mixed with wine and ghira and sinduvara (a medicinal plant) should be given to the patient for drinking or inhaling through the nose. This would provide relief to the patient. When a Kshatriya is bitten by a snake, his body is shaken and he faints and loses all the senses.

## \|\| 1.36.19 \|\|

*jāyate vedanā tasya ūrdhvaṃ caiva nirīkṣate \|*  
*tasya kuryātpratīkāraṃ yena saṃpadyate sukham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He feels painful and his eyes are turned upwards. Therefore, immediate treatment should be provided to him for extending relief.

## \|\| 1.36.20 \|\|

*arkamūlamapāmārgaṃ priyaṃgumindravāruṇīm \|*  
*etatsarpiḥ samāyuktaṃ pānaṃ nasyaṃ ca dāpayet \|*  
*etenaivopacāreṇa sukhī bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The root of swallow-wort or Calotropis gigantean, Chichira, Priyangu, black mustard seeds and plant Indravaruni should be mixed in ghi and given to the patient, who should take the same. With this treatment, the victim is cured of the ailment.

## \|\| 1.36.21-22 \|\|

*vaiśyenāpi hi daṣṭasya śṛṇu rūpāṇi yāni tu \|*  
*śleṣmaprakopo lālā ca na codvahati cetanām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mūrchā ca prabalā yasya ātmānaṃ nābhinaṃdati \|*  
*tasya kuryātpratīkāraṃ yena saṃpadyate sukham \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. When the serpent bites a Vaishya, then his condition after the snake bite is being stated by me. His cough is contaminated. Saliva starts dropping from his mouth and he faints at the same time. He becomes totally senseless, and then the process to provide quick relief to the victim should be started.

## \|\| 1.36.23 \|\|

*aśvagaṃdhā sagomūtrā gṛha dhūmaṃ saguggulam \|*  
*śirīṣārkapalāśena śvetā ca girikarṇikā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Ashvagandha, guggulu, acacia tree, swallow-wort (Madara), Palasha and Aparajita should be powdered and mixed in the urine of the cow, which should be given to the victim to drink it.

## \|\| 1.36.24 \|\|

*gomūtreṇa samāyuktaṃ pānaṃ nasyaṃ ca dāpayet \|*  
*eṣa vaiśyena daṣṭānāmagadaḥ parikīrttitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This process has also been prescribed for a Vaishya when he is bitten by a snake.

## \|\| 1.36.25-26 \|\|

*śūdreṇāpi hi daṣṭasya śṛṇu tattvena gautama \|*  
*kuthyate vepate caiva jvaraḥ śītaṃ ca jāyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aṃgāni culuculāyaṃte śūdradaṣṭasya lakṣaṇam \|*  
*tatrāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena saṃpadyate sukham \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. O Gautama, now you listen to the condition of a Shudra after the snake bite. You listen to the condition of a Shudra after he is bitten by a snake. The victim gets enraged, trembles and shivers with cold. Sensation develops in his limbs. These are the symptoms of a Shudra when bitten by a snake. I am now speaking about the treatment for the same, which provides immediate relief, when taken by the patient.

## \|\| 1.36.27-28 \|\|

*padmaṃ ca lodhrakaṃ caiva kṣaudraṃ padmasya kesaram \|*  
*madhūkasāraṃ madhu ca śvetāṃ ca girikarṇikām \|\| 27 \|\|*

*etāni samabhāgāni peṣayecchītavāriṇā \|*  
*pānalepāṃjanairnasyaiḥ sukhī bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The lotus, Lodha kamala, honey, the dust of small lotus, honey and the white Apamarga should be collected in equal quantity and powdered in the wine of Mahuva tree with cold water. The paste so prepared should be given to the patient to be consumed by mouth or inhale through the nose. By so doing a patient gets relief.

## \|\| 1.36.29 \|\|

*pūrvāhṇe carate vipro madhyāhne kṣatriyaścaret \|*  
*aparāhne caredvaiśyaḥ śūdraḥ saṃdhyācaro bhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The serpent of Brahmana type crawls in the forenoon, of Kshatriya type at noon, Vaishya type in the afternoon and Shudra type in the evening.

## \|\| 1.36.30 \|\|

*āhāro vāyupuṣpāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*mūṣikā kṣatri yāṇāṃ ca āhāro dvijasattama \|*  
*vaiśyā maṃḍūkabhakṣāśca śūdrāḥ sarvāśinastathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The learned people say that the Brahmana serpent consumes air and flowers serve the food; Kshatriya serpent consumes rats; Vaishya serpent consumes frogs, while Shudra serpent can consume anything.

## \|\| 1.36.31 \|\|

*agrato daśate vipraḥ kṣatriyo dakṣiṇena tu \|*  
*vāmapārśve sadā vaiśyaḥ paścādvai śūdra ādaśet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Brahmana serpent bites from the front side, a Kshatriya serpents bites from the right side, a Vaishya serpent from the left, while Shudra serpent bites from the back.

## \|\| 1.36.32 \|\|

*madakāle tu saṃprāpte pīḍyamānā mahāviṣāḥ \|*  
*avelāyāṃ daśaṃte vai maithunārtā bhujaṃgamāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. At the time of passion or intoxication, the serpent bites even untimely.

## \|\| 1.36.33 \|\|

*puṣpagaṃdhāḥ smṛtā viprāḥ kṣatriyāścaṃdanāvahāḥ \|*  
*vaiśyāśca ghṛtagaṃdhā vai śūdrāḥ syurmatsyagaṃdhinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A Brahmana serpent smells like a flower, a Kshatriya has the smell of sandalwood, a Vaishya smells like ghi, while the Shudra serpent smells like the fish.

## \|\| 1.36.34 \|\|

*vāsaṃ teṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*vāpīkūpataḍāgeṣu giriprasravaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*vasaṃti brāhmaṇāḥ sarpā grāmadvāre catuṣpathe \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. I am now describing the dwelling places of these serpents. The Brahmana serpents dwell over the step wells, rivers, wells, tanks, hills, springs, approached roads of the villages and the road crossings.

## \|\| 1.36.35-37 \|\|

*ārāmeṣu pavitreṣu śuciṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*vasanti kṣatriyā nityaṃ toraṇeṣu saraḥsu ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śmaśāne bhasmaśālāsu palāleṣu taṭeṣu ca \|*  
*goṣṭheṣu pathi vṛkṣeṣu vipra vaiśyā vasaṃti ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*avivikteṣu sthāneṣu nirjaneṣu vaneṣu ca \|*  
*śūnyāgāre śmaśāne ca śūdrā vipra vasaṃti ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. The Kshatriya serpent lives in the auspicious orchards, neat and clean houses, outer gates of houses, the cities and the tanks. The Vaishya serpent dwell in the cremation ground, banks of the rivers, near trees nearby paths. The shudra serpents live near cremation grounds, forests and at empty places.

## \|\| 1.36.38 \|\|

*śvetāśca kapilāścaiva ye sarpāstvanalaprabhāḥ \|*  
*manasvinaḥ sāttvikāśca brāhmaṇāste budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The white, yellow, bluish white, red like fire, intelligent and Sattvika serpents have been given the name of Brahmana serpents by the people of intelligence.

## \|\| 1.36.39 \|\|

*raktavarṇāḥ suvarṇābhāḥ pravālamaṇisaṃnibhāḥ \|*  
*sūryaprabhāstathā vipra kṣatriyāste bhujaṃgamāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. O Brahmana, similarly, the males with red, golden, coral and having the colour of gems or the lustre of the sun, are said to be of Kshatriya type.

## \|\| 1.36.40 \|\|

*nānāvicitrarājībhiratasīvarṇasannibhāḥ \|*  
*bāṇa puṣpasavarṇābhā vaiśyāste vai bhujaṃgamāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The snakes which have multi colours, or with strips like linseed seeds, spotted serpents etc. come under the category of the Vaishya serpents.

## \|\| 1.36.41 \|\|

*kākodaranibhāḥ kecidye ca aṃjanasannibhāḥ \|*  
*kākavarṇā dhūmravarṇāste śūdrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those who have the colour of crow’s belly, or of the colour of smoke or the crow are known as Shudra snakes.

## \|\| 1.36.42 \|\|

*yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya daṃśamaṃguṣṭhamaṃtaram \|*  
*bāladaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A snake which bites from a distance of a thumb, it should be treated as an infant snake, according to Kashyapa.

## \|\| 1.36.43 \|\|

*yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya daṃśaṃ dvyaṃgulamaṃtaram \|*  
*yauvanasthena daṣṭasya etadbhavati lakṣaṇam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The serpent which bites from a distance of two fingers, it should be treated as a young serpent.

## \|\| 1.36.44 \|\|

*yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya sārdhaṃ dvyaṃgulamataram \|*  
*vṛddhadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A serpent which bites at a distance of two and half fingers, it should be treated as an old serpent, according to the sage Kashyapa.

## \|\| 1.36.45 \|\|

*anaṃtaḥ prekṣate pūrvaṃ vāmapārśve tu vāsukiḥ \|*  
*takṣako dakṣiṇeneha karkoṭaḥ pṛṣṭhatastathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Ananta Naga bites from the front, while Vasuki bites from the left side, Takshaka bites from the right side and Karkotaka bites from the back.

## \|\| 1.36.46 \|\|

*calate bhramate padmo mahāpadmo nimajjati \|*  
*visaṃjñastiṣṭhate caiva śaṃkhapālo muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The serpent named Padma crawls moving here and there. Mahapadma crawls like the one drowning in the water. The serpent Shankhapala moves like the one who has lost his senses.

## \|\| 1.36.47-48 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ kurute rūpaṃ kulikaḥ pannagottamaḥ \|*  
*anaṃtasya diśā pūrvā vāsukestu hutāśanī \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇā takṣakasyoktā karkoṭasya tu nairṛtī \|*  
*paścimā padmanābhasya mahāpadmasya vāyujā \|*  
*uttarā śaṃkhapālasya aiśānī kaṃbalasya tu \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The serpent known as Kulika has been considered to be the best of all the serpents and is extremely beautiful. Ananta is the serpent of eastern direction, Vasuki of southeast quarter, Takshaka of southern direction, Karkotaka of south-west quarter, Padmanabha of western direction, Mahapadma of northwest, Shankhapala of north, while Kambala is the serpent of north-east direction.

## \|\| 1.36.49-50 \|\|

*anaṃtasya bhavetpadmaṃ vāsukeḥ syāttathotpalam \|*  
*svastikaṃ takṣakasyoktaṃ karkoṭasya tu paṃkajam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*padmasya tu bhavetpadmaṃ śūlaṃ padmetarasya tu \|*  
*śaṃkhapāle bhavecchatraṃ kulikasyārdhacandrakam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Ananta has a mark of lotus, Vasuki has a mark of blue lotus, Takshaka has the mark of Svastika, Karkotaka has the mark of lotus, Padma also has the mark of lotus, Mahapadma has mark of a trident, Shankhapala has a mark of an umbrella and Kulika has mark of a crescent.

## \|\| 1.36.51 \|\|

*anaṃtakapilau viprau kṣatriyau śaṃkhavāsukī \|*  
*mahāpadmastakṣakaśca vaiśyau vipra prakīrtitau \|*  
*padmakarkoṭakau śūdrau sadā jñeyau manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O Brahmana, Ananta and Kapila are Brahmanas; shankha and Vasuki are Kshatriyas; Mahapadma and Takshaka are Vaishyas; while Padma and Karkotaka are Shudras, as per the knowledge of ancient sages.

## \|\| 1.36.52-53 \|\|

*anaṃtakulikau varṇato brahmasaṃbhavau \|*  
*vāsukiḥ śaṃkhapālaśca raktau hyagnisamudbhavau \|\| 52 \|\|*

*takṣakaśca mahāpadma īṣatpītau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*padmakarkoṭakau vipra sarpau kṛṣṇau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Ananta and Kulika have Shukra varna or of golden colour and were born of Brahmi Vasuki and Shankhapala are of red colour and were born of the Agni. Takshaka and Mahapadma are of yellow colour and were born of Indra. Padma and Karkotaka are of black colour and were born of Yama.

## \|\| 1.36.54 \|\|

*hayaṃ yānaṃ vṛṣaṃ chatraṃ rājānamatha pāvakam \|*  
*dharaṇīmutpādya dhṛtānetānsiddhikarānviduḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. One achieves success by getting a horse, vehicle, a bull for riding, umbrella, fire and earth.

## \|\| 1.36.55 \|\|

*pūrṇakumbhaḥ patākā ca kāṃcanaṃ maṇayastathā \|*  
*śirīṣaṃ māṇikaṃ kaṇṭhe jīvajīveti suvrata \|*  
*eteṣāṃ darśanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kanyā caikaprasūyikā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The sight of a pitcher filled with water, flag, gold, gems, the garlands of acacia flowers for adorning the neck, partridge and the girl who had delivered only once is said to be quite meritorious. Therefore, a person desirous of welfare, should always have sight of them.

## \|\| 1.36.56 \|\|

*catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ samākhyātā bhogino ye tu pannagāḥ \|*  
*adṛśyāsteṣu ṣaṭtriṃśaddṛśyāstriṃśanmahīcarāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In this context, I shall narrate an episode. The serpents are of sixty four types. Of these thirty six are invisible, while twenty eight types are visible.

## \|\| 1.36.57 \|\|

*viṃśacca sragviṇaḥ proktāḥ sapta maṃḍalinastathā \|*  
*rājīvanto daśa proktā darvyaḥ ṣoḍaśa paṃca ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Out of them twenty species are garlanded, seven species are ring type, ten species are of Raji type, and twenty one of the species are of Dravya types.

## \|\| 1.36.58 \|\|

*duṃdubho ḍuṃḍubhaścaiva ceṭabhaśceṃdravāhanaḥ \|*  
*nāgapuṣpasavarṇākhyā nirviṣā ye ca pannagāḥ \|*  
*evameva tu sarpāṇāṃ śatadvinavati smṛtam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The serpents having the complexion of nutmeg are devoid of venom besides the species like Dundubha, Dunduma, Chetabha and Indravahana. In this way, two hundred and ninety species of serpents have been specified.

## \|\| 1.36.59 \|\|

*varāhakarṇīṃ gajapippalīṃ ca gāṃdhārikāṃ pippaladevadāru \|*  
*madhūkasāraṃ sahasiṃduvāraṃ hiṃguṃ ca piṣṭvā guṭikā ca kāryā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Therefore, the medicinal herbs like Varahakarni, Gajapippali, Sulphur, Pippala, Devadaru (cedar), Madhuka (wine), Sinduvara and asafetida should be powdered together and the pills should be made. This is the effective medicine for treatment of the snake bite.

## \|\| 1.36.60-61 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*ityuktavānpurā vīra gautamasya prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ sarvaināgānāṃ rūpavarṇau viṣaṃ tathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tasmātsaṃpūjayennāgānsadā bhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣatastu paṃcamyāṃ payasā pāyasena ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Sumantu said — O valorous one, in this way, Kashyapa narrated to Gautama the various symptoms of the serpents, their colours and forms, names of the different species and about the venom. Therefore, the serpents should always be adored with devotion. Particularly on the fifth moon day of the month, the milk and payasam should be offered to them.

## \|\| 1.36.62-63 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe māsi paṃcamyāṃ śuklapakṣe narā dhipa \|*  
*dvārasyobhayato lekhyā gomayena viṣolbaṇāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*pūjayedvidhivaddvāraṃ dadhidūrvākṣataiḥ kuśaiḥ \|*  
*gaṃdhapuṣpopahāraiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. On the bright fortnight of the month of Shravana on the fifth moon day, people should draw the figures of serpents, and curd, durva grass, unbroken rice, kusha, fragrance and flowers should be offered to them appropriately, serving food to the Brahmanas at the same time.

## \|\| 1.36.64 \|\|

*ye tvasyāṃ pūjaṃtīha nāgānbhaktipuraḥsarāḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ sarvapato vīra bhayaṃ bhavati karhicit \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O valorous one, a person who adores the serpents on the aforesaid day, he is freed from the danger of snake bite.

## Chapter 37. Naga-Panchami vrata of Bhadrapada

## \|\| 1.37.1-3 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*tathā bhādrapade māsi paṃcamyāṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*athālekhya naro nāgānkṛṣṇavarṇādivarṇakaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pūjayedgaṃdhapuṣpaiśca sarpiḥ pāyasaguggulaiḥ \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭiṃ samāyāṃti pannagāstakṣakādayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*āsaptamātkulāttasya na bhayaṃ nāgato bhavet \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena nāgānsaṃpūjayedbudhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Sumantu said — Thus a person, who on the fifth moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, drawing the figure of black cobras, adores them offering fragrance, flowers, ghi, and guggulu, he pleases Takshaka and other Nagas. Such a person has no danger from serpent’s upto seven generations. Therefore, all the intelligent people should adore the serpents.

## Chapter 38. End of Panchami Kalpa

## \|\| 1.38.1 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*tathā cāśvayuje māsi pañcamyāṃ kurunaṃdana \|*  
*kṛtvā kuśamayānnāgāngaṃdhāṃdyaiḥ saṃprapūjayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O son of Kuru race, similarly, in seventh month of the Hindu year on the fifth moon day, a figure of serpent should be drawn and adored offering the fragrant flowers etc.

## \|\| 1.38.2 \|\|

*ghṛtodakābhyāṃ payasā snapayitvā viśāṃpate \|*  
*godhūmaiḥ payasā svinnairbhakṣyaiśca vividhaistathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O king, initially the figure should be bathed with ghi, water and milk. Thereafter, the wheat mixed with milk should be offered besides other eatables.

## \|\| 1.38.3-5 \|\|

*yastvasyāṃ vidhivannāgāñchucirbhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayetkuruśārdūla tasya śeṣādayo nṛpa \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nāgāḥ prītā bhavaṃtīha śāṃtimāpnoti vā vibho \|*  
*sa śāṃtilokamāsādya modate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ityeṣa kathito vīra pañcamīkalpa uttamaḥ \|*  
*yatrāyamucyate maṃtraḥ sarvasarpaniṣedhakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Because those who worship the serpents on this particular fifth moon day, the shesha and other serpents getting pleased with them, bestow peace on them. Such a person lives for long with comfort and peace. O valorous one, thus the excellent Panchami Kalpa is concluded in which a mantra for the removal of snake venom has been prescribed as follows: Om Kurukulle Phat Svaha This mantra is meant for the removal of the venom of snakes.

## Chapter 39. Glory of the sixth moon day

## \|\| 1.39.1 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ phalāśano rājanviśeṣātkārtike nṛpa \|*  
*rājyacyuto viśeṣeṇa svaṃ rājyaṃ labhate'cirāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O monarch, during the sixth moon-day, one should consume fruits only. The sixth moon-day of the month of Karttika is of special importance. In case a king has been deprived of his kingdom due to any reason, but with the performing of this Shashthi vrata he regains his lost kingdom ж without delay.

## \|\| 1.39.2 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhī tithirmahārāja sarvadā sarvakāmadā \|*  
*upoṣyā tu prayatnena sarvakālaṃ jayārthinā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O great monarch, the shashthi moon-day fulfills all the desires always. Therefore, those desirous of victory should always perform this vrata.

## \|\| 1.39.3 \|\|

*kārttikeyasya dayitā eṣā ṣaṣṭhī mahātithiḥ \|*  
*devasenādhipatyaṃ hi prāptaṃ tasyāṃ mahātmanā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Similarly, Karttikeya also has a special liking for the sixth moon-day, because it was on this particular day that he was declared as the army of the divine forces.

## \|\| 1.39.4 \|\|

*asyāṃ hi śreyasā yukto yasmātskando bhavāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*tasmātṣaṣṭhyāṃ naktabhojī prāpnuyādīpsitaṃ sadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The credit of making Skanda as the elder son of Shiva goes to the sixth moon-day. During this vrata, the devotee fasts during the whole day and take food during the night. The person who does so, he succeeds in his efforts.

## \|\| 1.39.5-7 \|\|

*dattvārghyaṃ kārtikeyāya sthitvā vai dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ \|*  
*dadhnā ghṛtodakaiḥ puṣpairmantreṇānena suvrata \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saptarṣidāraja skanda svāhāpatisamudbhava \|*  
*rudrāryamāgnija vibho gaṅgāgarbha namo'stu te \|*  
*prīyatāṃ devasenānīḥ sampādayatu hṛdgatam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dattvā viprāya cātmānnaṃ yaccānyadapi vidyate \|*  
*paścādbhuṅkte tvasau rātrau bhūmiṃ kṛtvā tu bhājanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. After performing the worship, one should face towards south and offer oblation with curd, ghi, water and flowers to Skanda, reciting the mantra “Saptarshidaraja Skanda Svaha”. Thereafter, he should serve the best of the food to Brahmanas, which is prepared in the best possible manner. The remaining food should be taken, keeping it over the ground. Besides the above, he should give away anything else to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.39.8 \|\|

*evaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vrataṃ snehātproktaṃ skandena yatnataḥ \|*  
*tannibodha mahārāja procyamānaṃ mayākhilam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O great monarch, the procedure for performing the Shashthi vrata as told by Skanda himself, is being repeated by me to you, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.39.9-10 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ yastu phalāhāro naktāhāro bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śuklākṛṣṇāsu niyato brahmacārī samāhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasya siddhiṃ dhṛtiṃ tuṣṭiṃ rājyamāyurnirāmayam \|*  
*pāratrikaṃ caihikaṃ ca dadyātskando na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. On the sixth moon day of bright or dark fortnights, performing the Brahmacharya vrata in case one consumes the fruits only, lord Skanda getting pleased with him bestows success, patience, delight or bliss, kingship, long life, besides comforts in the present as well as the future world.

## \|\| 1.39.11-13 \|\|

*yo hi naktopavāsaḥ syātsa naktena vratī bhavet \|*  
*iha vāmutra so'tyantaṃ labhate khyātimuttamām \|*  
*svarge ca niyataṃ vāsaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*iha cāgatya kālānte yathoktaphalabhāgbhavet \|*  
*devānāmapi vandyo'sau rājñāṃ rājā bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yaścāpi śṛṇuyātkalpaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāḥ kurukulodvaha \|*  
*tasya siddhistathā tuṣṭirdhṛtiḥ syātkhyātisambhavā \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. He is surely lodged in the heaven. In case he is reborn over the earth, he also receives the aforesaid reward. He is honoured by the gods, besides becoming the king of kings. O leader of the Kuru race, those who listen to the narration of the vrata of Shashthi tithi, they also achieve success, patience as well the glory.

## Chapter 40. Description of Karttikeya

## \|\| 1.40.1-2 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*aho vrataṃ mahatkaṣṭaṃ saṃśayo hṛdi vartate \|*  
*kārtikeyasya māhātmyaṃ śrutvā janma tathā dvija \|\| 1 \|\|*

*anekajanitasyeha kārttikeyasya suvrata \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ sumahadvipra kathametadvibhāvyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Shatanika said — O Brahmana, listening to the story of Karttikeya’s birth and his glory, a painful doubt has developed in my mind. When the birth of Karttikeya was brought out by several personalities, then how could he earn so much of glory?

## \|\| 1.40.3-4 \|\|

*jātiḥ śreṣṭhā bhavedvīra uta karma bhavedvaram \|*  
*saṃśayastu mahānatra dṛṣṭvā me kṛttikāsutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*etadvada viniścitya na yathā saṃśayo bhavet \|*  
*janmataḥ karmaṇaścaiva yajjvāyastad bravīhi me \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. At the sight of the son of Krittika, I have developed a doubt in my mind as to whether the actions or the castes are to be treated as superior of the two. After thinking over the matter quite deeply, you enlighten me on the issue to enable me to have my doubt removed or in other words could the glory be achieved by one’s birth or his conduct or activities? You kindly let me have your views on this subject clearly.

## \|\| 1.40.5 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo brahmā śiṣyairmanīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*yaduktaṃ tena teṣāṃ ca tatte vacmi nibodha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Sumantu said — The intelligent disciples of Brahma also once had put him a question on this subject in the past and the reply which he gave to them is being repeated by me, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.40.6-7 \|\|

*surajyeṣṭhaṃ sukhāsīnamabhigamya maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya ca mahābāho viśvāmitrasya vipratām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā vismayamāgatya kautūhalasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*bhaktiṃ śraddhāṃ purodhāya praṇamyānatakandharāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. O long armed one, observing the attaining of Brahmanhood the Rishis were immensely surprised. They became anxious to know the cause of the same. Therefore, all of them went to Brahma who was comfortably seated, getting filled with devotion and faith, offered their salutation to him and started asking him.

## \|\| 1.40.8-11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bho brahmannādakalpe hi brāhmaṇyaṃ brūhi kiṃ bhavet \|*  
*jātyadhyayanadehātmasaṃskārācārakarmaṇām1 \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bāhyābhyantarasāmānyaviśeṣā yadi kṛtrimāḥ \|*  
*manovākkarmaśārīrajātidravyaguṇātmakāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*santyaktavyāḥ prasiddhā ye jātibhedavidhāyinaḥ \|*  
*vastubhūtāḥ parokṣairvā pramāṇairna viniścitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*avyaktāgamasiddhaścejjātibhedavidhirnṛṇām \|*  
*vikalpo'yaṃ na puṣṇāti bhavataḥ śemuṣībalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. The Rishis said — O Brahma, in the initial kalpa what were the reasons for becoming initially, were these due to the caste, study in the Vedas, the body, the traditional Samskaras the conduct or the performing of the Vedic studies, which could earn a person the Brahmanhood? In case it is said that the artificial object like the mind, speech, actions, body, the caste (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra etc.) or the Dravyas like the (earth» fire, water and lustre), the virtues or the forms etc. are the factor responsible for the caste of is it the same by inner or the outer vision» or does it remain the same in both the conditions or does it become popular in some special circumstances? Is it established because of the division in the castes or is it to be discarded when something is not attainable in special circumstances? Or is it something which could not be established by visible or invisible means or has to be totally discarded? Therefore, it could never be the cause of the caste. In case, the difference of castes of humans has been established by the Vedas alone, then this imagination is totally incompetent to support your wisdom.

## \|\| 1.40.12 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evametanna sandeho yathā yūyaṃ vadanti1 ha \|*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ yogino vākyaṃ satarkaṃ śiṣyaśreyase \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Brahma said — Whatever you have stated is correct. There is no doubt about it. But in this connection, you listen to the reasoning of Yogeshvara and by so doing, the disciple shall be befitted besides your doubts would also be removed.

## \|\| 1.40.13 \|\|

*yogeśvara uvāca \|*  
*pramāṇe hi prasiddhe tu bhinnārthaviṣaye yataḥ \|*  
*spaṣṭayogyārthaviṣayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tāvadīkṣate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Yogeshvara said — Though the evidence is always required in all the cases, but still the tangible or apparent proof is considered to be more authentic.

## \|\| 1.40.14 \|\|

*samānyātīndriyagrāhī siddhānto'bhyupagamyate \|*  
*sa eva bhagavānekaṃ pramāṇamiti cenna tat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Though even when you accept the ordinary or special principle, then in that case only the lord is established, is it not the case?

## \|\| 1.40.15 \|\|

*yasmādvividhame tatte saṅkaṭaṃ bhadra vartate \|*  
*vedasya pauruṣeyatvaṃ nityajātisamarthakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O noble one, the reason by which one faces the misfortune and for the removal of the same, it is essential for me to speak out something. It is said that the status of the Vedas being vigorous, is the eternal proof of the origin of the caste.

## \|\| 1.40.16 \|\|

*kāryā viśeṣā vedoktā na yuktamakṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tālvādikaraṇānāṃ ca vyāpārānantaraṃ śruteḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Therefore, it should be considered to be a definite proof of the Vedas, instead the impracticable terms or the speeches, which would be appropriate. As for example, because of the use of palate or the mouth one can hear the words.

## \|\| 1.40.17 \|\|

*vyāpārātparatastasya prāgabhāvaviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tadbhāvānuvidhāyitvamanvayavyatiraketaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Because of the use of palate there remains the urge to speak a non-existing word before the fixed time. Thereafter, the words become audible. It is thus established that after initiation of the urge in the palate, the words are heard and when this urge is not there, the words cannot be heard. This particular situation in the world has been interpreted that no task can be established without a definite cause.

## \|\| 1.40.18 \|\|

*tasmāddhūmāgnivadvārthaphalabhāvo'vatiṣṭhate \|*  
*na ca vyāpāravacasoranyathānupapattitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Therefore, with the spotting of the smoke, one should anticipate the presence of the fire and not by motion alone, otherwise there would be a doubt in the existence of the fire.

## \|\| 1.40.19-20 \|\|

*puruṣānugatā jātirbrāhmaṇatvādikāsti cet \|*  
*dvivarṇajātibhedena pratyākṣārthopalakṣaṇāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*govargamadhyaṃ ca gato yathāśvo nirdhāryate jñaiḥ suvicakṣaṇatvāt \|*  
*manuṣyabhāvādaviśiṣyamāṇastadvaddvijaḥ śūdragaṇānna bhinnaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The division of castes, viz. Brahmana, Kshatriya and Vaishya besides the Shudra, are too apparent. Therefore, it would not be appropriate to say that the presence of the human race itself is the supportive of the Brahmana caste, as the intelligent people could spot a horse in the herd of cows. Similarly, being a human in the absence of a distinguishing mark, Brahmana and Kshatriya cannot be recognized among the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.40.21 \|\|

*manuṣyajāterna paro viśeṣo yaḥ kalpyate sarvanarānuyāyī \|*  
*saṃskārayuktā hi kriyāviśiṣṭā dvijanmanāṃ śūdravivekahetuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The people who consider all humans to be equal, say that there is no race better than the human race. The performing of the thread ceremony separates a Brahmana from the Shudra.

## \|\| 1.40.22 \|\|

*jīvo'pi brāhmaṇaḥ prokto yairatattvajñamānavaiḥ \|*  
*prabhraṣṭabrāhmaṇatvāste jāyante viprasaṅgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Some ignorant persons are of the view that every jiva is a Brahmana, but after coming into contact with the fallen Brahmanas, their Brahmanhood had been lost. Therefore, this reason also cannot be accepted.

## \|\| 1.40.23-25 \|\|

*jarājanmāntarakleśaduṣṭagrāhakulākulam \|*  
*nara tiryagasacchūdra yoniduḥkhormisaṃkaṭam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dausthityarogaśokārtijanāvartasamanvitam \|*  
*śvānuśūkaracāṇḍālakṛmikūrmādikāyakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saṃsārasāgaraṃ ghoraṃ magnaḥ khalu pariplavan \|*  
*bhūripāpabharākrāntaḥ sa jīvo brāhmaṇaḥ katham \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. They further argue that when a jiva has to free old age, rebirth, the related miseries in the form of the ocean filled with crocodiles, having the waves of human forms, birds, untouchable Shudras and the misfortunes, the painful sufferings, ailments, grief, the whirlpools of the distressed people, besides the dogs, pigs, Chandalas, insects, worms, besides the tortoises and are drowning in the terrific ocean of the universe, overburdened with the heavy weight of the sins, then how could he become a Brahmana?

## \|\| 1.40.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*saptavyādhakathā viprā manunā parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*taṃ niśamya yaduśreṣṭha nityaṃ jātipadaṃ tyajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Brahma said — O Brahmana, listening to the story of the seven hunters, the discussion about the caste should be discontinued.

## \|\| 1.40.27-29 \|\|

*saptavyādhā daśārṇeṣu1 mṛgāḥ kālañjare girau \|*  
*cakravākāḥ sariddvīpe haṃsāḥ sarasi mānase \|\| 27 \|\|*

*te'pi jātāḥ kurukṣetre brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*prasthitā dīrghamadhvānaṃ mṛyaṃ kimavasīdatha \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tasmānna jīve brāhmaṇyaṃ paśyāmo hi kathañcana \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. Because all the seven hunters were first born in Dasharna country, Thereafter, they were reborn over the Kalanjara mountains as a deer, partridges in Sariddvipa, swans at Manasarovara lake and Brahmanas well versed in the Vedas at Kurukshetra. Therefore, having started for such a long journey, why do you all feel painful? In this way, a jiva can never become a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.40.30 \|\|

*śastrādimadbhārgavajātiyukto gajāśvagojoṣṭrakharādikānām \|*  
*śaktyā kṛto hyaṅgajavarṇadharmairbhedaḥ sphuṭaṃ lakṣaṇato'tra yadvat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The castes of Bhargava race, the carriers of weapons, besides the elephants, horses, cows, goats, camels and the donkeys could be distinguished on the basis of their limbs, their respective complexion, skin, etc. The difference which is too apparent from the powerful limbs, symbols, etc., similarly the differences in the jivas above too are apparent.

## \|\| 1.40.31 \|\|

*taduttarānnaiva vikartanīyā brāhmaṇyajātinṛṣu nāsti kācit \|*  
*nityākṛtirnānupabhedarūpā yathā hi bhedaḥ paramo'tra sidhyet \|*  
*sitādyasādhāraṇatulyarūpāḥ sanātano'ṅgeṣu na varṇabhedaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In this way, there could be no solution of the question about the Brahmana, because there is no caste of Brahmana among the humans. Therefore, this caste is not eternal, or are there any divisions for the same visible? The difference of having fair or black complexion also cannot be indicative of the caste, besides the formation and the beauty of the limbs are also imaginary.

## \|\| 1.40.32 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyamadhruvamidaṃ kila kṛtrimatvādakṛtrimaṃ bhavati sāmayikatvayogāt \|*  
*sāṅketikaṃ sukṛtaleśaviśeṣalabdhaṃ vāṇijyabheṣajakṛtāmiva jātibhedāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. They become everlasting due to the influence of time. There is an imaginary difference between a Vaishya and Vaidya (a trader and a physician), and they are indicative only.

## \|\| 1.40.33 \|\|

*kiṃ brāhmaṇā ye sukṛtaṃ tyajanti kiṃ kṣatriyā lokamapālayantaḥ \|*  
*svadharmahīnā hi tathaiva vaiśyāḥ śūdrāḥ svamukhyakriyayā vihīnāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Brahmanas who discarding the noble functions, the Kshatriyas who do not protect the people, and the Vaishyas who fall from their path of dharma, could they be said to belong to their own castes?

## \|\| 1.40.34 \|\|

*tasmānna gośvavatkaścijjātibhedo'sti dehinām \|*  
*kāryaśaktinimittastu saṅketaḥ kṛtrimo bhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There is no differentiation in the castes of humans like the cows and the horses, because of being the cause in the making of their own efforts, the indications are imaginary.

## \|\| 1.40.35 \|\|

*evaṃ pramāṇaiḥ pratiṣidhyamānāṃ sāṅketikīṃ yāti naro vyavasthām \|*  
*svakīyasiddhāṃ svamatairniṣiddhāṃ na budhyate mūḍhamanā varākaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Similarly, among the humans, the arrangement of Brahmana, Kshatriya which is void on the basis of evidence, should be accepted as indicative alone, which is beyond the understanding of the foolish people as to whether the arrangement is self made or is also contrary to it as well.

## \|\| 1.40.36-37 \|\|

*gomahiṣyajavājyuṣṭravāneyāvigajādhipāḥ \|*  
*preṣyavārdhuṣikākāryakaraṇodyatamānasāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vaṇikkārukriyāviṣṭā1 divyāste'pi ca ye dvijāḥ \|*  
*vinaṣṭāste tu vijñeyāḥ kravyādāśca kuśīlavāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Therefore, those who are engaged for the upkeep of cows, buffaloes, goats, horses, camels, sheep and elephants, the porters, those living on taking interest, those who work as traders, those who draw pictures on walls, those engaged in demoniacal professions, as well as the dancers, then inspite of their being Brahmanas, they would be treated as the fallen ones.

## \|\| 1.40.38-41 \|\|

*palāṇḍulaśunādāśca mṛgyuṣṭrīkṣīrapāyinaḥ \|*  
*māṃsasarvarasakṣīrakrayavikrayakāriṇaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*punarbhūvṛṣalīveśyācāṇḍālastrīniṣeviṇaḥ \|*  
*śūdrānnarasapuṣṭāṅgāḥ pretavastrānnabhojanāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*mṛtasūtakalabdhānnapānādyabhyavahāriṇaḥ \|*  
*brahmadevapitṛbhūtamanuṣyeṣu bahiṣkṛtāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*mātsaryamadavidveṣatṛṣṇākāmatamomayāḥ \|*  
*hīnācārā1 hi ye kecidapare piśunā dvijāḥ \|*  
*prakārairbahubhiḥ sarve te praṇaśyanti nānyathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. Similarly, the Brahmanas who consume onion and garlic, or drink the milk of dog or female camels, as well as those who consume flesh, all types of beverages or sell them or those Who unite with a woman having married twice, then Shudras woman and the Chandala woman, or those who live on the food supplied by Shudras, or those who use the costumes of pretas, or those engaged in the work of pretas (or dead bodies), those who take food during the birth or death of a person, such Brahmanas are discarded by the gods, manes, bhutas and other humans as well. In addition to these, the people who are infested with hostility, pride, jealousy, greed, lustfulness, backbiters and the Brahmanas who are devoid of the noble conduct, such Brahmanas should be treated to have been fallen from the noble path.

## \|\| 1.40.42-43 \|\|

*evaṃ śāstroditanyāyamārgabhraṣṭāstu ye narāḥ \|*  
*viśiṣṭagotrasaṃskārakalāpasakalātmakāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vedānadhyāpayanto'pi te'dhīyānāḥ śrutikramāt \|*  
*brāhmaṇatvādvihīyante durācāravighāyinaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Therefore, the caste of a person is not indestructible. Because a Brahmana, who has fallen from the path of the Vedas, inspite of him being high, inspite of him possessing the auspicious Samskaras or traditions and being well-versed in the Vedas and even when engaged in the study of the Vedas, because of his evil conduct, is treated to have fallen.

## \|\| 1.40.44-45 \|\|

*tasmānna jātirekatra bhūtātmāstyanapāyinī \|*  
*nāśitvādatra ca ślokānmānavāḥ samadhīyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sadyaḥ patati māṃsena lākṣayā lavaṇena ca \|*  
*tryaheṇa śūdro bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ kṣīravikayī \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Therefore, the caste of a person is not indestructible and because of its being destructible, the people believe that a Brahmana engaged in the sale of meat or flesh, the wax or salt, is treated as having fallen at the same time, while a Brahmana selling the milk, remains a shudra for three days.

## \|\| 1.40.46 \|\|

*gorakṣakānvāṇijikāṃstathā kārukuśīlavān \|*  
*preṣyānvārdhuṣikāṃścaiva śūdrāstānmanurabravīt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Similarly, the irrigation or farming is the job of a Vaishya besides that of protecting the cows. The Brahmanas who draw the figures on wails, singing or dancing, besides working as servants or money lending, have been treated by Manu as Shudras.

## \|\| 1.40.47 \|\|

*śūdro brāhmaṇatāmeti brāhmaṇaścaiti śūdratām \|*  
*kṣatriyo yāti vipratvaṃ vidyādvaiśyaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In this way, a Brahmana is turned as a Shudra, while a Shudra is turned as a Brahmana. Sometimes, a Kshatriya too becomes a Brahmana and a Vaishya too is turned to the higher caste.

## Chapter 41. The prudence of Brahmanas

## \|\| 1.41.1 \|\|

*mṛtimattvācca nāśitvaṃ nāśitvāccheṣabhūtavat \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — In case, the study of Vedas is the only quality of a Brahmana, the Vaishyas and Kshatriyas can also be called as Brahmanas, as Ravana and others were turned as Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.41.2 \|\|

*ācārahīnānna punaṃti vedā yadyapyadhītāḥ saha ṣadbhiraṅgaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Similarly, the Chandalas, who consume the dog’s meat, the slaves, the hunters, cowherd, or milkmen, also engage themselves in the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.41.3-6 \|\|

*yadā deśāntaraṃ gatvā brāhmaṇyaṃ kṣatriyaṃ śritāḥ \|*  
*vyāpārākārabhāvādyairvipratulyaiḥ prakalpitaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vedānadhītya vedau vā vedaṃ vāpi yathākramam \|*  
*prodvahanti śubhāṃ kanyāṃ śuddhabrāhmaṇajā narāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*athavādhītya vedāṃstu kṣatravaiśyaistu1 vā narāḥ \|*  
*gauḍapūrvāṃ kṛtāmeyurjātiṃ vā dākṣiṇātyajām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aparijñātaśūdratvādbrāhmaṇyaṃ yānti kāmataḥ \|*  
*tasmānna jñāyate bhedo vedādhyāyakriyākṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. As a Shudra, moving to some other region, working under some Brahmana or a Kshatriya follows the activities, language and traditions in business, also studies all the four Vedas or anyone of them and marries an auspicious Brahmana girl, or some Kshatriya or a Vaishya girl, and after the study of the Vedas mixes up in some Dravida or Gauda Brahmana. Similarly, a Shudra also, unknowingly becomes a Brahmana. Therefore, the study of the Vedas do not stand testimony for the caste.

## \|\| 1.41.7 \|\|

*śāstrakāraistathā coktaṃ nyāyamārgānusāribhiḥ \|*  
*te sādhu matamākarṇya santaḥ santi vimatsarāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Therefore, the noble people listening to the words of the judicious people, do not develop enmity with others.

## \|\| 1.41.8 \|\|

*śilpaṃ hi vedādhyayanaṃ dvijānāṃ vṛttaṃ smṛtaṃ brāhmaṇalakṣaṇaṃ tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A Brahmana who is well-versed in all the Vedas with is parts, cannot be purified by the Vedas in case of his possessing the evil conduct. For a Brahmana, the study of Vedas is an art, which happens to be his symptom itself.

## \|\| 1.41.9 \|\|

*adhītya caturo vedānyadi vṛtte na tiṣṭhati \|*  
*na tena kriyate kāryaṃ strīratneneva ṣaṇḍhakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A Brahmana, whoever after the study of the Vedas, does not patronize his professional dharma, then his life becomes infructuous as the life of a eunuch is infructuous, even after getting the gem of a woman.

## \|\| 1.41.10 \|\|

*śikhāpraṇavasaṃskārasandhyopāsanamekhalāḥ \|*  
*daṇḍājinapavitrādyāḥ śūdreṣvapi niraṅkuśāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Even the Shudras can patronize the tuft, the tradition of Omkara, performing of timely Sandhya, wearing of waistband of munja grass, a danda and the deer skin.

## \|\| 1.41.11-13 \|\|

*prasaṅgo'pi hi śūdrāṇāṃ na śakyo vinivāritum \|*  
*devottamatrayeṇāpi nivartante narāḥ svayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasmānnaite'pi lakṣyante vilakṣaṇatayā1 nṛṇām \|*  
*yajñopavītasaṃskāramekhalācūlikādayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ābhicārikamantrādyairdurlabhatvādibhāṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇasyaiva śaktiścetkenāsya vinihanyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Even Brahma and Vishnu cannot stop a person from becoming a Shudra, then what to speak of the human beings. Therefore, a yajnopavita samskara, the tuft, the waistband etc. are not at all indicative of the caste of a person. In case, the strength of a Brahmana is enshrined in tantras or mantras or delivering of sudden speeches, then in that particular sphere, who could destroy the competence of a Shudra?

## \|\| 1.41.14 \|\|

*tapaḥ satyādimāhātmyāddevatāsamayasmṛtiḥ \|*  
*mantraśaktirnṛṇāmeṣāṃ sarveṣāmapi vidyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Because the importance of truthfulness and performance of tapas and mantras, besides the knowledge of the gods is found in the Shudras and other human beings as well.

## \|\| 1.41.15 \|\|

*vañcanaṃ durvacasyāpi kriyate sarvamānavaiḥ \|*  
*śūdrabrāhmaṇayostasmānnāsti bhedaḥ kathañcana \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Besides the Shudras and other people denounce those who speak harsh words, therefore, no difference is possible in the Brahmanas and the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.41.16-17 \|\|

*śāpānugrahakāritvaṃ śaktibhedo na vidyate \|*  
*cauracāṭādirājanyadurjanābhihate nṛṇām \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ātmāduḥkhodayāpāyaṃ sveṣu jantuṣu rakṣaṇam \|*  
*kartuṃ na prabhavecchūdro brāhmaṇastadvadeva hi \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The powers to pronounce a curse and to grant forgiveness are also visualized in the Shudras equally well. Similarly, the thieves, betrayers, the princes and the evil people display no difference in adverse situations. When a person is attacked by an evil person, there appears no difference in castes or creed. As a Shudra is unable to get himself relieved of his miseries or cannot save his own people, similarly, a Brahmana too is unable to do so.

## \|\| 1.41.18 \|\|

*mā bhūdyuge kalāvetaddeśe cākāryakṛddvije \|*  
*syādanyadeśakālādau dvijānāmatiśāyinām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. During the time of Kaliyuga, in case the Brahmanas are not inclined towards the evil ways it would be better, though in some other time in some other country, the Brahmanas might be following the evil ways.

## \|\| 1.41.19 \|\|

*śāpānugrahasāmarthyamanyadvādhyātmagocaram \|*  
*brahmasādhanametaddhi liṅgaṃ kecitpracakṣate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Some people attribute the pronouncing of curses or boons and the spiritual thoughts as the symptoms of the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.41.20 \|\|

*saṃsārāraktacetaskā mohāndhatamasāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*patantyunmārgagarteṣu pratyagni śalabhā yathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. But (one who) is inclined to the affairs of the world, he falls in the confusion of darkness. All the people fall in the hell like the fire flies falling in the fire under compulsion.

## \|\| 1.41.21 \|\|

*jātidharmaḥ svayaṃ kiñjidviśeṣaḥ śrutisaṅgamāt \|*  
*asiddhaḥ śūdrajātīnāṃ prasiddho viprajātiṣu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Though because of the Vedic studies, of course some influence is exercised over the Brahmanas which is quite well known, but it is totally absent in the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.41.22 \|\|

*saṃskāro yonisādhyo vā sāmagrī prabhavo'tha vā \|*  
*śūdrebhyo'tiśayaṃ dhatte yaḥ sādhāraṇatāguṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Samskaras and the related material or the cause of the same which are found in the people in a simple way, it is rarely found in the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.41.23 \|\|

*viprāṇāṃ pañcadhā bhedaḥ kalpanīyastu paṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*na jātijastrayījo vā viśeṣo yuktibādhakāt \|*  
*kramākramakriyāḥ santi na sanātanavastunaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The learned people have imagined five types of classes in the Brahmanas. But this classification being inappropriate, has neither been accepted by the Vedas nor by the Brahmanas as a whole because in the ancient, eternal or everlasting matter, no activity is generated for no reason whatsoever.

## \|\| 1.41.24 \|\|

*nityo na heturvigatakriyatvāddheturbhavedvedaviśeṣataḥ saḥ \|*  
*sa tatsamastatpratisannidhānātkālātyayekṣitvamayuktameva \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Because of this, since no activity is possible in an everlasting matter, it cannot be the cause of anything else. Had there been a cause of it, then it could be due to the importance of the Vedas. It could be equated with the study of the Vedas, but with the missing of the opportunity, only destruction or the death of the body is achieved, which is said to be improper.

## \|\| 1.41.25 \|\|

*svāntaḥ śarīravṛttisthaḥ śrutiyogādudeti yaḥ \|*  
*so'nanyavedavijñātasvabhāvo'nyairna gamyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Samskara of the mind could be achieved or raised with the study of the Vedas, but it could not be available with a person who does not study the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.41.26 \|\|

*viśiṣṭādhītidharmatve kṛtrimā brahmasaṅgatiḥ \|*  
*yasyāsyatiśayastasya nānyo nāśrayate yadi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I It is the duty of a Brahmana to specialize in the Vedas, This is the only symptom! Therefore, the one who is not engaged in the study of the Vedas, cannot be treated as a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.41.27-29 \|\|

*dṛśyasvabhāvaṃ kimabhīṣṭametadbrāhmaṇyamāhosvidadṛṣṭarūpam \|*  
*sarvaiḥ pratīyeta hi dṛśyarūpaṃ tato'nyathāvadgatireva na syāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sāmagryabhāvātparamaṃ viśeṣaṃ bhūdevagātrasthamabhūmidevāḥ \|*  
*smaranti tenātmani puṇyapāpaṃ yathā tathetyetadayuktamuktam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sāmagryanuṣṭhānaguṇaiḥ samagrāḥ śūdrā yataḥ santi samā dvijānām \|*  
*tasmādviśeṣo dvijaśūdranāmnornādhyātmiko bāhyanimittako vā \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. Therefore, whatever are the reasons for visible and invisible Brahmanas, only the visible things move. There is no movement for the invisible things. In the absence of the material, the gods, who do not lie on earth, dwelling in their own respective souls, remember their salient features of evil or noble deeds. This is a doubtless situation. By virtue of performing the anushthanas with adequate materials, a Shudra is equated with a Brahmana. Therefore, there is no difference between a Brahmana and a Shudra. And visualizing an illustrious Shudra possessing the Samskara, no one talks about the past. Therefore, this cause would also be inappropriate or otherwise it cannot be established due to outward differences.

## \|\| 1.41.30-33 \|\|

*saṃskārataḥ so'tiśayo yadi syātsarvasya puṃso'styatisaṃskṛtasya \|*  
*yaḥ saṃskṛto vipragaṇapradhāno vyāsādikaistena na tasya sāmyam1 \|\| 30 \|\|*

*hetutvaṃ ghaṭate1 naiṣāṃ jātyādīnāmasambhavāt \|*  
*jāterakṛtakatvācca adhīte na viśeṣataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*saṃskārātiśayābhāvādantarasyāgate paraiḥ \|*  
*bhautikatvāccharīrasya samastānāmasaṃhataiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kiṃ cānyanāstikamleccha yavanādijaneṣvalam2 \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. In case, the Brahmana is the foremost due to his Samskara, then every such person whose Samskara have been performed, would be a Brahmana. But then how could he be equated with Vyasa and others, who were devoid of the Samskara? Therefore, no cause is acceptable in support of a caste. Though the caste is considered to be eternal, but no importance is found in its study. Whatever importance be there, it would not be possible during the initiation of the Vedas. The body also, because of the importance of the Samskara, though comprising of the five tattvas (earth, fire, water, wind and sky) is no cause of being a Brahmana, because all the elements (of which a body is comprised of) have individual existence (and unite for some time only). Another point of importance is that the atheists, Mlecchas, Yavanas and others have also the same types of human bodies.

## \|\| 1.41.34 \|\|

*vedoditabahirduṣṭacariteṣu durātmasu \|*  
*dharmādatiśayo3 dṛṣṭaḥ krūrasāhasikādiṣu \|*  
*tasmādvipreṣu jātyādisāmagrīprabhavo na saḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Similarly, the wicked people with evil conduct and the killers also sometimes possess the religious instinct as brought out in the Vedas. Therefore, the Samskara alone cannot be the cause for becoming a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.41.35-39 \|\|

*tasmānna ca vibhedo'sti na bahirnāntarātmani \|*  
*sukhādau na caiśvarye nājñāyāṃ nābhayeṣvapi \|\| 35 \|\|*

*na vīrye nākṛtau nākṣe na vyāpāre na cāyuṣi \|*  
*nāṅge puṣṭe na daurbalye na sthairye nāpi cāpale \|\| 36 \|\|*

*na prajñāyāṃ na vairāgye na dharme na parākrame \|*  
*na trivarge na naipuṇye na rūpādau na bheṣaje \|\| 37 \|\|*

*na strīgarbhe na gamane na dehamalasamplave \|*  
*nāsthirandhre na ca premṇi na pramāṇeṣu lomasu \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śūdrabrāhmaṇyorbhedo mṛgyamāṇo'pi yatnataḥ \|*  
*nekṣyate sarvadharmeṣu saṃhataistridaśairapi \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. Therefore, in case a person tries to trace out inward or outward differences between a Brahmana and a Shudra on the basis of pain or pleasure, the fortunes or commanding, fearlessness, semen, body, gambling, trade income, trivarga i.e., dharma, artha and kama, cleverness, beauty or complexion, aushadhis, women and their wombs, conjugal relations, dirt of the body, bones of the body, the pores of the body, love, height, health and hair, even when all the gods unitedly try to search differences in the bodies of a Brahmana and a Shudra, they would not be able to do so inspite of their best efforts.

## \|\| 1.41.40 \|\|

*uktamātrā visambhūtirvicārakramakāribhiḥ \|*  
*vṛddhavṛndārakādhīśairapradhṛṣyamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Thus whatever opinion has been expressed on the basis of the practical experience, they are true and cannot be countered by even the gods including Indra, who is well experienced.

## \|\| 1.41.41 \|\|

*na brāhmaṇāścandramarīciśubhrā na kṣatriyāḥ kiṃśukapuṣpavarṇāḥ \|*  
*na ceha vaiśyā haritālatulyāḥ śūdrā na cāṅgārasamānavarṇāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Because the Brahmanas are bright like the moon rays, Kshatriyas are of red colour resembling the Butea frondosa, Vaishyas are of green complexion, while the Shudras are of black colour resembling the coal.

## \|\| 1.41.42 \|\|

*pādapracāraistanuvarṇakeśaiḥ sukhena duḥkhena ca śoṇitena \|*  
*tvaṅmāṃsamedosthirasaiḥ1 samānāścatuṣprabhedā hi kathaṃ bhavanti \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. How could there be difference of four types like Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudras, when walking with feet, the complexion of the body, the hair, pleasure and pain, the blood, skin, flesh, marrow, bones and the juices are similar?

## \|\| 1.41.43 \|\|

*varṇapramāṇākṛtigarbhavāsavāgbuddhikarmendriyajīviteṣu \|*  
*balatrivargāmayabheṣajeṣu na vidyate jātikṛto viśeṣaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. This situation holds good when there is no difference among the four castes over the complexion, length, breadth, formation of body, stay in the womb, speech, intelligence, organs of activity viz., speech, hands, feet, anus, oratory passage, life, strength, trivarga — dharma, artha and kama and the quality of medicines, for a particular caste.

## \|\| 1.41.44 \|\|

*sa eka evātra patiḥ prajānāṃ kathaṃ punarjātikṛtaḥ prabhedaḥ \|*  
*pramāṇadṛṣṭāntanayapravādaiḥ parīkṣyamāṇo vighaṭatvameti \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Because of these facts, one and the same supreme soul is also the lord of all the people. Then how could there be the difference in castes with the quoting of any example, evidence or policy? Making use of any touch stone, none would be able to prove the differentiation.

## \|\| 1.41.45 \|\|

*catvāra ekasya pituḥ sutāśca teṣāṃ sutānāṃ khalu jātirekā \|*  
*evaṃ prajānāṃ hi pitaika evaṃ pitraikabhāvānna ca jātibhedaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. As for an example, when a father has four sons, surely they belong to one and the same caste. Similarly, there is only one father who produces all. When the father is one, where lies the differentiation in the caste.

## \|\| 1.41.46 \|\|

*phalānyathodumbaravṛkṣajāteryathāgramadhyāntabhavāni yāni \|*  
*varṇākṛtisparśarasaiḥ samāni tathaikato jātiratipracintyā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. As the fruit of the fig tree has the same information, colour, touch and the juice» similarly, a person after having been born of the same father, then the imagination of the caste in human is unjustifiable.

## \|\| 1.41.47-48 \|\|

*ye kauśikāḥ kāśyapagautamāśca kauṃḍinyamāṇḍavyavaśiṣṭhagotrāḥ \|*  
*ātreyakautsāṅgirasaḥ sagargā maudgalyakātyāyanabhārgavāśca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*gotrāṇi nānāvidhajātayaśca bhrātṛsnuṣāmaithunaputrabhāvāḥ \|*  
*vaivāhikaṃ karma na varṇabhedaḥ sarvāṇi śilpāni bhavanti teṣām \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. In this way, the Rishis like Kaushika, Kashyapa, Gautama, Kaundinya, Mandavya, Vasistha, Atreya, Kautsa, Angirasa, Garga, Maudgalya, Katyayana, besides of Bhargava gotra, brothers, daughters-in-law, Maithuna putra are the same and similar in the case with their marriages, beauty and complexion, besides the arts.

## \|\| 1.41.49-50 \|\|

*ye cānye2 paṇḍitāḥ prāhurdehabrāhmaṇatāṃ narāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ durdṛṣṭitimiramapanīyānukampya ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nyāyāñjanauṣadhairdivyaiḥ pariṇāmasukhāvahaiḥ \|*  
*upanītaḥ prayatnena sudṛṣṭiṃ saṃvidadmahe \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Though some learned people consider the body to be a Brahmana and claim that for their infested with darkness, the ointment that has been prepared by them to enable a person to view justice made by the mixture of the best medicines and bestows comfort to the users, are for curing their eyesight. Those who claim this are wrong.

## \|\| 1.41.51 \|\|

*dehādhāraniviṣṭānāṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ na prakalpyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Because the body has a definite figure and being subject to destruction, gets destroyed like the earth. Therefore, the body can never be claimed to be a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.41.52-53 \|\|

*ekaikovayavasteṣāṃ na brāhmaṇyaṃ samaśnute \|*  
*na cānekasamūhe'pi sarvathātiprasaṅgataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*pṛthivyudakavāyyagnipariṇāmaviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dehataḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ brāhmaṇatvaprasaṅgataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*
