52-53. Similarly, all the limbs of the body cannot be termed as the Brahmanas and this claim would be excessive, because all the bhutas (earth, water, wind, fire and the sky) make the body and in such a case, all the bhutas shall be called as Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.41.54 \|\|

*dehasya brāhmaṇatvaṃ yairatattvajñaiḥ prakalpyate \|*  
*saṃskartṝṇāṃ śarīrasya teṣāṃ na brahmatā bhavet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The ignorant people have accepted the body to be Brahmana. The person who performs the Samskaras cannot be claimed to be a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.41.55 \|\|

*mṛgyamāṇe prayatnena dehe tannopalabhyate \|*  
*tasmānna dehe brāhmaṇyaṃ nāpi dehātmakaṃ bhavet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Because even after making vigorous search with all the efforts, the Brahmanhood in a body could not be traced. Therefore, the body cannot be treated as a Brahmana. At the same time, Brahmanhood is not the form of the body.

## \|\| 1.41.56 \|\|

*varṇāpasadacāṃḍālaśvādādīnāṃ3 prasajyate \|*  
*yadi dehasya vipratvaṃ bhavadbhirupagamyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In such a situation, the degraded, the low caste ones, Chandalas, and those who consume the dog’s meat, would also be turned as those of the Brahmanas, in case you people keep insisting the body to be a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.41.57 \|\|

*dehaśaktiguṇaiḥ kṣīṇaiḥ kāyabhasmādirūpavat \|*  
*tasmāddehātmakenaitadbrāhmaṇyaṃ nāpi karmajam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Because the strength of the body and the virtues get destroyed and the body is reduced to ashes, therefore the Brahmanhood neither belongs to the body nor is it born out of the body.

## Chapter 42. The prudence of Brahmanas

## \|\| 1.42.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*aparaiśca sadācārayogayuktairmanīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*yadakāri mahāsattvaiḥ subhāṣitamidaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bahuvanaspatiśaṅkhapipīlikābhramaravāraṇajātimudāharan \|*  
*gatiṣu karmamito naṭavatsadā bhramati janturalabdhasudarśanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Brahma said — Such of the people who are noble souls, having good conduct, virtuous and immensely learned, who act as they speak out I am going to enlighten you about their beautiful words, you listen. They say that the jiva who could not have an audience with a noble person, takes his birth in several types of plants, besides conches, ants, bees, elephants and other creatures because of his past deeds.

## \|\| 1.42.3 \|\|

*rūpaiśvaryajñānakulairvibhavairvarmito bhūtvā dharmapathaṃ cedvijahāsi \|*  
*na vakṣye vrajanbhuvanāni tvamaṭiṣyaṃstasmādabhibhasmībhūte mada ātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Therefore, the beauty, complexion, fortunes, knowledge getting secured by magnanimity in case one does not follow the noble path of religion, then I can say that you would not have to wander through the downgraded people.

## \|\| 1.42.4 \|\|

*jātikularūpavayovarṇānekaśrutamadāndhāḥ klībāḥ \|*  
*paratra ceha ca hitamapyarthaṃ na paśyanti \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Because the caste, beauty, complexion, the age besides the arrogance of various types of prides, getting blinded like a eunuch, they hardly care for their welfare in this as well as the future world.

## \|\| 1.42.5 \|\|

*jñātvā bhavaparivarte jātīnāṃ koṭiśatasahasreṣu \|*  
*hīnottamamadhyatvaṃ ko jātimadaṃ budhaḥ kuryāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thus the world is a large pit, in the whirlpools of which hundreds and thousands of castes are drowning. Being aware of this fact, who is the person with wisdom, to become pride of his race or caste?

## \|\| 1.42.6 \|\|

*naikāñjātiviśeṣānindriyanivṛttipūrvakānsarvān \|*  
*karmavaśādgacchatyatra kasyaikā śāśvatī jātiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Such people are numerous, who having been born in the high race and their sense organs being satisfied, but because of their deeds they keep on coming in and going out from the world.

## \|\| 1.42.7 \|\|

*vidvatsadasi yo'pyāha saṃskārādbrāhmaṇo bhavan \|*  
*nyāyajñaiḥ1 sa nirākāryo vākyairnyāyānusāribhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The group of the learned people, which claims that one becomes a Brahmana by means of Samskaras alone, therefore, the judicious people contradict their ideology with their own ideas pertaining to morality and ethics.

## \|\| 1.42.8-10 \|\|

*garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*jātakarma nāmakarma tathānnaprāśanaṃ ca vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

*cūḍopanayanaṃ cāsya vratādeśastathaiva ca \|*  
*samāvartanamapyanyatpāṇigrahaṇameva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ityevamādisaṃskāravidhānairye'tisaṃskṛtāḥ \|*  
*ta eva brāhmaṇā yeṣāṃ nairantaryeṇa2 kāmanāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Because such of the people whose samskaras for conception, Pumsavana (ceremony performed in the third month of conception), Simanta (a ceremony performed during the fourth, sixth and eighth month of pregnancy), name giving ceremony, testing of food, showing of head, yajnopavita and start of Vedic studies, return of the disciple from the preceptor’s hermitage to his parental home, and the marriage ceremony are performed properly, they could be taken to be Brahmanas. But what about the people for whom these ceremonies have not been performed or those who indulge themselves in the degraded activities, how could they be called as the Brahmanas?

## \|\| 1.42.11 \|\|

*yasmādvai brāhmaṇā jātā brāhmaṇaiḥ kṛtasaṃskṛtaiḥ \|*  
*nāyuḥ śaktirhi kāntyādiviśeṣo vidyate sphuṭaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Similarly, no specialty is found in the progeny of the Brahmanas devoid of the Samskaras.

## \|\| 1.42.12 \|\|

*tau vā brāhmaṇagātrotthau saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtau narau \|*  
*iṣṭāniṣṭāptyanāptibhyāṃ na bhidyete parasparam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When two sons are born out of a Brahmana and Samskara for only one of them could be performed and the other one is without Samskaras, then it makes no difference in his getting or not getting something.

## \|\| 1.42.13 \|\|

*jñānādhyayanamīmāṃsā niyamendriyanigrahaiḥ \|*  
*vinā saṃskārayoge'pi puṃsaḥ śūdrānna bhinnatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Similarly, for a person without the Samskaras it makes no difference for him in achieving the knowledge, studies, philosophy, the rules and control of the sense organs.

## \|\| 1.42.14 \|\|

*saṃskāraḥ kriyamāṇaśca na śūdre ca pravartate \|*  
*saṃskṛtāṅgaśca1 pāpebhyo na paśyati nivartate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Though the Shudras are not required to go through the process of the Samskaras, still no sins are visible on the body of the people of high castes for whom the Samskaras have been performed.

## \|\| 1.42.15-16 \|\|

*vilāsinībhujaṃgādijanavanmadavihvalāḥ \|*  
*vyāmuhyanti sadācārādbrāhmaṇatvātpatanti3 ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*saṃskṛto'pi durācāro narakaṃ yāti mānavaḥ \|*  
*niḥsaṃskāraḥ sadācāro bhavedviprottamaḥ sadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Not only the lustful and wicked people getting blinded with arrogance, even the people with noble Samskaras are fallen from the noble path and Brahmanhood and fall in the hell inspite of their having performed all the Samskaras. On the other hand, the people without the Samskaras sometimes become the people with nobility or even the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.42.17 \|\|

*mantrapūtātmasaṃskārayukto'pi plavate na tu \|*  
*brāhmaṇyādavikalpaṃ sa paścādduścarito naraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Therefore, a person who is purified by the use of Mantras as well as the Samskaras, is overpowered by the delusion and confusion and getting deprived of the Brahmanhood, falls on the evil path forever.

## \|\| 1.42.18 \|\|

*sāmarthyātpatanaṃ tasmādbrāhmaṇyānmucyate dhruvam \|*  
*duranuṣṭhānasaktānāṃ puṃsāṃ puruṣapuṅgavaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. This is because the people who get involved in evil ways, getting blinded of their selfish motifs, are fallen as degraded ones. Thus they get themselves separated from the Brahmanhood.

## \|\| 1.42.19-20 \|\|

*kiṃ kvaciddṛṣṭamevaitatkiṃ vā spardhāvidatyayam \|*  
*tulyamutsahase kartumapyadṛṣṭaṃ tadā vada \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ācāramanuṣṭhinto vyāsādimunisattamāḥ \|*  
*garbhādhānādisaṃskārakalāparahitāḥ sphuṭam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Could you then notice the difference in the caste system or one talking all this out of jealousy? In case there be no specialty in the vision or otherwise, then it would be proper for you to say that “I have not witnessed the difference because the great sages like Vyasa, possessing good conduct and who was the best of all the Rishis, inspite of the fact that no Samskaras like conception or others were performed for him. This fact is quite clear.”

## \|\| 1.42.21 \|\|

*viprottamāḥ śriyaṃ prāptāḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtāḥ \|*  
*bahavaḥ kathyamānā ye katicittānnibodhata \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Among the great there were many who became adorable and respectable among the Brahmanas, the names of whom are being spoken by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.42.22-24 \|\|

*jāto vyāsastu kaivartyāḥ śvapākyāśca parāśaraḥ \|*  
*śukyāḥ śukaḥ kaṇādākhyastatholūkyāḥ suto'bhavat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mṛgījotharṣaśṛṅgopi vaśiṣṭho gaṇikātmajaḥ \|*  
*mandapālo4 muniśreṣṭho nāvikāpatyamucyate5 \|\| 23 \|\|*

*māṇḍavyo munirājastu maṇḍūkīgarbhasambhavaḥ \|*  
*bahavo'nye'pi vipratvaṃ prāptā ye pūrvavaddvijāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Vyasa was born of the daughter of a Kevata or a sailor. Parashara was born of a Chandala girl, Shuka was born of a parrot, Kanada from an owl, Rishi Shringi from a doe, Vasishtha from a whore, Mandapala from a quail, while Mandavya was born out of a female frog. Many such people attained the Brahmanhood and became Brahman as of high order.

## \|\| 1.42.25 \|\|

*yaccaitaccārucaritairarcyamuccaritaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tadvicāryācarannuccairācāropacitadyutiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then all these leaders who possessed beautiful character and whatever the respectable words have been spoken by these people, they should be followed by people and those who do so, surely become illustrious.

## \|\| 1.42.26-30 \|\|

*hariṇīgarbhasambhūta ṛṣyaśṛṅgo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tapasā brāhmaṇo jātaḥ saṃskārastena kāraṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śvapākīgarbhasambhūtaḥ pitā vyāsasya pārthiva \|*  
*tapasā brāhmaṇo jātaḥ saṃskārastena kāraṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ulūkīgarbhasambhūtaḥ kaṇādākhyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tapasā brāhmaṇo jātaḥ saṃskārastena kāraṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*gaṇikāgarbhasambhūto vaśiṣṭhaśca mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tapasā brāhmaṇo jātaḥ saṃskārastena kāraṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nāvikāgarbhasambhūto mandapālo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tapasā brāhmaṇo jātaḥ saṃskārastena kāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. Because Rishi Shringi, having been born out of the womb of a doe, achieved Brahmanhood on the strength of his tapas. Therefore, O king, Samskara plays a great role in achieving: Brahmanhood by a person. O king, similarly, Parashara — the father of Vyasa, was born out of the womb of a Chandala woman, Kanada from the womb of a female owl, the sage Vashishtha from the womb of a whore and the great sage Mandapala was born out of the womb of a quail. All of them achieved Brahmanhood on the strength of their tapas. Therefore, the Samskaras have their own importance.

## \|\| 1.42.31-32 \|\|

*vedatantrajasaṃskārakalāpanipuṇairapi \|*  
*vidyātapodhanabalādutkṛṣṭaṃ labhyate phalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*labdhasaṃskāradehāśca mahāpātakino narāḥ \|*  
*yasmānnivartate brahma tasmātsāṅketikaṃ viduḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The people, who are well-versed in the Vedic and the Tantrika Samskaras on the strength of their knowledge and tapas, they achieve excellence. But a person, not onto getting deprived of the Samskaras with his sinful ways, becomes a grave sinner and under these circumstances, he is fallen from the Brahmanhood. Therefore, the Brahmana caste should be treated as indicative or imaginary.

## Chapter 43. Arrangement of Varnas

## \|\| 1.43.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kiṃ cānyadaparaṃ yūyaṃ vedamantravido janāḥ \|*  
*praṣṭavyāḥ kasya saṃskāre viśeṣamupagacchata \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — The people who believe in the attainment of Brahmanhood by means of the Samskaras, (say) as to which particular Samskara leads one to attain the Brahmanhood.

## \|\| 1.43.2 \|\|

*kiṃ dehasyota yenāsau nisargamalinaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*śukraśoṇitasambhūtaḥ śamalodbhavakīṭavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Is it due to the body which emerges out of the excreta and refuse of semen like the worms?

## \|\| 1.43.3 \|\|

*niṣekādiśmaśānāntairvividhairvidhivistaraiḥ \|*  
*dehino'tiśayaṃ kecidupagacchanti mānavāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Or the Samskaras of the jiva starting from the conception to the carrying of the body to the cremation ground. In other words, some people believe that the performing of a Samskara leads one to achieve Brahmanhood.

## \|\| 1.43.4 \|\|

*teṣāṃ gūḍhamanaḥ kāyavāgviduṣṭaiḥ suceṣṭitaiḥ \|*  
*asaṃyatamanuṣyāṇāṃ pakṣo'yaṃ dūṣyate mayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The people having no control over their minds, their bodies and speech, always remain filled with wickedness. Their activities are full of blemishes. Therefore, I contradict their belief relating to the jiva.

## \|\| 1.43.5 \|\|

*vaidikākhilasaṃskārasārabhūtā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*sarvakāryakarānsarvānvṛṣalānatiśerate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas are the essence of the Vedic Samskaras, therefore all of them are considered to be superior to the Shudras who are engaged in low type of jobs.

## \|\| 1.43.6-9 \|\|

*caṇḍakarmā vikarmastho brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*steno goghnaḥ surāpāṇaḥ parastrīramaṇapriyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mithyāvādī madonmatto nāstiko vedanindakaḥ \|*  
*grāmayājakanirgranthau bahudoṣo durāsadaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ni1 ṣiddhācārasaṃsevī coraścāṭo madoddhataḥ \|*  
*dhūrto naṭaḥ śaṭhaḥ pāpī sarvāśī sarvavikrayī \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vāṅmanaḥ kāyajairduṣṭairhatā ye brāhmaṇādhamāḥ \|*  
*te na śuddhiṃ vrajantīha api yajñaśatairapi2 \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. But inspite of the performing of the Samskaras, the Brahmanas who are engaged in evil ways and indulged in killings and uniting with the wife of the preceptor, besides those who indulge in theft, killing of the cows, drinking, lustful, indulging in falsehood, intoxicated, disbelievers of the Vedas, denouncers of the Vedas, performing yajnas wandering in the villages, foolish, drunkards, unchaste and immoral, who indulge in falsehood, are arrogant, sinful in various ways, difficult to be overpowered, indulging in degraded activities and thefts, betrayers, who steal the riches, intoxicated, cheats, dancers, wicked, sinful, consumers of everything, sellers of everything, who are wicked of mind, speech and body, such Brahmanas cannot be purified even after performing of hundreds of the yajnas.

## \|\| 1.43.10 \|\|

*śūdrāṇāṃ yānyaniṣṭāni sampadyante svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*viprāṇāmapi tānyeva nirvighnāni bhavanti na \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Such of the tasks of the Shudras which do not get complete without obstruction, similarly the Brahmanas also unable to perform similar tasks without obstruction.

## \|\| 1.43.11 \|\|

*tasmānmantrognihotraṃ vā vedyāṃ paśuvadho'pi vā \|*  
*hetavo na hi vipratve śūdraiḥ śakyā kriyā yathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Therefore, even with the uttering of the mantras, worship of fire, performing of homa in the fire altar, offering of the animals as sacrifice, a Brahmana cannot achieve success in the same way as a Shudra making all the efforts to become successful, remains a Shudra.

## \|\| 1.43.12 \|\|

*ye cāpi karmabandhena baddhāḥ sīdanti jantavaḥ \|*  
*saṃsārānalasantāpaviklavīkṛtamānasāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The people who feel disturbed with the fire flames in the universe, having been held in bondage by the karmas, have to face the miseries.

## \|\| 1.43.13 \|\|

*te janmamaraṇāṭavyāṃ sukhāmṛtapipāsavaḥ \|*  
*kṛpaṇasyāśraye'ṭanto labhante naiva nirvṛtim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All of them always wander in the forest of the universe to fill the pitcher with nectar, like getting disappointed from the door of a miserly person, can never face comfort throughout their life.

## \|\| 1.43.14 \|\|

*caturvarṇā narā ye tu tattadvīrye narādhamāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sarvātmanā sarvairdharmaiḥ sāṅkaryamīkṣyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Therefore, all the humans of all the four varnas, they having been born out of the semen of one another, become degraded. In the performing of their religious activities, hybridity is visible.

## \|\| 1.43.15 \|\|

*śūdraviprādayo yonau na bhidyante parasparam \|*  
*sarvadharmasamānatvātsaṃskārādi nirarthakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There is no difference in the creation of a Brahmana and a Shudra, therefore in view of the equality of all the dharmas, the Samskaras are of no use.

## \|\| 1.43.16 \|\|

*tadanuṣṭhānavaidharmyaviyogamaraṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*asevyasevanairanyaiḥ śūdraviprādayaḥ samāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There is also a similarity in other spheres in the Brahmanas as well as the Shudras, like the performing of various religious functions, the birth and death as well as the consuming of the prohibited items of food etc.

## \|\| 1.43.17-30 \|\|

*buddhyā śaktyā svabhāvena dharmairjātyā1 dibhiḥ śriyā \|*  
*kartavyaiḥ puṇyapāpābhyāṃ śanaiḥ2 sarvaśarīragaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bandhanai rodhanairnānāyātanopāyapīḍanaiḥ \|*  
*daṇḍairadaṇḍakaraṇairviṣādaparivedanaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sāttvikaḥ pratidharmādyai rājasaiścitraveṣṭitaiḥ \|*  
*tāmasaistāpamohādyairdūyamānāḥ punaḥ1 punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śleśmamārutapittādyairmahābībhatsadarśanaiḥ \|*  
*kvacidvṛttinivṛttibhyāmamṛtānṛtahitāhitaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*alaṅkāropayogena manmathādyairviceṣṭitaiḥ \|*  
*dhanalābhāśayānaikajantusaṅghātapātanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*adhisiddhigatiṃ yāti nānāvidhamanorathaiḥ \|*  
*ātmasnehaparadveṣasvīkṛtadravarakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*atikṣībatvasaṃkṣobhakṣutakṣāmakṣamāmayaiḥ \|*  
*yātanopāyapaiśunyaśūnyatvopaśamaistathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*apraśastairanuṣṭhānaiḥ samīpasthāpadaḥ samāḥ \|*  
*hiṃsakāḥ prāṇinaḥ pāpavitathālāpabhāṣiṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sādhūnāṃbhāṣakāḥ stenā nirdayāḥ pāradārikāḥ \|*  
*nīcakarmasamācārāḥ sarvabhakṣāḥ piśācavat \|\| 25 \|\|*

*duṣkulīnā durācārā nṛpāṇāmupajīvinaḥ \|*  
*viprakāryā vikarmasthā dhanino duṣṭacetasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*lubdhakā hariṇānhatvā vāsaṃ kṛtvā yathā vane \|*  
*tathā khādanti piśunā bahavaśca3 kriyāvaśāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vedavādamadhīyānāḥ1 prāṇighātābhiśaṃsinaḥ \|*  
*puṣṇanti kapaṭairarthānvedavikrayiṇo'dhamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*māyino matsaragrastā lubdhā mugdhā madoddhatāḥ \|*  
*cāṭāḥ kārpaṭikāḥ kūrāḥ kadaryāḥ kalahapriyāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vācāṭaduṣṭakulaṭā aṭanto bhāṭakaiḥ saha \|*  
*bhaṇḍamānyā bhaṭāṭopaiḥ saṃkruddhāḥ suviluṇṭhakāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

17-30. Besides the deeds performed according to one’s wisdom, prowess, temperament, dharmas and castes or the good or bad deeds performed by them with their bodies, riches, performing of their duties, removal of bondages, or the pain caused by punishment by various means or the repentance, sufferings, their spiritual love in dharma or the activities which are caused by them due to rajoguna etc., or the sufferings caused by tamoguna or darkness, suffering again and again due to delusion, suffering from bilious cough, sometimes involvement or at times escaping, sometimes truth and at times falsehood, sometime benefit and at times the harm, to indulge in various types of activities getting decorated with excellent ornaments, getting overpowered with lust, to kill several creatures out of greed for wealth, to fulfill several types of desires, to extend lore and affection to one’s own kiths and kins and to be inimical with others, to protect one’s own riches by means of causing mental agony, hunger, thirst and other ailments or other painful means, to indulge in back-biting to min others by unfair means besides all other misfortunes which arrive (unwantedly) make the Brahmanas and the Shudras alike. Similarly, the terrific creatures, the sinners and those indulged in falsehood or the thieves who could at times speak noble words as well the merciless people, evil minded people or those indulging in evil activities or those who consume everything, like Pishachas, those who are born in the degraded races, those with evil conduct, the servants of the kings, those who oppose the people, those who always remain engaged in evil activities, rich, wicked, the forest dwellers or hunters who live killing the dear and consuming their meat and perform in various ways and the back biters cause destruction to many. The people who study the gist of the Vedas, or degraded people who advise for killing others, those who sell the Vedas and establish their task deceitfully, similarly the deceitful persons having been filled with jealousy, besides those who are greedy, lustful, intoxicated, treacherous, wearing the ochre coloured robes, cruel, quarrelsome, talkative, those who keep company of those born in evil race, those wandering with Bhairavas, the thieves who keep company with clowns of jesters out of vanity or arrogance and the enraged thieves.

## \|\| 1.43.31-33 \|\|

*paryaṭā bhāṭakā jīvāḥ kaṇṭhakaślokabhāṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*vikrīṇate hyavikreyamabhakṣyadravyabhakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śūdrakarmānutiṣṭhanto nistapāste narādhamāḥ \|*  
*sevādhyāpanavāṇijyakṛṣyādyārambhalambhitāḥ \|*  
*gṛhṇantaḥ sampado bāhayāddravyadhānyadhanādikāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*krodhādābhyantarāndoṣāṃstathā duṣṭamanorathān \|*  
*atyajanto viśiṣṭānāṃ śreṣṭhāste kacamardinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Those who wander making use of a vehicle on rent, those who arrogantly recite the verses they remember by heart or those who sell off the prohibited things and eat the prohibited food and other articles, such degraded people with their conduct, are fallen from their tapas like the Shudras. Similarly, the servants, teachers, professionals or those engaged in trade or those earning livelihood by farming, whatever is earned by them in the form of cereals or wealth or riches in any form which they earn from outside are accepted by them. Having been overpowered with enormous rage, they do not discard the sinful ways or the blemished intentions. They even while working are barbers and consider themselves as the best of all.

## \|\| 1.43.34 \|\|

*nopadeyāni vastrāṇi nityamādadate dvijāḥ \|*  
*hāpayanti na heyāni kathaṃ te guravaḥ kṣitau \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Therefore, a Brahmana, who embracing the evil ways or by the giving or taking of the clothes do not disown the things which are to be discarded, then how could he be respected in the world in the community of the Brahmanas?

## \|\| 1.43.35 \|\|

*dantikā diṇḍikā bhaṇḍāścaṇḍāścaṇḍālaceṣṭitā \|*  
*vaitaṇḍakāste nighnanti yathā siṃho mṛgānpaśūn \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Because of carrying a danda to beg on the tune of the musical instruments, to work with the jesters, to behave like a Chandala or the like, the quarrelsome persons keep on killing the humans like the lion killing the wild animals in the forest.

## \|\| 1.43.36 \|\|

*nirgranthaṃ munimālokya manyamānāḥ samunnatam \|*  
*paribhūyāvatiṣṭhante dhiktānriktānsavairiṇaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Those who think themselves to be great at the sight of an ascetic, have to face defeat. Disgrace to such people out of us, who unnecessarily develop enmity.

## \|\| 1.43.37 \|\|

*tasmātsaṃsārikāḥ sattvāścittakleśakalaṅkitāḥ \|*  
*dauḥśīlyadaurmanasyādyaistulyajātīyabandhanāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In this way, the jivas of the world, with the use of nobility, discarding of evil mindedness which are found in all the castes, remain disturbed.

## \|\| 1.43.38 \|\|

*śūdrāṃ prarocate vipro rāgiṇīṃ maithunaṃ prati \|*  
*sā kāmaduḥkhavigame garbhaṃ dhatte samāgame \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. As a Brahmana becomes desirous of a loving Shudra woman, the same woman after the subsiding of his passion, gets conceived.

## \|\| 1.43.39 \|\|

*kāmakāmāturābhyastu rocante śūdramānavāḥ \|*  
*maithunaṃ prati brāhmaṇye te'pi tāsāṃ sukhāvahāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, a lustful Brahmana woman becomes immensely desirous of a Shudra for uniting with him and he makes her comfortable. Therefore, Shudra too equates with a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.43.40 \|\|

*ye tu jātyādibhirbhinnā gavāśvoṣṭmataṅgajāḥ \|*  
*te vijātiṣu no garbhaṃ kurvate'pi sukhārthinaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. As the cow, horse, camel, elephant are all of different species, and even when they are desirous of some animal of others species, they cannot unite with them.

## \|\| 1.43.41-42 \|\|

*anaḍvāneva goreva kāmaṃ puṣṇāti saṅgame \|*  
*ghoṭakāśca ratiṃ samyakkurvate vaḍavāsu ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*patiṃ karabhamevāpya karabhī ramate mudā \|*  
*gajameva patiṃ labdhvā sukhaṃ tiṣṭhati hastinī \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Because the uniting of a bull with a cow delights both of them. Similarly, the horse enjoys uniting with a mare. The male camel enjoys company of a female camel, while a female elephant enjoys the company of her male elephant.

## \|\| 1.43.43 \|\|

*tiryagjātiḥ striyā sākaṃ kurvāṇā'pi hi maithunam \|*  
*na tasyāḥ kurute garbhaṃ naro nāpi sukhāsikām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Therefore, as by uniting with birds and animals, a woman cannot conceive, similarly a man, by uniting with birds and animals cannot conceive.

## \|\| 1.43.44 \|\|

*tiraścā saha kurvāṇā maithunaṃ manujāṅganā \|*  
*nādhatte tatkṛtaṃ garbhaṃ na yuktaṃ maithunaṃ tayoḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. While this is correct that a woman after her uniting with a bird or an animal cannot conceive, but such a type of union has not been allowed.

## \|\| 1.43.45 \|\|

*naivaṃ kaścidvibhāgosti maithune strīmanuṣyayoḥ \|*  
*yena saṃkṣīyate bhedaḥ prasphuṭaṃ dvijaśūdrayoḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore, there is hardly any difference between men or women by which a Shudra man or woman could be distinguished between the two castes.

## \|\| 1.43.46-49 \|\|

*vedapāṭhacchalenāyaṃ na kriyābhiḥ prapadyate \|*  
*bahubhirjaḍasaṅghātairaviśiṣṭe pade'hani \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dehe dehini cāmuṣminnaśucāvanavasthite \|*  
*rāgadveṣādibhirdoṣairadhikaṃ paripīḍite \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kulālacakravadbhrāntamānase viṣayārṇave \|*  
*ghoraduḥkhabhayākrānte samāje'nīśvarātmani \|\| 48 \|\|*

*janmamṛtyujarāśokāniṣṭayogāgnipīḍite \|*  
*hīnasattvaśarīrādau na viśeṣo vibhāvyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

46-49. Similarly, the caste cannot be distinguished by the study of the Vedas or any other activity. Because the body has been formed of several elements like earth and water etc., which is inauspicious as well as temporary. The body remains suffering due to love, jealousy and other blemishes which make the jiva to suffer. The difference in castes is therefore not possible. As in the ocean of worldly pleasures, a person keeps on rotating like the potter’s wheel. Similarly, in the atheist community which is suffering from birth and death, old age, grief and burning with fire as such, there is no specialty in the bodies of the humans.

## \|\| 1.43.50-52 \|\|

*tasmānmanuṣyabhedo'yaṃ saṅketabalanirmitaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ brāhmaṇāsaṅgādbrāhmaṇī copasevate \|\| 50 \|\|*

*patiṃ tyaktvā mukhasvādalālasairmadalālasaiḥ \|*  
*āsevyate viṭaṃ gatvā bandhakī ceṭakairapi \|\| 51 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇyātpracyavante'nye mahāpātakasevitāḥ \|*  
*vyalīkakalpanaivaiṣā tasmājjātyādikalpanā \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. Therefore, with the imagination of castes in human beings, even when a Brahmana woman remains chaste and she is known as a Brahmana woman, but because of the taste of the tongue or in arrogance, discarding the husband becomes desirous of another man becoming unchaste, then after her uniting with servants and other people, she falls from Brahmanhood. Therefore, the imagination of Brahmana or Kshatriya is surely false imagination.

## Chapter 44. Prudence of the Varna’s division

## \|\| 1.44.1-7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*heyopādeyatattvajñāstyaktānyāyapathāgamāḥ \|*  
*jitendriyamanovācaḥ sadācāraparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*niyamācāravṛttasthā hitānveṣaṇatatparāḥ \|*  
*saṃsārarakṣaṇopāyakriyāyuktamanorathāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*samyagdarśanasampannāḥ samādhisthā hatakrudhaḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyabhaktahṛdayāstyaktasaṅgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*viśokā vimadāḥ śāntā sarvaprāṇihitaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sukhaduḥkhasamālokā viviktasthānavāsinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vratopayuktasarvāṅgā dhārmikāḥ pāpabhīravaḥ \|*  
*nirmamā nirahaṅkārā dānaśūrā dayāparāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*satyabrahmavidaḥ śāntā sarvaśāstreṣu niṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*sarvalokahitopāyapravṛttena svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vāgīśvareṇa devena nābheyena bhavacchidā \|*  
*brahmaṇā kṛtamaryādāsta evaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Brahma said — What is to be discarded and what is to be accepted, a Brahmana should have a complete knowledge of the same and the one who is well-versed in the same, should discard the evil path, should control sense organs, exercise command over the mind and speech, and observe noble conduct. He is following the discipline and more for the welfare of others. He should be enthusiastic in doing welfare of others and perform meditation for attaining the knowledge of tattvas. He should discard anger, should be engaged in studies and devoid of attraction and jealousy, grief and arrogance. He should be peaceful and engaged for the welfare of all the creatures. He should evenly face pleasure and pain and embrace solitude, perform vratas mentally as well as physically, religious mined, without attraction, fearful of committing sins, devoid of pride, giver of charities, merciful, possess the truthful knowledge of Brahman, besides being well — read in all the scriptures. Only such of the disciplined people who within limits, are engaged for the good of all, has been termed as the Brahmanas by the self-born Brahma, the lord of speech, born of the navel and destroyer of Bhava.

## \|\| 1.44.8 \|\|

*mahātapodhanairāryaiḥ sarvasattvābhayapradaiḥ \|*  
*sarvalokahitārthāya nipuṇaṃ supratiṣṭhitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, Arya — the great ascetic who bestows protection to all the creatures, for the welfare of all the people, firmly decided this tradition.

## \|\| 1.44.9 \|\|

*vṛhattvādbhagavānbrahmā nābheyastasya ye janāḥ \|*  
*bhaktyāsaktāḥ prapannāśca brāhmaṇāste prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus inspite of his being so great, Brahma having been born out of the navel of the great Purusha — Vishnu, is known as Nabheya and such of the people who are devoted to him, are known as the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.44.10 \|\|

*kṣatriyāstu kṣatatrāṇādvaiśyā vārtāpraveśanāt \|*  
*ye tu śruterdrutiṃ prāptāḥ śūdrāsteneha kīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Similarly, the Kshatriyas protect others from destruction, the Vaishya are so called because they are engaged in farming or trade like professions. Those who run away from the study of the Vedas are called the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.44.11 \|\|

*ye cācāraratāḥ prāhurbrāhmaṇyaṃ brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*te tu phalaṃ praśaṃsanti yatsadā manasepsitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The people with noble conduct and possessing the knowledge of Brahman are known as Brahmanas. Their activities which are conducive to the performance of the noble people are always praised.

## \|\| 1.44.12-15 \|\|

*kṣamā damo dayā dānaṃ satyaṃ śaucaṃ dhṛtirghṛṇā \|*  
*mārdavārjavasantoṣānahaṅkāratapaḥśamāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dharmo jñānamapaiśunyaṃ brahmacaryamamūḍhatā \|*  
*dhyānamāstikyamadveṣo vairāgyaṃ ca śamātmatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pāpabhīrutvamasteyamamātsaryamatṛṣṇatā \|*  
*naiḥsaṅgyaṃ guruśuśrūṣā manovākkāya saṃyamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ya evambhūtamācāramanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ puṣkalaṃ teṣāṃ nityameva pravardhate \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Therefore, forgiveness, control of sense organs, mercy, giving of charities, truth, purity, patience, faith, sweetness, simplicity, patience, lack of arrogance, performing of tapas, self-control, quietness, dharma, knowledge, not to indulge in back biting, observing of Brahmacharya, possessing of learnings, meditation, believe in god, lack of jealousy, believing in the heaven or hell etc., lack of enmity, Vairagya, fear of sins, theft, to avoid desires and greed, besides those who serve the preceptors renouncing the world, who have controlled the mind and speech, as well as the body, such noble people always preserve in them enough of Brahmateja, which always keeps on increasing.

## \|\| 1.44.16 \|\|

*te svamatāsvādalabdhavarṇācārā mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*sarvaśāstrāvirodhena pavitrīkṛtamānasāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Such people attaining the varna as well as good conduct, become immensely illustrious and their minds become completely purified with the auspicious feelings of the Shastras.

## \|\| 1.44.17-18 \|\|

*sajjanābhimatāḥ prājñāḥ purāṇāgamapaṇḍitāḥ \|*  
*gītagītāgamācārāḥ smṛtikārāḥ paṭhanti ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*manvantareṣu sarveṣu caturyugavibhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramācārakṛtaṃ karma siddhyatyanuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Coming in contact with the noble people, they have become learned, besides being well-read in the Vedas and the Puranas, well — versed in the Gita and the creators of the fortunes. Such people say that with the division of four yugas in all the Manvantaras, following varna and ashrama one achieves the best of success.

## \|\| 1.44.19 \|\|

*saṃsiddhāyāṃ tu vārtāyāṃ tatasteṣāṃ svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*maryādāṃ sthāpayāmāsa yathārabdhaṃ parasparam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Therefore, after the success in efforts, Brahma established the limitations or maryada, which was mutually decided.

## \|\| 1.44.20-21 \|\|

*ye vai parigṛhītārasteṣāṃ sattvabalādhikāḥ \|*  
*itareṣāṃ kṣatatrāṇānsthāpayāmāsa kṣatriyān \|\| 20 \|\|*

*upatiṣṭhanti ye tānvai yācanto narmadāḥ sadā \|*  
*satyabrahma sadābhūtaṃ vadanto brāhmaṇāstu te \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Because of their being immensely strong in order to patronize the people and in order to save them from destruction, those who would work for people’s safety shall be known as Kshatriyas. Those who reaching the Kshatriyas, demand after pleasing them and propagate about the everlasting nature of Brahman, they would be known as the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.44.22-23 \|\|

*ye cānyepyabalāsteṣāṃ vaiśyakarmaṇi saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*kīlāni nāśayanti sma pṛthivyāṃ prāgatandritāḥ \|*  
*vaiśyāneva tu tānāha kīnāśānvṛttimāśritān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śocantaśva dravantaśca paricaryāsu ye narāḥ \|*  
*nistejaso'lpavīryāśca śūdrāṃstānabravīttu saḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Those who are weak and are engaged in the duties of Vaishya such as deep irrigation on earth, besides trading, they are known as Vaishyas. Such Vaishyas, inspite of their miserable condition, serve all the three varnas. Besides those who are weak and devoid of lustre, they are called as Shudras.

## \|\| 1.44.24 \|\|

*brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parasparam \|*  
*karmāṇi pravibhaktāni syabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus, the functions of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and the Shudras are totally different, based on their respective virtues.

## \|\| 1.44.25 \|\|

*śamastapo damaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāṃtirārjavameva ca \|*  
*jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Therefore, the natural activities of Brahmanas include peaceful nature, performing of tapas, self restraint, purity, patience, simplicity, knowledge, Vijnana and belief in god. These are the natural activities of the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.44.26 \|\|

*śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam \|*  
*dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Cruelty and cleverness in war, not to flee from the battle and gaining importance are the natural functions of the Kshatriyas.

## \|\| 1.44.27 \|\|

*kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam \|*  
*paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The fanning, the protections of cows and business are the functions of Vaishyas, while to serve others is the natural function of a Shudra.

## \|\| 1.44.28 \|\|

*yogastapo dayā dānaṃ satyaṃ dharmaśrutirghṛṇā \|*  
*jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyametadbrāhmaṇalakṣaṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thus, the performing of yoga, tapas, compassion, charities, truth, religious studies, hate, knowledge and belief in god are the symptoms of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.44.29 \|\|

*śikhā jñānamayī yasya pavitraṃ ca tapomayam \|*  
*brāhmaṇyaṃ puṣkalaṃ tasya manuḥ svāyambhuvo'bravīt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The one who possesses the tuft of the knowledge and the purity of the tapas, he is declared as the chief Brahmana by Manu.

## \|\| 1.44.30 \|\|

*yatra vā tatra vā varṇe uttamādhamamadhyamāḥ \|*  
*nivṛttaḥ pāpakarmebhyo brāhmaṇaḥ sa vidhīyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Accordingly, in a particular varna, none of the excellent, medium type or the lowest of the person does not indulge into sinful ways, he is said to be a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.44.31 \|\|

*śūdro'pi śīlasampanno brāhmaṇādadhiko bhavet \|*  
*brāhmaṇo vigatācāraḥ śūdrāddhīnataro bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Because a Shudra with a noble temperament has been declared to be better than a Brahmana and Brahmana who has fallen from the noble path, has been said to be equivalent to a Shudra.

## \|\| 1.44.32 \|\|

*na surāṃ sandhayedyastu āpaṇeṣu gṛheṣu ca \|*  
*na vikrīṇāti ca tathā sacchūdro hi sa ucyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Similarly, a person who does not store wine in his house or at the shop, he is said to be a touchable Shudra.

## \|\| 1.44.33 \|\|

*yadyekā sphuṭameva jātiraparā kṛtyātparaṃ bhedinī \|*  
*yadvā vyāhṛtirekatāmadhigatā yaccānyadharmaṃ yayau \|*  
*ekaikākhilabhāvabhedanidhanotpattisthitivyāpinī \|*  
*kiṃ nāsau pratipattigocarapathaṃ yāyādvibhaktyā nṛṇām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Therefore, it has been clearly ordained that human race is one but the division of the castes has been based on the distribution of the respective duties or in other words, the human race is one and the difference is only in dharma. Therefore, complete feelings and variations are the birth and death. The human race is involved in these variations and is unable to visualize the truth and the people get ready to divide the race into Brahmanas, Kshatriyas etc.

## Chapter 45. Description of Karttikeya

## \|\| 1.45.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*idaṃ śruṇu mayākhyātaṃ tarkapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ saṃśaye jāte kṛte vai jātikarmaṇoḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — Listen to my words of reasoning, which will remove the doubt about the caste and the activities.

## \|\| 1.45.2 \|\|

*punarvacmi nibodhadhvaṃ samāsānna tu vistarāt \|*  
*saṃsiddhiṃ yānti manujā jātikarmasamuccayāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I shall not speak in detail, but quite briefly. Therefore, all of you should listen to me with attention. A person attains success because of his caste and the activity.

## \|\| 1.45.3 \|\|

*siddhiṃ gacchedyathā kāryaṃ daivakarmasamuccayāt \|*  
*evaṃ saṃsiddhimāyāti puruṣo jātikarmaṇoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. As the success is achieved with the divine strength and the combination of it with the deeds, similarly with the combination of the caste and deeds, a person achieves success.

## \|\| 1.45.4 \|\|

*ityevamuktavānpūrvaṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ bodhane purā \|*  
*yogīśvaro mahātejāḥ samāsānna tu vistarāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In order to educate his disciples, the immensely illustrious Yogeshvara had briefly spoken these words.

## \|\| 1.45.5 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭaḥ purā brahmā ṛṣīnprovāca bhārata \|*  
*savitarkamidaṃ vākyaṃ viprarṣe jātikarmaṇoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Sumantu said — O Bharata, having been questioned by the Brahma. had informed them similarly that O Brahmana Rishi! The discussion of caste and performance is full of reasoning.

## \|\| 1.45.6 \|\|

*tasmāttvayā mahābāho na kāryo vismayo nṛpa \|*  
*kārtikeyaṃ prati sadā devānāṃ durvidā gatiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O large armed one, you should have no doubt about Karttikeya, because the movement of the divine beings are beyond comprehension.

## Chapter 46. Kartikeya Mahatmya

## \|\| 1.46.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*yeyaṃ bhādrapade māsi ṣaṣṭhī ca bharatarṣabha \|*  
*supuṇyeyaṃ pāpaharā śivā śāntā guhapriyā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O Bharata, the sixth moon day of the month of Bhadrapada is destroyer of sins and bestower of boons and merits. It is the favourite of Karttikeya.

## \|\| 1.46.2-3 \|\|

*snānadānādikaṃ sarvaṃ yasyāmakṣayyamucyate \|*  
*ye'syāṃ paśyanti gāṅgeyaṃ dakṣiṇāpathamāśritam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*brahmahatyādibhiḥ pāpairmucyante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmādasyāṃ sadā paśyetkārttikeyaṃ nṛpottama \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Therefore, the bathing and donations performed during the moon day, bestow the everlasting reward. The people who have an audience with Karttikeya and who earned his glory in the southern region, they are relieved of all the grave sins like killing of cows and others. O best of the rulers, one must have an audience with Karttikeya during this moon day.

## \|\| 1.46.4 \|\|

*pūjayanti guhaṃ ye'syāṃ narā bhaktisamanvitāḥ \|*  
*prāpyeha te sukhānkāmāngacchantīndrasalokatām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thus a person, who during this moon day, adore Karttikeya with faith and devotion, all his desired tasks are fulfilled and he finally achieves Indraloka.

## \|\| 1.46.5 \|\|

*yastu kārayate veśma sudṛḍhaṃ supratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*dārvaṃ śailamayaṃ cāpi bhaktayā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*gāṅgeyaṃ yānamāruhya gacchedgāṅgeyasadma vai \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Besides the people who build the beautiful temple of Karttikeya with wood and other material, they, riding over the vehicle of Karttikeya, travel to his place.

## \|\| 1.46.6 \|\|

*sammārjanādi yaḥ karma kuryādguhagṛhe naraḥ \|*  
*dhvajasyāropaṇaṃ rājansa gacchedrudrasadma vai \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those who clean the temple of Karttikeya and decorate the same with a flag, they achieve the place of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.46.7 \|\|

*candanāgarukarpūrairyaśca pūjayate guham \|*  
*gajāśvarathayānāḍhyaṃ saināpatyamavāpnute \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly, those who worship Karttikeya offering sandalpaste, guggulu and camphor, they getting the vehicles of elephants, horses, chariots and other types of vehicles, become the chiefs of the army of gods.

## \|\| 1.46.8-10 \|\|

*rājñāṃ pūjyaḥ sadā proktaḥ kārtikeyo mahīpate \|*  
*kārttikeyamṛte nānyaṃ rājñāṃ pūjyaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saṅgrāmaṃ gacchamāno yaḥ pūjayetkṛttikāsutam \|*  
*sa śatruṃ jayate vīra yathendro dānavānraṇe \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjayecchaṅkārātmajam \|*  
*pūjamānastu taṃ bhaktyā campakairvividhairnṛpa \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyastadā gacchecchivālayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Therefore, the rulers should always worship Karttikeya, because there is none else except Karttikeya to be adored by them. Thus worshipping Karttikeya, a warrior who approaches the battlefield, he achieves victory over the demons, like Indra. Therefore, Karttikeya — the son of Shiva, should always be worshipped. O king, making use of jasmine and other flowers, when a person worships Karttikeya, he getting relieved of all the sins, finally achieves the place of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.46.11 \|\|

*tailaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ na bhuñjīta na divā kurunandana \|*  
*yastu ṣaṣṭhyāṃ naro naktaṃ kuryāddhi bharatarṣabha \|*  
*sarvapāpaiḥ sa nirmukto gāṅgeyasya sado vrajet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O best of the race of Bharata, O son of Kuru race! During the sixth moon day, the food cooked in oil should not be taken because a person fasting on the sixth moon day at the night time, he getting relieved of all the sins achieves the place of Karttikeya.

## \|\| 1.46.12 \|\|

*trikṛtvo dakṣiṇāmāśāṃ gatvā yaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayeddevadeveśaṃ sa gacchecchāntimandiram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A person, who with devotion, going towards the southern direction worships Karttikeya, he achieves the place of Shiva.

## Chapter 47. Shaka-Saptami Vrata

## \|\| 1.47.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*saptamyāṃ sopavāsastu naktāhāro'pi vā bhavet \|*  
*saptamyāṃ devadevena labdhaṃ svaṃ rūpamādarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — During the seventh moon day of fortnight, one should observe a fast during the day or the night, because in this particular moon day, the Sun-god had achieved his illustrious form.

## \|\| 1.47.2-3 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃsthāpya svāṃ bhāryāmapatyāni tathaiva ca \|*  
*ājagāma sakāśaṃ vai dakṣasyāha ca kāraṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nāmnā rūpeti rūpeṇa nānyā nārī tathā 1 bhavet \|*  
*aṇḍastha eva suciraṃ sthito mārtaṇḍa ityataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. He was initially born with an egg. Then remaining in the egg, he had achieved the excellent knowledge. Under the same conditions, Daksha Prajapati had married his daughter named Rupa, having no parallel in the world to the Sun-god as his wife. Because of his stay inside the egg for a long time, he came to be known as Martanda.

## \|\| 1.47.4 \|\|

*dakṣājñayā viśvakarmā vapurasya prakāśayan \|*  
*prakāśatastato nāma tasya jātaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*aṇḍasthasyaiva sañjāto yamunā yama eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O lord of the humans, at the command of Daksha, Vishvakarma illuminated the body of the Sun, which earned him the name of Surya. Still, while remaining in the egg, he produced two children from his wife, known as Yamuna and Yama.

## \|\| 1.47.5-6 \|\|

*dākṣāyaṇī tasya bhāryā vairāgyāttanumadhyamā \|*  
*cintayāmāsa sā devī duḥkhānnirvedamāgatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aho tejomayaṃ rūpaṃ kāntaṃ kāntasya kāntimat \|*  
*na cāsya kiñcitpaśyāmi aṅgaṃ tejovimohitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Once his wife known as Dakshayani with slender waist, developed detachment due to some painful situation, she thought that she was unable to visualize the pleasant and illustrious form of her husband which has been absorbed in him because of his being illustrious.

## \|\| 1.47.7 \|\|

*śubhaṃ kanakatulyaṃ me rūpaṃ kāntaṃ sukāntimat \|*  
*sāmprataṃ śyāmatāṃ yātaṃ dagdhametasya tejasā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. My enormous beauty like the gold has been elapsed because of his lustre, turning blackish.

## \|\| 1.47.8 \|\|

*tasmāttapsye tapaścāhaṃ gatvā vai uttarānkurūn \|*  
*svāṃ chāyāmatra nikṣipya bhayācchāpasya rūpiṇī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Therefore, getting afraid of a curse, it would not be proper for me to desert him (the Sun). It would, therefore, be better, in case I leave my shadow here, to serve him and let me myself go to Uttara Kuru country, where I should perform tapas.

## \|\| 1.47.9-10 \|\|

*nikṣipyovāca tāṃ bālāṃ mā cāsmai vai vadiṣyasi \|*  
*evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā gatā vai uttarānkurūn \|\| 9 \|\|*

*svarūpaṃ tatra nikṣipya vaḍavārūpadhāriṇī \|*  
*cacāra sā mṛgaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahūnvarṣagaṇānnṛpa \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Having this resolve, she entrusted the care of the Sungod to her shadow and said to her — “This secret should not be revealed to anyone else.” Thus keeping her shadow there, she went to Uttara Kuru country. Reaching there, she took to the form of a mare and started wandering in the forest with other animals. O king, thus by her living in the forest with other animals, many years passed.

## \|\| 1.47.11 \|\|

*asāvapi ca mārtaṇḍaśchāyāṃ bhāryāmamanyat \|*  
*śaniṃ ca tapatīṃ caiva dve apatye ca jajñivān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Sun-god on the other hand, being unaware of the secret, took Chaya to be his own wife and produced two children named &ani as well as Tapati from her.

## \|\| 1.47.12-13 \|\|

*atha cchāyātmāpatyāni snehena paripālayet \|*  
*nātisnehena cāpaśyadyamunāṃ yamameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*atha tābhyāṃ vivādo'bhūdādityaduhitrordvayoḥ \|*  
*te ubhe vivadantyau tu parasparamasammatam \|*  
*yamunā tapatī cobhe nimnage sambabhūvatuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Chaya on the other hand, brought up her own children with loving care, but neglected Yama and Yamuna. After the lapse of sometime, there arose a quarrel between Yamuna and Tapati — the two daughters of Suryadeva and in great rage, both of them took to the form of two rivers.

## \|\| 1.47.14-17 \|\|

*yamo'pi yamunābhrātā chāyayā tāḍito bhṛśam \|*  
*pādamudyamya tasyā vai tasthau sammukha eva saḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*chāyā śaśāpa taṃ roṣādyasmātpādodyato mama \|*  
*tasmātte karma bībhatsaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇahiṃsanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati ciraṃ mūḍha ācandrārkaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*pādaṃ ca yadi bhūmau tvamimaṃ saṃsthāpayiṣyasi \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṛmayo bhakṣayiṣyanti macchāpakaluṣīkṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Thereafter, Yamuna’s brother, when she v/as so beaten by her step mother, went to his step mother and was about to kick her in anger. At this, Chaya getting enraged, cursed him — “You raised your foot to kick me therefore, this degraded action on your part would amount to the killing of innocent creatures. Therefore, O fool, till such time the sun and the moon exist, due to my curse, your foot with which you intended to kick me would be eaten up by worms, in case you place it on earth.

## \|\| 1.47.18 \|\|

*teṣāṃ vivadamānānāṃ mārtaṇḍo'bhyāgamattataḥ \|*  
*yamo'pyāha mahātmānaṃ mārtaṇḍaṃ lokapāvanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus when both of them were so quarreling, Martanda — the Sungod, reached there. Then Yama started speaking to Martanda, who purifies the world.

## \|\| 1.47.19 \|\|

*tāta nityamiyaṃ cāpi krūrabhāvena paśyati \|*  
*na cāsyāḥ susamā dṛṣṭirasmāsvastīti lakṣyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “O father, she (the mother) took at me with an evil eye. She does not treat us as her own children. This is well known to me.

## \|\| 1.47.20 \|\|

*provācātha sa tāṃ chāyāṃ mārtaṇḍo bhṛśakopanaḥ \|*  
*1 same apatye kiṃ mūḍhe samatvaṃ nānupaśyasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter, Martanda also getting enraged» spoke to Chaya — “O foolish lady, since all the children are equal they should be treated well equally. Why don’t you extend equal treatment to all?”

## \|\| 1.47.21 \|\|

*yamaḥ provāca pitaraṃ neyaṃ mātā pitarmama \|*  
*mātuśchāyā tviyaṃ pāpā śapto'hamanayā pitaḥ \|*  
*yamunā tapatī vṛttaṃ tatsarvaṃ vinyavedayat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Yama said — “O father, this is not my mother, on the other hand this sinful one is the shadow of my mother. This is the reason for her pronouncing a curse on me. Thereafter, he also narrated the story of Yamuna and Tapati.

## \|\| 1.47.22 \|\|

*atha provāca mārtaṇḍo mā te pādo mahītale \|*  
*māṃsaṃ rudhiramādāya kṛmayo yāntu bhūtalam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereafter, Martanda said to Yama — “Your foot will not touch the earth and on the contrary, the worm with blood and flesh shall go cm earth.

## \|\| 1.47.23 \|\|

*yamunāyāśca yattoyaṃ gaṅgātulyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*narmadāyāstapatyāśca samaṃ puṇyena vai dvija \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The water of Yamuna would resemble the water of the Ganga, while the water of Tapati would be pure like the water of Narmada.

## \|\| 1.47.24 \|\|

*vindhyasya dakṣiṇeneha tapatī pravahiṣyati \|*  
*tatsāyujyatayā sāgraṃ gaṅgā yāsyati śobhanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The river Tapati would flow to the south of Vindhya mountain and the Ganga would flow with water of Tapati.

## \|\| 1.47.25 \|\|

*gaṅgāmāsādya yamunā gaṅgā saiva bhaviṣyati \|*  
*saurasaumye ubhe puṇye sarvapāpapraṇāśane \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With the confluence of Yamuna with Ganga, Yamuna would also take the form of the Ganga. Both of them would become auspicious and destroyer of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.47.26 \|\|

*1 saurī ca vaiṣṇavī cobhe mahāpāpabhayāpahe \|*  
*tvaṃ putra lokapālatvaṃ brahmaṇo'jñāṃ sabhājayan \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti cchāyeyaṃ svadehasthā bhaviṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In this way, Yama born of Surya and Ganga born of Vishnu would collectively, destroy the grave sins. O son, at the command of Brahma, you would become a Lokapala and the Chaya in her position, would henceforth merge in the body.

## \|\| 1.47.27-28 \|\|

*dakṣo vijñāya tatsarvaṃ mārtaṇḍamidamāha vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rūpaṃ na paśyatī tubhyaṃ sā bhāryā uttarāngatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Thus the Sungod properly made arrangements for his children and wife Chaya, and went to the place of Yaksha and narrated to him the entire episode. Then Daksha said to the Sungod — “Because of your excessive lustre, your wife could not visualize your true form and had left for Uttara Kuru country.

## \|\| 1.47.29 \|\|

*rūpaṃ te prakaṭiṣyāmi yadi śakṣyasi vedanām \|*  
*asau provāca śakṣye'haṃ prakāśī kuru me vapuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In case you are able to bear the pain, then I can separate your lustre from your body.” On hearing this, the Sungod agreed to act accordingly.

## \|\| 1.47.30 \|\|

*atha sasmāra takṣāṇaṃ smṛta evājagāma saḥ \|*  
*provāca dakṣastakṣāṇaṃ mārtaṇḍaṃ vai prakāśaya \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereafter, Vishvakarma was remembered who arrived there. Then Daksha asked him to illuminate the lustre of the sun.

## \|\| 1.47.31 \|\|

*takṣā provāca mārtaṇḍaṃ vedanā visahiṣyase \|*  
*visahiṣyetha provāca takṣāṇaṃ dakṣacoditaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Vishvakarma said to Surya — “You would agree to bear this type of pain?" Daksha said — “He has already agreed to bear the pain.”

## \|\| 1.47.32 \|\|

*atha takṣā prakāśaṃ vai tasya rūpaṃ vibhāvasau \|*  
*mukhādārabhya pādāntaṃ tatakṣakaraṇaiḥ svakaiḥ \|*  
*kiraṇaistudyamāneṣu tasyāṅgeṣu punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇekṣaṇe mūrchayati mārtaṇḍo vedanāturaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thereafter, Vishvakarma making use of his weapons, chiseled out the entire body of the Sun from head to feet. But while chiseling out the body, the Sungod often fainted due to the pain.

## \|\| 1.47.33-34 \|\|

*tasya śāpabhayāttakṣā pādau gulphādiyāvataḥ \|*  
*cakārātho nirākārā aṅgulyo na prakāśayat \|\| 33 \|\|*

*paryāptaṃ takṣakarmedaṃ vedanā mama bādhate \|*  
*takṣā provāca mārtaṇḍaṃ vedanāṃ jahi gopate \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Getting afraid of the curse from the Sungod, Vishvakarma then chiseled his heels of the feet. When he was about to chisel the toes, the Sungod felt unbearable pain and became upset The Sungod said — “Stop it, enough is enough, I am feeling extremely painful.”

## \|\| 1.47.35-37 \|\|

*karavīrasya puṣpāṇi raktacandanameva ca \|*  
*karādārabhya gātrāṇi vilimpe dehajāni te \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tattatkṛtaṃ tathā tena sa rujaṃ tyaktavānraviḥ \|*  
*ataścemāni ceṣṭāni mārtaṇḍasyeha bhūpate \|\| 36 \|\|*

*karavīrasya puṣpāṇi tathā vai raktacandanam \|*  
*idamāha purā devo hyanūroragrato nṛpa \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. The Vishvakarma said— “Don’t worry, I shall plaster your body with the paste of red sandal and oleander flowers, which will subside your pain.” After so doing by Vishvakarma, the pain of Sun’s body got subsided. O monarch, therefore, these things gained favour with the Sungod. O king, in earlier times also, the Sungod had spoken about these things.

## \|\| 1.47.38-40 \|\|

*karavīrasya puṣpāṇi raktacandanameva hi \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ suparṇaguggulaṃ tathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yaḥ prayacchati me bhaktyā sa me prāṇānprayacchati \|*  
*tasmānna deyamanyanme bhaktiyuktena jānatā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*mārtaṇḍasyāṇḍajaṃ tejo gṛhītvā kila bhārata \|*  
*cakāra vajramajaraṃ 1 śatrulekhādināśanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. The oleander flowers, the red sandal paste, medicinal tree (Naga keshara) which are well known in the Vedas as well as the historical animals and guggulu when offered to me with devotion, it amounts to restoring life in me. Thus knowing fully well about them nothing else should be offered to me, because while chiseling the body of Martanda, his lustre was turned into a stiff and hard vajra, which could destroy the enemies.

## \|\| 1.47.41-42 \|\|

*mārtaṇḍaḥ parituṣṭo'bhūllabdhvā rūpaṃ gatavyathaḥ \|*  
*jagāma sa kurūnvegātsvabhāryādarśanotsukaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*mṛgamadhyagatāṃ dṛṣṭvā vaḍavārūpadhāriṇīm \|*  
*aśvarūpaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā svabhāryāmadhiruhya saḥ \|*  
*avāsṛjatsvakaṃ tejo vegenāruhya so'śvavat \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. That Martanda recovering himself from painful situation, felt extremely happy with the improved beauty of his body. At once, he developed an idea to have an audience with his wife. He at once proceeded to the Uttara Kuru country. He found his wife grazing in the form of a mare surrounded by the flocks of deer. The Sungod then took to the form of a horse and threw his lustre at her.

## \|\| 1.47.43 \|\|

*parapuruṣāśaṅkayā sā sthitā devasya saṃmukhī \|*  
*tejo nāsāpuṭābhyāṃ tu yugapatsākṣipatpunaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. His wife who was standing before him, taking him to be a stranger, at once emitted the lustre at once out of her both the nostrils.

## \|\| 1.47.44 \|\|

*tatra jātau devabhiṣajau nāsatyāvaśvināviti \|*  
*retaso'nte tu revanto virocanasuto mahān \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. As a result of this, two sons known as Ashvinikumaras were born, who functioned as the physicians of the gods. Thereafter, an illustrious son named Shveta was born to.

## \|\| 1.47.45 \|\|

*tapatī śaniśca sāvarṇiśchāyāpatyāni vai viduḥ \|*  
*yamunā yamaśca pūrvoktau saṃjñā 2 yāśca tathātmajau \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus, Tapati, Shani and Savarni were born to Chaya, while Yamuna and Yama were born to Samjna.

## \|\| 1.47.46 \|\|

*bhāryā labdhā vapurdivyaṃ tathā putrāśca bhārata \|*  
*saptamyāṃ devadevasya sarvamevamidaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*anena kāraṇeneṣṭā sadā devasya saptamī \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Bharata, the seventh moon day of the month, bestowed the Sungod the wife, son and the beautiful body. Therefore, the seventh moon day is favourite of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.47.47-49 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ sopavāsastu rātrau bhuñjīta yo naraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvopavāsaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu pañcamyāmekakālabhuk \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dattvā susaṃskṛtaṃ śākaṃ bhakṣyabhojyaiḥ samanvitam \|*  
*devāya brāhmaṇebhyaśca rātrau bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yāvajjīvaṃ naraḥ kaścidvratametaccarediti \|*  
*tasya śrīrvijayaścaiva trivargaścāpi vardhate \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. In this way, a person who taking food once in the fifth moon day, then fasting on the sixth moon day breaks the fast in the night of the seventh moon day, consuming vegetables and the best of eatables, offering to the Sungod and the Brahmanas, and takes food keeping silence and continues the vrata throughout the life, he becomes victorious and always gains uprising with trivarga (dharma, artha and kama).

## \|\| 1.47.50 \|\|

*mṛtaśca svargamāyāti 1 vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*sūryaloke sa ramate manvantaragaṇānbahūn \|*  
*iha cāgatya kālānte nṛpaḥ śānti samanvitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After his death, mounting over a beautiful plane, he lives comfortably for many Manvantaras in the place of the Sungod. In due course of time, he becomes a king with a peaceful nature.

## \|\| 1.47.51 \|\|

*putrapautraiḥ parivṛto dātā syānnṛpatiściram \|*  
*bhunakti hi dharāṃ rājanvigrahaiścājitaḥ parai \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Such people having their sons and grandsons give various kinds of charities, live a comfortable life on earth. They can never be defeated by the enemies.

## \|\| 1.47.52 \|\|

*ye narā rājaśārdūla śākāhāreṇa saptamīm \|*  
*upoṣya labdhaṃ tattīrthaṃ pitryaṃ vai rājasaṃjñikam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. O lion among the kings, the people, who living accordingly consume only vegetables on the seventh moon day, they gain their ancestral kingship as well as the holy place of Pushkara.

## \|\| 1.47.53 \|\|

*kuruṇā tava pūrveṇa śākāhāreṇa saptamīm \|*  
*dharmakṣetraṃ kurukṣetraṃ kṛtaṃ tasya vivasvatā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Kuru — your ancestor, had consumed only vegetables on the seventh moon day, as a result of which Kurukshetra was turned as the Dharmakshetra by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.47.54 \|\|

*saptamī navamī ṣaṣṭhī tṛtīyā pañcamī nṛpa \|*  
*kāmadāstithayo hyetā ihaiva narayoṣitām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O monarch, accordingly the seventh, ninth, sixth, third and fifth moon days fulfil all the desires of men and women.

## \|\| 1.47.55-56 \|\|

*saptamī māghamāse tu navamyāśvayuje matā \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhī bhādrapade dhanyā vaiśākhe tu tṛtīyikā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*puṇyā bhādrapade proktā pañcamī nāgapañcamī \|*  
*ityetāsteṣu māseṣu viśeṣāstithayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. The seventh moon day of the month of Magha, ninth moon day of the month of Ashvina, sixth moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, third moon day of the month of Vaishakha, and fifth moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, which is also known as Naga Panchami are considered to be quite auspicious and bestow excellence on people.

## \|\| 1.47.57 \|\|

*śākaṃ susatkṛtaṃ kṛtvā yaśca bhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*dattvā vipre yathāśaktyā paścādbhuṅkte niśi vratī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The vegetables should be cooked in a beautiful way and Brahmanas should be served the food with devotion and he himself should take food at night.

## \|\| 1.47.58 \|\|

*kārtike śuklapakṣasya grāhyeyaṃ kurunandana \|*  
*catubhirvāpi māsaistu pāraṇaṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. This particular fast should be started from the bright fortnight of the month of Karttika. O son of Kuru race, thus performing the vrata for four months and when the fast is broken, it is known as the first parana.

## \|\| 1.47.59 \|\|

*agastyakusumaiścātra pūjā kāryā vibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*vilepanaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tu dhūpaścaivāparājitaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The worship of the Sungod should be carried out offering the flowers of Agastya tree and those of Aparajita creeper besides vermilion and incense.

## \|\| 1.47.60-61 \|\|

*snānaṃ ca pañcagavyena tameva prāśayettataḥ \|*  
*naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ cātra devadevasya kīrtitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tadeva deyaṃ viprāṇāṃ śākaṃ bhakṣyamathātmanā \|*  
*śubhaśākasamāyuktaṃ bhakṣyapeyasamanvitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Thus bathing the Sungod with Panchagavya, the eatables should also be offered. Similar food and vegetables should also be given to the Brahmanas with beverages.

## \|\| 1.47.62-63 \|\|

*dvitīye pāraṇe rājañchubhagandhāni yāni vai \|*  
*puṣpāṇi tāni devasya tathā śvetaṃ ca candanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*aguruścāpi dhūpo'tra naivedyaṃ guḍapūpakāḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ kuśodakenātra prāśanaṃ gomayasya tu \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. O king, in the second parana (breaking of the fast), the frequent flowers, white sandal paste, guggulu, incense, eatables, sugarcane cakes and fired cakes should be offered. Then the Sungod should be bathed with milk and the kusha water and the liquid should be shipped by the devotee as a charinamrita.

## \|\| 1.47.64 \|\|

*tṛtīye karavīrāṇi tathā raktaṃ ca candanam \|*  
*dhūpānāṃ guggulaścātra priyo devasya sarvadā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. In the third parana the oleander flowers, red sandal paste, guggulu and incense should be offered, because these things are the favourite of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.47.65 \|\|

*śālyodanaṃ tu naivedyaṃ dadhimiśraṃ mahāmate \|*  
*tameva brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhakṣyalehyasamanvitam \|*  
*kālaśākena ca vibho yuktaṃ dadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Similarly, the cooked water-rice mixed with curd should be offered as the eatables besides seasonal vegetables of the time should also be offered to a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.47.66 \|\|

*gaurasarṣapakalkena snānaṃ cātra vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*tasyaiva prāśanaṃ dhanyaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Another part of the vrata is to offer bath with mustard oil as prescribed by the learned people. The same should be used as his own food as well, because it is quite praiseworthy and is the remover of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.47.67 \|\|

*tṛtīye pāraṇasyānte mahadbrāhmaṇabhojanam \|*  
*śravaṇaṃ ca purāṇasya vācanaṃ cāpi śasyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The food should also be offered to the Brahmanas, besides that it has also been prescribed to listen to the study of Puranas, or their recitation.

## \|\| 1.47.68 \|\|

*daivasya puratastāta brāhmaṇānāṃ tathāgrataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇādvācakācchrāvyaṃ nānyavarṇasamudbhavāt \|*  
*atha tānbrāhmaṇānsarvānbhaktyā śaktyā ca pūjayet \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O excellent one, the orator in the presence of the god or the Brahmana, should be a Brahmana alone and none else. He should take food through him only. Therefore, with the utmost devotion, according to one’s means, the orator should be adored.

## \|\| 1.47.69 \|\|

*vācakasyāmale rājanvāsasī sannivedayet \|*  
*vācake pūjite devaḥ sadā tuṣyati bhāskaraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Should the orator be given a pair of white clothes? Yes, it should be so done, because by adoring the orator, the Sungod gets always pleased.

## \|\| 1.47.70-71 \|\|

*karavīraṃ yatheṣṭaṃ tu tathā raktaṃ ca candanam \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ guggulaṃ tasya yatheṣṭaṃ pāyasaṃ sadā \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yatheṣṭā modakāstasya yathā vai tāmrabhājanam \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ ca ghṛtaṃ tasya yatheṣṭo vācakaḥ sadā \|*  
*purāṇaṃ ca yatheṣṭaṃ vai savituḥ kurunandana \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. O son of the Kuru race, in this vrata, the oleander flowers, red sandal paste, guggulu, pay as am, sweet balls, copper vase and ghi, must be offered to the reciter of the Purana.

## \|\| 1.47.72 \|\|

*ityeṣā saptamī puṇyā śākāhvā gopateḥ sadā \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naro bhaktyā bhāgyavāṃśca1 prajāyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. On the seventh moon day of Surya known as Shaka, fasting with devotion a person gains fortunes. This is always auspicious.

## Chapter 48. Glory of Aditya

## \|\| 1.48.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*vistarādvada viprendra saptamīkalpamuttamam \|*  
*mahābhāgyaṃ ca devasya bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O best of the Brahmanas, kindly describe the Saptami kalpa in which the fortunes of the Sungod have be mentioned.

## \|\| 1.48.2-4 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*atraivāhurmahātmānaḥ samvādaṃ puṇyamuttamam \|*  
*kṛṣṇena saha sattvena svaputreṇa mahīpate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhaktyā praṇamya vidhivadvāsudevaṃ jagadgurum \|*  
*ihāmutra hitaṃ śāṃbaḥ papraccha jñānamuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jāto jantuḥ kathaṃ duḥkhairjanmanīha na bādhyate \|*  
*prāpnoti vividhānkāmānkathaṃ ca madhusūdana \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Sumantu said — O lord of the earth, there had been a discussion on the subject between Lord Krishna and his son, Samba, which is going to be repeated by me. You please listen to the same. Once Samba, in order to attain the best of knowledge, offered his devoted salutation to lord Krishna which could be beneficial to the entire universe for the present as well as the future world and said — “O lord Madhusudana! Having been born in this world, how could a person, getting relieved of all the miseries, achieves success in all his efforts?”

## \|\| 1.48.5 \|\|

*paratra svargamāpnoti sukhāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*anubhūyocitaṃ kālaṃ kathaṃ muktimavāpnute \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In other words, after achieving the heaven, how could he, enjoying all the comforts on earth, could achieve liberation finally?

## \|\| 1.48.6 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaivaṃ mama nirvedo jāto vyādhirjanārdana \|*  
*dṛṣṭvemaṃ jīvitāśāpi rocate na hi me kṣaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Janardana, thus visualising the worldly creatures, I have attracted a terrific ailment. I have been overpowered by a great misfortune. So much so that presently I am not at all desirous of living on earth even for a moment.

## \|\| 1.48.7-8 \|\|

*kiṃ tvevamakṛtārtho'smi yanme prāṇā na yānti hi \|*  
*saṃsāre na patiṣyāmi jarāvyādhisamanvite \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yenopāyena tanme'dya prasādaṃ kuru suvrata \|*  
*ādhivyādhivinirmukto yathāhaṃ syāṃ tathā vada \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. But what should I do, the life does not leave my body, inspite of my best efforts to get rid of my life. O Suvrata! You kindly tell me the way out by which I do not have to be reborn in this world which is filled with ailments and old age. Besides I should be relieved of the present mental as well physical ailments and agony.”

## \|\| 1.48.9 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*devatāyāḥ prasādo'nyaḥ sarvasya paramo mataḥ \|*  
*upāyaḥ śāśvato nitya iti me niścitā matiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vasudeva said — All the people are of the opinion that in this connection there is no other firm method except to appease the gods and this is also my view.

## \|\| 1.48.10-11 \|\|

*anumānāgamādyaiśca samyagutpāditā mayā \|*  
*kadācidanyathā kartuṃ dhīyate kenacitkvacit \|\| 10 \|\|*

*prasādo jāyate tasya samyagārādhanakriyā \|*  
*yadā tāṃ ca samuddiśya kṛtā tadvedinā tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. With similar type of belief and imagination, I have pleased the gods. In case, a person intends to lead a comfortable life, then he should devote his mind towards them and please them.

## \|\| 1.48.12 \|\|

*viśiṣṭā devatā samyagviśiṣṭenaiva dehinā \|*  
*ārādhitā viśiṣṭaṃ ca dadāti phalamīhitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Because the important people adore the adorable god, and he achieves the beneficial reward.

## \|\| 1.48.13 \|\|

*śāmba uvāca \|*  
*astitve na ca sandehaḥ keṣāñciddevatāṃ prati \|*  
*nāstīti niścayo'nyeṣāṃ viśiṣṭāstvaṃ kathāḥ kuruḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Samba said — Though initially some people are not doubtful about the existence of the gods, but some of them are of the opinion that the gods do not exist, then of which particular god are you talking?

## \|\| 1.48.14 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*siddhaṃ tu devatāstitvamāgameṣu bahuṣvatha \|*  
*pramāṇamāgamo yasya tasyāstitvaṃ ca vidyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Krishna said — There is enough of evidence in the Vedas about the existence of the gods. Therefore those, whose existence is verified even by the Agamas, their existence is therefore certain.

## \|\| 1.48.15 \|\|

*anumānena vāpyadya tadastitvaṃ prasādhyate \|*  
*pramāṇamasti yasyedaṃ siddhā yasyeha cāstitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. As per presumption also, their existence is established because the presumption leads to the existence.

## \|\| 1.48.16 \|\|

*pratyakṣeṇāpi cāstitvaṃ devatāyāṃ prasādhyate \|*  
*taccāvaśyaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ sarvaśarīriṇām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The visible evidence establishes the existence of the gods, because such an evidence is visualised by all the people and because it has been termed as the visual evidence.

## \|\| 1.48.17 \|\|

*yadi nāmā viviktāstu tiryagyonigatā api \|*  
*notpadyate tathā hyasti vyavahāro yathā sthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the species of birds and animals, there is a lack in power of thinking and expression. Similarly, the people who are short of wisdom, are unable to visualize a particular type of people, which is difficult for them.

## \|\| 1.48.18 \|\|

*śāmba uvāca \|*  
*pratyekṣeṇopalabhyante samyagvai yadi devatāḥ \|*  
*anumānāgamābhyāṃ ca tadarthaṃ . na prayojanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Samba said — In case the existence of the gods is established by the visual evidence, then there is no need to accept the presumption or Agamas as evidence.

## \|\| 1.48.19 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*pratyakṣeṇopalabhyante na sarvā devatāḥ kvacit \|*  
*anumānāgamairgamyāḥ santi cānyāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Vasudeva said — The existence of all the gods cannot be established by visual evidence and the evidence of presumption testifies the presence of thousands of gods. Therefore, this should also be admitted as an evidence.

## \|\| 1.48.20 \|\|

*śāmba uvāca \|*  
*yā cākṣagocarā kācidviśiṣṭeṣṭaphalapradā \|*  
*tāmevādau mamācakṣva kathayiṣyasyathāparām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Samba said — Then tell me about the visible gods which are the giver of beneficial fruits.

## \|\| 1.48.21 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ devatā sūryo jagaccakṣurdivākaraḥ \|*  
*tasmādabhyadhikā kāciddevatā nāsti śāśvatī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Lord Krishna said — The Sun is the visible god, besides being the sight of the world. He is the creator of the day, therefore, there is no god more important and eternal than him.

## \|\| 1.48.22 \|\|

*yasmādidaṃ jagajjātaṃ layaṃ yāsyati yatra ca \|*  
*kṛtādilakṣaṇaḥ kālaḥ smṛtaḥ sākṣāddivākaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The universe was born of the Sun and it exists in him. Besides it is absorbed in the same. The time of krita and other yugas is also established by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.48.23-24 \|\|

*grahanakṣatrayogāśca rāśayaḥ 1 karaṇāni ca \|*  
*ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau vāyavo'nalaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śakraḥ prajāpatiḥ sarve bhūrbhuvaḥsvastathaiva ca \|*  
*lokāḥ sarve nagā nāgāḥ saritaḥ sāgarāstathā \|*  
*bhūtagrāmasya sarvasya svayaṃ heturdivākaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Therefore, the planets, constellations, zodiac signs, Karana, Aditya, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvinikumaras, Vayu (wind), Agni, Rudra, Prajapati, the earth, the sky, the heaven, besides all the rivers, mountains, the creatures, and others are established by the Sun alone.

## \|\| 1.48.25 \|\|

*asyecchayā jagatsarvamutpannaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*sthitaṃ pravartate caiva svārthe cānupravartate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As per his desire, the entire universe with all the mobile and immobile beings are born and engage themselves in their respective functions.

## \|\| 1.48.26-27 \|\|

*prasādādasya loko'yaṃ ceṣṭamānaḥ pradṛśyate \|*  
*asminnabhyudite sarvamudedastamite sati \|*  
*astaṃ yātītyadṛśyena kimetatkathyate mayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmādataḥ paraṃ nāsti na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*yo vai vedeṣu sarveṣu paramātmeti gīyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Similarly, with his pleasure, all the activities are regulated on earth. I have nothing more to say in this connection. All the four Vedas conceive him as the supreme soul. Therefore, no other god of more importance had ever been on earth, nor would be there in future.

## \|\| 1.48.28 \|\|

*itihāsapurāṇeṣu antarātmeti gīyate \|*  
*bāhyātmaiti suṣumṇāsthaḥ svapnastho jāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Because of this reason alone, he has been called as the inner soul of the world in the Puranas as well as other traditions. Besides the position of awakening, dream or sleep is attributed to him.

## \|\| 1.48.29 \|\|

*astaṃ yātītyadṛṣṭena kimetatkathyate mayā \|*  
*tasmādataḥ paraṃ nāsti na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But the Sungod also because of the unforeseen, the sun sets as well. Therefore, there had been no god superior to him, nor there shall be in future. Therefore, what more have I to speak about this.

## \|\| 1.48.30 \|\|

*yanna vāha iti khyātaḥ prerakaḥ sarvadehinām \|*  
*nānena rahitaṃ kiñcidbhūtamasti carācaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Because of his being in the universe, he is called Vaha. Without him, no mobile or immobile exists.

## \|\| 1.48.31 \|\|

*yo vedairvedavidbhiśca vistareṇeha śakyate \|*  
*vaktuṃ varṣaśatairnāsau śakyaḥ saṃkṣepato mayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Has any of the Vedic scholars define the glory of the Sun in hundreds of years in the past, than how could I do so?

## \|\| 1.48.32 \|\|

*1 tasmādguṇākaraḥ khyātaḥ sarvatrāyaṃ divākaraḥ \|*  
*sarveśaḥ sarvakartāyaṃ sarvabhartāyamavyayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Because the virtuous of the Sun are spread everywhere that he is the lord of all, creator, sustainer and is beyond destruction as well.

## \|\| 1.48.33 \|\|

*jātā matsyādayaḥ samyaggatimanto maheśvarāt \|*  
*maṇḍalavyatiriktaṃ ca jānāmi paramārthataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All the mobile creatures like fish etc. were born due to him. Except the mandala, all other things are meant for the benefit of the others.

## \|\| 1.48.34 \|\|

*tathāsya maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā2 yo hyenamupatiṣṭhate \|*  
*prātaḥ sāyaṃ ca madhyāhne sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Again, the one who making the visible mandala adore it, he achieves various types of success. There is nothing surprising in it.

## \|\| 1.48.35 \|\|

*kiṃ punarmaṇḍalasthaṃ yo japate paramārthataḥ \|*  
*vividhāḥ siddhayastasya bhavanti na tadadbhutam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A learned person, who is aware of the presence of the Sungod in his own body by his own wisdom, actually he is aware of his importance or sanctity.

## \|\| 1.48.36 \|\|

*maṇḍale ca sthitaṃ devaṃ dehe cainaṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*svabuddhyaivamasammūḍho yapaśyati sa paśyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Similarly, the one who is meditating upon him, adores him and performs japam for him besides the homa, all his tasks are established and he finally achieves the lord.

## \|\| 1.48.37 \|\|

*dhyātvaivaṃ 1 pūjayedyastu japedyo juhuyācca yaḥ \|*  
*sa sarvānprāpnuyātkāmāngaccheddharmadhvajaṃ tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Therefore, in case you are desirous of getting relieved of the miseries in the world, comforts in the present and the future world, you should adore the Sungod whose limbs had been chiseled and whose body has been covered with a coat of arms. You should adore him reciting the mantras and by so doing, you would achieve the desired success.

## \|\| 1.48.38-40 \|\|

*tasmāttvamiha duḥkhānāmantaṃ kartuṃ yadīcchasi \|*  
*ihāmutra ca bhogānāṃ bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca śāśvatīm \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ārādhayārkamarkastho mantrairiha tadātmani \|*  
*aṅgairvṛtaṃ vṛte caiva sthāne śāstreṇa śodhite \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kavacena ca saṅguste sarvato'streṇa rakṣite \|*  
*evaṃ prāpsyasi yatnena sarvadā phalamīpsitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. Therefore, during the morning, noon and the evening, one who adores the Sungod in a mandala, they achieve the best position.

## \|\| 1.48.41 \|\|

*duḥkhamādhyātmikaṃ neha tathā caivādhibhautikam \|*  
*ādhidaivikamatyugraṃ na bhaviṣyati te sadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. As a result of this, the spiritual, material as well as other miseries and pain would never disturb you.

## \|\| 1.48.42 \|\|

*na bhayaṃ vidyate teṣāṃ prapannā ye divākaram \|*  
*ihāmutra sukhaṃ teṣāmacchidraṃ jāyate sukham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Because, those who take refuge in Divakara or the Sungod, they receive protection as well as all the comforts in the future world.

## \|\| 1.48.43 \|\|

*sūryeṇedaṃ mamoddiṣṭaṃ sākṣādyajjñānamuttamam \|*  
*ārādhitena vidhivatkālena bahunā tathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Therefore, whatever spiritual knowledge concerning the Sungod has been imported to you by me, you should make use of it for long. It bestow the best place in the abode of the lord.

## \|\| 1.48.44 \|\|

*prāpyate paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra dharmadhvajaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*etatsaṃkṣiptamuddiṣṭaṃ kṣiprasiddhikaraṃ param \|*  
*yathā nānyadato'stīti svayaṃ tūryeṇa bhāṣitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus, a person who listens to this brief story, which speedily fulfills all the desires and happens to be the best of all, having been spoken by the Sungod himself. I have repeated the same to you briefly,

## \|\| 1.48.45 \|\|

*upāyo'yaṃ samākhyātastava saṃkṣepatastviha \|*  
*yasmātparataro nāsti hitopāyaḥ śarīriṇām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore, I have revealed this method to you in brief for the benefit of the people, because there is no other method better than this.

## Chapter 49. Glory of Sungod

## \|\| 1.49.1 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*athārcanavidhiṃ vakṣye dharmaketoranuttamam \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaṃ puṇyaṃ vighnaghnaṃ duritāpaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vasudeva said — Surya — the flag of dharma, has to be adored and the method of his adoration which is the best and makes all the desires successful, besides being auspicious, remover of obstructions and sins is going to be related by me. You please listen to the same.

## \|\| 1.49.2 \|\|

*sūryamantraiḥ puraḥ snāto yajettenaiva bhāskaram \|*  
*yatastataḥ pravakṣyāmi snānamādau samāsataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Uttering the mantras of the Sungod, one should take his bath and adore the deity. Therefore, initially, I briefly speak about the taking of the bath.

## \|\| 1.49.3-4 \|\|

*ācāntastamupālabhya mudrayā śuciśuddhayā \|*  
*kṛtvā nīrājanaṃ putra saṃśodhya ca jalaṃ tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*snānāddhṛdayapūtena 1 mantreṇa matkulodvaha \|*  
*utthāyācamya tenaiva vāsasī paridhāya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. O son, after initially sipping the water, one should cast a look at the Sun and the light should be offered to the deity. Then sanctifying the water with the reciting of the mantras one should take his bath. Thereafter, reciting the mantras with purity, one should I wear a dhoti and a scarf.

## \|\| 1.49.5-6 \|\|

*dvirācamyātha samprokṣya tanuṃ saptākṣareṇa ca \|*  
*utthāyācamya tenaivaṃ raveḥ kṛtvārghyameva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dattvā tena japitvā taṃ svakaṃ dhyātvārkavaddhṛdi \|*  
*gatvā cāyatanaṃ śubhramārkamārkī tanuṃ yajet \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Sipping the water twice, then the person uttering the seven letter mantra, should wipe out his body. After sipping, then one should offer oblation and then go to the Sun temple and worship his image.

## \|\| 1.49.7 \|\|

*pūrakaṃ kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā recakaṃ ca samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvoṅkāreṇa doṣāṃstu hanyātkāyādisambhavān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then perform pranayama uttering of Omkara, with puraka, kumbhaka and rechaka. By so doing, the blemishes of his body would be removed.

## \|\| 1.49.8 \|\|

*vāyavyāgneyamāhendravāruṇībhiryathākramam \|*  
*kilviṣaṃ vāruṇādbhiśca hanyātsiddhyarthamātmanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter, sprinkle the water from the pitchers placed over north-west, south-east, east and west directions for attaining success as well as for the removal of sins.

## \|\| 1.49.9 \|\|

*śoṣaṇaṃ dahanaṃ stambhaṃ plāvanaṃ ca yathākramāt \|*  
*vāyvagnīndrajanākhyābhirdhāraṇābhiḥ kṛte sati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter, with the Vayaviya, Agneyi, Mahendri and Varuni firmness, one should meditate upon, squeeze the body and perform the rites of combustion (excitement), shivering or shaking, careful wash should be completed.

## \|\| 1.49.10 \|\|

*dhyātvā viśuddhamātmānaṃ praṇamedarkamāsthitam \|*  
*dehaṃ tenaiva sañcintya pañcabhūtamayaṃ param \|\| 10 \|\|*
