10\. Thereafter, developing the feeling of utmost purity, one should offer salutation to the Sungod within himself and then think of the five materialistic bodies.

## \|\| 1.49.11-14 \|\|

*sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ tathākṣāṇi svasthāneṣu prakamya ca \|*  
*vinyasyāṅgāni khādīni hṛdādyāni hṛdyādiṣu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*khasvāhā hadayaṃ bhānoḥ khamarkāya śirastathā \|*  
*ulkā svāhā śikhārkasya yai ca huṃ kavacaṃ param \|*  
*khāṃ phaḍastraṃ ca saṃhārāścāditaḥ praṇavaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sa pūrve praṇavasyātho mantrakarmaprasiddhaye \|*  
*ebhirjalaṃ tridhā japtvā snānadravyāṇi tena ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*samprokṣya pūjayetsūryaṃ gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*tato mūrtiṣu sarvāsu rātrāvagnau prapūjayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. While meditating, one should think about the subtle and gross body, the eyes, and all other limbs at their respective places, besides the sense organs and the heart, and recite the mantra with Omkara followed with the words kha svaha and should touch the heart, reciting khamarkaya svaha he should touch the head, saying utkaya svaha he should touch the tuft, with hum the tuft, with kham phat the weapon and then conclude. For the bathing of the deity, the water should be sanctified thrice and adding the fragrant flowers, the oblation should be offered to the Sungod, Thereafter, all the figures of the god should be adored during the night, with fire.

## \|\| 1.49.15-18 \|\|

*prākpaścimodagabhyagrāṃ prātaḥ sāyaṃ niśāsu vai \|*  
*saptākṣareṇa tanmantraṃ dhyātvā ca padmakarṇikām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ādityamaṇḍalāntasthaṃ tatra dehaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*prabhāmaṇḍalamadhyasthaṃ dhyātvā dehaṃ yathā purā \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇaṃ sahasrakiraṇojjvalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*raktairgandhaiśca puṣpaiśca carubhirbalibhistathā \|*  
*raktacandanamiśrairvā vastrairāvaraṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*āvāhanādikarmāṇi rakṣāṃ tu hṛdayena ca \|*  
*taccittaśca sadā kuryājjñātvā karmakramaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Similarly, in the morning, evening and the night, one should conceive mentally in the east, west and the northern directions the Sun lodged in lotus flowers in mandalas. Again in the prabha mandala, his image, which should be complete in all respects, illuminating with a thousand rays, should be meditated upon. Then he should offer to the image the red flowers, sandalpaste, ochre colour mixed with red sandal paste and the five costumes. Then invoking the deity by heart, besides performing other rites, he should be worshipped with devotion.

## \|\| 1.49.19-20 \|\|

*kṛtvā cāvāhanaṃ mantrairekatra sthāpanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*yāvadyāgāvasānaṃ tu sānnidhyaṃ tatra kalpya ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dattvā pādyādikāṃ pūjāṃ śaktyā vārghyaṃ nivedya ca \|*  
*japitvā vidhivaddhyātvā tato devīṃ visarjayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Invoking the deity with the uttering of the mantras, it should be consecrated at a particular place till the completion of the yajna. Conceiving of the vicinity of the deity, one should offer, as per his means, the water, arghya, eatables besides japam. Thus one should meditate appropriately and then send off the deity.

## \|\| 1.49.21 \|\|

*eṣa karma kramaḥ proktaḥ sarveṣāṃ yajanakramāt \|*  
*pravakṣyāmi japasthānaṃ padmeśāvaraṇe tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. For the worship of the deity, the same process has been prescribed for all the people Now, I am speaking about the covering of the Sungod — the lord of lotus flowers, you please listen to me.

## \|\| 1.49.22 \|\|

*ādityaṃ karṇikāsaṃsthaṃ daleṣvaṅgāni pūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*somādīnrāhuparyaṃtāngrahāṃścaivodagāditaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In the pericarp of the lotus, the Sungod should be established and his limbs should be lodged towards the directions over the flower petals. Thereafter, starting from moon to Rahu, all the planets should also be lodged towards the north.

## \|\| 1.49.23 \|\|

*mūrtimallokapālāṃśca kramādāvaraṇeṣvatha \|*  
*tadastrāṇi ca rakṣārthaṃ svamantraiḥ pūjayetkramāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Similarly, the figures of the Lokapalas who are lodged as his shields should also be lodged with their weapons, reciting the mantras.

## \|\| 1.49.24 \|\|

*praṇavaiścābhidhānaiśca caturthyāṃ hyabhiyojitaiḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ kathitā mantrā mudrāśca kathayāmyataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Similarly, uttering the names of other deities should also be uttered, completing the formalities of invoking them. After this, I am speaking mantras for all of them together with their respective mudras.

## \|\| 1.49.25 \|\|

*vyomamudrā ratiḥ padmā mahāśvetāstrameva ca \|*  
*pañcamudrāḥ samākhyātāḥ sarvakarmaprasiddhaye \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Vyoma, Rati, Padma, Mahashveta and their weapons are the five which bring success in all the cases.

## \|\| 1.49.26-30 \|\|

*uttānau tu karau kṛtyā aṅgulyo grathitāḥ kramāt \|*  
*tarjanīṃ yanti yāvattāḥ same vādhomukhe sthite \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tarjanyo 1 madhyamasyaiva jyeṣṭhāgre vānugopari \|*  
*mudreyaṃ sarvamudrāṇāṃ vyoma mudreti kīrtitā \|*  
*sarvakarmasu yogo'yaṃ tathā sthānaṃ prakalpate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*padmavatprasṛtāḥ sarvā mahāśvetā raveḥ smṛtā \|*  
*javasaṃnihito nityaṃ rathārūḍho raviḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*hastāvūrdhvamukhau kṛtvā vāmāṅguṣṭhena yojitau \|*  
*dravyāṇāṃ śodhane yojyā rakṣārthaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*anayā mudrayā sarvaṃ rakṣitaṃ śodhitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*arghyaṃ datvā prayoktavyā pūjānte ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. All these mudras are highly beneficial for the performer. With all efforts and at a suitable place, these five mudras should be performed in due order. For sanctifying the dravyas and for their own. protection, with these mudras the people get purified and protected. Therefore, after offering oblation at the end of the it is essential to make use of the mudras.

## \|\| 1.49.31-34 \|\|

*japadhyānāvasāne ca yadīcchetsiddhimātmanaḥ \|*  
*anena vidhinā nityaṃ japedabdamatandritaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sa labhetepsitānkāmānihāmutra na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*rogārto mucyate rogāddhanahīno dhanaṃ labhet \|\| 32 \|\|*

*rājyabhraṣṭo labhedrājyamaputraḥ putramāpnuyāt \|*  
*prajñāmedhāsamṛddhīśca ciraṃ jīvati mānavaḥ \|*  
*surūpāṃ labhate kanyāṃ kulīnā puruṣo dhruvam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*saubhāgyaṃ strī kulīnāpi kanyā ca puruṣottamam \|*  
*avidyo labhate vidyāmityuktaṃ bhānunā purā \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. For the accomplishment of one’s task, at the end of meditation and japam one should make use of the mudras. In case, the japam is performed for full one year, then all the worldly as well as the desires for the other world are fulfilled. The person with ailments is relieved of the pains, a pauper achieves riches. A ruler who is deprived of his riches, gets back his kingdom, and a barren woman gets a son. Beside a person achieves sharp wisdom, progress and long life. Similarly, a man gets a beautiful girl of high caste, a woman gets the best of fortunes, a girl gets a good match and a fool achieves learnings. This is what has be spoken by the Sungod earlier.

## \|\| 1.49.35 \|\|

*nityayāgaḥ smṛto hyeṣa dhanadhānyasukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*prajāpaśuvivṛddhiśca niṣkāmasyāpi jāyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Therefore, this yajna should be performed regularly because with the performing of the same, a person who does so without any particular desire, he also achieves enough of cereals, comforts, progeny and there is enough of increase in his cattle stock.

## \|\| 1.49.36 \|\|

*tadaikaḥ stūyate svarge śabdyate ca narottamaḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā taṃ pūjayedyastu naraḥ puṇyataraḥ sadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He alone is called a king with reputation in the heaven. Thus the one who adores the Sungod with devotion, he is always considered to be an extremely auspicious person.

## \|\| 1.49.37 \|\|

*iha vai kāmikaṃ prāpya tato gacchenmanoḥ padam \|*  
*dvijastasya prasādena tejasā budhasannibhaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He achieving success in all his desires in this world, achieves the position of a Manu in the heaven. For the sake of his pleasure, the high ranking people, become illustrious like Mercury.

## Chapter 50. Glory of Saptami

## \|\| 1.50.1 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*naimittikaṃ tato vakṣye yajjñātvā ca samāsataḥ \|*  
*saptamyāṃ grahaṇe caiva saṃkrāntiṣu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vasudeva said — The casual worship of the Sungod, which is usually done on the seventh moon day or at the time of eclipse or on the first day of the month is being narrated by me, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.50.2-4 \|\|

*śuklapakṣasya saptamyāṃ havirbhuktvaikadā divā \|*  
*samyagācamya sandhyāyāṃ vāruṇaṃ praṇipatya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*indriyāṇi ca saṃyamya kṛtaṃ dhyātvā svapedadhaḥ \|*  
*darbhaśayyāgato rātrau prātaḥ snātaḥ susaṃyataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tataḥ sandhyāmupāsyātha pūrvoktaṃ ca manuṃ japet \|*  
*juhuyācca tadā vahniṃ sūryāgnī parikalpya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Prior to the bright seventh moon day (on the sixth moon day), a person should consume havishya once during the day. Then sipping the water in the evening, he should offer salutation to the Sungod. Then controlling all his sense organs, he should be seated over the seat of kusha grass and meditate. Then sleeping on the ground, he should spend the night. Getting up early in the morning, he should perform Sandhya and should recite the Manu mantra as stated above and perform homa in the fire.

## \|\| 1.50.5 \|\|

*sūryāgnikaraṇaṃ vakṣye tarpaṇaṃ ca samāsataḥ \|*  
*arcanāgāramullikhya praviśyārcya janairjanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then tarpana should be performed before Suryagni. The temple for worship should be decorated with various types of figures. Thereafter, homa should be performed.

## \|\| 1.50.6-8 \|\|

*prakṣipyāstīrya darbhaśca pātrādyālabhya ca kramāt \|*  
*pavitraṃ dvikuśaṃ kṛtvā sāgraṃ prādeśasammitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tena pātrāṇi samprokṣya saṃśodhyādha vilokya ca \|*  
*udagagre sthite pātre prajvālyātholmukena ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*paryagnikaraṇaṃ kṛtvā tathājyotyavanaṃ tridhā \|*  
*parimṛjya sruvādīṃśra darbhaiḥ samprokṣayettataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Kusha grass should be spread around the fire altar. Then the water should be sprinkled over the vases filled with water. Then he should wear pavitrakas made of two leaves of kusha grass and wear them round his fingers. The pavitrakas should be made of the foreparts of the kusha grass. Thereafter, the vases should be sprinkled with water of kusha grass. The heated ghi should be examined and should place it towards the north. Then with a burning stick, the fire should be ignited.

## \|\| 1.50.9-10 \|\|

*juhuyātprokṣya tānvahnau tatrārkaṃ pūrvavad vrajet \|*  
*abhūmau sthitapātreṇa viṣṭareṇa tu pāṇinā \|*  
*dānena yaduśārdūla nāntarikṣe sthale kvacit \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇena sruvaṃ gṛhya juhuyātpāvakaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*hadayena kriyāḥ sarvāḥ kartavyāḥ pūrvacoditāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Thereafter, one should go round the fire once. Then joining the thumb and little finger, the ghi should be stirred thrice and complete the Rupakriya, sprinkling should be made towards the Sungod (at the base, centre and end). The kusha grass used for the above purpose, should then be dropped in the fire. O lion of the Yadu race, then the Sungod should be worshipped as before. In this process, with some other support apart from the earth and the sky, a vase should be placed in which the Sungod should be invoked. Then completing all other formalities, all the rites should be concluded. This has been told by the learned people.

## \|\| 1.50.11-12 \|\|

*arkādārabhya saṃjñārthaṃ dadyāttūṣṇīṃ hutiṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*varuṇāya śatairmāghe saptamyāṃ varuṇaṃ yajet \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yathāśaktyā tu viprebhyaḥ pradadyātkhaṇḍaveṣṭakān \|*  
*dadyācca dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā prāpnoti yācitaṃ phalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Again starting from the Sungod, keeping silent for the sake of the gods, offerings should be poured in the fire. During the seventh moon day of the month of Magha, the Sungod should be worshipped in the form of Varuna and for this purpose a hundred offerings have been prescribed. Thereafter, the Brahmanas should be served with sweet food and giving dakshina according to one’s means, the function should be concluded and by so doing, one gets the desired reward.

## \|\| 1.50.13-15 \|\|

*evaṃ vai phālgune sūryaṃ caitre vaiśākha eva ca \|*  
*vaiśākhe māsi dhātāramindraṃ jyeṣṭhe yajedravim \|\| 13 \|\|*

*āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe māsi nabhaṃ bhādrapade yamam \|*  
*tathāśvayuji parjanyaṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ kārtike yajet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣe ca mitraṃ ca pauṣe viṣṇuṃ yajedyadi \|*  
*saṃvatsareṇa yatproktaṃ phalamiṣṭaṃ dinedine \|*  
*tatsarvamāpnuyātkṣipraṃ bhaktyā śraddhānvito vratī \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Similarly, the Sungod in the month of Phalguna, Shvetamshu in the month of Chaitra, Dhata in the month of Vaishakha, Indra in the month of Jyestha, Ravi in the month of Ashadha, Nabha in the month of Shravana, Yama in the month of Bhadrapada, Parjanya in the month of Ashvina, Tvashta in the month of Karttika, Mitra in the month of Margashirsha, and Vishnu in the month of Pause should be worshipped. Thus performing the vrata by appropriately worshipping all the twelve Sungods in the entire year, one achieves all the fortunes and reward for the performance.

## \|\| 1.50.16-22 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃvatsare pūrṇe kṛtvā vai kāñcanaṃ ratham \|*  
*saptabhirvājibhiryuktaṃ nānāratnopaśobhitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ādityapratimāṃ madhye śuddhahemnā kṛtāṃ śubhām \|*  
*ratnairalaṅkṛtāṃ kṛtvā hemapadmoparisthitām \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasmin rathavare kṛtvā sārathiṃ cāgrataḥ sthitam \|*  
*vṛtaṃ dvādaśabhirvipraiḥ kramānmāsādhipātmabhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*madhye kṛtvā svamācāryaṃ pūjayitvā yathāśrutiḥ \|*  
*sañcintyādityavarṇaṃ vai vastraratnādinārhayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ māsādhipānviprānsampūjyātha nivedayet \|*  
*ācāryāya rathaṃ chatraṃ grāmaṃ gāśca mahīṃ śubhām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*aśvānmāsādhipebhyastu dvādaśabhyo nivedayet \|*  
*evaṃ bhaktyā yathāśaktyā hemaratnādibhūṣaṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dattvā tasya namaskṛtya vrataṃ pūrṇaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ na doṣo'tra vratasyākaraṇeṣvapi \|\| 22 \|\|*

16-22. Similarly, at the end of the year, one should make a beautiful chariot in gold in which seven horses are yoked. In the centre of the chariot, a golden image of the Sungod should be consecrated over a lotus seat. The image should be studded with gems. The charioteer should be made to sit in front position. In this way, since the Sungod is the lord of the twelve months, twelve Brahmanas should be invited and an Acharya should be made to sit in the middle of those Brahmanas. All of them should be worshipped offering costumes and gems to ten. The images should then be donated to all of ten. The chariot, umbrella, villages and cows besides the land should be given in charity to the Acharya, and the Brahmanas who are related to the months should be given horses in charity, besides the ornaments studded with gems, should be given with devotion to them, offering salutation at the same time. They should also be apprised of the completion of the vrata of a year’s duration. Thereafter, if the vrata is not performed, one does not earn any blemish for the same.

## \|\| 1.50.23 \|\|

*evamastviti viprendraiḥ sahācāryaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*bahvīścaivāśiṣo dattvā pravadetprīyatāmiti \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After the offering of salutation, the Acharya as well as the other Brahmanas should accept the charity saying — “Be it so”, pronouncing other various types of blessings, with delight.

## \|\| 1.50.24 \|\|

*ādityo yena kāmena tvayā ārādhito vrataiḥ \|*  
*tubhyaṃ dadātu taṃ kāmaṃ sampūrṇaṃ bhavatu vratam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. They should pronounce — “The purpose for which you have performed the vrata, let the same be fulfilled,” to the performer of the vrata.

## \|\| 1.50.25 \|\|

*ācāryānviprarūpaistu praviṣṭo bhāskaraḥ svayam \|*  
*dāsyatyeva paraṃ kartumityuktaṃ bhānunā svayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Because, it has been ordained by the Sungod himself that in the form of Acharya and the Brahmanas, it is the Sungod who pronounces the blessings.

## \|\| 1.50.26 \|\|

*viprebhyo guṇavadbhyaśca nisvebhyaśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dīnāndhakṛpaṇebhyaśca śaktyā dattvā ca dakṣiṇām \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā ca vratametatsamāpayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Similarly, in the performing of the vrata, the poor Brahmanas who could also be blind, should particularly be patronised, and they should also be given charities and dakshina as per one’s means. Thereafter, the vrata should be concluded.

## \|\| 1.50.27 \|\|

*kṛtvaivaṃ saptamīmabdaṃ rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*puruṣaḥ strī bhavedrājñāṃ tādṛśāmatha vallabhā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In this way, when all the Saptami vratas for the year are completed appropriately, the king becomes religious minded. In case the vratas are performed by a lady, then she becomes the most favourite queen of the king.

## \|\| 1.50.28 \|\|

*śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ niḥsapatnamakaṇṭakam \|*  
*niṣpannamaṇḍalaṃ bhuṅkte sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ sukhī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The king on the other hand, who performs these vratas, becomes the undisturbed ruler for a hundred year, of a kingdom as vast as a hundred yojanas and leads a comfortable life.

## \|\| 1.50.29-30 \|\|

*vittahīno'pi yo 1 bhaktyā kṛttvā tāmramayaṃ ratham \|*  
*dadyādvratāvasāne tu kṛtvā sarvaṃ yathoditam \|*  
*so'śītiyojanaṃ bhuṅkte vistīrṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*evaṃ piṣṭamayaṃ yo'pi vittahīnaḥ karoti nā \|*  
*āṣaṣṭiyojanaṃ bhuṅkte dīrghāyurnīrujaḥ sukhī \|*  
*sūryaloke ca kalpāntaṃ yāvatsthitvedamāpnuyāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. In case a poor person making a chariot of copper, donates it with devotion at the end of the vrata, he also achieves the kingship of the kingdom of a hundred yojanas. He also enjoys long and comfortable life and ultimately, he lives in the Surya’s place for a kalpa.

## \|\| 1.50.31 \|\|

*manasāpi ca yo bhaktyā yajedarkamatandritaḥ \|*  
*sarvāvasthāsu so'pyatra vyādhibhirmucyate bhṛśam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A person who with a concentrated mind adores the Sungod even mentally, he also enjoys the best of health in all the situations.

## \|\| 1.50.32-33 \|\|

*āpado na spṛśantyenaṃ nīhārā iva bhāskaram \|*  
*kiṃ punarvratasampannaṃ bhaktaṃ 1 mantraiśca rakṣitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yata evaṃ tato jñātvā vidhānaṃ kalpacoditam \|*  
*sukhena phalasiddhyarthaṃ kuryātsarvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The misfortunes can never touch such a person as a fog cannot touch the Sun. The people who being well aware of this process, perform vratas with devotion for the achieving of the reward, are always protected by the mantras and they achieve enormous fortunes.

## \|\| 1.50.34 \|\|

*ityetatkathitaṃ sāmba purā sūryeṇa me śubham \|*  
*kalpo'yaṃ prathame kalpe sarvadā gopito mayā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Samba! In the earlier kalpa, this beneficial kalpa had been related to me by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.50.35 \|\|

*anena vidhinā vatsa viśuddhenāntarātmanā \|*  
*bhānumārādhayetkṣipraṃ yadīcchetphalamuttamam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O son, in case one be desirous of the best result, then following the same process with devotion, one should worship the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.50.36 \|\|

*mayāsyaiva prasādena prāptāḥ putrāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*asurā nirjitāścaiva surāḥ sarve vaśīkṛtāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Because of his pleasure, I achieved thousands of sons, victory over the asuras and all the gods accepting superiority.

## \|\| 1.50.37 \|\|

*tvayāpyayaṃ gopitavyaḥ kalpaḥ sūryasya sammataḥ \|*  
*prasādādasya kalpasya sadā sannihito raviḥ \|*  
*cakre'sminnirjitā yena surā suranaroragāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Therefore, you keep this kalpa a secret which is the favourite of the Sungod. Because due to the delight of this kalpa, the Sungod always remain close to my cakra with the use of which, the gods, demons, humans and the serpents have been defeated by me.

## \|\| 1.50.38 \|\|

*yadinādhiṣṭhitaṃ cakramidaṃ sūryāṃśubhiḥ svayam \|*  
*satataṃ syātprabhāyuktaṃ kathamadhyāhataṃ bhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Had the Sun with his rays not been linked to my cakra, then I would not have been able to gain such an enormous strength.

## \|\| 1.50.39 \|\|

*ahametaṃ japannityaṃ yajandhyāyaṃśca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*jāto'smi sarvakāmānāṃ pūjyaḥ śreṣṭhaśca tejasā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Therefore, I always worship him beside, performing japas as per my means. Because of my worship for him, all my desires are fulfilled because of his lustre.

## \|\| 1.50.40 \|\|

*tvamabhyasyaiva manasā vācā vā karmaṇāpi vā \|*  
*kuru bhaktimanenaiva vidhinā phalasiddhaye \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Devoting your mind, speech and activities to the Sungod, you should adore him for achieving of the success.

## \|\| 1.50.41-42 \|\|

*śṛṇuyādbhaktiyukto yo naraḥ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vidhānamāditaḥ putra saptamīṃ kurute ca yaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*seha 1 prāpyā'khilaṃ kāmamārogyaṃ ca jayaṃ tathā \|*  
*bhārgavyā parayā yukto gacchedvairocanaṃ sadaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. O son, a person who listens to this episode with devotion and also performs the Saptami vrata appropriately, he meets with all the success, good health, victory, and enormous riches. In due course of time, he reaches the abode of Surya.

## Chapter 51. Maha Saptami Vrata

## \|\| 1.51.1-2 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*māghasya śuklapakṣe tu pañcamyāṃ matkulodvaha \|*  
*ekabhaktaṃ sadākhyātaṃ ṣaṣṭyāṃ naktamudāhṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saptamyāmupavāsaṃ tu kecidicchanti suvrata \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ kecidvadantīha saptamyāṃ pāraṇaṃ kila \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Vasudeva said — O Suvrata, some people have spoken about performing the vrata by taking food once on the bright fifth moon day, to take food at night on the sixth moon day and observing a complete fast on the seventh moon day. Some people have prescribed the breaking of the fast on the sixth moon day or the seventh moon day.

## \|\| 1.51.3 \|\|

*kṛtopavāsaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu pūjayedbhāskaraṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*raktacandanamiśraistu karavīraiśca suvrata \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. But while fasting, the puja of Surya should be performed on the sixth moon day offering the red sandal paste as well as the oleander flowers.

## \|\| 1.51.4 \|\|

*guggulena mahābāho saṃyāvena ca suvrata \|*  
*pūjayeddevadeveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ 2 bhāskaraṃ ravim \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O large armed one, similarly, Lord Shiva and Surya should be worshipped offering guggulu and porridge.

## \|\| 1.51.5-6 \|\|

*evaṃ hi caturo māsānmāghādīnpūjayedravim \|*  
*ātmanaścāpi śudhyarthaṃ prāśanaṃ gomayasya ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*snānaṃ ca gomayeneha kartavyaṃ cātmaśuddhaye \|*  
*brāhmaṇāndivyabhaumāṃśca bhojayeccāpi śaktitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Similarly, in the four months including the month of Margashirsha, for self purification after worshipping the Sungod, cowdung should be taken. Besides the food to the Brahmanas should also be served mixing the same, as per one’s means.

## \|\| 1.51.7-8 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhādiṣvatha māseṣu śvetacandanamucyate \|*  
*śvetāni cāpi puṣpāṇi śubhagandhānvitāni vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāgarustathā dhūpo naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tenaiva brāhmaṇāṃstuṣṭānbhojayecca mahāmate \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. In the months of Jyestha and other months, the white sandal paste, white flowers, the incense, eatables and payasam should be offered to Brahmanas and they should be pleased with the same.

## \|\| 1.51.9-11 \|\|

*prāśayetpañcagavyaṃ tu snānaṃ tenaiva putraka \|*  
*kārtikādiṣu māseṣu agastikusumaiḥ smṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pūjayennaraśārdūla dhūpaiścaivāparājitaiḥ \|*  
*naivedyaṃ guḍapūpāstu tathā cekṣurasaṃ smṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tenaiva brāhmaṇāṃstāta bhojayasva svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*kuśodakaṃ prāśayethāḥ snānaṃ ca kuru śuddhaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. The process also includes bathing with water mixed with cowdung. O son, in the months of Karttika and others, the flowers of Aparajita and Agastya besides incense, eatables, jaggery, fried cakes and sugarcane juice should be offered to the deity and the same things should be offered to the Brahmanas as their food as per one’s means. Thereafter, he should purify himself by bathing with kusha water. Then, he should take the same.

## \|\| 1.51.12 \|\|

*tṛtīye pāraṇāsyānte māghe māsi mahāmate \|*  
*bhojanaṃ tatra dānaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O intelligent one, in the third breaking of the fast which is to be held in the Margashirsha, double the food and charities are required to be offered.

## \|\| 1.51.13 \|\|

*devadevasya pūjā ca kartavyā śaktito budhaiḥ \|*  
*rathasya cāpi dānaṃ tu rathayātrā tu suvrata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Therefore, the people with wisdom, as per their means, should worship the Sungod, performing puja, giving away of the chariot besides taking a chariot procession.

## \|\| 1.51.14-16 \|\|

*vratasya prāptihetorvai kartavyā vibhave sati \|*  
*dānaṃ svarṇarathasyeha yathoktaṃ vibhave sati \|*  
*ityeṣā kathitā putra rathāhvā saptamī śubhā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mahāsaptamī vikhyātā mahāpuṇyā mahodayā \|*  
*yāmupoṣya dhanaṃ putrānkīrtiṃ vidyāmavāpnuyāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tathākhilaṃ kuvalayaṃ candreṇa ca samorciṣā \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. In case a person is financially well off, he should make a chariot in gold. O son, this Saptami moon day linked with the chariot which is quite auspicious, is also known as Maha Saptami. It bestows enormous fortunes, and by observing a fast during the same moon day, one achieve riches, sons, learnings and the glory shining like the spotless moon rays. This is what has been told by me.

## Chapter 52. The Sun worship

## \|\| 1.52.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavāndevaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*antardhānaṃ gato vīraṃ śāmbasyeha prapaśyataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — In this way, Lord Krishna — the bolder of conch, disc and clubs, disappeared from there in full view of Samba.

## \|\| 1.52.2 \|\|

*śāmbo'pi kṛtvā vidhivatsaptamīṃ rathasaptamīm \|*  
*ādhi bhirvyādhibhirmukto jagāmāśu svamandiram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then Samba on his part, on the day of Ratha-Saptami, observed vrata and other formalities, got relieved of the ailments of the body, and proceeded towards his abode.

## \|\| 1.52.3 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*rathayātrā kathaṃ kāryā rathaḥ kāryaḥ rathaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*keneha martyalokeṣu rathayātrā pravartitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Shatanika said — How is the chariot of the Sun made and how is the chariot procession taken out? Who did actually start the tradition of taking out the Ratha yatra

## \|\| 1.52.4 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭaḥ padmayoniḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*rudreṇa kuruśārdūla āsīnaḥ kāñcane girau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Sumantu said — O lion of the Kuru race, once lord Shiva had asked the same question to Brahma, who was seated over the Meru mountain.

## \|\| 1.52.5 \|\|

*padmāsanaṃ padmayoniṃ sukhāsīnaṃ prajāpatim \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devo rudro vācamudairayat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Shiva asked Brahma who was comfortably seated there in Padmasana, bowing before him.

## \|\| 1.52.6 \|\|

*śrīrudra uvāca \|*  
*ya eṣa bhagavāndevo bhāskaro lokabhāskaraḥ \|*  
*kathameṣa bhrameddevo rathastho vimalaḥ sadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Shri Rudra said — Lord Surya illuminate the world, what type of chariot does he have over which does he move?

## \|\| 1.52.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yathā divi bhramettāta rathārūḍho raviḥ sadā \|*  
*tathā te vartayiṣye'haṃ rathaṃ cāsya trilocana \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Brahma said — O excellent one, the type of chariot riding which the Sungod roams about in the sky, I am going to describe the same.

## \|\| 1.52.8-9 \|\|

*rathena hyekacakreṇa pañcāreṇa triṇābhinā \|*  
*hiraṇyamayena kāntena aṣṭabandhaikaneminā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*cakreṇa bhāsvatā caiva divi sūryaḥ prasarpati \|*  
*daśayojanasāhasro vistāro'pyasya kathyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The illuminating chariot of the Sungod has a single wheel with five spokes. There are three navels which have been tied with eight bondages. The chariot’s wheel has the circumference besides the length and breadth of ten thousand yojanas, over which the Sungod is always seated.

## \|\| 1.52.10 \|\|

*triguṇā ca rathopasthādīṣā daṇḍapramāṇataḥ \|*  
*yugamasya tu vistīrṇamaruṇo1 yatra sārathiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The hind part of the chariot is thrice the length of a danda. The golden yoke of the chariot over which Arana is seated, is quite broad.

## \|\| 1.52.11-20 \|\|

*prāsaṅgaḥ kāṃcano divyo yuktaḥ pavanagairhayaiḥ \|*  
*chandobhirvājirūpaistu yataścakraṃ tataḥ sthitaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yenāsau paryaṭedvyomni bhāsvatā tu divaspatiḥ \|*  
*athaitāni tu sūryasya pratyaṅgāni rathasya tu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saṃvatsarasyāvayavaiḥ kalpitāni yathākramam \|*  
*1 nābhyastisrastu cakrasya trayaḥ kālāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ārāḥ pañcartavastasya nemyaḥ ṣaḍṛtavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*rathavedī smṛte tasya ayane dakṣiṇottare \|\| 14 \|\|*

*muhūrtā 2 iṣavastasya śamyāścāsya kalāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tasya kāṣṭhāḥ smṛtāḥ koṇā akṣadaṇḍaḥ kṣaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nimeṣāścāsya karṣāḥ syādīṣādaṇḍo lavāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*rātrirvarūtho dharmo'sya dhvaja ūrdhvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yugākṣikoṭī te tasya arthakāmāvubhau smṛtau \|*  
*aśvarūpāṇi cchandāṃsi vahante vāmato dhuram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gāyatrī caiva triṣṭup ca jagatyanuṣṭubeva ca \|*  
*paṅktiśca bṛhatī caiva uṣṇigeva tu saptamī \|\| 18 \|\|*

*cakramakṣanibaddhaṃ tu dhruve cākṣaḥ samarpitaḥ \|*  
*sahacakro bhramatyakṣaḥ sa cākṣo bhramati dhruve \|\| 19 \|\|*

*akṣaḥ sahaiva cakreṇa bhramate'sau dhruve sthitaḥ \|*  
*evamakṣavaśāttasya 3 sanniveśo rathasya tu \|\| 20 \|\|*

11-20. The horses, having the speed of the wind, are yoked in the same. They are in the form of chandas. The yoke is placed over the shoulders of the horses. The Sungod moves over them in the sky illuminating the same. All the limbs of the year are the parts of the chariot. The three kala chakras are the three navels of the chariot. The five seasons besides the circumference, Dakshinayana (winter solitude) and Uttarayana (summer solitude) are both the seats of the chariot. The Muhurta, pole star and the digits are the nails of the yoke. The directions, moments, akshadanda, twinkling of an eye, pulling of the chariot, fragment of a moment, akshadanda, night, the secret place in the chariot, banner of dharma, besides artha and kama are the foreparts of axle. The horses in the form of chandas, getting yoked in the chariot, drive it. Gayatri, Trishtupa, Jagati; Anushtupa, Pankti, Brihati and Ushnika are known to be the seven horses. The wheel rotates over the axle. The same axle is linked to Dhruva and the wheel is fixed in the axle. The axle is linked to Dhruva and the chariot moves with the same.

## \|\| 1.52.21 \|\|

*tathā saṃyogabhāvena saṃsiddho bhāskaro rathaḥ \|*  
*tena cāsau ravirdevo nabhaḥ saṃsarpate sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus having been linked to one another, the chariot of the Sun in which he moves, seated in it, in the sky, is ready.

## \|\| 1.52.22 \|\|

*yugākṣakoṭīsambaddhe dve raśmī syandanasya tu \|*  
*dhruve te bhramato raśmī na cakrayugayostu vai \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The reins of the horses which are tied to the yoke and the axle remain in the chariot and they do not rotate.

## \|\| 1.52.23 \|\|

*bhramato maṇḍalānyasya raverasya rathasya tu \|*  
*kulālacakravadyāti maṇḍalaṃ sarvatodiśam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The circular form of the wheel of the chariot resembles the potter s wheel and reaches in all the directions.

## \|\| 1.52.24 \|\|

*yugākṣakoṭī te tasya dakṣiṇe syandanasya tu \|*  
*ṛgyajurbhyāṃ gṛhītena vicakrāśvena vai dhruve \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The chariot moves like this since crores of yugas. On the right side of the chariot are yoked Rigveda and Yajurveda.

## \|\| 1.52.25 \|\|

*hrasete tasya raśmī tu maṇḍaleṣūttarāyaṇe \|*  
*dakṣiṇe'tha samṛddhe tu bhramato maṇḍalāni tu \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the Sun moves towards the Uttarayana, the rays are short and while moving in the Dakshinayana they get increased.

## \|\| 1.52.26 \|\|

*yugākṣakoṭī te tasya bhramete syandanasya tu \|*  
*saktāsaktaṃ ca bhramate maṇḍalaṃ sarvatodiśam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thus the chariot wheel rotating over the axle, becoming circular reaches in all the directions.

## \|\| 1.52.27 \|\|

*ākṛṣyete dhruveṇeha samaṃ tiṣṭhati suvrata \|*  
*tadā sābhyantaraṃ devo bhramate maṇḍalāni tu \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Dhruva attracts all the solar rays, because they are as cold as Dhruva itself. O Suvrata, at that point of time, the Sungod getting seated over the same, moves in a circular way.

## \|\| 1.52.28-30 \|\|

*dhruveṇa mucyamāne tu punā raśmiyugena vai \|*  
*tathaiva 1 bāhyataḥ sūryo bhramate maṇḍalāni tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*aśītimaṇḍalaśataṃ kāṣṭhayorubhayorapi \|*  
*saratho'dhiṣṭhito devairvibhramedṛṣibhiḥ saha \|\| 29 \|\|*

*gandharvairapsarobhiśca sarpagrāmaṇirākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*etairvasati vai sūrye māsau dvau dvau krameṇa tu \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Separated from Dhruva, Surya moves on bolding the reins of the horses in his hand in Uttarayana as well as in Dakshinayana. Thus, the hundred and eighty mandalas are formed. Surya is accompanied by the gods, Rishis, Gandharvas, Apsaras, serpents and chiefs of the Rakshasas in turn for period of two months each.

## \|\| 1.52.31-34 \|\|

*dhātāryamā pulastyaśca pulahaśca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*khaṇḍako vāsukiścaiva sakarṇo raśmireva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tumbururnāradaścaiva gandharvau gāyatāṃ varau \|*  
*kratusthalāpsaraścaiva yā ca sā puñjikasthalā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*grāmaṇīrathakṛtsnaśca rathaujāśvatarāvubhau \|*  
*rakṣo hetiḥ prahetiśca yātudhānau ca tāvubhau \|\| 33 \|\|*

*madhumādhavayoreṣa gaṇo vasati bhāskare \|*  
*tathā grīṣmau tu dvau māsau mitraśca varuṇaśca ha \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. As Dhata, Aryama, Pulastya, Khandaka, Vasuki, Tumburu and Narada well-versed in singing and music, Gandharvas, Kratusthala, Punjikasthala, Gramani, Rathauja, both the horses, Yatudhanas — Rakshaheti and Praheti, and all the ganas are lodged close to the Sun in the months of Chaitra and Vaishakha.

## \|\| 1.52.35-39 \|\|

*ṛṣiratrirvaśiṣṭhaśca takṣako'nanta eva ca \|*  
*menakā sahajanyā ca gaṃdharvo ca hahā hūhūḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*rathasvanaśca grāmaṇyau rathacitraśca tāvubhau \|*  
*pauruṣeyo vadhaścaiva yātudhānau mahābalau \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śuciśukrau tu dvau māsau vasantyete divākare \|*  
*indraścaiva vivasvāṃśca aṅgirā bhṛgureva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*elāparṇastathā sarpaḥ śaṅkhapālaśca pannagāḥ \|*  
*pramlocā dundukāścaiva gandharvau bhānudardurau \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yātudhānau tathā sarpastathā brāhmaśca tāvubhau \|*  
*ete nabho nabhasyau ca nivasanti divākare \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. Similarly, during the months of Jyeshtha and Ashadha, Rishis Atri and Vasishtha, Takshaka, Ananta, Menaka, Gandharvas known as Haha-Huha, Rathsvana and Rathachitra both the Gramains, Paurusheya and Vadha, besides the valorous Yatudhanas, accompany the sun during these two months. During the rainy season, Indra, Vivasvan, Angira, Bhrigu, Elaparna and Shankhapala — the serpents, Pralocha, Gandharvas — Dunduka, Bhanu and Dardura, Yathudhana, the serpents, Brahma, Nabha and Nabhasya accompany the sun.

## \|\| 1.52.40-43 \|\|

*śaradyete punaḥ śubhrā nivasanti sma devatāḥ \|*  
*parjanyaścaiva pūṣā ca bhāradvājaḥ sagautamaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*citrasenaśca gandharvastathā vasuruciśca yaḥ \|*  
*viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca te ubhe puṇyalakṣaṇe \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nāgastvairāvataścaiva viśrutaśca dhanañjayaḥ \|*  
*senajicca suṣeṇaśca senānīrgrāmaṇīstathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*āpo vātaśca dvāvetau yātudhānau prakīrtitau \|*  
*vasantyete tu vai sūrye iṣorjau kālaparyayāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. During winter, the white gods, Parjanya, Pusha, Bharadvaja, Gautama, Chitrasena, Gandharva, Vasuruchi, Vashvachi, Dhritachi, elephant Airavata, Dhananjaya, Senajit, Sushena, Gramani, Vata and both the Yatudhanas, accompany the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.52.45-49 \|\|

*bhujaṅgaśca mahāpadmaḥ sarpaḥ karkoṭakastathā \|*  
*āpo vātaśca dvāvetau yātudhānau prakīrtitau \|\| 45 \|\|*

*citrāṅgadaśca gandharvoruṇāyuścaiva tāvubhau \|*  
*sahe caiva sahasye ca vasantyete divākare \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pūṣā jiṣṇurjamadagnirviśvāmitrastathaiva ca \|*  
*kādraveyau mahānāgau kambalāśvatarāvubhau \|\| 47 \|\|*

*gandharvo dhṛtarāṣṭraśca sūryavārcāśca tāvubhau \|*  
*tilottamā ca rambhā ca sarvaloke ca viśrute \|\| 48 \|\|*

*1 grāmaṇīḥ senajiccaiva satyajicca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*brahmopetaśca vai rakṣo yajño yajñastathaiva ca \|*  
*ete tapastapasyai ca nivasanti divākare \|\| 49 \|\|*

45-49. In the autumn season, Amsha, Bhaga, Kashyapa, Kratu, Bhujanga, Mahapadma, Karkotaka, Yatudhanas known as Apa and Vata, Chitrangada and Arunayu Gandharvas, accompany him. At the end of the winter season, Pusha, Jishnu, Jamadagni, Vishvamitra, Kambala, the sons of Kadru, Ashvadara Gandharva, Dhritarashtra, Suryavarcha, Tillottama, Rambha, Senajit, Satyajit and all the yajnas with Brahma accompany the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.52.50 \|\|

*anye'pi ye mandehā rākṣasādhipatayo devadevaguhyatamasya rakṣārthaṃ sakala devairasmadādibhiḥ \|*  
*sanniyuktāstānbhavate kathayāmi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thus, for the protection of the Sungod, all the gods and the ganas of the Rakshasas, besides their lords are also there and I am going to speak about them.

## \|\| 1.52.51 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*vada brahmankathāṃ divyāṃ yāmahaṃ praṣṭumāgataḥ \|*  
*tāmeva vistareṇaiva kathayāśu mama prabho \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Rudra said — O Brahman, the divine episode knowing about which I had arrived here, you kindly relate the same to me in detail.

## \|\| 1.52.52 \|\|

*diviṣṭhaṃ bhāskaraṃ dṛṣṭvā nametkena vidhānataḥ \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ tasya vā deva samāpte bhavati karmaṇi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In which way salutation should be offered to the Sungod on looking at him in the sky and by so doing what type of the reward is achieved by a person?

## \|\| 1.52.53 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rudra samāsena bhāskarasya natikriyām \|*  
*yāṃ kṛtvā rogaduḥkhārtā mucyante pāpasañcayāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Brahma said-I am going to speak out the method of offering salutation to the Sungod, which relieves a person of all the ailments, sins and miseries. You please listen to the same.

## \|\| 1.52.54-56 \|\|

*sthaṇḍile maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā dvādaśāṅgulamānataḥ \|*  
*sadyo gomayalipte ca tatraivāvāhayedravim \|\| 54 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā gaṇeśādīnvāsudevaṃ ca sātyakim \|*  
*satyabhāmāṃ tathā lakṣmīmumāṃ devīṃ ca śaṅkaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

*maṇḍalasya samīpasthānpūrvoktānvedamantravit \|*  
*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya daṇḍavatpraṇametsakṛt \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. A circle of twelve angulas should be formed on earth, purifying it with the plaster of cowdung. The Sungod should be invoked in the same. Then Ganesha, Vasudeva, Satyaki, Satyabhama, Lakshmi, goddess Uma and lord Shiva should be invoked therein. Then he should go round the circle and then offer salutation to Surya prostrating on the ground.

## \|\| 1.52.57 \|\|

*śataṃ sahasramayutaṃ lakṣaṃ vā nijapāpataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śaktiṃ praṇamyātha sadā saṃyatamānasaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Keeping in view one’s sins, salutation should be made to the Sungod a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand or a lakh of times.

## \|\| 1.52.58-61 \|\|

*viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyānnirucchvāsaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*raktike ca hiraṇyasya śatamātre sahasrake \|\| 58 \|\|*

*māṣakāṇāṃ catuṣkaṃ cāyutaṃ daśaguṇaṃ diśet \|*  
*dakṣe daśaguṇaṃ proktaṃ dadyādrogavimuktaye \|\| 59 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛte virūpākṣa sarvarogādvimucyate \|*  
*idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ śṛṇuyādyo hi mānavaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tasya rogā vinaśyanti mārtaṇḍasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*anyacca te pravakṣyāmi yaccāpṛṣṭamumāpate \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva mayā proktaṃ rathayantṛniyāmakam \|\| 61 \|\|*

58-61. There is also a provision for giving dakshina to a Brahmana. He should not resort to deep breathing, nor should he repent. After offering salutation for a hundred times, one should give away a small quantity (two rattis) of gold. After offering salutation for a thousand times, one gram of gold should be given. After offering salutation for ten thousand times, one should give away gold equivalent to two grams; and when someone offers salutation for ten thousand times, he should give away gold ten times of the earlier quantity. After offering salutation a lakh of times, one should give away ten times gold of the earlier quantity. By so doing, all the ailments suddenly get removed. O Virupaksha, one who completes this process appropriately, he gets relieved of all the ailments. The people who listen to this top secret, they get relieved of all the ailments by the grace of the Sungod. O lord of Uma, I am also speaking about the chariot, charioteer and the controller, about whom no question has been asked.

## Chapter 53. Description of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.53.1-6 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tatrāruṇo mayā pūrvaṃ sārathye sanniyojitaḥ \|*  
*indreṇa māṭharo nāma vāyunā kalmaṣeṇa tu \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gāyatrī sāvitrī rathe sthite ubhe sandhye sadā sā devatā yā ravimaṇḍalaṃ nāpaiti \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vaiśākhena rājñā vasubhidāyudhāṅgārikau dvau agninā piṅgalaḥ \|*  
*saṃyantā mahādaṇḍāyudho bhavatā śeṣo mahāgaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*hasto yamena pāśahastombupatinā samindhanaḥ \|*  
*alakādhipatinā viṣṇuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*aśvibhyāṃ kālopakālau vākṣapradhānakau \|*  
*naranārāyaṇābhyāṃ kṣārau dhārau dhiṣaṇakṛṣṇau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vairājaśaṅkhapālaparjanyarajasāṃ diśāsu vidiśāsu diśāṃ pālanaṃ viśvedevā daduḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Brahma said — Initially, Aruna had been deputed by me to serve as a charioteer for that chariot. Similarly, Indra deputed Mathara (an attendant), the wind god gave the serpent, while Garuda gave Tarkshya, with the nails and beak as his weapons who fly in the front. Kala — the god of death gave away a Mahadanda. Vasu gave away the fiery weapon for penetration. Agni gave Pingala. Yama gave his Yamadanda. Varuna gave a noose, Kubera gave Vishnu, Ashvinikumaras gave away Kala and Upakala. Nara-Narayana gave him Vaksha and Pradhana. Vishvedevas gave Dhishana and Krishna. Besides Vairaja Shankhapala and Parjanya were given for the protection of directions and sub-directions.

## \|\| 1.53.7 \|\|

*saptaitā lokamātaraḥ sarvamaruto'dadan \|*  
*oṃkāro vaṣaṭkāro vedanisvanaḥ pinākī vināyakaḥ śeṣo'nanto vāsukiśca nāgasahasreṇātmatulyenādityasya rathamanuyānti 1 \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly, the seven Matrikas also gave all the Veda, Omkara-Vasatkara, Shiva gave Vinayaka, Shesha gave Ananta and Vasuki — the serpents who were as powerful as the thousands of the Nagas. All of them always follow the chariot of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.53.8 \|\|

*bhagavantaṃ sahasrakiraṇamavalambitum \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, Gayatri, Savitri and both the Sandhyas, there is no other deity who does not follow the Surya-mandala, which issues thousands of sun rays.

## \|\| 1.53.9-11 \|\|

*etadvai sarvadaivatyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ brahmavādinaṃ brahmayajñavādinīṃ yajñaḥ \|*  
*bhagavadbhaktānāṃ paramādityoyaṃ viṣṇurmāheśvarāṇām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sthānābhimānino hyete sadā vai vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*sūryamāpyāyayantyete tejasāṃ teja uttamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*grathitaiḥ svairvacobhistu stuvante ṛṣayo ravim \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasaścaiva gītanṛtyairupāsate \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. This mandala has been formed by all the gods. All those who are well-versed in Brahman or those who are form of Brahman, the performers of yajnas, the devotees of Vishnu, with the feelings of Paramaditya Vishnu and Maheshvara who bestow welfare on all, O Shiva — the bull-bannered one, by achieving the illustrious Sungod, all the ganas get fond of their respective positions and add to the lustre of the Sun. Not only this, the ascetics also offering prayers, Gandharvas and Apsaras with their songs and dance, sing the glory of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.53.12-13 \|\|

*viyadbhramaṇato rakṣāṃ kurvaṃti sma iṣugraham \|*  
*sarpā vahanti vai sūryaṃ yātudhānāstu yānti ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vālakhilyā 1 namantyetaṃ paricāryodayādravim \|*  
*divaspatiḥ svabhūścobhau agragau yojanasya tu \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. All of them fly in the sky for the protection of the Sun. The serpents turn themselves into the rays and carry the chariot, while the Rakshasas follow it. The Valakhilyas on the other hand on the pretext of rendering service, offer their salutation from all the sides. Similarly, Divaspati and Svayambhu move ahead of the chariot at a distance of a yojana.

## \|\| 1.53.14 \|\|

*bhargo'tha dakṣiṇe pārśve kañjajo vāmataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*sarve te pṛṣṭhagā jñeyā grahā lokeṣu pūjitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then Bharga is on the right side, Brahma is on the left. All other planets move to his right.

## \|\| 1.53.15-16 \|\|

*uparāgaśikhī cobhāvagrato nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*manuṣyadharmā dakṣiṇata uttareṇa pracetasaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sambhavanti tathā kṛṣṇa ubhāvetau sadāgragau \|*  
*vāmena vītihotrastu pṛṣṭhatastu hariḥ sadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Rahu and Ketu move in front of the chariot, Kubera moves to the south and Varuna to the north. Thus, both of them, besides Krishna move ahead. Vitihotra remains on the right and Hari follows him.

## \|\| 1.53.17-19 \|\|

*rathapīṭhe kṣamā jñeyā antarāle nabhastathā \|*  
*āśritya rathajāṃ kāntiṃ khaṃ divaḥ samayaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhvajo daṇḍaśca vijñeyo dhvajāgre vṛṣa eva ca \|*  
*ṛddhirvṛddhistathā śrīśca patākā pārvatīpriya \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dhvajadaṇḍāgre garuḍastadagre varuṇālayaḥ \|*  
*mainākaśchatradaṇḍastu himavāṃśchatramucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. O beloved of Parvati, earth is on the back of the chariot, the sky is in the middle, the heaven is the lustre of the chariot, danda is flag, dharma is lodged in the flag of the chariot, besides Riddhi (progress), Siddhi (success) and Shri (fortunes) are the banners. Garuda serves as the flag post, which remains in front. Varuna is lodged in front of them. O intelligent one, Mainaka is the part of Chatra while Himavan is the Umbrella. This is the opinion of the majority of the people.

## \|\| 1.53.20 \|\|

*kecidevaṃ vadantīha loke cānye mahāmate \|*  
*chatradaṇḍastathā kleśaḥ kleśaṃ chatraṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. But some people are of the opinion that anguish is the rod of the chatra as well as the chatra itself.

## \|\| 1.53.21 \|\|

*eteṣāmeva devānāṃ yathā vīryaṃ tathā tapaḥ \|*  
*yathāyogaṃ tathā sattvaṃ yathā sattvaṃ tathā balam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. According to the process of these gods, there is tapas. Yoga is the form of the Sattva, while Sattva is the form of prowess.

## \|\| 1.53.22 \|\|

*tathā tapatyasau sūryasteṣāṃ siddhaḥ svatejasā \|*  
*ete tapanti varṣanti yānti viśvaṃ sṛjanti ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Because of their prowess, the Sungod shines with their lustre. All the gods also shine accordingly and drop rains.

## \|\| 1.53.23 \|\|

*bhūtānāmaśubhaṃ karma vyapohanti ca kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ete sahaiva sūryeṇa bhramante sānugā divi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Accordingly, there occurs the destruction of the good and bad deeds, while moving with the Sun.

## \|\| 1.53.24 \|\|

*tapantaśca japantaśca hlādayantaśca vai dvijāḥ \|*  
*gopāyanti sma bhūtāni iha te hyanukampayā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Brahmanas too, with the strength of their tapas and japam, pleasing you, protect the creatures by your grace.

## \|\| 1.53.25 \|\|

*prīṇāti devānamṛtena sūryaḥ somena sūktena vivardhayitvā \|*  
*śuklena pūrṇā divasakrameṇa taṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe vibudhāḥ pibanti \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Though the Sungod with his rays, extracts the nectar like rays of the moon who on the full moon day increases his glory and then make the gods to consume the nectar during the dark fortnight who get pleased with the same.

## \|\| 1.53.26 \|\|

*pītaṃ hi somaṃ dvikalāvaśeṣaṃ kṛṣṇe tu pakṣe rucibhirjvalantam \|*  
*sudhāmṛtaṃ tatpitaraḥ pibanti ūrjāśca saumyāśca tathaiva kalpāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Still with the consumption of the nectar by the gods, they attain all the glory. Then only two kalas of the lustre or rays of the moon are left out in the dark fortnight, which are consumed by the manes.

## \|\| 1.53.27 \|\|

*sūryeṇa gobhiśca samṛddhitābhiradbhiḥ punaścaiva samujjitābhiḥ \|*  
*tathauṣadhībhiḥ satataṃ pibanti atyantapānena kṣudhā jayanti \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Sungod with his rays, extracts the water from the earth which is filled with water. The same water is dropped by the Sungod in the form of rain, by which the herbs are grown, and consuming which the hunger is subsided. The manes also consume the same.

## \|\| 1.53.28 \|\|

*māsārdhatṛptistu matābhiradbhirmāsena tṛptiḥ svadhayā pitṝṇām \|*  
*annena śaśvadvidadhāti martyaṃ tvayaṃ jagaccaiva bibharti gobhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. With the same rain water, with the water released by Svadha, the manes get satisfied during the entire month. The cereals produced with the rain satisfy the hunger of the humans. Similarly, the sun with his rays feeds the entire world.

## \|\| 1.53.29 \|\|

*ahorātraṃ rathenāsāvekacakreṇa vai bhraman \|*  
*saptadvīpasamudrāntāṃ saptabhiśca hayaiḥ saha \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The chariot of the sun has a single wheel which is driven by seven horses. Seated in the said chariot, the Sungod travels through all the seven continents and their oceans in a day and night

## \|\| 1.53.30-31 \|\|

*chandobhirvājirūpaistairyataścakraṃ tataḥ sthitaiḥ \|*  
*kāmarūpaiḥ sakṛdyuktairantarasthairmanojavaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*haribhiravyayairvaśyai kṣudhāśramavivarjitaiḥ \|*  
*dvyaśītimaṇḍalaśatamīhantyabdena vai hayāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The horses which are yoked in the chariot of the Sun are the form of Chandas, and are quite beautiful. They move with the speed of the mind, are always powerful, well controlled, free from hunger and thirst. They cover the journey of a hundred and eighty two masalas in a year.

## \|\| 1.53.32 \|\|

*bāhyato'bhyantaraṃ caiva maṇḍalaṃ divasakramāt \|*  
*kalpādau samprayuktāste vahantyābhūtasamplavam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In this way, with the sequence of days, the horses, with the start of the kalpa, move on to their journey, which is continued upto the time of dissolution forming the outer and the inner circles.

## \|\| 1.53.33-36 \|\|

*āvṛtā bālakhilyaistairbhramanti tānyahāni tu \|*  
*grathitaiḥ svairvacobhistu stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sevyate nṛtyagītaiśca gandharvairapsarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*pataṅgaḥ patagairaśvairvasate bhramayandivi \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vīthyāgryayā vicarate nakṣatrāṇi yathā śaśī \|*  
*madhyagāścāmarāvatyāṃ yadā bhavati bhāskaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vaivasvate saṃyamane uttiṣṭhandṛśyate tadā \|*  
*sukhāyāmardharātraṃ tu vibhāyāmastameti ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. At that point of time, as the Balakhilyas surround the chariot, the Rishis offer the prayers, while the Gandharvas and Apsaras dance and sing, similarly the Sungod passing through the moon and other constellations, moves on. Thus with the use of the high speed chariot, the Sungod moves in the sky. When the sun has noon time in Amaravati, at the same time it is the sunrise in the abode of Yama, midnight in the abode of Varuna and sunset in Vibhapuri of the moon.

## \|\| 1.53.37-39 \|\|

*vaivasvate saṃyamane madhyamastu raviryadā \|*  
*sukhāyāmatha vāruṇyāmuttiṣṭhandṛśyate tadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*rātryardhaṃ cāmarāvatyāmastameti yamasya vai \|*  
*somapuryāṃ vibhāyāṃ tu madhyagaścāryamā yadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*māhendrasyāmarāvatyāmuttiṣṭhati divākaraḥ \|*  
*ardharātraṃ saṃyamane vāruṇyāmastameti ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Similarly, when there is noon time in Yamapuri, at the same time it is sunrise in Sukhanagari, while in Amaravati it is the midnight. In the Vibhanagari when it is noon time, in Amaravati it is the time of sunrise In Yamapuri when it is midnight, then at Varuna’s place it is sunset.

## \|\| 1.53.40 \|\|

*evaṃ caturṣu pārśveṣu meroḥ kurvanpradakṣiṇam \|*  
*udayāstamane cāsāvuttiṣṭhati punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Thus while going round the Meru mountain, the sun rises and sets repeatedly.

## \|\| 1.53.41 \|\|

*pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇe ca dvau dvau devālayau punaḥ \|*  
*tapatyekaṃ tu madhyāhne tābhireva gabhastibhiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The first part of the day (forenoon) and the afternoon are supposed to be the two types of temples in which the Sungod shines his rays.

## \|\| 1.53.42 \|\|

*udito vardhamānābhirāmadhyāhnāttapedraviḥ \|*  
*tataḥ paraṃ hrasantībhirgobhirastaṃ niyacchati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The Sun till the time of sunrise to noon time, seats with the increase in his rays. In the later half, he with the decline of his rays, sets in the evening.

## \|\| 1.53.43 \|\|

*yatrodyandṛśyate sūryaḥ sa teṣāmudayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*praṇāśaṃ gacchate yatra sa teṣāmastamucyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The direction from which the Sun rises is known as the eastern direction. The direction in which the sun sets is known as the western direction.

## \|\| 1.53.44 \|\|

*evaṃ puṣkaramadhyena tadā sarpati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*triṃśadbhāgaṃ tu medinyā muhūrtena sa gacchati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus the Sun moves in the middle of Pushkara and in a muhurta in the scale of the expansion of the earth, he covers a thirteenth part of the distance.

## \|\| 1.53.45-47 \|\|

*yojanāgreṇa saṅkhyāṃ 1 tu muhūrtasya nibodha me \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ śatasahasrāśaṃ sahasraṃ tu trilocana \|\| 45 \|\|*

*pañcāśacca tathālpāni sahasrāṇyadhikāni tu \|*  
*mauhūrtiko gatirhyeṣā sūryasya tu vidhīyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yojanānāṃ sahasre dve dve śate dve ca yojane \|*  
*nimeṣāntaramātreṇa divi sūryaḥ prasarpati \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. O three eyed lord, thus with the scale of a yojana, the Sun travels a lakh and a half yojanas in a single muhurta. The Sun can travel a distance of more than five thousand yojanas in a very short time, such is the speed of the moving of the Sun. The distance travelled by him in a moment is two thousand and two hundred yojanas.

## \|\| 1.53.48 \|\|

*sa śīghrameva paryeti bhāskaro'lātacakravat \|*  
*bhramanvai bhramamāṇeṣu ṛkṣeṣu vicaratyasau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Like a fire brand disc, the Sun rapidly moves through all the planets and constellation.

## \|\| 1.53.49-51 \|\|

*indraḥ pūjayate sūryamuttiṣṭhantaṃ dine dine \|*  
*madhyāhne ca yamaḥ paścādastaṃ yāntamapāṃ patiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*somastathārdharātre tu sadā pūjayate ravim \|*  
*viṣṇurbhavānahaṃ rudraḥ pūjayāma niśākṣaye \|\| 50 \|\|*

*evamagnirnirṛtiśca vāyurīśāna eva ca \|*  
*pūjayanti krameṇaiva bhramamāṇaṃ divākaram \|*  
*śreyo'rthaṃ devaśārdūla sarve brahmādayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. At the time of sunrise, Indra is to be adored, Yama is adored in the noon, Varuna at sunset, while the moon is worshipped at midnight. O lion among the gods, with the end of the night, Vishnu, water, Rudra, fire, Rakshasas, windgod, Ishana, besides Brahma and other deities worship the sun.

## Chapter 54. The glory of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.54.1 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*aho haṃsasya māhātmyaṃ varṇitaṃ bhavatedṛśam \|*  
*kathyatāṃ punarevedaṃ māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasya tu \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rudra said — Thus listening to the glory of the Sungod from your mouth, my desire has increased. What I desire is that the same glory of the Sungod should be repeated to me.

## \|\| 1.54.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ādityamantramakhilaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*bhavatyasmājjagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Brahma said — The mantra of Surya is the basic cause of the creation of all the mobile and immobile beings in the world. All the gods, the universe, asuras and demons were created out of it

## \|\| 1.54.3 \|\|

*rudrendropendracandrāṇāṃ viprendratridivaukasām \|*  
*mahādyutimatāṃ kṛtsnaṃ tejo yatsārvalaukikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Thus Indra, Rudra, Vishnu, the moon, and all other gods actually possess the lustre of the Sun, because his lustre is spread in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.54.4 \|\|

*sarvātmā sarvalokeśo devadevaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*sūrya eṣa trilokasya mūlaṃ paramadaivatam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Because of Surya’s being the soul of all, the lord of all the lokas, the supreme lord besides being Prajapati, he happens to be the great god of all the lokas.

## \|\| 1.54.5 \|\|

*agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhati \|*  
*ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This is because the offerings made in the fire, actually reaches the Sungod. He causes the rain to fall. From the rains grow the cereals and with the food, the creatures gain their lives.

## \|\| 1.54.6 \|\|

*sūryātprasūyate 1 sarvaṃ tatra caiva pralīyate \|*  
*bhāvābhāvau hi lokānāmādityānniḥsṛtau purā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In this way, all the things grow in the world out of the Sun and they ultimately merge in the same. The creation and the destruction of the universe are within the competence of the Sungod. This has been ordained earlier.

## \|\| 1.54.7 \|\|

*etattu dhyānināṃ dhyānaṃ mokṣaṃ cāpyeṣa mokṣiṇām \|*  
*atra gacchanti nirvāṇaṃ jāyante'smātpunaḥ prajāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He alone is the aim of those who meditate upon in the world, besides being the place of final beatitude, who meditate for the purpose. The liberation is also achieved through him.

## \|\| 1.54.8 \|\|

*kṣaṇā muhūrtā divasā niśāḥ pakṣāśca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*māsāḥ saṃvatsarāścaiva ṛtavo'tha yugāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The moments, muhurtas, days, nights, fortnights, months, years, seasons and the yugas and their management is not possible without the Sun.

## \|\| 1.54.9-11 \|\|

*sadādityādṛte hyeṣā kālasaṅkhyā na vidyate \|*  
*kālādṛte na niyamo 2 nāgnirna havanakriyā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*3 ṛtūnāmavibhāgācca puṣpamūlaphalaṃ kutaḥ \|*  
*kutaḥ sasyaviniṣpattistṛṇauṣadhigaṇāḥ 4 kutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*abhāvo vyavahārāṇāṃ jantūnāṃ divi ceha ca \|*  
*jagatpratapanamṛte bhāskaraṃ vāritaskaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Without the management of time, the niyamas, fire, homas, and without the divisions of the seasons, the flowers, the roots, cereals, the grass, herbs and the human activities of the present and the future worlds, cannot be established in reality without the Sun.

## \|\| 1.54.12 \|\|

*nāvṛṣṭyā tapate sūryo nāvṛṣṭyā pariviśyate \|*  
*nāvṛṣṭyā vikṛtiṃ dhatte vāriṇā dīpyate raviḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The heating up of the Sun without rains, the sky getting overcast with clouds and other alterations are not possible without the Sun, because the Sun shines with the water alone.

## \|\| 1.54.13-14 \|\|

*vasante kapilaḥ sūryo grīṣme kāñcanasaprabhaḥ \|*  
*śveto varṇena varṣāsu pāṇḍuḥ śaradi bhāskaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*hemante tāmravarṇastu śiśire lohito raviḥ \|*  
*iti varṇāḥ samākhyātāḥ śṛṇu varṇaphalaṃ hara \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. In the spring season, the Sun has the whitish colour; during the summer, it has the golden lustre; during the rainy season it has the white lustre and during the autumn season it has the yellow complexion; during the cold season it is of copper colour, and in the winter season it is of red colour. I am now speaking about the varnas, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.54.15-16 \|\|

*kṛṣṇobhayāya jagatastāmraḥ senāpatiṃ vināśayati \|*  
*pīto narendraputraṃ5 śvetastu purohitaṃ hanti \|\| 15 \|\|*

*citro'tha vāpi dhūmro ravī raśmivyākulaṃ karotyuccaiḥ \|*  
*taskaraśastranipātairyadi na salilamāśu pātayati \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. O Shiva, as the Sun of black colour frightens all. When it is of copper colour it causes destruction of the army commander, and when the sun is of yellow colour it kills the prince of the king. When it is of white colour it destroys the royal priest. Similarly, when it is multi-coloured or of the colour of smoke and in case it does not rain at once, then the people suffer from thieves and pilferers.

## Chapter 55. The travel of the Solar Chariot

## \|\| 1.55.1 \|\|

*yajñaśca dakṣiṇāhīnaḥ saviturna praśasyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rudra said — How should the people perform the Ratha-yatra of Surya and what is the reward thereof, which one gets?

## \|\| 1.55.2 \|\|

*vidhinā kena kartavyā kasminkāle surottama \|*  
*kathaṃ ca bhrāmayeddevaṃ rathārūḍhaṃ2 divākaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O best of the gods, when and at what time should the Ratha-yatra be performed? What should be the method of it? How is the chariot of Surya taken out getting him seated over it?

## \|\| 1.55.3-6 \|\|

*devasya ye rathaṃ bhaktyā bhrāmayanti vahanti ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca kiṃ phalaṃ proktaṃ ye ca nṛtyakarā narāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhramanti ye na ca devena nṛtyagītaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*prajāgaraṃ ca kurvanti bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ ca kiṃ phalaṃ proktaṃ. rathaṃ yacchanti 3 ye raveḥ \|*  
*baliṃ bhaktaṃ ca ye bhaktyā diśantyāhi kabhojanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*etanme brūhi nikhilaṃ surajyeṣṭha savistaram \|*  
*lokānāṃ śreyase deva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. What type of reward is achieved by those, who drive the chariot with dancing and singing besides the awakening in addition to the offering of the food? O best of gods! I am quite anxious to learn about all these activities, besides the people would drive benefit out of the same. Therefore, you kindly narrate all the facts to me in detail.

## \|\| 1.55.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhūteśa gaṇeśo'si trilocana \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā vacmi yathāpraśnaṃ savistaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Brahma said — O lord of the goblins, having three eyes, you happen to be the lord of ganas. Therefore, you have put an excellent question. Therefore, you listen to me attentively. I shall answer in detail to each one of the question.

## \|\| 1.55.8 \|\|

*devasya rathayātreyaṃ bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*indrotsavastathā rudra mayā hyetau prakīrtitau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O Rudra, the Ratha-yatra of Suryadeva and the festival of Indra have already been described by me.

## \|\| 1.55.9-10 \|\|

*martyaloke śāntihetorlokānāṃ lokapūjita \|*  
*pravartitāvubhau yasmindeśe devamahotsavau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na tatropadravāḥ santi rājataskarasambhavāḥ \|*  
*tasmātkāryāvimau bhaktyā durbhikṣasyeha śāntaye \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. O adorable by the world, the land over which these festivals are organized, no torture from the king and no disturbance can be created by his servants. For the neutralization of the draught conditions, the performing of these festivals is necessary.

## \|\| 1.55.11-13 \|\|

*śuklapakṣe tu saptamyāṃ māsi bhādrapade hara \|*  
*ghṛtenābhyaṅgayeddevaṃ pañcapūtāṅgajena vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

*abhyaṅgayedmaheśaṃ yaḥ sarṣapaiḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*dine dine jagannāthaṃ praviṣṭaṃ varṇake ravim \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sa gacchedyānamārūḍho gairikaṃ kiṅkiṇīkṛtam \|*  
*vaiśvānarapuraṃ divyaṃ gandharvāpsaraśobhitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. On the bright seventh moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, ghi with panchagavya should be poured over all the limbs of the Sungod and the one who does so, he achieves travels in a plane, with small bells of gold, issuing pleasant sound and is attended by Gandharvas and Apsaras in the place of the lord almighty,

## \|\| 1.55.14-15 \|\|

*śālyodanaṃ khaṇḍamiśraṃ vajraṃ vajrasamanvitam \|*  
*varṇabhaktaṃ prayacchedyo bhāskarāya dine dine \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ārūḍhaḥ sa vimānaṃ tu jvālāmālākulaṃ śubham \|*  
*gacchenmama puraṃ deva stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. One who offers the Shali rice mixed with sugar with the flowers called vajra, red rice to the Sungod daily, he, getting seated over the lustreful plane, goes to my place where is adored by all the Rishis.

## \|\| 1.55.16 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena bhāskarāya naraḥ śiva \|*  
*varṇabhaktaṃ pradātavyaṃ praviṣṭasyeha varṇakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Therefore, the cooked red rice should always be offered to the Sun in the mandala.

## \|\| 1.55.17-18 \|\|

*ghṛtapūrṇaṃ khaṇḍaveṣṭaṃ kāsāraṃ modakaṃ payaḥ \|*  
*dadhyodanaṃ pāyasaṃ ca saṃyāvaṃ guḍapūpakān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ye prayacchanti devasya bhāskarasyeha varṇakam \|*  
*te gacchanti na sandeho narā vai mandiraṃ mama \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Similarly, one who offers the sweet balls of sugar with ghi, besides milk, curd, cooked rice, payasam, porridge and fired cakes to the Sungod lodged in the mandala with respect, he undoubtedly reaches my place.

## \|\| 1.55.19 \|\|

*ahanyahani yo bhaktyā bhāskarāya prayacchati \|*  
*abhyaṅgāya ghṛtaṃ deyaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person who offers with devotion the ghi for the application over the body, he surely achieves the best of position.

## \|\| 1.55.20 \|\|

*tathā yo varṇabhaktaṃ ca ahanyahani bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sa prāpyeha śubhānkāmāngacchetsa bhavasālayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Similarly, a person who offers the cooked red rice to the Sungod, he getting all his desires fulfilled, achieves finally the place of Surya.

## \|\| 1.55.21 \|\|

*cūrṇamudvartanāyeha yaḥ prayacchecchubhaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo divākaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One who offers the powder for plastering, he achieves the best place with the Sun.

## \|\| 1.55.22-23 \|\|

*tatastaṃ snāpayeddevaṃ pauṣe māsi vidhānataḥ \|*  
*saptamyāṃ śuklapakṣasya śṛṇuṣvaikamanāstathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tīrthodakamupānīya anyadvātha jalaṃ śubham \|*  
*vedoktena vidhānena pratimāṃ sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Similarly, a person who on the bright seventh moon day of the month of Pausha, bathes the Sungod, you listen to the related reward attentively. Bathing the image of Surya with the sacred or other water, his image should be consecrated with the reciting of the Vedic mantras.

## \|\| 1.55.24-31 \|\|

*yajeddhi tīrthanāmāni manasā saṃsmaranbudhaḥ \|*  
*prayāgaṃ puṣkaraṃ devaṃ kurukṣetraṃ ca naimiṣam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pṛthūdakaṃ candrabhāgāṃ śauraṃ gokarṇameva ca \|*  
*brahmāvartaṃ kuśāvartaṃ bilvakaṃ nīlaparvatam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gaṅgādvāraṃ tathā puṇyaṃ gaṅgāsāgarameva ca \|*  
*kālapriyaṃ mitravanaṃ śuṇḍīrasvāminaṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*cakratīrthaṃ tathā puṇyaṃ rāmatīrthaṃ tathā śivam \|*  
*vitastā harṣapaṃthā vai tathā vai devikā smṛtā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*gaṅgā sarasvatī sindhuścandrabhāgā sanarmadā \|*  
*vipāśā yamunā tāpī śivā vetravatī tathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*godāvarī payoṣṇī ca kṛṣṇā veṇyā tathā nadī \|*  
*śatarudrā puṣkariṇī kauśikī sarayūstathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tathānye sāgarāścaiva sānnidhyaṃ kalpayantu vai \|*  
*tathāśramāḥ puṇyatamā divyānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*evaṃ snānavidhiṃ kṛtvā arcayitvā praṇamya ca \|*  
*dhūpamarghyaṃ pradattvā tu pratimāmadhivāsayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

24-31. He should be bathed with the water from Prayaga, Pushkara, Kurukshetra, Naimisha Prithudaka, Chandrabhaga, Shona, Gokarna, Brahmavarta, Kushavarta, Bilvaka, Blue mountain, Haridvara, Kalapriya, Mitravana, Shundirasvamin, Chakratirtha, Ramatirtha Vitasta, Harshapamtha, Devika, Ganga, Sarasvati, Sindhu, Chandrabhaga, Narmada, Vipasha, Yamuna, Tapi, Shiva, Vetravati, Godavari, Payoshni, Krishna, Venya, Shatarudra Pushkarini, Kaushiki, Sarayu and other rivers besides the sacred water of the temples with images, and then he should perform puja, salutation, offering the incense, and arghya. The image should then be consecrated.

## \|\| 1.55.32-33 \|\|

*trirātraṃ saptarātraṃ vā māsaṃ māsārdhameva ca \|*  
*sthitaṃ snānagṛhe devaṃ pūjayedbhaktito naraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*catvare lepayedvediṃ caturasrāṃ śubhe kṛtām \|*  
*caturdiśaṃ śvetakumbhairvitānavaraśobhitām \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Thus by bathing on the third, seventh, fifteenth, or after a month, with devotion, the Sungod should be worshipped. A square altar should be made over a pedestal and should be plastered with the cowdung, it should be decorated with white colour on all the four sides. The image should be worshipped at that very place.

## \|\| 1.55.34 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe tu māghasya saptamyāṃ tripurāṃtaka \|*  
*kṛtvāgnikāryaṃ vidhivatkṛtvā brāhmaṇabhojanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O destroyer of Tripura, on the black seventh moon day of the month of Magha, the homa and worship of Surya should be performed, besides serving food to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.55.35-36 \|\|

*śaṅkhabherīninādaistu brahmaghoṣaiśca puṣkalaiḥ \|*  
*puṇyāhaghoṣavividhairbrāhmaṇānsvasti vācya ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tato'sya parayā bhaktyā sūryasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*rathena darśanīyena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*sūryaśca bhrāmayeddevaṃ mahotsavapuraḥsaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Playing on the conches and drums, the Sungod should be invoked, reciting the welfare mantras and the hymns from the Vedas. The chariot of the Sungod should be moved through the city with dangling bells. The festivities should therefore, be observed appropriately.

## \|\| 1.55.37-39 \|\|

*śuklapakṣe tu māghasya rathamāropayedravim \|*  
*kṛtvāgnihomaṃ vidhivattathā brāhmaṇabhojanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prīṇayitvā janaṃ sarvaṃ dakṣiṇābhojanādinā \|*  
*prapūjya brāhmaṇāndivyānbhaumāṃścāpi suvācakān \|\| 38 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vācako brāhmaṇottamaḥ \|*  
*tato devaśca iṣṭaśca sampūjyo yatnatastadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Similarly, during the month of Magha, on the bright seventh moon day, the Sungod should be placed over the chariot performing the homa and worship besides serving food to the Brahmanas. All other people should also be served with eatables and dakshina. Thereafter, they pleasing them, Bhauma and five other Brahmanas, and orators well-versed in the scriptures, should be adored. Thereafter, the performer should worship his family deity.

## \|\| 1.55.40 \|\|

*māghasya śuklapakṣasya pañcamyāmekabhaktakam \|*  
*ayācitaṃ caturthyāṃ tu ṣaṣṭhyāṃ naktaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On the bight moon day of the month of Margashirsha, one should consume the begged food. On the fifth moon day, one should take food once a day and on the sixth moon day, one should fast during the night.

## \|\| 1.55.41 \|\|

*saptamyāmupavāsaṃ tu āśramādropayedratham \|*  
*agnikāryaṃ tu vai kṛtvā rathasya purataḥ śiva \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O lord Shiva, thus fasting on the seventh moon day, one should perform homa before the chariot Then it should be moved.

## \|\| 1.55.42-45 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca rātrau bhūteśa rathasyehādhivāsanam \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā tu divyānbhaumāṃśca vācakān \|\| 42 \|\|*

*rathamāropayeddevaṃ saptamyāṃ bhūtabhāvanam \|*  
*sitāyāṃ māghamāse tu tasya devālayāgrataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tatrasthasyaiva devasya kuryādrātrau prajāgaram \|*  
*nānāvidhaiḥ prekṣaṇakairdīpavṛkṣopaśobhitaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śaṃkhatūryaninādaiśca brahmaghoṣaiśca puṣkalaiḥ \|*  
*kuryātprajāgaraṃ bhaktyā devasya purato niśi \|\| 45 \|\|*

42-45. O lord of the bhutas, initially on the night of the sixth moon day, Bhauma and the orators of the scripture should be served with food and the chariot should be made to rest. On the bright seventh moon day of the month of Margashirsha, the Sungod should be made to occupy the same chariot and the attractive lamps should be lighted. The trees should also be decorated with lamps. The musical instruments with the reciting of the Vedas should be played upon. With the blowing of conches and the beating of the drums, one should keep an awakening during the whole night.

## \|\| 1.55.46-48 \|\|

*tato'ṣṭamyāṃ ca yatnena devaṃ rathagataṃ nayet \|*  
*nagarasyottaraṃ dvāraṃ śaṅkhabherī nināditam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tataḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ ca dvāraṃ cāpi tathā param \|*  
*evaṃ hi kriyamāṇāyāṃ yātrāyāṃ vatsarāvadhau \|\| 47 \|\|*

*mānavāḥ sukhamedhante rājā jayati cāhitān \|*  
*nīrujaśca janāḥ sarve gavāṃ śāntirbhavettathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. Then on the eighth moon day, making all the efforts, the chariot should be drawn with the sound of conches and playing of drums, towards the north of the city. It should then be taken towards the east and then to the south. From there, it should be taken towards the west. Thus with the performing of the yatra for a year, a king overpowers an enemy, the people are relieved of their ailments and the cows get peaceful.

## \|\| 1.55.49 \|\|

*kartārabhrāpi yātrāyāḥ syargabhāgo bhavanti hi \|*  
*voḍhāraśca tathā vatsa sūryalokaṃ yajanti vai \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The people who participate in the yatra reside in the heaven and the people who drive the chariot, attain the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.55.50 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ sañcālyate brahmansthāpitā pratibhā sakṛt \|*  
*etanme vada deveśa sumahānsaṃśayo hi me \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Rudra said — O god of gods, when an image is once established then how is it manage thereafter? I have developed a great doubt in this regard, therefore, you kindly remove the same.

## \|\| 1.55.51 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*pūrvameva sahasrāṃśoryānahetormahātmanaḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsarasyāvayavaiḥ 1 kalpito'sya ratho mayā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Brahma said — I have initially spoken about the chariot which is built according to the months of the year or the parts of the same.

## \|\| 1.55.52-54 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ tu rathānāṃ vai sa rathaḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tatastvanye syandanā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kalpitāḥ sarvadevānāṃ somādīnāmanekaśaḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmakṛtaṃ prāpya rathaṃ devena putraka \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pūjārthamātmano dattaṃ manave satkulodvaha \|*  
*manunekṣvākave dattaṃ martyaiḥ sampūjyatāṃ raviḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. Since all the parts of the chariot were created before the chariot, therefore, Vishvakarma built the divine chariot of the gods on the basis of the same. O son, the chariot built by Vishvakarma was received by the Sungod and after so doing, he handed it over to Manu for worship, who passed it on to Ikshvaku, Therefore, all the people should worship the chariot.

## \|\| 1.55.55 \|\|

*atastu rathayānena 1 cālanaṃ vihitaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*tasmānna cālane doṣaḥ savituścala eva saḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. With the driving of the chariot, the movement of the Sun was organized. Therefore, there is no blemish in the movement of the Sungod, because he has been termed as the god who н always on the move.

## \|\| 1.55.56 \|\|

*yasmādrathena paryeti bhāskaraḥ pṛthivīmimām \|*  
*gacchanna dṛśyate caitanmaṇḍalaṃ savitustathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The chariot by which the Sungod crosses the world, no one is able to visualize the same. Similarly, no one is in a position to visualize the Surya-mandala.

## \|\| 1.55.57-59 \|\|

*adṛṣṭaṃ calate yasmāttasmādvai pārvatīpriya \|*  
*tadevaṃ rathayātrāsu dṛṣṭaṃ bhānormanīṣibhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*anyeṣāṃ cālanaṃ neṣṭaṃ devānāṃ pārvatīpriya \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ sthāpitānāṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tasmādrathena devasya yātrā kāryā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*prajānāmiha śāntyarthaṃ pratisaṃvatsaraṃ sadā \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. O beloved of Parvati, therefore, in order to visualize his movement, the people organize the Ratha-yatra. Similarly, with the consecrating of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, their movements do not become visible. Therefore, with the purpose of bestowing peace over the people, the Ratha-yatra of the Sungod should be organized every year.

## \|\| 1.55.60-63 \|\|

*kāñcano vātha raupyo vā dṛḍhadārumayo'pi vā \|*  
*dṛḍhākṣayugacakraśca rathaḥ kāryaḥ suyantritaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tasmin rathavare śreṣṭhe kalpite sumanorame \|*  
*āropya pratimāṃ yatnādyojayedvājinaḥ śubhān \|\| 61 \|\|*

*harillakṣaṇasampannānsumukhānvaśavartinaḥ \|*  
*kuṅkumena samālabdhāṃścāmarasragvibhūṣitān \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sadaśvānyojayitvā tu rathasyārghyaṃ pradāya ca \|*  
*vibudhāmpūjayityā tu dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. The chariot should be made of solid wood, decorated with the gold and silver. Its yokes and axle should be quite solid. Then decorating the chariot, the image of the Sungod should be consecrated in the same. The beautiful steed of green colour should be yoked in it. The saffron should be applied over them and should be decorated with garlands and flywhisks. After yoking the horses, the gods should be adored offering arghya to them, besides incense and garland of sandal. After worshipping the chariot, it should then be made to move.

## \|\| 1.55.64 \|\|

*āhārairvividhaiścāpi bhojayitvā dvijottamān \|*  
*dīnāndhakṛpaṇādīṃśca sarvānsaṃtarpya śaktitaḥ2 \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then the Brahmanas should be served with the best of food of various types. The poor, blind and helpless people should also be pleased with essential articles. This is essential.

## \|\| 1.55.65 \|\|

*na kañcidvimukhaṃ kuryāduttamādhamamadhyamam \|*  
*sūryakratau tu vitate evamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The learned people have ordained that in the yajna of Surya, all the people of high, middle and lower classes should be equally entertained. None of them should leave the place getting dissatisfied.

## \|\| 1.55.66 \|\|

*yaścintayati bhagnāśaḥ kṣudhāvātaprapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*adāturhi pitṝṃstena svargasthānapi pātayet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Because a person residing there, if leaves disappointed or hungry or thirsty, then the manes of the performer inspite of their remaining in the heaven, fall into the hell and have to face miseries.

## \|\| 1.55.67 \|\|

*tasmānnānāvidhaiḥ kāmairbhakṣyalehyasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The performing of the yajna of Surya, without giving dakshina to the deserving participants, cannot be appreciated. Therefore, the excellent food with various types of delicious dishes should be served to all the participants.

## \|\| 1.55.68-70 \|\|

*pūjayitvā janaṃ sarvamimamuccārayenmanum \|*  
*baliṃ gṛhṇantu me devā ādityā vasavastathā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*marutothāśvinau rudrāḥ suparṇāḥ pannagā grahāḥ \|*  
*asurā yātudhānāśca2 rathasthā yāstu devatāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*digpālā lokapālāśca ye ca vighnavināyakāḥ \|*  
*jagataḥ svasti kurvaṃtu ye ca divyā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. Worshipping the gods again, one should say thus — “All the Adityas, Vasus, Maruts, Ashvinikumaras, Rudra, Garuda, the serpents, planets, Asuras and Yatudhanas and all the gods lodged in the chariot besides Dikpalas and Lokapalas, Vighna Vinayaka and the divine great Rishis, should accept the offerings and bestow welfare.

## \|\| 1.55.71-72 \|\|

*mā vighnaṃ mā ca me pāpaṃ mā ca me paripanthinaḥ \|*  
*saumyā bhavantu tṛptāśca devā bhūtagaṇāstathā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vāmadevyaiḥ pavitraiśca mānastokarathantaraiḥ \|*  
*ākṛṣṇena rajasā ṛcamekāmudāharet \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. There should be no obstruction in our function. I should earn no blemish or sin, and nobody should be inimical to me. All the gods, bhutas and other noble people should be pleased with me.” Thus speaking, the recitations of Vamadeva and Manastoka should be carried out besides the richa commencing from Akrishna rajasa, should be carried out.

## \|\| 1.55.73 \|\|

*tataḥ puṇyāhaśabdena kṛtavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*rathakramaṇakaṃ kuryādvartmanā susamena tu \|*  
*puruṣaiścāpi voḍhavyaḥ sūryabhaktisamanvitaiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then reciting the welfare mantras, accompanied with cymbals and other musical instruments, the chariot should be driven by the devotees of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.55.74 \|\|

*sukṛtaiḥ ca 3 pragrahairdāntairbalīvarddairathāpi vā \|*  
*yathā paryaṭanaṃ ca syādviṣame pathi gacchataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Or alternatively, the strong bullocks should be yoked with strong ropes to enable the chariot to smoothly move even over the uneven paths.

## \|\| 1.55.75-77 \|\|

*upavāsasthitairviprairdivyairbhaumaiśca suvrataiḥ \|*  
*triṃśadbhiḥ ṣoḍaśairvāpi pratimāṃ bhāskarasya tu \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sthānātpracālyaṃ vai rudra rathamāropayecchanaiḥ \|*  
*rājñī ca nikṣubhā rudra bhārye tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*śanairāropayedrudra ubhayoḥ pārśvayo rathe \|*  
*nikṣubhāṃ dakṣiṇe pārśve rājñīṃ cāpyuttare tathā \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. The fasting Brahmanas, who should be thirty or sixteen, should take down the image of the Sungod from the chariot and get it established. On the side of the image, Nikshubha should be lodged on the right and the queen to the left.

## \|\| 1.55.78-82 \|\|

*dvāveva brāhmaṇau tasmindivyo bhaumaśca pārśvayoḥ \|*  
*brahmakalpastathā bhaumaḥ kūbarasyopari sthitaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*garuḍaṃ pṛṣṭhataścāsya valgamānaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*ātapatraṃ tathā śvetaṃ svarṇadaṇḍamanaupamam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*suvarṇabindubhiścitraṃ maṇimuktāphalojjvalam \|*  
*tatastvindradhanuḥprakhyaṃ svarṇadaṇḍamathāvraṇam \|\| 80 \|\|*

*dhvajaṃ prakalpayettasya patākābhiralaṅkṛtam \|*  
*bhūteśanānāvarṇābhissaptabhiḥ kāmanāśanaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*dhvajoparicaraṃ1 vyoma aruṇādhiṣṭhitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*rathatuṇḍagatānviprānnayedrathavaraṃ raveḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

78-82. Again on the sides of the god, the two learned Brahmanas should be seated in the space over the yoke. The bird Garuda should be seated at the back of the image of the sun. Thereafter, the white umbrella of white colour with a handle of gold, should be decorated with gems and the pieces of gold besides the beads with lustre. The gold staff of the umbrella should be well decorated, which should be totally new and decorated with seven flags of different colours. O lord of bhutas and destroyer of cupid, then in the upper part of the flag, Arupa should be seated. Thereafter, the chariot should be driven by the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.55.83 \|\|
