34-35. Therefore, with a concentrated mind, one should offer to the Sungod, the charming flowers, incense, fragrance, sandalpaste, ornaments, pair of costumes and various types of eatables, besides fruits.

## \|\| 1.63.36 \|\|

*ādyaṃ taṃ bhuvanādhāraṃ yathāśaktyā prasādaya \|*  
*ārādhya yāti taṃ devaṃ tasminneva naro layam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Because he is the base of the Bhuvanas. Therefore, one should please him as per his means, because by worshipping the Sun, a person gets absorbed in the same.

## \|\| 1.63.37-38 \|\|

*puṣpaistīrthodakairgandhairmadhunā sarpiṣā tathā \|*  
*kṣīreṇa snāpayedbhānuṃ graheśaṃ gopatiṃ khagam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dadhikṣīrahradānpuṇyāṃstato lokānmadhucyutaḥ \|*  
*prayāsyati gaṇaśreṣṭha nirvṛttiṃ ca vilakṣaṇām \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. O best of the ganas, in case a person worships the Sungod who is the lord of the planets and rays, by offering the flowers, water from holy places, fragrance, honey, ghi and milk, he achieves the tanks filled with honey, curd, milk besides the punyaloka and astonishing contentment.

## \|\| 1.63.39 \|\|

*stotrairgītaistathā vādyairbrāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*manasaścaiva yogena ārādhaya divākaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Therefore, you should recite the stotras in favour of the Sungod, the lord of the universe, worship him with musical instruments and satisfy the Brahmanas with utmost devotion.

## \|\| 1.63.40 \|\|

*ārādhya taṃ jagannāthaṃ mayā sargaḥ pravartitaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuśca pālayellokāṃstamārādhya divākaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Because by the adoration of the Sungod — the lord of the universe, I have created the world and lord Vishnu upkeeps it.

## \|\| 1.63.41 \|\|

*rudraśca prāptavāndevīṃ bhavānīṃ tatprasādataḥ \|*  
*dīpyante ṛṣayaścāpi tamārādhya divākaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is by his grace that Rudra achieved the goddess Bhavani and the Rishis get illuminated.

## \|\| 1.63.42 \|\|

*sa tvamebhiḥ prakāraistamupavāsaiśca bhāskaram \|*  
*toṣayābdaṃ hi tuṣṭo'sau bhānurdvaṃdvapraśāntidaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You should also, observing the fasts, worship the Sungod for full one year and please him. Because, the Sungod getting pleased, removes all the miseries and bestows tranquility.

## Chapter 64. Description of Phala-Saptami

## \|\| 1.64.1 \|\|

*diṇḍiruvāca \|*  
*upavāsaiḥ suraśreṣṭha kathaṃ tuṣyati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*parihārāṃstathācakṣva ye tyājyāścopavāsibhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Dindi said — O best of gods, how is the Sungod pleased by fasting? What is to be discarded by the people who are fasting and what is to be taken by them?

## \|\| 1.64.2 \|\|

*yadyatkāryaṃ yathā caiva bhāskarārādhane narai \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vistarādbrahmanyathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Brahman, by thus adoring the Sungod, what should be the performance of a person? You kindly explain all these points exhaustively.

## \|\| 1.64.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*smṛtaḥ sampūjito dhūpapuṣpānnairbhānurādarāt \|*  
*bhogināmupakārāya kiṃ punaścopavāsinām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Brahma said — Getting worshipped by the offerings of incense, flowers, food etc., the Sungod extends all the comforts even to the people who are involved in enjoying the worldly pleasures. Therefore, what to speak of the people who observe fast for him?

## \|\| 1.64.4 \|\|

*upāvṛttasya pāpebhyo yastu vāso guṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*upavāsaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sarvabhogavivarjitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. For getting oneself relieved of all the sins, people leading the virtuous life, resort to fasting.

## \|\| 1.64.5-6 \|\|

*ekarātraṃ dvirātraṃ vā trirātraṃ naktameva ca \|*  
*upavāsī raviṃ yastu bhaktyā dhyāyati mānavaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tannāmajāpī tatkarmaratastadgatamānasaḥ \|*  
*niṣkāmaḥ puruṣo diṇḍe sa brahma paramāpnuyāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O Dindi, therefore a person, who observes fasting for one, two or three nights continuously when gets devoted to the Sungod and gets engaged in the religious deeds without expecting any reward, he surely attains moksha or the highest position.

## \|\| 1.64.7 \|\|

*yaṃ ca kāmamabhidhyāya māskarārpitamānasaḥ \|*  
*upoṣati tamāpnoti prasanne khagame'khilam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When a person adores the Sungod expecting a desire, then with the pleasure of the Sungod, he achieves all the things he desired.

## \|\| 1.64.8 \|\|

*diṇḍiruvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdraiḥ strībhiśca kañjaja \|*  
*saṃsāragarte paṅkasthe sugatiḥ prāpyate katham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Dindi said — O born of lotus, how could the ladies of the Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra castes, who fall in the pit of mud, be rescued from their pitiable condition?

## \|\| 1.64.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*anārādhya jagannāthaṃ gopatiṃ dhvāntanāśanam \|*  
*nirvyalīkena cittena kaḥ prayāsyati sadgatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Brahma said — One who is the lord of the universe, who is the master of the rays and the destroyer of the darkness, who could achieve that excellent stage without adoring him?

## \|\| 1.64.10 \|\|

*viṣayagrāhi vai yasya na cittaṃ bhāskarārpitam \|*  
*sa kathaṃ pāpapaṅkākto naro yāsyati sadgatim \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Because the mind of those who are involved in the worldly pleasures never gets devoted towards the Sungod, as a result of this, they always remain entangled in the swamp of sins. Then how could such people achieve the highest position?

## \|\| 1.64.11 \|\|

*yadi saṃsāraduḥkhārtaḥ sugatiṃ gantumicchasi \|*  
*tadārādhaya sarveśaṃ bhāskaraṃ jyotiṣāṃ patim \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Therefore, getting fed up from the universe, in case you are desirous of the excellent stage, then you should adore Bhaskara — the lord of the planets.

## \|\| 1.64.12 \|\|

*puṣpaiḥ sugandhairhadyaiśca dhūpaiḥ sāgarucandanaiḥ \|*  
*vāsobhirbhūṣaṇairbhakṣyairupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You should observe fast offering him charming flowers, incense, guggulu, sandal paste, costumes, ornaments as well as the food grains.

## \|\| 1.64.13 \|\|

*yadi saṃsāranirvedādabhivācchasi sadgatim \|*  
*tadārādhaya mārtaṇḍaṃ bhaktipravaṇacetasā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In this way, getting detached from the miseries of the world, in case the best position is desired, then divert your mind with devotion to the Sungod and worship him.

## \|\| 1.64.14 \|\|

*puṣpāṇi yadi te na snuḥ śastapādapapallavaiḥ \|*  
*dūrvāṅkarairapi diṇḍe tadabhāve'rcayāryamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In case the flowers of the appropriate type are not forthcoming, then the Sungod should be adored offering the tender durva grass.

## \|\| 1.64.15 \|\|

*puṣpapatrāmbubhirdhūpairyathāvibhavamātmanaḥ \|*  
*pūjitastuṣṭimatulāṃ bhaktyā yātyekacetasā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Because whatever flowers» leaves, water and incense could be collected as per the means of a person, one should adore the lord with them, with utmost devotion and concentration of mind, which bestows utmost satisfaction to the performer.

## \|\| 1.64.16 \|\|

*yaḥ sadāyatane bhānoḥ kurute mārjanakriyām \|*  
*sa yātyuttamake sthāne sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Similarly, a person who cleans the Sun temple with a broom, he getting relieved of all the sins, achieves the highest position.

## \|\| 1.64.17 \|\|

*yāvatyaḥ pāṃsukaṇikā mārjyante bhāskarālaye \|*  
*dināni divi tāvanti tiṣṭhatyarkasamo naraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The one who cleans the Sun temple, then the number of the particles of dust cleansed by him, he lives in the perpetual heaven for an equivalent number of days.

## \|\| 1.64.18 \|\|

*ahanyahani yatpāpaṃ kurute gaṇanāyaka \|*  
*gocarmamātraṃ sammārjya hanti tadbhāskarālaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lord of the ganas, in this way, whatever the sins are committed by a person, they are simply washed out with the mere discarding of the use of the cow’s hide.

## \|\| 1.64.19 \|\|

*yaścānulepanaṃ kuryādbhānorāyatane naraḥ \|*  
*so'pi lokaṃ samāsādya haṃsena saha modate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Such of the persons who do the plastering of the Sun temple, he also enjoys all the pleasures in the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.64.20 \|\|

*mṛdā dhātuvikārairvā varṇakairgomayena vā \|*  
*upalepanakṛdyāti matpuraṃ yānamāsthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A person, who beautifies the Sun temple with earth, metals, or the cowdung, he boarding the plane, achieves my abode.

## \|\| 1.64.21 \|\|

*udakābhyukṣaṇaṃ bhānoryaḥ karoti sadā gṛhe \|*  
*so'pi gacchati yatrāste bhagavānyādasāṃ patiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Similarly, a person who washes and cleans the Sun temple with water, he achieves the abode of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 1.64.22 \|\|

*puṣpaprakaramatyarthaṃ sugandhaṃ bhāskarālaye \|*  
*anulipte naro dattvā na durgatimavāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person, who offers the fragrant flowers and other fragrant material besides performing adoring it, such a person never has to face the evil days.

## \|\| 1.64.23 \|\|

*vimānamatiśobhāḍhyaṃ sarvartusukhabhūṣitam \|*  
*samāpnoti naro dattvā dīpakaṃ bhāskarālaye \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In case a person offers a lamp in the Sun temple, a person is rewarded with a plane, which possesses all the fortunes and bestows comfort in all the seasons.

## \|\| 1.64.24 \|\|

*yastu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ tilapātraprado naraḥ \|*  
*dhvajaṃ ca bhāskare dadyātsamamatra phalaṃ labhet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person who offers a vase filled with sesamum seeds for a year, he also achieves the similar benefits.

## \|\| 1.64.25-26 \|\|

*vidhūto hanti vātena dāturajñānataḥ kṛtam \|*  
*pāpaṃ karturgṛhe bhānordivā rātrau narādhipa \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gītavādyādibhirbhānuṃ ya upāste tamopaham \|*  
*gandharvairnṛtyagītaiḥ sa vimānastho niṣevyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. When the flag flutters with the blowing of the wind, all his collected sins are washed out. O foremost of the humans! In this way, a person who adores the Sungod, the remover of darkness, throughout the day and night, he is made to board over a plane, where the Gandharvas appease him with the dancing and music.

## \|\| 1.64.27 \|\|

*jātismaratvaṃ medhāṃ ca tathaivoparame smṛtim \|*  
*prāpnoti gaṇāśārdūla kṛtvā pustakavācanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lion among the ganas, one who narrates before him, he is reminded of the caste of his previous birth. Even at the time of his death, he preserves his memory.

## \|\| 1.64.28 \|\|

*evaṃ khageśvaro bhaktyā yena bhānurupāsitaḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnoti gatiṃ ślādhyāṃ yāṃ yāmicchati cetasā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person who devoutedly worships the Sun who roams in the sky, he achieves the desired position.

## \|\| 1.64.29 \|\|

*devatvaṃ manujaiḥ kaiścidgandharvatvaṃ tathā paraiḥ \|*  
*vidyādharatvamaparaiḥ saṃrādhyeha divākaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Some among the humans achieved the position of the godhood, Gandharvas and Vidyadharas by his grace.

## \|\| 1.64.30 \|\|

*śakraḥ 1 kratuśateneśamārādhya jyotiṣāṃ patim \|*  
*devendratvaṃ gatastasmānnānyaḥ2 pūjyatamaḥ kvacit \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Even Indra could achieve his present position, after performing of a hundred yajnas to appease the Sungod. Therefore, there is no other deity more adorable that the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.64.31 \|\|

*brahmacārigṛhasthānāṃ vanasthānāṃ gaṇādhipa \|*  
*nānyaḥ pūjyastathā strīṇāmṛte devaṃ divākaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O foremost of the ganas, therefore, the Brahmachari, the householder, a recluse and the ladies should adore the Sungod, because, there is no other deity more adorable than the Sungod on earth.

## \|\| 1.64.32 \|\|

*madhye parivrājakānāṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*mokṣadvāraṃ viśantīha taṃ raviṃ vijitātmanām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. For the recluses, the Sungod with a thousand rays is the solitary gate for salvation, because such recluses, after controlling their senses, achieve the Sungod alone.

## \|\| 1.64.33 \|\|

*evaṃ sarvāśramāṇāṃ hi sahasrāṃśuḥ parāyaṇam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ caiva varṇānāṃ graheśo vai gatiḥ parā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Similarly, for the ashramas or the stages of life, Surya is the only god for all the castes in the world.

## \|\| 1.64.34 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣva gadataḥ kāmyānupavāsāṃstathāparān \|*  
*śṛṇu diṇḍe mahāpuṇyaphalakāṃ saptamīṃ parām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O Dindi, I am now speaking about the auspicious Saptami during which the fasting with or without desire, bestows the great merit.

## \|\| 1.64.35 \|\|

*ādityārādhanāyaināṃ sarvapāpaharāṃ śivām \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naro bhaktyā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Such of the people, who for the adoration of the Sun, prefer this Saptami which is the destroyers of sins, and resort to fasting with devotion, all their terrific sins are washed out.

## \|\| 1.64.36-38 \|\|

*tathā lokamavāpnoti sūryasyāmitatejasaḥ \|*  
*atha bhādrapade māsi śuklapakṣe samāgate \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sopoṣyā prathamaṃ tāta vidhānaṃ śṛṇu tatra vai \|*  
*ayācitaṃ caturthyāṃ tu pañcamyāmekabhojanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*upavāsaparaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*arcayitvā dinakaraṃ gandhadhūpanivedanaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. Besides that, they also achieve the abode of Surya which has no limitations. O excellent one, on the bright seventh moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, there is a provision for fasting. You please listen. On the fourth moon day, one should consume the food which he should get without a demand. After this, he should take food only once on the fifth moon day. While fasting on the sixth moon day, one should control his sense organs, discarding anger, then adore the Sungod offering incense etc.

## \|\| 1.64.39-41 \|\|

*purataḥ sthaṇḍile rātrau svapyāddevasya putraka \|*  
*pradhyāyanmanasā devaṃ sarvabhūtārtināśanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sarvadoṣapraśamanaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*vibuddhastvatha saptamyāṃ kuryādbrāhmaṇabhojanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā dinakaraṃ puṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ \|*  
*naivedyaṃ tāta devasya phalāni kathayanti4 hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. During the night, one should meditate upon the Sun mentally, who is the remover of all the pains of the people, remover of all the blemishes besides being the destroyer of all the sins. Then, with a devoted mind, adoring him attentively, one should sleep on the ground. Getting up early in the morning on the seventh moon day, one should adore the Sungod, offering him the flowers, incense, sandalpaste and eatables.

## \|\| 1.64.42 \|\|

*kharjūranālikerāṇi tathā āmraphalāni tu \|*  
*mātuliṅgaphalānyeva kathitāni manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. According to the words of the learned people, dates, coconuts, mangoes, myrobalan and lemon should be offered to the Sungod

## \|\| 1.64.43-45 \|\|

*etaiśca bhojayedviprānātmanā ca prabhakṣayet \|*  
*tathaiṣāṃ cāpyabhāvena śṛṇu cānyāni suvrata \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śāligodhūmapiṣṭāni kārayedgaṇanāyaka \|*  
*guḍagarbhakṛtānīha ghṛtapākena pāvayet \|\| 44 \|\|*

*cāturyāvakamiśrāṇi ādityāya nivedayet \|*  
*agnikāryamatho kṛtvā brāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Giving these fruits in charity to the Brahmanas, one should consume them himself as well. O Suvrata, in case these fruits are not available at that point of time, then in that case the rice or wheat powder should be mixed with sugarcane balls and should be fried in ghi making the fried cakes or porridge out of them in four types, which should be offered to the lord. Food should be offered to the Brahmanas, after performing of yajna.

## \|\| 1.64.46-47 \|\|

*itthaṃ dvādaśa vai māsānkāryaṃ vratamanuttamam \|*  
*māsi māsi phalāhāraḥ phaladāyī phalārcanaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*varṣānte tvatha kurvīta śaktyā brāhmaṇabhojanam \|*  
*snānaprāśanayoścāpi vidhānaṃ śṛṇu suvrata \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The vrata of twelve months has been prescribed to be performed in a similar way. Thus in every month, the fruits should be given for food and charity. The worship should also be carried out with fruits. At the end of the year, while worshipping the Sungod, one should feed the Brahmanas as per his means. Besides you listen to the provision of bathing, eating, etc.

## \|\| 1.64.48-49 \|\|

*gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam \|*  
*tilasarṣapayoḥ kalkaṃ śvetā mṛccāpi suvrata \|\| 48 \|\|*

*dūrvākalkaṃ ghṛtaṃ cāpi gośṛṃgakṣālitaṃ jalam \|*  
*jātigulmaviniryāsaḥ praśastaḥ snānakarmaṇi \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. The cowdung and the urine of the cow, milk, curd, ghi kusha water, powder of mustard seeds, white earth, durva-paste, clarified butter, the water purified with the horns of cows, jasmine flowers, are said to be the best for the taking of the bath.

## \|\| 1.64.50 \|\|

*prāśane cāpyathaitāni sarvapāpaharāṇi vai \|*  
*ādau kṛtvā bhādrapadaṃ yathā saṃkhyaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This is because, they are said to be the remover of sins. Therefore, these items could be consumed as well. The worship in the month of Bhadrapada should also be carried out in the same way.

## \|\| 1.64.51-56 \|\|

*itthaṃ varṣāntamāsādya bhojayitvā dvijottamān \|*  
*divyānbhogānmahādeva tatastebhyo nivedayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*phalāni tāta1 haimāni yathā śaktyā gaṇādhipa \|*  
*savatsāmatha vā dhenuṃ bhūmiṃ sasyānvitāmatha \|\| 52 \|\|*

*prāsādamatha vā bhaumaṃ sarvadhānyasamanvitam \|*  
*dadyātchuklāni2 vastrāṇi tāmrapātraṃ 3 savidrumam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*śaktiyuktasya caitāni daridrasya tu me śṛṇu \|*  
*phalāni piṣṭakānyeṣāṃ tilacūrṇānvitāni tu \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhojayitvā dvijāndadyādrājatāni4 phalāni tu \|*  
*dhāturaktaṃ vastrayugamamācāryāya nivedayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sahiraṇyaṃ mahādeva pañcaratnasamanvitam \|*  
*itthaṃ samāpyate tāta pāraṇaṃ vārṣikāntikam \|\| 56 \|\|*

51-56. O revered one, in this way, at the end of the year, offering the eatables to the Brahmanas, then the golden as well as the natural fruits should be given over to the Brahmanas. Thereafter, a cow with calf, the well irrigated and blossoming land, houses full of cereals and riches or the white garments, sapphire and the copper vases, should be given. This the provision made for the wealthy people. I am also speaking about the poor people, which you please listen. Brahmana should be served fruit or the powdered sesamum seeds used in sweets as food. Thereafter, the silver vase with fruits, besides the two red costumes should be given to the Brahmanas. Then the adoration should be concluded with five types of gems. After this, the vrata should be concluded.

## \|\| 1.64.57 \|\|

*ityeṣā vai puṇyatamā saptamī duritāpahā \|*  
*yāmupoṣya narāḥ sarve yānti sūryasalokatām \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In this way, by performing the vrata of this auspicious Saptami — the remover of all the sins, a person attains the abode of Surya.

## \|\| 1.64.58-60 \|\|

*1 pūjyamānaḥ sadā devairgandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*anayā mānavo nityaṃ pūjayedbhāskaraṃ sadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*dāridyaduḥkhaduritairmukto yāti divākaram \|*  
*brāhmaṇo mokṣamāyāti kṣatriyaścendratāṃ vrajet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vaiśyo dhanadasālokyaṃ śūdroḥ vipratvamāpnuyāt \|*  
*aputro labhate putraṃ durbhagā subhagā bhavet \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. Adoring the god Bhaskara in this way, the performer is freed from all the miseries, reaches the abode of the Sun, where he is adored by the gods, Gandharvas and Apsaras all the time. In this way, the Brahmanas achieve moksha (salvation), Kshatriya the abode of Indra, the Vaishya achieve the place of Kubera while the Shudras attain Brahmanhood. A childless woman gets a child and the unfortunate woman gains fortunes.

## \|\| 1.64.61-63 \|\|

*yāmupoṣya ca nārīmāṃ saptamīṃ lokapūjitām \|*  
*vidhavā vā satī bhaktyā anayā pūjayedravim \|\| 61 \|\|*

*nānyajanmani vaidhavyaṃ nārī prāpnoti mānada \|*  
*cintāmaṇisamā hyeṣā vijñeyā phalasaptamī \|\| 62 \|\|*

*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ diṇḍe sarvakāmapradā smṛtā \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. With the influence of this renowned Saptami vrata, the chaste widow is relieved of her widowhood in the next birth. O Dindi — the praiseworthy one, thus the Saptami-vrata is like the gem which removes all the worries and is said to be quite rewarding. Therefore, by reading it or listening to its glory, all the sins are removed.

## Chapter 65. Glory of Aditya-vrata

## \|\| 1.65.1 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ caiva saptamyāṃ bhojayedbhojakānbudhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — Hereafter, I shall speak about the Rahasya-Saptami during which by performing the vratas, a person himself crosses the ocean of the universe with his seven generations.

## \|\| 1.65.2-4 \|\|

*saptāparānsapta pūrvānpitṝṃścāpi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*rogāṃśchinatti duśchedyāndurjayāñjayate hyarīn \|\| 2 \|\|*

*arthānprāpnoti duṣprāpānyaḥ kuryānnāma saptamīm \|*  
*kanyārthī labhate kanyāṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*putrārthī labhate putrāndharmārthī dharmamāpnuyāt \|*  
*samayānpālayansarvānkuryāccemāṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. As the one, who completes tills Saptami-vrata is relieved of all his ailments, overpowers all his enemies, and achieves the valuables which are impossible to be achieved by others, similarly, a person who is desirous of a girl gets a girl, the one desirous of riches gets the same, a person desirous of a son gets a son and the one who is devoted to akarma achieves the dharma. Therefore, all the intelligent people should follow the method prescribed for the same.

## \|\| 1.65.5-6 \|\|

*samayāñchṛṇu bhūteśa śreyase gadato mama \|*  
*ādityabhaktaḥ puruṣaḥ saptamyāṃ gaṇanāyaka \|\| 5 \|\|*

*maitrīṃ sarvatra vai kuryādbhāskaraṃ vāpi ciṃtayet \|*  
*saptamyāṃ na spṛśettailaṃ nīlaṃ vastraṃ na dhārayet \|*  
*na cāpyāmālakaiḥ snānaṃ na kuryātkalahaṃ kvacit \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O leader of the bhutas, I am going to repeat the same for your benefit. You please listen. O leader of the ganas, a devotee of the Sungod should be friendly with all and should worship the Sungod. On the seventh moon day, he should, besides worshipping the Sungod, should not touch oil, should not wear the blue costumes. He should take bath with the water of myrobalan. He should not pick up a quarrel with anyone that particular day.

## \|\| 1.65.7 \|\|

*diṇḍiruvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ na spaśettailaṃ saptamyāṃ padmasaṃbhava \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Dindi said — O lord born of a lotus, why should one, not touch the oil on the day of Saptami. Why should the blue costumes not be used on that day? What is the harm?

## \|\| 1.65.8-12 \|\|

*kaśca doṣo bhaveddeva nīlavastrasya dhāraṇāt \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu diṇḍe mahābāho nīlavastrasya dhāraṇe \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dūṣaṇaṃ gaṇaśārdūla gadato mama kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*pālanaṃ vikrayaścaiva sadvṛttirupajīvanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*patitastu bhavedviprastribhiḥ kṛcchairviśuddhyati \|*  
*nīlīraktena vastreṇa yatkarma kurute dvijaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*vṛthā tasya mahāyajñā nīlasūtrasya dhāraṇāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nīlīraktaṃ yadā vastraṃ viprastvaṅgeṣu dhārayet \|*  
*ahorātroṣito bhūtvā pañcagavyena śuddhyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. Brahma said — O large armed one, O Dindi, I am going to relate the blemish one earns by wearing the blue costumes. As a Brahmana falls by indulging into sellings, evil conduct and taking refuge with someone, he gets purified only with the performing of the three krichchra or different vratas. Similarly, a Brahmana who begs wearing blue cloth, whatever the charities are performed by him, besides bathing, homa, studies, oblation to the manes etc., they all become infructuous. By wearing the costumes of blue colour, a Brahmana has too fast for a day and night. Thereafter, with the consuming of the cow’s dung, he gets purified.

## \|\| 1.65.13-14 \|\|

*romakūpe yadā gacchedraktaṃ nīlasya1 kasyacit \|*  
*patitastu bhavedviprastribhiḥ kṛcchrairviśuddhyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nīlīmadhyaṃ yadā gacchetpramādādbrāhmaṇaḥ kvacit \|*  
*ahorātroṣito bhūtvā pañcagavyena śuddhyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. A Brahmana is considered to be downgraded in case the blue colour enters the hair-pits in his body. He can be purified with the performing of the krichchra-vrata thrice. Thus, in case a Brahmana has to enter the blue colour, then he should fast for a day and a night and consume Panchagavya, with which he gets purified.

## \|\| 1.65.15 \|\|

*nīlīdāru yadā bhiṃdyādbrāhmaṇānāṃ śarīrake \|*  
*śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yatra dvijaścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When he is hurt with the blue wood, in case the blood oozes out, the concerned Brahmana should observe the Chandrayana vrata.

## \|\| 1.65.16 \|\|

*kuryādajñānato yastu nīlervā dantadhāvanam \|*  
*kṛtvā kṛcchradvayaṃ diṇḍe viśuddhaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Dindi, in case one brushes his teeth even by mistake with the stick of blue wood, than he could be purified by observing the krichchra-vrata.

## \|\| 1.65.17 \|\|

*vāpayedyatra nīlīṃ tu bhavettatrāśucirmahī \|*  
*pramāṇadvādaśābdāni tata ūrdhvaṃ śucirbhavet3 \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The field in which the indigo plant is sown, that land remains inauspicious for twelve years.

## \|\| 1.65.18 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ spṛśatastailamiṣṭā bhāryā vinaśyati \|*  
*ityeṣa nīlītailasya doṣaste kathito mayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Similarly, on the same Saptami day, in case one touches the blue oil, the beloved wife of the person meets with her end. Thus I have narrated to you the blemish of the blue oil.

## \|\| 1.65.19 \|\|

*na caiva khādenmāṃsāni madyāni na pibedbudhaḥ \|*  
*na drohaṃ kasyacitkuryānna pāruṣyaṃ samācaret \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Consuming of flesh, drinking, attraction towards others and to be harsh towards others, should also be avoided.

## \|\| 1.65.20 \|\|

*nāvabhāṣeta cāṇḍālaṃ striyaṃ naiva rajasvalām \|*  
*na vāpi saṃspṛśeddhīnaṃ mṛtakaṃ nāvalokayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. One should not touch a Chandala, a woman in period, or observe a dead body.

## \|\| 1.65.21-25 \|\|

*nāsphoṭayennātihasedgāyeccāpi na gītakam \|*  
*na nṛtyedatirāgeṇa na ca vādyāni vādayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*na śayīta striyā sārdhaṃ na seveta durodaram \|*  
*na rudyādaśrupātena na ca vācyaṃ ca śaukikam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ākṛṣenna śiroyūkā na vṛthāvādamācaret \|*  
*parasyāniṣṭakathanamatiśokaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*na kañcittāḍayejjantuṃ na kuryādatibhojanam \|*  
*na caiva hi divā svapnaṃ dambhaṃ śāṭhyaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*rathyāyāmaṭanaṃ vāpi yatnataḥ parivarjayet \|*  
*athāparo vidhiścātra śrūyatāṃ tripurāntaka \|\| 25 \|\|*

21-25. One should also discard uttering of irrelevant words, excess of laughing, singing of songs, the immensely passionate dance, sleeping with woman, gambling, crying with the drop of tears, to produce parrot like sound, to extract lice from the hair of the head, to cause harm to others uselessly, excess of grief, torture of living beings, excess of eating, sleeping during the day, wickedness, besides unnecessary wandering in the streets are all the blemishes and one should get rid of them. O killer of Tripura, now I am speaking out the other method, which you should listen.

## \|\| 1.65.26-29 \|\|

*caitrātprabhṛti kartavyā sarvadā nāma saptamī \|*  
*dhāteti caitramāse tu pūjanīyo divākaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*aryameti ca vaiśākhe jyeṣṭhe mitraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*āṣāḍhe varuṇo jñeya indro nabhasi kathyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vivasvāṃśca nabhasye'tha parjanyośvayuji smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pūṣā kārttikamāse tu mārgaśīrṣeṣurucyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

*bhagaḥ pauṣe bhavetpūjyastvaṣṭā māghe tu śasyate \|*  
*viṣṇuśca phālgune māsi pūjyo vandyaśca bhāskaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. The vrata of this Saptami should be started in the month of Chaitra. Dhata is the master of the month of Chaitra, Aryama is the master for the month of Jyestha; Varuna is for the month of Asadha; Indra for the month of Havana; Vivasvan for the month of Bhadrapada; Parjanya is for the month of Ashvina, Pausha is for the month of Karttika and Bhaga is for the month of Pausha; Tvasta is for the month of Magha and Vishnu is for the month of Phalguna. These are the forms of the Sungod, which should be adored.

## \|\| 1.65.30 \|\|

*saghṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ deyaṃ bhojayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus on each one of the Saptami day, the Brahmanas who are to be fed, should be served with suitable food with ghi.

## \|\| 1.65.31 \|\|

*bhojakāyaiva viprāya dakṣiṇāṃ svarṇamāṣakam \|*  
*saghṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ deyaṃ raktavastrāṇi caiva hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. They should be given a dakshina of one masha of gold. The food should contain ghi, which should be taken by them.

## \|\| 1.65.32 \|\|

*abhāve bhojakānāṃ tu dakṣiṇīyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tathaiva bhojanīyāśca śraddhayā parayā vibho \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In case the Brahmanas for the serving of the food are not available, then the Brahmanas from the southern region should be given food with devotion.

## \|\| 1.65.33-34 \|\|

*viśeṣato vācakaśca bāhmaṇaḥ kalpavitsadā \|*  
*ityeṣā kathitā tubhyaṃ saptamī gaṇanāyaka \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śrutā satī pāpaharā sūryalokapradāyinī \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. They should particularly feed the Brahmanas who should be able to recite the scriptures besides being aware of the kalpas. O leader of the ganas! Thus, I have explained to you the importance of Saptami by hearing winch all the sins are removed.

## Chapter 66. Description of Yajnavalkya

## \|\| 1.66.1 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmasamprāptau puruṣāṇāṃ viceṣṭatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O excellent one, lord Brahma, thus speaking to him, disappeared. Thereafter, Dindi also became attendant of the Sungod, after adoring him.

## \|\| 1.66.2 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*bhūyaḥ kathaya viprendra māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasya me \|*  
*śṛṇvato nāsti me tṛptiramṛtasyeva suvrata \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Shatanika said — O lord of vipras, listening to the nectar like glory of the Sungod, I still do not feel satisfied. Therefore, you kindly repeat the same.

## \|\| 1.66.3 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājansamvādaṃ dvijaśaṅkhayoḥ \|*  
*yaṃ śrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate mānavo1 nṛpa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Sumantu said — O king, in this connection, I am going to repeat the conversation between Rishi Shankha and a Brahmana, listening to which, you would be relieved of all the sins. You better listen to me attentively.

## \|\| 1.66.4-7 \|\|

*āsīnamāśrame śaṃkhaṃ dvijo draṣṭuṃ jagāma ha \|*  
*phalabhārānatacchāye vṛkṣavṛndasamākule \|\| 4 \|\|*

*parasparamṛgaśṛṅgakaṇḍūyitamṛgāvṛte \|*  
*barhirvanāmbarānītatīrthakandopabhogini \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prabhūtakusumāmodaṣaṭpadodgītaśālinī \|*  
*siddhadevarṣigandharvatīrthasevitavāriṇi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*muṇḍaiśca jaṭilaiścaiva tāpasairupaśobhite \|*  
*āśrame taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ śaṃkhāhvaṃ sukhamāsthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Once the sage Shankha reached the ashrama of the sage Dvija, where he was seated in comfortable position. The ashrama was surrounded by the trees laden with fruits, and the branches of the trees were bending down due to the weight. The trees were quite shady. The deer which were rubbing their horns with one another, surrounded the ashrama from all the four sides. The water has the fragrance of the kusha grass. The black wasps were extracting nectar from the ripe fruits by sitting on them. The wasps were issuing humming sound. It had enough of fragrant water which was being used by Siddhas, the gods, Rishis and the Gandharvas. The hermitage was decorated with the ascetics with matted locks of hair over the head, who were seated there with comfort Out of them, he spotted the ascetic Shankha.

## \|\| 1.66.8-9 \|\|

*stotraiḥ stotuṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ tadbhaktaṃ tatparāyaṇam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃhatya sahasā taṃ bhojakakumārakāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vinītā upasaṃgamya yathāvadabhivādya ca \|*  
*āsaneṣūpaviṣṭāsta upaviṣṭamathābruvan \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. When the ascetics, while seated on the ground, recite prayer for the Sungod to whom they were devoted, he went to the sage who was seated over his asana. The prince of the Bhojaka race then humbly welcomed the sage Shankha and gave him a seat, and asked.

## \|\| 1.66.10 \|\|

*bhagavantsarvavedeṣu2 cchiṃdhi naḥ saṃśayo mahān \|*  
*vinayenopapannānāṃ kumārāṇāṃ tato muniḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O lord, we have developed a serious doubt for all the Vedas. Therefore, you kindly be gracious enough to remove the doubt.

## \|\| 1.66.11-13 \|\|

*anādīṃścaturo vedānuvāca prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu paṭhatāmeva āśramaṃ tu yadṛcchayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*muniśreṣṭho'tha taṃ deśamājagāma dvijo nṛpa \|*  
*yathāvadarcitastena śaṅkhenāmitatejasā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vanditaśca kumāraistairabhavatprītamānasaḥ \|*  
*athaitānabravīcchaṃkhastānbhojakakumārakān \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Then the sage humbly explained enough to the boys about the Vedas as a result of which their doubt was cleared. Thereafter, started the study of the Vedas again. At that point of time the sage Dvija suddenly reached the ashrama. All the princes welcomed the sage Shankha. At the sight of the princes, the sage Dvija was also extremely pleased. Thereafter, the sage Shankha addressed the princes.

## \|\| 1.66.14-15 \|\|

*śiṣṭāgamādanadhyāyaḥ sa ca jāto viramyatām \|*  
*yathājñāpayasītyāhuḥ kumārāste ṛṣiṃ tataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*prapaccha siddhidaścaitānke hyete kiṃ paṭhanti ca \|*  
*śaṅkhovāca mahārāja kumārā bhojakātmajāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. On the arrival of the some respectable person, in order to welcome him, for sometime the studies are disturbed. Therefore, you stop your studies for some time. Respecting the command of the sage, the princes stopped their studies. Then Dvija asked the sage Shankha, “Who are they and what are they studying”? Shankha said — “O lord, these are the Bhojaka princess.”

## \|\| 1.66.16 \|\|

*sasūtrakalpāṃścaturo vipra vedānadhīyate \|*  
*tathaiva saptamīkalpe paricaryāṃ ca bhāsvataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. They are studying all the four Vedas with Sutras and Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.66.17 \|\|

*agnikāryavidhānaṃ ca pratiṣṭhākalpamāditaḥ \|*  
*adhyaṅgalakṣaṇaṃ 1 brahman rathayātrāvidhiṃ tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Similarly, the performing of homa, the consecration, the adoration of the limbs of the body of Surya, the mode of Ratha-yatra, is also being learnt by them.

## \|\| 1.66.18 \|\|

*dvija uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ kriyeta saptamyāṃ kabhrārcanavidhikramaḥ \|*  
*gandhapuṣpapradīpānāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ ravimandire \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Dvija said — In what way is the Sungod worshipped on the day of Saptami and with what material? What type of reward one achieves by offering the fragrant flowers to him in the temple?

## \|\| 1.66.19-20 \|\|

*kena tuṣyati dānena vratena niyamena ca \|*  
*dhūpapuṣpopahārādi kiṃ ca deyaṃ vivasvate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tanme brūhi tapodhana \|*  
*viśeṣatastu māhātmyaṃ brūhi māṃ bhāskarasya hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. With what type of charities and performance is he pleased? In what way the incense, flowers and the food items are offered to the Sungod? O performer of excellent tapas, you better explain all these in detail, besides the glory of Bhaskara, because I am particularly interested in the same.

## \|\| 1.66.21 \|\|

*śaṅkha uvāca \|*  
*imamarthaṃ vaśiṣṭhena pṛṣṭaḥ sāmbo yathā purā \|*  
*sa covāca vaśiṣṭhāya tadahaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Shankha said — In earlier times, the same question was asked by Samba from the sage Vasistha. The reply that Vasishtha gave to Samba is going to be related me.

## \|\| 1.66.22-26 \|\|

*atrāśrame puṇyatame tīrthānāmuttame prabhuḥ \|*  
*vavande niyatātmānaṃ vaśiṣṭhaṃ munisattamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vinayenopasaṃgamya vavande caraṇau muneḥ \|*  
*kṛtapraṇāmaṃ sāmbaṃ tu bhaktiprahvīkṛtānanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vilokya paramaprīto muniḥ papraccha taṃ tadā \|*  
*sarvataḥ sphuṭitaṃ gātraṃ kuṣṭhena mahatā tava \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kathaṃ ca lakṣmīradhikā rūpaṃ cātimanoharam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tejasvitātimahatī tathaiva2 sukumāratā \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. The sage Vasishtha, the best of the sages used to live in the same auspicious ashrama where he had controlled all his senses. He is the best of the sages. Samba reading there quite humbly, offered his salutation at the feet of the great sage. Samba who was expressing his extreme love by his performance, was lovingly thus addressed by the sage Vasishtha — “All the limbs of your body have been worn out with the ailment of leprosy. How have you regained the tenderness and beauty of all your limbs again?”

## \|\| 1.66.27 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*stuto nāmasahasreṇa lokanātho divākaraḥ \|*  
*darśanaṃ ca gataḥ sākṣāddattavāṃśca varānmama \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Samba said — I adored lord Surya reciting his thousand names. Getting pleased, he appeared before me and bestowed a boon.

## \|\| 1.66.28 \|\|

*vaśiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*kathamārādhitaḥ sūryastvayā yādavanaṃdana \|*  
*kaiśca vratatapodānairdarśanaṃ bhagavāngataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Vasishtha said — O son of the Yadava race, how did you adore the Sungod? By performing which vrata or charities, could you have an audience with the Sungod?

## \|\| 1.66.29 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito brahmansarvameva mayā yathā \|*  
*toṣito bhagavānsūryo vidhinā yena suvrata \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Samba said — O Brahman, the process by which I adored the Sungod pleasing him at the same time, I am going to repeat the whole of it to you. You please listen to me with attention.

## \|\| 1.66.30 \|\|

*mohānmayopahasito3 durvāsāḥ kopano muniḥ \|*  
*tato'haṃ tasya śāpena mahākuṣṭhamavāptavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Once I, out of arrogance, made fun of the sage Durvasa who is always filled with rage. Because of the curse pronounced by him on me, I attracted the ailment of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.66.31 \|\|

*tato'haṃ pitaraṃ gatvā kuṣṭhayogābhipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*lajjamāno'tigarveṇa idaṃ vākyamathābravam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Suffering immensely from leprosy, I shamefully went to my father and said to him with pride.

## \|\| 1.66.32 \|\|

*tāta sīdati me gātraṃ svaraśca parihīyate \|*  
*ghorarūpo mahāvyādhirvapureṣa jighāṃsati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O adorable one, I am feeling so painful in the body that I am unable to speak. This terrible disease is eating up my body.

## \|\| 1.66.33 \|\|

*aśeṣavyādhirājñāhaṃ pīḍitaḥ krūrakarmaṇā \|*  
*vaidyairoṣadhibhiścaiva na śāntirmama vidyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I, the performer of misdeeds, have been attracted by this ailment which is the worst of all the diseases. I could have no relief by the treatment of the physicians.

## \|\| 1.66.34 \|\|

*so'haṃ tvayā hyanujñātastyaktumicchāmi jīvitam \|*  
*yadi vāhamanugrāhyastato'nujñātumarhasi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Therefore, with your permission, I intend to end my life. In case you have some love and affection for me in your heart, then you kindly permit me to do so.”

## \|\| 1.66.35 \|\|

*ityuktavākyaḥ sa pitā ṣutraśokābhipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*pitā kṣaṇaṃ tato dhyātvā māmevaṃ vākyamuktavān \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At these words spoken by me, my father felt extremely painful at heart. After thinking for a while, he said.

## \|\| 1.66.36 \|\|

*dhairyamāśrayatāṃ1 putra mā śoke ca manaḥ kṛthāḥ \|*  
*hanti śokārditaṃ vyādhiḥ śuṣkaṃ tṛṇamivānalaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. “O son, be patient and develop no grief in your mind, because the disease destroys a grieving person like the fire destroying the strand.

## \|\| 1.66.37 \|\|

*devatārādhanaparo bhava putraka mā śucaḥ \|*  
*ityukte ca mayā prokto devamārādhayāmi kam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Therefore, O son, don’t worry. Worship the gods.” At these words of Shri Krishna, I said — “Who is the deity to be adored by me.

## \|\| 1.66.38 \|\|

*kamārādhya vimucye'haṃ tāta rogaiḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*ityevamukto bhagavānmāmuvāca pitā mama \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O excellent one, by adoring which one of the gods, I would be relieved of the misery?” Listening to this, the father said.

## \|\| 1.66.39 \|\|

*imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭaḥ padmayoniḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yājñavalkyena ṛṣiṇā yogīśena mahātmanā2 \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “This topic was breached by the sage Yajnavalkya with the eternal Brahma.”

## \|\| 1.66.40 \|\|

*yaduvāca mahātejāstasmai sa yadunandana \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva śucirbhūtvā ātmanaḥ śreyase suta \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. “O son of Yadu race, whatever the illustrious Brahma had spoken at that time is going to be repeated by me, you therefore listen to me attentively for your own benefit.

## \|\| 1.66.41-43 \|\|

*surajyeṣṭhaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ padmayoniṃ prajāpatim \|*  
*yājñavalkyo mahātejāḥ paryapṛcchatpitāmaham \|\| 41 \|\|*

*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi kiṃcidātmamanogatam \|*  
*samārādhya vibho devaṃ naro mucyeta vai bhavāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

*gṛhastho brahmacārī vā vānaprastho'tha bhikṣukaḥ \|*  
*ya icchenmokṣamāsthātuṃ devatāṃ kāṃ yajeta saḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. Then the sage Yajnavalkya said to the grandsire, who happens to be the foremost of all the gods and was born out of lotus — “Some doubts are developing in my mind, which I would like to get removed. O resplendent one, when a person is redeemed from the world, after adoring the gods, then who is the god to be worshipped by the Brahmachari, householder, Vanaprasthins and the recluses for achieving moksha?

## \|\| 1.66.44 \|\|

*kuto hyasya dhruvaḥ svargaḥ kuto naiḥ śreyasaṃ sukham \|*  
*svargataścaiva kiṃ kuryādyena na cyavate punaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Because the concerned person should surely achieve the heaven from where there be no chance of the fall on earth.

## \|\| 1.66.45 \|\|

*devātānāṃ tu ko devaḥ pitṝṇāṃ caiva kaḥ pitā \|*  
*tasmātparataraṃ yacca tanme brūhi pitāmaha \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O grandsire and god of gods and the father of manes, who is the best of the gods, you kindly tell me.

## \|\| 1.66.46 \|\|

*kena sṛṣṭamidaṃ viśvaṃ brahmansthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*pralayo ca kamabhyeti tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Brahman, the universe is full of mobile and immobile beings, who has created them and when does the dissolution take place? You please tell me.

## \|\| 1.66.47-48 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhavatā tuṣṭaścāsmi mahāmate \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ puṇyottaramanuttamam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kathayiṣye dvijaśreṣṭha śṛṇuṣvaikamanādhunā \|*  
*ātmanaḥ śreyase vipra śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Brahma said — Offering his salutation to the auspicious lord, I am going to speak out, which you should listen attentively and by so doing you would surely be benefitted. Presently, you should meditate upon him with an auspicious mind.

## \|\| 1.66.49 \|\|

*udyanya eṣa kurute jagadvitimiraṃ karaiḥ \|*  
*nātaḥ parataro devaḥ kimanyatkathayāmi te \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. With the rising of the Sungod, the entire world is filled with light. Therefore, who could be a god, better than him, to be referred by me.

## \|\| 1.66.50 \|\|

*anādi nidhano hyeṣaḥ puruṣaḥ śāśvato'vyayaḥ \|*  
*dīpayatyeva lokāṃstrīnravī raśmibhirulbaṇaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The Sungod is eternal, everlasting, indestructible, besides being free from the birth and death. He illuminates the entire universe with his sharp rays.

## \|\| 1.66.51-52 \|\|

*sarvadevātmako hyeṣa tapasā cāṃśutāpanaḥ \|*  
*sarvasya jagato nāthaḥ karmasākṣī śubhāśubhe \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kṣapayatyeṣa bhūtāni tathā visṛjate punaḥ \|*  
*eṣa bhāti tapatyeṣa vardhate ca gabhastibhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. He is the representative of all the gods. By performing of the hard tapas, he has achieved the sharp rays. He is the master of the entire universe and a witness to all the evil or good deeds. He is the creator as well as the destroyer of the living beings. He faces head from his own rays and deeps on growing.

## \|\| 1.66.53 \|\|

*eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca pūṣā1 prakṛtibhāvana \|*  
*na hyeṣa kṣayamāyāti nityamakṣayamaṇḍalaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He is the Dhata, Vidhata as well Pasha of the universe. He never deteriorates, because he has the everlasting mandala.

## \|\| 1.66.54-55 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ hi pitā devatānāṃ ca devatā \|*  
*dhruvaṃ sthānaṃ smṛtaṃ hyeṣa ādhāro jagatastathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sarvakāle jagatkṛtsnamādityātsaṃprasūyate \|*  
*pralaye ca tamabhyeti ādityaṃ dīptatejasam \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. He is the father of the manes, the lord of gods, stationary place, besides being the support of the universe. During all the times, the universe emerges out of the lustre of the Sun and it ultimately merges in the same.

## \|\| 1.66.56 \|\|

*yoginaścātra saṃlīnāstyaktvā gṛhakalevaram \|*  
*vāyubhūtā viśantyasmiṃstejorāśau divākare \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. All the yogins remain engrossed in him always and disowning their own bodies and abodes, ultimately enter in his lustre.

## \|\| 1.66.57 \|\|

*tasya raśmisahasrāṇi śākhā iva vihaṃgamāḥ \|*  
*vasantyāśritya munayaḥ saṃsiddhā daivataiḥ saha \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Taking refuge of the thousand rays like the birds in the tree branch, all the gods and the Rishis wander here and there.

## \|\| 1.66.58-59 \|\|

*janakādayo gṛhasthāstu rājāno yogadharmiṇaḥ \|*  
*vālakhilyādayaścaiva munayo brahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vyāsādayo vanasthāśca bhikṣuḥ pañcaśikhastathā \|*  
*sarve3 te yogamāsthāya praviṣṭāḥ sūryamaṇḍalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Janaka — the foremost of the great yogins, Brahmacharis like the Valakhilyas and others, Vyasa and other Rishis dwelling the forest, besides Bhikshu Pancashikha and others have entered the solar mandala by practicing yoga.

## \|\| 1.66.60 \|\|

*śuko vyāsātmajaḥ śrīmānyogadharmamavāpya tu \|*  
*ādityakiraṇānpītvā na punarbhavamāntavān \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Shukadeva — the son of Vyasa, consumed the sun rays by yogic practices and achieved eternity.

## \|\| 1.66.61 \|\|

*śabdamātrāḥ śrutisukhā brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣo'yaṃ smṛto devaḥ sūryastimiranāśanaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus the names of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva are heard by mouth alone, but the Sungod — the remover of darkness, is clearly visible.

## \|\| 1.66.62 \|\|

*tasmādanyavrate bhaktirna kāryā śubhamicchatā \|*  
*hṛṣṭena sādhyate yasmādadṛṣṭaṃ nityameva hi \|*  
*tvayātaḥ satataṃ vipra arcanīyo divākaraḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Therefore, the people desirous of welfare, should not adore any other god. On the other hand, depending upon the visible Sungod, one should achieve the invisible fortunes. Therefore, O Brahmana, you should always worship the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.66.63 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*aho ya eṣa kathito bhavatā bhāskaro mama \|*  
*devatā sarvadevānāṃ naitanmithyā prajāyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Yajnavalkya said — The discourse about the Sungod which has been delivered by you for me is all complete and away from falsehood.

## \|\| 1.66.64 \|\|

*tasya devasya māhātmyaṃ śrutaṃ subahuśo mayā \|*  
*devarṣisiddhamanujaiḥ stutasyeha mahātmanaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. This is because, I have listened to the glory of the Sungod from the gods, Siddhas and the humans, many times.

## \|\| 1.66.65 \|\|

*kaḥ stauti daivatamajaṃ yasyaitatsacarācaram \|*  
*akṣayasyāprameyasya kiraṇodgamanādbhavet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Who can offer prayer to the unborn god who is indestructible, beyond comprehension and created the mobile and immobile creatures with his rays? Who else can do so?

## \|\| 1.66.66-67 \|\|

*dakṣiṇātkiraṇādyasya sambhūto bhagavānhariḥ \|*  
*vāmādbhavāṃstathā jātaḥ kiraṇātkila kañjaja \|\| 66 \|\|*

*lālāṭādyasya rudrastu kā tulyā tena devatā \|*  
*tasya devasya kaḥ śaktaḥ pravaktuṃ guṇavistaram \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. From whose right rays Vishnu was born, Brahma was born of the left rays, while Shiva emerged out of his forehead. Who is the other god comparable to him in virtues and who can speak out about his glory?

## \|\| 1.66.68 \|\|

*so'hamicchāmi devasya tasya sarvātmanaḥ prabho \|*  
*śrotumārādhanaṃ yena nistareyaṃ bhavārṇakam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. I would like to learn about the worship of the supreme soul, by which I would try to cross the ocean of the universe.

## \|\| 1.66.69-70 \|\|

*kenopāyena mantrairvā rahasyaiḥ paricaryayā \|*  
*dānairvratopavāsairvā homairjapyairathāpi vā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*ārādhitaḥ samastānāṃ kleśānāṃ hānido raviḥ \|*  
*śakyaḥ samārādhayituṃ kathaṃ śaṃsa prajāpate \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. In what way, the Sungod is pleased removing all the miseries? What types of mantra, secretive devotion or meditation, charities, vratas, fastings, homas and the japam are prescribed for him? O Prajapati, in which way should I worship him?

## \|\| 1.66.71 \|\|

*janmanyavitathā saikā kriyā yārkaṃ samāśritā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Though in the life of the enthusiastic people, because of their being religious minded, they achieve success in kama and art ha. This is the only effort by which the Sungod should be worshipped, which could comparatively be more successful.

## \|\| 1.66.72 \|\|

*durgasaṃsārakāṃtāramapāramabhidhāvatām \|*  
*ekaḥ sūryanamaskāro muktimārgasya deśakaḥ2 \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Therefore, in the inaccessible forest of the world, having lost the way one who is aimlessly wandering, for him the adoration of the Sungod is the only way for salvation.

## \|\| 1.66.73-75 \|\|

*so'hamicchāmi taṃ devaṃ saptalokaparāyaṇam \|*  
*kālāyanamaśeṣasya1 jagato hadyavasthitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*ārādhayituṃ gopālaṃ graheśamamitaujasam \|*  
*śaṅkaraṃ jagato dīpaṃ smṛtamātrāghanāśanam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tamanādyaṃ suraśreṣṭhaṃ prasādayitumicchataḥ \|*  
*upadeśapradānena prasādaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. Therefore, I myself, would like to please the lord who is the foremost of the seven lokas, is enshrined in the heart of all the living beings, is the movement of the time, preserver of the earth, chief of the planets, immensely illustrious, bestower of welfare, the resplendence of the world, who can destroy the sins by his mere thinking, eternal and the best of the gods. You kindly enlighten me on the method to be used to please him.

## \|\| 1.66.76 \|\|

*tasyaitadvacanaṃ śrutyā bhaktimudvahato ravau \|*  
*jagāma paritoṣaṃ sa padmayonirmahātapāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus listening to his speech which was overwhelmed with the devotion, Brahma — the great tapasvi, was immensely pleased.

## \|\| 1.66.77 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yatpṛcchasi dvijaśreṣṭha sūryasyārādhanaṃ prati \|*  
*vratopavāsajapyādi tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Brahma said — O best of the Brahmanas, the worship of the Sungod is carried out by performing vratas, fasting, japam etc. I am speaking out whatever has been asked by you. You listen to me with apt attention.

## \|\| 1.66.78-80 \|\|

*anādi yatparaṃ brahma sarvaheyavivarjitam \|*  
*vyāpya yatsarvabhūteṣu sthitaṃ sadasataḥ param \|\| 78 \|\|*

*pradhānapuṃsoranayoryataḥ kṣobhaḥ pravartate \|*  
*nityayorvyāpinoścaiva jagadādau mahātmanoḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tatkṣobhakatvād brahmāṃḍaṃ sṛṣṭerheturnirañjanaḥ \|*  
*aheturapi sarvātmā jāyate parameśvaraḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. The Sungod is eternal, supreme Brahman, free from the worldly objects, pervading in all the living beings separated from sat and asat, everlasting and pervading in the entire universe. It is he by whom the disturbance is created in the beginning in the Pradhana Purusha. It is because of the disturbance, the universe was created. He is formless, the cause of the earth, universal soul and the supreme lord.

## \|\| 1.66.81 \|\|

*pradhānapuruṣatvaṃ ca tathaiveśvaralīlayā \|*  
*samupaiti tataścaivaṃ brahmatvaṃ chandataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The same lord also takes to the form of Pradhana Purusha with his divine sports.

## \|\| 1.66.82 \|\|

*tataḥ sthitau pālayitā viṣṇutvaṃ jagataḥ kṣaye \|*  
*rudratvaṃ ca jagannāthaḥ svecchayā kurute raviḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. By his own sweet will, he becomes the preserver of the universe. For the destruction of the universe, he takes to the form of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.66.83 \|\|

*tamekamakṣaraṃ dhāma sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|*  
*bhedābhedasvarūpaṃ taṃ praṇipatya divākaram \|*  
*3 varṇayiṣye'khilaṃ vipra tasyaivārādhanaṃ raveḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Therefore, the same Sungod, who is indestructible, is adored by all the gods, splitted and unsplitted for and is also called Divakara. I adore him.

## \|\| 1.66.84 \|\|

*guhyaṃ cāpi tathā tasya bhāskarasya śṛṇuṣva vai \|*  
*tuṣṭena hi purā mahyaṃ kathitaṃ bhāskareṇa tu \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O Brahmana, this is his secret possession, which you have already related to me with delight.

## Chapter 67. Talk between Brahma and Yajnavalkya

## \|\| 1.67.1-2 \|\|

*viśvago viśvabhūtaśca viśvātmā viśvasambhavaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pratyakṣatvamatho gatvā rahasyaṃ proktavānmama \|*  
*ahaṃ ca kṛtavānpraśnaṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyakṣato ravim \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Brahma said — In earlier times, I, with all humility, inspite of adoring another god, adoring the Sungod was face to face with him. At that very moment, he enlightened me on some re-creative issues. Coming face to face with him, I asked him.

## \|\| 1.67.3-5 \|\|

*taṃ devāścāsurāścaiva nānāmatasamāśritāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhūtabhavyaṃ tvayi sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*catvāro hyāśramā deva sarve gārhasthyamūlakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yajante tvāmaharaharnānāmūrtisamāśritāḥ \|*  
*pitā mātā hi sarvasya daivataṃ tvaṃ hiṃ śāśvatam \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. O lord in the Vedas and the post-Vedic literature besides the Puranas, you have been described as unborn, the ancient one and Dhata. Besides that, the five bhutas of the earth, the past, present and future are established in you. Similarly, the ashramas including that of the B which are the base of the householder, all of them taking to different forms, adore your various types of images. You are also parents for everyone, besides being the eternal lord.

## \|\| 1.67.6 \|\|

*yajase caiva kaṃ devameva cāpi na vidmahe \|*  
*kathyatāṃ mama deveśa paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Who is the god worshipped by you which I am not aware of? Therefore you enlighten me on this issue. It is because, I am feeling quite anxious to know about it.

## \|\| 1.67.7-15 \|\|

*itthaṃ mayokto bhagavānidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*avācyametadvaktavyamātmaguhyaṃ sanātanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tava bhaktimato brahmanvakṣyāmīha yathātatham \|*  
*yataḥ sūkṣmamavijñeyamavyaktamacalaṃ dhruvam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*indriyairindriyārthaiśca sarvabhūtaiśca varjitam \|*  
*sa hyantarātmā bhūtānāṃ kṣetrajñaśceti kathyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*triguṇavyatirikto'sau puruṣaśceti kathyate \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho bhagavānsaiva4 buddhiriti smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*mahāniti ca yogeṣu pradhānaśceti kathyate \|*  
*sāṃkhye5 ca paṭhyate śāstre nāmabhirbahubhiḥ sadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dhṛtaṃ caivātmakaṃ yena idaṃ trailokyamātmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*aśarīraḥ śarīreṣu lipyate na ca karmabhiḥ \|*  
*mamāntarātmā tava ca ye cānye dehasaṃjñakāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ sākṣibhūto'sau2 na karoti na lipyate \|*  
*saguṇo nirguṇo viṣṇurjñānagamyo hyasau smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarvataḥ pāṇipādo'sau sarvato'kṣiśiromukhaḥ \|*  
*sarvataḥ śrutiyukto'sau sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati \|\| 15 \|\|*

7-15. At these words spoken by me, he said — “This is not the subject to be talked to everyone. It is indistinct, extremely secret and ancient subject, but observing your devotion, I shall surely reveal the truth to you. He is the subtle Deva, who is invisible, immobile, unshakable, separated from the sense organs and all the living beings. He is the inner soul of the living beings, the creator, apart from the three gums i.e., sattva, rajas and tamas. He is the Pradhana Purusha, lord Brahma himself, the form of wisdom, the great personality in yoga, the foremost in the Samkhya yoga, has a universal form, the support of the world, soul of the world, the cause of the world. He is the carrier of the three lokas. Inspite of his being formless and with form, he is free from the deeds. He lives in my as well as your heart. He is the witness of the deeds of all the living beings. He is Vishnu basing attributes and who is without attributes as well. He can be known by divine wisdom He has many arms and feet wound him, besides many eyes, heads, mouths and the cars. He covers all like a curtain and stands there.

## \|\| 1.67.16-17 \|\|

*viśvamūrdhā4 viśvabhujo viśvapādākṣināsikaḥ \|*  
*ekaścarati kṣetreṣu svairacārī yathāsukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṣetrāṇyasya śarīrāṇi bījaṃ cāpi śubhāśubham \|*  
*tāni vetti sa yogātmā ataḥ kṣetrajña ucyate \|*  
*avyaktake pure śete tenā'sau puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. He is the bead of the world, besides the arms, eyes, nose. He is the one who wanders m the entire body at will. He is the form of body as well as its auspicious and inauspicious farms besides being the seeds thereof. With the use of yogic practices, he attains complete knowledge of all. Therefore, he is called Kshetrajna or the one who lives in the invisible abode. He is therefore called Purusha.

## \|\| 1.67.18 \|\|

*viśvaṃ bahuvidhaṃ jñeyaṃ sa ca sarvatra vidyate \|*  
*tasmātsa bahurūpatvādviśvarūpa iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Because of his all-pervading nature and his taking too many forms, he is known as one with a universal form.

## \|\| 1.67.19 \|\|

*mahāpuruṣaśabdaṃ hi bibhartyeṣa sanātanaḥ \|*  
*sa tu vai vikriyāpannaḥ sṛjatyātmānamātmanā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Similarly, the words as well as Sanatana are also used for him. He, with the use of his soul, incarnates on the earth.

## \|\| 1.67.20 \|\|

*ākāśātpatitaṃ toyaṃ yāti svādvantaraṃ yathā \|*  
*bhūme rasaviśeṣeṇa tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Like the water falling from the sky over different types of lands, develops different tastes.

## \|\| 1.67.21 \|\|

*eka eva yathā vāyurdehe tiṣṭhati pañcadhā \|*  
*ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca tathā tasya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As only one type of wind pervades in body and inspite of its being of five types has one as well as different forms.

## \|\| 1.67.22 \|\|

*sthānāntaraviśeṣeṇa yathāgnirlabhate parām \|*  
*saṃjñāṃ dāvāgrikādyeṣu tathā devo hyasau smṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. As the fire, by burning at a particular place is known as the forest fire, similarly the lord, inspite of his being of a single form, has been conceived to be of several forms.

## \|\| 1.67.23 \|\|

*yathā dīpasahasrāṇi dīpa ekaḥ prasūyate \|*  
*tathā rūpasahasrāṇi sa evaikaḥ prasūyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. As one can light several lamps with a single lamp, similarly he, being one, takes the thousands of forms.

## \|\| 1.67.24 \|\|

*sa yadā budhyatetmānaṃ tadā bhavati kevalaḥ \|*  
*ekatvaṃ pralaye cāsya bahutvaṃ syātpravartane \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When he becomes aware of his own soul, then he becomes absolute. Similarly, during the dissolution, he remains alone, but in the universe, he takes to many forms.

## \|\| 1.67.25 \|\|

*nityaṃ hi nāsti jagati bhūtaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*ṛte1 tamekamīśānaṃ puruṣaṃ bījasaṃjñitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In this mobile and immobile world, none is eternal, except the Purusha who is the form of seed.

## \|\| 1.67.26-28 \|\|

*akṣayaścāprameyadhra savargabhra sa ucyate \|*  
*tasmādavyaktamutpannaṃ triguṇaṃ sarvakāraṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*avyaktāvyaktabhāvasthā yā sā prakṛtirucyate \|*  
*tāṃ yoniṃ brahmaṇo viddhi yo'sau sadasadātmakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nāsti tasmātparo hyanyaḥ sa pitā sa prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*ātmā mama sa vijñeyastatastaṃ pūjayāmyaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. He is known as indestructible, beyond comprehension and all pervading. Therefore, he is believed to be the cause of all. Out of him Trigunatmika Prakriti was born, besides the Sakala-Prakriti. He happens to be the yoni or womb of Brahman. He is Sadasadatmaka, he creates as well as is Prajapati and nothing is beyond him. The same happens to be my soul and I worship the same.

## \|\| 1.67.29 \|\|

*svargatāścāpi ye kecittaṃ namasyanti dehinaḥ \|*  
*te tatprasādādgacchanti tenādiṣṭāḥ parāṃ gatim \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. All the living beings, proceeding on to the heaven, offer their salutation to him before leaving the earth. Because it is with his pleasure alone, that they receive the best position.

## \|\| 1.67.30 \|\|

*bhaktyā sampūjayantyādyaṃ gatiṃ caiṣāṃ dadāti saḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. All the gods and the asuras adore him with devotion in the form of various religious sects and they achieve the beatitude by his grace alone.

## \|\| 1.67.31 \|\|

*sa hi sarvagataścaiva nirguṇaścāpi kathyate \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā tamātmānaṃ pūjayāmi sanātanam \|*  
*bhāskaraṃ devadeveśaṃ sarvabhūteśamacyutam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He is therefore all pervading and devoid of attributes. A person, finding in him his own soul who also happens to be Bhaskara, god of gods, lord of the bhutas, besides being infallible, adores him.

## \|\| 1.67.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityuktavānpurā pṛṣṭo mayā devo divākaraḥ \|*  
*pūjaya tvaṃ mahātmānaṃ tapantaṃ vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Brahma said — Thus at my request, the lord Divakara said to me whatever has been spoken by me. Therefore, you should also worship the illustrious one.

## Chapter 68. Fast of Siddhartha Saptami

## \|\| 1.68.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vacmi te paramaṃ devaṃ sarvadevaiśca pūjitam \|*  
*ārādhayanti yaṃ devaṃ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — I am speaking about the great lord, who is adorable for all the gods. Even I myself, Vishnu and Shiva too adore him.

## \|\| 1.68.2-4 \|\|

*mandārapuṣpaiḥ pūjā tu sarvakuṣṭhavināśinī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jātipuṣpairdvijaśreṣṭha dhūpena vijayena tu \|*  
*vṛṣaṇaṃ sihlakaṃ vipra śrīkhaṇḍamagarustathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*karpūraṃ ca tathā mustā śarkarā satvacā dvija \|*  
*ityeṣa vijayo dhūpaḥ svayaṃ devena nirmitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. For the same, lotus like lord Surya is worshipped by Brahma with lotus and guggulu. The same Sungod of the sky is adored with the offering of the jasmine flowers and the incense known by the name of Vijaya, by lord Shiva. O Brahmana, the bull, incense, Shrikhanda, sandalpaste, guggulu, camphor, mixed with sugar is called Vijaya-incense. This was revealed to me by the lord himself.

## \|\| 1.68.5-9 \|\|

*keśavaścakrarūpaṃ tu sadā sampūjayedravim \|*  
*nīlotpaladalaśyāmo nīlotpalakadambakaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dhūpenāgurusaṃjñena bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*mayā sa pṛṣṭo deveśastasyaivārādhanāya vai \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kāni puṣpāṇi ceṣṭāni sadā bhāskarapūjane \|*  
*tena coktāni puṣpāṇi svayaṃ tāni nibodha me \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mallikāyāstu kusumairbhogavāñjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ puṇḍarīkaiśca bhajatyeva ca śāśvatam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*1 gandhakuṭajakaiḥ puṣpaiḥ paramaiśvaryamaśnute \|*  
*bhavatyakṣayamatyantaṃ nityamarcayato ravim \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Lord Vishnu has dark complexion like the lotus petal and he adores the Sungod with blue lotus flowers and guggulu. The Sungod has the form of a wheel. Once I asked Vishnu as to which type of flowers would be needed for the worship of the Sungod? You listen to the reply he gave. By worshipping the Sungod offering the jasmine flowers, a person earns great fortunes. By worshipping him with lotus flowers, there is a boost in his fortunes. By offering the Kutaja flowers to the Sungod, the devotee’s wealth is increased.

## \|\| 1.68.10-12 \|\|

*bilvapatraiśca kusumairmahatīṃ śriyamaśnute \|\| 10 \|\|*

*arkasrajā bhavatyarthaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*pradadyādūpiṇīṃ kanyāmarcito bakulasrajā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kiṃśukairarcito devo na pīḍayati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*pūjito'gastyakusumairānukūlyaṃ prayacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. With the worship of the Sun with the flowers of swallow wort, all types of leprosy is removed. By offering the wood apple as well as leaves of the same tree, besides the red flowers, one gets enormous riches. By using the garland of swallow wort flowers, all the desires are fulfilled. By offering garland of flowers of Bakula tree, one gets a beautiful girl; by offering of the Kimshuka flowers the Sungod is pleased, and with the offering of the Agastya all the desires of a person are fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.68.13-14 \|\|

*karavīraistu viprendra sūryasyānucaro bhavet \|*  
*tathā 1 mudgarapuṣpaiśca samabhyarcya divākaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

*haṃsayuktena yānena raveḥ sālokyatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*śatapuṣpasahasraistu pūṣasālokyatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*bakapuṣpairdvijaśreṣṭha yāti bhānusalokatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. With the offering of oleander flowers, the devotee becomes the attendant of the Sungod. With the offering of the mudgara flowers the devotee, boarding a plane driven by swans, reaches the abode of the Sungod, where he achieves his Salokya type of salvation. O best of Brahmanas, a person who offers a thousand flowers of Satapushpa, he achieves the Salokya salvation of the Pusha form of the Sungod By offering the white flowers to the Sungod, one gets Salokya salvation.

## \|\| 1.68.15 \|\|

*catuḥsamena gandhena samabhyarcya divākaram \|*  
*pañcabhūtālayasthānamāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the Sungod is adored with four types of fragrance, one achieves the place where the five bhutas get merged There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.68.16 \|\|

*devāgāraṃ tu sammārjya bhaktyā yastu pralepayet \|*  
*sa rogānmucyate kṣipraṃ dravyalābhaṃ ca vindati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. With the dusting and cleaning of the temple or plastering it with the cowdung, one is released of ailments besides earning riches.

## \|\| 1.68.17 \|\|

*tasya cāyatanaṃ bhaktyā gairikeṇopalepayet \|*  
*prāpnuyānmahatīṃ lakṣmīṃ rogaiścāpi pramucyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When the Sun temple is coloured and washed with ochre colour, one is relieved of the ailments besides earning wealth.

## \|\| 1.68.18 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśeha kuṣṭhāni ye cānye vyādhayo nṛṇām \|*  
*pralayaṃ yānti te sarve mṛdā yadyupalepayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. With the purification of the temple with the dust or clay, the eighteen types of leprosy disease of people are removed.

## \|\| 1.68.19 \|\|

*vilepanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ raktacandanamuttamam \|*  
*puṣpāṇāṃ karavīrāṇi praśastāni pracakṣate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Of the plasters, that of the red sandal paste is said to be the best. Out of the flowers, the oleander flowers are said to be the best for the Sun worship.

## \|\| 1.68.20 \|\|

*nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcidbhāsvatastuṣṭikārakam \|*  
*kiṃ tasya na bhavelloke yastvebhiḥ svarcayedravim \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Therefore, there is nothing else better than these things to please the Sungod. A person who does so, he gets the things which are impossible to get.

## \|\| 1.68.21 \|\|

*karavīraiḥ pūjayedyo bhāskaraṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddho'sau sūryakāmamavāpnuyāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Therefore, a person who worships the Sungod with oleander flowers, all his desires are fulfilled and he achieves the grace of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.68.22 \|\|

*vilepyāyatanaṃ3 yastu kuryānmaṇḍalakaṃ śubham \|*  
*sa sūryalokamāsādya modate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Purifying the temple by plastering, one who creates a mandala in the same quite neatly, he achieving the abode of the Sungod, lives there for many years.

## \|\| 1.68.23-25 \|\|

*ekenāsya bhavedartho dvābhyāmārogyamaśnute \|*  
*tribhiḥ santatyavicchinnā caturbhirbhārgavīṃ4 labhet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pañcabhirvipulaṃ dhānyaṃ ṣaḍbhirāyurbalaṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*saptamaṇḍalakārī syānmaṃḍalādhipatirnara \|\| 24 \|\|*

*āyurdhanasutairyuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate \|*  
*ghṛtapradīpadānena cakṣuṣmāñjāyate naraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. By thus creating a mandala one becomes healthy; by creating three masalas one gets land; wealth by five mandala, by drawing out six mandalas one gets long life and becoming mandaleshvara, he enjoys long life, wealth and sons. He ultimately achieves the place of the Sungod. Similarly with the offering of the lamps of ghi, a person enjoys a long life.

## \|\| 1.68.26-29 \|\|

*kaṭutailapradānena sa śatrūñjayate naraḥ \|*  
*tilatailapradānena sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

*madhūkatailadānena saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ vrajet \|*  
*saṃpūjya vidhivaddevaṃ puṣpadhūpādibhirbudhaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yathāśaktyā tataḥ paścānnaivedyaṃ bhaktito nyaset \|*  
*puṣpāṇāṃ pravarā jātī dhūpānāṃ vijayaḥ paraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*gandhānāṃ kuṅkumaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ lepānāṃ raktacandanam \|*  
*dīpadāne ghṛtaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naivedye modakaḥ paraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. By offering the mustard oil lamps, one becomes victorious over the enemy; by offering the sesamum oil lamps, one achieves grace in the Suryaloka; by offering the madhuka oil lamp, one achieves enormous fortunes. Similarly, adoration of the Sungod is made by offering various types of flowers as well, besides incense Vijaya, fragrance of saffron, paste of red sandal paste, the lamp of ghi and the sweet balls in the eatables. These are all considered to be the best.

## \|\| 1.68.30-31 \|\|

*etaistuṣyati deveśaḥ sānnidhyaṃ cādhigacchati \|*  
*evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivatkṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ devadevaṃ divākaram \|*  
*sukhāsīnastataḥ paśyedraverabhimukhe sthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Because having been adored in this way, the Sungod is immensely pleased and one also achieves his protection as well. Thus by adoring him with circumambulation and offering salutation, bowing one’s head, then the devotee should be seated before him and have a look at him.

## \|\| 1.68.32-35 \|\|

*ekaṃ siddhārthakaṃ kṛtvā haste pānīyasaṃyutam \|*  
*kāmaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā taṃ vāñchitaṃ naraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*pibetsatoyaṃ taṃ vipra aspṛṣṭaṃ daśanaiḥ sakṛt \|*  
*dvitīyāyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ dvau gṛhītvā tu suvrata \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tṛtīyāyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ grahītavyāstrayo'pi ca \|*  
*jñeyāścaturthyāṃ catvāraḥ pañcamyāṃ pañca eva hi \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ṣaṭ pibeccāpi ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|*  
*saptamyāṃ saptamāyāṃ tu sapta caiva pibennaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. Then carrying the mustard seed in one’s hand, recalling the purpose of his worship in his mind, he should consume it. The water so consumed should not be allowed to touch the teeth. The same process should be repeated on the second Saptami, when the devotee should consume two seeds of mustard; three seeds on the third Saptami; four seeds on the fourth Saptami; five seeds on the fifth Saptami; six seeds on the sixth Saptami and seven seeds on the seventh Saptami.

## \|\| 1.68.36 \|\|

*ādau prabhṛti vijñeyo mantro'yamabhimantraṇe \|*  
*siddhārthakastvaṃ hi loke sarvatra śrūyase yathā \|*  
*tathā māmapi siddhārthamarthataḥ kurutāṃ raviḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Every time the devotee should sanctify the seeds uttering the mantra — Siddharthakastvam hi loke etc.

## \|\| 1.68.37 \|\|

*tato havirupaspṛśya japaṃ kuryādyathepsitam \|*  
*hutāśanaṃ ca juhuyādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thereafter, touching with ghi the devotee should perform the japam as per his wish. Thereafter, homa should be performed in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 1.68.38-40 \|\|

*evameva parāḥ kāryā saptamyaḥ sapta sarvadā \|*  
*ekātprabhṛti kāryā sā sarvadodakasaptamī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ekaṃ toyena sahitaṃ dvau cāpi ghṛtasaṃyutau \|*  
*trīṃstathā madhunā sārdhaṃ dadhnā catura eva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yuktānnapayasā pañca ṣaṭ ca gomayasaṃyutān \|*  
*pañcagavyena vai sapta pibetsiddhārthakāndvija \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. The same process has been prescribed for all the seven Saptamis. There is another procedure for the same. One should consume a mustard seed with water. On the second Saptami one should consume two mustard seeds with ghi. On the third Saptami three seeds should be consumed with honey. On the fourth Saptami four mustard seeds should be consumed with curd. On the fifth Saptami, five mustard seeds should be consumed with milk or food. On the sixth Saptami, six mustard seeds should be consumed with cowdung, while on the seventh Saptami, seven mustard seeds should be consumed with Panchagavya or the five cow products.

## \|\| 1.68.41 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kuryātsarṣapasaptamīm \|*  
*bahuputro bahudhanaḥ siddhārthaścāpi sarvadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A person who performs the mustard seeds vrata appropriately, he achieves a number of sons, enormous riches and his desires are always fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.68.42 \|\|

*iha loke naro vipra pretyayāti vibhāvasum \|*  
*tasmātsampūjayeddevaṃ vidhinānena bhāskaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thus a person, getting all his desires fulfilled in this world, ultimately achieves the abode of Surya. Therefore, you also worship the Sungod accordingly.

## Chapter 69. Interpretation of dreams

## \|\| 1.69.1-5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*saptamyāmuṣito vipraḥ svapnadarśanamucyate \|*  
*svapne dṛṣṭe ca saptamyāṃ puruṣo niyatavrataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*samāpya vidhivatsarvaṃ japahomādikaṃ kramāt \|*  
*pūjayitvā dineśaṃ tu yathāvibhavamātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataḥ śayīta śayane devadevaṃ vicintayan \|*  
*samprasupto yadā paśyedudayantaṃ divākaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śakradhvajaṃ tathā candraṃ tasya sarvāḥ samṛddhayaḥ \|*  
*dṛśyaṃ janaṃ tathā śaktiṃ1 sragvigoveṇunisvanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śvetābjacāmarādarśakanakāsisutodbhavam \|*  
*rudhirasya srutiṃ sekaṃ pānaṃ caiśvaryakārakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Brahma said — It is said that a Brahmana who fasts on the day of Saptami in an appropriate manner, he surely has an audience with the Sungod. The performer of the vrata» after witnessing the dream, should perform Homa etc. and then complete the fast by worshipping the Sungod. Then conceiving of a dream, he should resort to sleeping asana. In case, he witnesses the flag of the Sungod besides the moon, he achieves all the prosperity. Similarly, when a person witnesses in his dream a beautiful and healthy person, a cow wearing a garland, voice of the lute, white lotus, flywhisk, mirror, gold, sword, the son’s birth, flow of blood, then one achieves all the wealth and riches.

## \|\| 1.69.6-7 \|\|

*śvetāyāḥ pañcapūtāyā darśanaṃ vṛddhikārakam \|*  
*prajāpaterghṛtāktasya darśanaṃ putradaṃ smṛtam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śastavṛkṣābhirohaśca kṣipramaiśvaryakārakaḥ \|*  
*dohanaṃ mahiṣīsiṃhīgodhenūnāṃ svake mukhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. When the jack fruit is seen in a dream it stands for prosperity, when Prajapate is seen soaked in ghi it results in having a virtuous sun, besides with the climbing over one auspicious tree in a dream, results in sudden receipt of wealth. Similar would be the result in case a person witnessing of a buffalo, a female tiger and the cows.

## \|\| 1.69.8-17 \|\|

*dhanuṣāṃ ca śarāṇāṃ ca nābhau ca drutanirgatiḥ \|*  
*abhihanyātsvayaṃ khādetsiṃhāngā bhujagāṃstathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*svāṃgaśīrṣaṃ2 hutavahe tasya śrīragrataḥ sthitā \|*  
*rājate haimane pātre yo bhuṃkte pāyasaṃ dvijaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*padmapatre yathā viprastasya jantorbalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*dyūte vāde'tha vā yuddhe vijayo hi sukhāvahaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*agnestu grasanaṃ vipra āgreyaṃ vṛddhikārakam \|*  
*gātrasya jvalanaṃ vipra śirovedhaśca bhūtaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mālyāmbarāṇāṃ4 yuktānāṃ śastānāṃ śuklapakṣiṇām \|*  
*sadā lābhaṃ praśaṃsanti tathā viṣṭhānulepanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*svāṅgasya kartane kṣepe rathayāne prajāgamaḥ \|*  
*nānāśirobāhutā ca hastānāṃ kurute śriyam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*agamyāgamanaṃ caiva śokamadhyayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*devadvijajanācāryaguruvṛddhatapasvinaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yadyadvadanti tatsarvaṃ satyameva hi nirdiśet \|*  
*praśastadarśanaṃ caiva abhiṣeko nṛpaśriyāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*syādrājyaṃ śiraśchedena bahudhā sphuṭitena tu \|*  
*ruditaṃ harṣasamprāptyai rājyaṃ nigaḍabandhane \|\| 16 \|\|*

*turaṅgaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ padmaṃ rājānāṃ śvetakuñjaram \|*  
*mahadaiśvaryamāpnoti yobhīkaścādhirohati \|\| 17 \|\|*

8-17. In case, the arrows enter in the navel and issue from the back or the arrows kill a lion, a cow and the serpents or one himself eats them up, or when a person witnesses the pouring of a lead in fire, he suddenly achieves the riches. When a person consumes the payasam in a gold or silver vase or the lotus leaf, he enters in controversy in fight or in gambling, besides victory in war. By inhaling of fire, a person’s power of digestion improves. With the burning of the body or when the head is captured, one achieves wealth. In case an auspicious bird drops its droppings over the head in a dream, one earns profits. With the witnessing of one’s own limbs floating in water and by boarding a chariot, one gets progeny. In case a person witnesses many hands, heads and arms, he unites with a forbidden woman. By grieving and resorting to studies, one earns riches. Whatever is spoken in a dream by the gods, Brahmanas, Acharyas, preceptors, an aged person, or an ascetic, it should be treated as true. By witnessing the crowning of the king, one achieves fortunes, with the cutting off of the head or breaking of it in many parts, or tying the same in the hair lock, one achieves kingship, besides the steed, bulls, lotus, kingship, and riding the white elephant by the passionate and merciless master, he achieves enormous wealth.

## \|\| 1.69.18-20 \|\|

*grasamāno grahāṃstārā mahīṃ ca parivartayan \|*  
*unmūlayanparvatāṃśca rājyalābhamavāpnuyāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dehānniṣkrāntirantrāṇāṃ tairvā vṛkṣasya veṣṭanam \|*  
*pātaḥ samudrasaritāmaiśvaryāṇi sukhāni ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*udadhiṃ saritaṃ vāpi tīrtvā pāraṃ prayāti ca \|*  
*adriṃ laṅghayateścāpi bhavantyarthajayāyuṣaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. By witnessing in dream the swelling of a star or a planet, up turning of the earth, besides uprooting of the mountains, one achieves enormous riches and throne. By taking out of intestines or circling the same around a tree or thus falling in a river or in the ocean, one achieves pleasures. In case a person crosses a river or returns after crossing it or by crossing the mountain, one gets long life.

## \|\| 1.69.21 \|\|

*ujjvalā strī viśedaṅkamāśīrvādaparāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*bhavatyarthāgamaḥ śīghraṃ kṛmibhiryadi bhakṣyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In case a fair complexioned lady enters into the limb or the ladies showering blessings and the body being eaten by worms, one receives the sudden wealth.

## \|\| 1.69.22-24 \|\|

*svapne svapna iti jñātaṃ dṛṣṭaprakathanaṃ tathā \|*  
*maṅgalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śubhaṃ darśanameva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*saṃyogaścaiva maṅgalyairārogyadhanakārakaḥ \|*  
*aiśvaryarājyalābhāya yasminsvapna udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tairdṛṣṭai rogiṇo rogānmucyante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*na svapnaṃ śobhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā svapyātprātaśca kīrtayet \|*  
*rājabhojakaviprebhyaḥ śucibhyaśca śucirnaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. To dream during a dream, or to relate the dream after the awakening, bestows welfare, besides good health and riches. Besides the dream, which results in to getting fortunes or kingship, in case the same is witnessed by an ailing person, then he is surely freed from his ailment. Thus after witnessing the pleasant dream, one should go to sleep again. After having a purifying bath in the morning, the noble king should repeat it to the Brahmanas.

## Chapter 70. Sarshapa Saptami

## \|\| 1.70.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tato madhyāhnasamaye snātaḥ prayatamānasaḥ \|*  
*tathaiva devānvidhivatpūjayitvā yathāsukham1 \|\| 1 \|\|*

*samyakkṛtajapo maunī naro hutahutāśanaḥ \|*  
*niṣkramya devāyatanādbhojakānbhojayettataḥ 1 \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Brahma said — Then during the mid-day getting relieved of the bath and sandhya adoration, a person should worship the Sungod and other deities appropriately, besides the japam. After finishing these activities, a person should serve food to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.70.3 \|\|

*tathā purāṇaviduṣa itihāsavido dvijān \|*  
*tathā vedavidaścaiva divyānbhaumāṃśca suvrata \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Thereafter, food should be offered to the Brahmanas well-versed in the Puranas, history and the Vedic scriptures.

## \|\| 1.70.4 \|\|

*raktāni vastrāṇi tathā ca gāvaḥ sugandhamālyādi haviṣyamannam \|*  
*payasvinī cāpyatha bhojakāya deyā tathānyatpriyamātmano yat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Suvrata, then the red costumes, cow, fragrance, garland, havishya food, milking cow, and the dearest object should be given over to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.70.5 \|\|

*bhavedalābho yadi bhojakānāṃ viprāstadārhanti jayopajīvinaḥ \|*  
*ye mantravidbrāhmaṇapāṭhakāśca ye ye'pi sāmādhyayaneṣu yuktāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the absence of the Bhojaka Brahmanas, the Brahmanas performing japam, well-versed in mantras or the reciter of the Vedas, could be made to officiate in place of the Bhojaka Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.70.6 \|\|

*prathamaṃ bhojakā bhojyāḥ purāṇaviduṣaiḥ2 saha \|*  
*teṣāmṛte mantravidastathā vedavido dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Initially, the Bhojakas are required to be served food with the Pauranika Brahmanas. In the absence of these Brahmanas, the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedic hymns, should be substituted.

## \|\| 1.70.7 \|\|

*kṛtvaivaṃ saptamī sapta naro bhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|*  
*śraddadhāno'nasūyaśca anantaṃ prāpnuyātsukham 3 \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. With utmost devotion and getting free from malice, fasting should be done on all the seven moon days and a person who does so earns enormous comforts.

## \|\| 1.70.8 \|\|

*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ kṛtānāṃ yatphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*tatphalaṃ saptamī2 sapta kṛtvā prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The merit one achieves by performing ten Ashvamedha sacrifices, a person gets the same reward by fasting on the seven moon days.

## \|\| 1.70.9 \|\|

*duṣprāpaṃ nāsti talloke anayā yanna labhyate \|*
