*na ca rogostyasau loke anayā yo na śāmyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Therefore, one who completes this process, nothing become beyond his reach during this birth and he is freed from all the ailments.

## \|\| 1.70.10 \|\|

*kuṣṭhāni cāpi sarvāṇi durucchedyānyapi dhruvam \|*  
*apayānti yathā nāgā garuḍasya bhayārditāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All types of leprosies, which are believed to be incurable, vanish in no time as the Nagas disappear getting frightened from Garuda.

## \|\| 1.70.11 \|\|

*vrataniyamatapobhiḥ saptamīḥ saptaevaṃ vidhivadiha hi kṛtvā mānavo dharmaśīlaḥ \|*  
*śrutadhanasutabhāgyārogyapuṇyairupeto vrajati tadanulokaṃ śāśvataṃ tigmaraśmeḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. With the performing of the vratas of all the seven Saptamis, a person is bestowed with sons, fortunes, good health and the merits. Ultimately, he reaches the abode of Surya.

## \|\| 1.70.12 \|\|

*imaṃ vidhiṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śrutvā kṛtvā ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*sahasraraśmiṃ sa viśeṣānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O best of the Brahmanas, with the performing and the listening of this method, a person enters the body of the Sungod. There is no need to have a second thought about the same.

## \|\| 1.70.13 \|\|

*surairvā munibhirvāpi purāṇajñairidaṃ śrutam \|*  
*sarve te paramātmānaṃ pūjayanti divākaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Therefore, all the deities, ascetics, the Pauranika Rishis and others, all getting well — versed in the same, adore the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.70.14 \|\|

*idamākhyānamārṣeyaṃ yanmayābhihitaṃ tava \|*  
*sūryabhaktāya dātavyaṃ netarāya 1 kadācana \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This is the topic revealed by the Rishis which is not to be revealed to anyone else except the devotees of the Sungod, and the same has been narrated by me to you.

## \|\| 1.70.15 \|\|

*yaścaitacchrāvayennityaṃ yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*sa sahasrārciṣaṃ devaṃ praviśennātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Therefore, who listens to the same or recites it to someone else, he surely enters the Sungod having a thousand rays.

## \|\| 1.70.16 \|\|

*mucyedārtastathā rogācchrutvemāmāditaḥ kathām \|*  
*jijñāsurlabhate kāmānbhaktaḥ sūryagatiṃ labhet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By listening to this episode from the start, a person is relieved of the distressed disease, a researcher becomes successful, while a devotee achieves the speed of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.70.17 \|\|

*kṣemeṇa gacchate'dhvānaṃ yastvidaṃ paṭhatedhvani \|*  
*yo yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ sa taṃ prāpnoti ca dhruvam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By so doing, even the pilgrims, make their pilgrimage successful, whatever articles are desired by them, they surely get the same.

## \|\| 1.70.18-19 \|\|

*ekāntabhāvopagata ekānte susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*prāpyaitatparamaṃ guhyaṃ bhūtvā sūryavrato naraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*lagnagarbhā pramucyeta garbhiṇī janayetsutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. In case, a person while performing this vrata, meditates upon the Sungod, then he surely achieves the abode of Bhaskara and the pregnant woman does not have to face the labour pains and she gives birth to a son.

## \|\| 1.70.20 \|\|

*vandhyā prasavamāpnoti putrapautrasamanvitam \|*  
*evametanmamākhyātaṃ bhāskareṇāmitaujasā \|*  
*mayāpi tava mākhyātaṃ bhaktyā bhānoridaṃ dvija \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With the shining lustre of the Sungod, the barren woman gets a son. O Brahmana, impressed with your devotion, I have narrated the story of the Sungod possessing the enormous lustre, which had been narrated to me earlier.

## \|\| 1.70.21 \|\|

*pūjanīyastvayā bhānuḥ sarvapāpopaśāntaye \|*  
*sa hi dhātā4 vidhātā ca sarvasya jagato guruḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Therefore, you should also worship the Sungod. By so doing, all the sins would disappear. It is because he is the creator as well as the preserver of all the living beings in the world. All the sins would vanish. You will be relieved of all the sins. He is also the preceptor of the universe.

## \|\| 1.70.22 \|\|

*udyanyaḥ kurute nityaṃ jagadvitimiraṃ karaiḥ \|*  
*dvādaśātmā sa deveśaḥ prīyatāṃ te'diteḥ sutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With his rays in the morning, he relieves the entire world of the darkness. He is twelve souled, the god of gods. Let the son of Aditi be pleased with you.

## Chapter 71. Name of Surya as spoken by Brahma

## \|\| 1.71.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nāmabhiḥ saṃstuto devo yairarkaḥ parituṣyati \|*  
*tāni te kīrtayāmyeṣa yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — The names, uttering which the Sungod gets delighted, I am repeating them here.

## \|\| 1.71.2 \|\|

*namaḥ sūryāya nityāya ravaye kāryabhānave \|*  
*bhāskarāya mataṅgāya mārtaṇḍāya vivasvate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. They are — Ravi, Surya, Karyabhanava, Bhaskara, Matanga, Martanda, Vivasvan, salutation to him.

## \|\| 1.71.3 \|\|

*ādityāyādidevāya namaste raśmimāline \|*  
*divākarāya dīptāya agnaye mihirāya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Aditya, Adideva, Rashmimali, Divakara, Dipta, Agni and Mihira, salutation to him always.

## \|\| 1.71.4 \|\|

*prabhākarāya mitrāya namaste'ditisambhava \|*  
*namo gopataye nityaṃ1 diśāṃ ca pataye namaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Prabhakara, Mitra, Aditi-Sambhava, Gopati, Dishapati, salutation to him always.

## \|\| 1.71.5 \|\|

*namo dhātre vidhātre ca aryamṇe varuṇāya ca \|*  
*pūṣṇe bhagāya mitrāya parjanyāyāṃśave namaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Dhata, Vidhata, Aryama, Varuna, Pusha, Bhaga, Mitra, Parjanya and Anshu, salutation to him always.

## \|\| 1.71.6 \|\|

*namo hitakṛte nityaṃ dharmāya tapanāya ca \|*  
*haraye2 haritāśvāya viśvasya pataye namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Hitakrita, Dharma, Tapana, Hari, Haritashva, Vishvapati, salutation to him always.

## \|\| 1.71.7 \|\|

*viṣṇave brahmaṇe nityaṃ tryambakāya tathātmane \|*  
*namaste saptalokeśa namaste saptasaptaye \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Vishnu, Brahma, Tryambaka, Atma, Saptalokesha, Saptasaptati, salutation to him always.

## \|\| 1.71.8 \|\|

*ekasmai hi namastubhyamekacakrarathāya ca \|*  
*jyotiṣāṃ pataye nityaṃ sarvaprāṇabhṛte namaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O having single wheel chariot, Jyotisham, preserver of all the living beings, salutation to you always.

## \|\| 1.71.9-11 \|\|

*hitāya sarvabhūtānāṃ śivāyārtiharāya ca \|*  
*namaḥ padmaprabodhāya namo vedādimūrtaye \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kādhijāya4 namastubhyaṃ namastārāsutāya ca \|*  
*bhīmajāya namastubhyaṃ pāvakāya ca vai namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dhiṣaṇāya5 namonityaṃ namaḥ kṛṣṇāya nityadā \|*  
*namo'stvaditiputrāya namo lakṣyāya nityaśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Well-wisher of all the living beings, Shiva, Artihara, Padma-Prabodhaya, Vedadi-murti, Bhima-putra, Mara-suta, Kadhija, Pavaka, Dhishna, Krishna, son of Aditi and Laksha, salutation to him always.

## \|\| 1.71.12 \|\|

*etānyādityanāmāni mayā proktāni vai purā \|*  
*ārādhanāya devasya sarvakāmena suvrata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In this way, O Suvrata, these names of the Sungod have been believed to be the bestower of success in all the desires, about which I have already discussed.

## \|\| 1.71.13 \|\|

*sāyaṃ prātaḥ śucirbhūtvā yaḥ paṭhetsusamāhitaḥ \|*  
*sa prāpnotyakhilānkāmānyathāhaṃ prāptavānpurā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person, who purifying himself during the morning and evening hours, recites these names attentively, all his efforts are made successful, as with me.

## \|\| 1.71.14-15 \|\|

*prasādāttasya devasya bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*śrīkāmaḥ śriyamāpnoti dharmārthī dharmamāpnuyāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āturo mucyate rogādbaddho mucyeta bandhanāt \|*  
*rājyārthī rājyamāpnoti kāmārthī kāmamāpnuyāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. As a result of the pleasure of the Sungod, a person desirous of dharma achieves dharma, the ailing person is relieved of the ailment, a person in bondage is freed, the person desirous of kingdom achieves the same, besides devotion to the religious deeds.

## \|\| 1.71.16 \|\|

*etajjapyaṃ rahasyaṃ ca saṃdhyopāsanameva ca \|*  
*etena japamātreṇa naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This is the secret Sandhya worship. This is suitable for japam. This is because with the recitation of the same, a person is relieved of all the sins.

## Chapter 72. Samba relieved of the curse of Durvasa

## \|\| 1.72.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ brahmavaco yogī śrutvā rājandivākaram \|*  
*vyomarūpaṃ samārādhya gataḥ sūryasalokatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O monarch, listening to the talk of Brahma, the yogins after adoring the Sungod, achieved the Salokya salvation.

## \|\| 1.72.2 \|\|

*tathā tvamapi rājendra pūjayitvā vibhāvasum \|*  
*gamiṣyasi paraṃ sthānaṃ devānāmapi durlabham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Therefore, O monarch, you also adore the Sungod, by which you will also achieve the place, which is beyond the reach of the gods.

## \|\| 1.72.3 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*ādyaṃ sthānaṃ raveḥ kutra jambūdvīpe mahāmune \|*  
*yatra pūjāṃ vidhānoktāṃ pratigṛhṇātyasau raviḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Shatanika said — O great sage, in this Jambu island, which is the place where the Sungod accepts the adoration appropriately?

## \|\| 1.72.4-5 \|\|

*candrabhāgātaṭe nāmnā puraṃ yatsāmbasaṃjñitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kālapriyaṃ3 tṛtīyaṃ tu triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*tathānyadapi te vacmi yatpurā brahmaṇoditam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Sumantu said — In this island, Mindravana, Mundira and Kalapriya are the three sites which are meant for the Sungod. Besides these places, there is another site which has been prescribed by Brahma, which I am going to tell you.

## \|\| 1.72.6 \|\|

*dvīpesmiñchāśvataṃ sthānaṃ yatra sūryasya nityatā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In this island, there is a place over the bank of the Chandrabhaga river known by the name of Samba, where the Sungod lives permanently. This is the permanent dwelling place of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.72.7-8 \|\|

*prītyā sāmbasya tatrarko janasyānugrahāya ca \|*  
*tatra dvādaśabhāgena mitro maitreṇa cakṣuṣā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*śastaḥ kasminnimitte'sau pitrā caivātmasambhavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Because of his attachment for Samba and I in order to grace the people of that place, the Sungod with his all the twelve parts, visualizes the world for its benefit, delightfully. The worship which is performed by people appropriately with devotion is also accepted by him there.

## \|\| 1.72.9 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*ko'yaṃ sāmbaḥ sutaḥ kasya kasya prīto divākara \|*  
*yasya cāyaṃ sahasrāṃśurvaradaḥ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ7 \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Shatanika said — Who is Samba? Who is his father? Who is he by whose auspicious deeds, Samba became favourite of the Sungod, and got the boon from the lord?

## \|\| 1.72.10 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*ya ete dvādaśādityā virājante mahābalāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ yo viṣṇusaṃjñastu sarvalokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Sumantu said — Out of the twelve valorous Suns, the Sungod named Vishnu is quite popular in the world.

## \|\| 1.72.11 \|\|

*ihāsau vāsudevatvamavāpa bhagavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*tasmātsāmbaḥ suto jajñe jāmbavatyāṃ mahābalaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He is also called Vasudeva. The son named Samba was born of Jambavati by him.

## \|\| 1.72.12 \|\|

*sa tu pitrā bhṛśaṃ śaptaḥ kuṣṭharogamavāptavān \|*  
*tenāyaṃ sthāpitaḥ sūryaḥ svānāmnā ca puraṃ kṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He attracted leprosy, because of a curse by father. Because of this, he built a city in which there was the shrine of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.72.13 \|\|

*nālpaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ vipra yenāsau śaptavānsutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Shatanika said — Why did the father cursed his son, who was born of him? O Brahmana, there does not appear to be as simple reason, by which the son was cursed by the father.

## \|\| 1.72.14-15 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājaṃstasya yacchāpakāraṇam \|*  
*durvāsā nāma bhagavānrudrasyāṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*aṭamānaḥ sa bhagavāṃstrīllokānpracacāra ha \|*  
*atha prāpto dvāravatīṃ madhusaṃjñocitāṃ purā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Sumantu said — O monarch, you attentively listen to the cause of the curse, which I am going to speak out. The sage named Durvasa was born of the amsha of Indra. Once he reached the city of Dvaravati which was earlier known by the name of Madhu.

## \|\| 1.72.16-17 \|\|

*tamāgatamṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā sāmbo rūpeṇa garvitaḥ \|*  
*piṅgākṣaṃ1 kṣudhitaṃ rūkṣaṃ virūpaṃ sukṛśaṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*anukārāspadaṃ cakre darśane gamane tathā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tasya mukhaṃ sāmbo vakra cakre tathātmanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. On the arrival of the Rishis, Samba getting pride of his beautiful body, initiated the lean and thin body of the Rishis which was quite ugly. The limbs of his body were shattered, while the hair ware disheveled, yellow and dry. Samba turned his face like the disfigured face of the sage. He also sported the caricature of the sage and walked erratically like him.

## \|\| 1.72.18-20 \|\|

*mukhaṃ kurukulaśreṣṭha garvito yauvanena tu \|*  
*atha kruddho mahātejā durvāsā ṛṣisattamaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sāmbaṃ covāca bhagavānvidhunvanmukhamātmanaḥ \|*  
*yasmādvirūpaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā svātmarūpeṇa garvitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*gamane darśane mahyamanukāraṃ samācaraḥ \|*  
*tasmāttu kuṣṭharogitvamacirāttvaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The performance of Samba enraged the sage, who shaking his head, pronounced a curse on Samba — “Getting arrogant of your body’s beauty and finding me disfigured, you are initiating my walking. Therefore, you will shortly attract the leprosy disease.”

## Chapter 73. Adoration of Surya by Samba

## \|\| 1.73.1-4 \|\|

*bruvāṇamevaṃ devaṃ tu nārado vākyamabravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvalokacaraḥ so'tha aṭamānaḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ sa vai draṣṭuṃ nityaṃ dvāravatīṃ purīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

*āyāti ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ krodhano munisattamaḥ \|*  
*athāgacchati tasmiṃstu sarve yadukumārakāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gatvā tu satvaraṃ sāmbaḥ praṇāmamakarotprabhoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Sumantu said — At the same time, the mental son of Narada also arrived at the spot, who enjoyed his glory in all the three worlds, while moving about. He visited the city of Dvaravati with other Rishis in order to have an audience with lord Vasudeva. At the arrival of Narada at that point of time, Pradyumna and other princes welcomed Narada as usual offering arghya and water for the washing of the feet.

## \|\| 1.73.5-7 \|\|

*sāmbastvavaśyabhāvitvāttasya śāpasya kāraṇam \|*  
*avajñāṃ kurūte nityaṃ nāradasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*rataḥ krīḍāsu vai nityaṃ rūpayauvanagarvitaḥ \|*  
*avinītaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa nāradaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*asyāhamavinītasya kariṣye vinayaṃ śubham \|*  
*evaṃ sañcintayityā tu vāsudevamathābravīt \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Samba on his part, always insulted Narada, since a curse from him was inevitable. Being proud of his strength and beauty, he always engaged himself in sports. Observing the adamant and discourteous behaviour of Samba, Narada thought — “I alone shall make this discourteous prince disciplined, by which he would be benefitted.” Thus thinking, he purposely said to lord Vasudeva.

## \|\| 1.73.8 \|\|

*imāḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasryaḥ striyo yādavasattama \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ hi sadā sāmbe bhāvo deva samāśritaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “O foremost of the Yadava race, your sixteen thousand wives love Samba.

## \|\| 1.73.9 \|\|

*rūpeṇāpratimaḥ sāmbo lokesminsacarācare \|*  
*sadā hīcchanti 1 tāstasya darśanaṃ cāpi hi striyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Because in this world of mobile and immobile living beings, there is none more beautiful than him. Therefore, these damsels also are always anxious to have an audience with him.”

## \|\| 1.73.10-12 \|\|

*śrutvaivaṃ nāradādvākyaṃ cintayāmāsa keśavaḥ \|*  
*yadetannāradenoktamanyadatra tu kiṃ bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vacanaṃ śrūyate loke cāpalyaṃ strīṣu vidyate \|*  
*ślokau cemau purā gītau cittajñairyoṣitāṃ dvijaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pauṃścalyāccalacittatvānnaiḥsnehyācca svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*rakṣitāḥ sarvato hyetā vikurvanti hi bhartṛṣu \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Listening to the words of Narada, Shri Krishna thought in his mind — “The words of Narada cannot be otherwise.” It is heard in the world that the damsels are unsteady. The intelligent Brahmanas, who are well aware of the minds of ladies, feel that they are by nature unchaste, devoid of love and even when they are well guarded, they remain dissatisfied with their husbands.

## \|\| 1.73.13 \|\|

*naitā rūpaṃ parīkṣante nāsāṃ vayasi niścayaḥ \|*  
*surūpaṃ vā virūpaṃ vā pumānityeva bhuñjate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For this purpose, they become unmindful of the appearance, age, beauty or ugliness, because they are only interested in the body of a man.”

## \|\| 1.73.14 \|\|

*manasā cintayanneva kṛṣṇo nāradamabravīt \|*  
*na hyahaṃ śraddadhāmyetadyadetadbhāṣitaṃ tvayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sumantu said — Thus thinking in his mind, Shri Krishna said to Narada — “Whatever has been spoken by you, I am unable to believe in the same at once.”

## \|\| 1.73.15 \|\|

*tathāhaṃ tatkariṣyāmi yathā śraddhāsyate bhavān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Narada said — “For that purpose, I shall manage in such a way that you are able to find truth in my words.”

## \|\| 1.73.16 \|\|

*evamuktvā yayau svargaṃ nāradastu yathāgataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ katipayāhobhirdvārakāṃ punarabhyagāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus speaking, Narada returned to the heaven by the same route by which he had arrived.

## \|\| 1.73.17 \|\|

*tasminnahani devo'pi sahāntaḥpurikairjanaiḥ \|*  
*anubhūya jalakrīḍāṃ pānamāsevate rahaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On the same day, lord Krishna, after enjoying the water sport with his wives in the inner apartments, was chewing the betel.

## \|\| 1.73.18-19 \|\|

*3 ramyaraivatakodyāne nānādrumavibhūṣite \|*  
*sarvartukusumairnityaṃ vāsite sarvakānane \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nānājalajaphullābhirdīrghikābhiralaṅkṛte \|*  
*haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭe cakravākopaśobhite \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. In the charming orchard of the Raivataka mountain, having various types of trees and filled with the fragrance of flowers of all the season. Various types of lotus flowers were blossoming there. The step-wells were filled with flowers and birds like cranes, sheldrake and other birds (were also present there).

## \|\| 1.73.20-21 \|\|

*tasminsa ramate devaḥ strībhiḥ parivṛtastadā \|*  
*hāranūpurakeyūraraśanādyairvibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*bhūṣitānāṃ varastrīṇāṃ cārvaṅgīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tābhiḥ sampīyate pānaṃ śubhagandhānvitaṃ śubham \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Shri Krishna always had his sport with the damsels. The damsels adorned with garlands anklets, armlets, waistbands and other ornaments and clad in beautiful garments, enjoyed the intoxicating and fragrant beverages.

## \|\| 1.73.22-24 \|\|

*etasminnantare buddhvā madyapānāttataḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*uvāca nāradaḥ sāmbaṃ sāmbottiṣṭha kumāraka \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tvāṃ samāhvāyate devo na yuktaṃ sthātumatra te \|*  
*tadvākyārthamabuddhaiva nāradenātha coditaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sāṣṭāṅgaṃ ca hareḥ sāmbo vidhivadvallabhasya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. When the ladies were overpowered with the consuming of excessive beverages, then Narada went to Samba and said to him — “O prince Samba, move quickly, Shri Krishna wants to meet you. Therefore, it would not be proper for you to remain here.” Without giving much thought to the words of Narada, and under his influence, he rapidly went to the place of his father and prostrated before him.

## \|\| 1.73.25 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra yāstu vai svalpasāttvikāḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sundaraṃ sāmbaṃ sarvāścukṣubhire striyaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Suddenly, the damsels having little of Sattva-guna and had never seen Samba earlier, at the sight of most beautiful Samba, developed blemish in their hearts.

## \|\| 1.73.26-28 \|\|

*na sa dṛṣṭaḥ purā yābhirantaḥpuranivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*madyadoṣāttatastāsāṃ smṛtilopāttathā nṛpa \|\| 26 \|\|*

*svabhāvatolpasattvānāṃ jaghanāni visusruvuḥ \|*  
*śrūyate cāpyayaṃ ślokaḥ purāṇaprathitaḥ kṣitau \|\| 27 \|\|*

*brahmacarye'pi vartantyāḥ sādhvyā hyapi ca śrūyate \|*  
*hṛdyaṃ hi puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā yoniḥ saṃklidyate striyāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. O monarch, under the influence of the intoxicants consumed by them, they lost their memory and due to the shortage of Sattva — guna in them, their thighs became wet. It is well-known in the Puranas that even the chaste women, at the sight of a beautiful person, becoming desirous of a union, emit discharge (making their legs wet).

## \|\| 1.73.29-30 \|\|

*loke'pi dṛśyate hyetanmadyasyātyarthasevanāt \|*  
*lajjāṃ muñcanti niḥśaṅkā hrīmatyo hyapi hi striyaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*samāṃsairbhojanaiḥ snigdhaiḥ yānaiḥ sīdhusurāsavaiḥ \|*  
*gandhairmanojñairvastraiśca2 kāmaḥ strīṣu vijṛmbhate \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. It has been observed in the world that because of the excessive drinking, even the sky damsels, discarding their shyness, become bold because of the eating of meat, consuming of\* excellent beverages and wearing of the fragrant and excellent clothes. There is a rise of passion in the women.

## \|\| 1.73.31 \|\|

*3 sīdhuprayuktaṃ śukreṇa satataṃ sādhu hīcchatā \|*  
*madyaṃ . na peyamatyartha puruṣeṇa vipaścitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. It has been ordained for the welfare of the people by Shukracharya that the learned people should not indulge in excessive drinking.

## \|\| 1.73.32 \|\|

*nāradopyatha taṃ sāmbaṃ preṣayitvā tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*ājagāmātha tatraiva sāmbasyānupadena tu \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By sending Samba there, Narada also rapidly followed.

## \|\| 1.73.33 \|\|

*āyāntaṃ tāśca taṃ dṛṣṭvā priyaṃ saumanasamṛṣim \|*  
*sahasaivotthitāḥ sarvāḥ striyastaṃ madavihvalāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. At the arrival of the excellent sage Narada there, the damsels who had been overpowered with drinking, suddenly got up.

## \|\| 1.73.34-37 \|\|

*tāsāmathotthitānāṃ tu vāsudevasya paśyataḥ \|*  
*bhittvā vāsāṃsi śubhrāṇi patreṣu patitāni tu \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tā dṛṣṭvā tu hariḥ kruddhaḥ sarvāstā śaptavānstriyaḥ \|*  
*yasmādgatāni cetāṃsi māṃ muktvānyatra ca striyaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*4 tasmātpatikṛtāṃllokānāyuṣoṃnte na yāsyatha \|*  
*patilokaparibhraṣṭāḥ svargamārgāttathaiva ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhūtvā cāśaraṇā yūyaṃ dasyuhastaṃ gamiṣyatha \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-37. At the time of standing, their semen fluid dropped down on the leaves. Observing that, Shri Krishna pronounced a curse on them — “Since your minds got attracted towards someone else leaving me, therefore the abode of your husband and the path of the heaven shall be achieved by you at the end. Then falling from the husbands’ abode and heaven, getting orphaned, you will have to live with the thieves.”

## \|\| 1.73.38 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śāpadoṣāttatastasmāttāḥ striyaḥ svargate harau \|*  
*hṛtāḥ pāñjanadaiścaurairarjunasya tu paśyataḥ \|*  
*alpasattvāstu yāstvāsangatāstā dūṣaṇaṃ striyaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Sumantu said — After the departure of Shri Krishna to heaven, because of the curse of Shri Krishna, the ladies, in full view of Arjuna, were abducted by the thieves in the land of five rivers. They had to face this blemish, because of their being short of Sattva.

## \|\| 1.73.39 \|\|

*rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca tathā jāmbavatī priyā \|*  
*naitā gatā dasyuhastaṃ svena sattvena rakṣitāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Rukmini, Satyabhama and the beloved Jambavati besides other women, who were protracted by their Sattvaguna, could not fall to the bondages of the thieves.

## \|\| 1.73.40-42 \|\|

*śaptvaiva tāḥ striyaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sāmbamapyaśapattataḥ \|*  
*yasmādatīva te kāntaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā imāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kṣubdhāḥ sarvā yatastasmātkuṣṭharogamavāpnuhi \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sāmbaḥ kṛṣṇasya bhārata \|\| 41 \|\|*

*uvāca prahasanrājansaṃsmarannṛṣibhāṣitam \|*  
*animittamahaṃ tāta bhāvadoṣavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*śapto na me'tra vai kruddho durvāsā anyathā vadet \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Thus pronouncing curse on the ladies, Shri Krishna also pronounced a curse on Samba — “Your excessive beauty aroused passion in the ladies, therefore, getting deprived of your beauty you would suffer from the disease of leprosy.” O Bharata, thus listening to the words of Shri Krishna, Samba was reminded of the words of the Rishis and spoke smilingly — “O excellent one, I had no evil thoughts about them. Therefore, I earned this curse without any cause. But you have done well, because the words spoken by Durvasa could never be proved otherwise.”

## \|\| 1.73.43-44 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*asmicchapte'nimitte'sau pitrā jāmbavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*prāptavānkuṣṭharogitvaṃ virūpatvaṃ ca bhārata \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sāmbena punarapyeva durvāsāḥ kopito muniḥ \|*  
*tacchāpānmusalaṃ jātaṃ kulaṃ yenāsya ghātitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Sumantu said — Samba — the son of Jambavati, thus having been cursed by the father without any reason, attracted the disease of leprosy as well as ugliness. Similarly, once again, Samba by misbehaving with the sage Durvasa, without any reason, attracted ugliness as well as leprosy. Because of that curse, a musala was born out of his body, which became the source of destruction of the entire race of Yadus.

## \|\| 1.73.45 \|\|

*śrutvā hyavinayāddoṣānsāmbenāptānkṣamādhipa \|*  
*nityaṃ bhāvyaṃ vinītena gurudevadvijātiṣu \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O lord, O resplendent one! Thus, because of the fault of indiscipline, observing the condition of Samba, one should display humility before the preceptor and the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.73.46 \|\|

*priyaṃ ca vākyaṃ vaktavyaṃ sarvaprītikaraṃ vibho \|*  
*kiṃ tvayā na śrutau ślokau yāvuktau vedhasā purā \|*  
*1 śṛṇvato devadevasya vyomakeśasya bhārata \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. One should be loveable to all and speak sweet voice. Have you not heard the words spoken by lord Shiva to Brahma?

## \|\| 1.73.47 \|\|

*yo dharmaśīlo jitamānaroṣo vidyāvinīto na paropatāpī \|*  
*svadāratuṣṭaḥ paradāravarjito na tasya loke bhayamasti kiñcit \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A person who follows dharma has no arrogance or anger, is humble, causes no pain to others, and the one who remains satisfied with his own wife and is unattracted with other women, can never be afraid of anyone else.

## \|\| 1.73.48 \|\|

*na tathā śītalasalilaṃ na candanaraso na śītalā chāyā \|*  
*prahlādayati ca puruṣaṃ yathā madhurabhāṣiṇī vāṇī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Because the sweet words could please a person much more than the cold water, sandal paste or cool shade.

## \|\| 1.73.49 \|\|

*tataḥ śāpābhibhūtena samyagārādhya bhāskaram \|*  
*sāmbenāptaṃ tathārogyaṃ rūpaṃ1 ca paramaṃ punaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thereafter, feeling painful due to the curse, Samba appropriately adored the Sungod and regained his beauty, besides getting relieved of his disease of leprosy.

## \|\| 1.73.50 \|\|

*rūpamāpya tathā'rogyaṃ bhāskarāddharisūnunā \|*  
*niveśito ravirbhaktyā svanāmnā kṣmādhipeśvara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O lord of forgiveness, Samba — the son of Shri Krishna, regained his beauty besides being relieved of his disease. Because of his devotion towards the Sungod, he established the Sungod there.

## Chapter 74. Twelve images of the San

## \|\| 1.74.1 \|\|

*lalāṭātkuruśārdūla nīrajākṣaṃ digambaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — Samba established the image of the Sungod over the bank of Chandrabhaga river. This is what you have stated. How could it be the original place of the Sungod?

## \|\| 1.74.2 \|\|

*caturthī tasya yā mūrtirnāmnā pūṣeti viśrutā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O Bharata, this is the original place of the Sungod. It was developed by Samba only. You listen.

## \|\| 1.74.3 \|\|

*atrādyo lokanātho'sau raśmimālī jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*mitratve ca sthito devastapastepe purā nṛpa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O monarch, in earlier times, the Sungod — the lord of the world, adorned with the garland of the sun rays, had performed tapas for the welfare of the world.

## \|\| 1.74.4 \|\|

*anādinidhano brahmā nityaścākṣaya eva ca \|*  
*sṛṣṭvā prajāpatīnbrahmā sṛṣṭvā ca vividhāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Sungod is eternal, is without birth and death, indestructible besides being the form of Brahman. He created Prajapatis as well as the various types of living beings.

## \|\| 1.74.5-6 \|\|

*sasarja mukhato devaṃ pūrvamambujasannibham \|*  
*kañjajastaṃ tato devaṃ vakṣasto nirmame nṛpa \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ṛbhavaḥ pādataḥ sarve sṛṣṭāstena mahātmanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. First of all, Vishnu emerged out of his lotus like mouth, then Brahma emerged out of his chest, while Shiva was produced out of his forehead. The same great soul produced the other gods from his feet.

## \|\| 1.74.7 \|\|

*tataḥ śatasahasrāṃśuravyaktaḥ puruṣaḥ svayam \|*  
*kṛtvā dvādaśadhātmānamadityāmudapadyata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, the invisible Purusha with a thousand rays, divided himself into twelve forms and produced from them Aditya.

## \|\| 1.74.8-10 \|\|

*indro dhātā ca parjanyaḥ pūṣā tvaṣṭāryamā bhagaḥ \|*  
*vivasvānaṃśurviṣṇuśca varuṇo mitra eva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ebhirdvādaśabhistena ādityena mahātmanā \|*  
*kṛtsnaṃ jagadidaṃ vyāptaṃ mūrtibhistu narādhipa \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasya yā prathamā mūrtirādityasyendrasaṃjñitā \|*  
*sthitā sā devarājatve dānavāsuranāśinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Those forms were — Dhata, Indra, Parjanya, Pusha, Tvashta, Aryama, Bhaga, Vivasvan, Amshu, Vishnu, Aruna and Mitra. He pervaded in the universe in these twelve forms and controlled the universe through them. O king, his first image known as Indra is meant for the destruction of Danavas and Asuras and attained the position of Indra.

## \|\| 1.74.11 \|\|

*dvitīyā cāsya yā mūrtirnāmnā dhāteti kīrtitā \|*  
*sthitā prajāpatitve sā vidhātrī sṛjate prajāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The second image is known as Vidhata in which he takes to the form of a Prajapati and creates the people.

## \|\| 1.74.12 \|\|

*tṛtīyā tasya yā mūrtiḥ parjanya iti viśrutā \|*  
*kareṣveva sthitā sā tu varṣatyamṛtameva hi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The third image is of Parjanya which merging in the sun rays, pours the nectar on earth.

## \|\| 1.74.13 \|\|

*mantreṣvavasthitā sā tu prajāḥ puṣṇāti bhārata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The fourth image is that of Pusha. The same getting enshrined in the mantras, preserves the populace.

## \|\| 1.74.14 \|\|

*mūrtiryā pañcamī tasya nāmnā tvaṣṭeti viśrutā \|*  
*vanaspatiṣu sā nityamoṣadhīṣu ca vai sthitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The fifth image is that of Tvasta, which pervades in the Aushadhis and Vanaspatis (greenery).

## \|\| 1.74.15 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhī mūrtistu yā tasya aryameti ca viśrutā \|*  
*prajāsamvaraṇārthaṃ sā pureṣveva sthitā sadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The sixth image is that of Aryama, who pervades in the cities for the protection of the people.

## \|\| 1.74.16 \|\|

*bhānoryā saptamī mūrtirnāmnā bhaga iti smṛtā \|*  
*bhūmau vyavasthitā sā tu kṣmādhareṣu ca bhārata \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Bhaga is the seventh figure of Surya, carving a space on earth, and carries the same.

## \|\| 1.74.17 \|\|

*aṣṭamī cāsya yā mūrtirvivasvāniti saṃjñitā \|*  
*agnau vyavasthitā sā tu 4 pacate'nnaṃ śarīriṇām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Bharata, Vivasvan is the eight figure of the Sungod, which gets enshrined in the fire and carries food through the fire of the stomach in all the living beings.

## \|\| 1.74.18 \|\|

*navamī citrabhānoryā mūrtirañśuriti smṛtā \|*  
*vīra candre sthitā sā tu āpyāyayati vai jagat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The ninth figure of Chandrabhanu is known as Amshu and getting enshrined in the moon, it is responsible for the growth of the world.

## \|\| 1.74.19 \|\|

*mūrtiryā daśamī tasya viṣṇurityabhidhīyate \|*  
*prādurbhavati sā nityaṃ gīrvāṇārivināśinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The tenth figure of the Sungod is the form of Vishnu, who incarnated on earth for the destruction of the enemies of the gods.

## \|\| 1.74.20 \|\|

*mūrtistvekādaśī yā tu bhānorvaruṇasaṃjñitā \|*  
*jīvāyayati sā kṛtsnaṃ jagaddhi samupāśritā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The eleventh figure of Bhanu, known by the name of Varuna, infuses life in the living beings in the form of water. Therefore, the entire world is dependent on the same.

## \|\| 1.74.21 \|\|

*apāṃ sthānaṃ samudrastu varuṇo'tra pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*tasmādvai procyate vīra sāgaro varuṇālayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O great warrior, ocean is the place for the water, because of which the ocean is known as the abode of water.

## \|\| 1.74.22 \|\|

*mūrtiryā dvādaśī bhānornāmato mitrasaṃjñitā \|*  
*lokānāṃ sā hitārthaṃ tu sthitā candrasarittaṭe \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The twelfth figure of the Sungod is known as Mitra which is lodged over the bank of the river Chandrabhaga.

## \|\| 1.74.23 \|\|

*vāyubhakṣā tapastepe yuktā maitreṇa cakṣuṣā \|*  
*anugṛhṇansadā bhaktānvarairnānāvidhaiḥ sadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Having been lodged in a friendly manner, bestowing various types of boons to his devotees, he had performed tapas inhaling the air only.

## \|\| 1.74.24 \|\|

*evamādyamidaṃ sthānaṃ puṇyaṃ mitrapadaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tatra mitraḥ sthito yasmāttasmānmitrapadaṃ smṛtam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Because of this it is known as the first auspicious place of Mitra. Because of his stay there in a friendly manner, he is considered as friendly always.

## \|\| 1.74.25 \|\|

*tayārādhya mahābāho sāmbenāmitatejasā \|*  
*tatprasādāttadādeśātpratiṣṭhā tasya vai kṛtā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O long armed one, thus Samba worshipped the Sungod who was pleased and at his instance, his image was installed there.

## \|\| 1.74.26-29 \|\|

*ābhirdvādaśabhistena bhāskareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*kṛtsnaṃ jagadidaṃ vyāptaṃ mūrtibhistu narādhipa \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmādvandyo namasyaśca dvādaśasvapi mūrtiṣu \|*  
*ye namasyanti cādityaṃ narā bhaktisamanvitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*te yāsyanti paraṃ sthāna 1 tiṣṭhedyatrāmbujeśvaraḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ dvādaśātmānamādityaṃ pūjayettu yaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sa muktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo yāti helisalokatām \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. In this way, the Sungod with his twelve figures, pervading in the entire universe, gets established. O foremost of the humans, the Sungod having been enshrined in his twelve figures is always adorable and respectable. A person who offers his salutation to the Sungod with devotion, he gains access to the place of the Sungod. A person who worships the Sungod with twelve forms, he, getting relieved of all the sins, ultimately achieves the abode of the Sungod.

## Chapter 75. Narada’s advice to Samba

## \|\| 1.75.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ sāmbaḥ prapanno'rkaṃ kena vā pratipāditaḥ \|*  
*ugraṃ śāpaṃ ca taṃ prāpya pitaraṃ sa kimuktavān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — How did Samba achieve the Sungod? Who advised him for the same? What did he do after receiving the terrific curse from his father?

## \|\| 1.75.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*uktameva purā vīra yathā śaptaḥ sa yādavaḥ \|*  
*pitrā sāmbo mahārāja hariṇāmbujadhāriṇā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O excellent warrior, I have already narrated to you as to how the curse was pronounced over Samba.

## \|\| 1.75.3 \|\|

*asyāyaṃ jagato nātho dvādaśātmā divākaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Feeling painful after receiving the curse from Shri Krishna, Samba humbly said to his father with folded hands.

## \|\| 1.75.4-6 \|\|

*kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ deva yena śaptosmyahaṃ tvayā \|*  
*ahaṃ tvadājñayā deva tvaramāṇotra āgataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kasmānnipātitaḥ śāpo mayi te'napakāriṇi \|*  
*na vai jānāmyahaṃ kiñcitprasīda jagataḥ pate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śāpaṃ niyaccha me deva prasādaṃ kuru me prabho \|*  
*kaśmalenābhibhūto'haṃ yena mucyeya kilbiṣāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. “O lord, what wrong I had done to receive the curse from you? I had arrived here at your express command. When I had done no wrong, then why was I cursed like that? O lord of the universe, I am unaware of anything in this regard. Getting pleased with me, kindly get the curse removed from me. O lord, I feel painful of this sin. You kindly save me from this misery, to enable me to become free from the sin.”

## \|\| 1.75.7 \|\|

*tamuvāca tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sāmbaṃ buddhvā hyanāgasam \|*  
*nāhaṃ putra punaḥ śakto rogasyāsya vyapohane \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the words so spoken by Samba and finding him innocent, Shri Krishna said — “O son, I have no competence to escape you of this ailment.

## \|\| 1.75.8 \|\|

*sahasraraśmirādityaḥ śaktaḥ putra vyapohitum \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Sungod — the lord of the universe, having twelve souls, also known as Divakara, alone can remove this ailment.

## \|\| 1.75.9 \|\|

*jñātaṃ mayādhunā caiva yathā tvaṃ nāradena tu \|*  
*roṣādvisarjitaḥ putra matsakāśaṃ mahātmanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I am realizing presently that it was Narada, who getting annoyed, had sent you to me.

## \|\| 1.75.10 \|\|

*tasmāttameva pṛccha tvaṃ prasādya ṛṣisattamam \|*  
*ākhyāsyati sa te devaṃ śāpaṃ yaste'paneṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, you go to the excellent sage Narada and ask him about the remedy. He will surely speak about the god who would be able to get you relieved of the ailment.

## \|\| 1.75.11-13 \|\|

*athaitatsa piturvākyaṃ śrutvā jāmbavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*dīnaḥ 1 śokaparītātmā tataḥ sañcintya bhārata \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvāravatyāṃ sthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ kadāciddraṣṭumāgatam \|*  
*vinayādupasaṅgamya sāmbaḥ papraccha nāradam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhagavanvedhasaḥ putra sarvalokajña suvrata \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru me vipra praṇatasya mahāmate \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Thus listening to the words of his father, pitiable and grieved Samba — the son of Jambavati, prayed to Narada who had arrived in Dvarika in order to meet Shri Krishna — “O lord, O son of Brahma, I offer my salutation to you. Be merciful on me.

## \|\| 1.75.14 \|\|

*ye me nīrujaṃ kāyaṃ kaśmalaṃ ca praṇaśyati \|*  
*taṃ yogaṃ ihi me vipra praṇatasyāsya suvrata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Brahman, you kindly tell me the way out by which my body could be freed from terrific ailment. I offer my salutation to you again.”

## \|\| 1.75.15 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*yaḥ stutyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ namasyaḥ pūjya eva ca \|*  
*pūjayitvāśu taṃ devaṃ tato vyādhiṃ prahāsyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Narada said — The Sungod, who is adorable by all the gods, besides being worshipped, you should also worship him. He alone can remove your ailment.

## \|\| 1.75.16 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*kaḥ stutyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ namasyaḥ pūjya eva ca \|*  
*kaḥ sarvagaśca sarvatra śaraṇaṃ yaṃ vajrāmyaham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Samba said — He is prayed by all the gods, being adorable. He is all pervading. I would like to take refuge with him.

## \|\| 1.75.17 \|\|

*pitṛśāpānalenāhaṃ dahyamāno mahāmune \|*  
*śāntyarthamasya kaṃ devaṃ śaraṇaṃ ca vrajāmyaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O great sage, I am burning with the fire of the curse of my father. With which deity should I take refuge?

## \|\| 1.75.18 \|\|

*etacchrutvā tu sāmbasya vacanaṃ karuṇāvaham \|*  
*hitvā tu 4 kāmajaṃ vīra nārado vākyamabravīt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Listening to the pathetic words of Samba, the anger of Narada was subsided and he said.

## \|\| 1.75.19 \|\|

*stutyo vandyaśca pūjyaśca namasya īḍya eva ca \|*  
*bhāskaro yaduśārdūla brahmādīnāṃ sadānagha \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O lion of the Yadu race, only Bhaskara is the deity adorable even by Brahma and other gods. He is respectable, praiseworthy, besides being worthy of salutation.

## Chapter 76. Talk between Narada and Samba

## \|\| 1.76.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kadācitparyaṭaṃllokānsūryalokamahaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tatra dṛṣṭo mayā sūryaḥ sarvadevagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — Once while wandering, I reached Suryaloka, where I found that all the gods were seated, surrounding the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.76.2-3 \|\|

*gandharvairapsarobhiśca nāgairyakṣaiśca rākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*tatra gāyanti gandharvā nṛtyantyapsarasastathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rakṣantyudgataśastrāstaṃ yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni mūrtimantīha sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*tatkṛtairvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ stuvanti ṛṣayo ravim \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Besides all the Gandharvas, Apsaras, Nagas, Yakshas and Rakshasas were also seen present there. The Gandharvas were singing, while the Apsaras were dancing. The armed Yakshas, Rakshasas and the serpents were guarding the Sungod. The Rigveda, Samaveda and Yajurveda, reciting the Vedic reds, were offering prayer, appearing in human forms, besides the Rishis.

## \|\| 1.76.4 \|\|

*mūrtimatyaḥ sthitāstatra tisraḥ saṃdhyāḥ śubhānanāḥ \|*  
*gṛhītavajranārācāḥ parivārya raviṃ sthitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Similarly, the Sandhyas armed with vajra and arrows, were guarding the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.76.5 \|\|

*aruṇā varṇataḥ pūrvā madhyamā cendusannibhā \|*  
*tṛtīyākṣmājasaṃkāśā 1 saṃdhyā caiva prakīrtitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Out of them the first was of red colour, the second resembled the moon and the third resembled the lotus flower.

## \|\| 1.76.6 \|\|

*ādityā vasavo rudrā marutothāśvinau tathā \|*  
*trisaṃdhyaṃ pūjayantyarkaṃ tathānye ca divaukasaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Similarly, the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Maruts, Ashvinikumaras and other gods together with the three Sandhyas, were adoring the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.76.7 \|\|

*īrayañjayaśabdaṃ tu indrastatraiva tiṣṭhati \|*  
*kavistu tryambako devastrisaṃdhyaṃ pūjayanti vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Indra and other gods shouted the slogans of victory. Shukra and Shiva also, together with the three Sandhyas, worship him.

## \|\| 1.76.8 \|\|

*2 dinādāvambujākāraṃ pūjayedambujāsanam \|*  
*cakrarūpaṃ tu madhyāhne ghṛtārciḥ pūjayetsadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Therefore, the Sungod, seated over the lotus seat, has the form of a lotus in the morning, while has the form of cakra at noon and the one who appeared like the fire flame in which the ghi is poured, should be worshipped always.

## \|\| 1.76.9 \|\|

*pūjayetsagaṇaṃ rātrau vipulājyasvarūpiṇam \|*  
*raviṃ bhaktyā sadā devaṃ 3 kaṃjārdhakṛtaśekharaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Because, the Sungod is adored even in the night (like the fire in which enough) of ghi is poured, together with his attendants. Because of this Shiva — Chandrashekhara, always worships him.

## \|\| 1.76.10 \|\|

*sārathyaṃ kurute tasya patagasyāgrajaḥ 1 sadā \|*  
*vahamāno rathaṃ divyaṃ kālāvayavanirmitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Aruna, the elder brother of Garuda, happens to be the charioteer of his chariot, which is made of divine parts.

## \|\| 1.76.11 \|\|

*haritaiḥ saptabhiryuktaṃ chandobhirvājirūpibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Six metres in the form of green steed are yoked in his chariot.

## \|\| 1.76.12 \|\|

*dve bhārye pārśvayostasya rājñīnikṣubhasaṃjñitā \|*  
*tathānyairnāmabhirdevāḥ parivārya raviṃ sthitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The sky in the form of a queen and a woman named Nikshubha stood behind the Sungod. Several gods surrounded him from all the sides. They were all seated.

## \|\| 1.76.13-14 \|\|

*piṅgalo lekhakastatra tathānyo daṇḍanāyakaḥ \|*  
*2 rājāśroṣau ca dvau dvāre sthitau kalmāṣapakṣiṇau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato vyoma catuḥśṛṅgaṃ meroḥ sadṛśalakṣaṇam \|*  
*diṇḍistathāgratastasya dikṣu cānye sthitāḥ surāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The writer named Pingala, Dandanayaka, the kings of various complexions, two birds and two gatekeepers which looked graceful like the four peaks of the Meru mountain, opposite to them stood their Dindi and the deities of the four quarters.

## \|\| 1.76.15 \|\|

*evaṃ sarvagamaṃ devaṃ pradīptaṃ jagati dvija \|*  
*brahmādyaiḥ saṃstutaṃ devaṃ gīrvāṇairṛṣabhottamam \|*  
*graheśaṃ bhuvaneśānamādityaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O Brahmana, thus the resplendent Sungod, who pervades in the entire universe, being prayed by Brahma and other gods, who is the best of gods and lord of all the Bhuvanas, you should take refuge with him, going to him.

## \|\| 1.76.16 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*tattvataḥ śrotumicchāmi kathaṃ sarvagato raviḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Samba said — would like to clearly know, as to how does the Sungod reaches everyplace?

## \|\| 1.76.17-19 \|\|

*kati vā raśmayastasya mūrtayaśca kati smṛtāḥ \|*  
*kā rājñī nikṣubhā kā ca kaścāyaṃ daṇḍanāyakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*piṅgalaścāpi kastatra kiṃ cāsau likhate sadā \|*  
*rājāśroṣau ca kau tatra kau ca kalmāṣapakṣiṇau \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kiṃ daivatyaṃ ca tadvyoma meroḥ sadṛśalakṣaṇam \|*  
*ko diṇḍiragratastatra ke devā dikṣu ye sthitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. How many rays has be? What is the number of his images, who are these ladies known by the names of Nikshubha and others? Who are Dandanayaka and Pingala and what do they write? Who is the king and Shrausha and the birds with various colours serving as gatekeepers? How is the sky of the place as vast as the Meru mountain, where are Dindi and the gods of directions lodged?

## \|\| 1.76.20 \|\|

*tattvato nigamaiścaiva vistareṇa vadasva māma \|*  
*yenāhaṃ tattvato jñātvā vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ dvija \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You please explain the situation to me as per the Vedic methodology in considerable details, as a result of which, I could be able to take refuge with the Sungod, well understanding the entire situation.

## Chapter 77. Description of the Sungod by Narada

## \|\| 1.77.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vistareṇānupūrvyā ca sūryaṃ nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*tataḥ śeṣānpravakṣye'haṃ namaskṛtya vivasvate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — I am now going to describe the Sungod exhaustively. You please listen. Thereafter, offering salutation to the Sungod, I shall also reveal his special features to you.

## \|\| 1.77.2 \|\|

*avyaktaṃ kāraṇaṃ yattannityaṃ sadasadātmakam \|*  
*pradhānaṃ prakṛtiśceti yamāhustattvacintakāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The sun’s invisible cause, which is conceived by the persons well-versed in the tattvas as eternal and Sad-sadatmaka Pradhana Prakriti.

## \|\| 1.77.3-5 \|\|

*gandhairvarṇai rasairhīnaṃ śabdasparśavivarjitam \|*  
*jagadyoniṃ mahadbhūtaṃ paraṃ brahmā sanātanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nigrahaṃ sarvabhūtānāmavyaktamabhavatkila \|*  
*anādyantamajaṃ sūkṣmaṃ triguṇaṃ prabhavāpyayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*anākāramavijñeyaṃ tamāhuḥ puruṣaṃ param \|*  
*tasyātmanā sarvamidaṃ jagadvyāptaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. He is free from fragrance, complexion, juice or essence, sound and touch. He is the source of origin of the universe, besides being supreme, eternal Brahman. He is the one who controls all the living beings, unmanifested, eternal, endless, unborn, having subtle form and three gunas, the creator as well as the destroyer, formless, not distinguishable besides being the supreme Purusha. The same great soul is pervading in the universe.

## \|\| 1.77.6 \|\|

*tasyeśvarasya pratimā jñānavairāgyalakṣaṇā \|*  
*dharmeśvaryakṛtā buddhirbrāhmī tasyābhimāninaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. His image represents knowledge of different sorts and the arrogant one has the Brahmi-intelligence born out of religious fortunes.

## \|\| 1.77.7 \|\|

*avyaktājjāyate tasya manasā yadyadicchati \|*  
*caturmukhasya brahmatve kālatve cāntakṛdbhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Out of the unmanifested one, the mentally desired things continue to emerge. He is four faced Brahma and the form of time, also known as Shiva.

## \|\| 1.77.8-10 \|\|

*sahasramūrdhā puruṣastisrovasthāḥ svayambhuvaḥ \|*  
*sattvaṃ rajaśca brahmatve kālatve ca rajastamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sāttvikaṃ puruṣatve ca guṇavṛttaṃ svayaṃbhuvaḥ \|*  
*brahmatve sṛjate lokānkālatve cāpi saṃkṣipet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*puruṣatve udāsīnastisro'vasthāḥ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*tridhā vibhajya cātmānaṃ trikālaṃ sampravartate \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. He is also the self-born Purusha with a thousand heads. He possesses the three gunas viz. y Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Out of these, Sattvika-Rajas represents Brahma, Rajas-Tamas Shiva, while lord Vishnu has the Sattvika position alone. This is the evaluation of his virtues. He creates the universe in the form of Brahma and squeezes it as Shiva. In the form of Purusha, he remains indifferent. In this way, the three situations of Prajapati are described. He is the one, who dividing himself in three forms, turns them into three ages or times.

## \|\| 1.77.11 \|\|

*sṛjate grasate caiva vīkṣate ca tribhiḥ svayam \|*  
*agre hiraṇyagarbhastu prādurbhūtaḥ svayambhuvaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus the task of creation, preserving and destruction are performed by him himself. He alone, initially emerged in the form of Hiranyagarbha.

## \|\| 1.77.12-14 \|\|

*ādityasyādidevatvādajātatvādajaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*deveṣu sa mahāndevo mahādevaḥ smṛtastataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarveśatvācca lokasya adhīśatvācca īśvaraḥ \|*  
*bṛhattvācca smṛto brahmā bhavatvādbhava ucyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pāti yasmātprajāḥ sarvāḥ prajāpatirataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pure śete ca vai yasmāttasmātpuruṣa ucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. He happens to be the foremost of all the gods, besides being unborn. Similarly, because of his being supreme of all the gods, he is also known as Mahadeva. Being the lord of all the lokas, he is known as Brahma. Because of his being of gigantic form, he is known as Brahma. Because of his appearing in the universe, he is known as Bhava; because of his maintaining the living beings, he is known as Prajapati and because of his dwelling in a Pura, he is known as Purusha.

## \|\| 1.77.15-16 \|\|

*notpādyatvādapūrvatvātsvayaṃbhūriti viśrutaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*hiraṇyāṇḍagato yasmādgraheśo vai divaspatiḥ \|*  
*tasmāddhiraṇyagarbho'sau devadevo divākaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Being unborn and unique, he is known as Svayambhu and Hiranyagarbha. Because of his stay in the golden egg, he is known as Grahesha, Divaspati, Divakara and Hiranyagarbha.

## \|\| 1.77.17 \|\|

*āpo nārā iti proktā ṛṣibhistattvadarśibhiḥ \|*  
*ayanaṃ tasya tā āpastena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Rishis well-versed in the tattvas, have interpreted Nara as water and since the same water serves as his abode, he is also called by the name of Narayana.

## \|\| 1.77.18 \|\|

*ara ityeṣa śīghrārtho nipātaḥ kavibhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*āpa evārṇavā bhūtvā na śīghrāstena tā narāḥ 1 \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Similarly, the poets expand the meaning of the word ‘Ara’. Therefore, the water takes the form of the ocean, which limits its movement within the shores.

## \|\| 1.77.19-20 \|\|

*ekārṇave purā tasminnaṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*nārāyaṇākhyaḥ puruṣaḥ suṣvāpa salile tadā \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣā 3 sumanāḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sahasrabāhuḥ prathamaḥ prajāpatistrayīpathe yaḥ puruṣo4 nigadyate \|*  
*ādityavarṇo bhuvanasya goptā apūrva ekaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. When the mobile and immobile beings of the world get submerged into the ocean, then the kind Narayana sleeps in the oceanic bed, having a thousand heads, unblemished mind, a thousand eyes, feet and arms. Initially, the same Prajapati known as Purusha in the three Vedas, protects the Bhuvanas as Aditya. He is unique, ancient Purusha beyond darkness and is said to be Hiranyagarbha.

## Chapter 78. Glory of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.78.1 \|\|

*ityetanmaṇḍalaṃ śuklaṃ bhāsvaraṃ helisaṃjñitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — Again, the time of lengthy night resembling thousands of yugas is passed, then arrives the morning, when the same Purusha take to the form of Brahma, for the purpose of creation.

## \|\| 1.78.2 \|\|

*salilenāplutāṃ bhūmi dṛṣṭvā kāryaṃ vicintya saḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā sa tu varāho vai apaḥ saṃviśate prabhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Finding the earth having been submerged in water, getting reminded of his duty of creation, the lord then takes to the form of Varaha and enters the middle of the water.

## \|\| 1.78.3 \|\|

*sañcityaivaṃ sa deveśo bhūmeruddharaṇe kṣamaḥ \|*  
*mahīṃ mahārṇave magnāmuddhartumupacakrame \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Thus thinking, the lord of gods, who is competent enough to raise up the earth, makes efforts to rescue the same.

## \|\| 1.78.4 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhatastasya jalārdrakukṣermahāvarāhasya mahīṃ vidhārya \|*  
*vidhunvato vedamayaṃ śarīraṃ romāntarasthā munayo 1 japanti \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then lifting the earth, he merges out of the water. The body of Mahavaraha turns like the Vedas, which he had himself stirred at that time, the Rishis lodged in his hairpits.

## \|\| 1.78.5 \|\|

*uddhṛtyorvīṃ sa salilātprajāsargamakalpayat \|*  
*manasā janayāmāsa putrānātmasamāñchubhān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then lifting up the earth out of the water of the vast ocean, he creates the people over the same. Initially, he mentally created the sons resembling himself.

## \|\| 1.78.6-7 \|\|

*bhṛgvaṅgirasamatriṃ ca pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ katum \|*  
*marīcimatha dakṣaṃ ca vaśiṣṭhaṃ navamaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nava prajāpatīnsṛṣṭvā tataḥ sa puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*prādurbhūto'diteḥ putraḥ prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Thereafter, he created the Rishis known as Bhrigu, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Maricha, Daksha and Vasishtha, who were the nine Prajapatis. Thereafter, he himself was born as a son of Aditi.

## \|\| 1.78.8 \|\|

*marīcātkaśyapaṃ 2 putraṃ yaṃ vedhā janayajjale \|*  
*prajāpatīnāṃ daśamaṃ tejasā brahmaṇaḥ samam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Maricha produced a son named Kashyapa, who had been produced by Brahma in the water. He also became the tenth Prajapati, having the lustre parallel to that of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.78.9 \|\|

*vṛkṣakanyā'ditirnāmnā patnī sā kaśyapasya tu \|*  
*aṇḍaṃ sā janayāmāsa bhūrbhuvaḥsvastrisaṃyutam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vriksha has a daughter known as Aditi who became the wife of Kashyapa. An egg was born out of her womb, in which the earth, sky and nether worlds were enshrined.

## \|\| 1.78.10 \|\|

*tatrotpannaḥ sahasrāṃśurdvādaśātmā divākaraḥ \|*  
*navayojanasāhasro vistāro'sya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vistārāstriguṇaścāsya pariṇāho vibhāvasoḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. From the same egg, the Aditya emerged which was spread into nine thousand yojanas, with a circumference of twenty seven thousand yojanas.

## \|\| 1.78.11 \|\|

*yathāpuṇyaṃ kadambasya samantātkeśarairvṛtam \|*  
*tathaiva tejasāṃ golaṃ samantādraśmibhirvṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Like the pericarp of the lotus flower, it was surrounded by the saffrons. It was surrounded by the sun rays like the Kadamba flowers in the form of a ball of lustre.

## \|\| 1.78.12 \|\|

*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣo brāhma yogamudāharan \|*  
*taijasasya ca golasya sa tu madhye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The thousand-headed Purana embracing Brahma-yoga, got himself enshrined in his own ball of lustre.

## \|\| 1.78.13 \|\|

*ādatte sa tu raśmīnāṃ sahasreṇa samantataḥ \|*  
*apo nadīsamudrebhyo hradakūpebhya eva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He extracts the waters from rivers, oceans, well as well as the tanks with his thousand rays.

## \|\| 1.78.14 \|\|

*saurī prabhā yā devasya astaṃ yāte divākare \|*  
*agnimāviśate rātrau tasmāddūrātprakāśate1 \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His lustre named Sauri merges in the lire during the night, because of which the fire looks shining from a distance.

## \|\| 1.78.15 \|\|

*udite ca tataḥ sūrye teja āgneyamāviśat \|*  
*pādena tejasaścāgnestasmātsa tapate raviḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He achieves in the early morning sunrise, which is known as Agneya. The sun emits heat always with the fire.

## \|\| 1.78.16 \|\|

*prakāśatvaṃ tathoṣṇatvaṃ sūrye'gnau ca prakīrtite \|*  
*parasparānupraveśādāpyāyete divāniśam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Similarly, the heat and light which have been found in the Sun as well as the fire, the same are exchanged by them between themselves which becomes the cause of day and night.

## \|\| 1.78.17-19 \|\|

*vyāpakatvaṃ ca raśmīnāṃ nāmāni ca nibodha me \|*  
*hetayaḥ kiraṇā gāvo raśmayo'tha gabhastayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*abhīṣavo ghanaṃ cosrā vasavo'tha marīcayaḥ \|*  
*nāḍyo dīdhitayaḥ sādhyā mayūkhā bhānavoṃśavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*saptārcayaḥ suparṇāśca karāḥ pādāstathaiva ca \|*  
*eṣāṃ tu nāmnāṃ raśmīnāṃ paryāyā viṃśatiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Because of the pervading rays, they have different names which are going to be related by me. You please listen. They are known as: Heti, Kirana, Gavo, Rashmi, Garbhasta, Abhisha, Ghana, Chosra, Vasu, Marichi, Mardyo, Didhiti, Sadhya, Mayukha, Bhanu, Amshu, Saptarshi, Suparna, Kara and Pada. These names are synonyms of the rays.

## \|\| 1.78.20 \|\|

*candanādīni vakṣyāmi nāmānyeṣāṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*sahasraṃ tāta kathitaṃ śītavarṣoṣṇaniḥśravam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O excellent one, there are other names which I am going to tell you, which are like Chandana etc., you please listen. Among them are those which emerged out of winter, rain and heat

## \|\| 1.78.21 \|\|

*teṣāṃ catuḥśataṃ nāḍyo varṣaṃte citramūrtayaḥ \|*  
*2 candanāccaiva mandāśca kotanāmānumāstathā \|*  
*amṛtā nāma te sarve raśmayo vṛṣṭihetavaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. His four hundred rays are known by the names of Chitramurti, Chandana, Manda, Kotanama and Amrita, which pour the rain. They have been described to be the root cause of the rains.

## \|\| 1.78.22-24 \|\|

*himodvahāstu tatrānye raśmayastriśataṃ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*candrāste nāmataḥ sarve pītāste tu gabhastayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*saumyeśāścaiva1 vāmaśca hlādino himasarjanāḥ \|*  
*śuklāśca kakubhaścaiva gāvo viśvabhṛtastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śuklāste nāmataḥ sarve triśataṃ dharmasarjanāḥ \|*  
*samaṃ bibhrati te sarve manuṣyā devatāstathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Similarly, there are three hundred rays known by the names of Chandra which cause Soma, belonging to Indra, blissful and the one which causes the rainfall. There are bright coloured ones known as Gava, Kukubha and Vishvabhrita. These three hundred rays create dharma. Thus these rays cause benefit to the humans and the gods alike.

## \|\| 1.78.25 \|\|

*manuṣyānoṣadhībhistu svadhayā ca pitṝnapi \|*  
*amṛtena surānsarvāṃstrayastribhiratarpayan \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Aushadhis saved the humans, Svadha served the pitris and the nectar (Amrita) is used by the gods.

## \|\| 1.78.26-27 \|\|

*vasante caiva grīṣme ca śataiḥ sa tapate tribhiḥ \|*  
*varṣāśaratsu caiveśastapate sampravarṣate \|\| 26 \|\|*

*hemante śiśiraṃ caiva himotsargaṃ ca sa tribhiḥ \|*  
*oṣadhīṣu balaṃ dhatte svadhāyāṃ ca svadhāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*amareṣvamṛtaṃ sūryastrayaṃ triṣu niyacchiti \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Similarly, in the spring as well as the summer season, three hundred rays create heat and rains. Again in the cold season, they pour the rains. The Sungod infuses strength in Aushadhis, Svadha to manes and the nectar to the gods.

## \|\| 1.78.28 \|\|

*kālognirvatsaraścaiva dvādaśātmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*tapatyeṣu suraśreṣṭhastrīṃllokānsacarācarān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In this way, Kala (time), Agni (fire), Vatsara (the year), the Sungod taking to the form of mobiles and immobiles, provides heat in all the three lokas.

## \|\| 1.78.29 \|\|

*eṣa brahmā tathā viṣṇureṣa eva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni eṣa eva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He is also having the forms of Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara, Rigveda, Yajurveda and Samaveda.

## \|\| 1.78.30 \|\|

*ṛcābhiḥ stūyate pūrvaṃ madhyāhne yajurbhiḥ sadā \|*  
*sāmabhistvaparāhṇeṣu maheśānaḥ prapūjyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Therefore, with the reciting of the reds (of Rigveda) in the morning, the Yajurveda at noon, Samaveda in the afternoon, lord Shiva always worships the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.78.31 \|\|

*pūjyamānastu nityaṃ vai tapatyeṣa divaspatiḥ \|*  
*sadaiṣa tejasāṃ rāśirdīptimānsarvalokagaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus the adorable Sungod, getting resplendent with his lustre, produces light rays, visiting all the people.

## \|\| 1.78.32 \|\|

*pārśvatordhvamadhaścaiva tāpayatyeṣa sarvataḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśānaiḥ pūjyamānastu nityaśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Having been worshipped by Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara, he serves the people above at the back and below.

## \|\| 1.78.33 \|\|

*yathā sarvagato vāyurvahamānastu tiṣṭhati \|*  
*tadvatsahasrakiraṇo graharājo divaspatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus the Sungod pervades in all the places with the form of windgod. He should also be treated as the all-pervading one.

## \|\| 1.78.34-35 \|\|

*sūryo gobhirjagatkṛtsnamādīpayati sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*trīṇi raśmiśatānyasya bhūrlokaṃ dyotayanti vai \|\| 34 \|\|*

*trīṇitrīṇi tathā cānyau dvau lokau tāpayantyuta \|*  
*śataṃ cāpi adhastāttu pātālaṃ tāpayantyuta \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. With his resplendent rays, the Sungod brightens the entire universe. His three hundred rays fall on earth, and three hundred on Bhuvarloka and Svargaloka. His one hundred rays fail also on the nether world.

## \|\| 1.78.36 \|\|

*nakṣatragrahasomānāṃ pratiṣṭhāyonireva ca \|*  
*vidhuṛkṣagrahāḥ sarve vijñeyāḥ sūryasabhbhavāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This is the bright and resplendent orbit of the Sun. Similarly, the constellations, planets, and Soma creeper are caused by him, besides the places of Indra, the moon, constellations, and planets are also created by you.

## \|\| 1.78.37-38 \|\|

*raveḥ karasahasraṃ yatprāṅmayā samudāhṛtam \|*  
*teṣāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ punaḥ sapta raśmayo grahasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*suṣumṇo harikeśaśca viśvakarmā tathaiva ca \|*  
*sūryaścaivāparo raśmirnāmnā viṣṇuriti2 smṛtaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. In this way, the Sungod has a thousand rays, about which I have spoken already. He also has seven special rays for the planets which are known by the names of Sushumna, Harikesha, Vishvakarma, Surya, Vapara, Rashmi and Vishnu. All of them like the strong kins, bestow life to the world.

## \|\| 1.78.39-40 \|\|

*sasattvaḥ sarvabandhustu jīvāyati ca vai jagat \|*  
*saptajaḥ prathamastatra kañjajaśca tathā paraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tāreyaścāparastatra guruḥ sumanasāṃ tathā \|*  
*ugrāhvaḥ pañcamasteṣāṃ putro'nyo vanamālinaḥ \|*  
*kaḥ śeṣaḥ saptamasteṣāmete vai sapta raśmayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Similarly, there are also seven other rays known by the names of Kanjaja which is the first one, Tareya the second one, third one Guru, fourth one Sumana, Ugra the fifth one, Vanamalina and Shesha the seventh one.

## \|\| 1.78.41 \|\|

*ādityamūlamakhilaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*bhavatyasmājjagatsarvaṃ sa devāsuramānuṣam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In the entire universe of mobiles and immobiles, the Sungod is the only creator, because he happens to be the creator of the world comprising of Devas, Asuras, humans and others.

## \|\| 1.78.42 \|\|

*rudrendropendracandrāṇāṃ viprendra tridivaukasām \|*  
*mahadyutimataḥ kṛtsnaṃ tejo yatsārvalaukikam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O Viprendra, Rudra, Indra, Upendra (Vishnu) besides the moon, possess the resplendence of the Sungod because of his all-pervading nature.

## \|\| 1.78.43 \|\|

*sarvātmā sarvalokeśo devadevaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*sūrya eva trilokasya mūlaṃ paramadaivatam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus, he is the soul of all beings, lord of all the lokas, god of gods, besides being Prajapati and the supreme god.

## \|\| 1.78.44 \|\|

*agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate \|*  
*ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The offering poured in the fire reaches the Sungod. Getting the same, the Sungod drops the rain, which produce the cereals, and which feed the people.

## \|\| 1.78.45 \|\|

*sūryātprasūyate sarvaṃ tasminneva pralīyate \|*  
*bhāvābhāvau tu lokānāmādityānniḥsṛtau purā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Accordingly, the entire universe is created by the Sungod and he also is the cause of its destruction. Therefore, the creation and destruction of the universe are done by him. This has been ordained from the earliest times.

## \|\| 1.78.46 \|\|

*etattu dhyānināṃ dhyānaṃ mokṣaścāpyeva mokṣiṇām \|*  
*atra gacchanti nirvāṇaṃ jāyante'smātpunaḥ prajāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He happens to be the object of adoration. For those who are desirous of moksha, he happens to be the form of moksha. The people achieve nirvana in him only. It is he from whom all the people emerge again.

## \|\| 1.78.47 \|\|

*kṣaṇā muhūrtā divasā niśāḥ pakṣāstu nityaśaḥ \|*  
*māsāḥ samvatsarāścaiva ṛtavo'tha yugāni ca \|*  
*athādityamṛte hyeṣāṃ kālasaṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The moments, muhurtas, days, nights, fortnights, months, years, seasons, besides the arrangements for yugas cannot be done without the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.78.48 \|\|

*kālādṛte na niyamā nāgnerviharaṇakriyā \|*  
*ṛtū nāmavibhāgācca puṣpamūlaphalaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Similarly, without the proper arrangement for the time how could the homos be performed? How could the fruits and flowers grow without dividing the seasons?

## \|\| 1.78.49 \|\|

*abhāvo vyavahārāṇāṃ jantūnāṃ divi ceha ca \|*  
*jagatpratāpanamṛte bhāskaraṃ vāritaskaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Without the Sungod, the heavenly and the worldly activities cannot be established.

## \|\| 1.78.50 \|\|

*nāvṛṣṭyā tapate sūryo nāvṛṣṭyā pariveṣyate \|*  
*ādityasya ca nāmāni sāmānyānīha dvādaśa \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The heat in the Sun cannot develop without the rains. Now I am speaking out separately the twelve names of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.78.51-54 \|\|

*dvādaśaiva pṛthaktvena tāni vakṣyāmyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*ādityaḥ savitā sūryo mihiro'rkaḥ pratāpanaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*mārtaṃḍo bhāskaro bhānuścitrabhānurdivākaraḥ \|*  
*ravirvai dvādaśaścaiva jñeyaḥ sāmānyanāmabhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*viṣṇurdhātā bhagaḥ pūṣā mitrendro varuṇo'ryamā \|*  
*vivasvānaṃśumāṃstvaṣṭā parjanyo dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*ityete dvādaśādityāḥ pṛthaktvena prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*uttiṣṭhanti sadā hyete māsairdvādaśabhiḥ kramāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. These names are Aditya, Savita, Surya, Mihira, Arka, Pratapana, Martanda, Bhaskara, Bhanu, Chitrabhanu, Divakara and Ravi. These are his common names. His destructive forms include Vishnu, Dhata, Bhaga, Pusha, Mitra, Indra, Varuna, Aryama, Vivasvan, Amshuman, Tvashta and Parjanya, which are used in the twelve months.

## \|\| 1.78.55-57 \|\|

*viṣṇustapati caitre ca vaiśākhe cāryamā tathā \|*  
*vivasvāñjyeṣṭhamāse tu āṣāḍhe cāṃśumāṃstathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*parjanyaḥ śrāvaṇe māsi varuṇaḥ proṣṭhasaṃjñake \|*  
*indraścāśvayuje māsi dhātā tapati kārtike \|\| 56 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣe tathā mitraḥ pauṣe pūṣā divākaraḥ \|*  
*māghe bhagastu vijñeyastvaṣṭā tapati phālgune \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Vishnu provides heat in the month of Chaitra, Aryama in Vaishakha and Vivasvan in Jyeshtha; Amshuman in Ashadha; Parjanya in Havana; Varuna in Bhadrapada; Indra in Ashvina; Dhata in Karttika; Pusha in Pausha; Bhaga in Margashirsha and Tvashta in the month of Phalguna.

## \|\| 1.78.58-60 \|\|

*taiśca dvādaśabhirviṣṇū raśmīnāṃ dīpyate sadā \|*  
*dīpyate gosahasreṇa śataiśca tribhiraryamā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*dvisaptakairvivasvāṃstu aṃśumānpañcakaistribhiḥ \|*  
*vivasvāniva parjanyo varuṇaścāryamā iva \|\| 59 \|\|*

*indrastu dviguṇaiḥ ṣaḍbhirdhātaikādaśabhiḥ śataiḥ \|*  
*mitravadbhagavattvaṣṭā sahasreṇa śatena ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. Accordingly, Surya known as Vishnu has twelve hundred rays, Aryama has thirteen hundred, Vivasvan has fourteen hundred, Amshuman has fifteen hundred, Parjanya has fourteen hundred, Vivasvan and Varuna like Aryama has thirteen hundred, Indra has twelve hundred, Dhata has eleven hundred like Tvashta, Mitra and Bhaga, which provide heat to the world.

## \|\| 1.78.61 \|\|

*uttaropakrame'rkasya vardhante raśmayaḥ sadā \|*  
*dakṣiṇopakrame bhūyo hrasante sūryaraśmayaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The sun-rays are always on the increase in Uttarayana, similarly in Dakshinayana, they keep on decreasing.

## \|\| 1.78.62 \|\|

*evaṃ raśmisahasraṃ tu sauryaṃ lokārthasādhakam \|*  
*bhidyate ṛtumāsaistu sahasraṃ bahudhā 1 bhṛśam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thus the thousand rays of the Sun, which are always on increase or decrease due to the change of seasons, make the efforts of the people successful.

## \|\| 1.78.63 \|\|

*evaṃ nāmnāṃ caturviṃśadekasyaiṣā prakīrtitā \|*  
*vistareṇa sahasraṃ tu punarevaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. As there are twenty four names of one and the same Sun, his thousand names have also been described exhaustively.

## \|\| 1.78.64 \|\|

*āsāṃ paramayatnena bruvate bhinnadarśanāḥ \|*  
*tāmasā buddhimohācca dṛṣṭāntāni bruvanti hi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Therefore, the different types of philosophers make enormous efforts to explain the significance of the sun rays. A person with excess of tamas in him, inspite of viewing him with confusion, hardly discards his ideals.

## \|\| 1.78.65-66 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kecitkecidāhurdivākaram \|*  
*kecidbhavaṃ paratvena āhurviṣṇuṃ tathāpare \|\| 65 \|\|*

*kāraṇaṃ tu smṛtā hyete nānārtheṣu surottamāḥ \|*  
*ekaḥ sa tu pṛthaktvena svayaṃbhūriti viśrutaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Though some people have described Brahma, some have conceived him as Surya or Shiva or Vishnu as the cause of the universe, but all these gods, getting influence with Surya, who is separate from all and is also known as Svayambhu, incarnating on earth, have different spheres of their functions.

## \|\| 1.78.67-68 \|\|

*vanamālinamugreśaṃ divi cakṣurivāntakam \|*  
*taṃ svayaṃbhūriti proktaṃ sa soparṇimanaupamam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yathānurajyate varṇervividhaiḥ sphāṭiko maṇiḥ \|*  
*tathā guṇavaśāttasya svayaṃbhoranurañjanam \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Therefore, Vanamali, Ugresha, the eye of the sky, Yama, all in the form of Surya, is the best among the gods as well as the self-born. Like the crystal gem, the self-born Sun also appears in various forms.

## \|\| 1.78.69 \|\|

*eko bhūtvā yathā meghaḥ pṛthaktvena pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*varṇato rūpataścaiva tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Like the single cloud turns its form and colour often, the Sun also keeps on changing according to the merits.

## \|\| 1.78.70 \|\|

*nabhasaḥ patitaṃ toyaṃ yāti svādāntaraṃ yathā \|*  
*bhūme rasaviśeṣeṇa tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Like the water falling from the sky is of different taste as compared to the water that comes into touch with the earth, similar are the qualities of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.78.71 \|\|

*yathendhanavaśādagnirekastu bahudhāyate \|*  
*varṇato rūpataścaiva tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. As the same fire with the burning materials of different kinds and colours (display different colours), similarly the qualities of colour etc. change in the Sun.

## \|\| 1.78.72 \|\|

*yathā dravyaviśeṣācca vāyurekaḥ pṛthagbhavet \|*  
*sugandhiḥ pūtigandhirvā tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. As one and the same wind change its form coming in contact with fragrance or bad smell, similarly, because of the change in the qualities, the Sun has to face the changes.

## \|\| 1.78.73 \|\|

*yathā vā gārhapatyogniranyatsaṃjñāntaraṃ vrajet \|*  
*dakṣiṇāhavanīyādibrahmādiṣu tathā hyasau \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Like the fire of the householder, which because of its usage is known by the names of Dakshinagni (sacrificial fire) and Atravaniya (the fire which is invoke), and several other names, similarly, Surya is also known by different names.

## \|\| 1.78.74 \|\|

*ekatve ca pṛthaktve ca proktametannidarśanam \|*  
*tasmādbhaktiḥ sadā kāryā deve hyasmindivākare \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Therefore, this is the example for his being a single god as well as having many forms. Therefore, lord Divakara should always be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.78.75-76 \|\|

*eṣo'ṇḍajo'dhigaścaiva eṣa eva bhṛgustathā \|*  
*eṣa rajastamaścaiva eṣa sattvaguṇastathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*eṣa vedāśca yajñāśca sarvaścaiva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sūryavyāptamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. He is Martanda, all pervading, Bhrigu and possesses Rajas, Tamas as well as Sattvaguna, besides Vedas, yajnas and having universal form. There is no doubt about it. He pervades in the entire universe in mobile and immobile forms.

## \|\| 1.78.77 \|\|

*1 ijyate pūjyate cāsāvatra yānātmako raviḥ \|*  
*sarvatra savitā devastanubhirnāmabhiśca saḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Surya is also known to the people in twelve forms, who worship him everywhere always.

## \|\| 1.78.78 \|\|

*vasatyagnau tathā vāte vyomni toye tathā vibho \|*  
*evaṃvidho hyayaṃ sūryaḥ sadā pūjyo vijānatā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Similarly, the dwellers of Agni, Vayu, the sky and water should always worship him.

## \|\| 1.78.79-80 \|\|

*ādityaṃ vetti yastvevaṃ sa tasminneva līyate \|*  
*apyekaṃ vetti yo nāma dhātvarthanigamai raveḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sa rogairvarjitaḥ sarvaiḥ sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate \|*  
*na hi pāpakṛtaḥ sāmba bhaktirbhavati bhāskare \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. A person who achieves some special material knowledge about Surya, he attains his Sayajjya (closeness) or moksha. A person who is aware of the single name of Surya, is quickly relieved of all the sins and diseases. Therefore, O Samba, the sinful people can never become the devotees of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.78.81 \|\|

*tathā tvaṃ parayā bhaktyā prapadyasva divākaram \|*  
*yena vyādhivinirmuktaḥ sarvānkāmānavāpsyasi \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Therefore, you worship the Sungod with utmost devotion, by which you getting relieved of the ailment, succeed in all your efforts.

## \|\| 1.78.82-83 \|\|

*yathā tava pitā sāmba yathā vedhā yathā haraḥ \|*  
*yathā guṇavaśāttasya svayambhoranurañjanam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*ekībhūya yathā meghaḥ pṛthaktvena pratiṣṭhate \|*  
*varṇato rūpataścaiva tathā guṇavaśāttu saḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. O Samba, like your father, Brahma and Shiva, the Sungod also appears according to merits. The clouds of different colour forms after mixing themselves with one another look differently, similarly, the Sun also changes himself by his merits.

## Chapter 79. Glory of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.79.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*etacchrutvā tu kārtsnyena hṛṣṭo jāmbavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*jātakautūhalo bhūyaḥ paripapraccha nāradam1 \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — Delightfully listening to the story by Samba, he again enquired from Narada.

## \|\| 1.79.2-3 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*aho sūryasya māhātmyaṃ varṇitaṃ harṣavardhanam \|*  
*yena me bhaktirutpannā parā hyasminvibhāvasau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tato rājñīṃ mahābhāgāṃ nikṣubhāṃ ca mahāmune \|*  
*diṇḍinaṃ piṅgalādīṃśca sarvānkathaya me mune \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Samba said — What a surprise? You have narrated the delighted glory of the Sungod, which has inculcated the sense of devotion for Surya in my heart. O great sage, you tell me further about auspicious Rajni and Nikshubha — the two great damsels, besides Dandi and Pingala.

## \|\| 1.79.4 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*prāgukte'rkasya dve bhārye rājñī nikṣubhasaṃjñite \|*  
*tayorhi rājñī dyaurjñeyā nikṣubhā pṛthivī smṛtā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Narada said — The two wives of the Sungod, about whom I have already stated earlier, happen to be the sky and the earth. This should be kept in mind.

## \|\| 1.79.5-6 \|\|

*saumyamāsasya2 saptamyāṃ dyāvārkaḥ saha yujyate \|*  
*māghakṛṣṇasya saptamyāṃ mahyā saha bhavedraviḥ \|*  
*bhūrādityaśca bhagavāngacchataḥ saṅgamaṃ tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ṛtusnātā mahī tatra garbhaṃ gṛhṇāti bhāskarāt \|*  
*dyaurjalaṃ sūyate garbhaṃ varṣāsviha ca bhūtale \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. On the bright seventh moon day of the month of Pausha, Rajni (sky) unites with the Sun, while on the dark seventh moon day of the month of Magha, Nikshubha (earth) unites with the Sun. With the combination of the Sun with the earth, like a woman having bath after the period, the earth conceives. This is provided by the Sun in the rainy season as rain water. In order to bestow fortunes on all the three worlds, the earth is filled with riches and cereals.

## \|\| 1.79.7-8 \|\|

*tatastrailokyabhūtyarthaṃ3 mahī sasyāni sūyate \|*  
*sasyopayogasaṃhṛṣṭā juhvatyāhutayo dvijāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*svāhākārasvadhākārairyajanti pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Thus, in order to show fortunes on all the three lokas, the earth produces riches as well as the cereals, receiving which, the Brahmanas perform homas. The creators of Svadha please the manes and the creators of Svaha, adore the gods.

## \|\| 1.79.9 \|\|

*nikṣubhā sūyate yasmādannauṣadhisudhāmṛtaiḥ \|*  
*martyānpitṝṃśca devāṃśca tena bhūrnikṣubhā smṛtā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. With the cereals thus produced besides aushadhis and sudha (nectar), the life is infused in humans, manes and the gods. Since the earth infuses life into all the living beings, she is known as Nikshubha.

## \|\| 1.79.10 \|\|

*yathā rājñī dvidhā bhūtā yasya ceyaṃ sutā matā \|*  
*apatyāni ca yānyasyāstāni vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Similarly, Rajni is of two forms, I am now revealing the names of her parents and her children.

## \|\| 1.79.11-13 \|\|

*marīcirbrahmaṇaḥ putro marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*tasmāddhiraṇyakaśiṣuḥ prahlādastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*prahlādasya suto nāmnā virocana iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*virocanasya bhaginī saṃjñāyā jananī śubhā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ pautrī diteḥ putrasya sā smṛtā \|*  
*sā viśvakarmaṇaḥ putrī prāhlādī procyate budhaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Brahma had a son named Marichi. Kashyapa was the son of Marichi, Hiranyakashipu was the son of Kashyapa who had a son named Prahlada, Virochana was the son of Prahlada, It has been heard that Virochana’s sister who was the grand-daughter of Hiranyakashipu — the son of Diti, was the daughter of Prahlada. She was married to Vishvakarma. She was the mother of Samjna.

## \|\| 1.79.14 \|\|

*atha nāmnā surūpeti marīcerduhitā śubhā \|*  
*putrī hyaṅgirasaḥ sā tu jananī tu bṛhaspateḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Samjna was the daughter of Marichi and was married to Angira. She was the mother of Brihaspati.

## \|\| 1.79.15-16 \|\|

*bṛhaspatestu bhaginī viśrutā brahmavādinī \|*  
*prabhāsasya tu sā patnī vasūnāmaṣṭamasya tu \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prasūtā viśvakarmāṇaṃ sarvaśilpakaraṃ varam \|*  
*sa vai nāmrā punastvaṣṭā tridaśānāṃ ca vārdhakiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The Brahmavadini — the sister of Brihaspati, was married to Prabha — the eighth Vasu, She produced Vishvakarma as a son, who was well-versed in all the arts. He was also called Tvashta, because he was engaged in the increase of the gods.

## \|\| 1.79.17-18 \|\|

*devācāryaśca tasyeyaṃ duhitā viśvakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*sureṇuriti vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu bhāminī \|\| 17 \|\|*

*rājñī saṃjñā ca dyaustvāṣṭrī prabhā saiva vibhāvyate \|*  
*tasyāttu yā tanucchāyā nikṣubhā sā mahīmayī \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The beautiful Samjna was the daughter of Vishvakarma. She was well known in the three words as Surenu. She also came to be known by the names of Rajni, Samjna, Dyau, as well as Tvashtri. The shadow of her body was known as Nikshubha.

## \|\| 1.79.19 \|\|

*sā1 tu bhāryā bhagavato mārtaṇḍasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sādhvī pativratā devī rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The same chaste damsel who was quite charming as well as beautiful, was married to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.79.20-22 \|\|

*na tu tāṃ nararūpeṇa sūryo bhajati vai purā \|*  
*ādityasyeha tadrūpaṃ mahatā svena tejasā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gātreṣvapratirūpeṣu nātikāntamivābhavat \|*  
*aniṣpatreṣu gātreṣu golaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mārtastvaṃ bhava cāṇḍastu mārtaṇḍastena sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ ca yatastvādistenāditya iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. But the Sungod did not unite with her in human form, because he was quite resplendent, which could not attract Samjna. Finding the resplendent body of the Sun, Brahma said — “You be an earthen egg. Surya is also known as Martanda, since he is the foremost of the gods, he is also known as Aditya.

## \|\| 1.79.23 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi prajāstasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*trīṇyapatyāni saṃjñāyāṃ janayāmāsa vai raviḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I am now speaking about their progeny. You please listen. The Sungod produced three children from the womb of Samjna.

## \|\| 1.79.24-25 \|\|

*varṣāṇāṃ tu sahasraṃ vai vasamānā piturgṛhe \|*  
*bhartuḥ samīpaṃ yāhīti pitroktā sā punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*agacchadvaḍavā bhūtvā tyaktvā rūpaṃ yaśasvinī \|*  
*uttarāṃśca kurūngatvā tṛṇānyanucacāra ha \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Though Samjna, who lived in her father’s house for a thousand years and her father asked her repeatedly to return to her husband home, but the chaste Samjna, discarding her human body took to the form of a mare. She grazed the grass in the Kuru country and passed her time.

## \|\| 1.79.26 \|\|

*pituḥ samīpaṃ yā bhāryā saṃjñā yā vacanena sā \|*  
*saṃjñāyā dhārayadrūpaṃ chāyā sūryamupasthitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. While Samjna was staying in her parents’ home, she sent her shadow in her place in the abode of the sun.

## \|\| 1.79.27 \|\|

*dvitīyāyāṃ tu saṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñeyamiti cintayan \|*  
*ādityo janayāmāsa putrau kanyāṃ ca rūpiṇīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Finding her (the shadow) there, the Sungod took her to be his real wife and produced two eons and a daughter out of her.

## \|\| 1.79.28 \|\|

*pūrvajasya manostulyau sādṛśyena ca tāvubhau \|*  
*śrutaśravāśca dharmajñaḥ śrutakarmā tathaiva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Both Shrutashrava and Shrutakarma — the noble sons resembled their ancestor Manu.

## \|\| 1.79.29 \|\|

*śrutaśravā manustābhyāṃ sāvarṇiryo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śrutakarmā tu vijñeyo graho yo vai śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Out of them, his son Shrutashrava was the future Manu and Shrutakarma became the planet Saturn.

## \|\| 1.79.30-31 \|\|

*kanyā ca tapatī nāma rūpeṇāpratirūpiṇī \|*  
*saṃjñā tu pārthivī teṣāmātmajānāṃ yathākarot \|\| 30 \|\|*

*na snehaṃ pūrvajānāṃ tu tathā kṛtavatī tu sā \|*
