*manustu kṣamate tasyā yamastasyā na cakṣame \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The beautiful girl was given the name of Tapati. On the other hand, Chaya could not extend the same type of affection to her step children. Though Manu could tolerate the evil treatment by his step mother, but it became difficult for Yama to do so.

## \|\| 1.79.32-34 \|\|

*bahuśo yātyamānastu pituḥ patnyā suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*sa vai kopācca bālyācca bhāvino'rthasya vai balāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*padā santarjayāmāsa saṃjñāṃ vaivasvato yamaḥ \|*  
*taṃ śaśāpa tataḥ krodhātsaṃjñā sā pārthivī bhṛśam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*padā tarjayase yanmāṃ piturbhāryāṃ garīyasīm \|*  
*tasmāttavaiṣa caraṇaḥ patiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Because of the excessive torture by the second wife of his father, Yama, once getting enraged, because of his childish habit and with the influence of the moves of destiny, kicked at Chaya, who also getting enraged pronounced a curse on Yama — “The foot with which you have kicked the glorious wife of your father, will surely fall.”

## \|\| 1.79.35 \|\|

*yamastu tena śāpena bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasaḥ \|*  
*manunā saha tanmātuḥ pituḥ sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Soon after, by badly suffering from the curse, Yama together with Manu, went to the Sungod and narrated to him the tale of their suffering at the hand of the (step) mother.

## \|\| 1.79.36 \|\|

*snehena tulyamasmāsu mātā deva na vartate \|*  
*niḥsnehāñjyāyaso hyasmātkanīyāṃ saṃ bubhūṣati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. They said — “O Deva, though we are entitled to equal love by her, she is more attached to the younger one and not we people.

## \|\| 1.79.37 \|\|

*tasyā mayodyataḥ pādo na tu deva nipātitaḥ \|*  
*bālyādvā yadi vā mohāttadbhavānkṣantumarhati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Deva! Though I had raised my foot to lack her, but I did not actually strike her. Therefore, the sin committed by me because of my childish ways, may be forgiven by you.

## \|\| 1.79.38 \|\|

*śapto'hamasmiṃllokeśa jananyā tapatāṃ vara \|*  
*tava prasādāccaraṇastrāyatāṃ mahato bhayāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O lord of the universe, O best of the ascetics, the mother has pronounced a curse on me. Therefore, your compassion can relieve me of the curse. (I am sure of this).

## \|\| 1.79.39 \|\|

*raviruvāca \|*  
*asaṃśayaṃ mahatputra bhaviṣyatyatra kāraṇam \|*  
*yena tvāmāviśatkrodho dharmajñaṃ dharmaśālinam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Sungod said — O son, there must be surely some deep rooted cause behind it. Because of your being noble minded one, you could never have been enraged to such an extent.

## \|\| 1.79.40 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva śāpānāṃ pratighātastu vidyate \|*  
*na tu mātrābhiśaptānāṃ kvacinmokṣo bhavediha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. But one thing is sure, after a curse is pronounced by a mother, a person can never be relieved of it.

## \|\| 1.79.41 \|\|

*na śakyametanmithyā me kartuṃ māturvacastava \|*  
*kiñcitte'haṃ vidhāsyāmi pitṛsnehādanugraham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Because of that, I am unable to remove the curse of your mother. But because of the fatherly attachment towards you, I shall surely shower my grace on you.

## \|\| 1.79.42 \|\|

*kṛmayo māṃsamādāya yāsyanti tu mahītale \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tasyā vacaḥ satyaṃ tvaṃ ca trāto bhaviṣyasi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The worms, extracting you flesh will move on earth and the foot would be saved. By so doing, her words would become true and you would also be saved.

## \|\| 1.79.43 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*ādityastvabravīcchāyāṃ kimarthaṃ tanayāvubhau \|*  
*tulyeṣvabhyadhikaḥ sneha ekatra kriyate tvayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Sumantu said — Surya then went to Chaya and asked her, though all the children are entitled to be same type of love from you, then why are you excessively attached to one of them only?”

## \|\| 1.79.44 \|\|

*sā1 tatpurābhavaṃ tasmai nācacakṣe vivasvate \|*  
*ātmānaṃ sa samādhāya vaktuṃ tasyāmapaśyat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Getting reminded of the words of Samjna, she kept quiet. But the Sungod looked at her expecting a reply.

## \|\| 1.79.45 \|\|

*tāṃ śaptukāmo bhagavānudyataḥ kupitastataḥ \|*  
*tataśchāyā yathāvṛttamācacakṣe vivasvate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then when Chaya found that the Sungod was about to pronounce a curse on her, she revealed the entire story to him.

## \|\| 1.79.46 \|\|

*vivasvāṃstu tataḥ kruddhaḥ śrutvā śvaśuramāgataḥ \|*  
*sā cāpi taṃ yathānyāyamarcayitvā divākaram \|*  
*nirdagdhukāmaṃ roṣeṇa sāntvayāmāsa taṃ śanaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing it, the enraged Sungod rushed to his father-in-law. His father-in-law welcomed him appropriately and gradually cooled him down.

## \|\| 1.79.47 \|\|

*viśvakarmovāca \|*  
*tavātitejasāviṣṭamidaṃ rūpaṃ suduḥsaham \|*  
*asahantī tu saṃjñā ca vane carati śādvale \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vishvakarma said — Unable to bear your lustre resplendence, Samjna is wandering in the forest full of grass.

## \|\| 1.79.48 \|\|

*drakṣyate tāṃ bhavānadya svāṃ māyāṃ śubhacāriṇīm \|*  
*rūpārthaṃ bhavatoraṇye carantīṃ sumahattapaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, the auspicious lady in order to gain resplendence comparable to you, is performing tapas in the forest. You should therefore go and appear before her.

## \|\| 1.79.49 \|\|

*rūpaṃ te brahmaṇo vākyādyadi vai rocate vibho \|*  
*praśātayāmi devendra śreyo'rthaṃ jagataḥ prabho \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O excellent one, in case you are desirous of having the beauty created by Brahma, then I would be prepared to chisel out your body. By so doing, the world would be benefitted.

## \|\| 1.79.50 \|\|

*santuṣṭastasya tadvākyaṃ bahu mene mahātapāḥ \|*  
*tato'nvajānāttvaṣṭāraṃ rūpanirvartanāya tu \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Surya — the performer of great tapas, then accepted the proposal of Vishvakarma. Then he said to Tvashta, who bestow beauty to the bodies (to do the job).

## \|\| 1.79.51 \|\|

*viśvakarmā hyanujñātaḥ śākadvīpe vivasvataḥ \|*  
*bhramimāropya tattejaḥ śātayāmāsa tasya vai \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. With the permission of the Sungod, Vishvakarma, making use of the Shakadvipa — yantra, put the Sungod over it and then started chiseling his lustre.

## \|\| 1.79.52 \|\|

*ājānulikhitaścāsau nipuṇaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*lekhanaṃ nābhyanandattu tatastena nivāritaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Vishvakarma quite cleverly chiseled out the body of the Sungod upto the knees, beautifying all the limbs. Thereafter, the Sungod declined to have the other limbs chiseled.

## \|\| 1.79.53 \|\|

*tatra tadbhāsitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasā prakṛtena tu \|*  
*kāntātkāntataraṃ bhūtvā adhikaṃ śuśubhe tataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. But the parts of the body which were chiseled out became more resplendent than before, making his body more beautiful.

## \|\| 1.79.54 \|\|

*dadarśa yogamāsthāya svāṃ bhāryāṃ vaḍavāṃ tathā \|*  
*adṛśyāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tejasā svena saṃvṛtām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thereafter, with the use of his yogic powers, he spotted his wife who had taken to the favour of a mare, who having been surrounded by her own lustre was wandering, unseen by other people.

## \|\| 1.79.55 \|\|

*aśvarūpeṇa mārtaṇḍastāṃ mukhena samāsadat \|*  
*maithunāya viceṣṭanto parapuṃso viśaṅkayā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Reaching there, the Sungod in the form of a horse, touched his face with his wife in the form of a mare, but finding him desirous of a union, she became doubtful of him.

## \|\| 1.79.56 \|\|

*sā taṃ vivasvataḥ śukraṃ nāsābhyāṃ samadhārayat \|*  
*devau tasyāmajāyetāmaśvinau bhiṣajāṃ varau \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Thereafter, she, with the semen of the Sungod which was held by her in her nostrils, produced the two Devas known as Ashvinikumaras, who ultimately became the best physicians of the gods.

## \|\| 1.79.57 \|\|

*nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca tau smṛtau nāmato'śvinau \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*taddṛṣṭvā cāpi saṃjñā tu tutoṣa ca mumoha ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Both of them were given the names of Nasatya and Dasra. Thereafter, the Sungod appeared in his true form, finding which Samjna was delightfully attracted towards the Sun.

## \|\| 1.79.58 \|\|

*tatastu janayāmāsa saṃjñā sūryasutaṃ śubham \|*  
*rūpeṇa cātmanastulyaṃ revataṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thereafter, Samjna produced another son from the Sungod, who was comparable with Sungod in the form and beauty and was known as Revataka.

## \|\| 1.79.59 \|\|

*pirtugṛhyāṣṭamaṃ so'śvaṃ jātamātraḥ palāyata \|*  
*sa tasmintsakṛdārūḍhastamaśvaṃ naiva muñjati \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Soon after his birth, Revataka fled away with the eighth horse of his father. Though he rode the horse only once, but thereafter, he could not leave it.

## \|\| 1.79.60 \|\|

*tato'rkeṇa samādiṣṭau daṇḍanāyakapiṅgalau \|*  
*aśvaṃ pratyānayethāṃ me mā balācchidrato'sya tu \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thereafter, the Sungod with his attendants Pingala and Dandi started to get back his horse without using force against his son. (He told that) rather the horse should be captured, finding some fault with Revataka.

## \|\| 1.79.61 \|\|

*pārśvasthau tiṣṭhatastasya aśvacchidrābhikāñkṣiṇau \|*  
*na cchidraṃ tu labhete tau tasyādyāpi mahātmanaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Though both the attendants started following Revataka in order to find some fault, but till date, they could not find any fault with the boy.

## \|\| 1.79.62 \|\|

*plavangacchatyasau yasmātsaṃjñāyāḥ śāntidaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*revṛstu ca gatau dhātū revantastena sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The child which bestowed peace on his mother Samjna, because of his moving while jumping, was given the name Revataka.

## \|\| 1.79.63 \|\|

*manuryamo yamī caiva sāvarṇiḥ sa śanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*tapatī cāśvinau caiva revantaśca raveḥ sutāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Accordingly, the Sungod had the children known as Manu, Yama, Yami, Savarni, Shanishchara, Tapati, Ashvinikumaras (Nasatya and Dasra) besides Revataka.

## \|\| 1.79.64 \|\|

*evameṣā purā saṃjñā dvitīyā pārthivī smṛtā \|*  
*yā saṃjñā sā smṛtā rājñī chāyā yā sā tu nikṣubhā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He had two wives Samjna as well as Chaya. In due course of time, Samjna came to be known as Rajni (queen) and Chaya as Nikshubha (the earth).

## \|\| 1.79.65-66 \|\|

*rājṛdīptau smṛto dhātū rājā rājati yatsadā \|*  
*adhikaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo rājate ca divākaraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*adhikaṃ rājate yasmāttasmādrājā sa ucyate \|*  
*rājñaḥ patnī tu sā yasmāttasmādrājñī prakīrtitā \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Because the root raj stands for resplendence, and the one possessing the resplendence becomes a king, but the Sun illuminates one and all. Therefore, because of his excessive resplendence, the Sun is known as the king and Samjna happens to be his queen.

## \|\| 1.79.67 \|\|

*kṣubha sañcalane dhāturniścalā tena nikṣubhā \|*  
*bhavantītyatha vā yasmātsvargīyāḥ 1 kṣudvivarjitāḥ \|*  
*chāyāṃ tāṃ viśate divyāṃ smṛtā sā tena nikṣubhā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Similarly, the root kshubha stands for movement, but the earth having been deprived of the same, is known as Nikshubha otherwise, the divine earth being devoid of hunger, enters the divine shadow, earning the name of Nikshubha.

## \|\| 1.79.68 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā janaṃ sadā tāta bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasam \|*  
*dharmeṇa rañjayāmāsa dharmarājastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O excellent one, finding the humans suffering from the mental agony, dharma always tries to comfort them and because of this, the Sungod is also known as Dharmaraja.

## \|\| 1.79.69 \|\|

*śuddhena karmaṇā tāta śubhena paramadyutiḥ \|*  
*pitṝṇāmādhipatyaṃ ca lokapālatvamāpa ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O excellent one, with his auspicious and pure deeds, he has gained enormous lustre, achieved superiority over the manes besides the status of maintaining the lokas.

## \|\| 1.79.70 \|\|

*sāmprataṃ vartate yo'yaṃ manurloke mahāmate \|*  
*yasyānvavāye jātastu śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. O intelligent one, during the present times, taking birth from the race of Manu, he has been adorned with the attributes of conch, disc and club.

## \|\| 1.79.71 \|\|

*yamasya bhaginī yā tu yamī kanyā yaśasvinī \|*  
*sābhavatsaritāṃ śreṣṭhā yamunā lokapāvanī \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The auspicious sister of Yama known as Yami, is the foremost of all the rivers and is known as Yamuna, which purifies the world.

## \|\| 1.79.72 \|\|

*manuḥ prajāpatistveṣa sāvarṇiḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyansa manustāta aṣṭamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Similarly, the glorious Manu would also become Savarni, who has been declared as the eighth Manu.

## \|\| 1.79.73 \|\|

*merupṛṣṭhe tapo divyamadyāpi carate prabhuḥ \|*  
*bhrātā śanaibhrarastasya grahatvaṃ sa tu labdhavān \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The same lord Manu and others are performing tapas over the Meru mountain. His Mother is known to be the planet Saturn.

## \|\| 1.79.74 \|\|

*tapatī nāma yā nāmnā tayoḥ kanyā garīyasī \|*  
*sā babhūva śubhā patnī rājñaḥ saṃvaraṇasya tu \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Tapati was the daughter of the Sungod as well as Chaya, who was the chaste wife of the king Samvarana.

## \|\| 1.79.75 \|\|

*tāpī nāma nadī ceyaṃ vindhyamūlādviniḥsṛtā \|*  
*nityaṃ puṇyajalā snāne paścimodadhigāminī \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The same starting from the foot of the Vindhya mountain came to be known as the river Tap!, the water of which is considered to be quite pure for taking of a bath. It flows towards the western ocean.

## \|\| 1.79.76 \|\|

*saumyayā saṅgatā sā tu sarvapāpabhayāpahā \|*  
*vaivasvatī yathā vīra saṅgatā 1 śivakāntayā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O valorous one, accordingly, she joining with Gangs — the spouse of lord Shiva, is also known as Vaivasvati, which removes all the sins.

## \|\| 1.79.77 \|\|

*aśvinau devavaidyatvaṃ labdhavantau yadūttama \|*  
*tayoḥ karmopajīvanti lokesminbhiṣajaḥ sadā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. O foremost of the race of Yadus, Ashvinikumaras became the best physicians of the gods and because of their qualities and virtues, even the physicians of the present time earn their livelihood.

## \|\| 1.79.78 \|\|

*revanto nāma yo'rkasya rūpeṇārkasamaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*2 aśvānāmādhipatye tu yojitaḥ sa tu bhānunā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The Sungod has bestowed the ownership of his horse to his own son Revataka.

## \|\| 1.79.79 \|\|

*kṣemeṇa gacchate'dhvānaṃ yastaṃ pūjayate pathi \|*  
*sukhaprasādyo martyānāṃ sadā yadukulodvaha \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. O son of the Yadu race, a person, who for performing of the safe journey adores him on the way, he provides comfort to him. He therefore completes the journey safely.

## \|\| 1.79.80 \|\|

*tvaṣṭāpi tejasā tena mārtaṇḍasyaiva cājñayā \|*  
*bhojānutpādayāmāsa pūjāyai satya suvrata \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O Suvrata, with the permission of the Sungod, Tvasta created eatables and lustre for him.

## \|\| 1.79.81-82 \|\|

*ya idaṃ janma devasya śṛṇuyādvā paṭheta vā \|*  
*vivasvato hi putrāṇāṃ sarveṣāmamitaujasām \|\| 81 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto yāti sūryasalokatām \|*  
*iha rājā bhavatyeva punaretya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. One who listens or reads the stories of the sons of the Sungod, he getting relieved of all the sins, achieves the abode of the Sungod. After his return to the earth, he surely becomes a king. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 80. Reward for the Sun worship

## \|\| 1.80.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ śrutvā kathāṃ divyāṃ helimāhātmyamāśritām \|*  
*sāmbaḥ papraccha bhūyo'pi nāradaṃ munisattamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — Thus listening to the divine story of the glory of the Sungod, Samba again said to Narada.

## \|\| 1.80.2-3 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*sūryapūjāphalaṃ yacca yacca dānaphalaṃ mahat \|*  
*praṇipāte phalaṃ yacca gītavādye ca yat phalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhāskarasya dvijaśreṣṭha tanme brūhi samantataḥ \|*  
*yena sampūjayāmyeṣa bhānuṃ devaiḥ1 sadārcitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Samba said — O best of the Brahmanas, you kindly speak out to me about the reward of worship of Sun, important charities for him, offering salutations to him or singing and dancing before him, to enable me to worship the adorable Sungod.

## \|\| 1.80.4-5 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*diṇḍinā yaduśārdūla śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sukhāsīnaṃ tathā devaṃ surajyeṣṭhaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā diṇḍiridaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Narada said — The same questions were asked in earlier times by Dindi to lord Brahma and you listen to the answers given by him. You please listen attentively. Once lord Brahma was seated comfortably, then Dandi offering his salutation to the lord, said to him.

## \|\| 1.80.6-8 \|\|

*diṇḍiruvāca \|*  
*sūryapūjāphalaṃ brūhi brūhi dānaphalaṃ tathā \|*  
*praṇāme yatphalaṃ deva yaccoktaṃ tauryakatraye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ kārite śravaṇe tathā \|*  
*purato devadevasya yatphalaṃ syāttaducyatām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mārjane lepane yacca devadevasya mandire \|*  
*bhāskarasya kṛte brūhi mama lokapitāmaha \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Dindi said — O Deva — the grandsire of the world, what is the reward for worshipping the Sungod, offering charities and salutations to him, besides singing and dancing before him? How would the narration of Holy Scriptures before him, besides the cleaning and dusting of his temples be rewarded?

## \|\| 1.80.9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*stutijapyopahāreṇa pūjayā na naro raveḥ \|*  
*upavāsena ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca sarvapāpaḥ pramucyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Brahma said — Eulogizing the Sungod on the sixth moon day, uttering the slogans of his victory, presenting gifts and fasting, a person gets relieved of all the grave sins.

## \|\| 1.80.10 \|\|

*praṇidhāya śiro bhūmau namaskāraparo raveḥ \|*  
*tatkṣaṇātsarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When a salutation is offered to the Sungod on earth, one is at once relieved of all his sins.

## \|\| 1.80.11 \|\|

*bhaktiyukto naro yastu raveḥ kuryātpradakṣiṇām \|*  
*pradakṣiṇī kṛtā tena saptadvīpā 1 bhavenmahī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A person who circumambulates his image or temple, it equates going round the earth seven times.

## \|\| 1.80.12 \|\|

*sūryalokaṃ vrajeccāpi iha rogaiśca mucyate \|*  
*upānahau parityajya anyathā narakaṃ vrajet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A person, who circumambulates bare footed, achieves the abode of the Sungod. A person, who goes round with his shoes on, falls in the hell.

## \|\| 1.80.13 \|\|

*sopānatko naro yastu ārohetsūryamandiram \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoramasipatravanaṃ vibho \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O excellent one, a person who climbs the steps of the temple of the Sungod with his shoes on, he falls in the horrible hell known as Asipatra.

## \|\| 1.80.14 \|\|

*sūryaṃ manasi yaḥ kṛtvā kuryādvyomapradakṣiṇām \|*  
*pradakṣiṇī kṛtāstena sarve devā bhavanti hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Devoting one’s mind towards the Sungod, one who performs circumambulation of the sky, it equates having gone round all the gods.

## \|\| 1.80.15 \|\|

*parituṣṭāśca te sarve prayacchanti gatiṃ śubhām \|*  
*sarve devā mahābāho hyabhīṣṭaṃ tu parantapa \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. O long armed erne, all the gods, then getting pleased with the performer, bestow success to him in all his desires, besides the highest position.

## \|\| 1.80.16 \|\|

*ekāhāro naro bhūtvā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ yo'rcayate ravim \|*  
*saptamyāṃ vā mahābāho sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O valorous one, when a person, consuming food once a day, adores the Sungod on the sixth or seventh moon day, he surely achieves the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.80.17 \|\|

*ahorātropavāsī sa pūjayedyastu bhāskaram \|*  
*saptamyāṃ vātha ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vā sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. While fasting for the day and night, one who adores Bhaskara on the sixth or seventh moon day, he also achieves the best position.

## \|\| 1.80.18-19 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣasya saptamyāṃ sopavāso jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*sarvaraktopahāreṇa pūjayedyastu bhāskaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*paṅkajaiḥ karavīrairvā kuṅkamodakacandanaiḥ \|*  
*modakaiśca gaṇaśreṣṭha sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. One who, with his sense organs under control, observes fast during the dark seventh moon day, offering the red presents, besides the flowers of lotus, oleander, saffron and the sweet balls and sandal paste to the Sungod, he surely achieves the abode of Surya.

## \|\| 1.80.20-22 \|\|

*śuklapakṣasya saptamyāmupavāsarataḥ sadā \|*  
*sarvaśuklopahāreṇa pūjayedyastu bhāskaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

*jātīmudgarakaiścaiva śvetotpalakadambakaiḥ \|*  
*pāyasena 1 tathā devaṃ savajreṇārcayedravim \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā vidhuḥ kāntyā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*haṃsayuktena yānena haṃsalokamavāpnute \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Similarly, on the bright seventh moon day, a person who after fasting offers jasmine, white lotus and kadamba flowers besides payasam and vajra pushpas and worships the Sun, he getting relieved of all the sins, gaining the lustre of the moon, achieves the place of swans, boarding the plane driven by the swans.

## \|\| 1.80.23 \|\|

*diṇḍiruvāca \|*  
*brūhi me vistarāddeva saptamīkalpamuttamam \|*  
*upoṣya saptamīṃ yena gamiṣye śaraṇaṃ raveḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Dindi said — O Deva, you kindly explain in detail about the process of fasting on the seventh moon day to enable me to take refuge with the Sungod, after fasting.

## \|\| 1.80.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhavatā saptamīkalpamuttamam \|*  
*yathā sahasrakiraṇaḥ purā pṛṣṭo'ruṇena vai \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Brahma said — By breaching the subject of Saptami-kalpa, you have put up an excellent question, which had earlier been asked by Aruna.

## \|\| 1.80.25 \|\|

*kathitāḥ sapta saptamyo bhānunā śreyase nṛṇām \|*  
*aruṇasya gaṇaśreṣṭha pṛcchataḥ kāraṇāntare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O best of the attendants, the Sungod, for the benefit of the people, at the instance of Aruna, had explained the method for the performing of all the Saptamis.

## \|\| 1.80.26 \|\|

*kasyacittvatha kālasya devadevaṃ divākaram \|*  
*dhyānamāśritya tiṣṭhantamaruṇo vākyamabravīt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Once Aruna, finding Surya — the god of all gods, seated in meditation, asked him.

## \|\| 1.80.27 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ devadevaśa dhyānamāśritya tiṣṭhasi \|*  
*dinaṃ na yāti deveśa kāraṇaṃ mama kathyatām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord of gods — “What for are you engaged in meditation. Why are the days not passing. You kindly speak out the reason for the same.” When so asked by Dindi, lord Surya said.

## \|\| 1.80.28 \|\|

*kuru caṅkramaṇaṃ deva vahamāno divaspate \|*  
*ityevaṃ bhagavānpṛṣṭa idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Deva, O lord of the day “Now you also make a move as well.” When thus asked by him, the Sungod said.

## \|\| 1.80.29-30 \|\|

*śṛṇu tvaṃ dvijaśārdūla yadarthaṃ dhyānamāśritaḥ \|*  
*arvāvasurdvijaśreṣṭhaḥ sa cāputraḥ khagottama \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ārādhayati māṃ nityaṃ gandhapuṣpopahārakaiḥ \|*  
*putrakāmaḥ khagaśreṣṭha na ca jānātyayaṃ yathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. O lion among the Brahmanas, I am going to tell you the purpose for which I am meditating. You please listen. Ю best of birds, there is a Brahmana named Arvavasu, who has no son. Therefore, he appropriately adores me with the desire of a son, with fragrance and garlands, regularly. But O best of birds, but he is unaware of the method by using which I would be able to grant him the desired boon.

## \|\| 1.80.31 \|\|

*putrado'haṃ bhave yena vidhinā pūjitaḥ khaga \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ ca vidhiḥ sarve yena prīto bhave nṛṇām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O bird, therefore, I am speaking out the method following which, I get pleased over the humans. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.80.32 \|\|

*saptamīkalpasaṃjño vai vidhīnāmuttamo vidhiḥ \|*  
*yastu māṃ pūjayennityaṃ tasya putrāndadāmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Of all the methods the one of Saptami-kalpa has been stated to be the best. A person who adores me making use of the same, I surely bestow a son on him.

## \|\| 1.80.33 \|\|

*gṛhṇīṣva saptamīkalpaṃ gatvā brūhi dvijottamam \|*  
*yenāhaṃ bahuputratvaṃ dadyāṃ tasya tathā khaga \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. You go to that place with the knowledge of Saptami-kalpa and reveal the same to the said Brahmana, to enable me to bestow sons on him.”

## \|\| 1.80.34-35 \|\|

*śrutvā bhānoḥ kṣaṇādeva jagāma sa khagottamaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ bhānorvacanamāditaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇasya khagaśreṣṭha sa ca śrutvā dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*cakāra saptamīkalpaṃ yathākhyātaṃ khagena tu \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. On hearing this, Arana — the best of birds, then proceeded on to that place. Reaching their he apprised the Brahmana of the entire talk he had with the Sungod. Then the Brahmana performed the Saptami-kalpa, as per the advice of the Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.80.36 \|\|

*ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathārogyaṃ prāpya putrāṃśca puṣkalān \|*  
*gato'sau sūryalokaṃ ca tejasā tatsamobhavat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thereafter, the Brahmana achieving several sons viz., Riddhi, Buddhi, Arogya and others, ultimately proceeded on to the abode of the Sungod.

## Chapter 81. Description of Vijaya Saptami

## \|\| 1.81.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jayā ca vijayā caiva jayantī cāparājitā \|*  
*mahājavā ca nandā ca bhadrā cānyā prakīrtitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — The seven Saptamis are known by the names of Jaya, Vijaya, Jayanti, Aparajita, Mahajaya, Nanda and Bhadra.

## \|\| 1.81.2 \|\|

*śuklapakṣasya saptamyāṃ sūryavāro bhavedyadi \|*  
*saptamī vijayā nāma tatra dattaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On the Saptami of the bright fortnight when it falls on Sunday, it is known as Vijaya — Saptami during which the charities given are multiplied many times.

## \|\| 1.81.3 \|\|

*snānaṃ dāna tathā homaṃ upavāsastathaiva ca \|*  
*sarvaṃ vijayasaptamyāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The homas, charities, bathing and fasting performed during the Vijaya-Saptami are several times productive in reward, besides washing out of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.81.4 \|\|

*pañcamyāmekabhaktaṃ syātpaṣṭhyāṃ naktaṃ pracakṣate \|*  
*upavāsastu saptamyāmaṣṭamyāṃ pāraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. During the fifth moon day, one should take food once in a day and should perform Nakta-vrata on the sixth moon day. Then tasting should be carried out on the seventh moon day, while on the eighth moon day the fast should be broken.

## \|\| 1.81.5-6 \|\|

*keciddevamuśantyeva neti cānye gaṇādhipa \|*  
*abhipretastu me 1 ṣaṣṭhyāmupavāso gaṇottama \|\| 5 \|\|*

*caturthyāmekabhaktaṃ tu pañcamyāṃ naktamādiśet \|*  
*upavāsastu ṣaṣṭhyāṃ syātsaptamyāṃ pāraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O foremost of the attendants, some people adore the god in a similar manner. But some people accept the adoration, while offering prayers at the same time. O best of the attendants, the person doing fasting should take food on the fourth moon day only once, observe night fasting on the night of the fifth moon day. Then he should fast on the sixth moon day and then break the fast on the seventh moon day.

## \|\| 1.81.7 \|\|

*upavāsaparaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāmabdeśaṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*gandhapuṣpopahāraiśca bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then with utmost faith and devotion observing the fast, he should worship the Sungod on the sixth moon day with fragrance as well as the garlands.

## \|\| 1.81.8-10 \|\|

*prakalpya pūjāṃ bhūmau tu devasya purataḥ svapet \|*  
*japamānastu2 gāyatrīṃ saurasūktamathāpi vā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*akṣaraṃ vā mahāśvetaṃ ṣaḍakṣaramathāpi vā \|*  
*vibuddhastvatha saptamyāṃ kṛtvā snānaṃ gaṇādhipa \|\| 9 \|\|*

*graheśaṃ pūjayitvā tu homaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayedbhaktyā śaktyā ca gaṇanāyaka \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. O foremost of the attendants, after performing the puja, one should sit before the god and should recite the Gayatri hymns or the Surya-sukta, Mahashveta or the six letters manta, and should sleep on the ground. Then waking in the morning of the seventh moon day and after taking his bath, he should worship the Sungod appropriately besides performing homa. Then he should feed the Brahmanas as per his means.

## \|\| 1.81.11 \|\|

*śālyodanamapūpāśca khaṇḍaveṣṭāṃśca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*saghṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ dadyāttathā vipreṣu śaktitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then using Shati rice, fried cakes, sugar mixed with other eatables, payasam mixed with ghi, should be offered to the Brahmana as per one’s means.

## \|\| 1.81.12-14 \|\|

*dattvā ca dakṣiṇā bhaktyā 1 tato viprānvisarjayet \|*  
*ityeṣā kathitā deva puṇyā vijayasaptamī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yāmupoṣya naro gacchetpadaṃ vairocanaṃ param \|*  
*karavīrāṇi raktāni kuṅkumaṃ ca vilepanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vijayaṃ dhūpamasyāṃ tu bhānostuṣṭikarāṇi vai \|*  
*eṣā puṇyā pāpaharā mahāpātakanāśinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Again giving the dakshina as per one’s means, the devotee should send off the Brahmana. Accordingly, I have described the auspicious form of Saptami. By fasting during this Saptami, a devotee surely achieves the place of the Sungod. In the worship of the Sungod, the red oleander flowers, saffron pate and Vijaya incense, when offered, then it delights the Sungod. Thus this auspicious Saptami, which removes all the sins as well as the grave sins, has been described as such.

## \|\| 1.81.15 \|\|

*atra dattaṃ hutaṃ cāpi kṣīyate na gaṇādhipa \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ tathā homaḥ pitṛdevābhipūjanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The charities given and the homas performed during the Saptami never get destroyed. Similarly, the bathing, charities, offerings made to the manes and the gods, also do not get destroyed.

## \|\| 1.81.16 \|\|

*sarvaṃ vijayasaptamyāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*ādityavāreṇa yutā smṛtā vijayasaptamī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This Saptami has been described as the destroyer of grave sins. In case this Saptami falls on Sunday, it is called as Vijaya.

## \|\| 1.81.17-18 \|\|

*ityeṣā kathitā vīra sarvakāmapradāyinī \|*  
*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ kīrtitaṃ śravaṇaṃ tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*smaraṇaṃ tu tathāsyāṃ tu puṇyadaṃ tripurāntaka \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. O great warrior, thus the day of Saptami has been defined in detail. O destroyer of Tripura, to listen to this even, or to recite it or to remember it always bestow grace, glory, long life and great merits.

## Chapter 82. Nanda-vidhi explained

## \|\| 1.82.1 \|\|

*nakṣatradarśanānnaktaṃ kecidicchanti mānada \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Dindi said — O Brahman, those who perform puja for the Sungod on Sundays, besides bathing, giving of charities, etc. what type of reward do they achieve? You kindly tell me.

## \|\| 1.82.2 \|\|

*puṇyā sā saptamī proktā yuktā tena pitāmaha \|*  
*vijayeti tathā nāma varṇyatāmasya 1 puṇyatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O grandsire, in case the particular Saptami have been described as the auspicious one, then you please tell me about its importance as well.

## \|\| 1.82.3 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ye tvādityadine brahmañchrāddhaṃ2 kurvanti mānavāḥ \|*  
*saptajanmasu te jātāḥ sambhavanti virogiṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Brahma said — O Brahman, a person, who performs the Shraddha on Sunday, he does not attract any ailment in the next seven births.

## \|\| 1.82.4-11 \|\|

*naktaṃ kurvanti ye tatra mānavāḥ sthairyamāśritāḥ \|*  
*japamānā paraṃ jāpyamādityahadayaṃ param \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ārogyamiha vai prāpya sūryalokaṃ vrajanti te \|*  
*upavāsaṃ ca ye kuryurādityasya dine sadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*japanti ca mahāśvetāṃ te labhante yathepsitam \|*  
*ahorātreṇa naktena trirātraniyamena vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*japamāno mahāśvetāmīpsitaṃ labhate phalam \|*  
*viśeṣataḥ sūryadine japamāno gaṇādhipa \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṣaḍakṣaraṃ3 tathā śvetāṃ gacchedvairocanaṃ padam \|*  
*dvādaśeha smṛtā vārā ādityasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nando bhadrastathā saumyaḥ kāmadaḥ putradastathā \|*  
*jayo jayanto vijaya ādityābhimukha sthitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*hṛdayo rogahā caiva mahāśvetapriyo'paraḥ \|*  
*śuklapakṣasya ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu māghe māsi gaṇādhipa \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yaḥ4 kuryātsa bhavedbhūpaḥ sarvapāpabhayāpahaḥ \|*  
*atra naktaṃ smṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ ghṛtena snapanaṃ raveḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

4-11. A person, with a stable mind, if recites the excellent Aditya-hridaya stotra, fasting during the night, he remains healthy and finally achieves the place of Surya. A person who lasting on Sundays regularly, performs japam for Mahashveta, all his desires are fulfilled. Accordingly, performing vrata for the day and night and performing Nanda-vrata, one who continuously for three nights performs japam for Mahashveta, he has his desire fulfilled. O foremost of the ganas, by performing the six letter or Mahashveta-japam one achieves the place of the Sungod. As twelve days have been earmarked for the Sun, similarly, their names have been given as Nanda, Bhadra, Saumya, Kamada, Putrada, Jaya, Vijaya, Adityabhimukha, Hridaya, Rogaha and Mahashvetapriya. O leader of the attendants, one who performs vrata on the sixth moon day of the bright fortnight of the month of the month of Margashirsha, he becomes a ruler and all his sins vanish. Therefore, fasting on that night, ghi should be offered to the Sungod for his bath.

## \|\| 1.82.12 \|\|

*agastyakusumānīha bhānostuṣṭikarāṇi tu \|*  
*vilepanaṃ sugandhastu śvetacandanamuttamam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Agastya flowers are favourite with the Sungod. After offering these flowers, fragrant paste, white sandal paste, incense of guggulu, fried cakes and other eatables should also be offered.

## \|\| 1.82.13 \|\|

*dhūpastu guggulaḥ śreṣṭho naivedyaṃ pūpameva hi \|*  
*dattvā pūpaṃ tu viprasya tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The fried cakes should also be offered to the Sungod first and then to the Brahmanas. Thereafter, he himself should eat the same, keeping silent.

## \|\| 1.82.14-16 \|\|

*muhūrtonaṃ dinaṃ kecitpravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nakṣatradarśanānnaktamahammanye gaṇādhipa \|*  
*prasthamātraṃ bhavetpūpaṃ godhūmamayamuttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yavodbhavaṃ vā kurvīta saguḍaṃ sarpiṣānvitam \|*  
*sahiraṇyaṃ ca dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇe setihāsake 2 \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Some people believe that while fasting during the night, the food should be taken after viewing the star or the constellation, while some people believe that when only a muhurta of the day is left, one can take food in the case of night fasting. O leader of attendants, I believe that the night-fasting could be performed after viewing the star. Accordingly, the fried cakes should be made out of a measure (nearly one kilogram) of wheat flour. In the absence of wheat flour, the flour of barley could be used mixing the sugarcane balls and ghi in it. Thereafter, in gold vase, it should be given to a Brahmana who is well-versed in Puranas and history.

## \|\| 1.82.17-20 \|\|

*bhaume divye'tha vā deyaṃ nyasedvā purato raveḥ \|*  
*dātavyo mantrataścāyaṃ maṇḍako3 grāhya eva hi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhūtvādityena vai bhaktyā ādityaṃ tu namasya ca \|*  
*ādityatejasotpannaṃ rājñīkaravinirmitam \|*  
*śreyase mama vipra tvaṃ pratīcchāpūpamuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kāmadaṃ sukhadaṃ dharmyaṃ dhanadaṃ putradaṃ tathā \|*  
*sadāstu te pratīcchāmi maṇḍakaṃ bhāskarapripam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*etau caiva mahāmantrau dānādāne ravipriyau \|*  
*apūpasya gaṇaśreṣṭha śreyase nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. It should be placed in an earthen pot or in any other metal pot, and should be handed over to a Brahmana, reciting the mantras. The Brahmana should also recite Kamada-sukhadam mantra and should receive the pot in his hands. He should at once return to the performer. For offering fried cakes to the Sungod, these mantras are quite dear to the Sungod. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.82.21 \|\|

*eṣa nandavidhiḥ prokto narāṇāṃ śreyase vibho \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu naraḥ4 pūjayate ravim \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Similarly, for the human welfare, I have described the Nanda-vidhi. A person, who worship the Sungod according to this method, they getting relieved of all the sins, are honoured in the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.82.22 \|\|

*na daridraṃ na rogaśca kule tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*yo'nena pūjayedbhānuṃ na kṣayaḥ santatestathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On the other hand, the concerned noble person does not attract disease or poverty in his family. Similarly, the person who thus performs, does not have lose of his progeny.

## \|\| 1.82.23 \|\|

*sūryalokāccyutaścāsau rājā bhavati bhūtale \|*  
*bahuratnasamāyukta6 stejasā dvijasannibhaḥ7 \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On his fall from the place of Sungod on earth, he becomes a powerful king possessing enormous riches and gems.

## \|\| 1.82.24 \|\|

*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ cedaṃ vidhānaṃ tripurāntaka \|*  
*kaṃ 1 dadātyacalaṃ divyamambujāmacalāṃ tathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O killer of Tripura, a person who properly listens or recites this process, he achieves immovable property as well as the riches (gems).

## Chapter 83. Bhadra-vidhi described

## \|\| 1.83.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*māsi bhādrapade vīra śukte pakṣe tu yo bhavet \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ gaṇakulaśreṣṭha sa bhadraḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — O valorous one, O gana of excellent race, the sixth bright moon day of the month of Bhadrapada when falls on Sunday, then it is known as Bhadra.

## \|\| 1.83.2 \|\|

*tatra naktaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādupavāsamathāpi vā \|*  
*haṃsayānasamārūḍho yāti haṃsasalokatām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. During this particular sixth moon day, when a person performs the fasting during night, he achieves a vehicle in which the swans are yoked, and reaches the abode of Hamsa or the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.83.3-8 \|\|

*mālatīkusumānīha tathā śvetaṃ ca candanam \|*  
*vijayaṃ ca tathā dhūpaṃ naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ param \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūjāyāṃ bhāskarasyeha kuryāttripurasūdanam \|*  
*itthaṃ sampūjya deveśaṃ madhyāhne ca dinādhipam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dattvā tu dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*pāyasaṃ gaṇaśārdūla saguḍaṃ sarpiṣā saha \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ya evaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā mānavastimirāpaham \|*  
*sarvakāmānavāpnoti putradāradhanādikān \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo vrajadbhānusalokatām \|*  
*eṣa bhadrā vidhiḥ prokto mayā yaste gaṇādhipa \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śrutvā kṛtvā ca yatpāpānmucyate mānavo bhuvi \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. O enemy of Tripura, the worship should include the offerings of flowers, sandalpaste, vijaya incense, eatables besides the payasam. Thus during the mid day, the Sungod should also be worshipped and offering dakshina to the Brahmanas, as per one’s means, the devotee should take food keeping silent. O lion among the attendants, a person, who after consuming payasam with sugarcane cakes, adores the Sungod — the remover of darkness, he has all his desires fulfilled, including the sons, wife, and riches etc. He, after having been relieved of all the sins, achieves the Salokya-moksha of the Sungod. O foremost of the attendants, thus I have explained the Bhadra method. On hearing Bhadra on earth, or performing the said vrata, the people are relieved of all the sins and shall do so even in future.

## Chapter 84. Saumya method described

## \|\| 1.84.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nakṣatraṃ rohiṇī vīra yadā vāre'sya vai bhavet \|*  
*yātyasau saumyatāṃ vīra1 sa saumyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — In case the constellation of Rohini also falls on the same day, then it is known as Saumya.

## \|\| 1.84.2 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevāditarpaṇam \|*  
*akṣayaṃ syānna sandehastvatra vāre mahātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. By taking bath, performing charities, japam, homos and offering oblations to the manes on this auspicious day, the performer attains everlasting merits.

## \|\| 1.84.3 \|\|

*naktaṃ samāśrito yo'tra pūjayedbhāskaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yāti lokaṃ sa devasya bhāskarasya na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The people, who performing the night fast and observing all the rules, adore the Sungod, he achieves the abode of Surya.

## \|\| 1.84.4 \|\|

*raktotpalāni vai tatra tathā raktaṃ ca candanam \|*  
*sugandhaścāpi dhūpastu naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ tathā \|*  
*brāhmaṇāya ca dātavyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ cātmanā tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Therefore, while performing puja on that particular day, offering red lotus flowers, red sandal paste, fragrance, incense, eatables and payasam, initially to the Brahmanas and then to the Sungod and then he should consume food himself.

## \|\| 1.84.5 \|\|

*ya evaṃ pūjayetsaumye citrabhānuṃ gavāmpatim \|*  
*sa vimuktastu pāpebhyastvāṣṭrīṃ kāntimavāpnuyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Sungod is adored with his gentle rays on that particular day. A person who does so, he achieves the Sungod, getting relieved of all the sins, besides the lustre of the Sun.

## Chapter 85. Kamada method described

## \|\| 1.85.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*prāpte mārgaśire māsi śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu yo bhavet \|*  
*sa jñeyaḥ kāmado vāraḥ sadeṣṭo bhāskarasya tu \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra yaḥ pūjayedbhānuṃ bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vimuktaḥ sarvapāpaistu prāpnute nandanādhipam1 \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Brahma said — The bright sixth moon day of the month of Margashirsha, when it falls on Sunday, is known as Kamada and it is quite favourite with the Sungod. A devotee, getting filled with devotion, when adores the Sungod on that particular day, he getting relieved of all the sins, gains the lordship of the Nandana-vana.

## \|\| 1.85.3-5 \|\|

*raktacandanamiśrāṇi karavīrāṇi suvrata \|*  
*dhūpaṃ ghṛtāhutiṃ vīra bhāskarasya prayojayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*naivedyaṃ cāpi kṛśaraṃ sugandhaṃ tīkṣṇameva ca \|*  
*kṛtvopavāsamatha vā naktaṃ tripurasūdana \|\| 4 \|\|*

*itthaṃ prapūjito hyatra bhāskaro lokabhāskaraḥ \|*  
*kāmāndadāti sarvānvai atoyaṃ kāmadaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. In performing this vrata, the red sandal paste, oleander flowers, incense and offerings are given to the Sungod. O valorous one, in the eatables, the mixture of cooked rice and pulse is included. The strong fragrance is also offered, which is said to be necessary. O killer of Tripura, while fasting or performing the night fast, the aforesaid articles should be offered with great respect, because, in case the Sungod who spread light in the world, gets pleased, he fulfills all the desires. And therefore, it is called Kamada.

## \|\| 1.85.6 \|\|

*sa putra putrakāmasya dhanakāmasya vā dhanam \|*  
*vidyārthine śubhāṃ vidyāmārogyaṃ rogiṇe vibho \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This particular vrata bestows son to the seeker of a son, wealth to a person who desires wealth, knowledge to a student, while the patient suffering from a disease is relieved of the ailment.

## \|\| 1.85.7 \|\|

*anyāṃśca vividhānkāmānmantraiḥ sampūjito raviḥ \|*  
*dadāti gaṇaśārdūla atoyaṃ kāmadaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lion among the attendants, on that particular date, the Sungod, getting worshipped with the reciting of the mantras, bestows all the boons desired by the devotee. Because of that, it is known as Kamada.

## \|\| 1.85.8 \|\|

*dadyādyo maṇḍakaṃ cātra gopatergotrabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*gotrāritejasā3 tulyo gopatergopuraṃ vrajet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whosoever offers for the Sungod, mandala and fried cakes, he, becoming illustrious like Indra, attains the abode of the Sungod.

## Chapter 86. Jayavara-tithi described

## \|\| 1.86.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*pañcatāraṃ bhavedyatra nakṣatraṃ te vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*vāre tu devadevasya sa vāraḥ putradaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — O bull-bannered one, when the start constellation appears five times a day, it is known as Putradaka (bestower of a son) day.

## \|\| 1.86.2 \|\|

*upavāso bhavettatra śrāddhaṃ kāryaṃ tathā bhavet \|*  
*prāśanaṃ cāpi piṇḍasya madhyamasya prakīrtitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On that particular day, one should perform fasting Shraddha and consuming of the centre of a pinda.

## \|\| 1.86.3-6 \|\|

*sopavāsastu yo bhaktyā pūjayedatra gopatim \|*  
*dhūpamālyopahāraistu divyagandhasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*evaṃ pūjya vivasvantaṃ tasyaiva purato niśi \|*  
*bhūmau svapiti vai vīra japañchvetāṃ mahāmate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prātarutthāya ca snānaṃ kṛtvā dattvārghyamuttamam \|*  
*raktacandanasammiśraiḥ karavīrairgaṇādhipa \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prapūjya grahabhūteśamaṃśumantaṃ trilocana \|*  
*vīraṃ 1 ca pūjayitvā tu tataḥ śrāddhaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. O intelligent one, thus by fasting and offering incense, garland, divine fragrance and other gifts to the Sungod, the devotee should bow down over the ground before him. Then reciting Mahashveta japam, he should sleep and in the morning taking early morning bath, he should offer arghya with red sandal paste and the oleander flowers. Then one should worship the lord of planets, besides the lamp. The Shraddha should be started thereafter.

## \|\| 1.86.7 \|\|

*pañcabhirbrāhmaṇairdeva divyaibhomaiśca2 suvrata \|*  
*magasaṃjñau3 tatra divyau brāhmaṇau parikalpayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Performing the Shraddha, five divine Bhauma Brahmanas should be invited, in which two of them should represent Surya and three Brahmanas should represent Bhauma (Mars).

## \|\| 1.86.8 \|\|

*trīnatra brāhmaṇānbhīmānprakalpyāndhakasūdana \|*  
*kuryādevaṃ tataḥ śrāddhaṃ pārvaṇaṃ bhāskarapriyam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O three-eyed one, O destroyer of Andhaka, this type of the performance is liked by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.86.9-14 \|\|

*śrāddhe tvatha samāpte tu dadyātpiṇḍaṃ tu madhyamam \|*  
*purato devadevasya sthitvā mantreṇa suvrata \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sa eṣa piṇḍo deveśa yo'bhīṣṭastava sarvadā \|*  
*aśnāmi paśyate tubhyaṃ tena me santatirbhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*prasādāttava deveśa iti me bhāvitaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*itthaṃ sampūjito hyatra bhāskaraḥ putrado bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ato'yaṃ putrado vāro devasya parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*evamatra sadā yastu bhāskaraṃ pūjayennaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*upavāsaparaḥ śrāddhe sa putraṃ labhate dhruvam \|*  
*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca ārogyaṃ sukhadaṃ tathā \|*  
*sūryalokaṃ ca samprāpya tato rājā bhavennṛṣu \|\| 13 \|\|*

*prabhayā dvijasaṃkāśaḥ kāntyā cāmbujasannibhaḥ \|*  
*vīryeṇa gopatestulyo gāmbhīrye sāgaropamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. At the close of the Shraddha the middle pinda should be placed before the Sungod reciting the mantra and should pray — “O lord of gods, this is the favourite pinda of yours, which is being eaten by me in your presence and by so doing, by your grace, I would surely have a son. This is the belief developing in my heart.” Thus by performing the worship appropriately, the Sungod surely bestow a son. Because of this, the vrata has been given the title of Putrada. In this way, a person who after fasting appropriately, adores the Sungod on that particular day, he surely achieves besides the son and riches, cereals, gold, comforts and the healthy life. Ultimately, he reaches the abode of Surya and falling from there, he becomes a king, having the resplendence of the moon and beauty like the lotus, prowess resembling the sun and the depth of the ocean.

## \|\| 1.86.15-17 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dakṣiṇe tvayane yaḥ syātsa jayaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*atropavāso naktaṃ ca snānaṃ dānaṃ japastathā \|*  
*bhavecchataguṇaṃ deva bhāskaraprītaye kṛtam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmānnaktādi kartavyaṃ yatsyācchataguṇaṃ vibho \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Brahma said — On Sunday, which falls on the Sun morning in Dakshinayana, the japam as already pointed out should be performed. When the fasting, night vrata, bathing, charities and japam are performed on that particular day in order to please the Sungod, the related merit is multiplied to a hundred times. Therefore, the night vrata etc. should be performed for the pleasure of the Sungod, because the related merit in such cases are also multiplied to a hundred times.

## Chapter 87. Method of Jayanta described

## \|\| 1.87.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jayanto hyuttare jñeyaścāyane gaṇanāyaka \|*  
*vāro devasya yaḥ syādvai tatra pūjyo divākaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — O leader of the Ganas, when the Surya is on the Uttarayana and a Sunday falls during this time, then it is known as Jayanta. On this particular Sunday, the Sungod must be adored.

## \|\| 1.87.2-3 \|\|

*pūjitastatra deveśaḥ sahasraguṇitaṃ phalam \|*  
*dadāti devaśārdūla snānadānādikarmaṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ghṛtena payasā yatra snānamikṣurasena tu \|*  
*vilepanaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tu praśastaṃ bhāskare priyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. When it is so done, the relative merit is multiplied a thousand times. The image of Sun should be bathed in ghi, milk and sugarcane juice. Then the saffron should be applied over the same, which is liked by the lord.

## \|\| 1.87.4 \|\|

*dhūpakriyā guggulena naivedye modakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*itthaṃ sampūjya deveśaṃ kuryāddhomaṃ tatastilaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayetpaścānmodakāṃstilaśaṣkulīḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Guggulu should be used for incense, while the sweet balls should be used for naivedya or eatable. Thus after worshipping the Sungod, homa should be performed and fried cakes made in sesamum seeds should be served as food to the Brahmanas. This has been prescribed.

## \|\| 1.87.5-6 \|\|

*itthaṃ yaḥ pūjayedbhānuṃ mantreṇaiva gaṇādhipa \|*  
*sahasraguṇitaṃ tasya phalaṃ devo dadāti vai \|\| 5 \|\|*

*snānadānajapādīnāmupavāsasya vai vibho \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O foremost of the ganas, the people who perform the worship of the Sungod is this way with the mantras, they earn a thousand times more reward for their bathing, giving of charities, performing of japam, etc. besides the fasting.

## Chapter 88. Vijayavara-vidhi described

## \|\| 1.88.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śuklapakṣasya saptamyāṃ prājāpatyarkṣasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sa jñeyo vijayo nāma sarvapāpabhayāpahaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — In case the bright seventh moon day falls on Sunday in the Rohini constellation, it turns as the destroyer of all the sins and is known as Vijaya-Sunday.

## \|\| 1.88.2 \|\|

*tatra koṭiguṇaṃ sarvaphalaṃ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ \|*  
*dadāti bhagavāndevaḥ pūjitaścandanādhipaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Because the Sungod who likes the sandal paste, rewards all the meritorious deeds a crore of times on that particular day.

## \|\| 1.88.3-4 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevādipūjanam \|*  
*naktaṃ cāpyupavāsastu sarvamatra divākaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kuryātkoṭiguṇaṃ sarvaṃ pūjito hyatra gopatiḥ \|*  
*tasmādatra sadā devaṃ pūjayedbhaktimānnaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. In case one takes a bath on that day and gives charities, performs japam or homa, adores the gods or the manes, besides fasting during the night or the day, he derives a crore of times merits for the same. Therefore, a person should adore the Sungod with devotion.

## \|\| 1.88.5-6 \|\|

*sarveśaṃ saptadvīpeśaṃ saptasaindhavavāhanam \|*  
*saptamyāṃ tu samārādhya saptaprakṛtisambhavam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saptalokādhipatyaṃ tu prāpnute saptaraśmibhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Thus the Sungod — the lord of the universe, using the chariot driven by seven horses is worshipped on the seventh moon day, and by which the performer achieves the sovereignty of the seven lokas.

## Chapter 89. Aditya-vidhi described

## \|\| 1.89.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣasya saptamyāṃ māghamāse bhavettu yaḥ \|*  
*sādityābhimukho1 jñeyaḥ śṛṇu cāsya vidhiṃ param \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — The dark seventh moon day of the month of Margashirsha when falls on Sunday, it is known as Adityabhimukha day. I am revealing its excellent method. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.89.2-3 \|\|

*prātaḥ kṛtvā tataḥ snānaṃ pūjayitvā divākaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ādityābhimukhastiṣṭhedyāvadastamanaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*japamāno mahāśvetāṃ lābhamāśritya suvrata \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. O killer of Tripura, on the first day one should take food once only. On that particular Sunday, one should take a bath early in the morning and worship the Sungod. Then the devotee should keep on standing facing the Sun, reciting the Mahashveta-stotra.

## \|\| 1.89.4 \|\|

*caturhastamṛjaṃ ślakṣṇamavraṇaṃ susamaṃ dṛḍham \|*  
*raktacandanavṛkṣasya stambhaṃ kṛtvā gaṇādhipa \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O lord of the ganas, a column of the red sandal wood should be made, which should have the length of four hands, slippery, without defects, besides being solid.

## \|\| 1.89.5-6 \|\|

*tamāśritya mahābhaktyā devadevaṃ divākaram \|*  
*paśyamāno japañśvetāṃ tiṣṭhedastamanādraveḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gandhapuṣpopahāraistu pūjayitvā divākaram \|*  
*brāhmaṇe dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Surya — the leader of the Devas, should be consecrated over it. The devotee should recite Shveta-stotra fixing his mind over it He should stand before the columns from the sunrise to sunset. Thereafter, worshipping the Sungod with fragrant flowers, he should then serve food to the Brahmanas, giving dakshina at the same time. This has been prescribed.

## \|\| 1.89.7 \|\|

*itthametaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādādityaprītaye naraḥ \|*  
*bhānumāṃstasya prītaḥ syātsarvaṃ prīto dadādi hi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. For the delight of the Sungod a person who performs accordingly, the Sungod getting pleased, bestows enormous objects to him, including riches, son, good health, cereals, land and glory.

## \|\| 1.89.8 \|\|

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā putramārogyaṃ bhārgavo yaśaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsampūjayedatra gīrvāṇādhipatiṃ hara \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Therefore, the Sungod, who is the leader of all the Devas, should be surely worshipped.

## Chapter 90. Hridayavara-vidhi described

## \|\| 1.90.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ravisaṅkramaṇe yaḥ syādravervāro gaṇādhipa \|*  
*sa jñeyo hṛdayo nāma ādityahadayapriyaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — O leader of the ganas, the arrival of the Sun to another zodiac sign when falls on a Sunday, is quite dear to him. It has therefore been conceived as hridaya.

## \|\| 1.90.2-3 \|\|

*tatra naktaṃ samāśritya devaṃ sampūjya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*gatvā ca sadane bhānorādityābhimukhasthitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*japedādityahadayaṃ saṅkhyayāṣṭaśataṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*atha vāstamanaṃ yāvadbhāskaraṃ ciṃtayeddhṛdi \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Therefore, on that particular day, observing the night fast, the Sungod should be worshipped with devotion in a Sun temple and one should recite the Aditya-hridaya stotra eight hundred times upto the evenings, devoting his mind to the Sun.

## \|\| 1.90.4 \|\|

*gṛhametya tato viprānbhojayecchaktitaḥ śiva \|*  
*bhuktvā tu pāyasaṃ vīra tato bhūmau svapedbudhaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O Shiva, then after performing homa, the devotee should feed the Brahmanas as per his means and himself consuming the payasam, should sleep on the ground.

## \|\| 1.90.5 \|\|

*yo'tra sampūyedbhānuṃ bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa kāmāṃllabhate sarvānbhāskarāddhṛdayasthitān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A person who adores the Sungod with utmost devotion and faith, the lord fulfills all his earth’s desires.

## \|\| 1.90.6 \|\|

*tejasā yaśasā tulyaḥ prabhayaiṣāṃ mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*śakragopāṇḍajānāṃ tu gopatergovṛṣekṣaṇa \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Such a devotee achieves the glory and lustre similar to Indra, the cowherd, Brahma and the Sun.

## Chapter 91. Method for the removal of ailment

## \|\| 1.91.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*pūṣṇo bhavedyadā ṛkṣaṃ bhavecca bhagadaivatam \|*  
*vāsaraḥ sa mahānproktaḥ sarvarogabhayāpahaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — When Purva-Phalguni constellation falls on a Sunday, it is said to be the remover of all the diseases.

## \|\| 1.91.2 \|\|

*yo'tra pūjayate bhānuṃ śubhagandhavilepanaiḥ \|*  
*sarvarogavinirmukto yāti bhānusalokatām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A person who on that particular day, worships the Sungod with fragrance and paste, he is relieved of all the ailments. He also achieves the Salokya devotion of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.91.3-6 \|\|

*arkapatrapuṭe kṛtyā puṣpāṇyarkasya suvrata \|*  
*devasya purato rātrau bhaktyā yaḥ sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sa muktaḥ sarvarogaistu3 gaccheddinakarālayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhaktyā ca pāyasaṃ vīra rātrau svapiti bhūtale \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu pūjayedatra vai ravim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasmādapi vrajellokaṃ phuṃkāraravahetinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. O excellent one, the flowers of swallow-wort should be collected with its leaves and placed with utmost devotion before the Sungod during the night. Since the flowers of swallow-wort are quite favourite of the Sungod, they should be offered to him. Thereafter, eatables should be offered to him. Thereafter, the food should be served to the Brahmanas and thereafter, he himself should consume the payasam. Then he should sleep on the ground at night. A person who adores the Sungod as per the above method, he, getting relieved of all the ailments, achieves the place of the Sungod. Thereafter, he achieves Indraloka where the vajra issues the hissing sound.

## Chapter 92. Method of Mahashveta

## \|\| 1.92.1 \|\|

*pūjayitvā mahāśvetāṃ raviṃ devaṃ samarcayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — On the day of a solar eclipse Ming on a Sunday, it is known as Mahashveta day, which is decorated with the Sun rays, and is quite dear to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.92.2 \|\|

*yastu pūjayate tasminpataṅgaṃ patagapriyam \|*  
*gandhapuṣpopahāraistu sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Therefore, on that particular day, if a person worships the Sungod — the favourite of a bird (Arupa), offering fragrance and flower garlands, he achieves the place of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.92.3-4 \|\|

*sopavāso gaṇaśreṣṭha ādityagrahaṇe śuciḥ \|*  
*japamāno mahāśvetāṃ khapoṣamatha vā śivam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūjayejjagatāmīśaṃ tamonāśanamāśugam \|*  
*pūjayitvā khapoṣaṃ tu mahāśvetāṃ tato japet \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. O leader of ganas, in this way, getting purified on the day of the solar eclipse, while fasting, a person should recite the mantra of Mahashveta or Shiva and also worship the Sungod who removes darkness.

## \|\| 1.92.5 \|\|

*mahāśvetāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya gandhapuṣpaiḥ supūjitām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is because the worship of Surya has been prescribed with Mahashveta with fragrant flowers.

## \|\| 1.92.6-10 \|\|

*tasyā eva bahiḥ2 kāryaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*śucau bhūmivibhāge tu vīraṃ saṃsthāpya yatnataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kuryāddhomaṃ tilaiḥ snātaḥ sarpiṣā ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ādityagrahavelāyāṃ japeñchvetāṃ mahāmate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mukte dinakare paścātsnānaṃ kṛtvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā mahāśvetāṃ khagolkaṃ3 ca grahādhipam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇān vācayitvā ca tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*ādityagrahayukte'sminvāre tripurasūdana \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yatkarma kriyate puṇyaṃ tatsarvaṃ śubhadaṃ bhavet \|*  
*snānadānajapādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ govṛṣadhvaja \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. Therefore, the pedestal should be raised over an auspicious land and the image of the Sungod should be consecrated over it, making all the efforts. The image should then be bathed. The homa should then be performed with ghi and sesamum seeds. Then Mahashveta-stotra should be recited. After the eclipse is removed, concentrating one’s mind, one should take his bath and should worship the Sun who is the lord of the planets as well as Mahashveta. The Brahmana should then be made to deliver discourse. Then after feeding the Brahmana, he himself should take his food keeping silence. O destroyer of Tripura, thus all the atrocities like bathing, giving of charities and japam performed on the day of the solar eclipse, bestow auspicious reward.

## \|\| 1.92.11 \|\|

*anantaṃ hi phalaṃ teṣāṃ bhavatyasminna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kṛtānāṃ tu gaṇaśreṣṭhā bhāskarasya vaco yathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O lord with a bull-banner, by performing all these activities, one receives the reward beyond measure, because whatever has been stated has the approval of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.92.12 \|\|

*tasmāddvijagaṇaiḥ kāryaṃ puṇyakarmavicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*ekabhaktaṃ ca naktaṃ ca upavāsaṃ gaṇādhipa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O leader of the ganas, the performer of the auspicious deeds should take food once a day, perform the night vrata, besides the fasting.

## \|\| 1.92.13 \|\|

*ye vādityadine kuryuste yānti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*dharmyaṃ puṇyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca putrīyaṃ kāmadaṃ tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The people who worship the Sungod on that particular day in an appropriate manner, they surely achieve the best position. The above performance leads to the earning of merits, glory, son besides getting all the desires fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.92.14-15 \|\|

*tasmindānamapūpasya godānena samaṃ bhavet \|*  
*dvādaśaite mahābāho vīrabhānormahātmanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tuṣṭidāḥ kathitāstubhyaṃ sarvapāpabhayāpahāḥ \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tāta kurvatāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The giving away of the fried cakes equates with the merit of giving away a cow in charity. O long armed one, by listening to the twelve stories of the Sun or by reading them, one achieves satisfaction, besides his sins are destroyed. I have spoken to you on the subject in detail.

## \|\| 1.92.16 \|\|

*kṛtvaikameṣāṃ vidhivadvāraṃ vṛṣabhavāhana \|*  
*vṛṣāditritayaṃ prāpya cātrijāmacalāṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O lord, having the bull as a vehicle, by performing the vrata even once in an appropriate manner, a person achieves dharma, artha and kama besides the stable riches.

## \|\| 1.92.17-18 \|\|

*tato yāti paraṃ lokaṃ vṛṣaketo mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tejasāmbujasaṃkāśaḥ prabhayāṇḍajasannibhaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*patrihetisamo vīrye kāntyā candrasamaprabhaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Thereafter, he gains the beauty resembling the lotus, the lustre like that of the sun, the strength equating with that of Indra, besides the resplendence resembling the moon. Thereafter, he moves on to the abode of Shiva.

## Chapter 93. Glory of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.93.1 \|\|

*grāmaṃ dadāti yo bhaktyā sūryāya matimānnaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — The people, whose religious activities are always centered around the Sungod, their races are free of poverty and disease.

## \|\| 1.93.2 \|\|

*devāyatanabhūmestu gomayenopalepanam \|*  
*yaḥ karoti naro bhaktyā sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Therefore, a person, who with utmost devotion, plasters the land of the temple with cowdung and purifies it, he atonce is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.93.3 \|\|

*śvetayā raktayā vāpi pītamṛttikayāpi vā \|*  
*upalepanakartā vai cintitaṃ labhate phalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By plastering the temple walls with white, yellow and red wash, the person has his desires fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.93.4 \|\|

*citrabhānuṃ virañcyaiva1 kusumairyaḥ sugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*pūjayetsopavāsastu sa kāmānīpsitāṃllabhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A person who, getting image of the Sungod made, then observe the fast and adores it with fragrant flowers, he gets his desire fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.93.5 \|\|

*ghṛtena dīpakaṃ jvālya tilatailena vā raveḥ \|*  
*prayāti sūryalokaṃ sa dīpakoṭiśatairvṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A person who bums the lamp of ghi or sesamum oil before the image of the Sungod, he getting established in the light of crores of lamps, achieves the abode of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.93.6 \|\|

*dīpatailapradānena na yāti narakaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*dīpatailaṃ tilāścaiva2 mahāpātakanāśanāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A person who offers an oil lamp to the Sungod, he never falls in the hell, because the oil of the lamp and the sesamum have been believed to be the destroyers of the grave sins.

## \|\| 1.93.7 \|\|

*dīpaṃ dadāti yo nityaṃ bhāskarāyataneṣu3 vai \|*  
*catuṣpatheṣu tīrtheṣu rūpaujasvī ha jāyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A person, who daily bums a lamp in a temple at a crossing or a scared place, he achieves the strength and beauty.

## \|\| 1.93.8 \|\|

*yastu kārayate4 dīpaṃ raverbhaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sa kāmānīpsitānprāpya vṛndārakapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A person who offers a lamp to the Sungod with devotion, all his desires are fulfilled and he achieves the heaven finally.

## \|\| 1.93.9-10 \|\|

*yaḥ samālabhate sūryaṃ candanāgurukuṅkumaiḥ \|*  
*karpūreṇa vimiśraiśca tathā kastūrikānvitaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śubhaṃ kālaṃ koṭiśataṃ vihṛtya5 ca bhavālaye \|*  
*punaḥ sañjāyate bhūmau rājarājo na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. A person who offers sandalpaste, guggulu, vermilion, camphor and musk-deer paste to the image of the Sungod, he, enjoying all the comforts in the heaven for crores of years, ultimately becomes an emperor on earth. Getting all his desires fulfilled, he is honoured in all the lokas.

## \|\| 1.93.11 \|\|

*candanodakamiśraiśca dattvārghyaṃ kusumai raveḥ \|*  
*saputrapautrapatnīkaḥ svargaloke mahīyate6 \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A person who offers oblation of water mixed with flowers and the sandalpaste, is honoured in the heaven, with his wife and children.

## \|\| 1.93.12 \|\|

*sugandhodakamiśraistu dattvārghyaṃ kusumai raveḥ \|*  
*devaloke ciraṃ sthitvā rājā bhavati bhūtale \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Similarly, a person who offers oblation of water with flowers, lives in the heaven for long and then becomes a king on earth.

## \|\| 1.93.13 \|\|

*sa hiraṇyena cārgheṇa raktodakayutena vā \|*  
*koṭīśataṃ tu varṣāṇāṃ svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person who offers water mixed with red sandal paste in a golden vase and to the Sungod, is honoured in the heaven for crores of years.

## \|\| 1.93.14 \|\|

*padmairabhyarcanaṃ kṛtvā raveḥ svargagato naraḥ \|*  
*padme vasati varṣāṇāṃ strīpadmaśatasaṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By worshipping the Sungod with lotus flowers, a person enjoys in the heaven the company of hundreds of Padmini damsels or Apsaras for crores of years.

## \|\| 1.93.15 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇātsarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A person who offers to the Sun guggulu incense with ghi, he is atonce relieved of all the sins. By offering the guggulu incense for a fortnight, a person is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 1.93.16 \|\|

*pakṣaṃ tu guggulaṃ dattvā mucyate brahmahatyayā \|*  
*saṃvatsareṇa labhate aśvamedhaphalaṃ śiva \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A person who does so for a year, he earns the merit of performing the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.93.17 \|\|

*dhūpena labhate svargaṃ turuṣkeṇa sugandhinā \|*  
*karpūrāgurudhūpena rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By offering frank incense to the Sungod, one achieves the heaven. In case the aguru mixed with camphor is offered, one achieves the merit equivalent to the performing of the Rajasuya-yajna.

## \|\| 1.93.18 \|\|

*pūrvāhṇe mānavo bhaktyā śraddhayā yo'rcayedravim \|*  
*sa tatphalamavāpnoti yaddatte kapilāśate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A person, who with utmost devotion and faith, worships the Sungod in the first half, he earns the merit equivalent to giving away in charity a hundred white cows.

## \|\| 1.93.19 \|\|

*madhyāhne yo'rcayetsūryaṃ prayatātmā jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*labhate bhūmidānasya gośatasya ca tatphalam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Similarly, when a laborious person, controlling all his senses, worships the sun at noon, he earns the merit of giving away of land and a hundred cows.

## \|\| 1.93.20 \|\|

*paścimāyāṃ tu sandhyāyāṃ yo'rcayedbhāskaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*śuciḥ śuklāmbaroṣṇīṣo gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A person, who in the evening, wearing a turban of auspicious cloth, adores the Sungod, he earns the merit of donating a hundred cows.

## \|\| 1.93.21 \|\|

*ardharātre tu yo heliṃ bhaktyā sampūjayennaraḥ \|*  
*jātismaratvamāpnoti kule jāto vṛṣānvitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A person who worships the Sungod at dead of night with utmost devotion, he besides regaining the memory of his past birth, is born in a high race.

## \|\| 1.93.22 \|\|

*pradoṣarātrivelāyāṃ yaḥ pūjayati bhāskaram \|*  
*sa gatvā sahasā vīra krīḍetsaumanasaṃ2 kṣayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O valorous one, a person who worships the Sungod during the evening, he suddenly achieves the heaven where he enjoys sports for a kalpa.

## \|\| 1.93.23 \|\|

*daṇḍanāyakavelāyāṃ prabhātasamaye punaḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā raviṃ bhaktyā vrajedanimiṣālayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person who worships the Sun with devotion at the day break, he achieves the heaven.

## \|\| 1.93.24 \|\|

*evaṃ velāsu sarvāsu avelāsu ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā pūjayate yo'rkamarkapuṣpaiḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*tejasādityasaṃkāśo hyarkaloke mahīyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When a person who adores the Sungod with a concentrated mind at any time, with swallow-wort flowers, he achieving the lustre of the Sun, is honoured in the solar region.

## \|\| 1.93.25 \|\|

*ayane tūttare sūryamatha vā dakṣiṇāyane \|*  
*pūjayedyastu vai bhaktyā sa gacchetkañjajālayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus during the time of Uttarayana as well as Dakshinayana, by worshipping the Sungod with devotion, a person achieves Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.93.26 \|\|

*tatrasthaḥ pūjyate keśaiḥ1 sarveḥ sumanasastathā \|*  
*gopatiḥ pūjyate yadvadgopatipramukhaiḥ suraiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There also, he gets most resplendent of all the gods and is worshipped as like the Sungod himself.

## \|\| 1.93.27 \|\|

*viṣuveṣūparāgeṣu ṣaḍaśītimukheṣu ca \|*  
*pūjayitvā raviṃ bhaktyā nātmānaṃ śocate naraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When the Sungod is worshipped at the time of equinoxes, eclipse or on the first day of the months, one does not have to worry for his own salvation.

## \|\| 1.93.28 \|\|

*vibudhya2 vā svayaṃ vāpi yo namaskurute ravim \|*  
*santuṣṭo bhāskarastasmai gatimiṣṭāṃ prayacchati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person who offers salutation to the Sungod at his own will or at the advice of others, he is bestowed the excellent position as per his desire by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.93.29 \|\|

*kṛśarāpāyasāpūpapalalonmiśramodakaiḥ \|*  
*baliṃ kṛtvā tu sūryāya sarvakāmamavāpnuyāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The rice and pulse cooked together, payasam, fried cakes, the powder of sesamum seeds and the sweet balls, when presented to the Sungod as an offering by a person, all his desires get fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.93.30 \|\|

*modakānāṃ pradānena3 pāyasasya ca suvrata \|*  
*madhumāṃsarasaiścāpi prīyate'tīvabhāskaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Suvrata, the sweet balls, payasam, honey and essence when offered to the Sungod, he gets pleased.

## \|\| 1.93.31 \|\|

*ghṛtena tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā sadā snigdho bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*tarpayitvā tu māṃsena sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With the offering of the oblation in ghi, a person always remains delightful and by offering meat, he is relieved of all his sins.

## \|\| 1.93.32 \|\|

*ghṛtena snapanaṃ kṛtvā ekāhamudaye raveḥ \|*  
*gavāṃ śatasahasrasya dattasya phalamaśnute \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In this way, with the bathing of the Sun image in ghi during early morning, a person is atonce relieved and achieves the merit equivalent to the giving away of a thousand cows in charity.

## \|\| 1.93.33 \|\|

*gavāṃ kṣīreṇa santarpya puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*rasena snāpayeddevamaśvamedhaphalaṃ 5 labhet \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With the offering of the oblation with cow’s milk, one achieves the merit of the Pundarika sacrifice and with the bathing of the image with a juice, he achieves a merit comparable with the performing of the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.93.34 \|\|

*sūryāya taruṇīṃ dhenuṃ gāmekāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*kañjajāmacalāṃ prāpya punarlekhapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By offering a cow for the Sungod, Lakshmi and the heaven are surely achieved.

## \|\| 1.93.35 \|\|

*gośarīre tu romāṇi yāvanti tripurāntaka \|*  
*sa tāvadvarṣakoṭīstu lekhaloke mahīyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O killer of Tripurantaka, as the number of hair are there over the body of the cow, the performer is honoured in the heaven for the period equivalent to the hair of cow’s body multiplied with crores.

## \|\| 1.93.36 \|\|

*gośataṃ bhānave dattvā rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya yaḥ sahasraṃ prayacchati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A person who gives away a hundred cows in charity for the Sungod, he earns the merit of performing the Rajasuya sacrifice and by giving away a thousand cows, one achieves the merit equivalent to the performing of an Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.93.37 \|\|

*guggulaṃ devadāruṃ ca dahennityaṃ ghṛtasravam \|*  
*ājyadhūmo6 hi devānāṃ prakṛtyaiva priyaḥ sadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The incense of guggulu and cedar wood mixed with ghi is naturally favourite of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.93.38 \|\|

*bheryādīni ca vādyāni śaṅkhaveṇvādikāni ca \|*  
*ye prayacchanti sūryāya yānti te haṃsamandiram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A person who presents the musical instruments like drum, conch, flute etc. to the Sungod, he achieves the abode of Surya.

## \|\| 1.93.39 \|\|

*vajramāharate yastu raverbhaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tīrthodakamathaivānyaḥ sa yāti vibudhālayam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, by offering the sesamum flowers and the water of the holy places, one achieves the heaven.

## \|\| 1.93.40 \|\|

*vimānaiḥ strīśatākīrṇaiḥ krīḍayitvā ciraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*mānuṣatvamanuprāpya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He, travelling in a plane with hundreds of women, sports with them for long, and is reborn as a religious king in human form.

## \|\| 1.93.41-42 \|\|

*chatraṃ dhvajaṃ vitānaṃ ca patākāścāmarāṇi ca \|*  
*hemadaṇḍāni vai dadyādraveryo bhaktimānnaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vimānena sa divyena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*sūryalokamato gatvā bhavatyapsarasāṃ patiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. A person who with devotion offers flag, canopy, banner and flywhisks with golden handles to the Sungod, he, boarding a divine plane decorated with small bells, reaches the abode of the Sungod and becomes the beloved husband of Apsaras.

## \|\| 1.93.43 \|\|

*tatroṣya suciraṃ kālaṃ svargātpratyāgataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*mānuṣye jāyate rājā sarvarājanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. After enjoying all the pleasures in the heaven for long, he is again born in human race and is respected by all the kings of the earth.

## \|\| 1.93.44 \|\|

*dattvā vāsāṃsi sūryāya alaṅkārāṃstathaiva ca \|*  
*krīḍate janalokastho yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A person who offers the costumes and ornaments for the Sungod, he spends his life sporting on earth till the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 1.93.45 \|\|

*gītavāditranṛtyaiśca kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasāṃ madhye krīḍate suciraṃ naraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A person who organizes festivities in favour of the Sungod, sports with Apsaras and Gandharvas for long.

## \|\| 1.93.46 \|\|

*gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā patraiḥ stotrairvā vividhaistathā \|*  
*ye stuvanti raviṃ bhaktyā te yānti patagālayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A person who worships the Sungod offering fragrant flowers, leaves and stotras in various ways, he achieves the place of Surya.

## \|\| 1.93.47 \|\|

*uṣaḥ stuvanti ye sūryamupagāyanti te sadā \|*  
*pāṭhakāścāraṇāścaiva sarve te svargagāminaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A person who offers prayers in favour of the Sungod at dawn regularly, he surely achieves the heaven, with the Charanas and the orators.

## \|\| 1.93.48-49 \|\|

*aśvayuktaṃ yugairyuktaṃ yo dadyādravaye ratham \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ vāpi raupyaṃ vā maṇiratnānvitaṃ śubham \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sa yānenārkavarṇena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*svargalokamito gatvā krīḍate'psarasā saha \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. When a person offers the chariot of gold and silver studded with gems and with the horses yoked in them to the Sungod, he becoming illustrious like the sun, moves to the heaven in the company of the Apsaras, boarding the plane decorated with the small bells.

## \|\| 1.93.50 \|\|

*yastu dārumayaṃ kuryādrave rathamanuttamam \|*  
*sa yātyarkasavarṇena1 vimānenārkamaṇḍalam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A person who gets an excellent chariot made of wood and offers the same to the Sungod, he is seated over a plane, like the Sungod himself and reaches the abode of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.93.51 \|\|

*yātrāṃ kurvanti ye bhānornarāḥ saṃvatsarādapi \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsādvā gaṇaśreṣṭha teṣāṃ puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O excellent gana, those who perform the Ratha-yatra of the Sungod annually or half yearly, I shall reveal the merits which they earn by so doing.

## \|\| 1.93.52 \|\|

*dhyānino yoginaścaiva prāpnuvantīha yāṃ gatim \|*  
*tāṃ gatiṃ pratipadyante sūryavartmāvagāhinaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. It is said that the person who performs the Ratha-yatra of the Sun, he is born as a yogi.

## \|\| 1.93.53 \|\|

*rathaṃ vahanti ye bhānornarā bhaktisamanvitāḥ \|*  
*arogāścādaridrāśca jātau jātau bhavanti te \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The people who pull the chariot with devotion, they always remain healthy in every birth and never have to face poverty.

## \|\| 1.93.54 \|\|

*kartāro rathayātrāyā ye narā bhāskarasya tu \|*  
*te bhānulokamāsādya viharanti yathāsukham \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The people who perform the Ratha-yatra of the Sungod, achieving the solar region they conduct themselves there with delight.

## \|\| 1.93.55 \|\|

*yātrābhaṅgaṃ tu yo mohātkrodhādvā kurute naraḥ \|*  
*mandehāste narā jñeyā rākṣasāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A person out of delusion, who disturbs the Ratha-yatra in anger, he should be treated as a Rakshasa.

## \|\| 1.93.56 \|\|

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ vā vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca \|*  
*ye prayacchanti sūryāya te yānti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Therefore, the chariot of the Sungod should be offered wealth, cereals, gold and various types of costumes and the people who do so, achieve the highest position.

## \|\| 1.93.57 \|\|

*gā vātha mahiṣīrvāpi gajānaśvāṃśca śobhanān \|*  
*ya prayacchati sūryāya tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I shall now point out the merit one achieves by giving in charity the cows, buffalos, elephants and beautiful horses for the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.93.58 \|\|

*akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*sahasraguṇitaṃ tacca dānamasyopatiṣṭhati \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. By this way, all the sins committed by a person mentally, physically or by speech, inspite of their being quite grave, get destroyed with the pleasure of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.93.59 \|\|

*mahīṃ dadāti yo'rkāya kṛṣṭāṃ phalavatī śubhām \|*  
*sa tārayati vai vaṃśyāndaśa pūrvāndaśāparān \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The relevant merits are multiplied a thousand times and become indestructible, fulfilling all the desires like Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.93.60 \|\|

*vimānena ca divyena gopuraṃ gopatervrajet \|*  
*krīḍatyapsarasāṃ madhye karīva kariṇīgaṇe \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A person who donates the cultivated land which always yields good crop, he redeems his future generations and ten earlier generations.

## \|\| 1.93.61 \|\|

*vimānenārkavarṇena sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thereafter, he, boarding an excellent plane, reaches the entrance gate of the abode of Surya, sports with the Apsaras like the male elephant sporting with the cow elephant.

## \|\| 1.93.62 \|\|

*ārāmānye prayacchanti patrapuṣpaphalopagān \|*  
*bhānave bhaktiyuktāstu te yānti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. A person, who with utmost devotion, donates a village for the sake of the Sungod, he gets seated over a plane with the lustre of the Sun, and achieves the best position.

## \|\| 1.93.63 \|\|

*mānasaṃ vācikaṃ vāpi karmajaṃ yacca duṣkṛtam \|*  
*sarvaṃ sūryaprasādena aśeṣaṃ ca praṇaśyati \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. A person who donates an orchard filled with trees, with leaves, flowers and fruits for the Sungod, he achieves the best position.

## \|\| 1.93.64 \|\|

*ārto vā vyādhito vāpi daridro duḥkhito'pi vā \|*  
*ādityaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatvā nātmānaṃ śocate naraḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Because a person in distress, an ailing person and the one suffering from pain when takes refuge in the Sungod, he does not have to bother for his own redemption.

## \|\| 1.93.65 \|\|

*ekāhenāpi yadbhānoḥ pūjāyāḥ prāpyate phalam \|*  
*tadvai kratuśatairiṣṭaiḥ prāpyate phalamuttamam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The merit for a day’s worship of the Sungod is equated with the performing of a hundred yajnas.

## \|\| 1.93.66 \|\|

*kṛtvā prekṣaṇakaṃ bhānordivyamāyatane śubham \|*  
*akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyaṃ rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. By decorating a Sun temple beautifully, one earns merit of the Rajasuya-yajna besides getting all his desires fulfilled.

## \|\| 1.93.67 \|\|

*veśyākadambakaṃ yastu dadyātsūryāya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*sa gacchetparamaṃ sthānaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati bhānumān \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. By arranging the music and dance of Apsaras or dancers in the Sun temple, one achieves the highest position in the abode of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.93.68 \|\|

*pustakaṃ bhānave dadyādbhāratasya gaṇādhipa \|*  
*sarvapāpavimuktātmā viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O lord of the ganas, a person who donates the book of the Mahabharata for the sake of the Sungod, he getting relieved of all the sins, is honoured in the abode of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 1.93.69 \|\|

*rāmāyaṇasya datvā tu pustakaṃ tripurāntaka \|*  
*vājapeyaphalaṃ prāpya gopateḥ puramāvrajet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O destroyer of Tripura, by donating the book of Ramayana, one achieves the merit of performing the Vajapeya sacrifice and achieves the place of Surya.

## \|\| 1.93.70 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃ sāmbasaṃjñaṃ vā dattvā sūryāya pustakam \|*  
*rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*
