9\. O excellent, you are asking me this observing the love between me and my husband, the beauty of both of us besides our excellent costumes. Therefore, I am replying to you.

## \|\| 1.115.10 \|\|

*tīrthodakaistathā gandhaiḥ snāpito yaddivākaraḥ \|*  
*tena kāntiriyaṃ nityaṃ devāṃstribhuvaneśvarān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Both of us had bathed the Sungod image with the fragrant water of holy places and because of that, both of us attained the beauty unparallel in the world.

## \|\| 1.115.11 \|\|

*manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ śarīre ye ca nirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*yatpriyatvaṃ ca sarvaṃ syāttadghṛtasnapanātphalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The mental success, the beauty of the bodies, peace and prosperity and whatever excellences is noticed in us, is all due to the bathing of the Sungod with ghi.

## \|\| 1.115.12-14 \|\|

*yānyabhīṣṭāni vāsāṃsi yaccābhīṣṭavibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*ratnāni yānyabhīṣṭāni yatpriyaṃ cānulepanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ye dhṛtā yāni mālyāni dayitānyabhavansadā \|*  
*mama bhartustadaivāsya tadā rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tāni sarvāṇi sarvajña sarvapātari bhānuni \|*  
*dattāni taṃ samuttho'yaṃ gandhadhūpātmako guṇaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Whatever the desired things like the costumes, ornaments and gems which are visible, were possessed by the king when he was the ruler. These include the paste, incense and the garlands. All these things were always presented by both of us to the Sungod. Because of that, our bodies still have the fragrance of incense etc.

## \|\| 1.115.15 \|\|

*āhārā dayitā ye ca pavitrāśca niveditāḥ \|*  
*trilokakartuḥ savitustṛptistadguṇasambhavā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. We also offered the pure food to the Sungod, who had been the lord of the three worlds, which pleased him immensely.

## \|\| 1.115.16 \|\|

*svargakāmena me bhartrā mayā ca śubhadarśane \|*  
*kṛtametatkṛtenābhūdāvayorbhavasaṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O damsel with excellent beauty, thus, with the desire of achieving the heaven, my husband had worshipped the Sungod, accordingly as a result of which, both of us have been saved from the cycle of birth and death.

## \|\| 1.115.17 \|\|

*ye tvakāmā narāḥ samyaktatkurvanti ca śobhane \|*  
*teṣāṃ dadāti viśveśo bhagavānmuktimīśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O graceful one, people who worships the Sungod without any desire, in the manner prescribed above, they are surely bestowed salvation by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.18 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*evamabhyarcya mārtaṇḍamarkaṃ deveśvaraṃ gurum \|*  
*prāpto'smyabhimatānkāmānkṛṣṇāhaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Brahma said — Similarly, I myself, worshipping lord Martanda, have got my desires fulfilled for years.

## \|\| 1.115.19 \|\|

*candanāgurukarpūrakuṅkumośīrapadmakaiḥ \|*  
*anulipto narairbhaktyā dadāti1 sāgarodbhavām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus, a person who presents sandal paste, agaru, camphor, saffron, fragrance of khas, paste to be applied over the body, he surely gets his desires fulfilled besides the wealth.

## \|\| 1.115.20-21 \|\|

*kāleyakaṃ turuṣkaṃ ca raktacandanameva ca \|*  
*yānyātmani sadeṣṭāni tāni śasyānyapākuru \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gandhāścāpi śubhā ye ca dhūpā ye vijayodayāḥ \|*  
*divākarasya dharmajña nivedyāssarvadācyuta \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. O religious minded and infallible one, a person should always offer gum resin, red sandal paste and the things liked by him besides fragrance, incense, etc., to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.22 \|\|

*na dadyātsallakīkṣāraṃ no mukhena ca saṃhṛtam \|*  
*dadyādarkāya dharmajña dhūpamārādhanodyataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O religious minded one, the saltish or the things tasted with mouth, should never be offered to the Sungod. The devotee should surely offer the incense to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.23-26 \|\|

*mālatī mallikā caiva yūthikā cātimuktikaḥ \|*  
*pāṭalāḥ karavīraśca japā sevantireva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kuṅkumastagaraścaiva karṇikāraḥ sakeśaraḥ \|*  
*campakaḥ ketaka kundo bāṇabarbaramālikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aśokastilako lodhrastathā caivāṭarūṣakaḥ \|*  
*śatapatrāṇi dhanyāni bakāhvānī viśeṣataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*agastiṃ kiṃśukaṃ tadvatpūjārthaṃ bhāskarasya tu \|*  
*amī puṣpaprakārāstu śastā bhāskarapūjane \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. The flowers like jasmine, Mallika, Yuthika, Atimuktika, oleander, Japapushpa, Sevanti, saffron, Kumkuma, coronaria, Artocarpus lancha, Michallia champaca, Paudarnus adoratissima (Ketaki), lotus, Banabarvara (a spreading shrub), Asoka, Tilaka, Lodhra, Adusa, lotus, Baka, Agastya and Butea frondosa are said to be the best of flowers for the worship of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.27 \|\|

*bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ patraṃ vā bhṛṅgarasya ca \|*  
*tamālapatraṃ ca hare sadaiva bhagavatpriyam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Similarly, the wood-apple leaves, the leaves of Sami, Bhringrasa and Catechu tree are quite favourite with the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.28 \|\|

*tulasī kālatulasī tathā raktaṃ ca candanam \|*  
*ketakī patrapuṣpaṃ tu sadyastuṣṭikaraṃ raveḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The holy basil, the black holy basil, red sandal paste, jasmine and their leaves, when offered to the Sungod, he gets pleased.

## \|\| 1.115.29 \|\|

*padmotpalasamutthāni raktaṃ nīlotpalaṃ tathā \|*  
*sitotpalaṃ tu bhānostu dayitāni sadācyuta \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Acyuta! The lotus, the red lotus, blue lotus and white lotus are particularly dear to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.30 \|\|

*kṛṣṇalokanmattakaṃ kāntaṃ tathaiva girimallikā \|*  
*na karṇikārikāpuṣpaṃ bhāskarāya nivedayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Krishna! The flowers of good-apple plants, Echitas untedysenterica and Artocarpus laucha should never be offered to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.31 \|\|

*kuṭajaṃ śālmalīpuṣpaṃ tathānyadgandhavarjitam \|*  
*niveditaṃ bhayaṃ rogaṃ niḥsvatāṃ ca prayacchati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. This is because by offering catechu, silk cotton tree and other flowers without fragrance lo the Sungod, one invites danger, ailments and poverty.

## \|\| 1.115.32 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ na pratiṣedho'sti gandhavarṇānvitāni ca \|*  
*tāni puṣpāṇi deyāni mānave lokabhānave \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Sungod, who illuminates the world, should be offered the flowers the use of which is not prohibited for him, having fragrance and beauty.

## \|\| 1.115.33 \|\|

*sugandhaiśca murāmāṃsīkarpūrāgarucandanaiḥ \|*  
*tathānyaiśca śubhairdravyairarcayedvanamālinam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With the fragrant leaves of Tala tree, Muramamsi, camphor, agaru, sandal paste and ocher excellent articles, the lord of the forests should be adored.

## \|\| 1.115.34 \|\|

*dukūlapaṭṭakauśeyavārkṣakārpāsakādibhiḥ \|*  
*vāsobhiḥ pūjayedbhānuṃ yāni cātmapriyāṇi tu \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Similarly, scarf of cotton or silk and whatever thing is liked by a person, besides ocher garments should be offered to the Sungod in adoration.

## \|\| 1.115.35 \|\|

*bhakṣyāṇi yānyabhīṣṭāni bhojyānyabhimatāni ca \|*  
*phalaṃ ca vallabhaṃ yatsyāttatte deyaṃ divākare \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Similarly, delicious dishes of food and pleasant fruits should also be offered to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.115.36 \|\|

*suvarṇamaṇimuktāni rajataṃ ca tathācyuta \|*  
*dakṣiṇā vividhā ceha yaccānyadapi vallabham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Acyuta! Gold, gems, beads, besides silver and other precious metals should also be offered to the Sungod. These metals can be offered to the Sungod as dakshina.

## \|\| 1.115.37 \|\|

*ātmānaṃ bhāskaraṃ matvā yajñaṃ tasmai nivedayet \|*  
*tattadavyaktarūpāya bhāskarāya nivedayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thus, realizing the sense of devotion in one’s mind, the Sungod should be worshipped while at the start of a yajna offering his favourite things to him. This is the supreme dharma of a person.

## Chapter 116. Worship of Ravi described

## \|\| 1.116.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇa rājā mahānāsīdyayātikulasambhavaḥ \|*  
*satrājiditi vikhyātaścakravartī mahābalaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — There had been a great king who had been born in the race of Yayati. He was an emperor and was quite popular.

## \|\| 1.116.2 \|\|

*prabhāvaistejasā kāntyā kṣāntyā balasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*dhairyagambhīryasampanno vadānyo yaśasānvitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He was quite influential, resplendent, possessed lustre, competence, prowess, strength, patience besides being quite deep in wisdom. He was possessing enormous virtues besides being generous and glorious.

## \|\| 1.116.3-4 \|\|

*buddhyā vikramadakṣaśca sampanno brāhmaṇāyataḥ \|*  
*kṛtī kavistathā śūraḥ ṣaṭpadākhyairna nirjitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sadā pañcasu raktaśca vasumadbhirna nirjitaḥ \|*  
*rudratā vasubhirjātaiḥ sattvaśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. He was intelligent like the Brahmanas, besides being quite strong, possessing enormous competence. He was a poet and valorous one. He was free from the blemishes like lust, anger, greed, attraction, jealousy and malice. He was invincible from Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshvara, Surya, Ganesha. He was devoted to the goddess Durga. He could not be defeated by the kings. Having been filled with competence and faith, he earned the position of a Rudra by means of Vasus.

## \|\| 1.116.5 \|\|

*ambujasyāṇḍajasyeva ātreyasya tathācyuta \|*  
*ambujāyāstathā kṛṣṇa vāryapātraṃ sa vai vibho \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O Acyuta! Like Brahma and Martanda, he was the favourite of Lakshmi as well.

## \|\| 1.116.6 \|\|

*gāṅgeyena bale tulyaḥ paulastyārcāśramo yathā \|*  
*gāṅgeyasya tathā kṛṣṇa dhiṣaṇasya hareryathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He possessed the prowess comparable with Bhishma and his city was as charming as the city of Lanka of Ravana. O Krishna! He was as valorous as Bhishma, intelligent like Brihaspati and possessed the beauty comparable with lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 1.116.7-8 \|\|

*kāmyaśca dvijabhaktastu tathā vālmīkivatsadā \|*  
*vyāsasya devaśārdūla jāmadagnyasya vā vibhoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*eṣāṃ naikairguṇairyuktaḥ sa rājā kṣmātale vibho \|*  
*śaśāsa sa mahābāhuḥ saptadvīpāṃ vasundharām \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. O lion among the gods! The desirable Brahmana devotee, possessing many qualities like Valmiki, Vyasa and Parashurama, becoming the lord of the earth, conquered all the seven islands on earth.

## \|\| 1.116.9-10 \|\|

*yasmingāthāṃ pragāyanti ye purāṇavido janāḥ \|*  
*satrājite mahābāhau kṛṣṇa dhātrīṃ samāśrite \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yāvatsūrya udeti sma yāvacca pratitiṣṭhati \|*  
*satrājitaṃ tu tatsarvaṃ kṣetramityamidhīyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. O valorous Krishna! The powerful Satrajit, when so became the ruler of the earth, the stories of his bravery were sung by the Brahmanas. They said that wherever the sun shines and sets, the entire land was under the rule of Satrajit.

## \|\| 1.116.11 \|\|

*sa sarvaratnasaṃyuktāṃ saptadvīpavatīṃ mahīm \|*  
*śaśāsa dharmeṇa purā cakravartī mahābalaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The valorous emperor established the religious rule over the earth, and the seven islands were filled with diamonds (during his reign).

## \|\| 1.116.12 \|\|

*nānyāyakṛnna cāśakto vadānyo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*tasyābhūtpuruṣā rājñaḥ samyagdharmānuśāsinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. While ruling properly his kingdom on religious lines, no injustice was done to anyone. There was no weak or destitute person there. All the people believed in justice and were quite strong, besides being large hearted.

## \|\| 1.116.13 \|\|

*catvāraḥ sacivāstasya rājñaḥ satrājitasya tu \|*  
*babhūvurapratihatāḥ sadā vāti balasya vai \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The powerful king Satrajit had four irresistible ministers, each possessing enormous strength.

## \|\| 1.116.14 \|\|

*tasya bhaktiratīvāsīnnisargādeva bhūpateḥ \|*  
*divākare jagadbhānau raktacandanamālini \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The said king had developed enormous devotion for the Sungod who is wearing the garland of red sandal wood.

## \|\| 1.116.15 \|\|

*tasyordhvamahimānaṃ ca vilokya pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*na kevalaṃ janasyāpi hyabhavattasya vismayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Because of that, observing the height of the glory of the said king, not only the people, but the contemporary rulers too were surprised.

## \|\| 1.116.16 \|\|

*sañcintayāmāsa nṛpaḥ samṛddhyā vismitastathā \|*  
*kathaṃ syāt sampadeṣā me punarapyanyajanmani \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Because with the so rapid rise of his prosperity, he himself once thought, as to how could he achieve the enormous wealth and fortunes in various births.

## \|\| 1.116.17 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bahuśo rājā tadā kṛṣṇa mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*cintayannapi tanmūlaṃ nāsadanniścayānvitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O Krishna! By thus thinking repeatedly, the immensely popular king could not find out the cause for the same.

## \|\| 1.116.18 \|\|

*yadā na niścayaṃ rājā sa yayau bhārgavīpriyaḥ \|*  
*tadā papraccha dharmajñānsa viprānsamupāgatān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When the beloved king of the earth himself could not know about the cause of the same, then he asked the learned Brahmanas, who had arrived at his place.

## \|\| 1.116.19-20 \|\|

*sarvāśca sasukhānvīra viviktāntaḥ purasthitaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya mahābāhurgrahītuṃ śāsanakriyāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viśvāsānugrahā buddhirbhavatāṃ mayi sattamāḥ \|*  
*tadahaṃ praṣṭumicchāmi kiñcittadvaktumarhatha \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Once in a solitary place in the inner apartment, the king offering his salutation to the learned Brahmanas, said to them — “All of you are highly noble and in case you are kind and favourable to me, then I would like to ask you something, which you kindly tell me.

## \|\| 1.116.21-22 \|\|

*sadvidyākhilavijñānasamyagdhautāntarātmabhiḥ \|*  
*bhavadbhiryadyanugrāhyaḥ syāmahaṃ vedavittamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tadyathāvanmayā pṛṣṭā bhavanto matprasādinaḥ \|*  
*vaktumarhatha vidvāṃsaḥ sarvasyaivopakāriṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The inner souls of all of you have been purified with the possession of immense sacred knowledge. You being well-versed in the Vedas if intend to shower your grace on me, then you should make me understand the topic which I shall express to you. Therefore, you kindly throw light on the topic which I am going to place before you. This is because the noble people by nature do good to others.”

## \|\| 1.116.23 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yaste manasi sandehastaṃ pṛcchādya mahīpate \|*  
*vadiṣyāmo yathānyāyaṃ yatte1 manasi varttate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Brahma said — The Brahmana Rishis said — You better speak out the doubt in your mind today. All of us shall try to remove the mental sin, as per our wisdom and capacity.

## \|\| 1.116.24 \|\|

*vayaṃ hi nṛpaśārdūla bhavatā pāritoṣitāḥ \|*  
*samyakprajāṃ pālayitrā dadatā bhojanaṃ sadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O lion among the rulers, you have always done your best, while maintaining your people to please us by supplying excellent food.

## \|\| 1.116.25 \|\|

*santuṣṭo brāhmaṇo'śnīyācchiṃdyādvā dharmasaṃśayam \|*  
*hitaṃ copadiśedvartma ahitādvā nivartayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the Brahmanas eat with satisfaction, they remove the doubts with the study of the Vedas. They guide about the path of welfare, discarding the path leading to misery, disowning the harmful ways. This is the rule.

## \|\| 1.116.26 \|\|

*vivakṣumatha bhūpālaṃ bhāryā tasyaiva dhīmataḥ \|*  
*praṇipātena cāhedaṃ vinayātpraṇayānvitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereafter, when the king was about to ask the question, he quickly got up and offering his salutation to the king and spoke with humility thus.

## \|\| 1.116.27 \|\|

*na strīṇāmavanīpāla vaktumīdṛgiheṣyate \|*  
*tathāpi bhūpate vakṣye sampadīdṛksudurlabhā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “O lord of the earth! Though, it would not be proper for the ladies to put such questions, still, O king, I would like to know about the wealth of the king. I am so speaking, because it is rather impossible for a person to possess such an enormous wealth.

## \|\| 1.116.28-29 \|\|

*bhūyo'pi saṃśayānpraṣṭumalamīśo bhavānṛṣīn \|*  
*nanvahaṃ puraṣavyāghra sadāntaḥ puracāriṇī \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tatprasādaṃ yadi bhavānkaroti mama pārthiva \|*  
*tanmadīyamṛṣīnpraṣṭuṃ sandehaṃ pārthivārhasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. You yourself can clear your doubt from the Rishis, who always remain in contact with you. O lion among the humans! I always remain in your inner apartments. Therefore, O lord, in case you be graceful on me, you better ask my doubt to be removed by the Rishis. This would provide me the great comfort.

## \|\| 1.116.30 \|\|

*satrājita uvāca \|*  
*brūhi subhrūrmataṃ yatte praṣṭavyā yanmayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*bhūyo'hamātmasandehaṃ prakṣyāmyetaddvijottamān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Satrajit said — O beautiful one, you better speak out your doubt which you desire to get removed from these Rishis. I shall get my doubt removed from the Rishis sometimes later.

## \|\| 1.116.31 \|\|

*vimalavatyuvāca \|*  
*śrūyante pṛthivīpāla nṛpā ye tu cirantanāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ ca sampadbhūpāla yathā te'dya kilābhavat \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Vimalavati said — O lord of earth! Of all our ancestors, those who were the ancient kings, it is learnt that they also had the wealth comparable with you.

## \|\| 1.116.32-33 \|\|

*tadīdṛksampado dhāma tavāśeṣaṃ kṣitīśvara \|*  
*yena karmavipākena tadvadantu maharṣayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ahaṃ ca bhavato bhāryā sarvasīmantinīvarā \|*  
*atīva karmaṇā yena tadvijñāne kutūhalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. O king, let the Rishis be gracious enough in enlightening us as to with the performing of which deeds, could you achieve the lustre and wealth? By performing which noble deeds, I became the chief queen out of all the other beautiful queens of the king? I am quite anxious to know about the same.

## \|\| 1.116.34 \|\|

*tathā sampatsamṛddhatvamanyeṣvapi hi vidyate \|*  
*nirastātiśayatvena nūnaṃ nālpena karmaṇā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Though the excess of wealth is found with many others people, but the everlasting wealth achieved by us, could never be the result of performing a petty deed.

## \|\| 1.116.35 \|\|

*tadanyajanmacaritaṃ naranātha nijaṃ bhavān \|*  
*munīnpṛccha tvayā cāhaṃ yanmayā ca purā kṛtam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O lord of the people, let us know from the Rishis about the noble deeds performed by us in our earlier births.”

## \|\| 1.116.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sa tathoktastayā rājā patnyā vismitamānasaḥ \|*  
*munīnāṃ purato māyāṃ praśaṃsanvākyamabravīt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Brahma said: — Thus having been asked by the chief queen, the king getting surprised, spoke, praising his chief queen at the same time.

## \|\| 1.116.37 \|\|

*sādhu devi mataṃ yanme tvayā yadidamīritam \|*  
*satyaṃ munivacaḥ puṃsāṃ syāddha vai gṛhiṇī tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O goddess, whatever has been spoken by you, it was also intended to be spoken by me. The words of the sages are true that the married wife happens to be half of the body of a person.

## \|\| 1.116.38 \|\|

*so'hametanmahābhāge pṛcchāmyetānmahāmunīn \|*  
*teṣāmaviditaṃ kiñcittriṣu lokeṣu na vidyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. “O excellent one, I am going to ask the same thing from the Rishis, because nothing is unknown to them in the three worlds.”

## \|\| 1.116.39 \|\|

*evamuktvā priyāṃ rājā praṇipatya ca tānṛṣīn \|*  
*yathāvadetadakhilaṃ papraccha dharaṇīdharaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thus speaking to his wife, the king of the land offered his salutation to the Rishis and asked than all the questions.

## \|\| 1.116.40 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*bhagavanto mamāśeṣaṃ prasādāvṛtacetasaḥ \|*  
*kathayantu yathāvṛttaṃ yanmayā sukṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The king said — All of you speak the truth. You kindly relate the noble deeds performed by me in my earlier births.

## \|\| 1.116.41 \|\|

*ko'hamāsaṃ purā viprāḥ kiṃsvitkarma mayā kṛtam \|*  
*kiṃ vānayā tu cārvaṃgyā mama patnyā kṛtaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Brahmana, where and in which yoni was I born earlier? What types of deeds did I perform? O Brahmana, what type of deeds were performed by my beautiful wife?

## \|\| 1.116.42 \|\|

*yenāvayoriyaṃ lakṣmīrmartyaloke sudurlabhā \|*  
*catvāraścāpratihatā amātyā mama gacchataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. By performing which deeds on earth, this inaccessible goddess Lakshmi and the four invincible ministers, who always follow me, were associated with me?

## \|\| 1.116.43 \|\|

*aśeṣā bhūbhṛto vaśyā dhanasyānto na vidyate \|*  
*balaṃ caivāpratihataṃ śarīrārogyameva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. All the rulers of the world are controlled by me. There is no end to my wealth. My healthy body is without any ailment.

## \|\| 1.116.44 \|\|

*pratibhāti ca me kāntyā bhāryāyāmakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*mamāpi vapuṣastejo na kaścitsahate dvijāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The beauty of my wife is spread m the entire world. O Brahmana, no one is able to bear the lustre of my body.

## \|\| 1.116.45 \|\|

*so'hamicchāmi tajjñātuṃ tathaiveyamaninditā \|*  
*nijānuṣṭhānamakhilaṃ yasyāśeṣamidaṃ phalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore, the rewards which have been received by me as per my deeds, besides those of my wife, during earlier births, are to be known by me. You kindly speak out.

## \|\| 1.116.46 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti pṛṣṭā narendreṇa samastāste tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*parāvasumathocuste kathyatāmasya bhūbhṛtaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Brahma said — When so enquired by the great king, Rishis asked Paravasu an excellent Rishi, to enlighten the king on all the points raised by him.

## \|\| 1.116.47-49 \|\|

*coditaḥ so'pi dharmajñairmahāśūrā mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*yogamāsthāya suciraṃ yathāvadyatamānasaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*jñātavānnṛpatestasya pūrvadehaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*sa tamāha munirbhūpaṃ vijñānecchaṃ mahāmatim \|\| 48 \|\|*

*satrājitaṃ mahātmānaṃ jitaśatruṃ manasvinam \|*  
*sapatnīkaṃ mahābuddhiṃ brāhmaṇānsatyavādinaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. At the desire of the religious minded Rishis, the intelligent and famous Rishi concentrated his mind with the strength of yoga and achieve the knowledge of the past life of the king. Thereafter, he spoke to Satrajit who was desirous of getting knowledge, being immensely wise, who had been victorious over his enemies, intelligent, in the presence of his wife and the truthful Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.116.50 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu bhūpāla sakalaṃ yasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam \|*  
*tava rājyādikaṃ subhrūryeyaṃ cāsīnmahīpate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Paravasu said — O lord of earth, the deed with the performing of which you have achieved the beautiful queen, is going to be spoken out by me. You please listen attentively.

## \|\| 1.116.51 \|\|

*tvamāsīḥ śūdrajātīyaḥ parahiṃsāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhārto daṇḍapāruṣye niḥsnehaḥ sarvajantuṣu \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O king, in your earlier birth, you taking birth in the family of a Shudra, always indulged in violence. In due course of time, you suffered from leprosy as a result of which you always felt painful. You were merciless and punished severely by all the creatures.

## \|\| 1.116.52 \|\|

*dvayaṃ ca bhavato bhāryā pūrvamapyāyatekṣaṇā \|*  
*nityaṃ babhūva tvaccittā bhavacchuśrūṣaṇe ratā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The queen with vast eyes happened to be your wife, who always served you with a devoted heart.

## \|\| 1.116.53 \|\|

*pativratā mahābhāgā bhartsyamānāpi niṣṭhuram \|*  
*tvadvākyeṣu ca sarveṣu vīra karmasu codyatā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O valorous one, because of your natural cruel nature, you scolded her mercilessly, quite often. But still the virtuous lady served you always with devotion, obeying your command always. She was always ready to perform all the tasks entrusted to her by you.

## \|\| 1.116.54 \|\|

*naiśvaryādasahāyasya tyajyamānasya bandhubhiḥ \|*  
*kṣayaṃ jagāma yortho'bhūtsañcitaḥ prapitāmahaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thereafter, inspite of your being extremely poor besides lean and thin, you had to take up service in those dire conditions. O king, feeling disturbed at that point of time, you disowned your wife even. Though you disowned your wife, but the chaste lady did not do so.

## \|\| 1.116.55 \|\|

*tasminkṣīṇe kṛṣiparastvamāsīḥ pṛthivīpate \|*  
*sāpi karmavipākena kṛṣirviphalatāṃ gatā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Again in company of the chaste lady, you took up the work of brooming and cleaning of a Sun temple.

## \|\| 1.116.56 \|\|

*tato niḥsvaṃ parikṣīṇaṃ pareṣāṃ bhṛtyatāṃ gatam \|*  
*tatyāja sādhvī neyaṃ tvāṃ tyajyamānāpi pārthiva \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In the said Sun temple, you attended to the cleaning work in the temple with utmost devotion.

## \|\| 1.116.57 \|\|

*anayā tu samaṃ sādhvyā bhānorāvasathe tvayā \|*  
*kṛtaṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ vṛttyā bhaktyā sammārjanādikam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Similarly, you fall from grace and became helpless and were also disowned by your relatives. The wealth with you, which had been collected during the time of your forefathers, was also lost.

## \|\| 1.116.58 \|\|

*niḥsnehaḥ sarvakāmebhyastanmayastvaṃ tadarpaṇaḥ \|*  
*ahanyahani visrambhāttasminnāvasathe raveḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O lord of the earth, at that point of time, you took farming for your livelihood. But because of the result of the evil deeds, you failed in that attempt as well.

## \|\| 1.116.59-61 \|\|

*kānyakubjapure vīra mahāśuśrūṣitaṃ tvayā \|*  
*divākarālaye nityaṃ kṛtaṃ tanmārjanaṃ tvayā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tathaivābhyukṣaṇaṃ bhūpa nityaṃ caivānulepanam \|*  
*patnyānayā nṛpa tathā yuṣmaccittānuvṛttayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*kāritaṃ śravaṇaṃ puṇyamitihāsapurāṇayoḥ \|*  
*dattvāṅgulīyakaṃ rājanpitṛdattaṃ tu vācake \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. O valorous one, the great service of brooming and cleaning of the Sun temple was undertaken by you in the city of Kanyakubja, living there. O king, by performing daily abhisheka and application of paste over the image of the Sungod with your wife, who always remained favourable to you besides being obedient, you also listened to the stories of the religious scriptures which were being recited in the temple and as a dakshina, you gave away the only finger ring which you got from your father to the reciter.

## \|\| 1.116.62 \|\|

*ahanyahani yatkarma yuvayornṛpakurvatoḥ \|*  
*tatraiva tanmayatvena pāpahānirajāyata \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O king, in this way you continued to serve the temple daily with utmost devotion. As a result of the performance by both of you, all your past sins were washed out.

## \|\| 1.116.63 \|\|

*bhānoḥ kāryaṃ mayā kāryaṃ paraṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*nāprabhātaṃ prabhātaṃ vā cinteyamabhavanniśi \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The whole night was spent by you thinking that all the tasks of the Sungod should be done by you, serving him at the same time irrespective of morning or noon etc.

## \|\| 1.116.64 \|\|

*evamāyatanaṃ ramyamityevaṃ ca sukhāvaham \|*  
*sūryavaccaivametatsyādityāsītte manastadā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. You thought that — “Let this Sun temple remains beautiful like the Sungod himself. This feeling always occupied your brain.

## \|\| 1.116.65 \|\|

*yogināṃ sukhadaṃ karma tathaiva sukhamityapi \|*  
*bhavaccittamabhūttatra yogakarmaṇyaharniśam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Like the noble deeds of the great yogins, the service performed by me in the temple bestows enormous comfort for me.” Thus thinking, your mind always remained engaged in the performing of the noble deeds throughout the day and night.

## \|\| 1.116.66-67 \|\|

*evaṃ tanmanasastatra kṛtodyogasya pārthiva \|*  
*bhūtānumāninaḥ samyagyathoktādhikakāriṇaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*smarato gopatiṃ nityaṃ cittenāpi dṛḍhātmanaḥ \|*  
*niḥśeṣamupaśāṃtaṃ te pāpaṃ sūryaniṣevaṇāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Thus, keeping yourself busy with a devoted mind, while serving the temple, you did much more than anyone else could do in such situations. As a result of which all your sins were washed out.

## \|\| 1.116.68-69 \|\|

*tato'dhikaṃ purastasmādagārasyānulepanam \|*  
*saṃmārjanaṃ ca bahuśaḥ sapatnīkena yatkṛtam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kevalaṃ dharmamāśritya tyaktvā vṛttimaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*anayā śravaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kāritaṃ vācakātsadā \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. You, together with your wife, attended to the maintaining and upkeep of the temple, pretty well. Discarding all your other evil ways, you did so only with a religious feeling alone. Your wife also heard the discourse from the reciter of the scriptures with devotion and repeated the same to others.

## \|\| 1.116.70-71 \|\|

*nānādhātuvikāraistu gomayena mṛdā tathā \|*  
*upalepanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaktyā tvayā pūrvaṃ surālaye \|\| 70 \|\|*

*athājagāma vai tatra kuvalāśvo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*mahāsainyaparīvāraḥ prabhūtagajavāhanaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. Once both of you, attended to the upkeep of the temple using various types of colours, cowdung and clay, beautifying the same. At that point of time, a great king Kuvalashva reached there with his huge army, which included many elephants and the horses.

## \|\| 1.116.72 \|\|

*sarvasampadupetaṃ taṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*vṛtaṃ bhāryāsahasreṇa dṛṣṭvā saṃkrandanodbalam \|*  
*spṛhā kṛtā tvayā tatra cārumaulini pārthive \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Observing the arrival of the king with a large number of queens adorned with several type of ornaments, you also developed a desire to be a king like him with a large number of queens. You desired yourself to be such a beautiful king with the crown over the head.”

## \|\| 1.116.73 \|\|

*sarvakāmapradaṃ karma kriyate bhāskārāśritam \|*  
*tenaitadakhilaṃ rājyamaśeṣaṃ cāptavānmahīm \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. With this desire in your mind, you attended to all the services of the Sungod, which fulfil all the desires. Because of the services so rendered by you, you could achieve such a vast kingdom on earth.

## \|\| 1.116.74 \|\|

*tejaścaivādhikaṃ yatte tathaiva śṛṇu pārthiva \|*  
*yogaprabhāvato labdhaṃ kathayāmyakhilaṃ tava \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O king! The lustre which has been achieved by you, that particular yoga is being revealed by me.

## \|\| 1.116.75 \|\|

*tatraivāvasathe dīpaḥ praśāntaḥ snehasaṃkṣayāt \|*  
*nijabhojanatailena punaḥ prajvalitastvayā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Once due to the shortage of oil, the lamp of the temple was extinguished, but the edible oil kept by you in your house for cooking purpose was brought and made use of it in relighting the lamp in the temple.

## \|\| 1.116.76-77 \|\|

*anyā cottarīyeṇa vīra vartyopabṛṃhitaḥ \|*  
*tava patnyā svayaṃ jvālya kāntirasyāstato'dhikā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tavāpyakhilabhūpālamanaḥ kṣobhakaraṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tejo narendra etasmātkimutārādhya bhāskaram \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. On the other hand, your queen tore out a piece from her costumes and made it serve as a wick of the lamp. O king, because of this, you could achieve the complete lustre which attracts the minds of the rulers. Then what to speak of a persons’ lustre who adores the Sungod appropriately?

## \|\| 1.116.78 \|\|

*evaṃ narendraḥ śūdratvādbhānukarmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tanmayatvena samprāpto mahimānamanuttamam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O king, inspite of your being a Shudra, you attended to all the jobs of the Sun temple, and therefore, you achieved this beautiful glory.

## \|\| 1.116.79 \|\|

*kiṃ punaryo naro bhaktyā nityaṃ śuśrūṣaṇāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*karoti satataṃ pūjāṃ niṣkāmo nānyamānasaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Therefore, a devotee when worships the lord without any specific desire, then what to speak of him?

## \|\| 1.116.80 \|\|

*sarvāmṛddhimimāṃ labdhvā sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvārkamīśeśaṃ tamārādhya na sīdati \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. He, possessing all the fortunes, achieves the superiority over all the people, because with the worship of the Sungod, one does not has to face any misery of any kind.

## \|\| 1.116.81 \|\|

*puṣpai dhūpaistathā vānyairdīpairvastrānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*ārādhayārkaṃ tadveśma sadā sammārjanādinā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Therefore, collecting flowers, incense, lamp, costumes and sandal paste, these should be offered to the Sungod and his temple should be cleaned, besides adoring him.

## \|\| 1.116.82 \|\|

*yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ kiñcidyadyanyattu durlabham \|*  
*taddatvā ca jagaddhātre bhāskarāya na sīdati \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. A thing, which is liked by a person the most, besides the things which are inaccessible, should be offered to the Sungod and by so doing, one does not have to face any pain of any kind.

## \|\| 1.116.83-84 \|\|

*sugandhāgurukarpūracandanāgurukuṃkumaiḥ \|*  
*vāsobhirvividhairdhūpaiḥ puṣpaiḥ srakcāmaradhvajaiḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*anyopahārairvividhaiḥ kṛtakṣīrābhiṣecanaiḥ \|*  
*gītavāditranṛtyādyaistoṣayasvārkamādarāt \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Therefore, the Sungod should be pleased by offering fragrance, agaru, camphor, sandal paste, saffron, costumes, various types of flowers, flywhisks, banners and other presents besides milk, and his abhisheka should be performed. Besides offering salutation to him, he should be pleased with sweet music and dance.

## \|\| 1.116.85-87 \|\|

*puṇyarātriṣu mārtaṇḍaṃ nṛtyagītairathojjvalam \|*  
*bhūpa jāgaraṇairbhaktyā homaḥ kāryaḥ sadā śuciḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇānāṃ śravaṇena . viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tathā vedasvanaiḥ puṇyairṛksāmayajubhirnṛpa \|\| 86 \|\|*

*evaṃ santoṣyate bhaktyā bhagavānbhavabhaṅgakṛt \|*  
*bhūyo vaivasvato bhūtvā bhavahṛdbhāskaro naraiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. O king, during an auspicious night, dance, singing and playing of musical instruments should be arranged with devotion and keeping awake, the homa should also be performed with purity. The stories from religious scriptures should also be recited. The Sungod should also be pleased with the singing of the hymns of Rigveda and Samaveda which are remover of the miseries. He should be pleased with these activities.

## \|\| 1.116.88-89 \|\|

*toṣito bhagavānbhānurdadātyabhimataṃ phalam \|*  
*daivakarmasamarthānāṃ prāṇināṃ smṛtisambhavaiḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*toṣito bhagavānkāmānprayacchati divākaraḥ \|*  
*naiṣa vṛttairna ratnaughaiḥ puṣpairdhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*sadbhāvenaiva mārtaṇḍastoṣamāyāti saṃsmṛtaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. The Sungod, getting pleased with his devotees, bestow the fruits desired by them. Similarly, with the performing of other religious deeds, who are well-versed in doing so, the people getting vigilant, when adore the Sungod, he is pleased and grants all the wishes. When the Sungod is worshipped with the offering of gems, flowers, incense and paste etc., he does not feel so pleased as he does by his worship done with utmost devotion.

## \|\| 1.116.90 \|\|

*tvayaikāgramanaskena gṛhasammārjanādikam \|*  
*kṛtvālpamīdṛśaṃ prāptaṃ rājyamanyena durlabham \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. With a concentrated mind, you attended only to the job of cleaning of the Sun temple, with the dedicated performing of the service in the Sun temple, and thereby, you achieved the great kingdom which is beyond the reach of the people.

## \|\| 1.116.91-92 \|\|

*anayā śravaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kārayitvā gṛhe raveḥ \|*  
*īdṛkprāptā sampadiyaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tu vācake \|\| 91 \|\|*

*prāptopakaraṇairyastamekāgramatiraṇḍajam \|*  
*santoṣayati nendro'pi bhavatā vai samaḥ kvacit \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. You made the Brahmanas to recite scriptures in the Sun temple and gave them the only gold ring of your ancestors, you possessed Because of the same, you achieved the enormous fortunes presently. Therefore, a person, who possessing all the means, pleases the Sungod, he achieves everything. Therefore, to some extent, even Indra cannot be compared with you.

## \|\| 1.116.93 \|\|

*tasmāttvamanayā devyā sahātyantavinītayā \|*  
*bhāskarārādhane yatnaṃ kuru dharmabhṛtāṃ vara \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Therefore, O best of the religious people, you worship the Sungod, with your wife, with all humility.

## \|\| 1.116.94 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etanmunervaco vīra niśamya sa narādhipaḥ \|*  
*bhāryāsahāyaḥ sa tadā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Brahma said — O valorous one, listening to the words of the sage, in this way, the king with his wife was overwhelmed with his pleasures.

## \|\| 1.116.95 \|\|

*kṛtakāryamivātmānaṃ manyamānastadābhavat \|*  
*uvāca praṇato bhūtvā rājā satrājito'cyuta \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. At that point of time, he realised of iris having been successful. O Acyuta, the king Satrajit again spoke with utmost humility.

## \|\| 1.116.96 \|\|

*satrājita uvāca \|*  
*yathāmaratvaṃ samprāpya yathā vāyurbalaṃ param \|*  
*paraṃ nirvāṇamāpnoti tathāhaṃ vacasā tava \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Satrajit said — As a person achieves immortality and the vast strength of the wind, besides redemption and then realises the relative bliss, similarly, by listening to your speech, I feel blissful and am getting drowned in the same.

## \|\| 1.116.97 \|\|

*kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhāsīno nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ajñānatamasācchanne yatpradīpastvayā dhṛtaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. I had been overpowered with ignorance but you have shown the light of knowledge to me. With that, I have become successful. I have achieved the supreme comfort, while being seated at ease.

## \|\| 1.116.98 \|\|

*ahameṣā ca tanvaṅgī vibhūtibhraṃśabhīrukaḥ \|*  
*dravyamāpāditaṃ brahmannihādya vacasā tava \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Myself and my wife both were lost in the enormous fortunes possessed by us. We had been upset over the thought of the possible vanishing of the fortunes. But, O Brahman, with your discourse, today I have realised for the first time that I have achieved the wealth which is beyond limits.

## \|\| 1.116.99 \|\|

*sampadaḥ kathitaṃ bījamāvayorbhavatā mune \|*  
*tvadvaktrādudyatā vāco vijñātā hi dvijottama \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. You have enlightened us on the basis of these vast fortunes. I have well understood all the words spoken by you.

## \|\| 1.116.100 \|\|

*na ratnairna ca vittaughairna ca puṣpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*ārādhyaśca jagannātho bhāvaśūnyairdivākaraḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The Sungod cannot be worshipped with enormous gems, flowers or the sandal pastes. On the other hand, the Sungod can better be worshipped well with selfless intentions alone.

## \|\| 1.116.101 \|\|

*bāhyārthanirapekṣaiśca manasaiva manogatiḥ \|*  
*niḥsvairārādhyate devo bhānuḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Therefore, instead of displaying the outward show, the Sungod should be worshipped with inner most devotion, like a pauper.

## \|\| 1.116.102-104 \|\|

*sarvametanmayā jñātaṃ yattvamāttha mahāmune \|*  
*yacca pṛcchāmi tanme tvaṃ prasādasumukho vada \|\| 102 \|\|*

*kathamārādhito devo naraiḥ strībhiśca bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*toṣamāyāti viprendra tadvadasva mahāmune \|\| 103 \|\|*

*rahasyāni ca devasya prītaye yā tithiḥ sadā \|*  
*cānyaśeṣāṇi me brūhi arkārādhanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-104. O great sage, the words you have spoken, have been well understood by me. Whatever is being now asked by me, you reply to me with a pleasant face. What type of adoration performed by a man or a woman pleases the Sungod? You speak out the secrets of Suryadeva, his favourite moon day and all other details may please be revealed to me quite gracefully, because I am desirous of worshipping him.

## \|\| 1.116.105 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu bhūpāla yairbhānurgṛheṣyārādhyate janaiḥ \|*  
*nārībhiścātighore'sminpatitābhirbhavārṇave \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Paravasu said — The men or women who are drowning in the terrific ocean of the universe, I am speaking about the method by which the Sun worship should be performed by them in their abodes.

## \|\| 1.116.106-109 \|\|

*samabhyarcya jagannāthaṃ devamakaṃ samādhinā \|*  
*ekamaśnāti yo bhaktaṃ dvitīyaṃ brāhmaṇārpaṇam \|\| 106 \|\|*

*karoti bhāskaraprītyai kārttikaṃ māsamātmanā \|*  
*pūrve vayasi yatnena jānatā'jānatāpi vā \|\| 107 \|\|*

*pāpamācaritaṃ tasmādbhidyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anenaiva vidhānena māsi mārgaśire punaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*samabhyarcya marakataṃ viprebhyo yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*bhagavatprīṇanārthāya phalaṃ tasya śṛṇuṣva me \|\| 109 \|\|*

106-109. For the pleasure of the Sungod in the month of Karttika, concentrating one’s mind and worshipping the Sungod who is the lord of the universe, one who takes food and offer the same to the Brahmanas, the sins of his early age which were committed knowingly or unknowingly, are uprooted. Similarly, following the same process, one who for the delight of the Sungod, donates the Brahmanas the emerald gem, its reward is going to be spoken by me.

## \|\| 1.116.110 \|\|

*madhye vayasi yatpāpaṃ yoṣitā puruṣeṇa vā \|*  
*kṛtamasmācca tenekto vimokṣaḥ paramātmanā \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Getting pleased with the adoration, lord Surya destroys all the sins committed by men and women.

## \|\| 1.116.111-112 \|\|

*tathā caivekabhaktaṃ tu yastu viprāya yacchati \|*  
*divākaraṃ samabhyarcya pauṣe māsi mahīpate \|\| 111 \|\|*

*tattacca prīṇayatyarkaṃ vārdhikenaiva yatkṛtam \|*  
*sa tasmānmucyate rājanpumānyoṣidathāpi vā \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. O lord of earth, similarly, in the month of Pausha, worshipping the Sungod, raking meal at night and by serving food to the Brahmanas, the Sungod is pleased, and destroys all the sins committed by a person in old age.

## \|\| 1.116.113 \|\|

*trimāsikaṃ vratamidaṃ yaḥ karoti nareśvara \|*  
*sa bhānuprīṇanātpāpairlaghubhiḥ parimucyate \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Thus, by performing the process of vratas for three months, those who conclude the same, the Sungod getting pleased with their efforts, relieves them of the petty sins.

## \|\| 1.116.114 \|\|

*dvitīye vatsare rājanmucyate copapātakaiḥ \|*  
*tadvattṛtīye'pi kṛtaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. O king, by performing the vratas in the same process in the second year, a person is relieved of even the petty sins. In case the same process of vrata is repeated in the third year, a person is freed from the grave sins.

## \|\| 1.116.115 \|\|

*vratametannaraiḥ strībhistribhirmāsairanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*tribhiḥ saṃvatsaraiścaiva pradadāti phalaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. It is therefore, essential for a person to complete the process of vratas in three months. In case, the same anushthana is continued for three consecutive years, a person earns enormous merits.

## \|\| 1.116.116 \|\|

*tribhirmāsairanuṣṭhānāttrividhātpātakānnṛpa \|*  
*trīṇi nāmāni devasya mocayanti ca vārṣikaiḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. O king! Thus, Surya, as worshipped with the three names, destroys the grave sins of the people, in three years.

## \|\| 1.116.117 \|\|

*yatastato vratamidaṃ vividhaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ bhāskarārādhane param \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Therefore, with the worship of the Sungod by a person, the method has been prescribed by the people of learnings.

## \|\| 1.116.118 \|\|

*satrājita uvāca \|*  
*katamāya tu viprāya dātavyaṃ bhaktito mune \|*  
*dvitīye dvijaśārdūla kathayasvākhilaṃ mama \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Satrajit said — O lion among the Brahmanas, which one of the Brahmanas should be given charities and served the food? You kindly tell me.

## \|\| 1.116.119 \|\|

*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*deye purāṇaviduṣe vastre viprottamāya ca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ cāpi vacanaṃ yaduktaṃ bhāskareṇa ca \|*  
*aruṇāya mahābāho pṛcchate yatpurā nṛpa \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Paravasu said — The best of the Brahmanas well-versed in the Pauranika literature, should be offered the costumes etc. O valorous one, in earlier times, similar topic was raised by Aruna before the Sungod, who replied to him accordingly.

## \|\| 1.116.120 \|\|

*udayācalamārūḍhaṃ bhāskaraṃ timirāpaham \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā nūnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Once over the Udayachala mountain, Sungod — the remover of the darkness, reached there. On his arrival there, Aruna offer his salutation to him and said.

## \|\| 1.116.121 \|\|

*kāni priyāṇi te deva pūjane santi sarvadā \|*  
*puṣpādīnāṃ samastānāmārādhanavidhau sadā \|*  
*uparāgādivastrādau brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā rave \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. “What is your most favoured thing, when the people make offering to you with devotion? Similarly your favourite flowers? What type of things should be given to the Brahmanas? You kindly tell me.”

## \|\| 1.116.122-123 \|\|

*bhāskara uvāca \|*  
*puṣpāṇāṃ karavīrāṇi tathā raktaṃ ca candanam \|*  
*guggulañcāpi dhūpānāṃ naivedye modakāḥ priyāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*pūjākaro bhojakastu ghṛtadīpastathā priyaḥ \|*  
*dānaṃ priyaṃ khagaśreṣṭha vācakāya pradīyate \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. Bhaskara said — As I like oleander of all the flowers, besides sandal paste, guggulu, incense and in eatables the sweet balls are my favourite, similarly in performing my puja, I like Bhojaka Brahmanas, lamp of ghi. O foremost of the birds, I like the most the wealth given to the reciter of the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.116.124-125 \|\|

*māmuddiśya ca yaddānaṃ dīyate mānavairbhuvi \|*  
*vācakāya1 tu dātavyaṃ tanmama prītaye khaga \|\| 124 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇāmyāmabhijño yastu vācakaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇo vai khagaśreṣṭha sampūjyaḥ prītaye mama \|\| 125 \|\|*

124-125. The people on earth should give charities for my sake to the Bhojaka Brahmanas alone and not to anyone else, because I get pleased with these types of Brahmanas. O best of birds, the duty of a reciter should be entrusted to a Brahmana who is well-versed in ancient lores and the Puranas. He alone should be worshipped by the people, which pleases me.

## \|\| 1.116.126 \|\|

*pūjite'sminsadā vipre pūjitohaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*bhavāmi khagaśārdūla yatastviṣṭaḥ sa me sadā \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. O lion among the birds, by adoring the reciter Brahmana, one actually worships me. There is no doubt about it, because he happens to be my great favourite.

## \|\| 1.116.127-128 \|\|

*vedavīṇāmṛdaṅgaiśca nātigandhavilepanaiḥ \|*  
*tathā me jāyate prītiryathā śrutvā khagottama \|\| 127 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇāni vācyamānāni vācakaiḥ \|*  
*ataḥ priyo vācako me pūjākartā ca bhojakaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

127-128. I don’t feel as much happy with the reciting of the Vedas, playing on Vina, cymbals, fragrant paste, as I do with the reciting or listening of the Puranas. Therefore, the reciter as well as the Bhojakas who worship me, are immensely liked by me.

## Chapter 117. Method of plastering

## \|\| 1.117.1 \|\|

*na tasya santatiḥ syādvai na cāhaṃ prītimānbhave \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Aruna said — O lord of the gods, you like only the Bhojaka Brahmanas, living in the temples. People of no other varna except the Bhojakas are dear to you. Why is it so? You please tell me.

## \|\| 1.117.2 \|\|

*kaścāyaṃ bhojako deva kasya putraḥ kimātmakaḥ \|*  
*varṇataścāsya me brūhi karma cāsya samantataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lord, who is this Bhojaka and who is his father? What is his caste? What are his functions? I would like to know all about the same.

## \|\| 1.117.3 \|\|

*āditya uvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te vainateya mahāmate \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sarvaṃ gadato mama khecara \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Aditya said — O immensely wise bird, let you meet with welfare. You have put me a noble question. O flier of the sky, I am speaking all these things and you please listen to me with attention.

## \|\| 1.117.4 \|\|

*viprādayastu ye tvanye varṇāḥ kaśyapanandana \|*  
*te pūjayanti māṃ nityaṃ bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O son of Kashyapa, the people like Brahmanas and others worship me with devotion daily.

## \|\| 1.117.5 \|\|

*devālayeṣu ye viprāḥ prītyā māṃ pūjayanti hi \|*  
*anyāśca devatāvṛttyā te syurdevalakāḥ khaga \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇānmahyaṃ bhojako dayitaḥ sadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O bird, such of the Brahmanas, who worship my images installed in the temples and always remain engaged in the same, they are called Devakas. But, those who remain devoted taking it to be their livelihood, they are known as Bhojakas, who are quite dear to me.

## \|\| 1.117.6 \|\|

*varṇato brāhmaṇaścāyaṃ svānuṣṭhānaparo yadi \|*  
*anuṣṭhānavihīno hi narakaṃ yātyasaṃśayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Bhojaka belongs to the Brahmana caste, therefore, he must perform the religious rites in the absence of which, he surely falls in the hell.

## \|\| 1.117.7 \|\|

*na tyājyaṃ bhojakaistasmātsvakaṃ karma kadācana \|*  
*mayāsau nirmitaḥ pūrvaṃ tejasā svena vai khaga \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O bird, therefore, the Bhojaka should not discard his daily performance, because in earlier times, I had produced Bhojaka from my own lustre.

## \|\| 1.117.8-11 \|\|

*pūjārthamātmano nūnaṃ karma cāsya prakīrtitam \|*  
*priyavratasuto rājā śākadvīpe mahāmatiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tena me kāritaṃ divyaṃ vimānapratimaṃ gṛham \|*  
*tasmindvīpe tadātmīye divyaṃ śilāmayaṃ mahat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sa madarcāṃ kārayitvā kāñcanīṃ lakṣaṇānvitām \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpanāya vai tasyāścintayāmāsa suvrataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṛtamāyatanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ teneyaṃ pratimā kṛtā \|*  
*ko vai pratiṣṭhāpayitā devamarkaṃ śubhālaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. I have enlightened them about the process by which they should worship me, I am going to narrate the relevant story. You please listen. The son of king Priyavrata was the intelligent ruler of Shakadvipa, who had built a beautiful plane like temple for me. In the said island, he built a stone image of mine, which was covered with gold. It had all the symptoms of gold. It was to be consecrated in the temple. Then he started building the temple. He therefore thought, I have built a beautiful temple as well as an image of Surya. But how should the task of consecrating the same be accomplished?

## \|\| 1.117.12-13 \|\|

*evaṃ sañcintayitvā tu jagāma śaraṇaṃ mama \|*  
*bhaktiṃ tasya ca sañcintya khagāhaṃ pārthivasya tu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gato'haṃ darśanaṃ tasya uktañcāpi mayā khaga \|*  
*kiṃ cintayasi rājendra kutaściṃtā samāgatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Thus thinking, he took refuge with me. O bird, observing the utmost devotion of the king, I appeared before him and said to him — “O Indra among the kings, why are you feeling worried? How have the worries attracted you?

## \|\| 1.117.14 \|\|

*brūhi yatte hṛdi prauḍhaṃ cintākāraṇamāgatam \|*  
*saṃpādayiṣye tatsarvaṃ vimanā bhava mā nṛpa \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Very well, you speak out to me, the particular cause of your concern? O king, I shall surely remove the cause of your worries. Therefore, don’t feel painful at heart.

## \|\| 1.117.15-16 \|\|

*atyarthaṃ duṣkaramapi kariṣye nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa mayā rājā idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dvīpe'smindevadevasya kṛtamāyatanaṃ tava \|*  
*mayā bhaktyā jagannātha tatheyaṃ pratimā kṛtā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. In case the task be extremely difficult, I shall still establish it. There is no doubt about it.” When these words were so spoken by me, the king replied — O god of gods, I have built your temple in this island, besides the Sun image covered with gold.

## \|\| 1.117.17 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayedyastu tava devālaye khaga \|*  
*yatra santi trayo varṇā dvīpesminkṣatriyādayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O mover of the sky, I would like to know, as to who should consecrate your image in the temple, because there live only people of three castes viz., Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Madras.

## \|\| 1.117.18 \|\|

*te mayoktā na kurvanti pratiṣṭhāṃ tava kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*na cāpyarcāṃ jagannātha brāhmaṇaścātra vidyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Even I command them to do so, they would not be able to consecrate the image of toe Sungod there. O lord of the universe, in this way, even the daily worship also cannot be done, because not a single Brahmana can be found at this place.

## \|\| 1.117.19 \|\|

*teneyamāgatā cintā hṛdi śalyaṃ tayārpitam \|*  
*tato mayokto rājā'sau vainateya vacaḥ śubham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Because of these problems, I feel worried and these worries are causing pain in my heart like the piercing of thorns. O son of Vinata, thereafter, I spoke to the king like these pleasant words.

## \|\| 1.117.20 \|\|

*evametanna saṃdeho yathāttha tvaṃ narādhipaḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyāditrayo varṇā dvīpe'sminnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O lord of humans, there is no doubt that only three varnas are there over this island and whatever is being spoken by you is correct.

## \|\| 1.117.21-24 \|\|

*te ca nārhanti me pūjāṃ na pratiṣṭhāṃ kadācana \|*  
*tasmātte śreyase rājanpratiṣṭhāmātmanastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sṛjāmi prathamaṃ varṇaṃ bhaga saṃjñamanaupamam \|*  
*ityuktvā tamahaṃ vīra rājānaṃ khagasattama \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jagāma paramāṃ cintāṃ tasya kāryasya siddhaye \|*  
*atha me cintayānasya1 svaśarīrādviniḥsṛtāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śaśikundendusaṃkāśāḥ saṃkhyayāṣṭau mahābalāḥ \|*  
*paṭhanti caturo vedānsāṃgopaniṣadaḥ khaga \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. None of them can perform my puja or consecrate the image. O king, for your welfare and for the consecration of my own image, I am creating a new varna person, known as Bhaga. O best of the birds, thus speaking, for the success of the task of the king, eight valorous humans of pleasant varna emerged out of my body. All of them, at that point of time, were reciting the Vedas with their parts.

## \|\| 1.117.25-28 \|\|

*kāṣāyavāsasaḥ sarve karaṇḍāmbujadhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*lalāṭaphalakāddvau tu dvau cānyau vakṣasastathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*caraṇābhyāṃ tathā dvau tu pādābhyāṃ dvau tathā khaga \|*  
*atha te ca mahātmānaḥ sarve praṇatakandharāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pitaraṃ manyamānā māmidaṃ vacanamabruvan \|*  
*tāta tāta mahādeva lokanātha jagatpate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ bhavatā sṛṣṭā vayaṃ devasya dehataḥ \|*  
*brūhi sarvaṃ kariṣyāma ādeśaṃ bhavato'khilam \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. All of them were clad in ochre coloured garments, carrying vase of bamboo in hands decorated with the lotus flowers. O bird, in this way, two persons were born each from my forehead, chest, feet and soles of the feet. The noble people then taking me to be their father, offered their salutation to me and said — “O excellent one, O Mahadeva, O lord of the universe, what for have you produced us from your own body? Give us your command, which shall be obeyed by us.

## \|\| 1.117.29-30 \|\|

*pitāsmākaṃ bhavāndevo vayaṃ putrā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ityuktavantaste sarve mayoktā devasambhavāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*priyavratasuto yoyamasya vākyaṃ kariṣyatha \|*  
*sa cāpyukto mayā rājā śākadvīpādhipaḥ khaga \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. You happen to be our father and we are your sons. There is no doubt about it.” At these words of those people, I told them. The son of Priyavrata is present here before you, you fulfil the desire of this king. O bird, thereafter, I also spoke to the king of Shakadvipa.

## \|\| 1.117.31 \|\|

*ya ete matsutā rājannarghyā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*kārayantu pratiṣṭhāṃ me sarvairebhirmahīpate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “O king, all of them are Brahmanas and happen to be my sons. O lord of earth, all of them shall get my image consecrated.

## \|\| 1.117.32 \|\|

*kārayitvā pratiṣṭhāṃ tu mamārcāyāṃ narādhipa \|*  
*paścādāyatanaṃ sarvameṣāmarpaya pūjane \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O king, after getting my worship performed, you better donate the temple to them.

## \|\| 1.117.33-36 \|\|

*ete matpūjane yogyāḥ pratiṣṭhāsu ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*samāpya na prahartavyaṃ bhojakebhyaḥ kadācana \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarvamāyatanārthaṃ tu gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*dhanadhānyādikaṃ rājanyanmamāyatane bhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ bhojakebhyastu dātavyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*dhanadhānyasuvarṇādi gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*yanmadīyaṃ bhavetkiñjidgrāme vā nagare kvacit \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tasya sarvasya rājendra madīyasya samantataḥ \|*  
*adhipā bhojakāḥ sarve nānye viprādayo nṛpa \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. All of them are quite competent to consecrate any image and to worship them. After the end of the ceremony of consecration, don’t snatch away the things offered to the Bhojakas. O king, you also offer residential part of the temple, the riches, cereals and other things collected at the spot, to the Bhojakas without fail. This is because, whatever things like riches, cereals, gold, the houses, land, fields, villages and cities etc. are collected in the temple for my sake, only the Bhojakas are entitled to receive the same and not any other Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.117.37 \|\|

*yathādhikārī putrastu pitṛdravyasya vai bhavet \|*  
*tathā madīyavittasya bhojakāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. As the parental property is to be received by the son only, similarly, the Bhojakas alone are entitled to receive the offerings made to me. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.117.38 \|\|

*ityuktena mayā rājñā tathā sarvaṃ pravartitam \|*  
*kārayitvā pratiṣṭhāṃ tu dattvā sarvasvameva hi \|*  
*bhojakebhyaḥ khagaśreṣṭha tato harṣamavāptavān \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O best of birds, the king then acted as per my advice. After the consecration, he handed over everything of that place to the Bhojakas, feeling delighted.

## \|\| 1.117.39-40 \|\|

*evamete mayā sṛṣṭā bhojakā garuḍāgraja \|*  
*ahamātmā tato hyeṣāṃ sarve sumanasastathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*matputreṇa samā jñeyāstathā mama hitāḥ sadā \|*  
*tasmāttebhyaḥ pradātavyaṃ na hartavyaṃ kadācana \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. O lord of Garuda! Thus, the Bhojakas have indeed been created by me and I happen to be their soul. They are my well-wishers to be like sons. The charities should be given to them alone, which should never be taken back.

## \|\| 1.117.41 \|\|

*bhojakasya haredyastu lobhāddveṣāttathāpi vā \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ tāmisraṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Due to greed or jealousy, one who usurps their property or belongings, he has to suffer in the Tamisra heaven for long period.

## \|\| 1.117.42 \|\|

*tasmādgrāmādikaṃ dravyaṃ yatkiñcinmama vidyate \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ bhojakasvaṃ hi pitṛparyāgataṃ mama \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Therefore, the villages or any other articles which have been offered to me, belongs to the Bhojakas and mine also, being their father.

## \|\| 1.117.43 \|\|

*bhojakaśca bhavedyādṛktatte vacmi khageśvara \|*  
*mamājñāṃ pāleyadyastu svānuṣṭhānaparaḥ sadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O lord of the birds! I am going to speak out the features of Bhojakas. A Bhojaka, while performing the religious rites, should always obey my command.

## \|\| 1.117.44 \|\|

*vedādhigamanaṃ pūrvaṃ dārasaṃgrahaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*abhyaṅgadhāraṇaṃ nityaṃ tathā triṣavaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After completing the study of the Vedas, he should carry it himself and become householder. He should take his bath daily, applying paste over the boy thrice a day.

## \|\| 1.117.45 \|\|

*pañcakṛtvaḥ sadā pūjyo hyahaṃ rātrau dine tathā \|*  
*devabrāhmaṇavedānāṃ nindā kāryā na vai kvacit \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He should worship me five times a day. He should never denounce the gods, Brahmanas and the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.117.46 \|\|

*nānyādevapratiṣṭhā tu kāryā vai bhojakena tu \|*  
*mamāpi ca na kartavyā tena ekākinā kvacit \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. A Bhojaka should never consecrate any other god except myself.

## \|\| 1.117.47 \|\|

*sarvameva nivedyānnaṃ nāśnīyādbhojakaḥ sadā \|*  
*na bhuñjīta gṛhaṃ gatvā śūdrasya garuḍāgraja \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O elder brother of Garuda, all the food stuffs should be offered to me first. The rest should not be consumed by him alone. He should not take shelter in the house of a Shudra.

## \|\| 1.117.48-49 \|\|

*śūdrocchiṣṭaṃ prayatnena sadā tyājyaṃ hi bhojakaiḥ \|*  
*ye'śnanti bhojakā nityaṃ śūdrānnaṃ śūdraveśmani \|\| 48 \|\|*

*te vai pūjāphalaṃ cātra kathaṃ prāpsyanti khecara \|*  
*gatvā gṛhaṃ tu śūdrasya na bhoktavyaṃ kadācana \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. A Bhojaka should similarly discard the leftover of the other Bhojakas. When a Bhojaka, visiting the abode of a Shudra, takes food there, then how could he achieve the reward for worshipping me? Therefore, he should never take food in the house of a Shudra.

## \|\| 1.117.50-51 \|\|

*gṛhāgataṃ ca śūdrānnaṃ tacca tyājyaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ādhmātavyombujo nityaṃ bhojakenāgrato mama \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sakṛtpravādite śaṃkhe mama prītirhi jāyate \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsānnātra sandehaḥ purāṇaśravaṇaṃ tathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. A Bhojaka should also discard the food received by him from the house of a Shudra. A Bhojaka should blow conch before me, because by blowing a conch once, I enjoy the same pleasure as one earns for listening to the Puranas for six months.

## \|\| 1.117.52 \|\|

*tasmācchaṃkhaḥ sadā vādyo bhojakena prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tasyeyaṃ paramā vṛttirnaivedyaṃ yanmadīyakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Therefore, a Bhojaka, making all the efforts, should blow the conch. The eatables which are offered to me are said to be the main source of living of a Bhojaka.

## \|\| 1.117.53 \|\|

*nābhojyaṃ bhuñjate yasmāttenaite bhojakā matāḥ \|*  
*magaṃ dhyāyanti te yasmāttena te magadhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Since the forbidden food is not to be taken by him, he is called as a Bhojaka with my consent, and keeping in mind the act of begging he is known as Magadha.

## \|\| 1.117.54 \|\|

*bhojayanti ca māṃ nityaṃ tena te bhojakā smṛtāḥ \|*  
*abhyaṅgaṃ ca prayatnena prāyaṃ śuddhikaraṃ param \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Since he provides food to me daily as well, he is called as Bhojaka. Therefore, the fast breaking should be done with all the purity and making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.117.55-56 \|\|

*abhyaṅgahīno hyaśucirbhojakaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*yastu māṃ pūjayedvīra abhyaṅgena vinā khaga \|\| 55 \|\|*

*muṇḍanaṃ śirasā kāryaṃ śikhā dhāryā prayatnataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. A Bhojaka, who takes bath without applying oil over the body, is considered impure. There is no doubt about it. O valorous one, O bird, having the body without oil, when a Bhojaka worships me, his progress of adoration does not extend. I also do not get pleased with him. He should always have his head shaven, keeping a tuft over it.

## \|\| 1.117.57 \|\|

*naktaṃ cādityadivase tathā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ pravartayet \|*  
*saptamyāmupavāsastu mama saṃkramaṇe tathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On Sunday and on the sixth day of the month, one should start the Saptami fasting for pleasing me.

## \|\| 1.117.58-59 \|\|

*kartavyo bhojakenaiva matprītyai garuḍāgraja \|*  
*trikālaṃ cāpi gāyatrīṃ japedvācā puro mama \|\| 58 \|\|*

*mukhamāvṛtya yatnena pūjanīyo'hamādarāt \|*  
*maunaṃ cāsya prayatnena tyaktvā krodhaṃ ca dūrataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. O elder brother of Garuda, in order to please me, the Bhojaka should obey the above commands. He should recite the Gayatri mantra thrice a day before me, covering his face and should worship me, keeping silence and free from anger.

## \|\| 1.117.60 \|\|

*śūdrebhyo yastu vaiśyebhyo lobhātkāmātprayacchati \|*  
*nirmālyaṃ mama vai vatsa sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O son, when a Bhojaka, out of greed or otherwise or out of lust, gives away the things offered to me to a Shudra or a Vaishya, he will surely have to fall in a hell.

## \|\| 1.117.61-62 \|\|

*lobhādvai bhojako yastu matpuṣpāṇi khagādhipa \|*  
*yacchatenyasya duṣṭātmā mayyanāropya khecara \|\| 61 \|\|*

*sa jñeyo me paraḥ śatruḥ sa māmarho na cārcitum \|*  
*nirmālyaṃ mama deyaṃ syādbrāhmaṇādiṣu vai nṛṣu \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. O companion of the Sun, a Bhojaka, who out of greed, gives away the flowers meant to be offered to me, to someone else, he should be considered to be my enemy and the (rest of the flowers) do not remain fit to be offered to me. The eatables offered to me should be given to Brahmanas alone.

## \|\| 1.117.63 \|\|

*naivedyaṃ yanmadīyaṃ tu tadaśnīyātsadaiva hi \|*  
*tenāsau śuddhyate nityaṃ haviṣyānnasamaṃ tathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He should also consume my naivedya (eatables) always, because by so doing, he always remain happy and pure.

## \|\| 1.117.64 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇādutkṣipedyastu mamāṃgātpuṣpameva hi \|*  
*nānyasya deyaṃ naivedyaṃ madīyamudake2 kṣipet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The flowers which are offered to me and the naivedya when not eaten by a Brahmana, they should not be given to anyone else. On the other hand, they should be dropped m water (or a river).

## \|\| 1.117.65-66 \|\|

*pañcagavyasamaṃ tasya manmataṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*mamāṅgalagnaṃ yatkiñcidgandhaṃ puṣpamathāpi vā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*dātavyaṃ na ca vaiśyāya na śūdrāya kadācana \|*  
*ātmanā tadgrahītavyaṃ na vikreyaṃ kathañcana \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Panchagavya is quite auspicious for him. The flowers which touch my body should not be given to a Vaishya or a Shudra, nor should they be sold out. They should be used by the Bhojaka for himself only.

## \|\| 1.117.67 \|\|

*yastu nāropya puṣpāṇi avyaṅgāni mamopari \|*  
*yaḥ kaścidāharelloke sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A person who takes the flowers without being offered to me, he surely falls in the hell.

## \|\| 1.117.68 \|\|

*snapanaṃ mama nirmālyaṃ pāvakaṃ yastu laṅghayet \|*  
*sa naro narakaṃ yāti saraudraṃ rauravaṃ khaga \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O bird, a person who crosses over the fire and my left over, falls in the terrific hell.

## \|\| 1.117.69 \|\|

*bhojakena sadā kāryaṃ snapanaṃ me prayatnataḥ \|*  
*yathā na laṅghayetkaścidyathā śvā nāpi bhakṣayet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Therefore, the Bhojaka should bathe me at such a place where no one can cross over it, or the dog does not consume it.

## \|\| 1.117.70-71 \|\|

*yadyayatnaparaḥ kuryādbhojakaḥ snapanaṃ mama \|*  
*yathā vai laṅghitamatirbhakṣyatāṃ ca khagādhipa \|\| 70 \|\|*

*sa yāti narakaṃ raudraṃ tāmiśraṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*ekabhaktaṃ sadā kāryaṃ snānaṃ traikālameva hi \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. O foremost of the birds, in case a Bhojaka washes my image carelessly and the dog consumes it, then he falls into Tamisra hell. The Bhojaka should take food once a day and should take bath thrice a day.

## \|\| 1.117.72 \|\|

*tricailaṃ parivarteta bhavitavyaṃ dinedine \|*  
*pūjākāle'rghakāle ca krodhastyājyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. While performing puja or offering oblation, he should not feel angry, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.117.73 \|\|

*amāṃgalyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ vaktavyaṃ ca śubhaṃ tadā \|*  
*īdṛgbhūto bhojako me preyān pūjākaraḥ sadā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He should discard the speaking of the evil words and should always speak auspicious words, because the Bhojaka, while performing puja, always happens to be my favourite.

## \|\| 1.117.74-75 \|\|

*sanmānyaḥ pūjanīyaśca viprādīnāṃ yathāsmyaham \|*  
*yaḥ karotyavamānaṃ tu vṛttirūpaṃ tu bhojake \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tasyāhaṃ roṣametyāśu kulaṃ hanmi samantataḥ \|*  
*priyo me bhojako nityaṃ yathā tvaṃ vinatāsuta \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. For other Brahmanas also, Bhojaka is as adorable as he is for myself. A person, who insults a Bhojaka, I at once destroy his entire race, getting annoyed O son of Vinata, a Bhojaka also, when resorts to cleaning of my temple like you, he also is quite dear to me.”

## \|\| 1.117.76 \|\|

*upalepanakartā ca sammārjanaparaśca yaḥ \|*  
*parāvasuruvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānbhānurbabhrāma rathamāsthitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Paravasu said — Thus speaking, lord Bhaskara, mounting his chariot, left the place.

## \|\| 1.117.77-78 \|\|

*aruṇo'pi tathā śrutvā mudayā parayā nṛpaḥ \|*  
*pūjyastasmānmahārāja bhojakastu mahīpate \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tasmāddevaṃ vācakāya dvitīyamaśanaṃ naraiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. O king! Aruna too, listening to these words, was immensely pleased. O lord with wisdom, the Bhojakas are adorable because of these facts. Therefore, a Bhojaka should be served food in preference to the other Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.117.79 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*itthaṃ śrutvā sa rājā tu karmaṇaḥ phalamātmanaḥ \|*  
*purātanaṃ mahābāhurmudamāpa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Brahma said — Thus listening to his earlier deeds, the valorous king was immensely pleased.

## \|\| 1.117.80-81 \|\|

*yadyadāyatanaṃ bhānoḥ pṛthivyāṃ paśyate nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃstasminkārayati upalepanamādarāt \|\| 80 \|\|*

*bhāryā tasyāpi suśroṇi puṇyaśravaṇamādarāt \|*  
*vācake vetanaṃ dattvā bhānordevasya mandire \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Since that time, the king wherever found a Sun temple, he cleaned it gracefully and his wife too deputed some reciter in a Sun temple to recite foe scriptures, paying him the remuneration and listened to foe auspicious stories daily.

## \|\| 1.117.82 \|\|

*itthaṃ rājā sapatnīkaḥ pūjya bhaktyā divākaram \|*  
*prāptāvubhau parāṃ prītiṃ gatiṃ cānuttamāṃ tathā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thus, the king, worshipping the Sungod with his queen, achieved the best of position.

## Chapter 118. Donating of a lamp in the Sun temple

## \|\| 1.118.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dīpaṃ prayacchati naro bhānorāyatane tu yaḥ \|*  
*tejasā ravisaṃkāśaḥ sarvayajñaphalaṃ1 labhet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — A person who donates a lamp in the Sun temple, he earns the glory resembling the Sungod, besides the merit for the performing of the yajnas.

## \|\| 1.118.2 \|\|

*kārttike tu viśeṣeṇa kaumāre māsi dīpakam \|*  
*datvā phalamavāpnoti yadanyena na labhyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. During the childhood in the month of Karttika, donation of a lamp removes all the sins.

## \|\| 1.118.3 \|\|

*kṛṣṇakṛṣṇātra te vacmi saṃvādaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*bhrātṛbhiḥ saha bhadrasya brāhmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I am going to relate the relevant story, which had been narrated by a Brahmana named Bhadra to his brothers.

## \|\| 1.118.4 \|\|

*jagatyasminpurī ramyā nāmnā māhiṣmatī purā \|*  
*tasyāmāsīddvijaḥ kṛṣṇa nāgaśarmeti viśrutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In earlier times, there had been a beautiful city named Mahishmati on earth. A Brahmana named Nagasharma lived there.

## \|\| 1.118.5 \|\|

*tasya putraśataṃ jātaṃ prasādādbhāskarasya ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ kaniṣṭho bhadrastu tatputrāṇāṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By the grace of the Sungod, the said Brahmana had a hundred sons, of whom his youngest son named Bhadra possessed enormous wisdom.

## \|\| 1.118.6 \|\|

*sa ca nityaṃ jagaddhāturdevadevasya bhāsvataḥ \|*  
*dīpavartiparastadvattailādyāharaṇodyataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He always took care for the lighting of the lamp in the Sun temple.

## \|\| 1.118.7 \|\|

*bhānorāyatane tasya sahasraṃ bhārgavīpriya \|*  
*pradīpānāṃ tu jajvāla divārātramaninditam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O beloved of Bhargavi! Thus, with his efforts, daily a thousand lamps were lighted in the Sun temple.

## \|\| 1.118.8 \|\|

*tasya dīptyā parābhūtāstasya lāvaṇyadharṣitāḥ \|*  
*sarve te bhrātaro bhadraṃ papracchuridamādarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. As a result of this, the lustre of his body increased immensely, observing which his brothers questioned about the reason of his gaining enormous lustre.

## \|\| 1.118.9 \|\|

*bho bhadra vada vai bhrātarbhadraṃ testu sadā dvija \|*  
*kautūhalaparāḥ sarve yatpṛcchāmastaducyatām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They said — “O Bhadra, O brother? Let you meet with welfare. We have a doubt about one thing and as such we wish to ask you about it You please tell me.”

## \|\| 1.118.10 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhadro vacanamabravīt \|*  
*viṣaye sati vaktavyaṃ yanmayā tadihocyatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On listening to their words, Bhadra said — “You ask me whatever you want to ask. I shall tell you.

## \|\| 1.118.11 \|\|

*nāhaṃ matsarayukto vai na ca rāgādidūṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhavanto mama sarve vai bhrātaro guravastathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. I do not suffer from jealousy or attraction, therefore, I would not try to conceal anything. All of you are my brothers and being my elders, you are my preceptors as well.

## \|\| 1.118.12 \|\|

*kathaṃ na kathayāmyeṣa bhavatāṃ putrasammitaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbruvantu māṃ sarve bhrātaro yadvivakṣitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I am like your son and I shall tell you the truth. Therefore, O brothers, whatever you are desirous of asking me, you can do so, without hesitation.”

## \|\| 1.118.13-15 \|\|

*bhrātara ūcuḥ \|*  
*na tathā puṣpadhūpeṣu na tathā dvijapūjane \|*  
*suprayatnaṃ tu paśyāmo bhānorāyatane param \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yathāhani tathā rātrau yathā rātrau tathāhani \|*  
*tava dīpapradānāya yathā bhadra sadodyamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tattvaṃ tatkathayāsmākaṃ haṃta kautūhalaṃ param \|*  
*yannāma dīpadānasya bhavatā viditaṃ phalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The brothers said — “O Bhadra, we notice the enormous efforts being made by you for the burning of lamps in the Sun temple. But such an effort is not seen for the worship of the god, nor for the worship of the Brahmanas by offering of flowers etc. We find enormous surprise and anxiety in this. Therefore, whatever merits accrue out of the donating of the lamp, you please tell us in detail.

## \|\| 1.118.16-17 \|\|

*tadetatkathayāsmākaṃ saviśeṣaṃ mahābala \|*  
*evamuktastatastaistu bhrātṛbhiścodito mudā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vyājahāra sa bhrātṝṇāṃ na kiñcidapi suvrata \|*  
*punaḥ punarasau taistu bhrātṛbhiścodito mudā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. O valorous one, you speak out the details about the same.” O Suvrata! At these words of the brothers, with a delightful heart Bhadra kept silent for some time. But on their insistence, Bhadra, who was bestowed with a virtue of compassion, started answering their questions appropriately.

## \|\| 1.118.18 \|\|

*dākṣiṇyasāro bhadrastu kathayāmāsa kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*bhavatāṃ kautukaṃ caitadatīvālpe'pi vastuni \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He said, O Suvrata! For this small issue, all of you are getting excited. But I am detailing about my vrata. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.118.19 \|\|

*tadeṣa kathayāmyadya yadvrataṃ mama suvrata \|*  
*ikṣvākurājñastu purā vaśiṣṭho'bhūtpurohitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In earlier times, Vasishtha had been the family priest of the Ikshvaku family.

## \|\| 1.118.20-21 \|\|

*tena cāyatanaṃ bhānoḥ kāritaṃ sarayūtaṭe \|*  
*ahanyahani śuśrūṣāṃ puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dīpadānādibhiścaiva cakre tatra sa vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*kārtike dīpako bhaktyā pradattastena vai sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. On the bank of the river Sarayu, he built a Sun temple. He served the Sungod daily by offering flowers, incense, sandal paste and the lamps etc. During the month of Karttika, he regularly offered the tamps in the temple.

## \|\| 1.118.22-23 \|\|

*āsīnnirvāṇa evāsau devārcāpurato niśi \|*  
*devatāyatane cāhamavasaṃ vyathito bhṛśam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pūyaśoṇitaniṣpandaṃ prāvahankāyataḥ sadā \|*  
*śīrṇa ghrāṇo hyarvaravo durgaṃdhapatitastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. It is said that during the night, the burning of a lamp in a Sun temple, bestows salvation. I also lived during the night in front of the temple. The blood and pus emerged out of my body. I was suffering badly. My nose had dried up and I could not speak out clearly. Because of the bad smell emanating from my body, I had become fallen.

## \|\| 1.118.24-25 \|\|

*duṣṭabuddhyā sadā yuktaḥ saptāśvaṃ prati suvrata \|*  
*yadṛcchyā dīpadānaṃ vartyādīnāṃ vibhāvasau \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tattadbhuktvā sadā tuṣṭiṃ vrajāmi dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*ekadā tu tatastasminbhānorāyatane gataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. O Suvrata, still I had always the evil feelings toward the Sungod. O best of Brahmanas, the wicks of the lamps which were lighted in the Sun temple were made use of by me, because I used to consume them by stealing them. I always used to perform like this.

## \|\| 1.118.26-27 \|\|

*rātrau dṛṣṭā mayā tatra bhaktā jāgaraṇāgatāḥ \|*  
*pratiśrayaṃ prārthitāśca taiśca datto dayānvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vyādhito'yaṃ sudīnaśca iti kṛtvā matiṃ śubhām \|*  
*tato'hamagnimāśritya sthitasteṣāṃ samīpataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Once I went to the temple during the night and found that the devotees were quite awake. I prayed them to allow me to stay on. Finding me an ailing and poor person, they allowed me to stay on there. I got myself seated besides them, before the fire.

## \|\| 1.118.28 \|\|

*duṣṭāṃ buddhiṃ samāśritya hartukāmo vivasvataḥ \|*  
*divyamābharaṇaṃ bhānośchidrānveṣī dvijottamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O best of the Brahmanas, finding the image of the Sungod adorned with ornaments, I thought of stealing them. Then I thought of the methods of stealing.

## \|\| 1.118.29 \|\|

*sthito'haṃ bhojakā hyatra yadi nidrāṃ vrajanti te \|*  
*yenāsya vairivadbhānorharāmyābharaṇaṃ śubham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I thought — “I am here and these Bhojakas are also here. When all of them shall go to sleep, I shall quietly steal all the ornaments.

## \|\| 1.118.30-32 \|\|

*atha suptā bhojakāste nidrayā mohitāstadā \|*  
*nirvāṇāścāpi dīpāstu tato'hamutthitastvaran \|\| 30 \|\|*

*mudā paramayā yukto gato vaiśvānaraṃ prati \|*  
*prajvālyaṃ pāvakaṃ yatnāddīpavartintato mayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yojayitvā tu vai dīpe dhṛto dīpo'grato raveḥ \|*  
*hartukāmenābharaṇaṃ bhānordevasya suvrata \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Thereafter, when all the Bhojakas went to sleep and the lamp was also extinguished, I hurriedly got up and feeling delightful, moved towards the fire. Making all the efforts, I lighted the fire. I also lighted the wick of the lamp and placed it before the image of the Sungod to enable me to have a full view of the ornaments, decorating the Sun image.

## \|\| 1.118.33 \|\|

*atha te bhojakāḥ sarve vṛddhā devasya putrakāḥ \|*  
*taistu dṛṣṭo hyahaṃ tatra dīpahasto vibhāvasoḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Suddenly, all the old Bhojakas who resembled the sons of the Sungod, spotted me. I was standing before the Surya image, holding a lamp in my hand.

## \|\| 1.118.34 \|\|

*puraḥ sthito dvijaśreṣṭhā gṛhītaścāpi tairiha \|*  
*tato'haṃ tejasā mūḍho bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O best of the Brahmanas, with the lustre of the Sungod, I felt like a blind person. Therefore, all the people caught me.

## \|\| 1.118.35 \|\|

*vilapankaruṇaṃ teṣāṃ pādayoravaniṃ gataḥ \|*  
*taiścāpi karuṇāṃ kṛtvā mukto'haṃ bhojakaistadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thereafter, I started lamenting pathetically and fell at their feet. The Bhojakas therefore, out of compassion, freed me.

## \|\| 1.118.36-37 \|\|

*gṛhīto rājapuruṣaiḥ pṛṣṭaścāpi samantataḥ \|*  
*kimidaṃ bhavatārabdhaṃ devadevasya maṃdire \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dīpaṃ prajvālya duṣṭātmankathyatāṃ mā ciraṃ kuru \|*  
*ityuktvā tu tatastaistu śastrahastaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Then, coming out of the temple, the soldiers of the king surrounded me from all the sides. They caught me and asked me — “What had you been doing in the Sun temple, burning the lamp. O wicked person, you speak out the reason for the same atonce. Don’t delay” Thus speaking, all of them, holding weapons in their hands, stood around me.

## \|\| 1.118.38 \|\|

*tato'haṃ vyādhinā kliṣṭo bhayena ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*hitvā prāṇāngato yatra svayaṃ devo vibhāvasuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O best of Brahmanas, I had been suffering from ailment. I got immensely afraid and life deputed out of me. Thereafter, I went to the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.118.39 \|\|

*sthitvā kalpaṃ tatastatra yuṣmākaṃ bhrātṛtāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*eṣa prabhāvo dīpasya kārtike māsi suvratāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I stayed there for a kalpa and thereafter, became you brother. O Suvrata, this all happened due to the giving away of a lamp in the month of Karttika.

## \|\| 1.118.40-42 \|\|

*dattasyārkasya bhavane yasyeyaṃ vyuṣṭiruttamā \|*  
*duṣṭabuddhyā kṛtaṃ yattu mayā dīpapravartanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*bhagāyatanadīpasya tasyedaṃ bhujyate phalam \|*  
*kṣudhābhibhūtena mayā devadevasya bhūṣaṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*dīpaśca devapurato jvālito bhāskarasya tu \|*  
*tato jātismṛtirjanma prāntaṃ brāhmaṇaveśmani \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. This is the result of the same, though I had lighted the lamp with an evil mind and was suffering from hunger at that point of time and I intended to steal the ornaments from the temple at that point of time. For the same purpose, I had placed the lamp before the Sun after lighting the same. This happens to be the divine effect of the same that preserving the past memory, I was born in the family of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.118.43 \|\|

*kuṣṭhinā cāpi śūdreṇa prāptaṃ brāhmaṇyamuttamam \|*  
*nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇi sāṃgaṃ vedaṃ samāptavān \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In earlier birth, I had been a Shudra suffering from leprosy, but presently, I have been born in a Brahmana family and am engaged in the study of several Vedas and other scriptures.

## \|\| 1.118.44 \|\|

*duṣṭabuddhyā dhṛtāddīpātphalametanmahādbhutam \|*  
*prāptaṃ mayā dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kiṃ punardīpadāyinām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Because of my evil mind, I had kept the lamp there, but I earned an enormously good reward, then what to speak of the people, who give away charities with good intentions?

## \|\| 1.118.45 \|\|

*etasmātkāraṇāddīpānahamevamaharniśam \|*  
*prayacchāmi raverdhāmni jñātamasya hi yatphalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore, visiting the Sun temple daily, I light the lamp there, being well aware of the merit thereof.

## \|\| 1.118.46 \|\|

*yuṣmākamidamuktaṃ vai snehātsatyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*eṣa prabhāvo dīpasya kārtike māsi suvratāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Suvrata, I have narrated to you truthfully, out of my love for you. There is no doubt about it. This it the reward for giving away of a lamp in the month of Karttika.

## \|\| 1.118.47-49 \|\|

*arkāyatanadīpasya bhadrovocadyathā purā \|*  
*dinedine japannāma bhāskarasya samāhitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dadāti kārtike yastu bhagāyatanadīpakam \|*  
*jātismaratvaṃ prajñāṃ ca prākāśyaṃ sarvajantuṣu \|\| 48 \|\|*

*avyāhatendriyatvaṃ ca samāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sarvakālaṃ ca cakṣuṣmānmedhāvī dīpado naraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*
