47-49. Bhadra had in earlier times, spoken about the lighting of a lamp in the Sun temple. Therefore, during the month of Karttika, meditating upon the Sungod, his name should be recited and a lamp should be lighted in his temple and one who does so, according to Bhadra, he retains his earlier memory and glory among the people. He also achieves the healthy sense organs. Thus, a person who gives away a lamp in charity, has always the bright sight besides being illustrious.

## \|\| 1.118.50-52 \|\|

*jāyate narakaṃ cāpi tamaḥ saṃjñaṃ na paśyati \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhīṃ vā saptamīṃ vāpi pratipakṣaṃ ca yo naraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dīpaṃ dadāti yatnādyatphalaṃ tasya nibodha me \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ maṇiyuktaṃ ca manojñamatiśobhanam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dīpamālākulaṃ divyaṃ vimānamadhirohati \|*  
*tasmādāyatane bhānordīpāndadyātsadācyuta \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. Even when he falls in the hell, he would not have to face the dark hell. Now a person who bums the lamp (in the Sun temple) on the sixth and the seventh moon day of every fortnight and donates it, I shall recite the merits thereof. You please listen. He is gracefully seated over the divine plane which is beautiful and is decorated with gold and gems and the garlands of lamps. Therefore, O Acyuta, one should always donate a lamp in the Sun temple.

## \|\| 1.118.53 \|\|

*tāṃśca dattvā na hiṃsyācca na ca tailaviyojitān \|*  
*kurvīta dīpahartā tu mūṣakondhaśca jāyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The damaging and stealing of the lamps in the Sun temple or stealing of the oil meant for lamps is prohibited, because the one who steals the lamp, is born as blind or a rat.

## \|\| 1.118.54 \|\|

*tasmāddadyānnāharedvai śreyo'rthī dīpakaṃ naraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Therefore, the people desirous of welfare, should not steal the lamp after donating it.

## Chapter 119. Method of donating lamp

## \|\| 1.119.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*andhe tamasi duṣpāre narake patitātkila \|*  
*saṃkrośamānānsaṃkṣubdhānuvāca yamakiṅkaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahms said — The messengers of Yama spoke once to the people suffering badly, having fallen in the terrific and horrible Tamisra hell.

## \|\| 1.119.2-3 \|\|

*vilāpairalamatreti kiṃ vo vilapite phalam \|*  
*yatpramādādibhiḥ pūrvamātmāyaṃ samupekṣitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrvamālocitaṃ naitatkathamante bhaviṣyati \|*  
*idānīṃ yātanāṃ bhuṅdhvaṃ kiṃ vilāpaṃ kariṣyatha \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. You stop crying here. Your crying here would be of no use, because of your arrogance, you did not think of the release of your soul earlier, neglecting it always. You never thought about it. Then what could be done on your arrival here? Therefore, you have to face the suffering presently. Then why are you crying?

## \|\| 1.119.4 \|\|

*deho dināni svalpāni viṣayāścātidurbalāḥ \|*  
*etatko na vijānāti yena yūyaṃ pramādinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Who is not aware of the instability of the body, which is short lived and the worldly pleasures which are, without essence, and people become arrogant because of the same as has been done by you.

## \|\| 1.119.5-6 \|\|

*janturjanmasahasrebhya ekasminmānuṣo yadi \|*  
*sa tatrāpyatimūḍhātmā kiṃ bhogānabhidhāvati \|\| 5 \|\|*

*putradāragṛhakṣetrahitāya satatodyatāḥ \|*  
*na jānanti tato mūḍhāḥ svalpamapyātmano hitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. After thousands of years, when one is born in a human race, but becoming extremely foolish, getting involved in the worldly pleasures, he makes all the efforts to enjoy them. He makes all the efforts to look after his sons, wife, house and the region all the times. Not only that, he also disregards about his own health. Therefore, he is called a foolish person.

## \|\| 1.119.7 \|\|

*vañcito'haṃ mayā labdhamidamasmādupāgatam \|*  
*na vetti mohitaḥ kaścitprakrāntanarako naraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus living on earth, no sinful person getting confused in the world, is unable to think that he is depriving himself of the self redemption and what shall he achieve in lieu thereof?

## \|\| 1.119.8 \|\|

*na vetti sūryacandrādīnkālamātmānameva ca \|*  
*sākṣibhūtānaśeṣasya śubhasyehāśubhasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Getting entangled in the net of confusion, he disregards the good or bad deeds’, witness (the Sungod), besides the moon, the time or the god of death, self consciousness etc.

## \|\| 1.119.9-10 \|\|

*janmānyanyāni jāyante putradārādidehinām \|*  
*yadarthaṃ yatkṛtaṃ karma tasya janmaśatāni tu \|\| 9 \|\|*

*aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ mamatvaṃ narakeṣvapi \|*  
*krandate mātaraṃ tātaṃ pīḍyamāno'pi yatsvayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. “Though the sons and the wife, besides others, are also possessed by other creatures in other births as well, but I have spent all my life for their sake alone. Because of this, I had to travel through several births (yonis)” He never thinks about the same. It is surprising to find such a great influence of the confusion, that while living in the heaven, the reason for which such a great attachment is developed with the family, that a person, even while undergoing the physical torture, still cries for father, mother and others.

## \|\| 1.119.11 \|\|

*evamākṛṣṭacittānāṃ viṣayaiḥ svādutarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*nṛṇāṃ na jāyate buddhiḥ paramārthavilokinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Therefore, getting attracted towards tasteful things, one always gets involved in the same. The people never develop wisdom for the spiritualistic ideals.

## \|\| 1.119.12 \|\|

*tathā ca viṣayāsaṅge karotyavirataṃ manaḥ \|*  
*ko hi bhāro ravernāmni jihvāyāḥ parikīrtane \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Because for owning of the worldly comforts, their minds always remain desirous. They never think of getting relieved of the same. Otherwise for the tongue of a person, it would not have been difficult for him to recite the name of Surya.

## \|\| 1.119.13 \|\|

*vartitaile'lpamūlye ca yadvarttirlabhyate sudhā \|*  
*ato vai kataro lābhaḥ kā taścintā bhavettadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Similarly, burning of the lamp by draping oil in it, is not of much consequence and this can be achieved without making much efforts. The lamp can be achieved which amounts to achieving nectar, similarly you also get benefited with the same, without causing any worry.

## \|\| 1.119.14-15 \|\|

*yenāyateṣu hasteṣu svātaṃtrye sati dīpakaḥ \|*  
*mahāphalo bhānugṛhe na datto narakāpahāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*naro vilapate kiñcididānīṃ dṛśyate phalam \|*  
*asvātaṃtrye vilapatāṃ svātaṃtrye sati māninām \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Therefore, by remaining independent, a person, who with his vast hands, has not offered the powerful lamp which destroys the hell, he alone cries here after coming to this place, which is being witnessed by me. I have therefore, come to the conclusion that a person cries when he is in bondage and become arrogant, when he is free from bondage.

## \|\| 1.119.16 \|\|

*avaśyaṃ pātinaḥ prāṇā bhoktā jīvo'pyaharniśam \|*  
*dattaṃ ca labhate bhoktaṃ kāmayanviṣayānapi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The life from the body has to depart one day or the other. The jiva is there to daily suffer for the pleasure and pain. Therefore, by giving away the charities, one enjoys the pleasures of his liking.

## \|\| 1.119.17 \|\|

*etatsthānaṃ duṣkṛtairvā yuktaṃ cādya mayekṣitam \|*  
*idānīṃ kiṃ vilāpena sahadhvaṃ yadupāgatam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The hell is achieved as a result of the sins committed by a person. This fact too is well known to me. Therefore, what would you gain by your cries now?

## \|\| 1.119.18-19 \|\|

*yadyetadanabhīṣṭaṃ vo yadduḥkhaṃ samupasthitam \|*  
*tadadbhutamatiḥ pāpe na kartavyā kadācana \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kṛte'pi pāpake karmaṇyajñānādaghanāśanam \|*  
*kartavyamanavacchinnaṃ pūjanaṃ savituḥ sadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. You tolerate whatever is present before you. Because in case, you are not desirous of the painful situation present before you, then while living in your home, you would not have been entangled in sins. In case some sin was committed out of ignorance, then you should have adored the Sungod, who is the destroyer of the sins.

## \|\| 1.119.20 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*nārakāstadvacaḥ śrutvā tamūcuratiduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhāstṛṭtāpavisaṃsphuṭitatālukāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Brahma said — The dwellers of the hell, who had been dried up of hunger and thirst and their palates were dry, felt painful and said.

## \|\| 1.119.21 \|\|

*bho bhoḥ sādho kṛtaṃ karma yadasmābhistaducyatām \|*  
*narakasthairvipāko'yaṃ bhujyate yatsudāruṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O noble ones, by your shedding light on the deeds performed by the people earlier, you please enlighten us as to which of the deeds were performed by us, which have forced us to face the painful situation in the hell.

## \|\| 1.119.22 \|\|

*kiṅkara uvāca \|*  
*yuṣmābhiyauṃvanonmādānmuditairavivekibhiḥ \|*  
*ghṛtalobhena mārtaṇḍagṛhāddīpaḥ purā hṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The messengers of Yama said — In earlier times, getting arrogant with your youthful age and getting confused with ignorance, all of you feeling greedy for ghi, had stolen the lamps of the Sun temple.

## \|\| 1.119.23 \|\|

*tenāsminnarake ghore kṣuttṛṣṇāparipīḍitāḥ \|*  
*bhavantaḥ patitāstīvre śītavātavidāritāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Because of the same, you have always to suffer from hunger and thirst. Your limbs have been shattered because of the cold wave of the wind. Under such conditions, you have to face the immensely painful situation of the hell.

## \|\| 1.119.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etatte dīpadānasya pradīpaharaṇasya ca \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ca kathitaṃ bhāskarāyatane'cyuta \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Brahma said — O Acyuta! Thus, I have related the sin of removing the lamp from the Sun temple and the merit for burning a lamp there.

## \|\| 1.119.25 \|\|

*sarvatraiva hi dīpasya pradānaṃ kṛṣṇa śasyate \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa jagaddhāturbhāskarasya niveśane \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Krishna! Therefore, the giving away of the lamp has always and everywhere been considered to be praiseworthy. But particularly in the temple of the Sungod, the burning of a lamp is extremely praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.119.26 \|\|

*ye'ndhā mūkā badhirā nirvivekā hīnāstaistairdānasādhanairvṛṣṇivīra \|*  
*taistairdīpāḥ sādhulokapradattā devāgārādanyataḥ kṛṣṇa nītāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Vrishni warrior! Therefore, the number of the people who are blind, dumb, deaf, foolish, those who are without resources, they must have surely stolen the lamps from the Sun temples.

## Chapter 120. Method of Sun worship

## \|\| 1.120.1 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*bhagavanprāṇinaḥ sarve viṣarogādyupadravaiḥ \|*  
*duṣṭagrahopaghātaiśca sarvakālamupadrutāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vishnu said — O lord, all the jivas are influenced with the worldly pleasures as well as the ailments and other disturbances, by which they feel painful.

## \|\| 1.120.2 \|\|

*ābhicārikakṛtyābhiḥ sparśarogaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*sadā sampīḍyamānāstu tiṣṭhantyambujasambhava \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lotus-born lord! He suffers from incantations causing disease, death and various other causes.

## \|\| 1.120.3 \|\|

*yena karmavipākena viṣarogādyupadravāḥ \|*  
*prabhavanti nṛṇāṃ tanme yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Therefore, as a result of such deeds, the poison and other ailments besides disturbances exercise their influence on human beings. You please enlighten me on these issues in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 1.120.4 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vratopavāsairyairbhānurnānyajanmani toṣitaḥ \|*  
*te narā devaśārdūla graharogādibhāginaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Brahma said — O lion among the gods, those who had not pleased the Sungod with the performing of vratas or fasting, they suffer from the planets as well as the ailments.

## \|\| 1.120.5 \|\|

*yairna tatpravaṇaṃ cittaṃ sarvadaiva naraiḥ kṛtam \|*  
*viṣagrahajvarāṇāṃ te manuṣyāḥ kṛṣṇa bhāginaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Similarly, the people who did not devote their mind in the adoration of the Sungod, they have to suffer from poison, the planets as well as the fevers.

## \|\| 1.120.6 \|\|

*ārogyaṃ paramāṃ vṛddhiṃ manasā yadyadicchati \|*  
*tattadāpnotyasaṃdigdhaṃ paratrādityatoṣaṇāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Because with the serving of the Sungod, one remains healthy, achieves prosperity and all his mental desires are fulfilled. He achieves all his desired things. Whatever he desires in his mind, the Sungod bestow him all those things.

## \|\| 1.120.7 \|\|

*nādhīnprāpnoti na vyādhīnna viṣayagrahabandhanam \|*  
*kṛtyāsparśabhayaṃ vāpi toṣite timirāpahe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the Sungod — the remover of darkness is pleased, all the mental and body ailments, the evil effect of the planets and other dangers are removed.

## \|\| 1.120.8 \|\|

*sarve duṣṭāḥ samāstasya saumyāstasya sadā grahāḥ \|*  
*devānāmapi pūjyo'sau tuṣṭo yasya divākaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, a person, with whom the Sungod gets pleased, all his enemies remain pacified. All the planets remain benevolent and he is adored even by the gods.

## \|\| 1.120.9-10 \|\|

*yaḥ samaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yathātmani tathā hite \|*  
*upavāsādinā yena toṣyate timirāpahaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*toṣite'sminprajānāthe narāḥ pūrṇamanorathāḥ \|*  
*arogāḥ sukhino nityaṃ bahudharmasukhānvitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. A person who treats all the living beings as equal and treats others in the same way as he treats his own kins besides the one who has pleasured the Sungod, with his vratas and fasting the Sungod gets pleased over him, after which all his desires are fulfilled. He always remains healthy, devoted to the faith and leads a comfortable life.

## \|\| 1.120.11 \|\|

*na teṣāṃ śatravo naiva śarīrādyabhicārakam \|*  
*graharogādikaṃ cāpi pāpakāryupajāyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Similarly, a person who has worshipped the Sungod, whenever some calamities or miseries befall on him, the Sungod surely and expeditiously removes them.

## \|\| 1.120.12 \|\|

*avyāhatāni devasya dhanajālāni taṃ naram \|*  
*rakṣanti sakalāpatsu yena śvetādhipo'rcitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Vishnu said — Those, who never worshipped the Sungod, had been facing various types of miseries. Then how should a person remain healthy, free from fever or other ailments? You please tell us.

## \|\| 1.120.13 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*anārādhitamārtaṇḍā ye narāḥ duḥkhabhāginaḥ \|*  
*te kathaṃ nīrujaḥ santu vijvarā gatakalmaṣāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Brahma said — O lord of gods and lord of the universe! You are the preceptor of the gods, you must worship the Sungod with flowers.

## \|\| 1.120.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ārādhayantu deveśaṃ puṣpeṇaivamanaupamam \|*  
*bhāskaraṃ tu jagannāthaṃ sarvadevaguruṃ param \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Vishnu said — O lord of the Devas! How should a person worship the Sungod, when he is suffering from desires? You kindly speak out to me for my own welfare.

## \|\| 1.120.15 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*doṣābhibhūtadehaistu kathamārādhanaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*karttavyaṃ vada deveśa bhaktyā śreyo'rthamātmanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Such a person has no enemy. His body remains unaffected by the outward evil forces. All his evil planets and ailments are pacified.

## \|\| 1.120.16-17 \|\|

*anugrāhyo'smi yadi te mamāyaṃ bhaktimāniti \|*  
*tanmayopadiśa tvaṃ ca mahadārādhanaṃ raveḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*anantamajaraṃ devaṃ duṣṭasandehanāśanam \|*  
*ārādhayitumicchāmi bhagavantastvadanujñayā \|*  
*yenāhaṃ tvatprasādena bhaveyamativikramaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. In case, I feel beholden to you being your devotee, then you should surely reveal to me the method of adoring the Sungod. Submitting to your command, I intend to worship the endless Sungod who is the destroyer of the doubts, besides the wicked people. By your pleasure and by the grace of the Sungod, let me gain enormous strength.

## \|\| 1.120.18 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*anugrāhyo'si devasya nūnamavyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*ārādhanāya te viṣṇo yadetatpravaṇaṃ manaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Brahma said — For the worship of the Sungod with imperceptible birth, when an idea has been culminated in your mind, at the same moment you have been beholden for the same.

## \|\| 1.120.19-20 \|\|

*yadi devapatiṃ bhānumārādhayitumicchasi \|*  
*bhagavantamanādyaṃ ca bhava vaivasvato'cyuta \|\| 19 \|\|*

*na hyavaivasvatairbhānurjñātuṃ stotuṃ ca śakyate \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ vā śakyate mūḍhaiḥ praveṣṭuṃ kuta eva tu \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. O Acyuta! Therefore, in case you intend to worship the Sungod, then try to first become favourite of the Sungod. Because without becoming his favourite, his knowledge, prayer and audience with him can never take place like ignorant people.

## \|\| 1.120.21 \|\|

*tadbhaktiprārthitāḥ pūtā narāstadbhakticetasaḥ \|*  
*vaivasvatā bhavantyevaṃ vivasvantaṃ viśanti ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With the developing of the sense of his devotion in your mind, one is known as his favourite.

## \|\| 1.120.22 \|\|

*anekajanmasaṃsāracite pāpasamuccaye \|*  
*nākṣīṇe jāyate puṃsāṃ mārtaṇḍābhimukhī matiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Therefore, with the accumulation of all the sins of the past births unless get destroyed, upto that time the adoration of the Sungod would not be possible.

## \|\| 1.120.23 \|\|

*pradveṣaṃ yāti mārtaṇḍe dvijānvedāṃśca nindati \|*  
*yo narastaṃ vijānīyādasurāṃśasamudbhavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person, who treats the Sungod of having been born of the race of demons, he is extremely jealous of the Sungod and denounces the Brahmanas as well as the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.120.24 \|\|

*pāṣaṇḍeṣu ratiḥ puṃsāṃ hetuvādānukūlatā \|*  
*jāyate dambhamāyāmbhaḥ patitānāṃ durātmanām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Because, the people who are drowned in farcical elements and illusion, get attracted towards falsehood because they are helped in useless discussions.

## \|\| 1.120.25 \|\|

*yadā pāpakṣayaḥ puṃsāṃ tadā vedadvijātiṣu \|*  
*bhānau ca yajñapuruṣe śraddhā bhavati naiṣṭhikī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus, with the destruction of the sins, the people develop natural faith in the Vedas, Brahmanas besides Surya, who happens to yajna Purusha.

## \|\| 1.120.26 \|\|

*yadā svalpāvaśeṣastu narāṇāṃ pāpasañcayaḥ \|*  
*tadā bhojakavipreṣu bhānau pūjāṃ prakurvate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Some of the accumulated sins of the people are left out and at that point of time, the people start adoration of Brahmanas, Bhojakas as well as the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.120.27 \|\|

*bhramatāmatra saṃsāre narāṇāṃ karmadurgame \|*  
*karāvalambano hyeko bhaktiprīto divākaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Because in the different world of the actions, it is only the Sungod who comes to the rescue of the people, holding their hands.

## \|\| 1.120.28 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ vaivasvato bhūtyā sarvapāpaharaṃ harim \|*  
*ārādhaya samaṃ bhaktyā prītimabhyeti bhāskaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Therefore, you becoming a Vaivasvata, must adore the Sungod who is the destroyer of the sins, because the Sungod gets pleased with those who are devoted to him.

## \|\| 1.120.29 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*kiṃ lakṣaṇā bhavantyete narā vaivasvatā guṇaiḥ \|*  
*yacca vaivasvataṃ kāryaṃ tanme kathaya kañjaja \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Vishnu said — O born of the lotus flower, what are the symptoms of the Vaivasvata people? What are their special merits? You also tell me about their Vaivasvata or present activities.

## \|\| 1.120.30 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā prāṇināṃ yo na hiṃsakaḥ \|*  
*bhāvabhaktaśca mārtaṇḍa kṛṣṇa vaivasvato hi saḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Brahma said — O Krishna! A person who does not cause the slightest injury by his mind, speech or actions and also remains devoted to the Sungod, he is known as Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.31 \|\|

*yo bhojakadvijāndevānnityameva namasyati \|*  
*na ca bhoktā parasvāderviṣṇo vaivasvato hi saḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Similarly, those who respect the Bhojaka, Brahmana and the gods daily and does not aspire to usurp the riches of others, he is called Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.32 \|\|

*sarvāndevānraviṃ vetti sarvāṃllokāṃśca bhāskaram \|*  
*tebhyaścānanyamātmānaṃ kṛṣṇa vaivasvato hi saḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A person who conceives the Sungod in all the gods and also views the lokas as Bhaskara taking him to be endless, he is called Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.33-34 \|\|

*devaṃ manuṣyamanyaṃ vā paśupakṣipipīlikam \|*  
*tarupāṣāṇakāṣṭhādibhūmyambhodhiṃ divaṃ tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ cāpi devaśādvyatiriktaṃ divākarāt \|*  
*yo na jānāti taṃ vidyātkṛṣṇa vaivasvataṃ naram \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. O Krishna! In the way, a person who does not consider the gods, humans, animals, birds, ants, trees, stones, wood, the oceans, sky and he himself to be anything other than Divakara, such a person should be known as Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.35 \|\|

*sarvo vaivasvato bhāgo yadbhūtaṃ yadvyavasthitam \|*  
*iti vai yo vijānāti sa tu vaivasvato naraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In fact, Vaivasvata is always found present in the past, present and future. Thus, the Vaivasvata Purusha is conceived.

## \|\| 1.120.36 \|\|

*bhavabhītiṃ haratyeṣa bhaktibhāvena bhāvitaḥ \|*  
*vivasvāniti bhāvo yaḥ sa tu vaivasvato naraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Getting respected with noble feelings of the features of the Sungod, the fear of danger is removed. A person who preserves such a feeling in his mind, such a person is known as Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.37 \|\|

*bhāvaṃ na kurute yastu sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā sa ca vaivasvato naraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The people, who by their action, thought and behaviour do not preserve any ill feelings against others, they are known as Vaivasvata Purushas.

## \|\| 1.120.38 \|\|

*bāhyārthanirapekṣo yaḥ kriyāṃ bhaktyā vivasvataḥ \|*  
*bhāvena niṣpādayati jñeyo vaivasvato hi saḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Remaining unconcerned with the outer elements of the Sun, those who, with devotion and benevolent feelings, remains active in adoring him always, they should be known as Vaivasvatas.

## \|\| 1.120.39 \|\|

*nārayo yasya na snigdhā na bhedādhīnavṛttayaḥ \|*  
*vīkṣate sarvamevedaṃ bhānuṃ vaivasvato hi saḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A person having no friend or a foe and who has no discriminating mind and who visualizes the universe as the Sungod, such a person is indeed Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.40-41 \|\|

*sutapteneha tapasā yajñairvā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ gatiṃ na narā yanti yāṃ tu vaivasvato gataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yena sarvātmanā bhānau bhaktyā bhāvo niveśitaḥ \|*  
*devaśreṣṭha kṛtārthatvācchlāghyo vaivasvato hi saḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Because the position which is achieved by a Vaivasvata, the same cannot be achieved with the performing of the prolonged tapas, or performing I yajnas giving huge amount of dakshinas to the people. O best of the gods, a person who dedicates his everything to the Sungod with utmost devotion, then because of his being successful, he is praiseworthy as a Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 1.120.42 \|\|

*api naḥ sa kule dhanyo jāyeta kulapāvanaḥ \|*  
*bhāskaraṃ bhaktibhāvena yastu vai pūjayiṣyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thus, a person, who with utmost devotion and noble feelings, adore the Sungod or get him adored from others, he would be graceful for the entire race and shall purify the same.

## \|\| 1.120.43 \|\|

*yaḥ kārayati devārcāṃ hadayālambinīṃ raveḥ \|*  
*sa naro'rkamavāpnoti dharmadhvajamanaupamam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A person who worships the image of Surya, he achieves dharma, flag and the Sungod in an excellent manner.

## \|\| 1.120.44 \|\|

*yaśca devālayaṃ bhaktyā bhānoḥ kārayate sthiram \|*  
*sa sapta puruṣāṃllokānbhānornayati mānavaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A person, who with devotion builds a strong Sun temple, he ensures his seven generations to live in the Sun loka.

## \|\| 1.120.45 \|\|

*yāvantobdānhi devārcā ravestiṣṭhati maṃdire \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi puṣpottaragṛhe vaset \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The period upto which the puja is carried out in that temple, the person would live in the Pushpaka plane for an equivalent number of thousands of years.

## \|\| 1.120.46 \|\|

*devārcālakṣaṇopeto yadgṛhe santato vidhiḥ \|*  
*niṣkāmaṃ ca mano yasya sa yātyakṣarasāmyatām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Therefore, the household in which the Sungod is daily worshipped and the mind of the performer of the puja is free from the desires, he achieves everlasting similarity with the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.120.47 \|\|

*puṣpāṇyatisugaṃdhīni manojñāni ca yaḥ pumān \|*  
*prayacchati jagannāthe saptāśve jyotiṣāṃ patau \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra jyotiḥ sanātanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. A person who offers the Sungod, mounted over the resplendent chariot, the garland of fragrant flowers, he achieves the excellent place in the eternal Brahman.

## \|\| 1.120.48-49 \|\|

*yasya yasya vihīno yo deśo yadvarjitaṃ ca yat \|*  
*dhūpāṃśca vividhāṃstāṃstāngaṃdhāḍhyaṃ suvilepanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*dīpavartyupahārāṃśca yaccābhīṣṭamathātmanaḥ \|*  
*naraḥ sonudinaṃ yajñānkarotyārādhanādraveḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Thus, various type of essences, fragrant sandal paste, lamp lighted with clarified butter and presents of other things which are dear to the devotee, when offered to the Sungod, it should be considered that he actually performs a yajna lay for the Sun.

## \|\| 1.120.50 \|\|

*yajñeśo bhagavānbhānurmakhairapi sa toṣyate \|*  
*bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsaṃbhāravistarāḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpyante dhanayutairmanuṣyairnālpasaṃcayaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Though, the Sungod who is the lord of the yajnas, is also pleased with the performing of the yajnas, but for performing of the yajna many sources have to be tapped besides enormous arrangements have to be made for that purpose. Therefore, the yajnas could be performed by wealthy people alone and not the people with limited means.

## \|\| 1.120.51 \|\|

*bhaktyā tu puruṣaiḥ pūjā kṛtā dūrvāṃkurairapi \|*  
*raverdadāti hi phalaṃ sarvayajñaiḥ sudurlabham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. But when a devotee worships the Sungod simply by offering of the durva grass, the Sungod bestow on such a person, the merit of performing all the yajnas, which is difficult to be achieved.

## \|\| 1.120.52-53 \|\|

*yāni puṣpāṇi hṛdyāni dhūpagandhānulepanam \|*  
*dayitaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ yacca tathā rakte ca vāsasī \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yāni cābhyavahāryāṇi bhakṣyāṇi ca phalāni ca \|*  
*prayaccha tāni mārtaṇḍa bhavethāścaiva tanmanāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Therefore, a person, by offering fragrant flowers as per his means, fragrant pastes, beautiful ornaments, two pieces of red cloth, the best of eatables and fruits, should remain devoted to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.120.54 \|\|

*ādyaṃ taṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ yathā bhaktyā prasādaya \|*  
*ārādhya yāti taṃ devaṃ yattadbrahma paraṃ smṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. First of all, a person should please the Sungod with his utmost devotion, because Brahman could be achieved only with the adoration of the gods.

## \|\| 1.120.55 \|\|

*puṇyaistīrthodakaiḥ puṣpairmadhunā sarpiṣā tathā \|*  
*kṣīreṇa snāpayeddevamacyutaṃ jagatāṃ patim \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Therefore, collecting the water from the auspicious places of pilgrimage besides flowers, honey, ghi, milk, the Sungod should be bathed.

## \|\| 1.120.56 \|\|

*dadhikṣīrahradānpuṇyāṃstato lokānmadhucyutaḥ \|*  
*prayāsyasi yaduśreṣṭha nirvṛtiṃ cāpi aiśvarīm \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O best of the race of Yadus, by so doing, you would achieve the banks full of curd, milk, honey, besides the auspicious lokas and the divine place.

## \|\| 1.120.57 \|\|

*stotrairhadyairyathā vādyairbrāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*manasaścaikatāyogādārādhaya divākaram \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Therefore, reciting the stotras which appeal the heart in company of the music for the pleasure of the Brahmanas, you should worship the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.120.58-59 \|\|

*ārādhyaṃ taṃ mahādevo mahacchabdamavāptavān \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ahaṃ cāpi samastānāṃ lokānāṃ sṛṣṭikārakaḥ \|*  
*tamārādhya vivasvantaṃ tatprasādājjanārdana \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Because by adoring the Sungod, lord Shiva achieved his glory earning him the title of Mahadeva. By adoring the same Sungod and by his grace, I have achieved the position of the creator of the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.120.60 \|\|

*tvamapyetaṃ hṛṣīkeśa tatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*samartho devaśatrūṇāṃ daityānāṃ nāśane sadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. O Hrishikesha! Therefore, by his grace, you also will have strength to destroy all the demons who are inimical to the gods. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.120.61 \|\|

*dakṣiṇaḥ kiraṇastasya yo devasya vivasvataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tasmātsamutpanno vedavedāṅgasammitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I have been born of Surya from his right ray, with all the Vedas and Vedangas.

## \|\| 1.120.62 \|\|

*vāmo yaḥ kiraṇaḥ kṛṣṇa raśmimālākulaḥ sadā \|*  
*tasmādīśaḥ samutpannaḥ pārvatīdayito'cyuta \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O Krishna! Similarly, from the left ray wearing the garland of rays, Shiva — the beloved of Parvati, was born.

## \|\| 1.120.63 \|\|

*vakṣasastvaṃ samutpannaḥ śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*tathāmbujakarā devī ambujānanavallabhā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. From his chest, you holding the conch, cakra and club, besides Lakshmi — your spouse, were born holding a lotus in her hand.

## \|\| 1.120.64 \|\|

*samārādhya balaṃ kīrtiṃ śriyaṃ cāvāptavānaham \|*  
*tathā ttvamapi rājendra tamārādhya divākaram \|*  
*yānyānicchasi kāmāṃstvaṃ tāṃstānsarvānavāpsyasi \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O Rajendra! Since I achieved all my glory and strength, besides fame by his devotion only, similarly, you should also have all your desires fulfilled by adoring the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.120.65 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ saṃvādaṃ vidhikṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*so'pi kāmānavāpyāgryāṃstato lokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thus, a person who would listen to the conversation between Brahma and Krishna daily, he would achieve the excellent success.

## \|\| 1.120.66-67 \|\|

*gairikaṃ yānamārūḍho yuktaṃ kuñjaravājibhiḥ \|*  
*tejasāmbujasaṃkāśaḥ prabhayāṇḍaja sannibhaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*kāntyā caṃdrasamo rājanvṛndārakagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*gandharvairgīyamānastu tathā cāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. By so doing, he will make him board the plane of silver, where he would demand for an excellent loka with a chariot in which the houses are yoked. At that point of time, he would possess the lustre resembling the Sungod, and the moon shine. He would be then pleased by the gods and the Apsaras, dancing at the tune of the music.

## Chapter 121. Chiseling of the body of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.121.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*śarīralekhanaṃ1 bhānoruktaṃ saṃkṣepatastvayā \|*  
*vistarācchrotumicchāmi tanmamācakṣva suvrata \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O Suvrata, you had briefly narrated the chiseling of the body of the Sungod. I intend to listen to the same exhaustively. You kindly do so.

## \|\| 1.121.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*piturgṛhaṃ tu yātāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ kurunaṃdana \|*  
*bhāskaraściṃtayāmāsa saṃjñā madrūpakāriṇī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O son of Kuru race, after the departure of Samjna to her parents’ home, the Sungod felt concerned, that Samjna was desirous of her pleasant body.

## \|\| 1.121.3-4 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare brahmā tatrāgatya divākaram \|*  
*avravīnmadhurāṃ vācaṃ raveḥ prītikarāṃ śubhām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ādidevo'si devānāṃ vyāptametattvayā jagat \|*  
*śvaśuro viśvakarmā te rūpaṃ nirvartayiṣyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. At the same time, Brahma arrived there and spoke in a pleasant voice. His words were quite pleasant which pleased the Sungod. He said — “You are the foremost of the gods and you presently pervade the entire world. Therefore, your father-in-law — Vishvakarma, would surely make you pleasant looking.

## \|\| 1.121.5 \|\|

*evamuktvā raviṃ brahmā viśvakarmāṇamabravīt \|*  
*nivartasya mārtaṇḍaṃ svarūpaṃ tatsuśobhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Brahma, after thus speaking to the Sungod, further said to Vishvakarma — “You make the body of Martanda beautiful with all the auspicious symptoms.”

## \|\| 1.121.6 \|\|

*tato brahmasamādeśādbhra mimāropya bhāskaram \|*  
*rūpaṃ nirvartayāmāsa viśvakarmā śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At the command of Brahma, Vishvakarma made the Sungod lie down on earth, slowly started changing his body, beautifying it. He made his body beautiful.

## \|\| 1.121.7 \|\|

*tatastuṣṭāva taṃ brahmā sarvadevagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*guhyairnānāvidhaiḥ stotrairvedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, together with all the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas, Brahma prayed the Sungod with various stotras.

## \|\| 1.121.8 \|\|

*svasti te'stu jagannātha dharmavarṣahimākara \|*  
*śāṃtiste sarvalokānāṃ devadeva divākara \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O lord of the universe, you are well-versed in dharma and abode of snow, let you meet with welfare. You are the lord of gods of all the lokas, let you be peaceful.

## \|\| 1.121.9 \|\|

*tato rudraśca viṣṇvādyāḥ stuvaṃtastaṃ divākaram \|*  
*tejaste vardhatāṃ deva likhyate'pi divaspate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter, Rudra and Vishnu also eulogized the Sungod. They said — “O lord of the days, let your lustre increase on chiseling your body.”

## \|\| 1.121.10 \|\|

*indraścāgatya taṃ devaṃ likhyamānamathāstuvat \|*  
*jaya deva jayasveti tattvado'si jagatpate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Indra also arrived there and then praised the chiseling of the body of the Sungod, saying — “O Deva, victory to you. O lord of the universe, you are the bestower of sattva”

## \|\| 1.121.11 \|\|

*ṛṣayastu tataḥ sapta viśvāmitrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ svastisvastītivādinaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the seven Rishis, making Vishvamitra to lead them, prayed welfare for the Sungod. They offered several stotras to him at the same time.

## \|\| 1.121.12-13 \|\|

*vedoktābhirathāśīrbhirvālakhilyāśca tuṣṭuvuḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ nātha mokṣiṇāṃ mokṣo dhyeyastvaṃ dhyānināmapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*prajābhyaścaiva deveśa śaṃ no'stu jagataḥ pate \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Then the Valakhilyas offering him blessings as prescribed in the Vedas, prayed him — “O lord, you bestow salvation to those who are desirous of it. You are the final goal for those who meditate upon you. You are the place desired by the people. All the creatures are lodged in you. Therefore, O lord of the Devas, for we people, you bestow welfare on us.

## \|\| 1.121.14 \|\|

*tvatto bhavati vai nityaṃ jagatsaṃlīyate tvayi \|*  
*tvamekastvaṃ dvidhā caiva tridhā ca tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The entire world emerged out of you and also gets absorbed in you. Thus inspite of your being one, you surely take to two or three forms.

## \|\| 1.121.15-16 \|\|

*tvayaikena jagatsṛṣṭaṃ tvayaikena prabodhitam \|*  
*tato vidyādharagaṇā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve śirobhiḥ praṇatā ravim \|*  
*ūcurevaṃvidhā vāco manaḥ śrotrasukhapradāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. You alone have created this universe besides making it conscious ” Thereafter, the Vidyadharas, Yakshas, Rakshasas and the serpents also offered their salutation to the Sungod with folded hand and lowered heads. They spoke the words, which pleased the mind as well as the ears.

## \|\| 1.121.17-18 \|\|

*sahyaṃ bhavatu te tejo bhūtānāṃ bhūtabhāvana \|*  
*hāhā hūhūstataścaiva tumbururnāradastathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*upagātuṃ samārabdhā gāmuccaiḥ kuśalā ravim \|*  
*ṣaḍjamadhyamagāṃdhāragrāmatrayaviśāradāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. O great lord! Let your lustre be tolerable for the living beings. Thereafter, the eminent singers like Haha-Huhu, Tumburu and Narada started singing for the Sungod quite loudly. All the three persons are well-versed in three types of Sadja, Madhyama and Gandhara styles of music.

## \|\| 1.121.19-21 \|\|

*mūrcchanābhistataścaiva tathā dhaivatapañcamaiḥ \|*  
*nānānubhāvamandraiśca ardhamandraistathaiva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*trisādhanaiḥ prakāraistu vādyatālasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca urvaśī ca tilottamā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*menakā sahajanyā ca rambhā cāpsarasāṃ varā \|*  
*hāvabhāvavilāsaiśca kurvatyo'bhinayānbahūn \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Thereafter, the musical feats were played on different notes, accompanied with three types of musical instruments. The Apsaras like Vishvachi, Ghritachi, Urvashi, Tilottama, Menaka, Sahajanya and other dancers including Rambha, displayed their performance of dances.

## \|\| 1.121.22 \|\|

*tato'tīva kalaṃ geyaṃ madhuraṃ ca pravartate \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ devasaṃghānāṃ manaḥ śrotrasukhapradam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereafter, sweet and beautiful songs of the gods started, which made the mind and the ears extremely comfortable.

## \|\| 1.121.23 \|\|

*pravādyaṃ tu tatastatra vīṇāvaṃśādi suvrata \|*  
*paṇavāḥ puṣkarāścaiva mṛdaṅgāḥ paṭahāstathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O Suvrata! In the dance, vina, flute, panva, small drums, pushkara, cymbals, kettle drums and the instruments producing deep sound, were used.

## \|\| 1.121.24-27 \|\|

*devadundubhayaḥ śaṃkhāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*gāyadbhiścaiva gandharvairnṛtyadbhiścāpsarogaṇaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tūryavāditraghoṣaiśca sarvaṃ kolāhalīkṛtam \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtaiḥ karapuṭaiḥ padyakuḍmalasannibhaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*lalāṭopari vinyastaiḥ praṇemuḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kolāhale tasminsarvadevasamāgame \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tejasaḥ śātanaṃ cakre viśvakarmā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. At places, the divine double drums were beaten. Hundreds and thousands of conches were blown. Thus, with the singing of the Gandharvas, dancing of Apsaras and sounding of trumpets, there rose a tumultuous sound. Thereafter, like the blossomed lotus flower, placing the folded hands over the head, all the gods offered their salutation to the Sungod. Then, in the very presence of the gods, during the thundering sound, Vishvakarma slowly chiseled out the lustre of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.121.28 \|\|

*iti himajalagharmakālahetorharakamalāsanaviṣṇusaṃstutasya \|*  
*tadupari likhanaṃ niśamya bhānorvrajati divākaralokamāyuṣonte \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Like water of the snow melts with the sunshine during the division of the time, the Sungod, who was being prayed by Brahma and Vishnu, got his body chiseled out. Those who listen to the story of the chiseling out of the body of the Sun, achieve the place of Divakara.

## Chapter 122. Prayer of Aditya (Sun)

## \|\| 1.122.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*tasminkāle samārūḍho likhyamāno divaspatiḥ \|*  
*brahmādibhiḥ stuto devairyathā vai tadvadasva me \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — At the time when the body of the Sungod was being scrapped, you please tell me the way in which Brahma and others offered prayer to him?

## \|\| 1.122.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājanyathā devo divaspatiḥ \|*  
*brahmādibhiḥ stuto devairṛṣibhiśca purā'nagha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O sinless king, the way the gods and the Rishis offered prayers to the Sungod, I am going to relate the same. You listen to the same attentively.

## \|\| 1.122.3 \|\|

*prayatnataḥ praṇatahitānukampine svarūpato lokavibhāvine namaḥ \|*  
*divaspate kamalakulāvabodhine namastamaḥ paṭasapaṭāvapāyine \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The living beings offer their salutation to the lord making all the efforts, for their benefit — “O compassionate lord, you are the creator of the universe from your own body. O lord of the day, salutation to you. You are the one who makes the bunches of the lotus flowers to bloom. You are the remover of darkness, like the tearing out of the cloth, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.122.4 \|\|

*pāvanātiśayapuṇyakarmaṇe naikakāmavibhavapradāyine \|*  
*bhāsurāmalamayūkhamāline sarvalokahitakāriṇe namaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You are immensely pure, performer of the auspicious deeds. You do not fulfil only a single desire, but bestow enormous riches as well. You are adored with the radiant and spotless garland of rays and are the bestower of welfare on all the lokas. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.122.5 \|\|

*ajāya lokatrayabhāvanāya bhūtātmane gopataye priyāya \|*  
*namo mahākāruṇikottamāya sūryāya lokatrayabhāvanāya \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. You are without birth, protector of all the lokas, besides Bhutatma, Gopati (lord of rays), loveable, the great and the lord with excellent compassion. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.122.6 \|\|

*vivasvate jñānakṛtāntarātmane jagatpratiṣṭhāya jagaddhitaiṣiṇe \|*  
*svayambhuve lokasamastacakṣuṣe surottamāyāmitatejase namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Sungod, you bestow knowledge to the inner soul. You establish the world doing good to the same. You are self born and the eyes of all the lokas. You are the best of the gods possessing enormous lustre. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.122.7 \|\|

*nijodayāya suragaṇamaulimaṇe jagatā tvaṃ mahitastvamurumayūkhasahasratapāḥ \|*  
*jagati vibho vatamasatuda vanatimirāsavapāvana madādbhavati vilohitavigrahatātimiravināśinamugraṃ sutarāṃ tribhuvanabhāprakaraiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You are the gem of the heads of the gods. The world has worshipped you for its upliftment. You, establishing yourself with your vastness, perform tapas always. O competent one, you destroy the darkness of the world. You purify the darkness of the forest. Your body has become red because of the arrogance you possess. You are the light of the three worlds. You remove the darkness of the three worlds. Salutation to your terrific form.

## \|\| 1.122.8 \|\|

*rathāmāruhya1 samāmayaṃ bhramasi sadā jagato hitadaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Mounting the chariot in order to move for a year, you always keep on roaming about. You are benevolent to the world.”

## \|\| 1.122.9 \|\|

*ityevaṃ saṃstuto devo bhāskaro vedhasā purā \|*  
*daivataiśca mahābāho śivaviṣṇvādibhirnṛpa \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O valorous one, similarly in earlier times, Brahma had offered prayer to the Sungod. Similarly, the gods like Shiva and Vishnu also eulogized the Sungod.

## Chapter 123. Prayer of Aditya (Sun)

## \|\| 1.123.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*bhūyo'pi kathayasvemāṃ kathāṃ sūryasamāśritām \|*  
*na tṛptimadhigacchāmi śṛṇvannetāṃ kathāṃ mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O sage, you kindly repeat the story relating to the Sungod, because the mind does not feel satisfied even after listening to it.

## \|\| 1.123.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvācaṃ \|*  
*bhāskarasya kathāṃ puṇyāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*vakṣyāmi kathitāṃ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā lokakartṛṇā1 \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — The auspicious story of the Sungod which destroys all the sins, which was narrated in earlier times by Brahma, the same is going to be repeated by me.

## \|\| 1.123.3 \|\|

*ṛṣayaḥ paripṛcchanti brahmaloke pitāmaham \|*  
*tāpitāḥ sūryakiraṇaistejasā sampramohitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Once the Rishis went to Brahmaloka. They were suffering from the heat of the sun, which made them almost fainting. They asked lord Brahma.

## \|\| 1.123.4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ko'yaṃ dīpto mahātejā havīrāśisamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*etadveditumicchāmaḥ prabhāvo'sya kutaḥ prabho \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Rishis said — O lord! Who is this lord who is illuminating resplendently, and is bright like the payasam, I would like to know. I also want to know as to where from, he achieved this lustre?

## \|\| 1.123.5 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tamobhūteṣu lokeṣu naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*pravṛtte guṇahetutve pūrvaṃ buddhirajāyata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Brahma said — He is the mobile and immobile form of the dark universe. After the destruction of the earth, at the time of Pravritti or restart, the intelligence emerged first of all.

## \|\| 1.123.6 \|\|

*ahaṃkārastato jāto mahābhūtapravartakaḥ \|*  
*vāyvagnirāpaḥ khaṃ bhūmistatastvaṇḍamajāyata \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. From that the arrogance or Ahamkara which rotates in the Mahabhutas is born. Then after the emerging of wind, fire, water, sky and earth, an egg was also born.

## \|\| 1.123.7 \|\|

*tasminnaṇḍa ime lokāḥ sapta vai saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*pṛthvī ca saptabhirdvīpaiḥ samudraiścāpi saptabhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The seven lokas were lodged in the same, together with the seven islands, seven oceans, and the earth was also lodged in the same.

## \|\| 1.123.8 \|\|

*tatraivāvasthito hyāsamahaṃ viṣṇurmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pramūḍhāstamasā sarve pradhyātā īśvaraṃ param \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, Vishnu and Maheshvara were also lodged in the same. Thereafter, tamoguna covered with darkness, started meditating for Ishvara (in the same).

## \|\| 1.123.9-10 \|\|

*tato bhidya mahātejaḥ prādurbhūtaṃ tamonudam \|*  
*dhyānayogena cāsmābhirvijñātaṃ savitustathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jñātvā ca paramātmānaṃ sarva eva pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*divyābhiḥ stutibhirdevaṃ saṃstotumupacakramuḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Thereafter, breaking the egg, the enormous lustre of the Sun emerged. It was known by us by means of dhyana yoga. Then realising about the great soul, all of them reciting stutis, individually started adorning the lord.

## \|\| 1.123.11 \|\|

*ādidevo'si devānāmīśvarāṇāṃ tvamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*ādikartāsi bhūtānāṃ devadeva sanātana \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O lord of gods, O eternal one! You are the eternal lord of the gods, the supreme Ishvara of all the Ishvaras, besides being the initial creator of the living beings.

## \|\| 1.123.12 \|\|

*jīvanaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ devagandharvarakṣasām \|*  
*munikinnarasiddhānāṃ tathaivoragapakṣiṇām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You happen to be the life of all the living beings, the gods, Gandharvas, sages, Kinnaras, Siddhas, serpents, the birds and others.

## \|\| 1.123.13 \|\|

*tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ mahādevastvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vāyurindraśca somaśca vivasvānvaruṇastathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. You represent Brahma, Shiva, Vishnu Prajapati, Vayu, Indra, Soma, Vivasvan and Varuna.

## \|\| 1.123.14 \|\|

*tvaṃ kālaḥ sṛṣṭikartā ca hartā trātā prabhustathā \|*  
*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā vidyudindradhanūṃṣi ca \|*  
*pralayaḥ prabhavaścaiva vyaktāvyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. You are Kala, creator, destroyer, rescuer and the lord. Similarly, you are the rivers, oceans, mountains, lightning, rainbow, destroyer and creator of all. You are eternal, visible and invisible lord.

## \|\| 1.123.15 \|\|

*īśvarātparato vidyā vidyāyāḥ parataḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*śivātparataro devastvameva parameśvara \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Vidya or knowledge is said to be greater than Ishvara. Shiva is better than that, you are better than Shiva as Parameshvara.

## \|\| 1.123.16 \|\|

*sarvataḥ pāṇipādastvaṃ sarvato'kṣiśiromukhaḥ \|*  
*sahasrāṃśustvaṃ tu deva sahasrakiraṇastathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Your hands, feet, eyes, heads and faces are spread out. You have a thousand rays.

## \|\| 1.123.17 \|\|

*bhūrādibhūrbhuvaḥ svaśca maharjanastapastathā \|*  
*pradīptaṃ dīptimannityaṃ sarvalokaprakāśakam \|*  
*durnirīkṣyaṃ surendrāṇāṃ yadrūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. You are also the Bhuloka, Bhuvarloka, Svargaloka, Maharloka, Janaloka and Tapaloka. You are illuminating light for the universe and beyond the view of the gods even. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.123.18 \|\|

*surasiddhagaṇairjuṣṭaṃ bhṛgvatripulahādibhiḥ \|*  
*śubhaṃ paramamavyagraṃ yadrūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Salutation to your pleasant form which is adored by the Siddhas, Devas, Ganas, Bhrigu, Atri, Pulaha and others.

## \|\| 1.123.19 \|\|

*pañcātītasthitaṃ tadvai daśaikādaśa eva ca \|*  
*ardhamāsamatikramya sthitaṃ tatsūryamaṇḍale \|*  
*tasmai rūpāya te deva praṇatāḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Deva, Panchatanmatra (Prithvi, Agni, Jala, Vayu and Akasha), the ten sense organs and the eleventh mind is there. You are beyond those. Crossing over the fortnights, you are lodged in the Surya mandala. All the gods offer their salutation to that form.

## \|\| 1.123.20 \|\|

*viśvakṛdviśvabhūtaṃ ca viśvānarasurārcitam \|*  
*viśvasthitamaciṃtyaṃ ca yadrūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You are adored by Vishvakarma, Vishvarupa, Agni and Vishvajit. You are beyond comprehension. Therefore, salutation to your that form.

## \|\| 1.123.21 \|\|

*paraṃ yajñāt paraṃ devātparaṃ lokātparaṃ divaḥ \|*  
*duratikrameti yaḥ khyātastasmādapi paraṃ parāt \|*  
*paramātmeti vikhyātaṃ yadrūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The one who has been stated to be better than the best, besides the yajnas, lokas, the sky, the heaven and difficult to be achieved, you are better than all of them and are well known as the supreme soul. Salutation to your above form.

## \|\| 1.123.22 \|\|

*avijñeyamacityaṃ ca adhyātmagatamavyayam \|*  
*anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ yadrūpaṃ tasya te namaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Salutation to the one who is unknown, beyond comprehension, divine, indestructible or endless Deva.

## \|\| 1.123.23 \|\|

*namonamaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya namonamaḥ pāpavināśanāya \|*  
*namonamo vaṃditavaṃdanāya namonamo rogavināśanāya \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. You are the cause of all the causes, destroyer of the sins, adorable by the adorable and remover of all the ailments. Salutation to you again and again.

## \|\| 1.123.24 \|\|

*namonamaḥ sarvavarapradāya namonamaḥ sarvabalapradāya \|*  
*namonamo jñānanidhe sadaiva namonamaḥ pañcadaśātmakāya \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You are the bestower of all the boons and the strength, besides being the treasure house of knowledge. You are the form of the five tattvas and ten sense organs. Salutation to that form.

## \|\| 1.123.25 \|\|

*stutaḥ sa bhagavānevaṃ tejasāṃ rūpamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vācaṃ kalyāṇīṃ ko varo vaḥ pradīyatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the illustrious and resplendent Sungod was so eulogized, he spoke in the voice which bestow welfare — “What type of boon is desired by you, which should be granted by me?”

## \|\| 1.123.26-27 \|\|

*tavātitejasā rūpaṃ na kaścitsahate vibho \|*  
*sahanīyaṃ bhavatvetaddhitāya jagataḥ prabho \|\| 26 \|\|*

*evamastviti gāmuktvā bhagavānsarvakṛtsvayam \|*  
*lokānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ gharmavarṣāhimapradaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The gods said — “O competent one, none of us can bear the lustre possessed by you. Therefore, O lord, for the benefit of the universe, you turn this form in such a way that it becomes bearable to the world.” Thereafter, lord Surya, the creator of the entire universe, turned himself in the form of the sunshine, rain and bestower of coolness.

## \|\| 1.123.28 \|\|

*ataḥ sāṃkhyāśca yogāśca ye cānye mokṣakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*dhyāyanti dhyānino nityaṃ hadayasthaṃ divākaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Therefore, the followers of the Samkhya philosophy, those desirous of moksha and those engaged in meditation, always remain near the Sungod in their hearts.

## \|\| 1.123.29 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇahīno'pi yukto vā sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ tarati vai pāpaṃ devakarmasamāśritaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But inspite of a person having been deprived of good symptoms and being extremely sinful, when a person takes refuge with the Sungod, all his sins are washed out.

## \|\| 1.123.30 \|\|

*agnihotraṃ ca vedāśca yajñāśca bahudakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*bhānorbhaktyā namaskārakalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Performing of all the homas, reciting of the Vedas or performing of the huge yajnas giving enormous dakshina, do not compare with the merit of offering salutation to the Sungod even once.

## \|\| 1.123.31 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*pavitraṃ ca pavitrāṇāṃ taṃ prapadye divākaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Therefore, I have taken refuge with the Sungod, who is the best tirtha of all the tirthas on earth, the best of all the prosperities, and much more auspicious than all the auspicious elements in the world.

## \|\| 1.123.32 \|\|

*brahmādyaiḥ saṃstutaṃ devairye prapadyanti 1 bhāskaram \|*  
*nirmuktāḥ kilbiṣaiḥ sarvaiste yānti ravimandiram \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Bhaskara had been eulogized by Brahma and other gods, and one who takes refuge in him, he getting relieved of all the sins, achieves the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.123.33 \|\|

*upacaryādibhiḥ sādhyo yathā vede divaspatiḥ \|*  
*lokānāmiha sarveṣāṃ tathā devo divākaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. As by rendering service to the Sungod, he is said to be attainable in the Vedas, similarly for the people of the world, the lord Sun is attainable by meditation.

## \|\| 1.123.34 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*śarīralekhanaṃ sūrye kathaṃ vai pratipāditam \|*  
*devaiḥ saṛṣibhirvāpi tanmamācakṣva suvrata \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Shatanika said — O person with good holy rites, the gods and the Rishis made the body of the Sungod to be chiseled out How was it done? You please tell me.

## \|\| 1.123.35 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*brahmaloke sukhāsīnaṃ brahmāṇaṃ te surāsurāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayaḥ samupāgamya idamūcuḥ samāhitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Sumantu said — Once Brahma was comfortably seated in Brahmaloka, when the gods, demons and Rishis reached there and prayed to him with all humility.

## \|\| 1.123.36 \|\|

*bhagavandevatāputro ya eṣa divi rājate \|*  
*tenāndhakāro nikṛttaḥ so'yaṃ jājvalitīti hi \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. They said — “O lord, the son of the Devas lodged in the sky, looks quite graceful. He has removed all the darkness with his resplendence, because he possesses enormous lustre.

## \|\| 1.123.37 \|\|

*asya tejobhirakhilaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|*  
*nāśamāyāti deveśa yathā kliṣṭaṃ nadītaṭam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O lord of the gods, not only this, with that scorching lustre like the hard banks of rivers, the world would be destroyed in no time.

## \|\| 1.123.38 \|\|

*vayaṃ ca pīḍitā sarve tejasā tasya mohitāḥ \|*  
*padmaścāyaṃ yathā mlāno yoyaṃ yonistava prabho \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. All of us are suffering from the heat of the same and are almost getting fainted. O lord of the lotus, the place of your birth is too fading out with the same heat.

## \|\| 1.123.39 \|\|

*divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca śarma nopalabhāmahe \|*  
*tathā kuru surajyeṣṭha yathā tejaḥ praśāmyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Therefore, you kindly make efforts urgently to cool up the lustre, because there is no peace presently in the sky, earth or even the heaven or space.

## \|\| 1.123.40 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa bhagavānpadmayoniḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*uvāca bhagavānbrahmā devānviṣṇupurogamān1 \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. At these words spoken by those people, Brahma — born of lotus, said to Vishnu and other gods.

## \|\| 1.123.41 \|\|

*mahādevena sahitā indreṇa ca mahātmanā \|*  
*tameva śaraṇaṃ devaṃ gacchāmaḥ sahitā vayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “Let us all, including Mahadeva and Indra, go to take refuge with the Sungod.”

## \|\| 1.123.42-43 \|\|

*tataste sahitāḥ sarve brahmaviṣṇvādayaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*gatvā te śaraṇaṃ sarve bhāskaraṃ lokabhāskaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

*stotuṃ pracakramuḥ sarve bhaktinamrā samantataḥ \|*  
*keśādidevatāḥ sarvā bhaktibhāvasamanvitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Thereafter, Brahma and Vishnu besides all other gods, took refuge with the Sungod, who is the remover of the darkness in the world. Getting filled with devotion, all of them started eulogising the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.123.44 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇvīśā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namonamaḥ suravara tigmatejase namonamaḥ suravara saṃstutāya vai \|*  
*jaḍāndhamūkānbadhirānsakuṣṭhānsaśvitriṇoṃ'dhānvividhavraṇāvṛtān \|*  
*karoṣi tāneva punarnavāntsadā ato mahākāruṇikāya te namaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva said — O foremost of the gods! Salutation to you, possessing an enormous lustre. The excellent gods had eulogized you. Therefore, we are offering our salutation to you. The people who are immovable, blind, dumb, deaf, those suffering from leprosy, ailing persons, those who are wounded, are cured only by your grace bestowing beauty on them, besides the new form. You are therefore, extremely compassionate. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.123.45 \|\|

*yadaudaraṃ jyotiratitvaranmahadyadalpatejo yadapīha cakṣuṣām \|*  
*yadatra yajñeṣvapanītamāhitaṃ tavaiva tadūpamanekataḥ sthitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You are the fire of stomach, the great submarine fire, the vision of the eyes of the people, besides the fire which is consecrated in the yajnas. All of these happen to be your forms.

## \|\| 1.123.46 \|\|

*suradviṣaḥ sāgaratoyavāsinaḥ pracaṇḍapāśāsiparaśvadhāyudhāḥ \|*  
*samucchritāste bhuvi pāpacetasaḥ prayāṃti nāśaṃ tava deva darśanāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Deva! The enemies of the gods, who live in the ocean are equipped with the terrific noose, the sword and battle axe. Those, as well as the sinners of the earth, get destroyed simply with an audience with you.

## \|\| 1.123.47 \|\|

*yato bhavāṃstīrthaphalaṃ samastaṃ yajñeṣu nityaṃ bhagavānavasthitaḥ \|*  
*namo bhavannatra vicāraṇāsti sadā samaḥ śāṃtikaro narāṇām \|*  
*yaccāpi loke tapa ucyate budhaistatte mahāteja uśaṃti paṇḍitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. You happen to be the merit of all the tirthas, remain present in all the yajnas and bestow peace on all the human beings. There is no need to think about it. Therefore, O lord, salutation to you. The activity which has been defined as tapas on earth, the learned people interprets it to be your lustre alone.

## \|\| 1.123.48 \|\|

*stutaḥ sa bhagavānevaṃ prajāpatimukhaiḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*avadhānaṃ tataścakre śravaṇābhyāṃ mahīpate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O lord of the earth! When the gods so eulogized Brahma, they started hearing from their ears something.

## \|\| 1.123.49 \|\|

*stuvanti te tato bhūyaḥ śivaviṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā māṃ purataḥ sarve bhaktinamrāḥ samantataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Still all the gods including Shiva and Vishnu, who were in the forefront, making me to lead, started eulogising with devotion.

## \|\| 1.123.50 \|\|

*1 namonamastribhuvanabhūtidāyine kratukriyāsatphalasampradāyine \|*  
*namonamaḥ pratidinakarmasākṣiṇe sahasrasaṃdīdhitaye namonamaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. They said — “O lord, you bestow fortunes on the people of all the lokas and make the performing of the yajnas successful. Salutation to you. You are the witness of all the daily activities, you possess a thousand rays, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.123.51 \|\|

*prasaktasaptāśvayuje kṣayāya dhruvaikaraśmigrathine namonamaḥ \|*  
*savālakhilyāpsarakinnaroragaiḥ saṃsiddhagandharvapiśācamānuṣaiḥ \|*  
*sayakṣarakṣogaṇaguhyakottamaiḥ stutaḥ sadā deva namonamaste \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. You are the remover of darkness, you have a chariot driven by seven horses over which you are always seated. You are surely bound with a single ray, salutation to you. The Valakhilyas, Apsaras, Kinnaras, serpents, Siddhas, Gandharvas, Pishachas, humans, Yakshas, Rakshasas and excellent Guhyakas always recite your name. Therefore, O god, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.123.52 \|\|

*yato rasānsaṃkṣipase śarīriṇāṃ gabhastibhirhimajalagharmanisravaiḥ \|*  
*jagacca saṃśoṣayase sadaiva atosi loke jagato viśoṣaṇam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. You extract the juices of the living beings, with your ray, which turns the snow into water, emerging in the form of the sunshine. You at times, squeeze it and keep on drying up the world. Therefore, you are known as trait in the world.”

## \|\| 1.123.53-54 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jñātvā teṣāmabhiprāyamuvāca bhagavānvacaḥ \|*  
*labdhvānujñāṃ tataḥ sarve surāḥ saṃhṛṣṭacetasaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tvaṣṭāraṃ pūjayāmāsurmanovākkāyakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmā tavādeśātkarotu tava saumyatām \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Brahma said — Thus, well understanding the cause of offering prayer by the gods, lord Surya said something. At his command, feeling extremely delighted, all the gods worshipped Vishvakarma, by action, thought and behaviour. Then they said to the Sungod — “At your command alone, Vishvakarma will beautify you.

## \|\| 1.123.55 \|\|

*tatastu tejaso rāśiṃ sarvakarmavidhānavit \|*  
*bhramimāropayāmāsa viśvakarmā vibhāvasum \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereafter, Vishvakarma, who was well — versed in all the crafts, placed the Sungod over chiseling machine.

## \|\| 1.123.56 \|\|

*amṛtenābhiṣiktasya tadā sūryasya vai vibhoḥ \|*  
*tejasaḥ śātanaṃ cakre viśvakarmā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then Vishvakarma, soaking the lustre of the Sungod with nectar, started chiseling the Sungod slowly.

## \|\| 1.123.57 \|\|

*ājānulikhitaścāsau samurāsurapūjitaḥ \|*  
*nābhyanandattato deva ullekhanamataḥ param \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Sungod, at that point of time, was worshipped by the gods as well as the demons, and allowed himself to be chiseled upto the knees. Thereafter, he declined to have it done further.

## \|\| 1.123.58 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti devasya caraṇau nityasaṃvṛtau \|*  
*tāpayanglāpayaṃścaiva yuktatejo'bhavattadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Therefore, his feet remained unchiseled. Since then, his lustre could cause heat to the world.

## \|\| 1.123.59 \|\|

*yaccāsya śātitaṃ tejastena cakraṃ vinirmitam \|*  
*yena viṣṇurjaghānogrānsadā vai daityadānavān \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The lustre which fell down on the ground while chiseling, Vishvakarma then made a cakra out of it, which was used by lord Vishnu for the killing of the terrific demons.

## \|\| 1.123.60 \|\|

*śūlaśaktigadāvajraśarāsanaparaśvadhān \|*  
*devatānāṃ dadau kṛtvā viśvakarmā mahāmatiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The intelligent Vishvakarma also made the trident, shakti (spear), gada, vajra, the bow and the battle axe, which were distributed to the respective gods.

## \|\| 1.123.61 \|\|

*tridevanirmitaṃ stotraṃ sandhyayorubhayorjapan \|*  
*kulaṃ punāti puruṣo vyādhibhirna ca pīḍyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus, with the prayer which was recited by the three gods, one who repeats the same in the morning as well as in the evening, he purifies his whole race, and never suffers from ailment.

## \|\| 1.123.62 \|\|

*prajāvānsiddhakarmā ca jīvetsāgraṃ śaracchatam \|*  
*putravāndhanavāṃścaiva sarvatra cāparājitaḥ \|*  
*hitvā puraṃ bhūtamayaṃ gacchetsṛryamayaṃ puram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He also achieves nice progeny and is successful in his efforts and enjoys life more than a hundred years. He achieves enough of riches and sons besides being always victorious. After his death, he is lodged in the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.123.63 \|\|

*bhūyo'pi tuṣṭuvurdevāstathā devarṣayo ravim \|*  
*vāgbhiritthamaśeṣasya trailokyasya samāgatāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The gods of all the three lokas besides the Rishis again eulogized the Sungod thus.

## \|\| 1.123.64 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namaste1 ravirūpāya somarūpāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namo yajuḥ svarūpāyātharvāyāṅgirase2 namaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The gods said — Salutation to your pleasant and nectar like form. Salutation to the form of Yajurveda and Atharvaveda besides Angirasa.

## \|\| 1.123.65 \|\|

*jñānaikadhāmabhūtāya3 nirdhūtatamase namaḥ \|*  
*śuddhajyotiḥsvarūpāya nistattvāyāmalātmane \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. You are the sole abode of knowledge. After the removal of darkness, you possess the spotless, resplendent form. Salutation to the spotless soul like you.

## \|\| 1.123.66 \|\|

*namo'khilajagadvyāptisvarūpāyātmamūrtaye \|*  
*sarvakāraṇabhūtāya niṣṭhāyai jñānacetasām \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Your lustre is spread in the entire world, the form of soul, cause of all, the faith of the learned people, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.123.67 \|\|

*namo'stu jñeyarūpāya prakāśe lakṣarūpiṇe \|*  
*bhāskarāya namastubhyaṃ tathā śabdakṛte namaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. You are visible, the darkness and light. You are creator of the words, therefore, salutation to Bhaskara.

## \|\| 1.123.68 \|\|

*saṃsārahetave caiva saṃdhyājyotsnākṛte namaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ sarvametadbhagavāñjagadvai bhramati tvayā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. You are the cause of the universe, creator of evening as well as the moon shine. Salutation to you. You are the lord of the universe, you are the cause of the movement of the world.

## \|\| 1.123.69 \|\|

*bhramatvāviddhamakhilaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*tvadaṃśubhiridaṃ sarvaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ jāyate śuci \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. After the creation of the mobile and immobile beings besides the universe, it gets purified with your ray alone.

## \|\| 1.123.70-71 \|\|

*kriyate tvatkarasparśājjalādīnāṃ pavitratā \|*  
*homadānādiko dharmo nopakārāya jāyate \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tāvadyāvanna saṃyogī jagatyatra bhavāñchuciḥ \|*  
*prātarhomaṃ praśastaṃ hi udite tvayi jāyate \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. With the touch of your ray, the water gets purified, besides the homas are considered to be inauspicious unless you rise in this world. Therefore, with your rise and your link with this world, the morning is considered to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.123.72 \|\|

*ṛco'tha sakalā hyetā yajūṃṣi tvaṃ jagatpate \|*  
*sakalāni ca sāmāni tapatyevaṃ jagatsadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O lord of the universe! All the stories of Rigveda, Samaveda and Yajurveda are represented by you and you shine in the world with their lustre.

## \|\| 1.123.73 \|\|

*ṛṅmayastvaṃ jagannātha tvameva ca yajurmayaḥ \|*  
*tathā sāmamayaścaiva tato nātha trayīmayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. O lord of the world, because of your being the form of Rigveda, Yajurveda and Samaveda you are equated with the three Vedas.

## \|\| 1.123.74 \|\|

*tvameva brahmaṇo rūpaṃ paraṃ cāparameva ca \|*  
*mūrto'mūrtastathā sūkṣmaḥ sdhūlarūpatayā sthitaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. You are the other form of Brahman and are established in the invisible, visible, subtle and gloss forms.

## \|\| 1.123.75 \|\|

*nimeṣakāṣṭhādimayaḥ kālarūpaḥ kṣayātmakaḥ \|*  
*prasīda svecchayā rūpaṃ svatejomayamādiśa \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Because of this, the moments, the ten directions, the form of kala as well as you have the artistic form. You kindly be pleased and issue command for this illustrious form.

## \|\| 1.123.76 \|\|

*itthaṃ saṃstūyamānastu devairdevarṣibhistathā \|*  
*mumoca svaṃ tadā tejastejasāṃ rāśiravyayaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. At the prayer offered by the gods as well as the Rishis, Surya, who is the abode of lustre and eternal, shed away his lustre.

## \|\| 1.123.77 \|\|

*yattasya ṛṅmayaṃ tejo bhavitā tena medinī \|*  
*yajurmayenāpi divaṃ svayaṃ sāmamayo raviḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. As a result of this, out of the lustre of the Rigveda earth was born, the heaven emerged out of the resplendence of Yajurveda and out of the lustre of Samaveda the Sungod himself was born.

## \|\| 1.123.78 \|\|

*śātitāstejaso bhāgā ye ca syurdaśa paṃca ca \|*  
*tasyaiva tena śarvasya kṛtaṃ śūlaṃ mahātmanā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The fifteenth part of the chiseled out lustre of the Sungod was turned into a trident for Shiva by Vishvakarma.

## \|\| 1.123.79 \|\|

*cakraṃ viṣṇorvasūnāṃ ca śaṃkarasya ca dāruṇam \|*  
*ṣaṇmukhasya tathā śaktiḥ śibikā dhanadasya ca \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Similarly, a cakra (disc) was made for Vishnu, the terrific weapons for Vasus and Shiva, shakti for Karttikeya and a palanquin was made for Kubera.

## \|\| 1.123.80 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ cāsurārīṇāṃ śastrāṇyugrāṇi yāni vai \|*  
*yakṣavidyādharāṇāṃ ca tāni cakre sa viśvakṛt \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Whatever the sharp weapons are there with Asuras and other enemies of gods, they all were made by Vishvakarma out of the chiseled lustre of the Sungod,

## \|\| 1.123.81 \|\|

*tataśca ṣoḍaśaṃ bhāgaṃ bibharti bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*tattejasaḥ paṃcadaśa śātitā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Then, only a sixteenth part of his lustre was owned by the Sungod and the rest of the fifteen parts were chiseled out by Vishvakarma.

## \|\| 1.123.82 \|\|

*tataḥ surūpadṛgbhānuruttarānagamatkurūn \|*  
*dadarśa tatra saṃjñāṃ ca vaḍavārūpadhāriṇīm \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thereafter, achieving a beautiful form, the Sungod proceeded on to the pilgrimage of Kuru country and found Samjna there roaming in the form of a mare.

## \|\| 1.123.83 \|\|

*ityetannikhilaṃ bhānoḥ kathitaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuyādyo naro bhaktyā aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O excellent sage, thus I have revealed before you the spotless secret of Surya. A person who listens to it with devotion, he earns the merit of performing Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## Chapter 124. Description of Bhuamakosha

## \|\| 1.124.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*vakṣyāmyahaṃ te punareva diṃḍe sūryasya sarvapravarapradhānam \|*  
*vyomnaḥ paraṃ tiṣṭhati yastu magnaḥ sa mucyate rudra ihāpi diṃḍī \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said — O Dindi! I am again repeating about the followers of the Sungod, which you please listen. The one who is always found blissful in the sky, ahead of all is known as Rudra, but here, he is known as Dindi.

## \|\| 1.124.2 \|\|

*sthitvā purā brahmaśiraḥ kilāsau pragṛhya tattasya śiraḥkapālam \|*  
*tato hyasāvāśramamuttamaṃ śivo bahūdakaiḥ puṣpaphalaiḥ samṛddham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Once in earlier times, while staying at a place named Brahmashira, Shiva, holding the skull of one of the heads of Brahma, appearing nude, moved on to an excellent ashrama with enough of water, flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 1.124.3 \|\|

*nagno yadā dāruvane munīnāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ bhaikṣyacaraṃ sureśam \|*  
*yoṣitsutāḥ saṃkṣubhitāstu sarve jagmurharaṃ taṃ munayaḥ sutuṣṭāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the terrific forest, finding the best of the gods so roaming about, the sages and their wives, feeling disturbed, reached before him.

## \|\| 1.124.4 \|\|

*sa hanyamāno munimukhyasaṃghairgṛhītaloṣṭairṛṣidaṃḍakāṣṭhaiḥ \|*  
*vihāya diṃḍiḥ sa tu tānsurarṣīṃstato raverlokamathājagāma \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The sages holding the brick-bats and the Rishis holding the rods of wood, attacked him. Having been thus beaten by them, deserting the Rishis Dindi again proceeded to the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.124.5 \|\|

*āgacchamānaṃ pramathāstamūcurdeveśa nityaṃ bhramase kimartham \|*  
*sa prāha tānpāpavimocanārthamaṭāmi tīrthāni surālayāṃśca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Finding his returning, the foremost ganas humbly said to him — “O lord of the gods, why do you wander always like this?” He replied to them— “I am wandering in the holy places as well as the temples to free myself of the sin.”

## \|\| 1.124.6 \|\|

*te bhūya ūcuḥ pramathāstamevamatraiva tiṣṭhasva raveḥ purastāt \|*  
*śuddhiṃ tavaiṣa prakariṣyatīti śuddhastato yāsyasi rudralokam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing this, the Shivaganas again said to the lord — “You better present yourself before the Sungod, who would surely purify you. Thereafter, you could return to Rudraloka.”

## \|\| 1.124.7 \|\|

*ityevamuktaḥ pramathaistu rudrastatraiva tasthau ravitoṣaṇāya \|*  
*nagno jaṭī muṣṭikapālapāṇī rūpeṇa caivāpratimastriloke \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At these words of the Pramathas, the humble lord Shiva, having matted locks of hair over his head, holding a skull in his hand, who could take to the most beautiful form in the three worlds, stayed there for the adoration of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.124.8 \|\|

*uktaḥ sa tuṣṭena tataḥ savitrā prītosmi devāgamanāttavāham \|*  
*maddarśanādeva bhavānviśuddho diṃḍīti nāmnā bhavitāsi loke \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then by meditating, he said to Shiva — “O Deva, I am happy with you arrived here. You have been purified simply by your having an audience with me. From today onwards, you will be known by name of Dindi in the world.

## \|\| 1.124.9-10 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśaite pramathāstu bhānoścaturdaśānye tu rave rathasthāḥ \|*  
*he devate dvau ca ṛṣipradhānau gaṃdharvasarpāvapi tāvadeva \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yakṣau ca siddhau ca niśācarau cādityātmajāvapsarasāṃ pradhānau \|*  
*vasaṃti te hyastamuṣaśca sūrye teṣāma śītiścaturottarā sā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Thus, besides Dindi, eighteen Pramathas, fourteen serpents, other attendants, two prominent Rishis, two Gandharvas, two Yakshas, two Siddhas, two demons, two Apsaras, two Adityas and their prominent sons always remained present in the chariot at the time of Sunset. The number of all of them four.

## \|\| 1.124.11 \|\|

*ityādidevapravarāstu sarve dhātvarthaśabdaiśca bhavaṃti siddhāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Siddhi of these gods, by means of grammar, form the related roots.

## \|\| 1.124.12 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*vistarādbrūhi me brahmanpravarāndhātuśabdajān \|*  
*yataśca kautukaṃ brahmannasmākamiha jāyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Rishis said — O Brahman, the names of the Devas are rooted in the dhatus. Therefore, you speak about them in detail. We are anxious to known about them.

## \|\| 1.124.13-14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*bhūyastava pravakṣyāmi daṃḍanāyakapiṃgalau \|*  
*rājñasrauṣādayaścānye digdevā diṃḍinā saha \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mayā saha samāgamya purā devairvicāritam \|*  
*eṣa kāruṇikaḥ sūryo yudhyate dānavaiḥ saha \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Brahma said — I shall repeat to you the same. You listen with apt attention. Once in earlier times, I myself together with Dandi, Dandanayaka, Pingala, Rajna, Shrausha and others besides the gods of all the directions, collectively started thinking that the Sungod was engaged in a fierce battle with the Danavas.

## \|\| 1.124.15 \|\|

*te tu labdhavarā bhūtvā amātyādyā hyabhīkṣṇaśaḥ \|*  
*ādityaṃ manyamānāste tapaṃtaṃ haṃtumudyatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On the other hand, the ministers of the Rakshasas have also been bestowed with boons. Therefore, they would surely be ready for the killing of the gods.

## \|\| 1.124.16 \|\|

*tasmātteṣāṃ vighātārthaṃ pravarāśca bhavāmahe \|*  
*asmābhiḥ pratiruddhāste na drakṣyaṃti divākaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Therefore, we should be forceful for the killing of the Rakshasas. Because with the obstruction created by us, they would not be able to find out the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.124.17 \|\|

*saṃmaṃtryaivaṃ tataḥ skaṃdo vāmapārśve raveḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*daṃḍanāyakasaṃjñastu sarvalokasya sa prabhuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With these discussions, Skanda stood to the left of Surya and he cane to be known as Dandaniyaka. He was entrusted with the safety of all the lokas.

## \|\| 1.124.18 \|\|

*uktaśca sa tadārkeṇa tvaṃ prajādaṃḍanāyakaḥ \|*  
*daṃḍanītikaro yasmāttasmāttvaṃ daṃḍanāyakaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thereafter, the Sungod said to Dandi — “You have been entrusted with the duty of the holder of staff.”

## \|\| 1.124.19 \|\|

*likhate yaḥ prajānāṃ ca sukṛtaṃ yacca duṣkṛtam \|*  
*agnirdakṣiṇapārśve tu piṃgalatvātsa piṃgalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then he said to Agni — “You stand to my right, you write down the good or evil performance of the people on earth. Because of your being Pingala, you will be known as Pingala”

## \|\| 1.124.20 \|\|

*āśvinau cāpi sūryasya pārśvayorubhayoḥ sthitau \|*  
*aśvarūpātsamupannau tena tāvaśvinau surau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then Ashvinikumaras were also made to stand on both the sides of the Sungod. Because of their having been born of the Sungod, they were known as Ashvinikumaras.

## \|\| 1.124.21 \|\|

*dvārapālau smṛtau tasya rājñaḥ śreṣṭhau mahābalau \|*  
*kārttikeyaḥ smṛto rājñaḥ śreṣṭhaścāpi haraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then there were the two gatekeepers of the Sungod. Out of them, first was Rajna or Karttikeya and the other one was Shreshtha or Shrausha. Both of them were quite valorous.

## \|\| 1.124.22 \|\|

*rājṛdīptau smṛto dhāturnakārastasya pratyayaḥ \|*  
*surasenāpatitvena sa yasmāddīpyate sadā \|*  
*tasmātsa kārtikeyastu nāmnā rājña iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Rajna emerges out of the root raja. Therefore, the commander of the army of gods has been known as Rajna, who always remains resplendent.

## \|\| 1.124.23 \|\|

*sru gatau ca smṛto dhāturyasya sa pratyayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*gacchatīti rahastasmātparyāyātsrauṣa ucyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The root shru is taken for movement or gati with the adding of sa suffix, the word shrusha emerges. Shrausha word is born of it.

## \|\| 1.124.24 \|\|

*prathamaṃ yadbhaveddvāraṃ dharmārthābhyāṃ samāśritam \|*  
*tatraitau saṃsthitau devau lokapūjyau dvijottamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O best of Brahmana, the first gate which is taken to be the centre of dharma and artha, both the world renowned gods are found present there.

## \|\| 1.124.25-26 \|\|

*dvitīyāyāṃ tu kakṣāyāmapradhṛṣṭau vyavasthitau \|*  
*pakṣipretādhipau nāmnā smṛtau kalmāṣapakṣiṇau \|\| 25 \|\|*

*varṇasya śabalatvācca yamaḥ kalmāṣa ucyate \|*  
*pakṣāvasyeti yaḥ pakṣī garuḍaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The door of the second class Kalmasha and birds remain present these, who are extremely terrible. They have the spotted complexion. Yama is known as Kalmasha and the one with wings is known as Pakshi or bird who is Garuda.

## \|\| 1.124.27 \|\|

*sthito dakṣiṇata tasya daṃḍahastasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*uttareṇa sthito'rkasya kuberaśca vināyakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Kubera holding a staff in his hand stands to the right of the Sungod. Vinayaka stands to the north of Surya.

## \|\| 1.124.28 \|\|

*kubero dhanado jñeyo hastirūpo vināyakaḥ \|*  
*kutsayā kupyatā śaptaṃ kuśarīramajāyata \|*  
*kuberaḥ kuśarīratvātsa nāmnā dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Dhanada has been interpreted as Kubera and the one with the elephant face has been known as Vinayaka. Once, while denouncing him, he pronounced a curse on him, as a result of which his body got deformed. Because of the said deformity, Dhanada came to be known as Kubera.

## \|\| 1.124.29 \|\|

*nāyakaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ tena nāyaka ucyate \|*  
*vividhaṃ nayate yasmātsa tu tasmādvināyakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Similarly, because of his being the leader of all the living beings, bestowing welfare on them, he is known as Vinayaka.

## \|\| 1.124.30 \|\|

*raivataścaiva diṃḍiśca tau raveḥ pūrvataḥ sthitau \|*  
*tato diṃḍiḥ smṛto rudro revatastanayo raveḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Similarly, Raivata and Dandi stood to the east of the Sungod, where Rudra is represented by Dandi, while Raivata is the son of Surya.

## \|\| 1.124.31 \|\|

*plutaṃ gacchatyasau yasmātsarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*revṛplavagatau dhātū revatastena sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Since Raivata moved always by jumping, he was given the name of Raivata.

## \|\| 1.124.32 \|\|

*ḍīṅgatāvasya vai dhātordiṃḍiśabdo nipātyate \|*  
*ḍayate'sau sadā diṃḍī tena diṃḍī prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Dindi also emerges from dinga root and therefore, with suffix da, the word Dindi gets derived.

## \|\| 1.124.33 \|\|

*ityete pravarāḥ proktā dhātvarthā naigamaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*eṣāṃ saṃkṣepato bhūyaḥ saṃkhyāṃ vo nigadāmi vai \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. I have spoken about the linking of the names of the gods with roots of grammar. Now, I shall speak about their number.

## \|\| 1.124.34-35 \|\|

*aśvinau tau tato jñeyau daṃḍanāyakapiṃgalau \|*  
*tau sūryadvārapau jñeyau rājñasrauṣau tataḥ smṛtau \|\| 34 \|\|*

*revataścaiva diṃḍiśca ityete pravarā mayā \|*  
*aṣṭādaśa samā khyātāḥ saṃkṣepātsaṃkhyayā mayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Two Ashvinikumaras, Dandanayaka, Pingala, the gatekeeper of the Sungod, Dandi, Raivata and others are eighteen in number.

## \|\| 1.124.36 \|\|

*ityebhirnāmabhistvanye dānavānāṃ jighāṃsayā \|*  
*parivārya sthitāḥ sūryaṃ nānāpraharaṇāyudhāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. For the killing of the demons, these people are well equipped with the weapons and they guard the Sungod from all the sides.

## \|\| 1.124.37 \|\|

*sarūpāścānyarūpāśca virūpāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*parivārya sthitāḥ sūryaṃ garuḍaśca mahābalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Similarly, there are those with the similar faces, those with different faces, those with deformities, those who can change their forms at will, besides valorous Garuda, remain in attendance of Surya surrounding him.

## \|\| 1.124.38 \|\|

*dhāturdiviti vai prokto krīḍāyāṃ sa tu ucyate \|*  
*krīḍaṃte divi vai yasmāttasmātte daivatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The root dir is used in the sense of sports. Therefore, for sporting in the heaven, they are called the gods or Devas.

## \|\| 1.124.39 \|\|

*ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni yānyuktānīha vai mayā \|*  
*nānārūpaiḥ sthitānyeva ravestāni sama ntataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Besides whatever has been earlier told by me about Rig, Yajuh and Sama, all of them taking to the suitable forms, remain present around Surya.

## \|\| 1.124.40 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*ityevamuktavānbrahmā ṛṣīṇāṃ pṛcchatāṃ purā \|*  
*te śrutvārādhya deveśaṃ saṃsiddhā divi saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Sumantu said — When asked by the Rishis in earlier times, Brahma had spoken accordingly. All the Rishis, listening to the words of the Brahma, worshipping the Sungod, achieved success and attained the heaven for all times to come.

## Chapter 125. Description of Bhuvana

## \|\| 1.125.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*yadetaddṛśyate vyoma sūryasya purato dvija \|*  
*taducyate kimātmā ca kathaṃbhūtaśca kathyatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O Brahman a, the Vyoma or space of the Sungod, visible from here, what is it’s size? How did it originate? You please tell me.

## \|\| 1.125.2 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*haṃta vyoma pravakṣyāmi sūryapraharaṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*yadātmakaṃ hi yatproktaṃ yathā vasaṃti devatāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — I am going to tell you about the auspicious weapon of the Sungod, about his shape? What is its name? How do the gods live there?

## \|\| 1.125.3 \|\|

*satyāśca bhūtarajasaḥ sādhyāśca tadanantarā \|*  
*ṣaṭsu manvantareṣvevaṃ devā dvādaśadvādaśa \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Vyoma is a weapon of the Sungod, which also happens to be his refuge as well. There are four lightnings before it. The word Shringa is used for the lord, who represents all the gods.
