## \|\| 1.125.4-6 \|\|

*gairikārṇavasaṃbhūtaṃ yadaṃtargarbhamāśritam \|*  
*tatrotpannamidaṃ vyoma kalervyoma mahī smṛtā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*varuṇasya yathā pāśo huṅkāro vedhaso yathā \|*  
*viṣṇoścāpi yathā cakraṃ triśūlaṃ tryaṃbakasya ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*indrasya ca yathā vajraṃ tathā vyoma raveḥ smṛtam \|*  
*tasminvyomni trayastriṃśatkrīḍanto yajñiyāḥ surāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The tattva that was lodged in the womb of the ocean, produced vyoma. In the age of Kali, the earth was known as vyoma. As the noose of Varuna, humkara of Brahma, cakra of Vishnu, the trident of Tryambaka Shiva, vajra of Indra are the weapons, similarly, Surya has the weapon known as vyoma. The thirty three gods of yajnas have their sport in vyoma.

## \|\| 1.125.7 \|\|

*haraśca varṣaśuddhaśca tryaṃbakaścāparājitaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣākapiśca śaṃbhuśca kapardī raivatastathā \|*  
*īśvaro bhuvanaścaite rudrā ekādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hara, Varsha-Shuddha, Tryambaka, Aparajita, Vrishakapi, Shambhu, Kapardi, Raivata, Ishvara, Bhuvana and Rudra are known as the eleven Rudras. There are twelve Adityas.

## \|\| 1.125.8-9 \|\|

*ādityānāṃ ca nāmāni viṣṇoścakrasya dīyatām \|*  
*aryamā ca tathā mitro bhago'tha varuṇastathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vivasvāntsavitā caiva pūṣā tvaṣṭā tathaiva ca \|*  
*aṃśo bhagaścātitejā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Their names compare well with the chakras of Vishnu. Adityas are known by the names of Aryama, Mitra, Bhaga, Varuna, Vivasvan, Savita, Pusha, Tvashta, Amsha, Bhaga, Atiteja and Bhaga.

## \|\| 1.125.10 \|\|

*dhruvo dharaśca somaśca āpaścaivā'nilo'nalaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣaśca prabhātaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The eight Vasus are known by the names of Dhruva, Dhara, Soma, Apa, Anila, Anala, Pratyusha and Prabhata.

## \|\| 1.125.11 \|\|

*nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca smṛtau dvāvaśvināvubhau \|*  
*viśvedevānpravakṣyāmi nāmatastānnibodhata \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Nasatya and Dasra are the two Ashvinikumaras. Vishvadevas are also lodged there. I am going to speak out their names, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.125.12 \|\|

*kraturdakṣo vasuḥ satyaḥ kālakāmau dhṛtiḥ kuruḥ \|*  
*śaṅkumātro vāmanaśca viśvedevā daśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They are known as Kratu, Daksha, Vasu, Satya, Kala, Kama, Dhriti, Kuru, Shanka-matra and Vamana. These are ten Vishvedevas.

## \|\| 1.125.13-14 \|\|

*vartamānā ime devā bhaviṣyānantare śṛṇu \|*  
*yamaśca tuṣitāścaiva1 vasavo2 vaśavartinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pārāvatāstathā cānye te hyāsaṃstuṣitaiḥ saha \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. All the aforesaid gods always pervade in vyoma. I am also speaking beyond that as well. Yama, Tushita and Vashavartin are obedient to the Sungod. Satya, Bhuta, Rajas and Sadhya are there. Besides them, there are the twelve gods of the twelve Manvantaras who live there. Besides Paravata, Tushita and other gods are also there.

## \|\| 1.125.15-16 \|\|

*sādhyāndevānpravakṣyāmi nāmatastānnibodha me \|*  
*mano'numantā prāṇaśca naro nārāyaṇastathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vṛttilambo manuścaiva samo4 dharmaśca vīryavān \|*  
*vittasvāmī prabhuścaiva sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Now I am speaking out the names of Sadhyas. You please listen. They are known as — Manu, Anumanta, Prana, Nara, Narayana, Vrittilamba, Manu, Sama, Dharma, Viryavan, Vittasvami and Prabhu. These are the twelve names.

## \|\| 1.125.17 \|\|

*ete yajñabhujo devāḥ sarvalokeṣu pūjitāḥ \|*  
*ādityāmeva te dhīra kaśyapasyātmajāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. These gods also enjoy the share in the yajnas and are adored by all the lokas. O patient one, since they were born from Aditi – the wife of Kashyapa, therefore, they are also known as the sons of Kashyapa.

## \|\| 1.125.18 \|\|

*viśve ca vasavaḥ sādhyā vijñeyā dharmasūnavaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dharmasutaḥ somastṛtīyo vasuriṣyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Similarly, Vishvedevas, Vasus and Sadhyas should be known as Dharma putras. The third Vasu known as Soma is also the son of Dharma.

## \|\| 1.125.19 \|\|

*dharmo'pi brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ purāṇe niścayaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*atha cendrānvasūṃścaiva nāmabhiśca nibodha me \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Dharma is the son of Brahma. This has been established in the Puranas. Now I am speaking about Indra Vasu.

## \|\| 1.125.20 \|\|

*svāyambhuvo manuḥ pūrvaḥ tataḥ svārociṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*uttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Initially, Svayambhuva Manu was there. After him came, Svarochisha, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata and Chakshusha.

## \|\| 1.125.21 \|\|

*ityete ṣaḍatikrāntāḥ saptamaḥ sāmprato manuḥ \|*  
*vaivasvateti vijñeyo bhaviṣyāḥ sapta cāpare \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The period of these six Manus has come to an end, because the present seventh Manu is known as Vaivasvata. There will be seven Manus after him.

## \|\| 1.125.22-23 \|\|

*eṣāmādyorkasāvarṇirbrahmasāvarṇireva ca \|*  
*tasmācca bhavasāvarṇirdharmasāvarṇirityuta \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pañcamo dakṣasāvarṇiḥ sāvarṇiḥ5 pañca kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*raucyo bhauvyaśca dvāvanyāvityete manavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Out of these, the first is Surya Savarni, Brahma Savarni, Bhava Savarni, Dharma Savarni and the fifth one is Daksha Savarni. After these rive Savarnis, two other Manus named as Rauchya and Bhauvya linked together, make the number of Manus as seven.

## \|\| 1.125.24-26 \|\|

*indrastu viṣṇubhugjñeyo vidyutistadanantaram \|*  
*vibhuḥ prabhuścaiva śikhī tathaiva ca manojavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ojasvī sāmpratisvindro balirbhāvyastataḥ param \|*  
*adbhutastridivaścaiva daśamastvindra ucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*susāttvikaśca1 kīrtiśca śatadhāmā2 divaspatiḥ \|*  
*iti bhūtā bhaviṣyāśca indrā jñeyāścaturdaśa \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Of the Indras, the first one is known as Vishnubhuk, then Vidyuti, Vibhu, Prabhu, Shakti, Manojava, Ojasvi, Bali, Adbhuta and tenth was Tridiva. Then, there were Susattvika, Kirti, Shatadhama and Divaspati. These are the fourteen Indras, who shall happen in the past as well future. Out of these Indras, one named Ojasvi happens to be the modern one.

## \|\| 1.125.27 \|\|

*kaśyapo'trirvaśiṣṭhaśca bharadvājaśca gautamaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitro jamadagniḥ saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Similarly, Kasyapa, Atri, Vasistha, Bhardvaja, Gautama, Visvamitra and Jamadagni are known as Saptarsis.

## \|\| 1.125.28-29 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi maruto'gniparigrahān \|*  
*pravahothāvahaścaiva udvahaḥ saṃvahastathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vivaho nivahaścaiva parivāhastathaiva ca \|*  
*antarikṣacarā3 hyete pṛthaṅmārgavisāriṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Further, I am narrating the names of Maruts and Agni. You please listen. They are known as — Pravaha, Avaha, Udvaha, Samvaha, Vivaha, Nivaha and Parivaha. These are the seven names of Maruts, They move m the space in separate routes.

## \|\| 1.125.30 \|\|

*sūryo'gniśca śucirnāmnā vaidyutaḥ pāvakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nirmanthaḥ pavamāno'gnistrayaḥ proktā imegnayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The fire god Agni is born out of the Sungod and is also known by the name of Shuchi, The fire which emerged out of lightning is known as Pavaka. The fire which is produced with the churning of the sticks is known as Pavamana. Thus, there are three types of fires.

## \|\| 1.125.31 \|\|

*agnīnāṃ putrapautrāstu catvāriṃśattathaiva tu \|*  
*marutāmapi sarveṣāṃ vijñeyāḥ saptasaptakāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. These Agnis have forty sons as well as the grandsons. The number of Maruts is seven multiplied by seven i.e., forty nine.

## \|\| 1.125.32 \|\|

*ṛtuḥ saṃvatsaro'hyagnirṛtavastasya jajñire \|*  
*ṛtuputrāśca vai pañca iti sargaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Samvatsara of Agni is known as Ritu. Five sons were born of them. Thus, it is known as the eternal creation.

## \|\| 1.125.33-35 \|\|

*saṃvatsarastu prathamo dvitīyaḥ parivatsaraḥ \|*  
*idvatsarastṛtīyastu caturthastvanuvatsaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*pañcamo vatsarasteṣāmityevaṃ pañca te smṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣu saṃvatsaro hyagniḥ sūryastu parivatsaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*soma idvatsarasteṣāṃ vāyuścaivānuvatsaraḥ \|*  
*rudrastu vatsaro jñeyaḥ pañcaitā yugadevatāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. These five sons are known by the names of Samvatsara, Parivatsara, Idvatsara, Anuvatsara and Vatsara, who happens to be the fifth son. Out of these, Samvatsara has Agni as his god, Parivatsara has the Sun as his god, Idvatsara has the moon as his god, Anuvatsara has the wind as his god, while Vatsara has Rudra as his god.

## \|\| 1.125.36 \|\|

*ārtavā pitaro jñeyā ye jātāḥ ṛtusūnavaḥ \|*  
*pitāmahāstu vijñeyāḥ pañcābdā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The aforesaid Rituputras (or the sons of the seasons) and the pitris, emerged out of Brahma. The sons of Brahma, always remain as old as of five years.

## \|\| 1.125.37 \|\|

*saumyā barhiṣadaścaiva agniṣvāttāśca ye trayaḥ \|*  
*ete vai pitarasteṣāṃ ye jīvatpitṛkā narāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Pitris named Saumya, Barhishad and Agnishvatta belong to the persons, whose fathers are alive.

## \|\| 1.125.38-39 \|\|

*ādityaścaiva somaśca lohitāṅgo budhastathā \|*  
*bṛhaspatiśca śukraśca tathā helisutaśca yaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*uparāgaḥ śikhī cobhau navaite nu grahāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*trailokyasya tvime nityaṃ bhāvābhāvanivedakāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Similarly, the Sun, Moon, Bhauma, Budha, Brihaspati, Shukra, Ishani, Rahu and Ketu are the nine planets, which communicate the activities of all the three lokas.

## \|\| 1.125.40 \|\|

*ādityaścaiva somaśca dvāvetau maṇḍalagrahau \|*  
*rāhuśchāyāgrahasteṣāṃ śeṣāstārā grahāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Sun and the Moon are the planets with spherical zones. Rahu is the planet with shadow. The others are star planets.

## \|\| 1.125.41 \|\|

*nakṣatrādhipatiḥ somo graharājo divākaraḥ \|*  
*paṭhyate cāgnirāditya udakaścandramāḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The Moon is the lord of constellations, while the Sun is the lord of the planets. Out of these, the Sun is the form of Agni and Moon is the form of water.

## \|\| 1.125.42 \|\|

*ādityaḥ paṭhyate brahmā viṣṇusteṣāṃ tu candramāḥ \|*  
*maheśvarastu vijñeyastṛtīyastārakagrahaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. At the same time, Aditya is the form of Brahma, while the Moon represents lord Vishnu. The star Mars represents Maheshvara.

## \|\| 1.125.43 \|\|

*kaśyapasya sutaḥ sūryaḥ somo dharmasutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*devāsuragurū dvau tu nāmatastau1 mahāgrahau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The Sun is the son of Kashyapa, while the Moon is the son of Dharma. Brihaspati is the preceptor of the gods, where as Shukra is the preceptor of the Asuras.

## \|\| 1.125.44 \|\|

*prajāpatisutāvetāvubhau śukrabṛhaspatī \|*  
*budhaḥ somātmajaḥ śrīmāñchanī ravisutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Both of them are the sons of Prajapati. The intelligent Budha (Mercury) is the son of the Moon, while Saturn is the son of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.125.45 \|\|

*siṃhikāyāḥ suto rāhuḥ ketustu brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ ca grahāṇāṃ hi adhastāccarate raviḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Rahu is the son of Simhika, while Ketu is the son of Brahma. Surya moves below all the planets.

## \|\| 1.125.46-47 \|\|

*tato dūraṃ smṛtaṃ tāvadvidhornakṣatramaṇḍalam \|*  
*nakṣatrebhyaḥ kujabudhau śvetāhvastadanantaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tasmānmāheśvaraścorddhvaṃ dhiṣaṇastadanantaram \|*  
*kṛṣṇaścordhvaṃ tatastasmādatha citraśikhaṇḍijaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The Moon is away from him. The constellations are above then and further above then is Budha. Thereafter, Venus and Mars are located. Beyond Mars, Jupiter is lodged, beyond whom is Saturn. The people are lodged above the Saturn.

## \|\| 1.125.48 \|\|

*eṣāmeva kramaḥ proktāścāsaktaṃ tridivaṃ dhruve \|*  
*ādityanilayo rāhuḥ kadācitsomamārgagaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. This has been stated about the location of all the planets. In the same sequence, remaining in the heaven, all are linked with Dhruva or Pole star. Though Rahu always lives in the abode of the Sun, but at times he follows the path of the Moon.

## \|\| 1.125.49 \|\|

*sūryamaṇḍalasaṃsthastu1 śikhī sarpati sarvadā \|*  
*navayojanasāhasro vistāro bhārgavasya2 tu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In the sphere of the Moon is lodged Ketu, who moves quite slowly. The circumference of Sun is said to be a thousand yojanas.

## \|\| 1.125.50 \|\|

*dviguṇaḥ sūryavistārādvistāraḥ śaninaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*triguṇaṃ3 maṃḍalaṃ jñeyaṃ nākṣatraṃ vistarādvidhoḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The circumference of Saturn and Moon is double than that of the Sun. The circumference of the constellations is double that of the Moon.

## \|\| 1.125.51 \|\|

*nakṣatramaṇḍalāttatra pādahīno bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspateḥ pādahīnaḥ śukroṅgāraka eva hi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In case, one fourth of the area of circumference of these planets extracted from that of the Moon, the area of Jupiter (Brihaspati) would be worked out. Then, if one fourth of the area of the Jupiter is extracted from the same, the area of Venus and Mars would be worked out.

## \|\| 1.125.52 \|\|

*vistāro maṇḍalānāṃ tu pādahīnastayorbudhaḥ \|*  
*budhatulyāni ṛkṣāṇi sarvaṛkṣāṇi yāni tu \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. One fourth of the circumference, when extracted from the same, the area of Mercury would be worked out. All other constellations have an area equivalent to that of Mercury.

## \|\| 1.125.53 \|\|

*yojanānyardhamātrāṇi tebhyo hrasvaṃ na vidyate \|*  
*rāhuḥ sūryapramāṇaśca kadācitsomasannibhaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The planet whose area has been stated to be of half of yojana, no other planet is there with an area smaller than that. The area of Rahu is as big as that of the Sun. Sometimes, its area equates with that of the Moon.

## \|\| 1.125.54 \|\|

*nakṣatragrahamānastu1 ketustvaniyataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*avijñātagatiścaiva cañcalatvannarādhipa \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O lord of the people, the size of Ketu is not supposed to be definite. Besides, being of unstable nature, his race too is unknown.

## \|\| 1.125.55-56 \|\|

*tathālakṣitarūpastu bahurūpadharo hi saḥ \|*  
*bhūrlokaḥ pṛthivī proktā antarikṣaṃ bhuvaḥ smṛtam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*svarlokastridivaṃ jñeyaṃ śeṣādūrdhvaṃ yathākramam \|*  
*bhūpatistu sadā tvagnistenāsau bhūpatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Though he usually remains invisible, but he occasionally also takes to different forms. The earth has been called as Bhuloka, the space as Bhuvarloka and the Svarloka has been known as the heaven. The rest of the lokas are lodged in the sky. Being the lord of the earth, the fire god has been called as Bhupati.

## \|\| 1.125.57-59 \|\|

*vāyurnabhaspatistena tathā sūryo divaspatiḥ \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasaścaiva guhyakāḥ siddharākṣasāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*bhūrlokavāsinaḥ sarve antarikṣacarāñchṛṇu \|*  
*marutaḥ saptamaskaṃdhe rudrāstatraiva cāśvinau \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ādityā vasavaḥ sarve tathaiva ca gavāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*caturthe tu maharloke vasante kalpavāsinaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. Similarly, the wind god is the lord of space, the Sun is known as Divaspati. The Gandharvas, Apsaras, Guhyakas, Siddhas and the Rakshasas are the dwellers of Bhuloka (or earth). Now, I shall speak about the dwellers of the sky. You please listen. Maruts (winds) live in seventh region (the heaven). Rudra and Ashvinikumaras, Aditya, Vasus and all the gods also live there. Fourth is Maharloka, where the Kalpavasi people live.

## \|\| 1.125.60 \|\|

*prajānāṃ patibhiḥ sarveḥ sahitāḥ kurunandana \|*  
*janaloke pañcame ca vasante bhūmidāḥ sadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Janaloka is the fifth, in which all the Prajapati besides those who donate land, live.

## \|\| 1.125.61 \|\|

*ṛtuḥ sanatkumārādyā vairājabhra tathāśrayāḥ \|*  
*satyastu saptame loke hyapunarmārgagāminām \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Ritus, Sanatkumaras and Vairajas dwell in Satyaloka and reaching that place, none has to be reborn.

## \|\| 1.125.62 \|\|

*brahmalokaḥ samākhyāto hyapratīghātalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*itihāsavido yatra krīḍante kurunandana \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thus, I have revealed to you the unobstructed features of Brahmaloka, which is testified by the aforesaid statement. The people who have specialized on history or the Mahabharata, always enjoy the sports there.

## \|\| 1.125.63 \|\|

*śṛṇvanti ca purāṇāni ye sadā bhīmanaṃdana \|*  
*mahītalātsahasrāṇāṃ śatādūrdhvaṃ divākaraḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O son of Bhima! One who listens to the stories of the Puranas daily, he also dwells in that place. The Sun gets explained at a distance of a hundred thousand yojanas from the earth.

## \|\| 1.125.64 \|\|

*śatayojanakoṭyastu1 bhūmerūrdhvaṃ dhruvaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tato viṃśatilakṣastu trailokyotsedha ucyate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Dhruva (North Pole) is located at a distance of seven crores of yojanas from the earth. Thus, the height of all the three lokas works out to be twenty lakhs yojanas.

## \|\| 1.125.65 \|\|

*dviguṇaistu sahasraistu yojanānāṃ śateṣu ca \|*  
*lokāṃtaramatho caivaṃ dhruvādūrdhvaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. At double the distance from the Pole star, other lokas are lodged.

## \|\| 1.125.66 \|\|

*devadānavagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*bhūtā vidyādharāścaiva aṣṭau te devayonayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. There are eight type of divine creations including Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, serpents, goblins and Vidyadharas.

## \|\| 1.125.67-68 \|\|

*yasminvyomni tvime lokāḥ sapta vai sampratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*marutaḥ pitaro hyete tasminnevāgnayo grahāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yāstvapyetāḥ samākhyātā mayāṣṭau devayonayaḥ \|*  
*mūrtāścāmūrtayaścaiva sarvāstā vyomni saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. The part of the sky in which the seven lokas, Maruts and Pitris are lodged, in the same place Agni, Guha, the eight Devayonis which have been described earlier, besides the visible and invisible ones, are all well settled there.

## \|\| 1.125.69 \|\|

*evaṃvidhamidaṃ vyoma sarvavyomamayaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*sarvadevamayaṃ caiva sarvagrahamayaṃ tathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Therefore, the sky is known as Sarvavyomamaya, besides the abode of all the planets.

## \|\| 1.125.70 \|\|

*tasmādyo hyarcayedvyoma tena sarve'rcitāḥ surāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena śubhārthī vyoma cārcayet \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Therefore, the one, who worships vyoma, it is sure that it amounts to worshipping the gods. Therefore, a person desirous of his own welfare, should worship vyoma making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.125.71 \|\|

*yastvarcate sadā vyoma bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣadhvajasado rājansa gacchennātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Having been filled with the devotion and faith, one who always worships the vyoma, be surely achieves the place of lord Shiva.

## Chapter 126. Glory of Vyoma

## \|\| 1.126.1-2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*ākāśaṃ khaṃ diśo vyoma antarikṣaṃ nabho'mbaram \|*  
*puṣkaraṃ gaganaṃ merurvipulaṃ ca bilaṃ tathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āpochidraṃ tathā śūnyaṃ tamo vai rodasī tathā \|*  
*nāmānyetāni te vyomnaḥ kīrtitāni mahīpate \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sumantu said — O lord of the earth, Kha, Vyoma, Antariksha, Nabha, Ambara (sky), Pushkara, Gagana, Meru, Vipula, Bila, Apochidra, Shunya and Rodasi are all the names of the sky.

## \|\| 1.126.3-4 \|\|

*lavaṇakṣīradadhyamlaghṛtamadhvikṣavastathā \|*  
*svādūdakaśca saptaite samudrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho nīla eva ca \|*  
*śvetaśca śṛṅgavāṃścaiva ṣaḍete varṣaparvatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. There are seven oceans comprising of saltish water, bitter water, curd, ghi, honey, juice of sugarcane, besides the sweet water. There are six varsha mountains known by the names of Hemakuta, Nishadha, Nila, Shveta and Shringavan.

## \|\| 1.126.5-6 \|\|

*madhyasaṃsthastathaiteṣāṃ mahārājataparvataḥ \|*  
*māhendrī cāpyathāgneyī yāmyā ca nairṛtī tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vāruṇī cātha vāyavyā saumyaiśānī tathaiva ca \|*  
*etāḥ puryastu devānāṃ tathopari samāśritāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Sumeru mountain is lodged in the centre of these mountains over the top of the same, the divine cities of the gods are located, which are known as — Mahendri, Agneyi, Yamya, Nairriti, Varuni, Vayavya, Saumya and Aishani.

## \|\| 1.126.7-9 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ tu sthito vīra lokālokastu parvataḥ \|*  
*tataścaṇḍakapālaṃ tu tasmāttatparatastu yaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tato'gnirvāyurākāśaṃ tato bhūtādirucyate \|*  
*tato mahānahaṅkāraḥ prakṛtiḥ puruṣastataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*puruṣādīśvaro śreya īśvareṇāvrṛtaṃ jagat \|*  
*īśvaro bhagavanbhānustenedaṃ pūritaṃ jagat \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. The Lokaloka mountain is lodged on earth. It is said that after that Agni is lodged in Chanda-kapala, then wind in Agni, while the bhutas are lodged in the sky. Thereafter, Mahat, Ahamkara, Prakriti, Purusha and Ishvara are lodged to the north. Thus the entire world is surrounded by Ishvara. Lord Bhaskara is always remembered in the sense of Ishvara, because, it is he, who has created the universe.

## \|\| 1.126.10 \|\|

*sahasrāṃśurmahātejāścaturbāhurmahābalaḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvamapyatha lokāstu prāṅmayā ye prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The valorous Sungod has four arms. Therefore, the lokas which have been described by me earlier, are lodged in the upper regions.

## \|\| 1.126.11-14 \|\|

*bhūyastānsampravakṣyāmi aṇḍāvaraṇakārakān \|*  
*bhūrlokastubhuvarlokastṛtīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*maharjanastapaḥ satyaḥ saptalokāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*1 tatastavaṃḍakapālaṃ tu tasmācca parastapaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tato'gnirvāyurākāśaṃ tato bhūtādirucyate \|*  
*tato mahānpradhānaśca prakṛtipuruṣastataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*puruṣādīśvaro jñeya īśvareṇāvṛtaṃ jagat \|*  
*bhūmeradhastātsaptaiva lokānabhimatāñchṛṇu \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. I am going to speak about those lokas again, which are covering the entire globe. These are the seven lokas, known as — Bhuloka, Bhuvarloka, Svargaloka, Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka and Satyaloka. They are said to be lodged in the upper regions. After them, Andda-kapala, Agni, wind, sky, Bhutas etc., besides Mahan, Pradhana, Prakriti, Purusha and Ishvara have been described, in which the importance of Purusha like Ishvara goes on increasing progressively. Thus the entire universe is surrounded by Ishvara. Now listen to the lokas existing under the earth.

## \|\| 1.126.15 \|\|

*talaṃ sutalapātāle talātalaṃ tathātalam \|*  
*vitalaṃ ca kuruśreṣṭha saptamaṃ ca rasātalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The lokas lodged underground are known as Tala, Sutala, Patala, Talatala, Vitala, Kuru and Rasatala, the seventh one.

## \|\| 1.126.16-17 \|\|

*tato'gnirvāyurākāśaṃ tato bhūtādirucyate \|*  
*tato mahānpradhānaśca prakṛtiḥ puruṣastataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*puruṣādīśvaro jñeya īśvareṇāvṛtaṃ jagat \|*  
*evaṃ meroḥ pramāṇaṃ tu sarvametatprakīrtitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. There also as stated earlier, there are Agni, Wind, Sky, Bhutas etc., Mahan, Pradhana, Prakriti, Purusha and Ishvara, whose importance is gradually increased. The same world is getting surrounded with Ishvara. Thus all the evidence of Meru has been discussed.

## \|\| 1.126.18 \|\|

*caturasraścatuḥ śṛṃgaḥ sa meruḥ kāñcanaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ saṃsthito madhye siddhagandharvasevitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Meru mountain is square in shape, with four peaks. Being auspicious, it is having the complexion of gold. It is said to have been lodged in the middle of the earth, which is always served by the Siddhas and the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.126.19 \|\|

*caturbhiḥ kāñcanaiḥ śṛṃgairdivyairdivamivollikhan \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi caturāśītirucchritaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. All the four peaks of this mountain appear like a line protruding from the earth. It is eighty four thousand yojanas in height.

## \|\| 1.126.20 \|\|

*praviṣṭaḥ ṣoḍaśādhastādaṣṭaviṃśativistṛtaḥ \|*  
*vistārastriguṇaścāsya pariṇāhastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Its depth in the earth is sixteen thousand yojanas. Its width is eighteen thousand yojanas. Its length is said to be three times more than the width.

## \|\| 1.126.21 \|\|

*tasya saumanasaṃ nāma śṛṃgamekaṃ tu kāñcanam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ padmarāgābhaṃ jyotiṣkaṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Its first peak is made of the Saumanasa (beautiful) gold. The second peak is made of resplendent ruby diamonds.

## \|\| 1.126.22 \|\|

*tṛtīyaṃ nāmataścitraṃ sarvadevamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*caturthaṃ rājataṃ śuklaṃ candraujaskamiti smṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The third peak is known by the name of Chitra which represents all the gods. The fourth peak is known by the name of Chandraujaska and is said to comprise of the silver.

## \|\| 1.126.23-24 \|\|

*yattu saumanasaṃ nāma śṛṃgaṃ gāṅgeyamucyate \|*  
*tadeva codayo nāmnā yatrodyandṛśyate raviḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*uttareṇa parikramya jambūdvīpaṃ divākaraḥ \|*  
*dṛśyo bhavati bhūtānāṃ śikharaṃ ca samāsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Saumanas peak is said to be made of gold and the Sun can be seen rising from the same. Therefore, it is also known by the name of Udayachala and Gangeya. To its north, circumambulating the Jambudvipa, when the Sun reaches its peak, the people believe him to be the god. At that point of time, he becomes visible to the people.

## \|\| 1.126.25 \|\|

*kāñcanasya ca śailasya tejasārkasya cāhṛte \|*  
*ubhe sandhye prakāśete ātāmre pūrvapaścime \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When the Sun shines over the peak of the Meru mountain, then the eastern and western directions appear to be in copper or red colour.

## \|\| 1.126.26 \|\|

*śṛṃge saumanase sūrya uttiṣṭhatyuttarāyaṇe \|*  
*jyotiṣe dakṣiṇe cāpi viṣuve madhyatastayoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. During the period of Uttarayana the Sun rises from the Saumanas mountain. During Dakshinayana the Sun rises from the Jyotishikha peak. During the Vishuva or intervening period the Sun rises from the middle of the two peaks.

## \|\| 1.126.27-28 \|\|

*īśendrodriśca aiśānyāṃ tatrāgniḥ pūrvadakṣiṇe \|*  
*nairṛte'pi tato jñeyo vāyavye marutastathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*madhye tu kaṃjajaḥ sākṣādgrahā jyotīṃṣi caiva hi \|*  
*ādityastena rūpeṇa tasminvyomni pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. To the north-east of the same, Indra is located; fire is located to the south-east of it; the pitris are lodged to the south-west; the Maruts are lodged in the north-west, while Brahma himself is lodged in the centre of it, besides the constellations as well as the planets and the stars. The said area is known as vyoma as well, because the Sun is lodged in that place in his own form.

## \|\| 1.126.29 \|\|

*idaṃ devamayaṃ vyoma tathā lokamayaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*pūrvakoṇasthite śṛṃge sthitaḥ śukro mahīpate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Vyoma has therefore, been believed to be representing the gods as well as the lokas. O lord of earth, on the peak in eastern direction is lodged the planet Venus.

## \|\| 1.126.30 \|\|

*helijaścāpare jñeyo dhananāthastathāpare \|*  
*somaścāpi caturthe tu sthitaḥ śṛṃge janādhipa \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On the other part, there is Helija or Sun, Kubera on the third, while the Moon is lodged over the fourth peak.

## \|\| 1.126.31-32 \|\|

*madhye keśāsthito rājanhuṅkāraśca pinākinaḥ \|*  
*śṛṃge pūrvottare rājansthito devo vidhukṣaye1 \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tataḥ sthito mahādevo gopatirlokapūjitaḥ \|*  
*pūrvāgneyīsthite śṛṃge sthito vai śāṇḍilaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. O king, in the centre of the mountain lives Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Over the north-east peak of the mountain, dark sides of the Moon Mahadeva, besides the Sungod who is adorable by all. On the peak to the south-east, the son of Shandilya resides.

## \|\| 1.126.33-34 \|\|

*tataḥ sthito mahātejāḥ kīnāśo helinandanaḥ \|*  
*sthito vai nairṛte śṛṃge virūpākṣo mahābalaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tasmādanantaro devaḥ sthito vai yādasāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sthito mahātejā vīra mitro mahābalaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Thereafter, lives Yama — the son of the Sungod. On the south-west peak lives Virupaksha. After him lives Varuna. Thereafter, lives the valorous Mitra.

## \|\| 1.126.35 \|\|

*vāyavyaṃ śṛṃgamāśritya sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|*  
*tataḥ sthito daśabalo naramāruhya bhārata \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On the north-east mountain peak, there lives Dashabala making a human as his vehicle.

## \|\| 1.126.36 \|\|

*brahmā madhye sthito devo hyanantaścādha eva hi \|*  
*upendraśaṅkarau devau brahmaṇo'nte samāsthitau \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Brahma is lodged in the middle. In the lower part of it, Ananta with Vishnu, Brahma and Shiva are lodged.

## \|\| 1.126.37 \|\|

*eṣa merustathā vyoma eṣa dharmaśca paṭhyate \|*  
*sarvadevamayaścāyaṃ merurvyoma iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In this way, the Meru mountain is also known by the names of Vyoma and Dharma as well. Because of its representing all the gods, it is known by the name of Vyoma.

## \|\| 1.126.38 \|\|

*tathā vedamayaścāpi paṭhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgāṇi vedāścatvāraḥ pūrvaśṛṃgādayo viduḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It is also surely the form of the Vedas, because all its four peaks are said to be representing the four Vedas.

## Chapter 127. The story of Samba

## \|\| 1.127.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*kathamārādhitaḥ sūryaḥ sāmbenāmitatejasā \|*  
*vimuktastu kathaṃ rogairbrūhi māṃ dvijasattama \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O best of Brahmanas, how did the immensely illustrious Samba worship the Sungod? How was he relieved of his ailment? You kindly let me know.

## \|\| 1.127.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra śṛṇu sāmbakathāṃ purā \|*  
*vistārādvacmi te sarvāṃ kathāṃ pāpavimocinīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said — O Indra of the rulers, you have put up an excellent question. Therefore, I am relating the story of Samba. I am going to relate this story which relieves one of all the sins, quite exhaustively.

## \|\| 1.127.3-4 \|\|

*purā saṃśrutya māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasya sa nāradāt \|*  
*vinayādupasaṅgamya vacaḥ pitaramabravīt \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kaśmalenābhibhūto'smi malena vyādhinācyuta \|*  
*vaidyairoṣadhibhiścāpi na śāntirmama vidyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Earlier Samba, having heard the glory of lord Bhaskara from the sage Narada, humbly went to his father and said to him — “O Achyuta, I feel helpless because of my suffering from the disease of leprosy, because I am getting no relief from the medicines given to me by the great physicians.

## \|\| 1.127.5 \|\|

*vanaṃ gacchāmi bhagavannanujñāṃ dātumarhasi \|*  
*śivena puṇḍarīkākṣa dhyāya māṃ puruṣottama \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O lord, therefore, you permit me to go to the forest. O lotus eyed lord, O Purushottama! You kindly pay special attention to my request.”

## \|\| 1.127.6 \|\|

*anujñātaḥ sa kṛṣṇena sindhoruttarakūlataḥ \|*  
*gatvā santārayāmāsa candrabhāgāṃ mahānadīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then, at the command of Shri Krishna, he went to the northern bank of the river Sindhu, from where he crossed the river Chandrabhaga.

## \|\| 1.127.7-8 \|\|

*tato mitravanaṃ gatvā tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*upavāsaparaḥ sāmbaḥ śuṣko dhamanisantataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ārādhanārthaṃ sūryasya guhyaṃ stotraṃ1 jajāpa ha \|*  
*vedaiścaturbhiḥ samitaṃ purāṇāśrayabṛṃhitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. From there, he went to the Mitravana tirtha. His veins had been dried out because of his continuous fasting. He started the worship of the Sungod by a secret stotra, which was related to in all the four Vedas and also mentioned in the Puranas.

## \|\| 1.127.9-10 \|\|

*yadetanmaṇḍalaṃ śuklaṃ divyaṃ hyajaramavyayam \|*  
*yuktaṃ manojavairaśvairhārītairbrahmavādibhiḥ2 \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ādireṣa1 hi bhūtānāmāditya iti saṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*trailokyacakṣurevātra paramātmā prajāpatiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He is spotless, having white complexion, is indestructible, eternal, is the solar disc, which is quite visible. It is driven by the horses, having the speed of the wind. It was being served by a Harita bird and the Brahmanas well-versed in Brahman. He is the foremost of all the living beings. Therefore, he is known by the name of Aditya. He is the lord of the three worlds, besides being the supreme soul and Prajapati.

## \|\| 1.127.11-12 \|\|

*eṣa vai maṇḍale hyasminpuruṣo dīpyate mahān \|*  
*eṣa viṣṇuracintyātmā brahmā caiṣa pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*rudro mahendro varuṇa ākāśaṃ pṛthivī jalam \|*  
*vāyuḥ śaśāṅkaḥ parjanyo dhanādhyakṣo vibhāvasuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. He is resplendent in the mandala, who is visible like a great person. He alone represents inconceivable Vishnu, Brahma — the grandsire, Rudra, Mahendra, Varuna, the sky, earth, water, wind, the moon, clouds, Kubera and Vibhavasu.

## \|\| 1.127.13 \|\|

*yaṣa eṣa maṇḍale hyasmin puruṣo dīpyate mahān \|*  
*ekaḥ sākṣānmahādevo vṛtramaṇḍanibhaḥ sadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The lustre in this mandala or the disc, resembling a great personality, represents lord Mahadeva, who remains covered (with a sheath) like an egg.

## \|\| 1.127.14-16 \|\|

*kālo hyeṣa mahābāhurnibodhotpattilakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ya eṣa maṇḍale hyasmiṃstejobhiḥ pūrayanmahīm \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhrāmyate hyavyavacchinno vātairyo'mṛtalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*nātaḥ parataraṃ kiñcittejasā vidyate kvacit \|\| 15 \|\|*

*puṣṇāti sarvabhūtāni eṣa eva sudhāmṛtaiḥ \|*  
*antasthānmlecchajātīyāṃstiryagyonigatānapi \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Therefore, this lord with long arms, should be treated as Kola who creates the universe. By dwelling in this mandala, he has covered the entire earth with his lustre. He is nectar like and wanders everywhere on earth like the wind without any obstruction. There is nothing else in the world beyond his lustre. He nourishes all the living beings with his nectar like rays, including the people of low origin as well as the birds.

## \|\| 1.127.17 \|\|

*kāruṇyātsarvabhūtāni pāsi tvaṃ ca vibhāvaso \|*  
*śvitrakuṣṭhyaṃdhabadhirānpaṃgūṃścāpi tathā vibho \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O graceful one, because of compassion, you protect all the people of high and low rank#. Similarly, you also protect those who are suffering with leprosy, blind, dumb as well lame.

## \|\| 1.127.18-19 \|\|

*prapannavatsalo deva kurute nīrujo bhavān \|*  
*cakramaṇḍalamagrāṃśca nirdhanālpāyuṣastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pratyakṣadarśī tvaṃ deva samuddharasi līlayā \|*  
*kā me śaktiḥ stavaiḥ stotumārto'haṃ rogapīḍitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. O Deva, you shower your grace on the people who take refuge in you. Therefore, you remove the ailments of all the people. O Deva, those who are absorbed in the solar disc, be they poor or having short life, being benevolent, are redeemed. Therefore, where do I have the enough strength to offer prayer to you by reciting the stotras because I am suffering from disease.

## \|\| 1.127.20-21 \|\|

*stūyase tvaṃ sadā devairbrahmaviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ \|*  
*mahendrasiddhagandharvairapsarobhiḥ saguhyakaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*stutibhiḥ kiṃ pavitrairvā tava deva samīritaiḥ \|*  
*yasya te ṛgyajuḥ sāmnāṃ tritaya maṇḍalasthitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. As Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva always offer prayers to you, similarly, Mahendra, Gandharvas, Apsaras and Guhyakas also eulogise you. O Deva, the auspicious stutis are offered to you, while Rik, Yajuh and Sama are already lodged in your mandala.

## \|\| 1.127.22 \|\|

*dhyānināṃ tvaṃ paraṃ dhyānaṃ mokṣadvāraṃ ca mokṣiṇām \|*  
*anantatejasākṣobhyo hyaciṃtyāvyaktaniṣkalaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Deva, you are the excellent source of meditation for the meditators. You are the door of moksha for the people desirous of redemption. Because of you possessing the enormous lustre beyond measure, you are undisturbed, beyond comprehension, reversible and fruitless.

## \|\| 1.127.23 \|\|

*yadayaṃ vyāhataḥ kiñcitstotre'smiñjagataḥ patiḥ \|*  
*ārtiṃ bhaktiṃ ca vijñāya tatsarvaṃ jñātumarhasi \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. You are the lord of the universe. Thus, whatever little has been said in this stotra, you kindly take into consideration my precarious condition as well as my devotion and well understand the situation.

## \|\| 1.127.24 \|\|

*tamuvāca tataḥ sūryaḥ prītyā jāmbavatīsutam \|*  
*prīto'smi tapasā vatse brūhi tanmāṃ yadicchasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter, the Sungod, delightfully spoke to Samba — the son of Jambavati — “O Son, I am happy with your devotion. You express your desire before me.”

## \|\| 1.127.25 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*yadi prasanno bhagavāneṣa eva varo mama \|*  
*bhaktirbhavatu me'tyarthaṃ tvayi deva sanātana \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Samba said — O eternal Deva, in case you are pleased with me, then grant me a boon, that I get the maximum of your prowess.

## \|\| 1.127.26 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*bhūyastuṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te varaṃ varaya suvrata \|*  
*sa dvitīyaṃ varaṃ vavre tadaiva varadaṃ vibhum \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Surya said — O Suvrata, let you meet with welfare. I am extremely happy with you. Therefore, you beg for any other boon you like. Thereafter, Samba expressed for his desire to have another boon.

## \|\| 1.127.27 \|\|

*malaḥ śarīrasaṃstho me tvatprasādātpraṇaśyatu \|*  
*yena me śuddhamakhilaṃ vapurbhavatu gopate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He said — “O lord of rays, let the ailment in my body disappear by your grace and my body should become spotless neat and clean.

## \|\| 1.127.28 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*sa tathāstviti tenokto bhāskareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*tāṃ mumoca rujaṃ sāmbo dehāttvacamivoragaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Sumantu said — Lord Bhaskara, then said to Samba — “Be it so.” At the mere speaking of these words by the Sungod, the disease left the body of Samba in the same way as the skin leaves the body of the serpent.

## \|\| 1.127.29 \|\|

*tato rūpeṇa divyena rūpavānabhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ purato'vasthito'bhavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then, attaining the divine form, Samba offered his salutation to the Sungod and stood before him.

## \|\| 1.127.30 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*bhūyaśca śṛṇu me sāmbaṃ tuṣṭo'haṃ yadbravīmi te \|*  
*adya prabhṛti tvannāmnā mama sthānāni suvrata \|*  
*kṣitau ye sthāpayiṣyanti teṣāṃ lokāḥ sanātanāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Sungod said — O Samba. I am extremely happy with you. Today you listen to me whatever is spoken by me. O Suvrata, whosoever shall make a place with my name on earth and shall consecrate my image there, he would become eternal.

## \|\| 1.127.31 \|\|

*sthāpayasvaiva māmasmiṃścandrabhāgātaṭe śubhe \|*  
*tava nāmnā ca sāmbedaṃ parāṃ khyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Therefore, O Samba! At the auspicious bank of the river Chandrabhaga, you should establish my image there. It would become more popular by your association with the same.

## \|\| 1.127.32 \|\|

*kīrtistavākṣayā loke khyātiṃ yāsyati suvrata \|*  
*bhūyaśca te pradāsyāmi pratyahaṃ svapnadarśanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You will earn infallible glory in the world. Still, I shall daily appear in your dream.

## \|\| 1.127.33 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*evaṃ dattvā varaṃ tasmai vṛṣṇisiṃhāya cāparam \|*  
*pratyakṣadarśanaṃ dattvā tatraivāntaradhāddhariḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Sumantu said — In this way, the Sungod, not only appeared before the prince of the Yadava race, but then disappeared from the same place.

## \|\| 1.127.34-35 \|\|

*ya idaṃ paṭhate stotraṃ trikālaṃ bhaktimānnaraḥ \|*  
*trisaptaśatamāvartya homaṃ vā saptarātrakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*rājyakāmo labhedrājyaṃ dhanakāmo labhedadhanam \|*  
*rogārto mucyate rogādyathā sāmbastathaiva saḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Therefore, a person, who recites this stotra thrice a day or performs homa reciting the mantra a hundred and twenty one times for seven nights, he achieves the kingdom in case he be desirous for the same, in case he be desirous for riches, he gets the same. In case of an ailing person, he is relieved of the disease like Samba.

## \|\| 1.127.36 \|\|

*sūryalokaṃ vrajeccāpi bhaktyā pūjya divākaram \|*  
*ramate ca tathā tasmindevaiśca parivāritaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. By adoring the Sungod with devotion, one can achieve even the abode of the Sungod, where such persons have sports with the gods like their own family members.

## Chapter 128. Prayer of Samba

## \|\| 1.128.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*astāvīcca tata sāmbaḥ kṛśo dhamanisantataḥ \|*  
*rājannāmasahasreṇa sahasrāṃśuṃ divākaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O king, Samba had become so weak that only the veins had been left in his body. He actually had started eulogising the thousand rayed Sungod with his Sahasranama stotra.

## \|\| 1.128.2 \|\|

*khidyamānaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā sūryaḥ kṛṣṇātmajaṃ tadā \|*  
*svapne'smai darśanaṃ dattvā punarvacanamabravīt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Sungod, then finding that the son of Krishna was having a disturbed mind, appeared in his dream and said.

## \|\| 1.128.3 \|\|

*śrīsūrya uvāca \|*  
*sāmba sāmba mahāvāho śṛṇu jāmbavatīsuta \|*  
*alaṃ nāmasahasreṇa paṭha cemaṃ śubhaṃ stavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Sungod said — O valorous Samba — son of Jambavati, you listen. You stop the uttering of thousand names of mine, you start reciting the auspicious stotra of my names.

## \|\| 1.128.4 \|\|

*yāni guhyāni nāmāni pavitrāṇi śubhāni ca \|*  
*tāni te kīrtiyiṣyāmi prayatnādavadhāraya \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I am revealing to you my secret and auspicious names. You pleasantly remember all the names which are being spoken by me.

## \|\| 1.128.5-7 \|\|

*vaikartano vivasvāṃśca mārtaṇḍo bhāskaro raviḥ \|*  
*lokaprakāśakaḥ śrīmāṃllokacakṣurgraheśvaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*lokasākṣī trilokeśaḥ kartā hartā tamisrahā \|*  
*tapanastāpanaścaiva śuciḥ saptāśvavāhanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*gabhastihasto brahmā ca sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*ekarviśatirityeṣa stava iṣṭassadā mama \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. These names are — Vaikartan, Vivasvan, Martanda, Bhaskara, Ravi, Lokaprakasha, Shriman, Lokachakshu, Graheshvara, Lokasakshi, Trilokesha, Karta, Harta, Tamisraha, Tapan, Tapana, Shuchi, Saptashvavahana, Gabhastihasta, Brahma and Sarvadeva, This stotra, with twenty one names, is always liked by me.

## \|\| 1.128.8 \|\|

*śarīrārogyadaścaiva dhanavṛddhiyaśaskaraḥ \|*  
*stavarāja iti khyātastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The reciting of these names removes body ailment, enhances riches and wisdom, besides the glory, because it is known in the three worlds as Stavaraja or the foremost of all the stotras.

## \|\| 1.128.9 \|\|

*ya etena mahābāho dve sandhye'stamanodaye \|*  
*stauti māṃ praṇato bhūtvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O valorous one, before the rising or the setting of the sun, on both the Sandhyas, when a person humbly recites this stotra, he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.128.10 \|\|

*mānasaṃ vācikaṃ vāpi kāyikaṃ yacca duṣkṛtam \|*  
*ekajāpyena tatsarvaṃ praṇaśyati mamāgrataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. All the sins committed by action, thought and behaviour are washed out by reciting this stotra only once.

## \|\| 1.128.11 \|\|

*eṣa japyaśca homaśca sandhyopāsanameva ca \|*  
*balimantro'rghyamantro'tha dhūpamantrastathaiva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Therefore, this stotra should be recited as well as used in the performing of the homa. Like the performing of Sandhya, the offering and arghya can be given with the reciting of this stotra. This is also the mantra for offering incense.

## \|\| 1.128.12 \|\|

*annapradāne snāne ca praṇipāte pradakṣiṇe \|*  
*pūjito'yaṃ mahāmantraḥ sarvapāpaharaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This mantra can also be used while giving away food in charity, while bathing, or while circumambulating with devotion. This Mahamantra should be recited, because it is auspicious and is destroyer of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.128.13-14 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavānbhāskaro jagatāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*āmantrya kṛṣṇatanayaṃ tatraivāntarhito'bhavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sāmbo'pi stavarājena stutvā saptāśvavāhanam \|*  
*prītātmā nīrujaḥ śrīmāṃstasmādrogādvimuktavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Thereafter, the Sungod, being sent off by the son of Shri Krishna, disappeared from that place. Samba, on the other hand, after eulogising the Sungod with seven horses, with the reciting of Stavaraja, delightfully becoming free of disease, left for his place.

## Chapter 129. Consecration of Surya image by Samba

## \|\| 1.129.1-2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*atha labdhavaraḥ sāmbo varaṃ prāpya purātanam \|*  
*manyamānastadāścaryaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva sārdhamanyaistapasvibhiḥ \|*  
*snāpanārthaṃ nātidūraṃ candrabhāgāṃ nadīṃ yayau \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sumantu said — Thereafter, regaining his earlier beauty, having been filled with delight and surprise, Samba went in the company of other Rishis for taking a bath at the bank of Chandrabhaga river at a little distance.

## \|\| 1.129.3 \|\|

*kṛtvātmamaṇḍalākāraṃ śraddadhāno dinedine \|*  
*sasnau sañcintayāmāsa kiṃ rūpaṃ sthāpayāmyaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Developing a great devotion in his mind, creating daily a mandala or a circle, he started taking bath there. He also thought as to how to consecrate the Surya image there.

## \|\| 1.129.4 \|\|

*sa snātaḥ sahasaivātha praṇamya1 tu prabhāvatīm \|*  
*uhyamānāṃ jalaughena pratimāṃ sammukhīṃ raveḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then once, when he took a bath in the river, he found an image with lustre emerging out of the water. It was facing the Sun and was being washed with waves of the water. He offered his salutation to the image.

## \|\| 1.129.5 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya vīrasya samutpannamidaṃ yathā \|*  
*devena yattadājñaptaṃ tadidaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the very look at the image, an idea flashed in the mind of Samba, that the image could be the same, as commended by the Sungod earlier. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.129.6 \|\|

*sa tāmuttārya salilādānīya ca mahīpate \|*  
*tasminmitravanoddeśe sthāpayāmāsa tāṃ tadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O king, Samba took out the image from water and consecrated it in the Mitravana.

## \|\| 1.129.7 \|\|

*nidhāya pratimāṃlloke sāmbastasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*mitraṃ mitravane ramye sthāpayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Samba kept the image of Surya there itself, and consecrated the image in the Mitravana appropriately, giving the image the name of Mitra.

## \|\| 1.129.8 \|\|

*tatastāmeva papraccha praṇamya pratimāṃ raveḥ \|*  
*keneyaṃ nirmitā nātha bhavato hyākṛtiḥ śubhā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter, offering his salutation to the image, he asked the same — “Who has prepared this beautiful image?”

## \|\| 1.129.9 \|\|

*pratimā tamuvācātha śṛṇu sāmba bruve svayam \|*  
*nirmitā yena cāpyeṣā madīyā puruṣākṛtiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The image himself replied to him — “O Samba! You listen, I am going to reveal the identity of the person who gave me the human shape.

## \|\| 1.129.10 \|\|

*mamātitejasāviṣṭaṃ rūpamāsītpurātanam \|*  
*asahyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato'smyabhyarcitaḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*sahyaṃ bhavatu te rūpaṃ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāmiti \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. My earlier form possessed enormous splendour which was unbearable for the living beings. Therefore, the gods eulogised me, saying — “O lord, your lustre is unbearable for the living beings. You kindly do something by which your lustre becomes bearable by the people.

## \|\| 1.129.11 \|\|

*tato mayā samādiṣṭo viśvakarmā mahātapāḥ \|*  
*tejasāṃ śātanaṃ kurvanrūpaṃ nirvartayasva me \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereafter, I commanded Vishvakarma — a great ascetic, that the excessive lustre of my body should be removed.

## \|\| 1.129.12 \|\|

*tatastu matsamādeśāttenaiva nipuṇaṃ tadā \|*  
*śākadvīpe bhramiṃ kṛtvā rūpaṃ nirvartitaṃ mama \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At my command, the excellent Vishvakarma brought a lathe from Shakadvipa and improved my beauty.

## \|\| 1.129.13 \|\|

*prītyā teṣāṃ prapañco'yaṃ sa mayā kāritaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*teneyaṃ kalpavṛkṣāttu nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the request of those people, in order to delight them, I got this image made. Vishvakarma has built my image with the wood of Kalpavriksha.

## \|\| 1.129.14 \|\|

*kṛtvā himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe purā siddhaniṣevite \|*  
*tvadarthaṃ candrabhāgāyāṃ tatastenāvatāritā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In earlier times, he had floated this image m the river Chandrabhaga for your sake only.

## \|\| 1.129.15-16 \|\|

*bhavatastāraṇārthaṃ hi tataḥ sthānamidaṃ śubham \|*  
*ruciraṃ sarvadā sāmba sānnidhyaṃ me'tra yāsyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sānnidhyaṃ mama pūrvāhṇe sutīre drakṣyate janaiḥ \|*  
*kālapriye ca madhyāhne'parāhṇe cātra nityaśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. For the sake of your redemption, this place has been found quite sacred for me, besides being beautiful. Therefore, O Samba, I shall remain here. In the forenoon time, I shall appear before the people in the Sutira region. During the noon time, I shall appear in Kalapriya region and in the evening time, I shall remain here.

## \|\| 1.129.17-18 \|\|

*pūrvāhṇe pūjayed brahmā madhyāhne cakradhṛtsvayam \|*  
*śaṅkaraścāparāhṇe tu māṃ pūjayati sarvadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ityukto'sau bhagavatā bhāskareṇa sa yādavaḥ \|*  
*harṣamāpa mahābāho bhāskaro'ntardadhe tataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. This is because Brahma adores me in the forenoon, Vishnu — the holder of cakra adores me in the noon, while Shiva adores me always in the afternoon. O long armed one, in this way, the Sungod revealed all the subjects to Samba in a detailed manner, who felt fully delighted. Thereafter, lord Bhaskara disappeared from that place.

## Chapter 130. Features of Surya temple

## \|\| 1.130.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ sāmbena viprendra pratiṣṭhā kāritā raveḥ \|*  
*kasya vā vacanāttena prāsādaḥ kārito raveḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — O lord of the rulers, how was the Surya image consecrated by Samba? At whose advice was the Sun temple built by him?

## \|\| 1.130.2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*atra te vacmi rājendra yathā sāmbena dhīmatā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā kāritā bhānoḥ prasādaśca mahīpate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sumantu said-I am going to speak out to you the way, Samba consecrated the Surya image, after building a Sun temple. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.130.3 \|\|

*sulabdhvā pratimāṃ bhānościntayāmāsa nāradam \|*  
*sa cāpi cintitaścāgādyatra jāmbavatīsutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Samba — the son of Jambavati, after receiving the image, started thinking deeply about Narada. At the same time, Narada arrived there.

## \|\| 1.130.4 \|\|

*tamāgatamabhiprekṣya nāradaṃ munisattamam \|*  
*sampūjya vidhivatsāṃbo nāradaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the arrival of Narada — the best of the sages there, Samba worshipped him in an appropriate manner. Then he said to him.

## \|\| 1.130.5 \|\|

*prāsādaṃ kārayedyastu bhāskarasya naro dvija \|*  
*kiṃ phalaṃ tasya devarṣe pratiṣṭhāṃ yaśca kārayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He said — “O Brahmana, what is the merit for the building of a Sun temple and consecrating a Sun image there?”

## \|\| 1.130.6 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*prāsādaṃ śobhane deśe yastu kārayate raveḥ \|*  
*sa yāti naraśārdūla sūryalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Narada said — O lion among the humans, a person who builds a temple for the Sun at an auspicious place, he achieves the Sungod. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.130.7 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ kuryādāyatanaṃ kasmindeśe dvijottama \|*  
*kīdṛkchastaṃ cāyatanaṃ devadevasya1 vai dvija \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Samba said — O best of Brahmanas, which type of temple should be there and in which country? What type of temple has been said to be praiseworthy for the Sungod?

## \|\| 1.130.8 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*yatra prabhūtaṃ salilamāgame ca vināśane \|*  
*devatāyatanaṃ kuryādyaśodharmavivṛddhaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Narada said: — At the start of the rainy season and also at the end of the rainy season the place which remains filled with water, at the bank of that tank, a person for the increase of dharma as well as his own glory, should built a temple of the god.

## \|\| 1.130.9 \|\|

*iṣṭāpūrtena labhate lokāṃstāṃśca1 vibhūṣitān \|*  
*devānāmālayaṃ kāryaṃ dvayaṃ yatra ca dṛśyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It is because with the building of a water tank and the performing of the yajna, one achieves the beautiful place. Therefore, the temple of a god should be built in a beautiful orchard or over the bank of a tank.

## \|\| 1.130.10 \|\|

*salilādyaṃ ca ārāmaḥ kṛteṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*sthāneṣveteṣu sānnidhyamupagacchanti devatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Because with the location of an orchard and a tank near the temple, the gods live there.

## \|\| 1.130.11-12 \|\|

*saraḥsu nalinīcchannanirastaraviraśmiṣu \|*  
*haṃsasaṃkṣiptakahlāravīthīvimalavāriṣu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*haṃsakāraṇḍavakrauñcacakravākavirāviṣu \|*  
*paryantavimalacchāyāviśrāntajanacāriṣu \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The tank in which the spreading of the lotus leaves or flowers are such that the sun rays do not penetrate into the surface of the water, the lines of the lotus flowers in case are squeezed with the movement of the swans, when the water is pure and clean, the birds like ducks, cranes and rudy birds issue chirping sound, and the shades of the trees are found around the tank over the banks of which the travellers or the walkers take rest always.

## \|\| 1.130.13-15 \|\|

*krauñcakāñcīsulāpāśca kalahaṃsakalasvanāḥ \|*  
*nadyastoyāṃśukā yatra śapharīkṛtamekhalāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*phulladrumottamāvāsāḥ saṅgamaśroṇimaṇḍalāḥ \|*  
*pulinādyunnatoraskā rasahāsāśca nimnagāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vanopāntanadīśailasaṃskaropāntabhūmiṣu \|*  
*ramante devatā nityaṃ pureṣūdyānavatsu ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Close to such tanks, the cranes should be issuing pleasant sound like the waistbands. The pleasant sound of the swans, the rivers putting the costumes of water with small fish serving them as waistbands, the blossoming trees should be over these banks, the sound of confluence of rivers, the sandy banks serving as breasts and the movement of water should be serving as sports. The closely flowing rivers should be in the vicinity of the mountains. By building a temple with an orchard at such a place, the gods always live there.

## \|\| 1.130.16 \|\|

*bhūmayo brāhmaṇādīnāṃ yāḥ proktā vāstukarmaṇi \|*  
*tā evaṃ teṣāṃ śasyante devatāyataneṣvapi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As has been told about the getting of land for the Brahmanas, similar type of land has been said to be praiseworthy for the temple of the god.

## \|\| 1.130.17-18 \|\|

*catuḥṣaṣṭipadaṃ kuryāddevatāyatanaṃ sadā \|*  
*dvāraṃ ca madhyamaṃ tasminsamadiksampraśasyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yo vistāro bhavettasya dviguṇā tatsamunnatiḥ \|*  
*ucchrāyastu tṛtīyo'tha tena tulyā kaṭirbhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The temple of the god should be sixty four feet in length. The door should be in the centre of it The temple doors should be square in shape. The height of the temple should be double its length. The middle part of the temple should be a third of its height.

## \|\| 1.130.19 \|\|

*vistārārdho bhavedgarbho bhinnayonyāḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*garbhapādonavistīrṇaṃ dvāraṃ dviguṇamucchritam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Half the part of the temple should locate its garbha-griha and in the other parts, there should be a boundary wall all around. The door should be made of one fourth width of the garbha-griha and its height should be the double of it.

## \|\| 1.130.20 \|\|

*ucchrayātpādavistīrṇā śākhā tadvadudumbarī \|*  
*vistārātpādapratimādbāhulyaṃ śeṣayoḥ smṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Similarly, the branches of udumbara and other trees should be made of the size equivalent to one fourth of the length.

## \|\| 1.130.21-22 \|\|

*nṛpaṃ saptanavabhiḥ śākhābhistatpraśasyate \|*  
*atha śākhācaturbhāge pratihārau niveśayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śailamaṅgalyavihagaḥ śrīvṛkṣaḥ svastikairghaṭaiḥ \|*  
*mānāṣṭamena1 bhāgena pratimā syātsapiṇḍikā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. For human use, a door with five, seven or nine branches has been considered to be praiseworthy. In the one fourth part of the branch, the images of two gatekeepers should also be lodged. The remaining parts of the door should be decorated with auspicious birds, kalpavriksha and auspicious pitchers. Like the one eighth part of a branch, the image should be made with high pedestal.

## \|\| 1.130.23-25 \|\|

*dvibhāgā pratimā tatra tṛtīyo bhāgapiṇḍikā \|*  
*pūrve merurmahābāho kailāsaśca tathāpare \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhavanti cāpare vīra vimānacchadanaṃ tathā \|*  
*samudrapadmagaruḍanandivarddhanakuñjarāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gṛharājo vṛṣo haṃsaḥ sarvatobhadrako ghaṭaḥ \|*  
*siṃho vṛṣaścatuṣkoṇaḥ ṣoḍaśāṣṭāśrayastathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. The image should have the height of two parts, the pedestal should be of one third of the height. O long armed one, in the first part, Meru, Kailua, plane, ocean, lotus, Garuda, Nandi, elephant, Agni, Bull, Swan, Sarvatobhadra, vase, lion, bull, square building with four comers, with sixteen or eight storeys can be built.

## \|\| 1.130.26 \|\|

*ityete viṃśatiḥ proktāḥ prāsādā yadunandana \|*  
*yathoktānukrameṇaiva lakṣaṇāni vadāmi te \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In this way, twenty types of temples are built, which have been described by me in a sequence.

## \|\| 1.130.27 \|\|

*navatriṃśaducchritamerurdvādaśabhaumo vividhakuharaśca \|*  
*dvārairyutaścatubhirdvātriṃśaddhastavistīrṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A temple known as Meru has the height of forty nine hands. It has twelve storeys, several types of basements and four gates. It is twenty five feet in width.

## \|\| 1.130.28 \|\|

*triṃśaddhastāyāmo daśabhaumaḥ sapta mandaraḥ \|*  
*śikharayutaḥ kailāso'pi śikharavānaṣṭāviṃśoṣṭabhaumaśca \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The temple with ten storeys, seven peaks and thirty hands in length, is known as Mandara. The temple known as Kailasa has eight stories, which is spread in twenty eight hands.

## \|\| 1.130.29 \|\|

*jālagavākṣairyukto vimānasaṃjñastrisaptakāyāmaḥ \|*  
*nandana iti vai bhaumo dvātriṃśatṣoḍaśāṅgayutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The temple known as Vimana has nets like ventilators. It is spread by twenty one hands. The Nandana Bhavana is spread in thirty two hands and has six storeys.

## \|\| 1.130.30 \|\|

*vṛttaḥ samudganāmā padmākṛtirayaṃ cāṣṭau \|*  
*śṛṅgeṇaikena bhavedekena ca bhūmikā tasya \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The building known as Samudra is circular in shape. The building named Padma resembles the lotus flowers and is spread in eight hands. It has a single peak and a single storey.

## \|\| 1.130.31 \|\|

*garuḍākṛtiśca garuḍo nandī vai ṣaṣṭivistīrṇaḥ \|*  
*kāyaśca saptabhaumo vibhūṣitoṃ'gaiśca saptaviṃśatibhiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The building named Garuda resembles the bird of the same name. The building with an area equivalent to eight hands is known as Nandavartana and has seven storeys. It has twenty seven compartments.

## \|\| 1.130.32 \|\|

*kuñjara iti gajapṛṣṭhaḥ ṣoḍaśāhastocchrito madhye \|*  
*gṛharājaḥ ṣoḍaśakastricakraśālā bhavedvalabhī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The mansion resembling an elephant is of the height of sixteen hands. It resembles the back of the elephant. It is known by the name of Kunjara. The mansion known as Griharaja has the three moon halls, each having the length of sixteen hands.

## \|\| 1.130.33 \|\|

*vṛṣa evaṃ mṛmiśṛṅgo dvāvaśahastaḥ samunnato vṛttaḥ \|*  
*haṃso haṃsākāro ghaṭo'ṣṭasahasrakalaśarūpaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A single storey mansion is of the length of sixteen hands. It has a single top and is of circular shape. It is known by the name of Vrisha or a Bull. A mansion of the size of swan is known as Hamsa. A building with eight thousand pitchers is known as Ghata palace.

## \|\| 1.130.34-35 \|\|

*dvārairyutaścaturbhirbahuśikharo bhavati sarvatobhadraḥ \|*  
*bahuruciracandraśālaḥ ṣaptaviṃśadbhāgabhūmiśca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*siṃhaḥ siṃhākāro1 dvādaśakoṇo'ṣṭahastaśca \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. There is a palace named Sarvatobhadra. The Simha prasada has several doors, several peaks has beautiful grills like moon. It is spread in an area of twenty six hands. Simha prasada has twelve comers and is spread in an area of eight hands.

## \|\| 1.130.36-37 \|\|

*sahasratritayaṃ caiva kathitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*prāhuḥ sthāpayataścātra matamekaṃ vipaścitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kapotapālinīyuktamato gacchati tulyatām \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. In this way, the learned people have unanimously supported this description. Vishvakarma has defined three thousand types of houses. In case, the upper portions of the houses are somewhat lower, then nests for the pigeons should be made in order to complete the same.

## \|\| 1.130.38 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*ya ete kathitā vipra prāsādā viṃśatistvayā \|*  
*teṣāṃ sūryasya kaḥ kāryaḥ prāsādo bhāskarasya tu \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Samba said — O Brahmana, you have spoken about the methods of making twenty types of palaces, which one of these twenty designs would be praiseworthy?

## \|\| 1.130.39-40 \|\|

*sthānāni yāni coktāni prāsādasya dvijottama \|*  
*teṣāṃ tvayoktaṃ hi puraṃ vyayavadbhirnarairyutam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tasminpradeśe vai kāryaṃ bhānormandiramuttamam \|*  
*diśāṃ bhāge ca katame brūhi śeṣaṃ dvijottama \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. O best of the Brahmanas, you have mentioned about the places for the building of the palaces, you have already mentioned that the people who spend for religious purposes, should build the Sun temple, close to their cities. But O Brahmana, you tell me as to on which side should the temple be built?

## \|\| 1.130.41-42 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*puramadhyaṃ samāśritya kuryādāyatanaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*diśāṃ bhāge'tha vā pūrve pūrvadvārasamīpataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*bhūmiṃ parīkṣya pūrvaṃ tu kuryādāyatanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*iṣṭagandharasopetā nimnā2 bhūmiḥ praśasyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Narada said — The land in the middle or to the east gate should be examined because for the purpose of building a temple, the land with fragrance and with following features, has been said to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.130.43 \|\|

*śarkarātuṣakeśāsthikṣārāṅgāravivarjitā \|*  
*meghadundubhinirghoṣā sarvabījaprarohiṇī \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The land with husk, hair, bones, saltish and with that of coal is net to be used for the building of a temple. The place where the sound of the beating of drums or thundering of clouds is heard, the place where all types of seeds could sprout, such a land is fit for the building of a palace.

## \|\| 1.130.44 \|\|

*śuklā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā ca kathitā kṣitiḥ \|*  
*dvijarājanyavaṃśyānāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca yathākramam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Similarly, the resplendent, red, yellow and the black soil earth is said to be suitable for the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Madras, respectively.

## \|\| 1.130.45-47 \|\|

*parīkṣitāyāṃ tasyāṃ tu madhye tasyāḥ pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*upalipya caturhastaṃ caturasraṃ ca samantataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*hastamātramadhaḥ kṛtvā madhye tasyā daśāṅgulam \|*  
*gartamutkīrya tenaiva pāṃsunā pratipūrayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

*same samaguṇā jñeyā hīne hīnaguṇā bhavet \|*  
*vardhamāne tu vai pāṃsau bhavedvṛddhikarī kṣitiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Initially, after examining the land, the four hands square land in the middle of it should be plastered with the cowdung. Thereafter, a pit of a hand in length and ten fingers in depth, should be dug. After so doing, the same pit should be filled with the same earth. In case, the pit is filled completely with the dug up earth, then it would be of equal merit. In case the sand falls short, then the land is not considered to be appropriate. In case, some of the sand is left out after filling the pit, then the land would be productive.

## \|\| 1.130.48 \|\|

*nityaṃ sammukhamarkasya kadācitpaścimāmukham \|*  
*sthāpanīyaṃ gṛhaṃ samyakprāṅmukhasthānakalpanāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The entrance gate of the house should be to the east. In case, it could not be so arranged due to some reason, then it could face the west as well. But efforts should be made to keep the entrance door to the east.

## \|\| 1.130.49 \|\|

*bhavanāddakṣiṇe pārśve raveḥ snānagṛhaṃ bhavet \|*  
*agnihotra gṛhaṃ kāryaṃ raveruttarataḥ śubham \|*  
*udaṅmukhaṃ bhavecchambhormātṝṇāṃ gṛhameva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. At the right back of the Sun temple, there should be a bathroom, the homa kunda should be lodged to the north. The shrines of lord Shiva and mothers, should be towards the north.

## \|\| 1.130.50 \|\|

*brahmā paścimataḥ sthāpyo viṣṇuruttaratastathā \|*  
*nimbastu dakṣiṇe pārśve vāme rājñī prakīrtitā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Brahma should be lodged to the west of the image of Surya, while Vishnu should be placed to the north. Nimabastu should be lodged to the right of the Sungod, while Rajni should be placed to the left.

## \|\| 1.130.51 \|\|

*piṃgalo pakṣiṇe7 bhānorvāmato daṇḍanāyakaḥ \|*  
*śrīmahāśvetayoḥ sthānaṃ puratastvaṃśumālinaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Pingala should be to the right and Dandanayaka should be facing the Sungod with Mahashveta.

## \|\| 1.130.52-54 \|\|

*tataḥsthāpyāśvinoḥ sthānaṃ pūrvadevagṛhādvahiḥ \|*  
*dvitīyāyāṃ tu kakṣāyāṃ rājñāsrauṣau vyavasthitau \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tṛtīyāyāṃ tu kakṣāyāṃ sthitau kalmāṣapakṣiṇau \|*  
*jaṇḍakāmacarau1 sthāpyau dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśritau \|\| 53 \|\|*

*udīcyāṃ sthāpanīyastu kubero lokapūjitaḥ \|*  
*uttareṇa tatastasya revataḥ savināyakaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. Ashvinikumaras should be lodged outside the temple. In the other apartment, the king Srausa should be lodged. In the third apartment, Kalamasha and the bird should be there. In the southern side, there should be the root and worker should be on the north. Kubera should be lodged to the north. In the north, Raivata and Vinayaka should be placed.

## \|\| 1.130.55 \|\|

*yatra vā vidyate sthānaṃ dikṣu sarvā guhādayaḥ \|*  
*dve maṇḍale'rghyadānārthaṃ kārye savyāpasavyataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In case, there be any space in the directions, the Skanda should be placed there. Similarly, to the south and north, mandalas are made for the offering of the arghya.

## \|\| 1.130.56 \|\|

*dadyādudayavelāyāmarghaṃ sūryāya dakṣiṇe \|*  
*uttare maṇḍale dadyādarghyamastamane raveḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. At the time of sunrise, arghya (oblation) should be given to the Sun from the southern mandala. At the time of sunset, oblation should be offered from the north mandala.

## \|\| 1.130.57 \|\|

*cakrākṛtāṃ tathānyasmindevasya pratimāṃ raveḥ \|*  
*sthāpayedvidhivadvīra caturbhiḥ kalaśaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O valorous one, the image of Surya should be consecrated over a pedestal with four pitchers.

## \|\| 1.130.58 \|\|

*nānātūryaninādaiśca śaṅkhaśabdaiśca puṣkalaiḥ \|*  
*tṛtīye maṇḍale hyeva pūjanīyo divākaraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. It should be established with the sounding of the small drums and other musical instruments, besides the blowing of conches. The Sungod should again be worshipped in the third mandala.

## \|\| 1.130.59 \|\|

*caturasraṃ catuḥśṛṅgaṃ vyoma devagṛhāgrataḥ \|*  
*pratimāyāstu sūtreṇa kāryaṃ madhye'sya maṇḍalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the forefront of the temple, there should be four peaks as well as a square vyoma. In the centre of it, a mandala should be made with cotton thread.

## \|\| 1.130.60 \|\|

*diṇḍī sthāpyaḥ purastasmādādityābhimukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*yadetatkathitaṃ vyoma sarvadevamayaṃ mayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Dindi is to be placed in front of the image of the Sungod. Thus is the vyoma representing all the gods, which has already been described by me.

## \|\| 1.130.61 \|\|

*madhyāhne tasya dātavyamarghyamatra yadūttama \|*  
*atha vā maṇḍalaṃ cānyattṛtīyaṃ cakrasammitama5 \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O best of Yadus, the arghya should be offered to the Sungod here itself or otherwise this could be done in another circular mandala as well.

## \|\| 1.130.62 \|\|

*sthāpayitvā tu deveśaṃ dātavyo'rghaḥ supaṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*devasya purataḥ kāryaṃ vyomasthānaṃ samīpataḥ \|*  
*pustakavācanasthānamatha vā yatra rocate \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thus consecrating the Sungod, the learned people should offer arghya to him daily. Vyoma should be created close to the image of Surya. The place for reciting of the scriptures should also be earmarked close to the image of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.130.63 \|\|

*eṣa sthānavidhiḥ prokto devatānāṃ yathākramam \|*  
*gṛharājño'tha rudrastu dvāvetau bhāskarapriyau \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus, the method of the consecration of the place for temple has been defined by me, for the gods. The Sarvatobhadra and Griharaja types are the most favourite of the Sungod.

## Chapter 131. Testing of wood

## \|\| 1.131.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*atha te sampravakṣyāmi pratimāvidhivistaram \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva devānāmādityasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — Then I am relating to you the method of preparing the images of all the gods and more particularly of Surya. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.131.2-3 \|\|

*arcā1 saptavidhā proktā bhaktānāṃ śubhavṛddhaye \|*  
*kāñcanī rājatī tāmrī pārthivī śailajā smṛtā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vārkṣī cālekhyakā ceti mūtisthānāni sapta vai \|*  
*vārkṣīvidhānaṃ te vīra varṇayiṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Though for the increase of the welfare of the devotees, seven types of images made of gold, silver, copper, clay, stone and wood, besides the paintings have been prescribed, but I shall initially speak about the preparation of the wooden images.

## \|\| 1.131.4 \|\|

*kartranukūle divase saṃvatsaraviśodhite \|*  
*śubhairnimittaiḥ śakunaiḥ prasthānaiśca vanaṃ viśet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On a favourable day and time as per astrology and keeping in view the auspicious time, one should start from his home.

## \|\| 1.131.5-9 \|\|

*kṣīriṇo varjitāḥ sarve durbalāste svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*catuṣpatheṣu na grāhyā ye ca putrakavṛkṣakāḥ2 \|\| 5 \|\|*

*devatāyatanasthā ye tathā valmīkasambhavā \|*  
*utkīrṇā devatā yeṣu caityavṛkṣāśca ye smṛtāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śmaśānabhūmijā ye ca pakṣiṇāṃ nilayāśca ye \|*  
*sakoṭarāśca ye vṛkṣāḥ śuṣkāgrā ye ca pādapāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śastreṇa nihatā ye ca kuñjarāśāstathā kṛtāḥ \|*  
*sāmādyāḥ sarujo'dhaśca vyādhinaśca tathaiva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*akāle puṣpitā ye ca kāle te ca vivarjitāḥ \|*  
*śīrṇaparṇāśca taravo rakṣodhvāṃkṣaniṣevitāḥ \|*  
*ekaśākhātiśākhāśca triśākhāśca tathādhamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Reaching the forest, one should discard the selection of a tree for making an image of the deity from which the milk like fruit oozes, then by nature, the tree growing at a crossing, young tree, the tree growing in a temple, the tree infested with white ants, the tree near the abode of gods, Chaitya tree, the tree of the cremation ground, the one with the nests of the birds, hollow tree, the tree the top of which has dried up or the one which has been cut off with a weapon, the tree which is the fodder of the elephants, the tree with ailments or the one which spreads downwards, the tree which blossoms initially, the trees which do not flower during the season, the trees with shattered leaves, the trees which serve as the dwelling places for the demons as well as crows, and the trees having a single or three branches.

## \|\| 1.131.10-11 \|\|

*madhūko devadāruśca vṛkṣarājaśca candanaḥ \|*  
*bilvaścāmrātakaścaiva khadirothāñjanastathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nimbaḥ śrīparṇavṛkṣaśca panasaḥ saralo'rjjunaḥ \|*  
*raktacandanaparyantāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ syuḥ pratimādrumāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Similarly, the trees like Bassia latifolia, pine or Chedara, Vriksharaja, sandal wood tree, wood apple, myrobalan, catechu, nima tree, Shri parna, jack tree, Arjuna and red sandal wood tree should be patronised for the making of an image, because these trees have been said to be the best for the purpose.

## \|\| 1.131.12 \|\|

*varṇānāmānupūrvyeṇa dvau dvau vṛkṣau prakīrtitau \|*  
*nimbādyāḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ vṛkṣā sādhāraṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The trees like Bassia latifolia are the trees, two of which have been prescribed for each one of the two varnas as the best. Similarly, nima and other trees are said to be the ordinary ones for each one of the four varnas.

## \|\| 1.131.13 \|\|

*kathyamānānviśeṣeṇa śṛṇu vīra tathāparān \|*  
*suradāruḥ śamī caiva madhūkaścandanastathā \|*  
*ete vai taravastāta brāhmaṇānāṃ śubhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O valorous one, some other trees are also being mentioned by me. You listen. The pine trees, Shami, Bassia latifolia, sandal wood are the trees which are best for the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.131.14 \|\|

*kṣatrasya ca tathāriṣṭaḥ khadirastindukastathā \|*  
*aśvatthaśca tathā sāmba drumaḥ karakataḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Samba, similarly, the nima, pippala and myrobalan trees are auspicious for the Kshatriyas.

## \|\| 1.131.15 \|\|

*vaiśyānāṃ tadvadeva syuḥ khadiraścandanastathā \|*  
*puṇyāśca taravaścaite śubhadāstu tathaiva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the same way, catechu, sandal wood, trees are beneficial for the Vaishyas.

## \|\| 1.131.16 \|\|

*kesaraḥ sarjakaścāmraḥ śālavṛkṣastathetaraḥ \|*  
*ete vai taravaḥ puṇyāḥ śūdrāṇāṃ śubhadāyakāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The saffron, sarvaka mango and Sala trees are good for the Shudras.

## \|\| 1.131.17 \|\|

*liṅgaṃ ca pratimāṃ caivamavasthāpya yathāvidhi \|*  
*vṛkṣaṃ cābhimataṃ gatvā pūjayedbalipuṣpakaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By making the wooden image, it should be consecrated appropriately. Going close to the desired tree, one should initially worship with offerings etc.

## \|\| 1.131.18-19 \|\|

*śucau deśe vivikte ca keśāṃgāravivarjite \|*  
*prāgudaksūcake deśe lokakaṣṭavivarjite \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vistīrṇaskandhaviṭapaḥ ṣatravānṛjuvṛddhigaḥ \|*  
*ātaṅkahīno vivaśaḥ sattvakparṇaḥ śubhastathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The tree should be such which should be auspicious and stand in a plain ground. There should be no coal in it nor should there be thorns. It should have slopes on the north and the east. The people should not be feeling uncomfortable there. It should have vast branches, full of leaves. It should be standing erect and quite high. There should be no terror around. Its skin and leaves should be quite beautiful. Such trees are praiseworthy for making an image.

## \|\| 1.131.20-21 \|\|

*svenaiva patitā ye ca hastibhiḥ pātitāstathā \|*  
*śuklāśca vahnidagdhāśca pakṣibhiścāpi varjitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*taravo varjanīyāśca grahītavyāḥ śubhā drumāḥ \|*  
*snigdharūpāḥ saparṇāśra sapuṣpāḥ saphalāstathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Similarly, the tree which has fallen by itself or has been uprooted by the wind, which is dry, burnt out and without the nests of the birds, should be discarded. Thereafter, an auspicious tree should be selected. The trees which are soft, slippery with enough of leaves, flowers and fruits, are considered to be auspicious.

## \|\| 1.131.22-24 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu grahaṇaṃ cāṣṭamāseṣu kārttikādiṣu \|*  
*bhūtvā śubhadine caiva sopavāso'dhivāsayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

*samantādupalipyātha tasyādhastādvasundharām \|*  
*gāyatryā paripūtena paritaḥ prokṣya vāriṇā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śukle ca paridhūte ca paridhāya ca1 vāsasī \|*  
*pūjayedgandhamālyaiśca sadhūpabalikarmabhiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Thus, these trees are to be patronised for eight months from the month of Karttika. On an auspicious day, one should observe fast, the land around the tree should be plastered with cowdung. The water should be sipped reciting the Gayatri mantra. He should then wear new white clothes. Then the tree should be worshipped offering the fragrance flower garland, incense and other presents.

## \|\| 1.131.25-26 \|\|

*tataḥ kuśaiḥ paristīrṇe hutvāgnau tasya cāntike \|*  
*devadārusamidbhiśca mantreṇānena tattvavit \|\| 25 \|\|*

*oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvariti tato vṛkṣaṃ ca pūjayet \|*  
*oṃ prajāpataye satyasadāya nityaṃ śreṣṭhantarātmantsacarācarātman \|*  
*sānnidhyamasminkuru deva vṛkṣe sūryāvṛtaṃ maṇḍalamāviśeśca namaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Kusha grass should then be spread all round. Then, he should light the pine wood. He should perform homa reciting Gayatri mantra, while concluding the puja. Then with his folded hands, he should say — “For the abode of Prajapati, you are the best inner soul besides being the mobile and immobile soul. Salutation to you. O lord, you enter in this tree with the mandala of Surya.”

## \|\| 1.131.27 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sampūjayityā tu vākyaistaṃ parisāntvayan \|*  
*vṛkṣalokasya śāntyarthaṃ gaccha devālayaṃ śubham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Narada said — Thus worshipping the tree, one should speak peaceful words for the same, saying — “O tree, you move (in part) to the temple of the god for bestowing peace to the people.

## \|\| 1.131.28 \|\|

*deva tvaṃ sthāsyase tatra cchedadāhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*kāle dhūpapradānena sapuṣpairbalikarmabhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O Deva, you will not feel hurt with the strike of this weapon. To the contrary, the people will adore you with incense, offerings flowers etc.

## \|\| 1.131.29-32 \|\|

*lokāstvāṃ pūjayiṣyanti tato yāsyasi nirvṛtim \|*  
*vṛkṣamūle kuṭhāraṃ tu dhūpamālyaiḥ prapūjya ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pūrvatastu śiraḥ kṛtvā sthāpanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*paramānnamodakaudanapalapūpikādibhirbhakṣyaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*madyaiḥ kusumairdhūpairgandhaiśca taruṃ samabhyarcya \|*  
*surapitṛpiśācarākṣasabhujaṅgasuragaṇavināyakādyānām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kṛtvā pūjāṃ rātrau vṛkṣaṃ saṃspṛśya ca brūyāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. With this, you will achieve eternal peace. Thereafter, the axe should be placed at the root of the tree and worship it with incense and flower garlands. Then turning his face to the east, he should place it there itself. Again, offering excellent food, sweet balls, cooked rice, fried cakes and other eatables besides the beverages for the worship the gods, pitris, Pishachas, Rakshasas, serpents, Devas, Vinayakas and others, and then touching the tree during the night, he should utter.

## \|\| 1.131.33-34 \|\|

*arcāsu devadeva tvaṃ devaiśca parikalpitaḥ \|*  
*namaste vṛkṣa pūjeyaṃ vidhivatparigṛhyatām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yānīha bhūtāni vasanti tāni baliṃ gṛhītvā vidhivatprayuktam \|*  
*anyatra vāsaṃ parikalpayantu kṣamantu te cādya namo'stu tebhyaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. O god of gods! The gods have created you for adoration. Therefore, salutation to you. O tree! You please accept the puja performed by me appropriately. All the creatures dwelling in this tree should shift their abodes somewhere else. They should all forgive me. I offer my salutation to them.”

## \|\| 1.131.35 \|\|

*prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ punaḥ sampūjya taṃ nagam \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyastato dattvā bhojakebhyaśca dakṣiṇām \|*  
*chindyādvanaspatīṃstajjñaistai kṛtasvastivācanaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In the early morning, he should again worship the tree and also offer food to the Brahmanas as well as the Bhojakas, besides the dakshina. Again, the welfare mantras should be recited. Thereafter, the cutting of the tree should be entrusted to an expert carpenter.

## \|\| 1.131.36 \|\|

*pūrvasyāṃ diśi pāto'sya aiśānyāṃ cāpi yo bhavet \|*  
*athavā uttarasyāṃ tu tathā chindyāttu1 nānyathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The tree should be made to fall towards the north or the north-east side. The cutting of the tree should be made accordingly.

## \|\| 1.131.37 \|\|

*aindryaiśānyorudīcyāṃ caḥ pātastisṛṣu śasyate \|*  
*nairṛtyāgneyayāmyāsu dikṣu pāto na śobhanaḥ \|*  
*vāyavyāṃ caiva vāruṇyāṃ tasya pātastu madhyamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Because, the fall of the tree to the north, east, or north-east is said to be praiseworthy. Similarly, its fall towards south-west, southeast and the southern side is not considered to be auspicious. Its fall on north-west or west side is of medium type.

## \|\| 1.131.38 \|\|

*yasya bāhyasthitā śākhā dikṣu naṣṭā catasṛṣu \|*  
*vāstupūrvaṃ tataḥ sthitvā tataḥ paścādavasthitā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The branches of a tree, which having spread on all sides of the house and the tree which had grown already before the building of the house, has to be discarded for the purpose of making of an image.

## \|\| 1.131.39-40 \|\|

*avilagnamaśabdaṃ tu patanaṃ tu praśasyate \|*  
*utpadyeddvidalaṃ yasya drāvaśca madhuro bhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sarpistailaṃ kṣaredyasya pādapaṃ taṃ vivarjavet \|*  
*śubhadaṃ yaduśārdūla śṛṇu tvaṃ kathaye śuci \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The falling of a tree having no link or contact is taken to be quite beneficial. A tree which with it mere fall, break into two parts or releases juice like the honey, oil or ghi, such a tree is not considered to be fit for making an image. I am now going to speak about the auspicious and beneficial trees, you listen.

## \|\| 1.131.41-42 \|\|

*vṛkṣaṃ prabhāte salilairniṣiktaṃ pūrvottarasyāṃ diśi sannikṛtya \|*  
*madhvājyadigdhena kuṭhārakeṇa pradakṣiṇāṃ śoṣamabhiprahaṇyāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pūrvottare'pyuttaradigvibhāge pāte yadā vṛddhikarastadā syāt \|*  
*āgneyakoṇakramaśo'gnidāha ugrograrogāḥ sudhanakṣayaśca \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. In the early morning of the next day, water should be sprinkled over the tree. The honey and ghi should then be applied over it. Then holding the axe, he should go round the tree form the north-east side and he should strike the tree. It is because in case the tree falls to the north or the north-east direction, then it is taken to be beneficial. In case it falls to the south or south-west directions, then it causes violence or makes one suffer from a violent disease or results in loss of huge riches.

## \|\| 1.131.43 \|\|

*gāruḍe diśi pāṣāṇaṃ kapoto gṛhagodhikā \|*
