*sitavarṇaṃ jalaṃ jñeyamaṅguṣṭhābhaṃ bhavetkṛmiḥ \|*  
*doṣairetairvinirmuktaṃ mudā kālaṃ samuddharet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When the tree falls towards Garuda direction and stones, pigeon or lizard are found, or the white water oozes from it, then the insects as big as the thumb would emerge from it. Therefore, it is considered to be unblemished one and would be quite suitable for the making of an image. It should be therefore, accepted with delight.

## Chapter 132. Iconography of the Sun Image

## \|\| 1.132.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*hanta te sarvadevānāṃ pratimālakṣaṇaṃ param \|*  
*vacmi te yaduśārdūla ādityasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — O lion of the race, I shall now speak out the iconographical features of the Surya image. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.132.2 \|\|

*ekahastā dvihastā vā trihastā vā pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*tathā sārddhatrihastā ca savituḥ pratimā śubhā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The image of Surya should be of the height of one, two, three or three and a half cubits, which is considered to be quite auspicious.

## \|\| 1.132.3 \|\|

*prasādāddvārato vāpi pramāṇaṃ ca prakalpitam \|*  
*tadvatprayāṇaṃ kartavyaṃ satataṃ śubhamicchatā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The devotee should keep in mind the size of the Surya image in relation to the size of the temple as well as the temple doors.

## \|\| 1.132.4-5 \|\|

*ekahastā bhavetsaumyā dvihastā dhanadhānyadā \|*  
*trihastā pratimā bhānoḥ sarvakāmapradā smṛtā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sārdhatrihastā pratimā subhikṣakṣemakāriṇī \|*  
*agre madhye ca mūle ca pratimā sarvataḥ samā \|*  
*gāndharvī sā tu vijñeyā dhanadhānyāvahā smṛtā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Because the image of a single cubit height is geode, of two cubits bestows riches. The Surya image with the height of three cubits fulfills all the desires. The image of three and a half cubit height is well protected and bestows welfare. The image which is of the same dimensions in front, middle, base and in all the sides, is known as Gandharvi, which increases cereals as well as the riches.

## \|\| 1.132.6 \|\|

*devāgārasya yaddvāraṃ tasmādaṣṭāṃśamudyatā \|*  
*vibhāgaiḥ piṇḍikāḥ kāryā dvau bhāgau pratimā bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The image should be made of one eighth size of the door of the temple. The pedestal should be of the size of one third of it. The image should be made of the height of two parts.

## \|\| 1.132.7 \|\|

*aṅgulaiśca tathā mūrtiścaturaśītisaṃmitaiḥ \|*  
*vistārāyāmataḥ kāryā vadanaṃ dvādaśāṅgulam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In other words, the image should be of the height of eighty four angulas or fingers. The size of the face is of twelve angulas in length.

## \|\| 1.132.8-9 \|\|

*mukhāttribhāgaiścibukaṃ lalāṭaṃ nāsikā tathā \|*  
*karṇau nāsikayā tulyau pādau cāniyatau tayoḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nayane dvyaṃgule syātāṃ tribhāgā tārakā bhaveta \|*  
*tṛtīyatārakābhāgātkuryāddṛṣṭiṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The chin should be one third of the size of the face. The rest should cover the nose and the forehead. Similarly, both the ears should be as big as the nose. The eyes should be of two angulas, while the feet remain unspecified The eye ball should be one third of the size of the eye. A learned person should create the vision in one third part of the same.

## \|\| 1.132.10 \|\|

*lalāṭamastakotsedhaṃ kuryāttatsamameva ca \|*  
*pariṇāhastu śiraso bhaveddvāviṃśadaṅgulaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Though the height of the head and the forehead is similar, but the head should be of twenty angulas.

## \|\| 1.132.11 \|\|

*tulyā nāsikayā grīvā mukhena hadayāṃtaram \|*  
*mukhamātrā bhavennābhistato meḍhramanantaram \|*  
*mukhavistāraṇamurastato'rddhaṃ tu kaṭiḥ smṛtā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The neck is same as nostrils and the part of heart is made like the face. The navel resembles the face, and thereafter there is the penis. The expansion of face is like the chest and half of it is the waist.

## \|\| 1.132.12 \|\|

*bāhū pravāhatulyau tu ūrū jaṅghe ca tatsame \|*  
*gulphādhastāttu pādaḥ syāducchritaścaturaṅgulaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In this way, the long arms fall upto the thighs. Below the ankles upto four angulas, the feet are formed.

## \|\| 1.132.13 \|\|

*ṣaḍaṅgulasuvistārastasyāṅguṣṭhāṅgulatrayam \|*  
*pradeśinī ca tattulyā hīnā śeṣā nakhairyutāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The feet are six angulas in width. The big toes of the feet are of three angulas. The forefinger (toe) is of the size of the big toe. The rash of the toes are smaller and are studded with nails.

## \|\| 1.132.14 \|\|

*caturdaśāṅgulaḥ pāda āyāmātparikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyuktā pratimārcyā bhavetsadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The feet have the length of fourteen angulas. The images with these features is always adorable.

## \|\| 1.132.15 \|\|

*aṃsau harestathaivorū lalāṭaṃ ca sanāsikam \|*  
*niyate nayane gaṇḍau mūrteḥ kuryātsamunnate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The shoulders, the thighs, nose, eyes and temples, and the forehead of the images are always shown raised.

## \|\| 1.132.16 \|\|

*viśāladhavalāvāmapakṣmalāyatalocane \|*  
*sasmitānanapadmasya cārubimbādharastathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The image should have broad eyes looking beautiful. The face should have a serene smile resembling the blossomed lotus flower. The lips should be like the red gourd.

## \|\| 1.132.17 \|\|

*ratnaprodbhāsimukuṭakaṭakāṅgadahāravān \|*  
*avyaṅgapadamadhyādisamāyogo'pi śobhitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The image should be made to wear the shining crowns studded with gems, besides bracelets, garlands, and other ornaments. The image should be so built that the limbs of the middle of the body are beautiful, well built and their beauty is visible.

## \|\| 1.132.18-19 \|\|

*suprabho maṇḍalaścārurvicitramaṇikuṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*karābhyāṃ kāñcanīṃ mālāṃ prodvahansasaroruhām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*evaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyuktāṃ kārayedīhitapradām \|*  
*prajābhyaśca sadā bhānuḥ śivārogyābhayapradaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Its mandala should be resplendent. The ears should be adorned with the ear-rings studded with gems. There should be a garland of gold in hand and should resemble the lotus flowers. The Sungod in this form bestows welfare to the people.

## \|\| 1.132.20-22 \|\|

*alpāṅgāyāṃ nṛpabhayaṃ hīnāṅgāyāmakalpatā \|*  
*khātodaryāṃ ca kṣutpīḍā kṛśāyāṃ tu daridratā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sakṣatāyāṃ bhayaṃ śastrātsphuṭitā mṛtyukāriṇī \|*  
*dakṣiṇāvanatāyāṃ tu śaśvadāyuḥ kṣayo bhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*uttarāvanatāyāṃ tu viyogo bhavati dhruvam \|*  
*nālokyā nāpyanālokyā rakṣyāmūrtiḥ praśasyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. In case, the limbs of the image are shorter (than usual), the king has to face danger. In case, the image is short of a limb, it attracts disease; when the belly is protruding, it makes the people to suffer from hunger; when it is thin, it makes the people to face poverty. In case a limb of the image is broken, there would be danger from arms or weapons, while the broken image causes death. In case, the image is tilted to the right (or south), it causes the reduction of age, and in case it is bent towards the north, it causes separation. In case, the image is over illuminated or in short of light, it is not said to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.132.23 \|\|

*tasmādbhāskarabhaktena lokadvayahitaiṣiṇā \|*  
*tanmūrteścādaraḥ kāryastadadhīnāstu sampadaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Therefore, the medium type of image is taken to be protective and praiseworthy. Therefore, for the welfare of the people, the devotees should extend more respect to the Surya image, because he is the controller of all the pleasures, comforts and riches.

## \|\| 1.132.24 \|\|

*śirorugaṇḍavadanaiḥ sarvāṅgāvayavaistathā \|*  
*evaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā pratimā bhavate śubhā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The head, thighs, temples, face and all the limbs (should be made well proportioned) with auspicious symptoms. Such an image will bestow welfare on all.

## \|\| 1.132.25 \|\|

*nāsālalāṭajaṅghorudaṇḍavakṣobhiranvitā \|*  
*kuryādādityaveṣaṃ tu gūḍhapādodaraṃ tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The image of the Sungod should be so made that his nose, forehead, the thighs, knees and the chest should be well made. The feet and belly of the image should remain covered.

## \|\| 1.132.26 \|\|

*kamalodarakāntinibhaḥ kañcukaguptaḥ prasannamukhaḥ \|*  
*raktotpalaprabhāmaṇḍalaśca kartuḥ śubhaṃ karotyarkaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Because the belly has the shine of the lotus flowers, the image should have smiling face, should be wearing a bodice, the mandala should be resembling the red lotus flowers. Such an image is said to be quite praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.132.27-28 \|\|

*kuṇḍalabhūṣitavadanaḥ pralambahāro'pi gṛhavṛttaḥ \|*  
*nṛpatibhayaṃ vyaṅgāyāṃ hīnāṅgāyāmakalpanā kartuḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*khātodaryāṃ kṣudbhayamarthavināśaḥ kṛśāṅgāyām \|*  
*maraṇaṃ tu sakṣatāyāṃ śastranipātena nirdiśetkartuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The image should be lodged in a circular temple, is adorned with the earrings and a long garland of flowers, because in case this is not well prepared, then there is danger for the king; in case it has defect in a limb, there spreads the disease; and in case the image has a deep pit like belly, there spreads the hunger and uneasiness and thinness in body.

## \|\| 1.132.29 \|\|

*vāmonnatā tu patnīṃ dakṣiṇāvanatā hinastyāyuḥ \|*  
*andhatvamūrddhvadṛṣṭiḥ karoti cintāmadhomukhī dṛṣṭiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In case, the left part is raised, one has to face separation from the wife. In case, the right side is raised, the age declines. In case, the image has the vision upwards, one becomes blind and in case, the look of the image is cast downwards, the maker of the image always remains worried.

## \|\| 1.132.30 \|\|

*sarvapratimāsvevaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ bhāskareṇoktam \|*  
*brahmā kamaṇḍalukaraścaturmukhaḥ paṅkajasthaśca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The good and evil effects of the images have been revealed by the Sungod himself. The image of four-faced Brahma, lodged over the lotus flowers, should also be made like this.

## \|\| 1.132.31 \|\|

*skandaḥ kumārarūpaḥ śaktidharo barhiketuśca \|*  
*śuklaścaturviṣāṇo dvipo mahendrasya vajrapāṇitvam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The image of Skanda should have the child like face, holding a shakti. The peacock should serve as his vehicle, besides a flag should also be held by the god. Similarly, the image of Indra should be of white complexion, holding a vajra and seated over a white elephant with four trunks.

## \|\| 1.132.32 \|\|

*tiryagūrdhvalalāṭasaṃsthaṃ tṛtīyamapi locanaṃ cihnam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In the forehead of lord Shiva, a horizontal third eye should be shown, which is essential.

## Chapter 133. Description of Universe Form

## \|\| 1.133.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*tato'dhivāsanaṃ kuryādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*aiśānyāṃ diśi vai kuryādadhivāsanamaṇḍapam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — Thereafter, the Adhivasa ceremony is performed appropriately. A mandala or a canopy should be arranged towards the north-west side.

## \|\| 1.133.2 \|\|

*catustoraṇasampannaṃ sarvābharaṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*diśāsu vidiśāsveva patākābhistu bhūṣitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It should be decorated with four torana gates and should be decorated with all the ornaments. The flags should be placed in all the directions.

## \|\| 1.133.3-5 \|\|

*āgneyyāṃ diśi raktāḥ syuḥ kṛṣṇāḥ syuryāmyanairṛte \|*  
*śvetā diśyaparasyāṃ tu vāyavyāmeva pāṇḍurā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*citrā cottara pārnye tu pītā pūrvottare tathā \|*  
*śriyamāyurjayaṃ caiva balaṃ yaśo yadūttama \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dadāti sā vīra kṛtā sampadardhe na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*hitāya sarvalokānāṃ mṛṇmayī pratimā bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. The flags of red colour should be hang on the north-east side; in the south and south-west sides, the flags should be of black colour; in the west side, they should be white. In the north-east side, the flags should be of yellow colour. The flags in the northern side should be of different colours and in the north-east side, they should be of yellow colour. O messenger of Yama, O valorous one, with the desire to achieve Lakshmi or riches, when the image is made, it bestows long life, japam strength and fame. There is no doubt about it. Therefore, for the welfare of all the people, an image should be made in clay as well.

## \|\| 1.133.6-8 \|\|

*subhikṣakṣemadā nityaṃ sarvā maṇimayīkṛtā \|*  
*gāṅgeyā1 puṣṭidā raupyā syādvai kīrtipravartinī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prajāvṛddhiṃ tāmramayīṃ kuryānnityamasaṃśayaḥ \|*  
*bhūmerlābhaṃ tu vipulaṃ kuryādaśmamayī sadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pradhānapuruṣaṃ hanti trapulohamayī sadā \|*  
*sarvadevamayasyaivamarcā kuryātprayatnataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The image which is thus made, bestows increase in fortunes; the image made in silver bestows fame; the one made in copper increase the progeny. The image made of stone bestows gain in land; while the image made of glass and iron causes the death of the prominent person. Therefore, the image of the Sungod should be worshipped making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.133.9 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*sarvadevamayatvaṃ hi brūhi me bhāskarasya tu \|*  
*sarvadevamayo hyeṣa kathaṃ nārada kathyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Samba said — O Narada, Bhaskara represents all the gods, you tell me also as to how the Sungod represents all the gods?

## \|\| 1.133.10 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*sādhu sāmba mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*budhasomau smṛtau netre lalāṭe ceśvaraḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Narada said — O long armed one, you listen to my excellent words. The Sun has two eyes viz., the Moon and Mercury. Shiva is lodged in the forehead.

## \|\| 1.133.11-13 \|\|

*surajyeṣṭhaḥ śirastasya kapāle'sya bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*ekādaśe tathā rudrāḥ kaṇṭhamasya2 samāśritāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nakṣatrāṇi grahāścaiva daśaneṣu samāśritāḥ \|*  
*dharmādharmau ca devasya oṣṭhasampuṭake sthitau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarvaśāstramayī devī jihvāyāṃ ca sarasvatī \|*  
*diśaśca vidiśaścaiva sarvāḥ śrotreṣu saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Similarly, Brahma is lodged in the head, Brihaspati or Jupiter in the skull, eleven Rudras in the throat The planets and constellations are lodged in the teeth, dharma and adharma are lodged in the lips. Sarasvati, who is well-versed in the scriptures, is lodged over the tongue. All the decoration are lodged in the ears.

## \|\| 1.133.14 \|\|

*brahmendrau tāludeśe tu sthitau devaiśca pūjitau \|*  
*ādityā dvādaśa vibhobhrurvormadhye samāśritāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the palate region, both Indra and Brahma are lodged. In the middle of the eyebrows, the twelve Adityas are lodged.

## \|\| 1.133.15-17 \|\|

*ṛṣayo romakūpeṣu samudrā jaṭhare sthitāḥ \|*  
*yakṣakinnaragandharvāḥ piśācā dānavāstathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rākṣasāśca gaṇāḥ sarve hṛdaye syuḥ sthitāḥ raveḥ \|*  
*nadyo bāhugatāścaiva nagāḥ kakṣāntare sthitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭhamadhye sthito meruḥ stanayorantare kujaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro dharmarājaḥ sthito vai nābhimaṇḍale \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The Rishis dwell in the hair-pits, while Yakshas are lodged in the heart, in addition of Kinnaras, Pishachas, Danavas and all the Rakshasas. The rivers dwell in the arms, the mountains in the armpits, Meru in the middle of the back, Mars in the middle of the chest, while Dharmaraja in the navel.

## \|\| 1.133.18 \|\|

*kaṭideśe pṛthivyādyā liṅge sṛṣṭiḥ samāśritā \|*  
*jānunī cāśvinīdevāvūrū tasyācalā smṛtāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The earth, creation in linga and Ashvini — kumaras are lodged in knees and the mountains are lodged in the thighs.

## \|\| 1.133.19 \|\|

*sapta pātālalokāstu nakhamadhye samāśritāḥ \|*  
*sasāgaravanā pṛthvī pādamadhye'sya vartate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Similarly, Patala and the seven lokas are lodged in the nails. The earth with mountains and the oceans lives in the middle of the feet.

## \|\| 1.133.20 \|\|

*devaḥ kālāgnirudro yo dantānteṣu samāśritaḥ \|*  
*sarvadevamayo bhānuḥ sarvadevātmakastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At the roots of the teeth, Kalagni Rudra remains present. In this way, the Sungod is said to be the representation of all the gods.

## \|\| 1.133.21 \|\|

*vyaṃgeṣu vāyavaścaiva lokālokaṃ carācaram \|*  
*vyāptaṃ karmaśarīreṇa vāyunā tasya vai vibhoḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Like the wind which remains present in the mobiles, immobiles, the visible as well as the things in darkness, similarly, the Sungod is also present in all the lokas with his active body.

## \|\| 1.133.22 \|\|

*sa eṣa bhagavānarko bhūtānugrahaṇe sthitaḥ \|*  
*etatte paramaṃ jñānametatte paramaṃ padam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thus, the Sungod, in order to shower his grace on the creatures, always remains active. This is the great source of information for you.

## \|\| 1.133.23 \|\|

*tasya sthānavibhāgena pratimāsthāpanaṃ yathā \|*  
*tatte sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathoktaṃ brahmaṇā purā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The way the image of Surya is consecrated, I shall speak out to you in the same way, as Brahma had narrated the same in earlier times.

## Chapter 134. Method of making Mandala

## \|\| 1.134.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*pratipacya dvitīyā ca caturthī pañcamī tathā \|*  
*daśamī trayodaśī caiva paurṇamāsī ca kīrtitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — The moon days like Dvitiya, Tritiya, Chaturthi, Dashami, Trayodashi and the full moon day are said to be auspicious for the consecration of the images.

## \|\| 1.134.2 \|\|

*somo bṛhaspatiścaiva śukraścaiva budhastathā \|*  
*ete saumyā grahāḥ proktāḥ pratiṣṭhāyajñakarmaṇi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Monday, Thursday, Friday, besides Wednesday are believed to be quite auspicious for the performing of the Pratishtha yajna.

## \|\| 1.134.3 \|\|

*triṣūttarāsu revatyāmaśvinyāṃ brāhmabhe tathā \|*  
*punarvasvostathā haste vāsave1 śravaṇe'thavā \|*  
*bharaṇyāṃ caiva nakṣatre bhānoḥ1 sthāpanamuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Similarly, Uttara, Revati, Ashvini, Rohini, Punarvasu, Hasta, Pushya, Shravana and Bharani constellations are believed to be quite auspicious for the consecration of the Surya images.

## \|\| 1.134.4-5 \|\|

*śodhayitvā tu vai bhūmiṃ tuṣakeśavivarjitām \|*  
*vālukāṅgārapāṣāṇāsthivihīnāṃ viśodhya tu \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caturhastasamāyuktā vedī vistarato raveḥ2 \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The land which has no husk, hair, sand, coal, stones and bones should be selected, and square pedestal should be made there.

## \|\| 1.134.6 \|\|

*maṇḍapastu pramāṇena daśahastaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*maṇḍalaṃ vṛkṣaśākhābhiḥ kārayedvidhipūrvakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The size of the mandala should be of ten cubits, in which a mandala of tree branches should be made.

## \|\| 1.134.7 \|\|

*nadīsaṅgamatīrotthāṃ mṛttikāṃ ca samānayet \|*  
*upalipya tato bhūmiṃ kārayetkuṇḍamuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The earth from the confluence of the rivers should be brought and the land should be plastered with the cowdung. Then, a fire altar should be made therein.

## \|\| 1.134.8-9 \|\|

*caturasraṃ śriyā yuktaṃ pūrvaṃ kuṇḍaṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*dakṣiṇe cārdhacandraṃ syādvāruṇyāṃ diśi vartulam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*padmākāraṃ tu vai kuryāduttare4 ca vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*toraṇāni tataḥ kuryātpañcahastāni suvrata \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. It should be square in the east. The beautiful altar should be made. In the southern direction, it should be of the type of half moon. It should be circular in the west, while in the north the altar should be of the type of a lotus. O Suvrata, the arch should be of five cubit height in the mandala.

## \|\| 1.134.10 \|\|

*nyagrodhodumbarau caiva bilvapālāśameva ca \|*  
*aśvatthaśca śamī caiva candanaśceti kīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The branches of the trees like banyan, holy fig tree, Sami and sandal wood are quite praiseworthy for the making of an arch.

## \|\| 1.134.11 \|\|

*śuklavastrasamāyuktaścitrapaṭṭasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*japamālānvitaḥ kuryāttoraṇāni vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The torana decorated with pieces of cloths and garlands, should be made by the Brahmas.

## \|\| 1.134.12-13 \|\|

*agnimīḷeti mantreṇa yajedvai pūrvatoraṇam \|*  
*iṣetvorjeti mantreṇa yajeddakṣiṇatoraṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*agna āyāhīti mantreṇa paścimaṃ tu samarcayet \|*  
*śaṃ no devīti mantreṇa yajeduttaratoraṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. The arch on the east should be worshipped uttering the word — Agnimile. Then, uttering the mantra Ishetvorjeti, the arch on the south should be worshipped. Then uttering the mantra Agna ayahi, the western arch should be worshipped. Then uttering the mantra Shamnodevi, the arch to the north should be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.134.14-15 \|\|

*kalaśāṃstu samādāya hemagarbhasamanvitān \|*  
*śvetacandanapaṅkena kaṇṭhasvastikabhūṣaṇān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yavaśāliśarāvānnavastrālaṅkāravigrahān \|*  
*ājighreti ca mantreṇa kalaśāṃstu niveśayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The necks of the pitchers which are kept in the tor and should be painted with white sandal paste and decorated with the Svastika mark, in the cups filled with barley and rice and decorated with clothes and ornaments. These cups should be consecrated uttering the mantra Ajighreti...

## \|\| 1.134.16-19 \|\|

*dukūlaścitrapaṭṭaiśca veṣṭayetstambhamālikām \|*  
*dhvajādarśapatākābhiścāmaraistu vitānakaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śaṅkhaghaṇṭāninādaiśca geyamaṅgalavācanaiḥ \|*  
*tūryabherīninādaiśca vedadhvanisamanvitaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*puṇyaiśca jayaśabdaiśca kārayeta mahotsavam \|*  
*patākābhirvicitrābhiḥ pūjāmālyopaśobhitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vicitrasragvitānāḍhyaṃ prakīrṇakusumāṅkuram \|*  
*tanmadhye tu kuśāstīrṇe devārcāṃ sthāpayed budhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. Then again, using the clothes of different colours, the pillars of the mandapa should be decorated. The mandapa should then again be decorated with flags, mirrors, banners, flywhisks. The conches and bells should be sounded; the trumpets and small drums, should be played upon, besides the other musical instruments. The sounds of victory should be raised with the reciting of the Vedic hymns creating huge sound. Thus, having been decorated with the surprising types of banners, the garlands of vast canopy should be decorated. The kusha grass should be spread to serve as a bed over which the flowers should be spread. Thereafter, the image should be consecrated by the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.134.20-27 \|\|

*patākāṃ pītavarṇāṃ tu pūrve śakrāya dāpayet \|*  
*āgneyyāṃ raktavarṇābhāṃ12 yamāśāyāṃ yamopamān \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nīlāñjanasamaprakhyāṃ nairṛtyāṃ ca pradāpayet \|*  
*vāruṇyāṃ sitavarṇāṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ vāyavyagocare \|\| 21 \|\|*

*haritāṃ yakṣarājāya aiśānyāṃ sarvavarṇikām \|*  
*śvetaraktakacūrṇena padmamālekhayettataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vaidyā vedīti mantreṇa vedyā ālabhanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*pūrvāgrānuttarāgrāṃśca kuśānāstīrya yatnataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yogeyogeti mantreṇa kuśaścāstaraṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śayyā tatraiva kartavyā divyāstaraṇasaṃyutā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gaḍuke dve vicitre tu tanmadhye sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*vicitradīpamālābhirbhakṣyabhojyānnapānakaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pūpakānsuvicitrānvai modakāṃśca pradāpayet \|*  
*pāyasaṃ kṛśaraṃ caiva dadhyodanasamanvitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dadhi candrasamaprakhyaṃ śubhacchatraṃ ca vinyaset \|\| 27 \|\|*

20-27. The yellow coloured flags should be placed in the east. The banner of red colour should be provided for Indra in the south-east. The banners of black colour should be provided in south. The banners of blue black colour should be provided in the south-east. The flags of white colour should be provided in the west, while the flags of black colour should be provided in the north-east. The banner of green colour should be provided for Kubera in the north. The banners of all the colours should be placed in the north-east. Thereafter, making use of white and red powder, the pedestal should be made reciting the mantra Vaidya-vedi, and the image should be placed over the pedestal. Then turning the pedestal towards north and east, the kusha grass should be spread before it. The kusha grass should serve as the bed and while making the bed, the mantra Yoga-yoga should be recited. Thus after the divine bed has arranged, the Brahmanas should place two cushions over the bed in the middle of it. Thereafter, the surprising type of garland of lamps should be provided. Then, the divine food should be arranged besides the fried cakes, the excellent sweet balls, payasam, curd and boiled rice should be served. A white chatra should also be provided there.

## Chapter 135. Bathing of the Image

## \|\| 1.135.1 \|\|

*aśucivratasaṃyuktaḥ śyāmadanto'tha matsarī \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — Hereafter, I shall enlighten you about the bathing of the image of the Sungod. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.135.2 \|\|

*bhojako bhojakaiścānyairbrāhmaṇaiśca tathā vṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A Brahmana with enormous wisdom, being well-versed in the Vedas and the solar literature, such a type of Bhojaka or other Brahmana should be engaged for the bathing of the image of Surya.

## \|\| 1.135.3-8 \|\|

*rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ ghṛtādyairlabhate phalam \|*  
*yastu kārayate snānaṃ yastu bhaktyā prapaśyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*hastinā śakaṭenāpi bhaktyā brahmarathena ca \|*  
*maṃgalairbrahmaghoṣaiśca devaṃ prāsādamānayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhadrapīṭhaṃ samādāya bhadraṃ karṇeti mantrataḥ \|*  
*sūtradhārastathā proktaḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*snāpayetkalaśaṃ gṛhya devadevaṃ vibhāvasum \|*  
*sāmudraṃ toyamāhṛtya jāhnavaṃ yāmunaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sārasvataṃ jalaṃ puṇyaṃ cāndrabhāgaṃ sasaindhavam \|*  
*puṣkarasya jalaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ giriprasravaṇodakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anyadvāpi śuci toyaṃ nadīnadataḍāgajam \|*  
*yathāśaktyā upāhṛtya kalaśaiḥ kāñcanādibhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. Towards the north-east of the mandala, a bhadrapitha should be created. The image should be placed over it for bathing. The image of Surya should be brought there through a vehicle or a Brahma-ratha, with the reciting of the welfare mantras. Then reciting the mantra — bhadram-karna, the image which is placed over the pedestal, should be adorned with yajnopavita and auspicious costumes. Then, the water from the pitcher should be poured over the image, which should be pure and collected from the ocean or rivers like Ganga or Yamuna, Sarasvati, Chandrabhaga, Sindhu, Pushkara or the mountain springs or other sacred rivers, in golden pitchers.

## \|\| 1.135.9-14 \|\|

*bhojakāścāṣṭabhiḥ sūryaṃ kalaśaiḥ snāpayanti vai \|*  
*tatastu maṇiratnāni sarvabījauṣadhīstathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sugandhīni ca mālyāni sthalajānyambujāni ca \|*  
*candanāni ca mukhyāni gandhāśca vividhāstathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*brāhmī suvarcalā mustā viṣṇukrāntā śatāvarī \|*  
*dūrvā ca śibipuṣpī ca priyaṅgū rajanī vacā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sambhṛtyaitāṃstu sambhārānsnānakarmavibhāgavit \|*  
*balāśvatthaśirīṣāṇāṃ pallavaiḥ kuśasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kalaśopari vinyasya dadyādarghyaṃ raveḥ sadā \|*  
*kāñcanai rājataistāmrairmṛṇmayaiḥ kalaśaistathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sākṣataiḥ sahiraṇyaiśca sarvauṣadhisamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*gāyatryā paripūtaistu ṣoḍaśaiḥ snāpayedravim \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. The Bhojakas should bathe the image of the Sungod, with eight pitchers of water. The diamonds, gems, all the seeds, all the herbs, fragrant flower garlands, the lotus flowers, the sandal paste and various other fragrances, Brahmi herb, Suvarachala (a type of salt), a weed, Aparajita, Shatavari, Durva grass, Shibi herb, Priyangu seed, Rajani and Vacha (a herb) should be poured into the water of the pitchers. These are essential, because the Brahmanas who are well-versed, lay emphasis for the use of these items in the bath, besides the shoots of banyan, fig tree, acacia tree and kusha grass should be placed over the pitchers and oblation should be offered to the Sungod. Thus, with water and all the herbs in the pitchers of gold, silver, copper or baked clay, the oblation should be offered to the Sungod This way, the pitchers made of gold, silver, copper or baked clay, should be placed and purified with the uttering of the Gayatri mantra. Then the water of the sixteen kalashas, should be used for the bathing of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.135.15 \|\|

*kuśottarāṃ1 tataḥ kṛtvā vediṃ pakveṣṭakāmayīm \|*  
*tasyāṃ vedyāṃ samāropya paridhāpya ca vāsasī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The pedestal should then be made of the bricks of baked clay, and something should be spread. The devotee should be clad in two clothes and make offerings and consecrete the image.

## \|\| 1.135.16-17 \|\|

*pratimāmabhiṣiñcecca sopavāsaḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*mūrdhni sarvauṣadhīḥ kṛtvā tathaivāmalakāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mantreṇa mṛttikāṃ cāpi mantrataśca jalaṃ tathā \|*  
*tvaṃ devī vanditā devaiḥ sakalairdaityadānavaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. While fasting, he himself should perform the crowning ceremony of the image. In the process of performing of the , initially, all the herbs and myrobalan should be placed over the head purifying the water and then the mantras should be recited — “O goddess, you are adorable by all the gods and the demons.

## \|\| 1.135.18-20 \|\|

*tena saṃsthāpitā mūrdhni mayā devasya śuddhaye \|*  
*ādistvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ devatānāṃ ca sarvathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rasānāṃ pataye tubhyamāhvānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*itthaṃ paurāṇikairmaṃtraivaidikaiśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kāryaṃ hi vāruṇaṃ snānaṃ devasya yadunaṃdana \|*  
*itthamuccārayedvācaṃ kuryātsnānaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Therefore, for the purification of the Surya image, I have initially placed the offerings ova — the head. You happen to be the origin of all the living beings as well as the gods. You are the goddess of all the juices. Therefore, you have been invoked by me.” O son of the race of Yadus, thus reciting the hymns of the Vedas as well as the image should be bathed. He should recite the same mantras while taking his own bath.

## \|\| 1.135.21 \|\|

*devāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*vyomagaṅgā ca pūrṇena dvitīyakalaśena tu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O best of the gods! At the time of abhisheka, he should offer prayer once again, saying — “Let Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and Akasha Gangs, besides other gods perform abhisheka tor you.” This speaking, he should pour water ova the image.

## \|\| 1.135.22 \|\|

*sārasvatasya pūrṇena kalaśena surottama \|*  
*śakrādayobhiṣiṃcantu lokapālāḥ surottamāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Let god Indra — the best of gods, perform abhisheka for you, with the third pitcher filled with water of Sarasvat! river.

## \|\| 1.135.23-27 \|\|

*sāgarodakapūrṇena caturthakalaśena tu \|*  
*vāriṇā paripūrṇena padmapatrasugandhinā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pañcamenābhiṣiñcantu nāgāśca kalaśena tu \|*  
*himavaddhemakūṭādyāścābhiṣiñcantu vāriṇā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nairṛtodakapūrṇena ṣaṣṭhena kalaśena tu \|*  
*sarvatīrthāmbupūrṇena padmareṇusuvāsinā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*saptamenābhiṣiñcantu ṛṣayaḥ sapta ye varāḥ \|*  
*vasavaścābhiṣiñcantu kalaśenāṣṭamena vai \|\| 26 \|\|*

*aṣṭamaṅgalayuktena devadeva namo'stu te \|*  
*tato vai kalaśairdivyaiḥ snānakarma samārabhet \|\| 27 \|\|*

23-27. The fourth pitcher filled with water of the ocean and fragmented with lotus flowers, besides with the water of the fifth pitcher. Let the Nagas perform abhisheka for you.” Thus speaking, he should bathe the image with the fifth pitcher. Then the sixth pitcher which has been kept in the south-west direction, should be used for abhisheka by Hemakuta or Himavan. Thus speaking, he should pour the water of sixth pitcher over the head of the image. Using the seventh pitcher filled with water of all the holy places and having the fragrance of dust of lotus flowers, let the Rishis perform the abhisheka for you. Thus speaking, the water of the seventh pitcher should be poured over the head of the image. The eighth pitcher is filled with eight mangalas and all the gods combined should perform the abhisheka. Salutation to gods. Thus praying with humility, the water of the eighth kalasha should be poured over the head of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.135.28-29 \|\|

*samudraṃ gaccha yaḥ prokto mantrametamudīrayet \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbheti ca yo mantrastaṃ samudīrayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

*samudrajyeṣṭheti mantreṇa kṣālayenmṛttikānvitam \|*  
*sinīvālīti mantreṇa dadyādvalmīkamṛttikām \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Then reciting the mantras — Samudram gaccha, Hiranya garbha and Samudra jyeshtha, the clay from the body of the image should be washed out. Thereafter, reciting the mantra — Sinivali, the earth of white ants should be applied over the body of the image.

## \|\| 1.135.30 \|\|

*śamyudumbaramaśvatthaṃ nyagrodhaṃ ca palāśakam \|*  
*yajñaṃ yajñeti mantreṇa dadyātpañcakaṣāyikam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Reciting the mantra — Yajnam yajna, a paste should be made of Shami, wild fig tree, holy fig tree, banyan and leaves of palasha trees. All the leaves should be boiled in water and the same boiled water should be poured over the head of the image.

## \|\| 1.135.31-32 \|\|

*pañcagavyaṃ pavitraṃ ca āharettāmrabhājane \|*  
*gāyatryā caiva gomūtraṃ gandhadvāreti gomayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*āpyāyasveti ca kṣīraṃ dadhikrāvṇeti vai dadhi \|*  
*tejo'sīti ghṛtaṃ tadvaddevasya tvā kuśodakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Then keeping the auspicious gavya in a copper vase, the image may be bathed. Reciting the mantra — Gandhadvara and the Gayatri mantra, the cow’s urine should be used. Reciting the mantra — Apyaya, the milk and curd should be offered. Uttering the mantra — Tejosi, the ghi should be offered. Reciting the mantra — Devasyatva, the water with kusha grass should be offered.

## \|\| 1.135.33 \|\|

*evamādividhiyutaṃ pañcagavyaṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*yā1 oṣadhīti maṃtreṇa snānamoṣadhibhiḥ kramāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The combination of all these is known as Panchagavya. Thereafter, uttering the mantra — Ya oshadhi and using the aforesaid herbs, the image should be bathed.

## \|\| 1.135.34 \|\|

*drupadābhiḥ punastasya kuryāccodvartanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*śiraḥ snānaṃ tato dadyānmānastokābhimantritam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Uttering the Drupadabhih mantra, the Brahmana should rub the limbs of the image. Then, the water should be sanctified with the mantra — Manastoka, and it should be poured over the head of the image.

## \|\| 1.135.35-36 \|\|

*viṣṇorarāṭamantreṇa dadyādgandhodakaṃ śubham \|*  
*tato nadyudbhavenaiva kṣālayecchuddhavāriṇā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*jātavedasamuccārya vastrapūtena vāriṇā \|*  
*tata āvāhayeddevaṃ raktamālyāmbaraṃ śubham \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Reciting the mantra — Vishnorarat, the water should be sanctified. The pure water of the rivers should be sanctified uttering the mantra — Jatavedam, and the water should be filtered with cloth. The same water should be used for the bathing of the Surya image. With the bathing of the Sungod in an appropriate manner offering red costumes and the garland of the same colour, the Sungod should be invoiced.

## \|\| 1.135.37 \|\|

*ehyehi bhagavanbhāno lokānugrahakāraka \|*  
*yajñabhāgaṃ gṛhāṇārghyamarkadeva namo'stu te \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He should say — “O lord! Come here, come here. O lord! You are graceful on the people. You kindly accept my arghya as a part of the yajna.

## \|\| 1.135.38 \|\|

*hiraṇyena tu pātreṇa devāyārghyaṃ pradāpayet \|*  
*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame mantreṇārghyaṃ samarpayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. “O Sungod! Salutation to you.” Thus speaking, one should offer arghya in verse of gold. At the time of offering oblation, he should utter the mantra Idam Vishnuchakrame.

## \|\| 1.135.39-42 \|\|

*pārthivaiḥ prathamaṃ kalaśaiḥ snāpayedbhāskaraṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*tatastvaudumbarairvīra rājataistadanantaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tatastu kāñcanairdevaṃ snāpayedyadunandana \|*  
*sarvatīrthajalairyuktaṃ sarvauṣadhisamanvitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śaṅkhamādāya devasya tato mūrdhani śaṅkara \|*  
*dattvā puṣpāṇi devasya mūrdhni yatnādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*toyamutkṣipya yatnena tataḥ snapanamācaret \|*  
*prathamaṃ snāpayeddevaṃ vāriṇā yadunandana \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. Initially, the learned people should perform abhisheka with the water from the earthen pitchers. O valorous one, this should be followed with the pouring of the water from the silver and golden pitchers. Then, the water from all the holy places in which the herbs have been dropped, should be used for the washing of the head of the image with the use, of conches. At the time of offering water, the people of wisdom should place flowers on the head of the image and then pour the water over it.

## \|\| 1.135.43 \|\|

*tatastu payasā rājanpāyasena tatastu vai \|*  
*ghṛtena madhunā vāpi tathā ikṣurasena ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O son of the race of Yadus, initially, water should be poured over the image followed by milk, curd, ghi, honey and sugarcane juice.

## \|\| 1.135.44-45 \|\|

*agniṣṭomasya yajñasya gomedhasya ca suvrata \|*  
*jyotiṣṭomasya rājendra vājapeyasya vai vibho \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kriyamāṇaṃ tu devasya snānaṃ yadukulodvaha \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. O Suvrata Rajendra! The merit one earns with the performing of A Gomedha, Jyotishtoma, Vajapeya, and Ashvamedha sacrifices, an equivalent merit is achieved by a person by bathing the Sun image in the aforesaid manner.

## \|\| 1.135.46 \|\|

*ya ete kathitā yajñā eteṣāṃ kramaśaḥ phalam \|*  
*arcāṃ ca kuruśārdūla dṛṣṭvā vai labhate phalam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O lion of the race of Kurus, one also earns merit, simply with the observing of the process of bathing of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.135.47 \|\|

*snānaṃ tu yatnataḥ kāryaṃ devadevasya suvrata \|*  
*yathā na laṅghayetkaściddevasya snapanaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O Suvrata, abhisheka for the Sungod should thus be performed in an appropriate manner delightfully. No one should bypass the prescribed procedure.

## \|\| 1.135.48 \|\|

*na prāśnanti yathā kākāstīrthaṃ lokavigarhitāḥ \|*  
*snānodakaṃ tu devasya athavā paya eva hi \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Similarly, the denounced dogs, crows etc. should not cross or consume the left over of the washing of the image of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.135.49 \|\|

*bhūmau gataṃ yathā caiva prāśnāti yadunaṃdana \|*  
*rogaṃ prāpnoti kartā vai duḥkhaṃ kārayitā tathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Because the milk etc., spread over the ground, may be misused by anyone, then the performer attracts ailment and when performs the puja, he has also to suffer.

## \|\| 1.135.50 \|\|

*tasmādyatnena kartavyaṃ devasya snapanaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Therefore, the bath rite of the Sungod should be performed making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.135.51-55 \|\|

*snāpayitvā krameṇetthaṃ snānakarma vidhānavit \|*  
*tato vardhanikāṃ gṛhya vāridhārāṃ samutsṛjet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*trivārānpurato'rkasya ācamasveti ca bruvan \|*  
*ve \|*  
*dosīti ca mantreṇa upavītaṃ pravāpayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

*bṛhaspateti mantreṇa vastrayugmaṃ pradāpayet \|*  
*yatnakramaṃ prakurvāṇaḥ puṣpamālāṃ pradāpayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

*samiddhoñjanamantreṇa añjanaṃ tu pradāpayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

*yuñjānīti ca mantreṇa rocanāṃ tasya dāpayet \|*  
*ārārtikaṃ ca vai kuryāddīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcase \|\| 55 \|\|*

51-55. Bathing the Sungod in this way, those well-versed in this procedural performance, resort to the performing of for the pleasure of the god. For that purpose, saying Achamasva, the water should be dropped thrice before the Sungod. Afterwards, reciting the mantra — Vedosi, the yajnopavita should be offered. Reciting Brihaspateti mantra, white clothes should be offered. Thereafter, the flower garland should be offered. Uttering the mantra — Dhurasi, guggulu should be offered. Then uttering the mantra — Samiddhonjana, an eye ointment should be offered. Then reciting the Yunjani mantra, tilakam should be offered. Reciting Dirgha yushtvaya varchase, the Arati should be performed.

## \|\| 1.135.56 \|\|

*snānakarma tvidaṃ proktaṃ bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*bhojakā brāhmaṇāścaiva kriyāṃ kuryuḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The performing of the process of the bathing of the Sungod, has been prescribed in this way. The Bhojakas and the Brahmanas should perform this sacred rite making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.135.57-60 \|\|

*bahavṛco'tharvaṇaścaiva chandogodhvaryureva ca \|*  
*snāpakasya ca cihnāni ye ca mūrtidharāstathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi vibho śṛṇu caikamanāḥ kila \|*  
*sampūrṇagātro matimāñchāstrajñaḥ priyadarśanaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kulīnaḥ śraddadhānaśca āryadeśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*na sthūlo na kṛśo dīrghaḥ sauraśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yaśca yukto jitātmā ca gurubhakto jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*pañcaviṃśatitattvajñaḥ sthāpakaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. O excellent one, the symptoms of those who are engaged in the bathing of the Sungod, are being spoken by me. You please listen. They should be well-versed in the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda with all the related literatures. They should be extremely wise, scholars of scriptures, beautiful, should belong to the noble race, besides being faithful, born in Arya country, disciplined, devoted to the preceptors, having their sense organs well under their control. Besides they should be well-versed in twenty five tattvas, besides being spiritual.

## \|\| 1.135.61-67 \|\|

*varjanīyāṃśca vakṣyāmi yaistu karma na kārayet \|*  
*hīnāṅgaścādhikāṅgaśca vāmano vikaṭastathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*nātigauro na kṛṣṇaśca snāpanāya prayojayet \|*  
*cārvāko yājakaścaiva nityaṃ gomukhadambhakaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kopano duṣṭaśīlaśca yuvā vā vṛddha eva ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

*śvitrī kuṣṭhī ca rogī ca kāṇo durmatireva ca \|*  
*saṃkīrṇo jātihīnaśca tathā na vṛṣalīpatiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kubjaścādhastathā vyaṃgaḥ khalvāṭo vikalendriyaḥ \|*  
*avinīto durātmā ca vikalaḥ paṅgureva ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tithinakṣatrayogānāṃ vārāṇāṃ ca tathā vibho \|*  
*sūcako jīvikārthaṃ3 hi yaśca mūlyena pāṭhayet \|\| 66 \|\|*

*īdṛśānsnāpakānsarvānvarjayeta prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena parīkṣyāḥ snāpakā budhaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

61-67. I am also going to speak about the persons who should not be associated with the worship of Surya. You please listen. A person who is deprived of a limb, has excess limbs, is dwarfish, terrific in appearance, with excessive fair complexion or having extremely black complexion, such people should not be engaged to perform the worship of the Sungod. A person who is heretic, a beggar, having the face like that of a cow, deceitful, inauspicious, having black teeth, a cheat, wrathful, wicked, youthful, old, having white spots on the body, ailing, one eyed, of low caste, having no caste, Shudra by caste, having a Shudra wife, hunch-back, blind, lame, having deformed body, bald headed, having deformed limbs, wicked, evil, insane, lame, or the one, who earns his living by telling the day, tithis constellation and yoga etc., and one who performs recitation with a price, all such types of people are prohibited from the performing the worship of the Sungod. Therefore, the learned people, making all the efforts and appropriate tests of the performers of puja, should he engaged in the worship of the Sungod.

## Chapter 136. Consecration of the Sungod

## \|\| 1.136.1-2 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi adhivāsanamuttamam \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣo maṇḍapaṃ yatnato viśet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tato'nye ca śucau deśe asaṃspṛṣṭopalepane \|*  
*maṇḍalaṃ pañcavarṇaistu ālikheccaturasrakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Narada said — Thereafter, I shall tell you about the excellent adhivasana or residence. You please listen. Reciting the mantra — Sahasrashirsha Purusha, one should enter the mandapa. The auspicious spot should be plastered and a square masala should be prepared in five colours.

## \|\| 1.136.3 \|\|

*patākātoraṇacchatradhvajamālyādyalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*vicitrasuvitānāḍhyaṃ prakīrṇakusumotkaraiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It should be decorated with flags, torana (arches), chatras, banners and the flower garlands. With the beautiful costumes, a canopy should be made. These canopies should be like half blossomed and divine.

## \|\| 1.136.4 \|\|

*tasya madhye kuśāstīrṇe mūrtiḥ sthāpyā vivasvataḥ \|*  
*tatrāsyāvāhanaṃ kṛtvā dadyādarghyaṃ vivasvate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the middle of the canopy, the bed of kusha grass should be made. The image of Surya should then be placed over it. Then invoking the god, he should offer oblation to him.

## \|\| 1.136.5 \|\|

*suvarṇamadhuparkādi kṛtvā1 tatra vidhānataḥ \|*  
*devasya darśayedgāṃ ca savatsāṃ rohiṇīṃ śubhām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Therefore, the gold and Madhuparka (mixture of curd, clarified butter, water and honey) should be offered to the Sungod appropriately. They should then be made to have a look at a cow in Rohini Nakshatra.

## \|\| 1.136.6 \|\|

*namo gopataye tubhyaṃ sahasrāṃśo prasīda me \|*  
*evamarghyeṇa sammantrya paridhāya ca vāsasī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. At that point of time, he should utter — salutation to you. O lord of the rays, O lord with a thousand rays, you be pleased with me.” Thus speaking, he should worship him offering the arghya. He should offer two pieces of clothes to the deity.

## \|\| 1.136.7 \|\|

*yajñopavītamātithyaṃ tathābhyaṅgaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*vatsare vatsare tasya navamavyaṅgamāharet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, the yajnopavita, paste and welcoming the deity like a guest, he should be honoured. Similarly, fresh type of paste should be offered to the deity.

## \|\| 1.136.8 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe māsi rājendra pavitraṃ tasya taddhi vai \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā tu varṣevarṣe prayojayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O lord of rulers, the paste has also been prescribed to be offered in the month of Shravana, because the same has been defined to be auspicious for the lord. In this way, the Brahmana should be offered food every year, gracefully.

## \|\| 1.136.9-11 \|\|

*avyaṅgaṃ yaduśārdūla śrāvaṇe māsi bhāskaram \|*  
*sarvagandhaiḥ samālabhya candanāgurukuṅkumaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*alaṅkārairalaṅkṛtya kusumaiśca sugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*mālābhiśca vicitrābhirābaddhābhiranekaśaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tato dhūpaṃ nivedyāśu pratimāgre prayatnataḥ \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣo maṇḍapaṃ ca praveśayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. O lion of the Yadu race, in thin way, in the month of Shravana, the paste containing all the fragrances, sandal paste, agaru and saffron, should be offered to the Sungod. The image of Surya should then be adored with the flowers an well as the flower garlands. The image of Surya should then be offered the incense. Reciting the hymn Sahasrashirsha Purusha, the image should be carried Into the mandapa.

## \|\| 1.136.12-14 \|\|

*namaḥ śambhaveti mantreṇa śayyāyāṃ viniveśayet \|*  
*viśvataścakṣurityeva kuryātkamalaniṣkalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*punareva ca vakṣyāmi saṅkalīkaraṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*snāpane tu yathākāryaḥ svadehe nyāsa uttamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pratimāyāṃ tathā kāryo yathā cālambhanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*oṃ huṃ khaṣolkāya namo mūlamantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Then uttering the hymn — Namah Shambhavaya, the image should be consearated over the pedestal. ‘Then, reciting the hymn Vishvatashchakshuriti, placing it over the lotus seat, one should perform nyasa with his own body. The nyasa of the image should be done in the same way, following the same process. For that purpose, the hymn “On hum khasholkaya” has been prescribed.

## \|\| 1.136.15-17 \|\|

*ādityo'yaṃ svayaṃ devo hyakṣareṇopabṛṃhitaḥ \|*  
*oṃkāraṃ vinyasenmūrdhni huṃkāraṃ nāsikopari \|\| 15 \|\|*

*khakāraṃ ca lalāṭe tu ṣakāraṃ vadane nyaset \|*  
*lakāraṃ caiva kaṃṭhe tu kakāraṃ hṛdaye nyaset \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yakāraṃ tu bhuje vāme nakāraṃ dakṣiṇe bhuje \|*  
*makāraṃ vāmakukṣau ca visargaṃ dakṣiṇe nyaset \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. With the use of the aforesaid mantra and with Omkara, the head of the Surya image should be touched. Uttering hamkara, the tip of the nose is to be touched; with khakara, the forehead; then uttering shakara, face should be touched, the neck should be touched uttering takara. Kakara should be uttered while touching the heart, with yakara the left arm, with nakara the right arm, with makara the left waist and with visarga, the right waist should be touched.

## \|\| 1.136.18-19 \|\|

*oṃkāraṃ tu sadā dhyāyejjvālāmālāsamākulam \|*  
*huṅkāraṃ śuddhavarṇābhaṃ prasuvantamalaṃ śubham \|\| 18 \|\|*

*khakāraṃ cintayetprājño bhinnāñjanasamaprabham \|*  
*taruṇādityavarṇābhaṃ khakāraṃ cintayedbudhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Thereafter, one should meditate upon Omkara adorned with the garland of flames. The bright complexion and glory is the Hamkara. Khakara has the black complexion resembling the piece of collyrium and should be meditated upon, having the lustre of the rising Sun.

## \|\| 1.136.20 \|\|

*ṣokāraṃ tu mahābāho hemavarṇaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*śuklapadmanibhākāramakāraṃ ciṃtayedbudhaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O long armed one, Shokara has the complexion of the glittering, gold. Akara has the white colour, resembling a lotus flower.

## \|\| 1.136.21-23 \|\|

*jātīkusumasaṃkāśaṃ hrīṃkāraṃ sarvavarṇakam \|*  
*kṣīravarṇaṃ sakāraṃ tu cintayetsatataṃ budhaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nakāraṃ himakundābhaṃ makāramamṛtākṣaram \|*  
*hrīṃkāraṃ vidyutsaṃkāśaṃ hrīṃkāraṃ sarvavarṇakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kṣīravarṇaṃ sakāraṃ tu cintayetsatataṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*nakāraṃ svarṇavarṇābhaṃ makāraṃ kanakaprabham \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Hrimkara represents all the varnas and the colour of jasmine flowers. Sakara has the colour of milk, Nakara resembles the jasmine flowers. Makara resembles the nectar, Hrimkara resembles the lightning or all the colours. Sakara is of the colour of milk, Nakara and Makara resemble the gold.

## \|\| 1.136.24-25 \|\|

*tato devaṃ mahātmānaṃ sahasrakiraṇaṃ ravim \|*  
*prasādābhimukhaṃ devaṃ śayanīye niveśayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*agnikāryaṃ tataḥ kuryuragnikuṇḍeṣu vai dvijāḥ \|*  
*tato'raṇyāṃ samutthāpya agniṃ laukikameva vā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Thereafter, the image of the Sungod with a thousand rays, with a delightful face, should be made to lay down. Thereafter, the fire rites should be completed in the fire altar by the Brahmanas, in which the fire should be produced from the wooden sticks or by igniting the ordinary fire, and the learned Brahmanas should complete the homa in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 1.136.26-27 \|\|

*prajvālyāgniṃ vidhānena kuryāddhomaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*bahvṛcaḥ pūrvakāṇḍeṣu yāmyāṃ madhyandinastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*paścime caiva cchandoga uttare'tharvaṇo mataḥ \|*  
*madhye ca bhojakaḥ kuryāddhomaṃ yajñe yaduttama \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The homa should be performed as per the Rigvedic rites in the altar to the east; the homa as per Madhyandina rites should be performed in the kunda to the south; the rites should be performed in the altar to the west; while the rites as per the should be performed in the altar to the north. In the middle kunda, the homa should be performed by the Bhojakas.

## \|\| 1.136.28-30 \|\|

*śamīpālāśodumbarāṇi hyapāmārgastathaiva ca \|*  
*dvādaśa tu sahasrāṇi aṣṭau catvāri eva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dve trīṇi ca sahasrāṇi atha vā ekameva hi \|*  
*agnirmūrdheti mantreṇa kuṇḍasyālambhanaṃ bhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ullikhyābhyukṣya tenaiva agniṃ dūtamiti smṛtāḥ \|*  
*sambudhyasvāgne mantreṇa garbhādhānaṃ tu kārayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. For the performing of homa, the Shami or Palasha wood should be used, besides the Udumbara and Apamarga. The fire should be ignited. Thereafter, a thousand, two thousand, four thousand or eight or twelve thousand offerings should be made in the fire altar. This has been provided in the scriptures. Initially, reciting the hymn — Agnir one should touch the fire altar. Then, the water should be sprinkled over it. The hymn — Agnimdutamiti should be recited, completing the process. Then, uttering the hymn — Sambudhyasvdgne the conception ceremony should be performed.

## \|\| 1.136.31 \|\|

*sīmanteti punastatra mahāmantreṇa homayet \|*  
*jātakarma tathā proktaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Uttering the hymn — Simanteti, the homa should be completed. Thereafter, there is the provision of names giving ceremony as well as the performing of pranayama have been prescribed by the people of learnings.

## \|\| 1.136.32-34 \|\|

*namaḥ svāheti mantreṇa nāmakaraṇameva ca \|*  
*annaprāśanamantreṇa annaprāśanamādiśet \|\| 32 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhamagreti mantreṇa tena cūḍopakarmaṇi \|*  
*vratabandhasya mantreṇa vratabandhaṃ samādiśet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*samāvartanamityeva ākṛṣṇeti ca homayet \|*  
*patnīsaṃyojanaṃ caiva svayameva prakalpayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Uttering the mantra for etc., Jyeshthamagra mantra should be recited. The hymns relating to C ceremony and Yajnopavita ceremony should also be recited, besides the mantra Akrishna. All these ceremonies should be completed. Thereafter, the mantras relating to the marriage ceremony should also be recited.

## \|\| 1.136.35 \|\|

*agnihotrādikaṃ karma yajñakarmāṇi yāni ca \|*  
*mahāvyāhṛtimantreṇa hotavyāni samantataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The ceremonies relating the fire and performing of homa have been prescribed which should be performed. Then, uttering the hymn of Mahavyahriti, the homa should be completed.

## \|\| 1.136.36 \|\|

*mātṝṇāṃ yajñabhūtānāṃ balikarma pradāpayet \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhyarthaṃ kārayedadhivāsanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The offerings should then be made to the Matrikas as well as the Bhutas of the yajna. For the accomplishment of all the desires, the Adhivasana of the image should be performed, which is quite essential.

## \|\| 1.136.37-39 \|\|

*trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ ca ahorātramathāpi vā \|*  
*tataḥ tvalaṅkṛtāṃ snātāṃ maṇiratnairvibhūṣitām \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kṛtarakṣāṃ prayatnena pratimāmadhivāsayet \|*  
*devāgārādathaiśāne digbhāge divyamandiram \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kṛtvā kuśaparistīrṇe varāstaraṇasaṃvṛte \|*  
*pūrvaśīrṣāṃ tathā śayyāṃ śuklāṃ śuklāmbarottarām \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Accordingly, on one, three or five days and nights, taking a bath, the Adhivasana of the image, decorated with gems and diamonds, should be done. To the north-east of the temple of the god, a divine place should be erected. The kusha grass should be spread over it, and the white bed should be arranged with head part facing the east. It should be decorated with a white flowers.

## \|\| 1.136.40 \|\|

*tasyāmāveśayetsamyaṅmahāśvetamupāharet \|*  
*nikṣubhā dakṣiṇe pārśve vāme rājñī ca kīrtitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Surya image should be made to sleep over the same. Nikshubha should be lodged to the right of the image, while Rajni should be on the left side. This has been prescribed in the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.136.41-43 \|\|

*daṇḍapiṅgalakau cāsya sthitau pādapraveśitau \|*  
*tasyāṃ saṃveśitāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ pratimāṃ raveḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vasettāṃ rajanīṃ tatra stūyamānaścatudiśam \|*  
*brāhmaṇairbandibhiścāpi gītajñaiścāraṇaistathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ tatra sūryabhaktisamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ bodhayedṛgvidhānataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. Towards the feet of the image should stand Danda (or Dandi) as well as Pingala. During the period when the image is supposed to be in sleep, the recitation of stotras should continue throughout the night. Because for the Brahmanas, bards as well as the Charanas are required to sing the glory of the Sungod, remaining awake throughout the night. In the morning, as per the provision of the Rigveda} the deity should be waken up.

## \|\| 1.136.44 \|\|

*haviṣyaṃ bhoktukāmāṃstu brāhmaṇānbhojakāṃstathā \|*  
*dakṣiṇābhiśca sampūjya taiḥ kṛtasvastivācanaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Brahmanas and the Bhojakas who are desirous of the havishya food, they should be adored, and giving dakshina to each one of them they should be made to recite the welfare mantras.

## \|\| 1.136.45 \|\|

*tato garbhagṛhasthāya madhye kṛtvā tu piṇḍikām \|*  
*vidhivattatra sauvarṇaṃ nyasetsaptahayaṃ ratham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The pedestal should then be placed in the centre of the garbha-griha and a chariot of gold with seven horses should be placed over it.

## \|\| 1.136.46 \|\|

*sarvabījauṣadhaiścaiva tatra dhṛtvā vidhānavit \|*  
*dattvārghyaṃ sthāpayettatra yajamānaḥ sahāyavān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then appropriately placing all the herbs, the yajamana with his wife, should offer arghya there.

## \|\| 1.136.47 \|\|

*śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣairjaladhārāsahākṣataiḥ \|*  
*kṛtyā puṇyāhaśabdaṃ tu ālayasya pradakṣiṇām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Producing the sound from the conches as well as the big drums, the water mixed with unbroken rice should be poured, reciting the welfare mantras, and one should circumambulate the temple.

## \|\| 1.136.48 \|\|

*śubhalagne dine ṛkṣe pūrvāhṇe bhānave kṣaṇe \|*  
*muhūrte ca śubhe bhānoḥ pratimāṃ sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The learned person say that at the start of an auspicious day, lagna, constellation and muhurta, the image of Sungod should be consecrated.

## \|\| 1.136.49 \|\|

*nādhomukhīṃ nordhvamukhīṃ na pārśvāvanatāṃ tathā \|*  
*samāmabhimukhīṃ cemāṃ pratimāṃ tu niveśayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The face of the image should neither be raised nor bent down. It should not be bent at the back. Thus, a well-built smiling image should be consecrated.

## \|\| 1.136.50 \|\|

*patnyau cāsya tataḥ samyakpārśvayorviniveśayet \|*  
*nikṣubhā dakṣiṇe pārśve rave rājñī tu vāmataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Both the wives of the Sungod should be established at his back, according to which Nikshubha should be at the right back, while Rajni should be to the left.

## \|\| 1.136.51-53 \|\|

*tatastadupahārārthaṃ sambhāraṃ prāktamāhṛtaiḥ \|*  
*modakāyūṣikāpūpaśaṣkulībhūtaśīrṣakaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kṛśaraiḥ pāyasonmiśraiḥ sarvadikṣu kṣipedbalim \|*  
*indrāya devapataye baline vajrapāṇaye \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śatayajñādhipataye tasmai indrāya te namaḥ \|*  
*trātāramindramantreṇa indrasyāvāhanaṃ bhavet \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. The food and other items collected for the Sungod, should then be offered to him including the sweet balls, juicy fried cakes, puri and other eatables, besides payasam should be placed as offerings in all the directions. Accordingly, speaking — “Salutation to Devapati, Bali, Vajrapani, besides Indra — the lord of a hundred yajnas”, offerings should be made to Indra and reciting the hymn Tratarami Indra, the image should be invoked.

## \|\| 1.136.54 \|\|

*agnaye raktanetrāya jvālāmālārcitāya vai \|*  
*śaktihastāya tīvrāya tathā caivājavāhine \|*  
*āgreyyāmagrimantreṇa vahnerāvāhanaṃ smṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Salutation to the fire god having red eyes, wearing the garland of flames, holding a shakti in his hand, forceful, having a goat as a vehicle. Before reciting the above, offering should be made to the fire-god invoking him at the same time, reciting the mantra — Agneyyamgni.

## \|\| 1.136.55-57 \|\|

*daṇḍahastāya kṛṣṇāya mahiṣottamavāhine \|*  
*sūryaputrāya devāya dharmarājāya vai namaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yamāya tviti mantreṇa mudrāstasyaiva kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*nairṛte khaḍgahastāya nīlalohitakāya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sarvabāhyādhipataye virūpākhyāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*āyaṃ gauriti mantreṇa nairṛtyāṃ tu prakalpayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Salutation to Yama, holding a danda in his hand, having black complexion, having a vast male buffalo as his vehicle, son of Surya, besides being Dharmaraja. Thus speaking, offering should be made to Dharmaraja. He should be invoked uttering the hymn — Yamayatviti etc., displaying his mudrCL Holding a sword in his hand, He is of red and blue colour. He is the leader of the universe. Salutation to this form. Thus speaking, the offering should be made to him. Then uttering the mantra — Ayam Gauriti he should be invoked and established in the south-west direction.

## \|\| 1.136.58 \|\|

*vāruṇyāṃ pāśahastāya varuṇāyeti kalpayet \|*  
*mantreṇāvāhanaṃ vidyātpañcanadyaḥ sarasvatīm \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then Varuna should be adored holding a noose in his hand, offering him the Bali in the western direction. He should be invoked uttering the hymn — Panchanadyah Sarasvati.

## \|\| 1.136.59-61 \|\|

*prāṇātmakāya dhūpāya avyaṅgāyānilāya ca \|*  
*dhvajahastāya bhīmāya namo gandhavahāya ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasyāpyāvāhanaṃ vidyādyaddevādevaheḍanam \|*  
*gadāhastāya somāya śuṣmiṇe nṛgatāya ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

*gadāpaṭṭiśahastāya somarājāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*īśāvāsyaṃ ca guhyā vai somamantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. Salutation to the Wind god — the lord of life, holding a flag in his hand and who carries the fragrance. Speaking the above passage, the offering should be made to the Wind god. Soma carries a club in his hand, looks illustrious. Salutation to the Moon god. Thus speaking, offering should be made to Somaraja. The hymn for invoking him is — Ishavasyam cha guhyam.

## \|\| 1.136.62-63 \|\|

*caturmukhāya devāya padmāsanagatāya ca \|*  
*kṛṣṇājinaniṣaṇṇāya namo lambodarāya ca \|\| 62 \|\|*

*gaṇādhipataye deva nīlakaṇṭhāya śūline \|*  
*virūpākṣāya rudrāya trailokyādhipate namaḥ \|*  
*abhi tvā śūra no mantra īśānāya prakalpayet \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Then salutation should be made to Lambodara-Ganesha seated over a lotus and black hide of a buck. Thus speaking, offering should be made to Lambodara. Then, one should say — “Salutation to the lord of the ganas, blue throated, holding a trident, Virupaksha is the lord of all the three worlds. Salutation to Rudra.” Thus speaking, the offering should be made to him. The hymn for invoking him is — Abhitva shura no.

## \|\| 1.136.64-65 \|\|

*sarvanāgādhirājāya śvetavarṇāya bhogine \|*  
*sahasraphaṇine nityamanantāya namonamaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*namo'stu sarpebhya iti mantraścaiva prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*pañcarātrādibhirnyāso hyaṃganyāsaḥ prayujyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Lord of all the serpents, having white complexion, having a thousand hoods, a Bhogi, salutation to Anantadeva. The mantra for invoking him is — Namostu sarpebhya. Thus, during the Adhivasana period of five nights, anga-nyasa should be continued to be performed.

## \|\| 1.136.66 \|\|

*tathopakṣīrapānaiśca stutistotraiśca bhāskaram \|*  
*viprebhyo bhojakebhyaśca tato dadyācca dakṣiṇām \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. For the Sungod, the payasam should be offered reciting the stotras. The Brahmanas and Bhojakas should thereafter, be given the dakshina.

## \|\| 1.136.67-68 \|\|

*sūryakratuṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ naiva kuryādadakṣiṇam \|*  
*sthāpyate'nena vidhinā tadbhaktaiḥ pratimā ca yā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*sā tu vṛddhikarā nityaṃ sānnidhyācca sadā bhavet \|*  
*saptajanmasu teṣāṃ tu na rogāḥ sambhavanti hi \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Thus, the performance of this yajna has been said to be quite meritorious. It should never be performed without giving dakshina. A devotee of the Sungod, when performs this yajna consecrating the image of the Sungod, then the same image always showers fortunes over the devotee. The Sungod always remains close to that image. The person who consecrates the image, does not have to suffer from any ailment for seven future births.

## \|\| 1.136.69 \|\|

*upāsate trirātraṃ ye bhānoryātrābhivāsane \|*  
*gandhamālyopahāraistu te yānti bhuvanaṃ raveḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A person who meditates upon the Sungod for three nights during the period of Adhivasana offering fragrant flowers, he achieves the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.136.70 \|\|

*ātmīyaṃ parakīyaṃ vā pratimāsthāpanaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paśyati pumānbhaktyā sa svarlokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Or alternatively, one, who watches the process of the consecration of the Surya image in a temple with devotion, he surely achieves heaven.

## \|\| 1.136.71 \|\|

*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ vājapeyaśatasya ca \|*  
*phalaṃ prāpnoti puruṣaḥ pratiṣṭhāpya divākaram \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One gets the merits of performing ten Ashvamedha and a hundred Vajapeya sacrifices simply by consecrations of Surya image.

## \|\| 1.136.72 \|\|

*yāvatkīrtiḥ puṇyakṛtā bhānoḥ sthāne niveśite \|*  
*tāvatsa tu yaduśreṣṭha sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O best of Yadus, by consecrating the Surya image at an auspicious place, the period upto which the merit lasts, upto that time the concerned person is worshipped in the Satyaloka.

## \|\| 1.136.73 \|\|

*sthāpane cāsya vai mantraḥ prokto lokeṣu pūjitaḥ \|*  
*dhruvā dyauśca dhruvā pṛthvī dhruvaṃ viśvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*śreyase yajamānasya tathā tvaṃ dhruvatāṃ vraja \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. While consecrating the image of the sun, one should recite the mantra — “The entire sky, the earth besides the universe are fixed” Therefore, the performer, for his own benefit, should also remain steadfast.

## \|\| 1.136.74 \|\|

*sthāpayitvā raviṃ bhaktyā vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*māse māse ṛtuphalaṃ labhante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Having been overwhelmed with devotion by consecrating the Surya image, the concerned person achieves in every month, the merit of performing a yajna.

## \|\| 1.136.75 \|\|

*ekāhenāpi yadbhānoḥ pūjayā prāpyate phalam \|*  
*na tu kratuśatairvīra prāpyate mānavairbhuvi \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. O valorous one! The merit one gets by worshipping the Sungod for a day, the merit equivalent to that cannot be achieved on earth by performing hundreds of yajnas.

## \|\| 1.136.76 \|\|

*kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ yaḥ paścātsevate ravim \|*  
*sa yāti sūryalokaṃ tu naro vigatakalmaṣaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Therefore, even after committing a grave crime, if a person adores the Sungod, then also getting his sins washed, be becomes sinless and proceeds on to the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.136.77 \|\|

*na bhavediṣṭakānāṃ ca dravaṇaṃ bhūmisaṃmiti \|*  
*svarge mahīyate tāvatkārako devaveśmanaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Till such time the brick of a temple is reduced to dust, upto that period the one who builds the temple, is honoured in the heaven.

## \|\| 1.136.78 \|\|

*khaṇḍasphuṭitasaṃskāraṃ kṛtvā yatphalamāpyate \|*  
*na tu kratusahasraistu prāpyate phalamuttamam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The merit one earns by repairing or restoring the damaged images, could never be achieved with the performing of thousand of yajnas.

## \|\| 1.136.79-80 \|\|

*sikatāyāmapi gṛhaṃ yastu kuryādvibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*gopateḥ sa priyasadaḥ pragacchedgopatervaram \|\| 79 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ suravarasya tasya bhānorbhūtānāṃ sthitinilayaprasūtihetoḥ \|*  
*śrībhāgī bhavati naro niketakārī kalpānāṃ vasati śataṃ sa sūryaloke \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Thus, a person who has made an abode of Surya in sand or intends to build the same, the Sungod gets fascinated for the same and he continues to do so. The person, who builds the same, achieves the excellent place and the same shall also be available in future. Therefore, one who builds a temple for the Sungod — the main cause of the birth and death of the people, he remains in the abode of Surya for a hundred kalpas.

## Chapter 137. Method of Consecration

## \|\| 1.137.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*yaḥ prāsādaṃ racayati pumāndevatānāṃ prayatnāttatra prītyā sapadi kurute sthāpanāṃ bhānubhaktaḥ \|*  
*divyānbhogāṃllabhati ca sadā kāmataścāprameyāṃstānbhuktvāsau punarapi bhaveccakravartī pṛthivyām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — The devotee of Surya, who builds a majestic Deva temple, making all the efforts and then quickly enshrines the Surya image there, he surely enjoys the divine comforts and all his boundless desires are fulfilled. On his rebirth on earth, he becomes a Chakravarti emperor.

## \|\| 1.137.2 \|\|

*ye mānavāstridaśamūrtiniketanāni kurvanti sādhujanadṛṣṭimanoharāṇi \|*  
*teṣāṃ mṛte'pyaparamārthamaye śarīre loke paribhramati kīrtimayaṃ śarīram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Therefore, the people who have built the images of the deities, the sight of which delights the eyes of the noble people, the glory of such people always remain in the body, on earth even after their death.

## \|\| 1.137.3 \|\|

*iti te kathitamidaṃ devapūjyasya savituḥ sthāpanamivādhānam \|*  
*sādhāraṇaṃ vidhānaṃ śṛṇu devānāṃ pratiṣṭhāpane vīra \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O valorous one! Thus, I have spoken to you the method of consecrating an image in the temple which is quite vast. Now, I shall speak out the ordinary procedure for the consecration of the other gods, which you please listen.

## \|\| 1.137.4 \|\|

*snāto bhukto vastrālaṅkṛtakusumairgandhaiḥ pratimāyā āstīrṇāyāṃ śayyāyāṃ sthāpanaṃ kuryāt \|*  
*suptāyāṃ tu sa nṛtyagītairjāgaraṇaiḥ samyagevādhivāsya daivajñena pratidiṣṭakāle saṃsthāpanaṃ kuryāt \|*  
*abhyarcya kusumagandhānulepanaiḥ śaṅkhatūryanirghoṣaiḥ prādakṣiṇyena nayedāyatanasya prayatnena kṛtvā baliṃ pratimāmabhyarcya brāhmaṇāṃśca sādhūndattvā hiraṇyakalaśaṃ vidhinā nikṣipetpiṃṇḍikāmadhye suśvabhre sthāpakadaivajñadvijānsamyagviśeṣato'bhyarcyākalpāntaṃ bhogī bhavatīha paratra sukhī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Initially, the image should be washed, and then food and costumes should be offered to the same. Then, fragrance and flowers should be offered to the same. It should then be made to lay over the bed of kusha grass. While singing and dancing, he should keep himself awake during the night. The image should then be consecrated on some auspicious day and time. The fragrance and flowers should be offered to the image. With the sound of musical instruments, the image, after circumambulating it, should be carried to the temple, where it should be worshipped. The offerings to the gods should be made, while the food should be given to the sages and the Brahmanas, besides the dakshina. Thereafter, the pedestal should be appropriately made in the temple. The image should be thereafter, consecrated over the spotless place. A person, who on such occasions, honours well the astrologers and the Brahmanas, he enjoys all the comforts till the end of the kalpa.

## \|\| 1.137.5 \|\|

*viṣṇorbhāgavatā matāśca savituḥ śambhoḥ sabhasmadvijā mātṝṇāmapi mātṛmaṇḍalavido viprā vidurbrāhmaṇāḥ \|*  
*sarve yasya vimuktaśuklavasanā buddhasya raktāmbarā ye yaṃ devamupāśritāḥ suvidhinā taistasya kāryā kriyā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The devotees of Vishnu are known as Bhagavatas or Vaishnavas; the devotees of the Sun are known as Bhagas or Bhojakas. The devotees of Shiva have their bodies smeared with ashes; the devotees of Matrikas are the learned people of Matri-mandala; the devotees of Buddha do not wear white robes, and are clad in red garments. Therefore, they should get the image of such a deity consecrated, to whom they are devoted.

## \|\| 1.137.6 \|\|

*sāmānyamidaṃ devānāmadhivāsanaṃ bhavati mayā kathitam \|*  
*kriyamāṇamidaṃ dṛṣṭvā devānāṃ pratiṣṭhāpanam \|*  
*naro bhaktyā iha kāmānavāpya svargabhājanaṃ bhavati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thus, the ordinary way of the setting up of the images of gods has been spoken by me. A person, who witnesses the process of consecration of the images of the gods with devotion, he gets all his desires fulfilled in the world and then achieves heaven.

## \|\| 1.137.7-8 \|\|

*idaṃ te kathitaṃ rājanpratiṣṭhāpanamāditaḥ \|*  
*yatkṛtvā savituḥ snānaṃ naro yāti manogatim \|\| 7 \|\|*

*itthaṃ kuryānnaro bhaktyā savituḥ sthāpanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*kārayetpurato bhaktayā savituḥ sthāpanaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. O king! Thus, I have narrated from beginning to end, the process of consecration of the images in which a householder gets all his desires fulfilled simply by bathing the image of the Sungod, then what to speak of a person who performs his puja in an appropriate manner? Therefore, a person should consecrate the Surya image with devotion.

## \|\| 1.137.9 \|\|

*itihāsapurāṇasya śravaṇaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*tābhyāṃ hi śravaṇādvīra sānnidhyaṃ yāti bhāskaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Similarly, the listening of the scriptures and the Puranas is said to be the reliever of the sins, because with the listening of the same the Sungod always remains present there in the image.

## \|\| 1.137.10 \|\|

*kṛte tvāyatane tasminye cānye cāpi devatāḥ \|*  
*tasmātkāryaṃ budhairnityaṃ dharmaśravaṇamāditaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When the recitation is carried out in the temple, the other gods also get delighted there. Therefore, the learned person should listen to the recitation from the beginning.

## \|\| 1.137.11 \|\|

*vācakaṃ pūjayitvā tu brāhmaṇānupapūjya ca \|*  
*kārayedvācanaṃ vīra pustakasyāgrato raveḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus, worshipping the reciters as well as the other Brahmanas, the holy book should be read in front of the image of Surya.

## \|\| 1.137.12 \|\|

*sarvasvaṃ sthāpake dadyādyatkiñjidgṛhamāgatam \|*  
*godānamathavā dadyāttasya cittaṃ prasādayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The yajamana, who has the consecration made, should give away everything in donation. On his return to his place of residence, he should also give away a cow in charity or whatever is left out, should also be performed. The reciters should always be kept happy.

## \|\| 1.137.13 \|\|

*ityeṣa kathito vīra pratiṣṭhākalpa āditaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā dṛṣṭvā ca śrutvā ca yaṃ naro'rkamavāpnuyāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O valorous one! I have thus narrated to you the process of consecration of the Surya image from beginning to end, with the performing or listening of which a person surely achieves the abode of Surya.

## Chapter 138. Hoisting of the flag

## \|\| 1.138.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*hanta te kathayiṣyāmi dhvajāropaṇamuttamam \|*  
*yaduktaṃ brahmaṇā pūrvamṛṣabhādhipate puraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — I am speaking out the process of hoisting of the flag, which in earlier times was narrated by Brahma to the lord Rishabha.

## \|\| 1.138.2 \|\|

*purā devāsure yuddhe yāni devairjayepsubhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtānyupari cihnāni vāhanāni dhvajāni tu \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the terrific war between the Devas and the Rakshasas, the gods who were desired of victory had made marks over their chariots, they are known by the name of Bhaga and those which were in the form of the vehicles, they became the vehicles for all times to come.

## \|\| 1.138.3 \|\|

*lakṣmacihnadhvajaṃ keturiti paryāyanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*kīrtitaḥ sa ca tasyeha pramāṇaṃ gadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The pole of the flag should be of a superior quality of a bamboo. It should be neither too low nor curved. Dhvaja or flag should be embossed with four letters and the space for putting or fixing the bamboo in it.

## \|\| 1.138.4 \|\|

*dhvajo vaṃśasya kartavyastvaviddha ṛjuravraṇaḥ \|*  
*prāsādavyāsa tulyasya dhvajavaṃśapramāṇataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The flags are therefore, known by the names of — Lakshana, Cihna, Dhvaja and Ketu. I am going to speak out the evidence for the same.

## \|\| 1.138.5 \|\|

*devāgārasya ye proktā mañjarīkalaśādayaḥ \|*  
*atha vā tatpramāṇastu dhvajadaṇḍaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. For the purpose of a flag, first of all, there should be a bamboo pole, which should be straight, devoid of holes and without any defect. The length of the flag should be commensurate with the area of the house.

## \|\| 1.138.6 \|\|

*antargṛhasya yā vedī sūtrataḥ parikalpitā \|*  
*tasyā vyāso bhavedvaṃśaḥ prasādasya yadūttama \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Or otherwise, the kalasha in the temples should have the height similar to the same.

## \|\| 1.138.7 \|\|

*atha vā mūlasūtreṇa yo vyāso'ntargṛhasya tu \|*  
*prāsādavyāsa iti te proktaśceha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O best of the race of Yadu! Similarly, in the garbha griha, Vedi should be measured with a cord and the height of the bamboo should be equal to the diameter of the palace, which is said to be the best.

## \|\| 1.138.8 \|\|

*keturbhavedvaro vaṃśo na nimno na ṛjustathā \|*  
*patraṃ dhvaje yugaṃ caiva nalikāpuruṣastathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Or it should be like the mula-sutra because the garbha-griha’s length is said to be the length of the building. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.138.9-11 \|\|

*caturhastā bhavantyete praśastāḥ kṛṣṇanandana \|*  
*aṣṭahastapramāṇastu viṃśārdhasya1 pramāṇataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sāmānyo dhvajadaṇḍastu sarvasādhāraṇo mataḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapāṇidhvajo yastu smṛtaḥ ṣoḍaśahastavān \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viṃśaddhastātparo daṇḍo na kāryaḥ sarvathā raveḥ \|*  
*yugmahastastu kartavyo dhvajadaṇḍo manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. O son of Krishna! The flag of four cubit is believed to be praiseworthy. Besides, the bamboo is also of the length of eight cubits and ten cubits as well. But these are all ordinary flag poles. A Dandapani flag has the length of sixteen cubits. However, for Sungod, the flag pole should not be more than twenty cubits. The learned people should make the flag pole of two cubits length.

## \|\| 1.138.12 \|\|

*caturaṅgulavistīrṇaḥ suvṛtto dvyaṅgulopari \|*  
*nātisūkṣmo na ca sthūlo na kāryo nataparvakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It should be four angulas thick and about two angulas it should be circular and beautiful. It should not be very thin, nor very thick or with curved knots.

## \|\| 1.138.13-14 \|\|

*samaparvātu kartavyaḥ sudṛḍhaḥ sūkṣma eva hi \|*  
*vakraḥ putravināśāya savraṇo'rthavināśanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rogado yugmahastastu bhinno duḥkhamanantakam \|*  
*karoti hāni dharmasya hīno yastu pramāṇataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Therefore, a bamboo pole with four knots which should be extremely sound, should be used for the purpose of the flag. In case it is curved, the son gets destroyed. In case of its being defective or with a hole in it, there is the loss of riches; in case of its being two cubits in height, one attracts ailment. In case it is cracked, the person has to face sufferings. In case it is smaller than that which is prescribed, dharma declines.

## \|\| 1.138.15-16 \|\|

*vaiṣamyamasamaparvā dadyātkṛcchramadhonnataḥ \|*  
*jayo jayanto jaitreyaḥ4 śatruhantā jayāvahaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nandopanandanau caivendropendrau gaditau tathā \|*  
*daśaite kīrtitā bhedā dhvajasyānandasammitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Similarly, when the pole has the length of old numbers of cubits and with uneven knots while raising from below, one has to suffer. Thus, the poles have been described to be of ten types — Jaya, Jayanta, Jaitreya, Shatruhanta, Jayavaha, Nanda, Upananda, Indra and Upendra. These are the ten different types of the poles.

## \|\| 1.138.17-19 \|\|

*dvijahastastu jayo daṇḍo jayanto dviguṇo mataḥ \|*  
*dvādaśahastastu jaitreyaḥ śatruhantā kalānvitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jayāvahastu viṃśārdho nanda ādityasannibhaḥ \|*  
*caturdaśopanandastu indraḥ ṣoḍaśa ucyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*upendro'ṣṭādaśaḥ5 proktastathendro viṃśatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhinno vakro'sādhitaśca na kāryo daṇḍa eva hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. The flag pole of two cubits is known as Jaya, while the flag of double the size is known as Jayanta. The flag with twelve cubits length is known as Jaitreya and the flag of eight cubits height is known as Shatruhanta. The flag with the length of ten cubits height is known as Jayavaha, while that of the length of fourteen cubits is known as Nanda. The flag with the height of sixteen cubits is known as Indra. The flag with eighteen cubits length is known as Upendra, while that of twenty cubits is called Indra or Ananda. Therefore, the damaged, curved or without specifications flags of bamboos, should not be put to use.

## \|\| 1.138.20 \|\|

*mūlamantreṇa kartavyo vyāsato'ntargṛhasya tu \|*  
*dhvajadaṇḍo mahābāho atha vā vāstumānataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. According to the inner measurement of a house, the length is decided with the cord and the flags should be of the same length, or like the vastu of the building.

## \|\| 1.138.21 \|\|

*mañjarīmānato vāpi tadardhenāthavā vibho \|*  
*patākā vai śubhā kāryā dhvajavaṃśāvalambinī \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O competent one! The flag past can be made like a new shoot, cluster or the ear of com or half of its size. The cloth hanging from the flag should be half of its size. The hanging cloth of the flag should also be of benevolent form.

## \|\| 1.138.22 \|\|

*devāgārasya śikharāttribhāgaparimārjanī \|*  
*sā proktā daśadhā vīra mānatomānatastathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O valorous one, in order to purify the three parts of the Shikhara of the temple, the flags which are of measured or unmeasured dimensions, are of ten types.

## \|\| 1.138.23-26 \|\|

*aṅkuraḥ pallavaścaiva skandhaḥ śākhā tathaiva ca \|*  
*patākā kadalī vīra keturlakṣma jayastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dhvajaśca daśamaḥ proktaḥ sarvadevamayovyayaḥ \|*  
*aṅkuro dvayaṃgulaḥ proktaḥ pallavaścaturaṅgulaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*skandhaḥ ṣaḍaṅgulaḥ proktaḥ śākhā cāṣṭāṅgulo matā \|*  
*ekādaśapatākā tu kadalī ca caturdaśa \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ketustu ṣoḍaśaḥ prokto lakṣmāṣṭādaśamucyate \|*  
*jayā viṃśati vai proktā etāvattvaṅgulāni tu \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. O valorous one! The different types of flags are known sprout, foliage, trunk, branch, flag, young shoot, sign or mark, Jaya, Lakshma and banner. These are the ten different types of flags which represent all the deities besides being indestructible. In this clarification, Ankura (sprout) is of the size of two angulas; Pallava or foliage is of four angulas size, Skandha of six angulas size; branch or Sakha is of eight angulas size; Pataka is of eleven angulas size; Kadali is of fourteen angulas size; Ketu is of sixteen angulas size; Lakshma is of eighteen angulas size; while Jaya is of twenty angulas size.
