The flag has been described to be of the same size.

## \|\| 1.138.27 \|\|

*devāgārasya kumbhasya prasannā sā pramārjanī \|*  
*aṅkureti patākā sā vijñeyā yadunandana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O son of the race of Yadus! The flag which purifies the first kalasha of the temple of a deity while fluttering, is known by the rime of Ankura.

## \|\| 1.138.28 \|\|

*pallaveti dvitīyasya mārjanī parikīrtitā \|*  
*tribhāgamārjanīskandhaḥ śākhā vai pañcamasya tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Similarly, the one which purifies the second kalasha is known as Pallava. The flag which purifies the third kalasha of the temple is known as Skandha. Sakha is the flag which purifies the fifth part of the temple.

## \|\| 1.138.29-30 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhasyoktā patākā tu kadalī saptamasya tu \|*  
*aṣṭamasya tathā keturlakṣma ca navamasya tu \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatastu daśamaḥ prokto jayanto yadunandana \|*  
*vṛṣasthānāvamārgī tu dhvajastu parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The flag which purifies the sixth part of the temple is known as Pataka; while the seventh part is purified by Kadali. Ketu purifies the eighth part of the temple, while Lakshma purifies the ninth part. Jayanta purifies the tenth part which is Vrisha-sthana or the place of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.138.31-32 \|\|

*gajo meṣo'tha mahiṣaḥ kabandhastu vṛṣastathā \|*  
*hariṇo'tha naraścaiva naraśca narasattama \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sthānānyetāni bhūyo'tha1 prayuktasya dhvajasya tu \|*  
*diśabhāge tu pūrvāttu krameṇa parikalpayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Therefore, the flags should be embossed with elephant, ram, buffalos, torso, bull, stag, boar, and the serpent. Starting from the east, the flags are required to be hoisted in all the directions. This has been prescribed.

## \|\| 1.138.33 \|\|

*evaṃ daśavidhā proktā patākā tattvadarśibhiḥ \|*  
*kartavyā sā yathāpūrvaṃ tacchṛṇu tvaṃ narādhipa \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In this way, people, who are well-versed in the tattvas, have prescribed the hoisting of the ten types of flags. O lord of the people! I am going to speak out the method of the preparation of the flags. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.138.34 \|\|

*śuklavastramayī citrā saghaṇṭā sumanoharā \|*  
*nānācāmarasampannā kiṅkiṇījālamaṇḍitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The flag should be of white and other different colours, with a bell and should be extremely beautiful, decorated with the flywhisks of various colours and the small bells.

## \|\| 1.138.35-36 \|\|

*dhvajāgre caiva kartavyo devatāliṅgasūcakaḥ \|*  
*kāñcano vātha raupyo vā maṇiratnamayo'pi vā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*raṅgakairlikhyate vāpi tadvāhanasamākṛtiḥ \|*  
*dhvajadaṇḍo'tra vinyastaḥ kartavyo yadunandana \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The god to which the flag is dedicated should be embossed in the forefront of the flag. Similarly, using the gems, gold and silver, the vehicle of the same god should also be embossed over the flag or alternatively, the colour should be used for the purpose. O son of the race of Yadu! Therefore, the flag pole should be consecrated as stated earlier.

## \|\| 1.138.37-41 \|\|

*garutmātmāṃstu dhvajo viṣṇorīśvarasya dhvajo vṛṣaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ paṅkajaṃ kāryaṃ raverdharmaḥ smṛto dhvajaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*haṃso1 jalādhipasyoktaḥ somasya tu naro dhvajaḥ \|*  
*baladevasya kālastu kāmasya makaradhvajaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*siṃho dhvajastu durgāyāḥ kīrtito yadunandana \|*  
*godhā cāpi umādevyā raivatasya hayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kacchapo varuṇasyokto vātasya hariṇo mataḥ \|*  
*pāvakasya tathā meṣa ākhurgaṇapatermataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*brahmarṣīṇāṃ kuśaḥ prokta ityeṣā dhvaja kalpanā \|*  
*yasya yadvāhanaṃ proktaṃ tattasya dhvaja ucyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. For example, Garuda should appear in the flag of Vishnu; the bull in the flag of Shiva; the lotus in the flag of Brahma; Dharma in the flag of Surya; swan in the flag of ocean; a human in the flag of the Moon; Baladeva in the flag of Kala; tortoise in the flag of Kamadeva; and a lion in the flag of Durga should be made. Again, lizard should be mad in the flag of Uma; a horse for Raivata; tortoise for Varuna; a stag for the wind god; a ram for the fire god; a mouse for Ganapati and for Brahmarishis the symbol of kusha grass should be shown. The flag should be conceived accordingly. Because whatever be the vehicle of the god or goddess, the same should appear over his or her flag.

## \|\| 1.138.42 \|\|

*viṣṇordhvaje tu sauvarṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*patākā cāpi pītā syādgaruḍasya samīpagā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Therefore, a learned person should decorate the flag of Vishnu with a golden flag pole, in which the image of Garuda should be embossed in yellow colour.

## \|\| 1.138.43 \|\|

*īśvarasya dhvaje daṇḍo rājato yadunandanaḥ \|*  
*patākā cāpi śuklā syādvṛṣabhasya samīpagā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O son of Yadu race! The pole of the flag of Shiva should be made of silver, with a bull embossed over the white cloth.

## \|\| 1.138.44 \|\|

*pitāmahadhvaje daṇḍaḥ smṛtastāmramayo budhaiḥ \|*  
*padmavarṇā patākā syātpaṅkajasya samīpagā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. As per the people of wisdom, the flag of Brahma should have a pole of copper. The image of lotus should be embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.45 \|\|

*ādityasya ca sauvarṇo dhvaje daṇḍaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*pañcavarṇā patākā syāddharmasyādhogatā nṛpa \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The flag of the Sungod should have the pole of gold. The flag should be of five colours over which Dharma should be embossed.

## \|\| 1.138.46 \|\|

*kiṅkiṇījālasampannā nānabudbudasannibhā \|*  
*puṣpamālopasampannā nānāvādibhirāvṛtā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It should be decorated with small bells and should appear graceful like the foam, decorated with flower garlands, besides the musicians playing on musical instruments appearing in human forms.

## \|\| 1.138.47 \|\|

*daṇḍa indradhvajasyoktaḥ kāñcano yadunandana \|*  
*patākā bahuvarṇā syātkuñjarasya samīpagā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O son of Yadu race! The flag pole of Indra should be made of gold. The flag should be of different colours, with elephant embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.48 \|\|

*āyasaścāpi daṇḍokto yamacihnaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*patākā varṇataḥ kṛṣṇā mahiṣasya samīpagā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Yama should have the flag with a pole of iron. The colour of its flag should be of black colour and a male buffalo should be embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.49 \|\|

*jalādhipadhvajo daṇḍo rājataḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*patākā sarvataḥ śvetā vicitrā sā ca kathyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Varuna should have the flag pole of silver, the flag should be of white colour decorated with different colours.

## \|\| 1.138.50 \|\|

*dhvaje cāpi kuberasya daṇḍo maṇimayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*patākā cāpi raktā syānnarapādasamīpagā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The pole of the flag of Kubera should be made of gems. The flag should be of red colour with a human embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.51 \|\|

*baladevadhvaje daṇḍo rājato yadunandana \|*  
*patākā varṇataḥ śuklā tālasyādhogatā smṛtā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The flag post of Baladeva should be made of silver, the flag should be of white colour with a tala tree embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.52 \|\|

*kāmadhvaje trilohaḥ syāddaṇḍo yadukulodvaha \|*  
*patākā rohiṇī tatra makarasya samīpagā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the flag post of Kamadeva, three types of iron should be used. It should have a flag of red colour and a makara or a crocodile should be embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.53 \|\|

*māyūraṃ kārttikeyasya cihnaṃ lokeṣu gīyate \|*  
*trilohadaṇḍamārūḍhaṃ bahuratnavibhūṣitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The symbol of Karttikeya is said to be a peacock and its flag pole should also be made of three types of iron. His flag should be decorated with several gems.

## \|\| 1.138.54 \|\|

*bahuvarṇakacitrā tu patākā kathitā budhaiḥ \|*  
*hastidantabhavaṃ daṇḍaṃ kuryādgaṇapaternṛpa \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The learned people have prescribed his flag to be of different colours. O king! The flag pole of Ganapati should be made of ivory colour.

## \|\| 1.138.55 \|\|

*tāmradaṇḍaṃ samāruḍhaṃ saṃśuddhaṃ sampratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*śuklā patākā kartavyā supramāṇā mahīpate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Alternatively, a pole of mixed copper could also be made or it can be made of pure copper. O lord of earth! His flag should be of white colour with a symbol of mouse embossed over it.

## \|\| 1.138.56 \|\|

*mātṝṇāṃ cāpi kartavyo naikarūpo dhvajo budhaiḥ \|*  
*patākābhiranekābhibarhuratnābhiranvitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The people of learnings should make different types of flags for mother, which should be decorated with various types of gems for various flags.

## \|\| 1.138.57 \|\|

*revatasyāpi kartavyo dhvajo vājī narādhipa \|*  
*raktā patākā tatrāpi kartavyā yadunandana \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. O king! the flag of Revata should be embossed with the symbol of a horse. The flag should be of red colour.

## \|\| 1.138.58 \|\|

*cāmuṇḍāmandire kāryaḥ śiromālākulo dhvajaḥ \|*  
*nīlā patākā kartavyā daṇḍo lohamayastathā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In the temple of the goddess Chamunda, the flag should be of blue colour and decorated with human skulls. The flag pole should be made of iron.

## \|\| 1.138.59 \|\|

*rītīmayaśca mātṝṇāṃ revatasya ca kārayet \|*  
*gauryā dhvajastāmramayaḥ patākā gopasannibhā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The flag pole of the mothers as well as that of Revata should be made of brass. The flagstaff of Gauri should be made of copper. The flag should be of different colours resembling that of Indra. The flag should be of dark red colour.

## \|\| 1.138.60 \|\|

*svarṇadaṇḍastu vīrasya dhvajo meṣasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*patākā bahuratnāḍhye1 kartavyā yadunandana \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The flag pole of the fire god should be that of gold and the flag which should be of different colours which should be decorated with different gems.

## \|\| 1.138.61 \|\|

*aśmasāramayo daṇḍo dhvajo vātasya ucyate \|*  
*patākā kṛṣṇavarṇā tu hariṇasya samīpagā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The flag of the wind god should be that of iron and its flag should be of black colour with a stag embossed on it.

## \|\| 1.138.62 \|\|

*bhagavatyā dhvajo daṇḍaḥ sarvaratnamayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*patākā tu trivarṇā syātsiṃhasyādhogatā nṛpa \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The flag post of the goddess Bhagavati should be made of all the gems. The flag should be of three colours and a lion should be embossed over the same.

## \|\| 1.138.63 \|\|

*evaṃvidhamimaṃ kṛtvā dhvajaṃ lakṣaṇalakṣitam \|*  
*adhivāsya tato rājaṃstata āropayedbudhaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Decorating the flags with these symbols, the learned people should get them consecrated, performing the adhivasana.

## \|\| 1.138.64 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvauṣadhībhiśca snāpayitvā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*samālabhya ca badhnīyānmadhye pratisarānnṛpa \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thereafter, mixing up all the herbs, one should bathe it with delight and consecrate at the rear part of the palace.

## \|\| 1.138.65 \|\|

*kalpayitvā śubhāṃ vediṃ kalaśairupaśobhitām \|*  
*tasyāṃ vedyāṃ samāropya tāṃ rātrimadhivāsayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. A beneficial pedestal should be made, and the kaiashas (pitchers filled with water) should be placed over it. The flag should be installed in the same. Adhivasa should be performed on the same night.

## \|\| 1.138.66 \|\|

*nānākusumacitrāṃ ca srajaṃ tasyānulambayet \|*  
*samabhyarcya prayatnena dhūpamasya nivedayet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Hanging flower garlands of various types, (the flag) should be adored, offering incense to the same.

## \|\| 1.138.67-70 \|\|

*balikarma tataḥ kṛtvā kṛśarāpūpakādibhiḥ \|*  
*palālapūpikābhiśca dadhipāyasasūpakaiḥ2 \|\| 67 \|\|*

*uddiśya lokapālebhyo baliṃ dadyācca vāyasaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānsvasti vācyātha kṛtvā puṇyāhamaṅgalam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*vāditrakṛtanirghoṣaṃ jalaṃ saṃskārasaṃyutam \|*  
*nānābudbudasapannaṃ veṣṭitaṃ navavāsasā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*śubhe lagne dine ṛkṣe dhvajaṃ cāropayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*vinyasya svarṇakalaśaṃ śvabhrarājaṃ dhvajasya tu \|\| 70 \|\|*

67-70. After making the offerings, mixed food, fried cakes, curd, payasam, pulses, etc. should be distributed for the sake of the crows as well as the lokapalas. The Brahmanas should be made to recite the welfare mantras, the auspicious tunes of musical instruments should be sounded, and the rites should be performed. The flag should be decorated variously with a new cloth. It should then be installed by the learned people on an auspicious day at an auspicious time. Having been associated with the golden pitchers, the lines of the flag should be quite prominent.

## \|\| 1.138.71 \|\|

*evamāropayedyastu dhvajaṃ devālayopari \|*  
*sa śriyā vardhate nityaṃ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. A person, who installs such type of flag over the temple of a god or deity, he always meets with increase in fortunes.

## \|\| 1.138.72 \|\|

*asurā vāsamicchanti dhvajahīne surālaye \|*  
*tasmāddevālayaṃ prājño dhvajahīnaṃ na kārayet \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The temples which are without flags become the dwelling places for the Asuras. Therefore, the people of wisdom should not leave a temple without a flag.

## \|\| 1.138.73-75 \|\|

*mantraśca sthāpane prokto vidhānajñairdhvajasya tu \|*  
*ehyehi bhagavandeva devavāhana vai khaga \|\| 73 \|\|*

*śrīkaraḥ śrīnivāsaśca jaya jaitropaśobhita \|*  
*vyomarūpa mahārūpa dharmātmaṃstvaṃ ca vai gateḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*sānnidhyaṃ kuru daṇḍe'sminsākṣī ca dhruvatāṃ vraja \|*  
*kuru vṛddhiṃ sadā kartuḥ prāsādasyārkavallabha \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. The learned people have prescribed the following hymns for the installation of the flag — “O lord, O Deva! You are the one who moves in the sky. You possess all the fortunes. You are the creator of fortunes, and are the abode of Shri. You are adorned with japam and victory. You are the form of vyoma — the great form, the soul of Dharma, you are the movement. You enter this pole as a witness and become stable. O beloved of Surya, you always bestow growth and the grace on the performer.

## \|\| 1.138.76 \|\|

*oṃ ehyehi bhagavannīśvaravinirmita uparicaravāyumārgānusāriñchrīnivāsa ripudhvaṃsa \|*  
*yakṣanilaya sarvadevapriyaṃ kuru sānnidhyaṃ śānti svastyayanaṃ ca mebhayaṃ sarvavighnā vyapasarantu \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. You roam about in the upper regions created by Ishvara, you move over the path of the wind god. O lord Shrinivasa! You are the destroyer of enemies, you enter in this flag pole which is abode of the Yakshas, with all the gods and bestow peace over me, besides welfare and freedom from danger, as a result of which all the obstructions be removed.”

## \|\| 1.138.77 \|\|

*mantreṇānena rājendra śvabhre daṇḍe niveśayet \|*  
*patākāṃ pūrvamantreṇa sthityā pūrvamukho nṛpa \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Reciting this mantra together with Omkara and standing facing the east, the flag should be fixed over the flag-pole.

## \|\| 1.138.78 \|\|

*kṣipedūrdhvamathākāśaṃ prāsādaśikharādvibhoḥ \|*  
*yajamānastataḥ paśyetpatākāṃ yadunandana \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. By the grace of the competent Deva, having perched over the top of the flag post, the yajamana should have a look at it.

## \|\| 1.138.79-80 \|\|

*prāsādapurato vāpi patākāṃ pātayedyadi \|*  
*indralokaṃ tadā kartā viśedvai yadunandana \|\| 79 \|\|*

*āgneyyāmagnilokaṃ tu yāmyāṃ yamasado bhajet \|*  
*naiṛtyāṃ naiṛtaṃ lokaṃ vāruṇyaḥ vāruṇaṃ vrajet \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. If the flag flutters over the building, then the person who installs the flag, achieves Indraloka. In case, the flag flutters in the southeast, the performer achieves Agniloka; in case it flutters to the south, then he achieves the abode of Yama. In case the flag flutters to the south-west, he achieves Nairrtyaloka, and when fluttering towards the west, he earns Varunaloka.

## \|\| 1.138.81 \|\|

*yasya devasya yadveśma kṛtaṃ yadukulodvaha \|*  
*tasya lokamavāpnoti vṛṣasthānagato yadi \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The god for whom the abode is erected, by fluttering of the flag towards the place of Vrisha or bull, he earns Devaloka.

## \|\| 1.138.82 \|\|

*vāyavye vāyumāpnoti saumyāyāṃ somamāpnuyāt \|*  
*aiśānyāmīśamāpnoti kartā vai devaveśmanaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. In case, the flag flutters towards the northwest, he achieves Vayuloka; when it flutters towards the north, he achieves the place of Moon; and in case it flutters towards the northeast, he achieves the place of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.138.83-84 \|\|

*ya evaṃ kārayedbhaktyā dhvajasyāropaṇaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*sa hi bhuktvā parānbhogānsūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 83 \|\|*

*tejasāmbujasaṃkāśaḥ kāntyā cāmbujasannibhaḥ \|*  
*dvijātitulyaḥ prabhayā vikrameṇa ca gopateḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. A person, who getting filled with devotion, installs the flag like this, he achieves beauty of the lotus, lustre of a Brahmana and strength of the Sungod. Enjoying all the pleasures on earth, he goes to the solar region, where he is adequately honoured.

## Chapter 139. Arrival of Bhojakas

## \|\| 1.139.1 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*tvatprasādānmayā prāptaṃ rūpametatpurātanam \|*  
*pratyakṣadarśanaṃ cāpi bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Samba said — By your grace, I could visualize my earlier form as well as have an audience with lord Bhaskara face to face.

## \|\| 1.139.2 \|\|

*sarvametattu samprāpya punaścintākulaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*devasya paricaryāyāḥ pālanaṃ kaḥ kariṣyati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Inspite of achieving all this, my mind is worried as to who would perform puja for the Sungod?

## \|\| 1.139.3 \|\|

*guṇayuktaṃ dvijaṃ kiñcitsamarthaṃ paripālane \|*  
*mamaivānugrahādbrahmandvijaṃ vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Brahman, being graceful on me, you kindly speak out the name of a Brahmana who could be able to perform puja of the Sungod.”

## \|\| 1.139.4-5 \|\|

*evamuktastu sāmbena nāradaḥ pratyuvāca tam \|*  
*na dvijāḥ parigṛhṇanti devasya svīkṛtaṃ dhanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vidyate hi dhanaṃ hyatra guṇaścāyaṃ pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*devacaryāgatairdravyaiḥ kriyā brāhmī na vidyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. At this, Narada said to Samba — “The wealth which is meant for the god, cannot be owned by a Brahmana, because it is given in the form of charity. In case, a Brahmana accepts the riches offered to the deity as a part of the puja, the Brahmanahood of the Brahmana gets lost.

## \|\| 1.139.6 \|\|

*avajñayā ca kurvanti ye kriyāṃ lobhamohitāḥ \|*  
*apāṅkteyā bhavantīha te vai devalakā dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In case, a Brahmana disregards this process out of greed, he is fallen from the race of the Brahmanas. The Brahmanas who accept such type of offerings of riches, are called Devalakas.

## \|\| 1.139.7 \|\|

*devasvaṃ brāhmaṇatvaṃ ca yo lobhādupajīvati \|*  
*sa pāpātmā naro loke gṛdhrocchiṣṭena jīvati \|*  
*tato na brāhmaṇaḥ kaściddevacaryāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A person who, out of greed, earns his living by the offerings made to the god, he is treated as a sinful person and consumes the left over like the vultures. Therefore, no Brahmana can accept the performing of puja of a Deva temple.

## \|\| 1.139.8 \|\|

*vidhijñaṃ jñānavantaṃ ca paricaryākṣamaṃ tathā \|*  
*deva eva tamākhyātuṃ tasmāttaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Brahmanas well-versed in the scriptures, the learned, those fit for serving the deity can be declared by the Sungod alone. Therefore, you take refuge with the Sungod for the purpose.

## \|\| 1.139.9 \|\|

*athavā yaduśārdūla ugrasenapurohitam \|*  
*gatvā1 gauramukhaṃ pṛccha sa te kāmaṃ vidhāsyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Otherwise, O lion of the race of Yadus! You have a discussion with Gauramukha — the priest of Ugrasena, on this subject. He would certainly do your job.

## \|\| 1.139.10 \|\|

*nāradenaivamuktastu sāmbo jāmbavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*sukhāsīnaṃ gṛhe vīra ugrasenapurohitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At the advice of Narada, Samba — the son of Jambavati, reached the place of the priest Ugrasena, who was seated there comfortably.

## \|\| 1.139.11 \|\|

*kṛtapūrvāhṇikaṃ vīra vipraṃ gauramukhaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*vinayenopasaṅgamya sāmbo vākyamathābravīt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then Samba reached before the priest, who was seated getting free from all the religious duties. Then he prayed to him.

## \|\| 1.139.12-13 \|\|

*mayā bhānoḥ prasādena kāritaṃ vipulaṃ gṛham \|*  
*sapatnīkaṃ sasainyaṃ ca pṛthivyāṃ sāravatsthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ tasminmayā dattaṃ kṛtaṃ mūrteśca maṇḍalam \|*  
*tasmādiṣṭvā viśiṣṭebhyo deyaṃ dānaṃ manogatam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. “By the grace of the Sungod, I have built a vast Sun temple. The images of Surya and his wives have been installed therein. These are the best in the world. I have donated everything for the sake of the temple. In the yajna, I have given away all the things which are my favourite.

## \|\| 1.139.14 \|\|

*tatsarvaṃ mama samprītyā gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*sāmbavākyamidaṃ śrutvā pratyuvāca mahāmuniḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I intend to give all of them to a particular person. O great sage, be pleased with me and accept them all, exercising your grace on me.” Listening to the words of Samba, the great sage replied to Samba.

## \|\| 1.139.15 \|\|

*gauramukha uvāca \|*  
*bravīmyahamaśeṣeṇa yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ vipro bhavānrājā sa ca devaparigrahaḥ \|*  
*aparasparamevaṃ tu grahaṇaṃ me virudhyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Gauramukha said — I am going to reveal to you all the related aspects. I am a Brahmana and you are a ruler. All the riches which are meant for the god as his donations, I have no traditional association with them. Therefore, I cannot accept such things which are against my (tradition).

## \|\| 1.139.16 \|\|

*brahmavidyāpraṇītāni svakarmāṇi dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*kurvāṇā na prahīyante anyathā bhinnavṛttayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A Brahmana who earns his living by means as spelt in the Vedas, is never fallen. A Brahmana who earns his livelihood by means other than those prescribed in the Vedas, is fallen.

## \|\| 1.139.17 \|\|

*kṣāntiradhyāpanaṃ2 jāpaḥ satyaṃ ca yadunandana \|*  
*etāni viprakarmāṇi na devārthaparigrahaḥ3 \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O son of the Yadu race, the duties of the Brahmanas are — to be compassionate, to give teaching, performing of japam and to be truthful. These are the duties of the Brahmanas and not to accept the riches offered to the gods.

## \|\| 1.139.18 \|\|

*yadi devārthadānaṃ1 syāttato devalakā dvijāḥ \|*  
*devadravyābhilāṣaśca brāhmaṇyaṃ tu vimuñcati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Brahmanas who accept the riches offered to the god, are known as Devalakas. A Brahmana who desires for the riches offered to the god, gets deprived of the Brahmanahood.

## \|\| 1.139.19 \|\|

*devadvāre ca yaddānaṃ brāhmaṇāya prayacchati \|*  
*dvāvetau pāpakartārāvātmadoṣeṇa mānavau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person who gives charities to a Brahmana in a temple, both of them, the giver as well as the taker because of their respective sins, become the sinners.

## \|\| 1.139.20 \|\|

*devārthadānaṃ2 vārṣṇeya yadgṛhītvā ca yo dvijaḥ \|*  
*śrāddhe vā yadi vā satre tajjuhoti dadāti vā \|*  
*bhinna vṛtto dvijaḥ pāpo rākṣasaḥ so'bhijāyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O born of the race of Vrishni, a Brahmana, who accepting the money of the god, performs Homa or Shraddha, or gives it to others, he becomes a sinful Rakshasa because of his performing the practice, which is against Dharma.

## \|\| 1.139.21 \|\|

*dvijo devalako yatra paṅktyāṃ bhuṅkte mahīpate \|*  
*annānyupaspṛśennīcā sā paṅktiḥ pāpamācaret \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O lord of earth, a Devalaka Brahmana when takes his food seated in a line or touches the food which is to be consumed, the whole line is considered to be sinful as well as degraded.

## \|\| 1.139.22 \|\|

*dvijo devalako yasya saṃskāraṃ samprayacchati \|*  
*so'dhomukhānpitṝnsarvānākramya vinipātayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When a Devalaka Brahmana performs the religious rites, he actually attacks his own pitris and becomes the cause of their fall, head on.

## \|\| 1.139.23 \|\|

*ātmānaṃ pātayedyastu sonyānuddharate katham \|*  
*uddhariṣyati cātmānamityeṣā kalpanādhamā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Therefore, a person, who becomes the cause of his own fall, how could he redeem others? That he can redeem himself is a mere fallacy.

## \|\| 1.139.24 \|\|

*yo haṭhācca bhayāccaiva kurute raviveśmanaḥ \|*  
*vṛttiṃ vidhatte vipratvātpatitassa tu jāyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person, who being a Brahmana, becomes stubborn, greedy and accepts the subsistence out of fear, he is surely fallen.

## \|\| 1.139.25 \|\|

*sapratigrahamantreṇa dvijo'śnāti parigraham \|*  
*devapratigrahārtheṣu vedavākyaṃ na vidyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Though a Brahmana accepts the donation reciting the mantras and makes use of it, but there is no provision in the Vedas for acceptance of the riches of the gods.

## \|\| 1.139.26 \|\|

*tasmādrājā na devārthaṃ vipre dadyātkathañcana \|*  
*brahmasūtramahaṃ chittvā gamiṣyāmīti gamyatām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Therefore, a king should never give away the donations made to the god, to anyone else. “I shall be able to do so only after breaking the yajnopavita”. By so saying, in case anyone wants to do so, let him do so.

## \|\| 1.139.27 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*agrāhyaṃ ceddvijātibhyaḥ kasmai deyamidaṃ mayā \|*  
*śrutaṃ vā dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ vā tanme vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Samba said — In case my donation is not acceptable by the Brahmanas, then what should I do with the same? To whom should I give it? You kindly tell me.

## \|\| 1.139.28 \|\|

*gauramukha uvāca \|*  
*magāya samprayaccha tvaṃ purametacchubhaṃ vibho \|*  
*tasyādhikāro devānne devatānāṃ ca pūjane \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Gauramukha said — O excellent one, you give away all that to Magas, because they alone are entitled to accept the food and riches given to the gods.

## \|\| 1.139.29 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*ko'yaṃ mageti te proktāḥ kva vāsau vasate vibho \|*  
*kasya putro dvijaśreṣṭha kimācāraḥ kimākṛtiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Samba said — O excellent one, who are the Magas? Where do they live? Who are their parents? What is their conduct as well as the form?

## \|\| 1.139.30 \|\|

*gauramukha uvāca \|*  
*yo'yaṃ mageti vai prokto mago divyo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*nikṣubhāyāṃ 1 suto vīra ādityātmaja ucyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Gauramukha said — The Magas, about whom I have told you, are divine and excellent Brahmanas and they were born of Nikshubha. They are believed to be the sons of Surya.

## \|\| 1.139.31 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ sa nikṣubhāputraḥ kathaṃ vīrasutastathā \|*  
*kathaṃ cādityatanayo mago'sāvucyatena'gha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Samba said — O sinless one, how were Magas born of Nikshubha and could be the sons of Surya?

## \|\| 1.139.32 \|\|

*gauramukha uvāca \|*  
*mānuṣatvaṃ gatā devī nikṣubhā kila yādava \|*  
*gatā śāpamavāpyeha bhāskarāllokapūjitā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Gauramukha said — Goddess Nikshubha, who is adorable by the world, was born in human form, because of the curse from the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.139.33 \|\|

*gotraṃ mihiramityāhustasmai brāhmaṇyamuttamam \|*  
*sujihvā nāma dharmātmā ṛṣiputraḥ purānagha \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In earlier times, an excellent Brahmana was born in the Mihira gotra. O sinless one, a pious and virtuous Brahmana known by the name of Sujihva was born as a son of a Rishi.

## \|\| 1.139.34 \|\|

*tasyātmajā samutpannā nikṣubhā sā varāṅganā \|*  
*rūpeṇāpratimā loke hāralīlā matā tu sā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Nikshubha was born as his daughter with beautiful limbs. She was famous in the world as the garland of gems.

## \|\| 1.139.35 \|\|

*piturniyogātsā kanyā viharejjātavedasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With the permission of her father, she used to play with fire.

## \|\| 1.139.36 \|\|

*viharantī yathānyāyaṃ samiddhe pāvake tathā \|*  
*atha tāṃ devadeveśo hyaṃśumālī dadarśa ha \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thus sporting with the fire flames, she was spotted by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.139.37 \|\|

*rūpayauvanasampannāṃ tataḥ kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa deveśaḥ kathaṃ tāṃ vai bhajāmyaham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Finding the youthful maiden, the Sungod was infested with passion. Then he thought of making use of her.

## \|\| 1.139.38 \|\|

*anayāvahṛto yo'yaṃ pāvako devapūjitaḥ \|*  
*vanamāviśya tanvaṅgīṃ bhajeyaṃ lokapūjitām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He thought that she had exercised her influence over the fire god. Therefore, I shall enjoy the company of this slim girl, carrying her in the forest.

## \|\| 1.139.39 \|\|

*iti sañcintya deveśaḥ sahasrāṃśurdivaspati \|*  
*viveśa pāvakaṃ vīra tatputraścābhavattadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. With this resolve, the Sungod, with a thousand rays, entered the fire. A son was thus born to her.

## \|\| 1.139.40 \|\|

*tato vilāsalāvaṇyarūpayauvanaśālinī \|*  
*samiddhaṃ laṅghayitvāgniṃ jagāmāyatalocanā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Once the beautiful damsel with vast eyes, because of the youthful arrogance, crossed the fire flames.

## \|\| 1.139.41-43 \|\|

*kruddhaḥ svarūpamāsthāya dṛṣṭvā kanyāṃ sa pīḍitaḥ \|*  
*karaṃ kareṇa saṅgṛhya tatastāṃ havyavāhanaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*uvāca yaduśārdūla nodito bhāskareṇa tu \|*  
*vedoktaṃ vidhimutsṛjya yathāhaṃ laṃghitastvayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tasmānmattaḥ samutpanno na ca putro bhaviṣyati \|*  
*jaraśabda iti khyāto vaṃśakīrtivivardhanaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. At that point of time, the lustful Sun who had already entered the fire, getting enraged, held her hand with his own hand and said — “The Sun have not resign at that time. Disowning the provisions of the Vedas, you have crossed over me, therefore, your son, inspite of his having been born of me, cannot be called as your son. Rather he shall be known by the name of Jara.”

## \|\| 1.139.44 \|\|

*agnijātyā magāḥ proktāḥ somajātyā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*bhojakādityajātyā hi divyāste parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. And, he shall enhance the glory of his race. Accordingly, Magas of Agni race, the Brahmanas of lunar race and Bhojakas of solar race, shall be known in the world. All of them shall gain their respective glory.”

## \|\| 1.139.45 \|\|

*tāmevamuktvā bhagavānādityo'ntaratastadā \|*  
*athotpannāṃ prajāṃ jñātvā dhyānayogena vai ṛṣiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus speaking to him, the Sungod disappeared. At the same time, the Rishi also came to know by dhyana yoga about the birth of his sons.

## \|\| 1.139.46-47 \|\|

*patitaḥ syānmahātejā ṛgjihvaḥ sumahāmatiḥ \|*  
*śāpamudyamya tejasvī ṛgjihvo vākyamabravīt \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ātmāparādhātkāminyā yathā garbho nalāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*sambhūtaste mahābhāge apūjyo'yaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Learning about the factual position, the Rishi Rigjihva was fainted. Thereafter, getting enraged, he pronounced a curse — “Getting yourself lustful because of your own fault, you conceived. Therefore, the son born of you would be devoid of worship.”

## \|\| 1.139.48 \|\|

*putraśokābhisantaptā bālā paryākulekṣaṇā \|*  
*cintayāmāsa duḥkhārtā tamekaṃ jvalanākṛtim \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. At these words of the sage, the gravid lady with tears in her eyes, feeling painful thought of the fire god with flames.

## \|\| 1.139.49 \|\|

*tato devavariṣṭhasya mama yonisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ datto mahāśāpaḥ pūjyatāṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. She said — “The excellent children born of me, have been declared by the Rishi as inauspicious. Therefore, you make them auspicious.

## \|\| 1.139.50-52 \|\|

*bhavetpūjyo hi me putro deveśvara tathā kuru \|*  
*evaṃ ciṃtayamānastu bhagavānaryamā kila \|\| 50 \|\|*

*āgneyaṃ rūpamāśritya cedaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*snigdho gambhīranirghoṣaḥ śānto jvaravivarjitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ṛgjihraḥ sumahātejā dharmaṃ carati suvrata \|*  
*tenotsṛṣṭaṃ mahāśāpaṃ nānyathā kartumutsahe \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. O god of gods, you do something to make my children auspicious.” Finding her so anxious, the Sungod, taking to the form of Agni, said to her “O beloved, the Rishi Rigjihva is of deep voice, peaceful and highly illustrious. He follows Dharma. Therefore, the curse pronounced by him cannot be negated by me.

## \|\| 1.139.53 \|\|

*kiṃ tu kāryagarīyastvādātmano yogyamuttamam \|*  
*tava putraṃ vidhāsyāmi cāpūjyaṃ vedapāragam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. But because of your performing the excellent deeds, I shall make your sons excellent, competent and well-versed in the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.139.54-55 \|\|

*vaṃśaśca sumahāṃstasya nivasiṣyati bhūtale \|*  
*mamāṅgāni mahātmāno vāśiṣṭhā brahmavādinaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*madgāyanā madyajanā madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*mama śuśrūṣakāścaiva mama ca vratacāriṇaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. They shall have great family tradition over the earth. All of them shall be my limbs, great souls, shall belong to the gotra of Vasishtha, well-versed in Brahman, resembling me, full of devotion for me. They will serve me and shall follow all my traditions.

## \|\| 1.139.56 \|\|

*tvāṃ ca māṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ vedaṃ tattvārthadarśinaḥ \|*  
*pūjayiṣyanti niratāḥ sadā madbhāvabhāvitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. They will be learned in the tattvas of the Vedas, highly devoted and shall adore you and me as well.

## \|\| 1.139.57 \|\|

*matkarmaṇāṃ madaṅgānāṃ madbhāvaviniveśanāt \|*  
*virajā matprasādena māmevaiṣyantyasaṃśayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Because of this performing for me, they would be called as my parts or limbs. Because of their devotion towards me, they would surely achieve me.

## \|\| 1.139.58 \|\|

*jaṭāśmaśrudharā nityaṃ sadā mayi parāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*pañcakālavidhānajñā vīrakālasya yajvinaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Wearing the moustaches and matted locks of hair, remaining always truthful, they would be well-versed with all the five types of traditions of time. They would surely worship the time of bravery.

## \|\| 1.139.59-60 \|\|

*pūrṇekadakṣiṇe pāṇau varma vāmena dhārayan \|*  
*patidānena vadanaṃ pracchādya niyataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*prāṇaṃ hi mahatāṃ kṛtvā tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*ayamāccāprasādācca vyākulendriyacetasā \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. They would keep the right hand full and hold the weapons in the left hands. Covering their faces, becoming disciplined and purified like great personalities, they shall consume food in an appropriate manner. They would also perform irregular homos with disturbed minds and perform my yajnas without reciting of related mantras.

## \|\| 1.139.61 \|\|

*vidhihīnaṃ maṃtrahīna ye vai yakṣyanti māmataḥ \|*  
*te'pi svargāccyutāḥ klāntā ramante sūryasannidhau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Still they would be able to achieve the heaven. They would feel painful, but they shall remain with the Sungod with delight.

## \|\| 1.139.62 \|\|

*evaṃvidhāstava sutā bhaviṣyanti mahītale \|*  
*magavaṃśe mahātmāno vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. These types of your sons would start the Maga race on the earth, they shall become learned and will be well-versed in the Vedas as well as the post Vedic literature.”

## \|\| 1.139.63 \|\|

*evamāśvāsya tāṃ devīṃ bhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ \|*  
*antadardhe mahātejāḥ sā ca harṣamavāpa ha \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus assuring the goddess, the water thief and resplendent Bhaskara disappeared from the scene. The goddess also felt delighted.

## \|\| 1.139.64 \|\|

*evamete samutpannā bhojakāḥ kṛṣṇanandana \|*  
*viṣṇubhāste tathādityā utpannā lokapūjitāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. O son of Krishna! Thus, the Bhojakas having been born of the fire as well as the Sun, became illustrious like the Sun as well as Vishnu, and were respected in the world.

## \|\| 1.139.65 \|\|

*teṣāmetatpuraṃ dehi paryāptāste pratigrahe \|*  
*tvadīyasyāsya me vīra tathā bhāskarapūjane \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. These people should be made eligible for such a charity and Sun worship, because they alone are eligible to receive this charity.

## \|\| 1.139.66-67 \|\|

*tasya gauramukhasyedaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā sa yādavaḥ \|*  
*sāmbo jāmbavatīputraḥ praṇamya śirasoktavān \|\| 66 \|\|*

*kva vasante mahātmāna ete bhāskaraputrakāḥ \|*  
*bhojakā dvijaśārdūla yena tānānayāmyaham \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Listening to the words of Gauramukha, Samba — the son of Jambavati, offered his salutation, lowering his head and said — “O best of the Brahmanas, where do the Bhojakas — the sons of Bhaskara reside, so that I may go there?

## \|\| 1.139.68 \|\|

*gauramukha uvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ jāne mahābāho vasante yatra vai magāḥ \|*  
*jānīte tānravirvīra tasmāttaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Gauramukha said — O long armed one, the dwelling place of Magas is unknown to me. It is known to the Sungod alone. Therefore, you take refuge with him to get the required information.

## \|\| 1.139.69 \|\|

*brāhmaṇenaivamuktastu praṇamya śirasā ravim \|*  
*jagāda bhāskaraṃ sāmbaḥ kaste pūjāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. At these words of the Brahmana, Samba offered his salutation to the Sungod, lowering his head. Then he said to him— “Who would perform your daily puja?”

## \|\| 1.139.70 \|\|

*vijñaptastveva sāmbena pratimā tamuvāca ha \|*  
*na yogyāḥ paricaryāyāṃ jambūdvīpe mamānagha \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. At these words of Samba, the image of the Sungod spoke — “O sinless one, there is none in Jambudvipa to perform my daily puja here.

## \|\| 1.139.71-74 \|\|

*mama pūjākaraṃ gatvā śākadvīpādihānaya \|*  
*lavaṇodātpare pāre kṣīrodena samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*jambūdvīpātparo yasmācchākadvīpa iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tatra puṇyā janapadāścaturvarṇasamanvitāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*magāśca magagāścaiva gānagā1 mandagāstathā \|*  
*magā brāhmaṇabhūyiṣṭhā magagāḥ kṣatriyāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*vaiśyāstu gānagā jñeyāḥ śūdrāsteṣāṃ tu mandagāḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ saṅkaraḥ kaściddharmāśrayakṛte kvacit \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. You better bring someone from Shakadvipa to do the job. Across the ocean of saline water, the place is away from Jambudvipa. It is surrounded by the ocean of saline water and is known as Shakadvipa. Four types of people known as — Magas, Magagas, Ganagas and Mandagas live there. The best of Brahmanas are Magas, the Kshatriyas are Magagas, the Vaishyas are known as Ganagas, while Shudras are known as Mandagas. In that religious city, number of mixed caste can be found.

## \|\| 1.139.75 \|\|

*dharmasyāsya vicāro vā hyekataḥ sukhinaḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*tejasaste madīyasya nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. All the people there enter into the religious discussion, because of which the people always live there with comfort. Vishvakarma had built it out of my lustre.

## \|\| 1.139.76 \|\|

*tebhyo vedāstu catvāraḥ sarahasyā mayoditāḥ \|*  
*vedoktairvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ parairguhyairmayā kṛtaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. For those people, I had written the four Vedas with their commentators, besides the secret stotras of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.139.77-78 \|\|

*te ca dhyāyanti māmeva yajante māṃ ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*manmānasā madyajanā madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*mama śuśrūṣakāścaiva mama ca vratacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*avyaṅgadhāriṇaścaiva vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. All of them daily worship me and are devoted to me. They are my mind born sons, are my devotees and adore me. They serve me with devotion and also perform my vratas. They also wear avyaAga or sacred thread appropriately.

## \|\| 1.139.79 \|\|

*kurvanti te sadā bhadrāṃ mama pūjāṃ mamānugāḥ \|*  
*tathā devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca saha cāraṇaiḥ \|*  
*viharante ramante ca dṛśyamānāśca taiḥ saha \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. They are my followers and worship me. They are also found sporting with the Devas, Gandharvas, Siddhas and Charanas also.

## \|\| 1.139.80-81 \|\|

*jambūdvīpe tvahaṃ viṣṇurvedavedāṅgapūjitaḥ \|*  
*śakro'haṃ śālmalīdvīpe krauñcadvīpe hyahaṃ bhagaḥ1 \|\| 80 \|\|*

*plakṣadvīpe tvahaṃ bhānuḥ śākadvīpe divākaraḥ \|*  
*puṣkare ca smṛto brahmā tataścāhaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. In Jambudvipa I am adored with Vedas and post-Vedic literature as Vishnu. In the Shalmalidvipa I am adored as Indra; Shiva in Kraunchadvipa; as Sungod in Plakshadvipa; as Divakara in Shakadvipa; as Brahma in Pushkara, and as Maheshvara in Kushadvipa.

## \|\| 1.139.82 \|\|

*tānmagānmama pūjārthaṃ śākadvīpādihānaya \|*  
*āruhya garuḍaṃ sāmba śīghraṃ gatvāvicārayan \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Therefore, the Magas should be brought here from Shakadvipa. O Samba! You should proceed, mounted on Garuda quite quickly. There is no need for hesitation or thinking.

## \|\| 1.139.83 \|\|

*tatheti gṛhya tāmājñāṃ raverjāmbavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*punardvāravatīṃ gatvā kāntyātīva samanvitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Then Samba — the son of Jambavati, obeying the command of the Sungod, proceeded on to the city of Dvaravati.

## \|\| 1.139.84 \|\|

*ākhyātavānpituḥ sarvaṃ svakīyaṃ devadarśanam \|*  
*tasmācca garuḍaṃ labdhvā yayau sāmbo'dhiruhya tam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Reaching there, he narrated the event of his having an audience with the Sungod. Thus, mounted over Garuda, Samba started for Shakadvipa.

## \|\| 1.139.85 \|\|

*śākadvīpamanuprāpya samprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*tatrāpaśyadyathoddiṣṭānsāmbastejasvino magān \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Reaching there, he met the Magas who worshipped the Sungod offering the incense, lamp etc. Observing this, he felt delightful and I his hair stood at end.

## \|\| 1.139.86 \|\|

*vivasvantaṃ pūjayanto dhūpadīpādibhiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*so'bhivādya ca tānpūrvaṃ kṛtvāpyeṣāṃ pradakṣiṇām \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Initially, he circumambulated the Magas, thereafter, he honoured them.

## \|\| 1.139.87 \|\|

*pṛṣṭvā cānāmayaṃ teṣāṃ praśaṃsāsāmapūrvakam \|*  
*yūyaṃ hi puṇyakarmāṇo draṣṭavyārthe śubhārthinaḥ \|*  
*ratā ye'rkasya pūjāyāṃ yeṣāṃ caiva varapradaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. After peacefully enquiring about their welfare, he praised them saying that they were quite auspicious and were desirous of the visible things. The one who is devoted to the Sungod, the lord surely bestows boons to him.

## \|\| 1.139.88 \|\|

*tanayaṃ vitta māṃ viṣṇoḥ sāmbaṃ nāmnā ca viśrutam \|*  
*candrabhāgātaṭe cāpi mayā sūryo niveśitaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. “I am the son of Vishnu (Krishna) and my name is Samba. I consecrated the image of Surya over the bank of Chandrabhaga river.

## \|\| 1.139.89 \|\|

*tenāhaṃ preṣitaścātra uttiṣṭhadhvaṃ vrajāmahe \|*  
*te tamūcustataḥ sāmbamevametanna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. It is he who has deputed me to this place. Therefore, all of you should get up and accompany me to my place.” At these words of Samba, they also spoke similarly to him. They said — “The things are like that. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.139.90 \|\|

*asmākamapi devena vyākhyātāṃ pūrvameva hi \|*  
*aṣṭādaśa kulānīha magānāṃ vedavādinām \|*  
*yāsyanti ye tvayā sārdhaṃ yathā devena bhāṣitam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. We had already been informed by the Sungod about it. Therefore, the eighteen races of Maghas shall accompany you.”

## \|\| 1.139.91 \|\|

*tatastāni daśāṣṭau ca kulānīha samantataḥ \|*  
*āropya garuḍe sāmbastvaritaḥ punarabhyagāt \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Thereafter, Samba, accompanied with eighteen families of Magas and seated over Garuda, returned to his place without delay.

## \|\| 1.139.92-93 \|\|

*so'lpenaiva tu kālena prāpto mitravanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*kṛtvājñāṃ tu raveḥ sāmbaḥ kṛtsnaṃ tvevaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 92 \|\|*

*raviḥ śobhanamityuktvā prasannaḥ sāmbamabravīt \|*  
*mama pūjākarā hyete prajānāṃ śāntikārakāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. Obeying the command of the Sungod, he went to Mitravana and apprised the Sungod of the factual position. The Sungod said — “It is very well done.” Then delightfully, he spoke to him — “These people are required to worship me.”

## \|\| 1.139.94 \|\|

*mama pūjāṃ kariṣyanti vidhānoktāṃ yadūttama \|*  
*tatkṛte na punaścintā tava kācidbhaviṣyati \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. O best of the race of Yadu, they will worship appropriately and you will never have to be worried about the same.

## Chapter 140. Creation of Bhojakas

## \|\| 1.140.1-2 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa ānayitvā tu magānsāmbo mahīpate \|*  
*sa mahātmā purā sāmbaścandrabhāgāsarittaṭe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*puraṃ niveśayāmāsa sthāpayitvā divākaram \|*  
*kṛtvā dhanasamṛddhaṃ tu bhojakānāṃ samarpayat \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sumantu said — O king, Samba brought the Magas from the Shakadvipa and lodged them in the city he had built over the bank of the river Chandrabhaga. The image of Surya had been consecrated therein. It was given over to the Bhojakas.

## \|\| 1.140.3 \|\|

*tatpuraṃ savituḥ puṇyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*sāṃbena kāritaṃ yasmāttasmātsāmbapuraṃ smṛtam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The auspicious city of the Sungod is well known in the universe, which had been built by Samba and was therefore, known by the name of Sambapura.

## \|\| 1.140.4 \|\|

*tasminpratiṣṭhito devaḥ puramadhye divākaraḥ \|*  
*satkṛtya sthāpitāḥ sarve ātmanāmāṅkite pure \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the centre of the city, the image of the Sungod has been consecrated. Samba also rehabilitated the Magas in the city, which was known after his name.

## \|\| 1.140.5-7 \|\|

*magānāṃ tu sadācāro dṛṣṭācārakulocitaḥ \|*  
*devaśuśrūṣaṇaṃ gītaṃ vedaproktena karmaṇā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kṛtakṛtyastadā sāmbo varaṃ labdhvā punaryuvā \|*  
*ādidevaṃ surajyeṣṭhamādityaṃ praṇipatya saḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*anantaraṃ magānsarvānpraṇipatyābhivādya ca \|*  
*prasthito nirmalaḥ sāmbaḥ purīṃ dvāravatīṃ tadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. The etiquette and conduct of Magas, besides their family traditions were performed by them according to the Vedas. Observing the worship of the Sungod, Samba was overwhelmed. He attained the birth of this getting back his youthful life. He offered his salutation to the Sungod besides all other gods. Then he welcomed humbly all the Magas and getting purified, he again returned to the city of Dvaravati.

## \|\| 1.140.8 \|\|

*magānāṃ kāraṇārthena prārthitā bhojavaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*vasudevasya pautreṇa gotrajena mahātmanā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then Samba — the grandson of Vasudeva, prayed to the families of Bhoja families, for marriage with Maga families.

## \|\| 1.140.9-10 \|\|

*kanyādānaṃ kṛtaṃ teṣāṃ magānāṃ bhojakottamaiḥ \|*  
*sarvāstāḥ sahitāḥ kanyāḥ pravālamaṇibhūṣitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*arcayitvā tu tāḥ sarvāḥ preṣitāḥ saviturgṛham \|*  
*punargatvā tu sāṃbena pṛṣṭo devo divākaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. After duly performing kanyadana, Bhojakas also gave away their girls to Magas in marriage. All the girls were adorned with coral and gems and were sent to the Sun temple.

## \|\| 1.140.11 \|\|

*magānāṃ jñānamākhyāhi1 vedānavyaṅgameva ca \|*  
*sāmbasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bhāskaro vākyamabravīt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Once Samba went to the temple and asked the Sungod as to how the knowledge of the Vedas could be completed? On hearing the words of Samba, the Sungod said.

## \|\| 1.140.12 \|\|

*pṛccha tvaṃ nāradaṃ gatvā sa te sarvaṃ vadiṣyati \|*  
*evamukto'tha vai sāmbo gatavānnāradaṃ prati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “You better go to Narada and ask him about it. He will enlighten you on the whole matter.” When so advised by the Sungod, Samba went to Narada.

## \|\| 1.140.13 \|\|

*gatvā kṛtsnamidaṃ sarvaṃ tasmai tena niveditam \|*  
*sa cāpyāha tataḥ sāmbaṃ na jāne jñānamuttamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Reaching there, he enquired of him everything. Then, Narada said — “O Samba, I am not aware of the knowledge of Bhojakas.

## \|\| 1.140.14 \|\|

*bhojakānāṃ yaduśreṣṭha jñānaṃ vyāso mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*taṃ gatvā paripṛccha tvaṃ praṇamya śirasā munim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O best of the race of Yadus, this information is known to the sage Vyasa. Therefore, you go to the adorable sage Vyasa and find out the facts from him, offering salutation to him.

## \|\| 1.140.15-16 \|\|

*kṛṣṇānurodhātte sarvaṃ sa vakṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nāradenaivamuktastu sāmbo jāmbavatīsutaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vyāsāśramaṃ sa gatvā tu praṇamya śirasā munim \|*  
*kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. At the instance of lord Krishna, he would reveal everything to you. There is no doubt about it.” At these words of Narada, Samba — the son of Jambavati, reached the hermitage of the sage Vyasa. Then offering his salutation to him with folded hands, he said to the sage Vyasa.

## \|\| 1.140.17-19 \|\|

*śākadvīpaṃ mayā gatvā ānītā magapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*bālā yauvanasampannāḥ sanniviṣṭā magottamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*satkṛtya pūjayitvā tu puraṃ teṣāṃ samarpitam \|*  
*samprāpya tu puraṃ te vai jyeṣṭhamadhyakanīyasaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhojavaṃśasamutpannāḥ kanyakāḥ samalaṅkṛtāḥ \|*  
*varayitvā kṛtaṃ teṣāṃ viprapraṇayanaṃ śubham \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. “I brought the Magas from Shakadvipa and have honourably rehabilitated them here in a city, which has been dedicated to them. O Brahmana, becoming the dwellers of that city, those who are seniors, of middle age or juniors, have been married with the daughters of the Bhoja family.

## \|\| 1.140.20 \|\|

*aho sabhāgyāḥ ślāghyāśca kṛtapuṇyāśca te sadā \|*  
*pūjāyāṃ ye ratā bhānoryeṣāṃ caiva varapradaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is surprising that getting engaged in the worship of the Sungod, they have become virtuous, praiseworthy and auspicious. The Sungod showers all types of boons on them.

## \|\| 1.140.21 \|\|

*paryāptaṃ sarvameteṣāmiha cāmuṣmikaṃ phalam \|*  
*anitye sati mānuṣye devapūjāratā hi ye \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The human bodies are perishable and realising this, these people always worship the Sungod. Therefore, they have achieved sufficient merits of the present as well as the future world.

## \|\| 1.140.22 \|\|

*kintu cintayataḥ sūryaṃ cintayitvā tu bhojakān \|*  
*jñānaṃ prati tathā caiṣāṃ hadaye saṃśayo mama \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thinking about the Sungod, I am more and more worried about the Bhojakas. How could we know about the source of their origin?

## \|\| 1.140.23 \|\|

*kathaṃ pūjākarā hyete ke magāḥ ke ca bhojakāḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ kiṃ paramaṃ teṣāṃ jñeyasteṣāṃ ka eva tu \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I have developed a great doubt in regard to the origin of Magas and the Bhojakas. Who are they? What is their excellent knowledge? What more is to be known about them?

## \|\| 1.140.24 \|\|

*divyeti te kathaṃ proktāḥ kimarthaṃ kūrcadhāraṇam \|*  
*sauravrataṃ kimarthaṃ tu vācakāste kathaṃ smṛtāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Why are they known as divine? Why do they preserve beard? Why do they fast for the Sungod alone? Why are they called as the reciters?

## \|\| 1.140.25 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ tejasā vedāngāyantaścaiva te katham \|*  
*athāhikañcukasyāṅgaṃ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ ca kasya vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Why do they illuminate the Vedas with their own lustre? Who do they wear the kavachas of Surya? What is the evidence in support of the same?

## \|\| 1.140.26 \|\|

*kasya vai kā samākhyātā yadutpannaṃ kathaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*kathaṃ devāṃśca gāyanti yajñaṃ kurvanti te katham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. What is their source of origin? Who is the father of their mother? Why are they known as having been born in the race of Yadus?

## \|\| 1.140.27 \|\|

*agnihotraṃ ca kiṃ teṣāṃ pañca dolāśca kāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samākhyāhi bhojakānāṃ viceṣṭitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. What is the system of their homa? What are their five periods? Kindly enlighten me on all these aspects of the Bhojakas.”

## \|\| 1.140.28 \|\|

*sāmbasya vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ \|*  
*kālīsuto mahātejā uvāca paramaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Listening to these words of Samba, the immensely illustrious son of Kālī, known as Krishnadvaipayana Vyasa, spoke with excellent speech.

## \|\| 1.140.29 \|\|

*sādhusādhu yaduśreṣṭha sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi suvrata \|*  
*durjñeyaceṣṭitaṃ kiñcidbhojakānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Vyasa said — “You are not only a saintly person, but a great saintly person. You have put up an extremely nice question. The above information about the Bhojakas can be known with great difficulty. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.140.30 \|\|

*bhāskarasya prasādena mamāpi smṛtimāgatam \|*  
*yathākhyātaṃ vaśiṣṭhena tathā te vacmi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By the grace of the Sungod, I have also recollected all the information. I am repeating to you in the same way as Vasishtha had told the same to me in earlier times.

## \|\| 1.140.31-32 \|\|

*magānāṃ caritaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ kṛṣṇanandana \|*  
*jñānavedina evaite karmayogaṃ samāśritāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śrūyante ṛṣayaḥ sarve maunena niyamasthitāḥ \|*  
*bhuñjate cāpi maunena sarve vai paramarṣayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. O son of Krishna! The story of the origin of Magas is worth knowing. Therefore, you listen from me. They are learned, the great performers and follow the rules silently. They also take food silently.

## \|\| 1.140.33 \|\|

*municaryākṛtaste'pi śākadvīpanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*tasmānmaunena bhoktavyamaguṇatvamanicchatā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Even while living in Shakadvipa, they conduct themselves like the sages and also take food silently. It is a matter of principle with them. They do not follow the useless rulers.

## \|\| 1.140.34 \|\|

*vacaḥ sūryasamākhyātaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca varaṃ tathā \|*  
*arcāyāṃ te ca te nityamarcayantaśca te smṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They have followed the words of the Sungod beside, receiving his boons. The Sungod is their main cause to whom they worship daily.

## \|\| 1.140.35-36 \|\|

*bhojakanyāsujātatvādbhojakāstena te smṛtāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ yathā prokto vedāścatvāra eva tu \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ṛgvedo'tha yajurvedaḥ sāmavedastvatharvaṇaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇoktāstathā vedā magānāmapi suvrata \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Since they were born of the daughter of Bhojakas, they are known as Bhojakas. As the commentary on the four Vedas has been made for the Brahmanas, similarly, Brahma had established the Vedas for the Magas.

## \|\| 1.140.37-38 \|\|

*ta eva viparītāstu teṣāṃ vedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*vedo viśvamadaścaiva vidvadvahnirasastathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vedā hyete magānāṃ tu purovāca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*magā vedamadhīyante vedāṅgāstena te smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. These Vedas have different methods and are meant for Magas alone. These are known by the names of Vishvamada, Vidvad and Vahnirasa. These are the Vedas which are meant for Magas as per the desire of Prajapati. Magas study the Vedas, therefore they are known as Vedangas.

## \|\| 1.140.39 \|\|

*śeṣo na hi mahābhāgaḥ sarvasattvasukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*sasūryarathamāsādya rathibhiḥ saha varṣati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. These virtuous scriptures bestow welfare on all. They travel with the Sungod in his chariot and drop rain of his rays.

## \|\| 1.140.40 \|\|

*yastasya tu punarmokaṃ sa raverhi mahānakaḥ \|*  
*vanditavyo magānāṃ tu astramantreṇa nityaśaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Their skin is a kavacha for the Sungod, which is always adorable by the Magas.

## \|\| 1.140.41-42 \|\|

*yathā srajo dvijānāṃ tu pūjākāle pramīyate \|*  
*sarvasaṃskārayajñeṣu yathā darbhā dvijātiṣu \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pavitrāḥ kīrtitāsteṣāṃ tathā dharmo magasya tu \|*  
*ebhirjayanti bhūyiṣṭhaṃ tasmindvīpe magādhipāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. As during the performing of the religious rites by the Brahmanas, kusha is treated as quite auspicious, similarly, Dharma for the Magas has been defined. In the said land, the lord of Magas becomes victorious.

## \|\| 1.140.43 \|\|

*vidyāvantaḥ kulaśreṣṭhāḥ śaucācārasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*yajñāvasaktā1 bhaktāśca japanto mantramāditaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. They are always learned, born in high race, they are auspicious and have noble character, besides being devotees and the performers of the yajnas. They recite the mantras of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.140.44 \|\|

*priyāstu yaduśārdūla bhojakā yadunandana \|*  
*astramiva vai mantro vedasya paripaṭhyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O lion of the Yadu race, the Bhojakas are the favourites of the Sungod, because they are weapons or like the Vedic hymns for him.

## \|\| 1.140.45-46 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu sāvitrī parikalpyate \|*  
*asmākaṃ tu yaduśreṣṭha mahāvyāhṛtipūrtikā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*amohakenātha vimānabhuñjī maunena caivāpi yathā hi yuktam \|*  
*na cāpi kiñcitsmṛtikaṃ spṛśecca taccāpi nātraiva ca saṃspṛśeddhi \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. They say that as Savitri is concerned for the Brahmanas, similarly, we people, associating ourselves with bhu, bhuva and svah (or upper regions) it becomes the Surya — mantra for us with the serpent skin. We take our food silently. This is the rule for us. They do not touch the dead body or any other inauspicious things. Other people should also not touch them.

## \|\| 1.140.47-48 \|\|

*śvasantyanicchaṃstu parikṣipettu svābhīṣṭasūryaṃ tu nametsadaiva \|*  
*yathā yajñaṃ hi mantreṇa vedaproktena karmaṇā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tattvamanyanmagānāntu vidhimantrapuraskṛtam \|*  
*haviḥ sampadyate yasmāttena te yajvinaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. As the breathing takes place without anyone’s wanting, similarly, they always adore their family god Surya. As the yajna is performed as per the provision of the Vedic hymns, similarly, the Magas chiefs perform the Surya yajnas using the Vedic hymns. They are therefore known as Yajnikas.

## \|\| 1.140.49 \|\|

*yathāgnihotraṃ prathitaṃ dvijānāṃ tathādhvahotraṃ vihitaṃ magānām \|*  
*acchaṃ ca nāmeti tadadhvarasya munervaco nātra vicāraṇāsti \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. As the performing of homa in fire is prescribed for the Brahmanas, similarly, for the Magas Adhvahotra has been prescribed. The name of their yajna is known as Accha. Therefore, there is no need to think about their performance.

## \|\| 1.140.50 \|\|

*pañcadhūpāḥ pradātavyāḥ siddhirasyeha sarvadā \|*  
*daṇḍanāyakavele dve trisandhyaṃ bhāskarasya tu \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The offering of incense to Sungod five times, has been prescribed (for them). Those who perform accordingly, they always achieve success. At the time of Dandanayaka, incense should be offered twice.”

## Chapter 141. Bhojakas Race

## \|\| 1.141.1 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*bhojakānāṃ yattvayoktamavyaṅgo dehaśodhakaḥ \|*  
*vratabandhastvasau proktasteṣāṃ jātiśca kā smṛtā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Samba said — You have spoken about the means for the Bhojakas to keep their bodies purified and the rites about their yajnopavita. Now you speak out about their castes.

## \|\| 1.141.2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*te pṛṣṭā bhavatā sarve bhojakānāṃ kumārakāḥ \|*  
*kimākhyātaṃ tatastaistu tadevācakṣva kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Vyasa said — What reply was given by the Bhojaka boys to you when you asked them same questions? You speak out the whole of it

## \|\| 1.141.3 \|\|

*sāmba uvāca \|*  
*sanniveṣā mayā proktā bhojakānāṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*mamaiva brūta tattvaṃ tadvarṇaḥ ko'tra kathaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Samba said — Entering the group of Bhojaka boys, I asked them — “You tell me the caste to which each one of you belongs and where do you live?”

## \|\| 1.141.4-6 \|\|

*tatastu bhagavānprāha vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*ye tvayoktā śrutāḥ sāmba bhojakānāṃ kumārakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mamaivaite magā jñeyā aṣṭau śūdrā madaṅgajāḥ \|*  
*etadbuddhvā tu vacanaṃ praṇamya śirasā ravim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dattā bhojakulotpannā daśabhyo daśakanyakāḥ \|*  
*tatastu mandakebhyo'pi dattāścāṣṭau hi kanyakāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Thereafter, lord Surya, who is well-versed in speech, said — “O Samba, out of the Bhojaka boys who have been questioned by you, ten of them have been born out of my own limbs, while other eight, though have also been born out of my body, but they are Shudras.” Knowing about it, I offered my salutation to him lowering my head and said — “Ten girls for the high caste Bhojakas have been provided, while eight girls of low caste have been provided for the shudra Bhojakas.

## \|\| 1.141.7-9 \|\|

*tato niveśitaṃ teṣāṃ mayā sāmba puraṃ smara \|*  
*dāsakanyāstu yāścāṣṭau bhojakanyāśca yā daśa \|\| 7 \|\|*

*etāsteṣāṃ kumārāṇāṃ jñeyāstā daśa cāṣṭa ca \|*  
*tatra te bhojakanyāsu dvijairutpāditāḥ sutāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhojakāstāngaṇānprāhurbrāhmaṇāndivyasaṃjñitān \|*  
*dāsakanyāsu ye jātā mandagairantyasaṃjñitaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Thereafter, the city in which I have rehabilitated them is known as Sambapura. Eight slave girls and ten Bhojaka girls had been given to the boys, as their wives. Living toe, the Bhojaka boys had produced sons out of the Bhojaka girls, who are called the divine Bhojaka Brahmanas. Similarly, the sons born out of the slave girls, are called Mandagas.

## \|\| 1.141.10-11 \|\|

*madaṅgā nāma te jñeyāḥ savituḥ paricārakāḥ \|*  
*te ca viprapure tasminputradāraśubhairvṛtāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*svadharmairyaṣṭumārabdhaiḥ śākadvīpe'rcito raviḥ \|*  
*nānāvidhairvaidikaistu mantrairmunivarottamāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Those who serve the Sungod are known as Mandagas. O Brahmanas! Those people, also with their sons and daughters, living in the city of Shakadvipa, perform the yajnas for the Sungod, which they had already started.

## \|\| 1.141.12-14 \|\|

*avyaṅgadhāriṇo martyāḥ pūjayante divaspatim \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā vyaṅgaṃ tu vai teṣāṃ kautūhalasamanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sāmbaḥ prāha namaskṛtya bhūyaḥ satyavatīsutam \|*  
*kathaṃ varo'yamavyaṅgaḥ kathito munisattama \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kuta eṣa samutpannaḥ kasmācca sa śuciḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bandhanīyaḥ kadā cāyaṃ kimarthaṃ caiva dhāryate \|*  
*kiṃ pramāṇaṃ ca bhagavanvyaṅgaścāyaṃ kimucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. The people wearing avyanga (girdle), worship the Sungod. Therefore, finding the people using avyanga (girdle), Samba was surprised. Therefore, he asked about the same from Vyasa — the son of Satyavati, offering iris salutation to him— “O great sage, why is avyanga (girdle) considered to be the best? Where did it originate? How was it sanctified? When should it be tied? Why do the people use it? What is the size of (girdle) avyanga?

## \|\| 1.141.15 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ vyāso jāmbavatyāḥ sutasya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Sumantu said — Listening to the talk of Samba — the son of Jambavati, Vyasa — the son of Kali, said.

## \|\| 1.141.16-17 \|\|

*uvāca kuruśārdūla sāmbaṃ kālīsutaḥ sa tu \|*  
*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*etacca me yathoktastvaṃ jātireṣāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*avyaṅgasyāpi te vacmi lakṣaṇaṃ gadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Vyasa said — O lion of Kuru race, I have explained to you about their caste quite well. Now, I describe the details about (girdle) avyanga.

## Chapter 142. Genesis of Avyanga

## \|\| 1.142.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*devatā ṛṣayo nāgā gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*yakṣarakṣāṃsi vai bhānau nivasanti ṛtukramāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said — According to the seasons, all the gods, Rishis, serpents, Gandharvas, Apsaras Yakshas and Rakshasas, accompany the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.142.2-5 \|\|

*tatra tu vāsukirhyabdamudyatsūryarathaṃ javāt \|*  
*svasthānamājagāmāśu namaskṛtya divākaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*avyaṅgameva sūryāya prītyarthaṃ vai samarpayat \|*  
*gāṅgeyabhūṣitaṃ divyaṃ nātiraktasitaṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*babandha taṃ ca tatprītyai madhyabhāge tamātmanaḥ \|*  
*nāgarājāṅgasambhūto dhṛto yasmācca bhānunā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tattasmāddhāryate sūryaprītyai tadbhaktimicchatā \|*  
*vidhānena ca tattvena śucirbhavati bhojakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. The serpent Vasuki is included in these, who keep on moving with the speed of the chariot approaching the end of the year. Arriving at the appropriate time, Vasuki offered salutation to the Sungod and atonce he wanted to took his seat, offering a girdle to him. That is called avyanga or a girdle. It is made of gold, besides being divine and glittering. It was not of dark red colour, but was auspicious. The Sungod, expressing his delight, bound it around his waist. The girdle had emerged out of the body of the serpent, and the Sungod wore it around his waist. The devotees of the Sungod also use it, while Bhojakas feel delighted by wearing it.

## \|\| 1.142.6-7 \|\|

*nityaṃ ca dhāraṇāttasya bhavetprīto divākaraḥ \|*  
*na dhārayanti ye tvevaṃ bhojakāḥ pūjakāḥ raveḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saurahīnā na te yājyā ucchiṣṭā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*smṛtyācāre te hi bhagnā raviṃ nārhanti pūjitum \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. By wearing it daily, the Sungod gets pleased. If a Bhojaka does not wear the girdle at the time of worship, he is deprived of the devotion of the Sungod and other religious rites. Thus having been discarded, he becomes unfit for the puja of the Sungod. He even falls from noble conduct and becomes unfit to perform puja of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.142.8 \|\|

*pūjayanto raviṃ te hi narakaṃ yānti rauravam \|*  
*na vai hasenna uttiṣṭhedyāvadarcā labhanti te \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Inspite of that, if he still worships the Sungod, then he falls in a terrific hell. Leaving aside the pleasure of the Sungod with his devotion, he even does not move from his place.

## \|\| 1.142.9-10 \|\|

*itthaṃ jñātvā na sandeho hyavyaṅgena vinā raviḥ \|*  
*nāgarājasya saṃspṛṣṭo hyārasustena saṃsmṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ekavarṇaḥ sa kartavyaḥ kāryasiddhikarastathā \|*  
*pramāṇenāṅgulānāṃ tu śatāddhi śatamuttaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Therefore, one should not worship the Sungod without a girdle deliberately. The girdle resembling that of Vasuki, should be of one colour, which ensures success in one’s task. It is made in the size of one to a hundred angulas.

## \|\| 1.142.11 \|\|

*utkṛṣṭo'yaṃ pramāṇena madhyamo viṃśaduttaraḥ \|*  
*śatamaṣṭottaraṃ hrasvo na tu hrasvatarastataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It is claimed to be the best of evidence. The girdle of a hundred and twenty angulas is considered to be of medium type, while that of a hundred and eight angulas is considered to be of small size. The girdle should never be smaller than this.

## \|\| 1.142.12 \|\|

*tadākṛtiḥ kṛtaścaiṣa nirmito viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*madhyame bhojakānāṃ tu paraḥ śata udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It should be of the same type as was initially made by Vishvakarma. For Bhojakas, a girdle of a hundred angulas has been considered to be of medium type.

## \|\| 1.142.13 \|\|

*saṃskṛto'pi vinā tena śucirnaiva bhavatyuta \|*  
*tenāsya dhāraṇādvīra śucireva tadā bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the time of the performing of the religious rites of the Bhojakas, one cannot be considered as having been purified without wearing it. Therefore, in order to purify oneself, the girdle must be worn.

## \|\| 1.142.14-17 \|\|

*havirhomādikāḥ sarvā bhavantyasya kriyāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*avyaṅgaḥ patitāṅgaśca avyaṅgo'tha mahīpate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*eṣa sāraśca sā ramyā vai jñeyā jayanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*aheraṅgātsamutpanno hyavyaṅgastu tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yasmādasmādaheraṅgamavyaṅgastena cocyate \|*  
*arheti pūjāyāṃ dhātoḥ pratyayo ṇvultataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pūjitaśca pavitraśca yasmāttenārhakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sārasārtaḥ smṛtaṃ rūpaṃ pradhānaṃ sāra ucyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. All the rites like the performing of homa etc. could be successful only after wearing the girdle. O lord of earth, avyanga (or girdle) is also known by the names of patitanga and sara avyanga. They all bestow success or victory. If emerged out of the body of the snake, it is called avyanga. The Arha root is meant for adoration. Out of the word Sarasarta, the word sara emerges.

## \|\| 1.142.18-19 \|\|

*ṣaṇa bhaktau smṛtau dhātustasmātsārasanaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yasmādarcitamevaṃ tu suvarṇamaṇimauktikaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sa jñeyaḥ patitāṅgastu nityayajñairupāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*ityete kathitā vīra avyaṅgā vyaṅgabhojakāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The word Sara is also used for devotion. Since the girdle is made of gold and is decorated with gems and beads, it becomes auspicious. When it gets patronised in the yajnas, it is known as Patitanga. This has been termed as essential for the Bhojakas.

## \|\| 1.142.20-23 \|\|

*ṛddhivṛddhikaro nityaṃ kāyaśuddhikarastathā \|*  
*sarvavedamayaścāyaṃ sarvadevamayastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarvabhūtamayaḥ sāmba sarvalokamayastathā \|*  
*madhye'sya saṃsthito brahmā mūle viṣṇurmahāmate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śaśāṅkamaulirantye tu saṃsthito yadunaṃdana \|*  
*ṛgvedo'sya sthito mūle yajurvedo'sya madhyagaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*agre sthitaḥ sāmavedo granthirāṅgirasonagha \|*  
*pṛthvī mūlamāśritya sthitā ca yadusattama \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23. It bestows prosperity, success, besides purifying the body. It represents all the Vedas and the deities. It should also be taken to represent all the bhutas and all the lokas of the universe. Brahma is lodged in the middle of it, Vishnu at the start and the son of the race of Yadus at the base, while Shiva is lodged at the end. Further, Rigveda at its root, Yajurveda at the foremost and Samaveda at the end.

## \|\| 1.142.24 \|\|

*mūlāśanāstvapaḥ sāmba madhye devo vibhāvasuḥ \|*  
*tāsāmanantaraṃ vāta ākāśo'gre samāsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Samba! The Sungod had created water in the middle of it. Besides them, the wind god and the sky are also lodged in the forefront.

## \|\| 1.142.25 \|\|

*mūle sthitastu bhūrloko bhuvarlokastu madhyagaḥ \|*  
*svarlokaścāgramāśritya sthito vyaṅgasya yāvatā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Bhuloka is at the root, Bhuvarloka in the middle and the Svarloka is in the forefront of the girdle.

## \|\| 1.142.26 \|\|

*evaṃ devamayaḥ sāṃba evaṃ lokamayastathā \|*  
*dhāraṇīyo mahānbhaktyā pūjakaḥ prītaye raveḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It represents the gods as well as the lokas. Therefore, those who worship in order to please the Sungod, should wear the girdle making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.142.27 \|\|

*pūjayanti raviṃ ye vai vinānena yadūttama \|*  
*pūjāphalaṃ na teṣāṃ syānnarakaṃ ca vrajanti hi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Those who worship the Sungod, without wearing it, they not only are deprived of the merits of their devotion, rather they fall in the hell.

## \|\| 1.142.28-29 \|\|

*tathā teṣāṃ bhavennityamavyaṅgo bhojakaḥ sadā \|*  
*anyakāle yaduśreṣṭha ityetatkathitaṃ tava \|\| 28 \|\|*

*bandhane kāraṇaṃ vīra bhūṣaṇāni ca suvrata \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Therefore, the Bhojakas should always war the girdle, but not with impurity. I have thus spoken about the importance of wearing the girdle. The limbs of the body are bound with the ornaments, similarly, the girdle too binds the limbs of the body.

## Chapter 143. Offering of incense etc.

## \|\| 1.143.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*śrutvaivameva sāmbena vyāsātsatyavatīsutāt \|*  
*avyaṅgasya ca utpattiṃ punarāgānmahāmatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — Thus listening to the origin of the girdle from Vyasa — the son of Satyavati, the wise Samba returned to his abode from that place.

## \|\| 1.143.2-7 \|\|

*athāgatya mahātejāḥ sāmbo gatvāśramaṃ punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nāradasya mahābāhornāradaṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*kathamutkṣipya vai dhūpaṃ bhojakaiḥ saviturmune \|\| 3 \|\|*

*snānamācamanaṃ caivamarghyadānaṃ mahātmane \|*  
*sāmbasya vacanaṃ śrutvā nārado munisattamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*uvāca kuruśārdūla sāmbaṃ jāmbavatīsutam \|*  
*hanta te kathayiṣyāmi raverdhūpavidhikramam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*snānamācamanaṃ caiva svarṇadānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ācāntastristataḥ snātvā vāsasī nirmale śubhe \|\| 6 \|\|*

*anārdre saṃvasītaiva pavitre paridhāya ca \|*  
*udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vāpyācāmecca prayatnataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. Thereafter, the immensely illustrious Samba, went again to the ashrama of Narada and said to him — “O Sage, you tell me as to how the Bhojakas should offer incense, bath, sipping of water and arghya to the Sungod?” Listening to the words of Samba, Narada — the best of the sages, then spoke to the son of Jambavati, O lion of the Kuru race! I am going to reveal to you the process of offering incense, bathing, sipping and donating of gold for the Sungod. You please listen. A person should resort to sipping thrice and then take bath with spotless water. Then, he should wipe out his body and hands with dry cloth and then wear pavitris or rings of kusha grass. Then, facing north or east, he should sip the water.

## \|\| 1.143.8 \|\|

*jale jalastho nācāmejjalāduttīrya yatnataḥ \|*  
*apsu sūryastathāgniśca mātā devī sarasvatī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Standing in the water, the sipping should not be done, because the Sungod, Agni and the goddess Sarasvati always remain present in water.

## \|\| 1.143.9-10 \|\|

*tasmāduttīrya cācāmennācāmettu jalāśaye \|*  
*upaviśya śucau deśe prayataḥ prāgudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pādau prakṣālya hastau ca antarjānustathācamet \|*  
*prasannāstriḥ pibettvāpaḥ prayataḥ susamāhitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Therefore, the sipping should be done out of the river or tank water and not in it. Seated at any auspicious place, facing east or north, hands, feet and the knees could be washed. Thereafter, he should delightfully do the sipping of water thrice.

## \|\| 1.143.11 \|\|

*sammārjanaṃ tu dviḥ kuryāttribhirabhyukṣaṇaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*mūrdhānaṃ khāni cātmānamupaspṛśyānu pūrvaśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should sprinkle water over himself twice. He should sip the water thrice. Then he should touch with his right hand his head, ears, nose, eyes and all other parts of the body.

## \|\| 1.143.12 \|\|

*ācānto'rkaṃ namaskṛtya śauceṣu śucitāmiyāt \|*  
*kriyāṃ yaḥ kurute mohādanācamyeha nāstikaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In an auspicious country, after sipping the water when a person offers salutation to the Sungod, he surely achieves purity. A person who do not performs like this with the sipping of water, he is termed as faithless.

## \|\| 1.143.13 \|\|

*bhavantīha kriyāḥ sarvā vṛthā tasya na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śucikāmā hi vai devā vedairevamudāhṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the same time, all his religious activities become infructuous, there is no doubt about it. It has been ordained in the Vedas that the gods are always desirous of purity.

## \|\| 1.143.14 \|\|

*inopāsākṛtaścaiva sarve devāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*śaucameva praśaṃsanti śaucāṅgairhi vidhīyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. All the gods who adore the Sungod, always praise for purity and purifying their own limbs, start the religious activities.

## \|\| 1.143.15-16 \|\|

*ācānto maunamāsthāya devāgāraṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*śvāsarodhanimittaṃ tu prāṇamācchādya vāsasā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śiraḥ prāvṛtya yatnena keśodakanivṛttaye \|*  
*tataḥ pūjāṃ raveḥ kuryātpuṣpairnānāvidhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. After performing the sipping, one should keep silence and then enter the temple. Reaching there, in order to stop breathing, a cloth should be used. In order to stop the dropping of the water from the head, the cloth should be used. Then he should worship the Sungod, offering various types of fragrant flowers.

## \|\| 1.143.17 \|\|

*gāyatrīṃ saśiraskāṃ ca yajamānaḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*dhūpaṃ tato'gnaye dadyātprathamaṃ guggulāhutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The tuft should be bound reciting the Gayatri hymn. Thereafter, incense and guggulu should be offered to the fire as the offerings.

## \|\| 1.143.18-19 \|\|

*puṣpāñjaliṃ tato gṛhya tacchikhāyāṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*ravermūrdhani taṃ dadyāddevamantramudāharan \|\| 18 \|\|*

*oṃ vratena yadvratino varjayanti devā manuṣyāḥ pitaraśca sarve \|*  
*tasyādityaṃ prasaraṃ ca manāmahe yastejasā prathamaṃ nāvibhāti \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Then with the bunch of flowers, reciting the mantra — om vritena, they should be dropped over the tuft in the head. Then, he should pray the place of the Deva for whom vrata is being performed. The humans and pitris who cannot reach, the Sungod surely reaches them in his vest form. This is what I believe, because earlier they are not visible due to their lustre.

## \|\| 1.143.20 \|\|

*dhūpavelāḥ smṛtāḥ pañca dhūpeṣveva tu pañcasu \|*  
*havanādyāḥ kriyāḥ pañca rakṣiṣye'haṃ tathā punaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Five periods have been prescribed for the offering of five types of incense. I shall remain well protected in those five activities as well as in the homa.

## \|\| 1.143.21 \|\|

*daṇḍanāyakavelā tu pratyūṣe ṛkṣadarśanāt \|*  
*nājñāvelā pradoṣastu tattvakāryaṃ vijānatā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The two times of Dandanayaka, while the three Sandhyas of Surya are the five times which have been prescribed. The people well versed in the tattvas have been informed that the offering of incense at evening time is forbidden.

## \|\| 1.143.22-23 \|\|

*trikālaṃ tu raveḥ pūjā kartavyā sūryadarśanāt \|*  
*ardhoditastu pūrvāhṇe tato'rddhastu ravirvibhuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*helayeti ca pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne jvalanāya ca \|*  
*tathaiva maṇḍale deyaṃ nīcāhne jvalanāya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The worship should be performed thrice a day, when the Sungod is visible. The time of sunrise is known as Heli. The noon time is known as Jvalana. The third arghya should be offered before the sunset uttering the same word Jvalana.

## \|\| 1.143.24-26 \|\|

*candanodakamiśrāṇi gandhodakayutāni ca \|*  
*padmāni karavīrāṇi tathā raktotpalāni ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kusumodakamiśrāṇi kuruṃṭakusumaṃ tathā \|*  
*gandhādīni ca divyāni kṛtvā vai tāmrabhājane \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dhūpaṃ dattvāgnaye vīra prayatnādguggulāhutim \|*  
*arghyapātraṃ tadā gṛhya kuryādāvāhanaṃ raveḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. The fragrant water mixed with sandal paste, besides lotus, red lotus, water with fragrance of flowers, flowers of medicinal plants and the best of fragrance, should be stored in a copper vase. Initially, guggulu should be poured in the fire. Thereafter, holding the vase of arghya, the first offering of guggulu should be poured in the fire and then invoke the Sungod saying.

## \|\| 1.143.27 \|\|

*ehi sūrya sahasrāṃśo tejorāśe jagatpate \|*  
*anukampya māṃ deva gṛhāṇārghyaṃ divākara \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Surya, having the resplendent rays, O lord of the universe, O Divakara! You kindly accept the sipping here, beholden me.

## \|\| 1.143.28 \|\|

*anenāvāhanaṃ kṛtvā jānubhyāmavanīṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ravernivedayedarghyamādityahṛdaye gataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After invoking the Sungod thus, one should kneel down meditating the Sungod in mind, and offering arghya to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.143.29 \|\|

*oṃ namo bhagavate1 ādityāya viśvāya kheśāya brahmaṇelokakartṛṇe \|*  
*īśānāya purāṇāya sahasrākṣāya te namaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thereafter, uttering Omkara, he should think of lord Aditya, having the universal form, lodged in the sky, creator of the universe, Brahma, Ishana, ancient and having a thousand eyes, salutation to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.143.30 \|\|

*somāya ṛgyajuratharvāya \|*  
*oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥoṃmahaḥ oṃjanaḥ oṃtapaḥ oṃ satyaṃ brahmaṇe muṇḍe madhye purataḥ ādityāya namaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He is the form of Moon, Rigveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda and also bhu, bhuvah, svah etc., and then offer salutation to the Sungod, invoking him at the same time.

## \|\| 1.143.31-33 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*sāvitryāśca pare tantre trailokyatrāṇakāriṇe \|*  
*paritaḥ parigṛhyātha dhūpabhājanamutkṣipet \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nivedayettato dhūpaṃ vācametāmudīrayet \|*  
*tvameka eva rudrāṇāṃ vasūnāṃ ca purātanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*devānāṃ gīrbhirabhitaḥ saṃstutaḥ śāśvato divi \|*  
*pūrvāhṇe ca tvayā tena madhyāhne cāpareṇa tu \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Narada said — You are the one who stays away from Savitri, protector of the three worlds. Thus saying, the incense vase should be carried to all the sides and should be offered. He should keep on uttering that— “You are the foremost of the Rudras, ancient most of the Vasus, you are always adored by the gods in the heaven.”

## \|\| 1.143.34-40 \|\|

*oṃ namo bhagavate jñānātmane tvāṃ ca \|*  
*viṣṇostatparamaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*divākarastu sāyāhne mantreṇārghyaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*oṃ \|*  
*namo varuṇāya śambhave \|\| 35 \|\|*

*oṃ ākṛṣṇena rajasā vartamāno niveśayannamṛtaṃ martyaṃ ca \|*  
*hiraṇyayena savitā rathenādevo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan \|\| 36 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā dattvā dhūpaṃ sūryāya bhojakaḥ \|*  
*utkṣipeccaiva dhūpena viśedgarbhagṛhaṃ tataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tataḥ praviśya dhūpaṃ tu pratimārthaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*mantreṇa mihirāyeti nikṣubhāyeti nityaśaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tato rājñai namaśceti nikṣubhāyai tato namaḥ \|*  
*daṇḍanāyakasaṃjñāya piṅgalāya ca vai namaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tathā rājñāya srauṣāya tatheśāya garutmate \|*  
*tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kurvandigdevebhyo nivedayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

34-40. This process should be repeated in the morning, noon and in the evening, and the oblation should be offered. Reciting Omkara one should say — “O lord of knowledge, salutation to you. You are the supreme pada of Vishnu, for which the people of learnings always aspire for.” For that purpose, the relevant hymn is — Divakarastu Sayahne. Salutation to Surya, the form of Varuna and Shiva. A person reciting the hymn — Akrishnena raj as a, should offer incense to the Sungod, which should enter the body of Bhojaka. For that image there, the incense should be offered saying — “Salutation to Mihira, Nikshubha and Rajni. Thereafter, the names of Pingala, the Dandanayaka, Rajna, Shrausha, Isa and Garuda should be spoken while going round, and offer the incense to the gods of the directions.

## \|\| 1.143.41-42 \|\|

*diṇḍine tu tato dadyāddhemantāya yadūttama \|*  
*maheśvarāya dadyāttu tathā vyomāya yādava \|\| 41 \|\|*

*oṃ brahmaṇe muṇḍapataye ādityāya puruṣeśvarāya sūryāya namonamaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*
