*yugānurūpo yaḥ kṛtvā lokānanuvaraṃ kramāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kṣaṇānkalāśca kāṣṭhāśca kālavaikalyameva ca \|*  
*muhūrtāstithayo māsāḥ pakṣāḥ saṃvatsarāstathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ṛtavaḥ kālayogāśca pramāṇaṃ vividhaṃ nṛṣu \|*  
*āyuḥ kṣetrāṇyapacayopacayāṃścaiva yo'karot \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. It is he who divided the share of all with Brahmakarma. The big and small lokas were created according to the yugas, besides kshanas (moments) kala, kashtha, directions, kala, muhurtas, tit his, months, fortnights, year and the seasons were created. In this way, the Sungod created several periods and the yugas. Creating the body as well as the age, the development and the decline of the body was arranged.

## \|\| 1.157.26-28 \|\|

*sṛṣṭā lokāstrayonaṃtā yena jñānena vartmanā \|*  
*sarva bhūtagaṇāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ sarvabhūtātmanā sadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*praṇāmatrayapūrveṇa yogena ramate ca yaḥ \|*  
*yo gatāgatipotena trātāsti jagadīśvaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yo gatirvṛṣayuktānāṃ gatiryo'pāpakarmaṇām \|*  
*cāturvarṇyaprabhāvaśca vapurhotrasya rakṣitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. It is he, who making use of his jnanayoga, created the three lokas several times, while becoming the universal soul, he created all the living beings. He is the one who feels delighted when salutation is offered thrice to him with yogic practices. He is the one, who becoming the form of Jagadishvara, protects the moving ship. He is the solar refuge for the religious minded people as well as the auspicious and sinless people. Creating his influence on all the four castes, his body protects performer of the yajnas.

## \|\| 1.157.29-37 \|\|

*dhātuvaidyasya yo vettā caturāśramasaṃśrayaḥ \|*  
*digaṃbarānubhūtaśca vāyurvāyuvibhāvanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*agnīṣomātmakaṃ jyotiryogīśaḥ kṣaṇadāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paraṃ śrūyate jyotiryaḥ paraṃ śrūyate tapaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yaṃ paraṃ paramaṃ prāhuḥ paramātmānamacyutam \|*  
*brahmādibhiḥ stuto devo yaśca daityāṃtakṛdvibhuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yugāṃteṣvataṃko yastu yaśca lokāṃtakottamaḥ \|*  
*seturyo lokasetūnāṃ madhye yo madhyakarmaṇām \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vettā yo vedaviduṣāṃ prabhuryaḥ prabhaviṣṇunām \|*  
*saumyabhūtastu saumyānāmagnibhūtognivarcasām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mānuṣāṇāṃ manobhūtastapobhūtastapasvinām \|*  
*vinayo nayavṛttīnāṃ tejastejasvināmapi \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vigraho vigrahāṇāṃ ca gatirgatimatāmapi \|*  
*ākāśaprasavo vāyurvāyuḥ prāṇo hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*devāhutipradānodyatprāṇāgnistamanāśanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*rasāddhi śoṇitaṃ bhavati śoṇitānmāṃsamucyate \|*  
*māṃsānmajjāvasorjanma majjanosthīni janmataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*asthimajjñaḥ samabhavattato vai śukramādiśet \|*  
*śukrādgarbhaḥ samabhavadrasamūlena karmaṇā \|*  
*tatrāpaḥ prathamo bhāgaḥ sa saumyo rāśirucyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

29-37. He is well known to the metals as well as the physicians. He is found in all the four ashramas, without robes, well-known as the wind or the mover of the wind, offering of the fire, flame, lord of ascetics, destroyer of the night, the super flame, the excellent tapas, besides the supreme soul as well as Acyuta. He is eulogised by Brahma and other gods. He is the destroyer of daityas as well as the pervading one. He is the destroyer of the creation at the time of the end of yuga, the best of the upper region, the best of all the upper bridges. In the middle region, he attends to medium types of deeds and well known to the learned people who are well-versed in the Vedas. He is the lord of the influential people, best of the beautiful people, the fire in the fire flames, Manu among the humans, tapas for the ascetics, humility among the humble people, the body among the living beings, speed in the moveables, the source of the origin of the wind, besides being the sky, life, fire, offerings for the Devas as the fire, besides being the destroyer of darkness, the blood from liquid, flesh from blood, marrow from blood, bones from marrow. The semen issues from the bones. The conception takes place from semen, the first part of which is water, which is treated auspicious or beautiful.

## \|\| 1.157.38-40 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣmāsaṃbhavo jñeyo dvitīyo rāśirucyate \|*  
*śukraṃ somātmakaṃ vidyādātmarūpaṃ yadātmakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bhavo rasātmakasteṣāṃ vīryaṃ ca śaśipāvakam \|*  
*kaphavarge bhavecchukraṃ pittavarge ca śoṇitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kaphasya pṛthivī sthānaṃ pittaṃ nābhau pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*devasya madhyahṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ tu manasaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*nābhikoṣṭhāṃtarasthaṃ tu tatra devo divākaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. Kshama emerges out of it, which is called the other matter. The semen is also related to Soma (or the Moon). This is one’s own form. The semen is liquid and resembles the Moon. It has the lustre of fire. At times, the semen comes under the cough, while the pitta falls under the blood. In the class of cough is included the semen, while the blood falls in the category of pitta. Earth is the place for cough, while pitta is lodged in a navel. The place of the soul or the mind is considered to be the heart. In the cavity of the navel is the place for the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.157.41-52 \|\|

*manaḥ prajāpatirjñeyaḥ kaphaḥ somo vibhāvyate \|*  
*pittamagniḥ smṛto yasmādagnīṣomātmakaṃ jagat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*evaṃ pravartite garbhe vardhiteṃ'budasannibhe \|*  
*vāyuḥ praveśaṃ saṃcakre saṃgataḥ paramātmanā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tatoṃ'gāni visṛjate bibharti parivartayan \|*  
*prāṇo'pānaḥ samānaśca udāno vyāna eva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*prāṇosya prathamaṃ sthānaṃ vardhayanparivartate \|*  
*apānaṃ paścime kāya udānordhvaṃ śarīragaḥ \|*  
*vyāno'tha vyāpako dehe samānaḥ sannivartate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*bhūtāvāptistatastasya jāyatīṃdriyagocarā \|*  
*pṛthivī vāyurākāśa āpo jyotiśca paṃcamaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasyeṃdriyāṇi piṣṭāni svaṃsvaṃ yogaṃ pracakramuḥ \|*  
*pārthivaṃ dehamāhustu prāṇātmānaṃ ca mārutam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*nidrā hyākāśayoniśca jalāśraye pravartate \|*  
*jyotiścakṣuṣi tajjanma tadaṃśastāmasaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*grāmāśca viṣayāścaiva yasya vīryaṃ pravartitam \|*  
*evaṃ yaḥ sṛjate lokānsadevāsuramānavān \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ devadeveśo garbhameṣyati cāṃśumān \|*  
*yathodaramadityāstu yaḥ svayaṃ cāviśatpurā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*evaṃ me saṃśayo brahmanneṣa me vismayo mahān \|*  
*kathaṃ raviryayau garbhabhāvaṃ dvijavareti me \|\| 50 \|\|*

*āścaryaṃ paramaṃ pṛcche tvāmahaṃ bhāskarasya vai \|*  
*bhānorutpattimāścaryaṃ hṛdi me parivartate \|\| 51 \|\|*

*etadāścaryamākhyānaṃ kathayasva mahāmune \|*  
*samākhyāhi balaṃ vīrya bhānoramitatejasaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

41-52. The mind born Prajapati or Brahma resembles cough. Pitta resembles Agni. This has been explained in the definition of Agnishomatmika world. Thus, the womb inflates with the wind, thereafter, develop the limbs. Rearing and changes come with the wind. This wind is of the types of prana, apana, samana and udana. The expansion at the initial stage and the changes are caused by prana vayu, the back of the body is increased by apana vayu, the upper part is developed by udana-vayu. Vyoma develops the body and the wind remains pervading equally in the entire body. With the entry of the jiva in the body, the sense organs appear in the body which are the earth, wind, sky, water and the flame. In the forms of the flame, they themselves get established. The body is known as Parthiva and the wind is known as Prana. The sleep remains present in the water pond. Some parts of the vision are lodged in the eyes, which are also known as tamas. All the sense organs, the prowess of which can be visualised in the worldly pleasures and who created the Devas, Asuras and the humans, how could such a great Sungod, enter the womb? This is the great wonder which has developed in my mind. This is the cause of my asking you. The birth of the Sungod has created a wonder in my heart. O great sage, the Sun has enormous lustre. Thus, story about him is quite surprising which may please be revealed to me together with his strength and prowess.”

## Chapter 158. Birth of Surya in solar religions

## \|\| 1.158.1 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*praśnabhāro mahāṃstāta tvayokto raśmimālini \|*  
*yathāśakti tu vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ bhānavaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — You have put a series of question about the Sungod with garland of rays. Therefore, I am talking to you as per my capacity.

## \|\| 1.158.2 \|\|

*bhānoḥ prabhāvaśravaṇe yasya te matirutthitā \|*  
*haṃta bhānoḥ pravṛttiṃ ca śṛṇu divyāṃ mayeritām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. You wisdom is getting interested to listen to the glory of the Sungod. Therefore, I am revealing the story of Surya. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.158.3-11 \|\|

*sahasrāsyaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ sahasrakiraṇaṃ ca yam \|*  
*sahasraśirasaṃ devaṃ sahasrakarama vyayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sahasrajihvaṃ bhāsvaṃtaṃ sahasramukuṭaṃ prabhum \|*  
*sahasradaṃ sahasrāriṃ sahasrabhujamavyayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*savanaṃ bhavanaṃ caiva havyaṃ hotārameva ca \|*  
*pātrāṇi samatītāni vedadīkṣī caruṃ śubham \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śrotriyaṃ śūrpamusalaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇāyanam \|*  
*adhvaryuṃ sāmagaṃ vipraṃ sadasyaṃ sadanaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yūpaṃ samitsruvaṃ darvīṃ musalolūkhalāni ca \|*  
*prāgvaṃśaṃ jayabhūtiṃ ca hotāraṃ cayanaṃ ca yat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*rahasyāni pramāṇāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitāni dārḍhyaṃ ca sthaṃḍilāni kuśāṃstathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*maṃtrayajñavahaṃ vahnibhāgaṃ bhārgavameva ca \|*  
*agrebhujī somabhujāṃ yaśca triṣu udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āyurvedavido viprā yajaṃte śāśvataṃ vibhum \|*  
*tasya bhānoḥ sureśasya vīra caṃdanamālinaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*prāhurbhāvasahasrāṇi samatītānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*bhūyaścaiva bhaviṣyaṃti vinaśyaṃti dinedine \|\| 11 \|\|*

3-11. The Sungod has a thousand eyes, a thousand faces, a thousand rays, a thousand heads and a thousand hands. He is indestructible, has a thousand tongues and a thousand shining crowns. He is the giver of a thousand charities, he becomes victorious over a thousand enemies, having a thousand arms, indestructible. He has the form of vana, bhavana, havya, the yajna, vase, Veda and the Vedic altar, auspicious cam, Shrotriya, shupa (winnowing basket), musala, spray of water, Dakshinayana, Adhvaryu, Samaga, Brahmana, yupa, abode, pillar, fire sticks, ladle, durva, mortar, the first race Jayabhuti, hota (the performer), besides being the form of collection. He is secret evidence of immobile and mobile things, as a result of which he is firmly established. He is well known on earth, kusha, mantras, yajna, Agni, Bhargava, Abrebkuji. He is well known in the three worlds; he is the one who is adored by the Brahmana of Ayurveda regularly. The same Sungod has taken to thousands of births, still he would be born and got destroyed day after day.

## \|\| 1.158.12-14 \|\|

*yatpṛcchasi mahārāja puṇyāṃ divyāṃ kathāṃ śubhām \|*  
*yadarthaṃ bhagavānbhānuḥ kaśyapasya suto'bhavat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tāmahaṃ tvaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*hitārthaṃ sarvamartyānāṃ lokānāṃ prabhavāya ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bahuśaḥ sarvabhūtātmā svayaṃ samabhijāyate \|*  
*tathā samabhavaddevaḥ kaśyapasyāditeḥ sutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. O great king, the auspicious and divine story which is being related by you, in which the Sungod has been the son of Kashyapa, the same story is going to be related by me. You please listen for the welfare of the people and for the creation of the lokas, the Sun who happens to be the soul of all the living beings, is several times born, in various forms, similarly, he became the son of Kashyapa from Aditi.

## \|\| 1.158.15-26 \|\|

*tuṣṭo dattvā varaṃ vīra virañcasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*yaṃ yaṃ janayate putramaditiḥ kaśyapādvibhoḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sa sa yāti vināśaṃ vai tatkṣaṇādeva bhārata \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sutānnaśyamānānputraśokānvitā 'ditiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jagāma kaśyapābhyāśe śokavyākulitekṣaṇā \|*  
*sāpaśyattaṃ ca mārīcaṃ muniṃ dīptaṃ taponidhim \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ādyaṃ devaguruṃ vipraṃ divyaṃ triṣavaṇāṃbubhiḥ \|*  
*tejasā vahnisaṃkāśaṃ sauraṃ vṛkasamaprabham \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nyastadaṇḍaśriyā yuktaṃ baddhakṛṣṇājināṃbaram \|*  
*valkalājinasaṃvītaṃ pradīptaṃ brahmavarcasam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hutāśamiva dīvyantaṃ tapantamiva bhāskaram \|*  
*athāditiśca dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhartāramamitaujasam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śokagadgadayā vācā idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*kimarthaṃ bhagavāndevo nirudyogastu tiṣṭhati \|\| 21 \|\|*

*jātojāto hi me putraḥ sadya eva vinaśyati \|*  
*śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasyāḥ kaśyapo munisattamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*cakāra gamane buddhiṃ brahmalokaṃ prati prabho \|*  
*sa gatvā brahmabhavanaṃ nānābhāvasamanvitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tadvākya muktaṃ taṃ sarvaṃ yaduktaṃ tasya jāyayā \|*  
*kaśyapasya vacaḥ śrutvā kañjajo vākyamabravīt \|\| 24 \|\|*

*putra gacchāma sadanaṃ bhānoḥ paramadurlabham \|*  
*ityuktvā yānamāruhya āgneyaṃ padmalocanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vedhā jagāma bhavanamādityasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*aditiḥ kaśyapo brahmā jagmurvipulamāśritāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

15-26. The Sungod, getting pleased, bestowed the boon to Brahma. Whatever sons were born by Aditi in union with Kashyapa, they were instantly destroyed. Thus worried about the destruction of her sons, she looked at Kashyapa with tearful eyes. Then she walked towards the hermitage of Kashyapa and reaching there, she saw him who was the son of Maricha, a sage, resplendent, performer of tapas, foremost of all, the preceptor of the gods, dear, divine, who took bath thrice a day, had lustre like the fire flames, having the grace of discarded danda, resplendent like the fire, illustrious like the crow or wolf, wearing the skin of the black buck, clad in back garments, resplendent, possessing the lustre of Brahman, divine like the fire, burning like Bhaskara. Finding her husband with such a lustre, Aditi, getting worried, spoke in choked voice — “Why is my fortunate husband seated unmindful of getting a son? Are you not aware that all my sons perish soon after their birth? The sage Kashyapa, listening to the words of his wife, thought of visiting Brahmaloka. He went there as well, reaching the Brahmaloka having several types of creations, he narrated to Brahma all whatever his wife had told him. Listening to the words of Kashyapa, Brahma said — “O son, I am going to the place of Surya, which is difficult to be reached. You also get along with me.” Thus speaking, the lotus eyed Brahma seated over the plane of fire and moved towards the abode of the Sungod, Aditi also accompanied them both.

## \|\| 1.158.27 \|\|

*te muhūrtena saṃprāptāḥ sūryalokaṃ suvarcasam \|*  
*divyakāmagamairyānairyathārhaṃ kurunandana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O son of the race of Kuru, boarding the plane, all of them reached the solar region in a moment.

## \|\| 1.158.28-39 \|\|

*ādityaṃ praṣṭumicchaṃti tejasāṃ rāśimuttamam \|*  
*gacchantaste ca vistīrṇāmādityasya parāṃ sabhām \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ṣaṭpadodgītaninadāṃ sābhagaistu samīritām \|*  
*kratavo bahvṛcamukhāḥ proktāḥ puṇyavadakṣarāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tuṣṭuvuḥ puruṣavyāghraṃ vitateṣu ca karmasu \|*  
*yajñasandhau vedavidāṃ padakramavidāṃ tathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ghoṣeṇa paramarṣīṇāṃ sarvaṃ tatra nināditam \|*  
*yajñasaṃstavavidbhiśca śikṣāvidbhistathā dvijaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*aṣṭādaśapurāṇajñaiḥ sarvavidyāviśāradaiḥ \|*  
*mīmāṃsāhetuvādajñaiḥ sarvavādaviśāradaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*lokāyatikamukhyaiśca tuṣṭuvuḥ sūryamīritam \|*  
*tatratatra ca viprendrān niyatāñchaṃsitavratān \|\| 33 \|\|*

*japahomaparānyogyāndadṛśuḥ kaśyapādayaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ sabhāyāmāste sa raśmimālī divākaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*surāsuraguruḥ śrīmāñchuśubhe vīra māyayā \|*  
*upāsate ca tatraiva prajānāṃ patimīśvaram \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dakṣaḥ pracetāḥ pulaho marīciśca dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*bhṛguratrirvaśiṣṭhaśca gautamo nāradastathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*divyā ātmāṃtarikṣaṃ ca vāyustejobalaṃ mahī \|*  
*śabdaḥ sparśaḥ svarūpaṃ ca rasagandhau tathaiva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prakṛtiśca vikārāśca yaccānyatkāraṇaṃ mahat \|*  
*sāṃgopāgāśca catvāro vedā lokapate tathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*lavāśca ṛtavaścaiva saṃkalpapraṇavāstathā \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavo bhānumaṃtamupāsate \|\| 39 \|\|*

28-39. Reaching there in the excellent assembly, all of them narrated the tale of suffering to the Sungod, which echoed in the assembly of the Sungod in Shatapada metres, and was sung by the Brahmanas of Samaveda. In the same assembly, creator was praising the Sungod He had been a Vedic scholar, all the Rishis were singing the Vedic hymns in loud voice. The prayer there was being offered by the Brahmanas who offered prayer in the yajnas. The Brahmanas, well versed in the education field, those well-versed in the eighteen Puranas, those who were well educated in the six systems of Hindu philosophy, science of logic, discussion on all the subjects, the followers of Charvaka philosophy, were offering prayers to the Sungod. It appeared as if the Sungod himself had been speaking in the forms of all those Brahmanas. Kashyapa on his part, hard an audience with highly placed Brahmanas, observing all the rules, discipline and the related vratas and who performed the homas. In the said assembly, where the Sungod, who is the lord of rays, was looking graceful in the presence of the gods, asuras and the preceptors together with his own Мaya. At the same place, the Sungod, who was the lord of the people, was being worshipped. The Sungod was being worshipped by Daksha, Pracheta, Pulaha, Marichi — the best of Brahmanas, Bhrigu, Atri, Vasistha, Gautama, Narada, the supreme and divine soul, the lustre, prowess, earth, words, touch, form, liquid (rasa) fragrance, nature, blemish, petty and big reasons, all the Vedas with their parts and the lords of the lokas were also present there. The moments, the seasons, kalpas as well as Pranava were all worshipping the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.158.40-47 \|\|

*artho dharmaśca kāmaśca mokṣaśca saviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dveṣo harṣaśca mohaśca matsaro māna eva ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vṛko viṣṇusutaḥ putraḥ puṣpajo dhiṣaṇastathā \|*  
*māheśvarastathā sauro viṭapo vikacastathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*māruto viśvakarmā ca aśvi nāvanyavāhanau \|*  
*evamuktaḥ suvacanairbhānunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*jagāma kaśyapo vīra sahādityā svamāśramam \|*  
*aditirdevamātā ca taṃ garbhaṃ nidadhe svayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*bhūtātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|*  
*pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu pravṛtto garbha uttamaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*surāṇāṃ śaraṇaṃ devaścāsurāṇāṃ vināśanaḥ \|*  
*garbhasthena tu tenaiva paritrātaḥ sutastathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ādadānastu tejāṃsi trailokyasya narādhipa \|*  
*tasmiñjāte tu deveśe trailokyasya sukhāvahe \|\| 46 \|\|*

*prahatya daityasaṃghāṃśca surāṇāṃ nādavardhane \|*  
*abhavatparamānandaḥ sarveṣāṃ tatra tasthuṣām \|\| 47 \|\|*

40-47. Specially, the artha, dharma, moksha, jealousy, delight, delusion, envy, pride, Agni, Pradyumna, Kamadeva, Brihaspati, Maheshvara, besides the son of Surya, Vitapa, Vikacha, Maruta, Vishvakarma, Ashvinikumaras and the vehicles of all, were adoring the Sungod. Thereafter, the influential Sungod, listening to the words of Kashyapa, reassured him with sweet words, which satisfied Kashyapa. Thereafter, Kashyapa with his wife Aditi returned to his abode. After sometime, Aditi — the mother of the gods, conceived and the conception continued for a thousand divine years. After the lapse of a thousand years, the pregnancy, which was the abode of the gods and destroyer of the asuras, was freed. While remaining in the womb, he patronized the lustre of the three lokas saving the world at the same time. At the birth of the leader of the gods, who was to bestow comforts on all the three lokas and destruction of the daityas to enhance the pleasure of the gods. All the people enjoyed all the bliss.

## Chapter 159. Incarnation of Surya

## \|\| 1.159.1-2 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prajāpatiścaiva namaskāraṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*vidyotamāno vapuṣā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*upātiṣṭhata deveśaṃ bhānuṃ carṣigaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*tato gaṃdharvamukhyeṣu praṇadatsu vihā yasi \|*  
*bahubhiḥ saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pragāyatsu mahīpate \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sumantu said — Daksha Prajapati, whose body was decorated with all the ornaments, looking graceful, offered his salutation to the Sungod. The Rishis also started adoring the Sungod. The chief Gandharvas, together with his associates, started singing in the sky.

## \|\| 1.159.3-4 \|\|

*evaṃ te devagaṃdharvā upāgāyaṃta bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*utpannaṃ dvādaśātmānaṃ bhāskaraṃ vāritaskaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*indro vivasvānpūṣā ca tvaṣṭā ca savitā tathā \|*  
*bhargoṃ'śumānaryamārkaḥ pṛśnirmārtaṃḍa eva ca \|*  
*ityekādaśa evaite dvādaśo viṣṇurucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Thus, the Gandharvas were engaged in pleasing the Sungod with their songs and music. Displaying their art with devotion, they were trying to delight the Sungod, who was born in twelve forms. He was the thief of the water. The names of Surya have been defined to be Indra, Vivasvan, Pusha, Tvashta, Savita, Bharga, Amshuman, Aryama, Arka, Prishni and Martanda. The twelfth name of Surya is known as Vishnu.

## \|\| 1.159.5 \|\|

*evaṃ dvādaśadhā jātamaṃśumaṃtaṃ mahādbhutam \|*  
*stuvanti devatāḥ sarve gatāśca tarasā mahīm \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then with the birth of Surya in twelve forms, all the gods at once descended on earth and started eulogising him.

## \|\| 1.159.6-7 \|\|

*mṛgavyādhaśca śarvaśca mṛgāṃkāṃko mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*ajaikapādahirbudhnyaḥ patiḥ kācaḥ paraṃtapaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*damanaśceśvaraścaiva kapālī ca viśāṃpate \|*  
*sthāṇurbhagaśca bhagavānrudrāścaite'vatasthire \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The gods like Mrigavyadha, Sarva, Mriganka, Mahayasha, Aja, Ekapada, Ahirbudhnya, Pita, Kacha, Parantapa, Damana, Ishvara, Vishampata, Kapali (Shiva), Sthanu, Bhaga, and lord Rudra also were present there.

## \|\| 1.159.8 \|\|

*aśvinau vasavaścāṣṭau garuḍaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*viśvedevāśca sādhyāśca tasthuḥ prāṃjalayo nṛpa \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The gods like Ashvinikumaras, eight Vasus, the valorous Garuda, Vishvedeva and Sadhyas also stood there with folded hands.

## \|\| 1.159.9-10 \|\|

*nāgarājo mahārāja vāsukiḥ prāṃjaliḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*anye ca bahavo nāgā rākṣasāśca mahābalāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tārkṣyaścāriṣṭanemiśca garuḍaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*aruṇaścāruṇiścaiva tatra prāṃjalayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Nagaraja Vasuki stood with his hands folded with other serpents, the terrific Rakshasas, Garuda, Arishtanemi, Rishi Kashyapa, Arana with his sons, all stood there with their hands folded.

## \|\| 1.159.11-13 \|\|

*pitāmahaśca bhagavānsvayamāgamya lokakṛt \|*  
*prāha devaguruḥ śrīmāntsuraiḥ sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yasmātprekṣayate sarvaṃ prabhaviṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*tasmāllokeśvaraḥ śrīmānvivasvāṃśca bhavatviti \|\| 12 \|\|*

*devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ gaṃdharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*yasmādayamādidevastasmādāditya eva hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Brahma — the creator of the universe, Devaguru Brihaspati accompanied with all the Rishis and the gods, prayed with the Sungod — “You are extremely influential and eternal form, visualising the presence of all the people present here. Therefore, O Sungod — the lord of the universe, besides being the eternal lord of the Devas, Danavas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Nagas and those of the Rakshasas, he would be known as Aditya.

## \|\| 1.159.14 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu bhagavānsārdhaṃ devarṣibhiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtvā susaṃpūjya yayau tatsadanaṃ prati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus, lord Brahmi, together with other Rishis adored him pretty well and offering salutation to him, left for their place.

## \|\| 1.159.15-21 \|\|

*yā gatiryajñaśīlānāṃ yā gatiḥ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*yā gatiḥ siddhayogānāṃ yā gatiśca mahātmanām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yasyāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ samabhūddevasattamam \|*  
*yaṃ prāpya śāśvataṃ viprā nāvartaṃte bhavārṇave \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vālakhilyādayo ye ca sarvāśramanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*sevaṃte yaṃ yatātmāno duścaraṃ vratamāsthitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yo'naṃta iva nāgeṣu yasya te sarvayoginaḥ \|*  
*sahasramūrdhā raktākṣaḥ śeṣādibhiranuttamaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yo yajña iti vipreṃdrairarcyate sukhamīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*sarve ca yaṃ yataprāṇā dhyāyanti brahmarūpiṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yaṃ vedavido gāyaṃti vettāraṃ yajñadāyi nam \|*  
*taṃ putraṃ dvādaśātmānaṃ kaśyapaḥ prāpya sattamam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mudaṃ lebhe sahādityā sukhaṃ ca paramaṃ vibho \|*  
*lokaśca mumude sarvo rākṣasā bhayamāpnu van \|\| 21 \|\|*

15-21. He is the spirit behind those performing the yajna, the auspicious people, the Siddha — yogins and the great souls. He is the excellent Deva, with which also emerged the fortunes as well as the eight virtues. Achieving whom, the Brahmanas never get involved in the ocean of the universe. The Balakhilyas and other dwellers of the ashrama, perform severe tapas controlling their sense organs, and serve the Sungod. He is of unlimited form (ananta). At times, he appears as a Yogi. He has thousand heads far better than those of the serpent Shesha. His eyes are red. The Brahmana desirous of comfort, adore him as the form of yajna. All the yogis worship him in the form of Brahman. The people well-versed in the Vedas, sing for him. He is a great observer and the bestower of the yajnas. The same Sun, having twelve forms, was attained by Kashyapa and Aditi in the form of a son. Feeling delighted, then they enjoyed the bliss (of the birth of the Sungod as their son). All the lokas felt delighted, but the Rakshasas felt panic stricken.

## \|\| 1.159.22-24 \|\|

*madhupiṃgalo mahābāhuḥ kaṃbugrīvo hasanniva \|*  
*iṃgudībaddhamukuṭo diśaḥ prajvalayanniva \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sa uvāca mahātejāḥ kaśyapaṃ carṣisatta mam \|*  
*eṣohaṃ tava putratvaṃ gato garbhasya siddhaye \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dattvā varaṃ purā vipra viraṃcasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvamṛṣiśārdūla kuru sṛṣṭimanaupamām \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Then Kashyapa — the best of the Rishis, having the complexion of honey, having the beautiful neck resembling a conch, having long arms, the illustrious sage, had serene smile over his face. Because of his fixing Ingudi in the crown, all the direction gods illuminated. Then Kashyapa — the best of the Rishis, said — “For the success of the pregnancy, he has become your son.” O Brahmana, I had bestowed this boon to Brahma. Therefore, O lion among the Rishis, you start creation of the unprecedented world.

## \|\| 1.159.25 \|\|

*evamārādhya deveśaṃ brahmā sṛṣṭimavāptavān \|*  
*ārādhya kaśyapaścāpi bhāskaraṃ sutamāptavān \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus adoring the lord Surya, Brahma achieved success in creating the world. Similarly, by adoring Bhaskara, Kashyapa got a son.

## Chapter 160. The universal form of Surya

## \|\| 1.160.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*aho devasya caritaṃ bhāskarasya tvayoditam \|*  
*brahmādayo'pi yaṃ nityaṃ pūjayaṃti vidhānataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — You have narrated the story of Surya, which is really wonderful. Brahma and other gods adore him appropriately daily.

## \|\| 1.160.2 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇuḥ surā brahmaṃstamārādhya divākaram \|*  
*dadṛśustasya kiṃbhūtaṃ rūpaṃ yattanmahādbhutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Brahman! Brahma, Vishnu and other gods worship the Sungod and had an audience with him often. What type of the form of the Sungod was visualised by them, which was indeed wonderful?

## \|\| 1.160.3-5 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*ārādhya devamīśānaṃ bhāskaraṃ sūtivācakam \|*  
*kaviṣṇū kuruśārdūla jagmatustau himācalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gopateraṃtikaṃ vīra prahṛṣṭau vibhudarśane \|*  
*kuṃdeṃdusaṃnibhaṃ draṣṭuṃ kaṃjajaścācyutaśca tau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dadṛśaturmahātmānaṃ caṃdrārdhakṛtaśekharam \|*  
*pūjayaṃtaṃ vivasvaṃtaṃ bhāskaraṃ vīravannṛpa \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Sumantu said — O lion of the Kuru race, in order to get the details of the origin of Ishana, worshipping the Sungod, both Brahma and Vishnu went to Himalaya in order to have an audience with the Sungod. The place was close to the Sungod. In order to have a look at the lotus like Surya, both Brahma and Vishnu reaching there, found lord Jiva engaged there in meditation for Surya.

## \|\| 1.160.6 \|\|

*ārcyocaturmahātmānaṃ kaviṣṇū taṃ trilocanam \|*  
*bhobho bhīma suraśreṣṭha paśyāvāmiha cāgatau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then both of them said to the three eyed god Shiva~ “O great Shiva, look here, both of us have come here before you.

## \|\| 1.160.7-12 \|\|

*śrutvovāca tayorvākyaṃ kaṃjajasyācyutasya ca \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā bhūmau kṛtvā pūjāṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*uvāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ śikṣākṣarasamanvitam \|*  
*harṣa gadgadayā vācā diśaḥ sannādayanniva \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kimārādhya raviṃ prāptau sarvadevavaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*kathyatāṃ nikhilaṃ devau paramaṃ kautukaṃ mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭavaṃtau paraṃ kiṃcidrūpaṃ devasya śaṃkaram \|*  
*avyayasyāprameyasya bhānoramitatejasaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*niśamya vacanaṃ vīra śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ūcatustau mahātmānau kaviṣṇū devasattamau \|\| 11 \|\|*

*na tatpaśyāvahe rūpaṃ yattatparamamadbhutam \|*  
*ārādhayitumevāpi hyāgatau teṃtikaṃ ca tam \|\| 12 \|\|*

7-12. Listening to the words of Brahma and Vishnu, lord Shiva welcomed both of them, offering his salutation to them. Then lord Shiva spoke sweet words as if advising them, in choked voice, illumining the directions, Shiva said — “What have you gained by adoring the Sungod, who is the best of all the gods? I am quite anxious to know about it. You speak out all the details to me. Could you have a look at the invincible, unlimited, immensely resplendent forms of the Sungod winch bestows welfare?” Listening to the words of lord Shiva, both Brahma and Vishnu said to him — “We have not been able to have an audience with the noble form of Surya. Therefore, in order to have an audience with him as well as for performing his worship, we have arrived before you.

## \|\| 1.160.13 \|\|

*tasmādārādhayāmo hi ekībhūya vibhāvasum \|*  
*gatvodayagiriṃ puṇyaṃ parvataṃ kanakojjvalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Both of us shall together worship the Sungod over the bright Udayachala mountain.

## \|\| 1.160.14 \|\|

*śrutvā tu vacanaṃ vīra kaṃjajācyutayorharaḥ \|*  
*tathetyāha mahābāho harṣādutphullalocanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Listening to the words of Brahma and Vishnu, Shiva said — “Be it so”, and conveyed his consent to them. Both of them felt delighted and their eyes blossomed.

## \|\| 1.160.15-20 \|\|

*atha te rājaśārdūla vivigogatayo nṛpa \|*  
*jagmustaṃ parvataśreṣṭhamudayācalamāśu vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tamāsādya nagaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṃgaistribhiralaṃkṛtam \|*  
*nānā dhātupinaddhāṅgaṃ nānādhātuvibhūṣitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ārādhanāya vidhivadyatnaṃ cakrurvibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*stuvantaste samarcaṃto dhyāyaṃtaśca vibhāvasum \|\| 17 \|\|*

*divyavarṣasahasrāṃte tapaṃtaḥ saṃsthitā nage \|*  
*padmāsanagato brahmā dhyāyamāno divākaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sthāṇuvatsaṃsthito bhūmāvūrdhvabāhustrilocanaḥ \|*  
*paṃcāgniṃ bhajamānastu sthito viṣṇuravākchirāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ varṣasahasrāṃte tapaścakruḥ sudāruṇam \|*  
*ārādhayaṃto vidhivadgopatiṃ putramālinam \|\| 20 \|\|*

15-20. Thereafter, Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva — all the three of them proceeded to the mountain Udayachala. Reaching there, they found that the mountain was having three peaks abounded with several metals. Then, they started making efforts for the worship of the Sungod. All of them started adoring the Sungod. All of them kept on performing tapas there for a thousand divine years, Shiva adored Divakara standing on the ground, raising both his hands. Vishnu kept his head hanging against five types of fires, while Brahma adored the Sungod, seated in Padmasana.

## \|\| 1.160.21-22 \|\|

*atha brahmeśaviṣṇūnāṃ kurvatāṃ tapa uttamam \|*  
*tutoṣa bhagavānbhānuruvāca ca mahīpate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*brahmañchaṃbho hare brūta mattaḥ kimabhivāṃchatha \|*  
*tuṣṭohaṃ bhavatāṃ dātu mihāyāto varaṃ svayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The Sungod was extremely pleased with the worship of all the three gods and he said to hem — “O Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, what do you desire from me? Having been pleased with your vrata, I have personally reached here to reward you for your tapas.

## \|\| 1.160.23-25 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*niśamya vacanaṃ bhānoḥ śāṃtaṃ hṛdyaṃ manoramam \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā keśā idaṃ vacamabruvan \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kṛtakṛtyā vayaṃ sarve prasādāttava gopate \|*  
*tvāmārādhya purā deva tvattaḥ prāpya varaṃ śubham \|\| 24 \|\|*

*utpattisthitināśānāṃ vayaṃ sarve divākara \|*  
*saṃbhūyeha samarthā vai tvatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Sumantu said — Listening to the sweet and pleasant words of the Sungod, all the three of them offered their salutation, lowering their heads and said — “O lord of the rays, we have been beholden with your grace because we have already achieved the excellent boons by adoring you. By your grace, we be able to create, maintain and destroy the universe. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.160.26-27 \|\|

*kiṃ tvekaṃ devadeveśa varamicchāmahe vibho \|*  
*yatte paramakaṃ rūpaṃ durlabhaṃ durdṛśaṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmādasmājjagannātha rūpaṃ darśaya te'cyutam \|*  
*sarvadevamayaṃ yatte yattvayoktaṃ purānagha \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. O great lord, of course, we are desirous of another boon. We intend to have a look at your extremely difficult and terrific form, you kindly display the same before us. Therefore, you kindly display your universal form before us, which had been mentioned by you earlier.”

## \|\| 1.160.28 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaviṣṇvīśabhāṣitam \|*  
*darśayāmāsa tadrūpamadbhutaṃ lokapūjitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Listening to the words of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, the Sungod displayed his adorable and the wonderful form.

## \|\| 1.160.29-40 \|\|

*anekavaktraśirasamanekādbhutadarśanam \|*  
*sarvadevamayaṃ divyaṃ sarvalokamayaṃ tathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhūḥ pādau dyauḥ śiraścāpi tatrāgnī locane mate \|*  
*pādāṃgulyaḥ piśācāśca hastāṃgulyaśca guhyakāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*viśve devāḥ smṛtāstasya jaṃghāsaṃghāḥ surottamāḥ \|*  
*yakṣāḥ kukṣiṣu saṃlīnāḥ keśāścāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭidhṛṣṭyaśca vipulāḥ keśā vīrāṃśavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tārakā romarūpāṇi romāṇi ca maharṣayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bāhavo vidiśastasya diśaḥ śrotre narādhipa \|*  
*aśvinau śravaṇe cāsya nāsā vāyurmahābalaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prasādaśca kṣamā caiva mano dharmastathaiva ca \|*  
*satyamasyābhavadvāṇī jihvā devī sarasvatī \|\| 34 \|\|*

*grīvāditirmahādevī tālū rudraśca vīryavān \|*  
*dvāraṃ svargasya nābhirvai mitrastvaṣṭā picaṃḍakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*mukhaṃ vaiśvānaraścāsya vṛṣaṇau ca bhagastadā \|*  
*hṛdayaṃ bhagavānbrahmā hyudaraṃ kaśyapo muniḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭhe'sya vasavo devā marutaḥ sarvasaṃdhiṣu \|*  
*sarvacchaṃdāṃsi daśanā jyotīṃṣi vimalā prabhā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prāṇo rudro mahādevaḥ kukṣau cāsya mahārṇavāḥ \|*  
*udare cāsya gaṃdharvā bhujagāśca mahābalāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*lakṣmīrmedhā dhṛtiḥ kāṃtiḥ sarvā vidyāśca vai kaṭau \|*  
*lalāṭamasya paramaṃ vayaḥsthānaṃ parātmanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sarvajyotīṃṣi jānīhi tapaścakraśca deva rāṭ \|*  
*tadetadādidevasya tanau hyāhurmahātmanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

29-40. He had many mouths, heads and wonderful divine appearance, displaying all the gods, all the lokas, the earth, both the feet, the head in the sky, the fire as both the eyes, vast toes, the fingers of hands as Indra, Vishvedeva as thigh joints. The Yakshas were in the armpits, the Apsaras in the hair, audacity in the eyes, the locks of hair as rays. The great Rishis were the hair on the body, the directions were in the arms, the sides were in cars besides the Ashvinikumaras, Wind-god in the nostrils, the happiness, forgiveness, mind and dharma, truthfulness and the goddess Sarasvati in the tongue, Aditi — the great goddess on neck, the valorous Rudra over palate, gate of heaven in the navel, Mitra, Tvashta and Pichandaka, Vaishvanara (fire), mouth, both the testicles. Lord Brahma was the heart and sage Kashyapa was shown in the belly. Maruta was in all the joints, the teeth in all the metres, and the flames were the lustre. Mahadeva Rudra was the prana, Mahasagara was in the armpit, Gandharva in the belly. In the waist the valorous serpent, Lakshmi, Medha, Dhriti, resplendence and all the knowledge were lodged. The Wind god was lodged in the forehead, besides Jyotishlingas, and the wieldier of disc form is also lodged there. The body of the great universal soul should be thus conceived, who has been defined as above. The great souls have thus described the form of the universal form.

## \|\| 1.160.41-44 \|\|

*stanau kukṣau ca vedāśca teṣṭau cāsya makhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*yaṣṭavyapaśubaṃdhāśca dvijānāṃ veṣṭi tāni ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sarvadevamayaṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpamarkasya te nṛpa \|*  
*brahmā haro harirdevāḥ paraṃ vismayamāgatāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ vepamānā dharāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*bhayagadgadayā vācā idaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 43 \|\|*

*samīkṣya rūpaṃ te deva bhīmaṃ jvālāsamākulam \|*  
*anekamukhabāhūrucaraṇaṃ cakitā vayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

41-44. Both the breasts, the armpits, and all the four Vedas combined, form his Yaksha form. O king, thus observing the universal form of the Sungod, all the three — Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesha were extremely surprised. They offered their salutation to him lowering their heads. They shook in fright and then spoke in choked voice — “O Deva, you appear as if in flames of fire, you have numerous faces, arms, thighs and feet. At the sight of this form, we feel surprised.

## \|\| 1.160.45 \|\|

*digjñānaṃ hṛtamasmākaṃ tatprasīda jagatpate \|*  
*upasaṃhara viśvātmandraṣṭuṃ śaktā na te vayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O lord of the world, we have lost the sense of directions, therefore, you kindly be pleased O soul of the world or universal soul, you better discard your present form, because we are unable to look at it.”

## \|\| 1.160.46 \|\|

*iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā devadevo divākaraḥ \|*  
*prasanno bhagavānāha vacastānprahasannidam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing the words spoken by them, Surya — the lord of gods, getting delighted, smiling spoke.

## \|\| 1.160.47-48 \|\|

*āditya uvāca \|*  
*yadetatparamaṃ puṇyamadbhutaṃ lokabhāvanam \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ bhavadbhirdeveṃdrā mama sarvajaganmayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*etanmayā prasannena yuṣmākaṃ śreyase'naghāḥ \|*  
*darśitaṃ pūjiteneha yogināṃ yanmahālayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Aditya said — “O lord of the Devas, the extremely auspicious, wonderful, displaying the world force, universal form, has been visualised by the people, O sinless one, you people have worshipped me, therefore getting delighted for your welfare, I have displayed this form before you. This is like the great temple of the yogins.”

## \|\| 1.160.49 \|\|

*brahmeśācyutā ucuḥ \|*  
*evametanna saṃdeho yathāttha tvaṃ divaspate \|*  
*yogināmapi deveśa darśanaṃ hyasya durlabham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Thereafter, Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva spoke — “O lord of the day, whatever has been spoken by you is correct. There is no doubt about it. The sight of your universal form is beyond the reach of even the great yogins.

## \|\| 1.160.50 \|\|

*tvāmārādhya jagannāthaṃ nāprāpyamiha vidyate \|*  
*tasmātpūjyatamo loke nānyo deveṣu vidyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Because of your worship rendered by us here, nothing is now beyond our reach, therefore, none else among the gods is more adorable than you are.

## \|\| 1.160.51 \|\|

*evamuktvā'diteḥ putro jagāmādarśanaṃ raviḥ \|*  
*brahmādayopi te harṣaṃ prāpurdevasya darśanāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereafter, Sungod — the sun of Aditi, then disappeared. Brahma and other gods felt delighted at the sight of the universal form of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.160.52 \|\|

*evaṃ brahmādayo devāḥ pūjayitvā divākaram \|*  
*gatāste paramāṃ siddhiṃ gaṃdharvā ṛṣayastathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Similarly, Brahma and other gods, Gandharvas and Rishis also adored the Sungod and achieved great success.

## Chapter 161. Merits of the Sun worship

## \|\| 1.161.1 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*evametadyathāttha tvaṃ bhāskaro daivataṃ param \|*  
*nāstyādityasamo devo nāstyādityasamā gatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shatanika said — You have described the Sungod as Mahadeva. This is totally correct No god comparable with the Sungod exists.

## \|\| 1.161.2-3 \|\|

*ādityamūlamakhilaṃ trailokyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*bhavatyasmājjagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rudreṃdropeṃdrakeṃdrāṇāṃ vipreṃdra tridivaukasām \|*  
*dyutirdyutimatāṃ kṛtsnā tejo yatsārvalaukikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. There is no doubt that the Sungod is the main cause of the entire universe, who creates the gods, humans, the Rakshasas besides the entire world. O great Brahmana! Shiva, Indra and Upendra (Vishnu) besides all other gods posses the lustre of the god of the sky. The entire world is illuminated by the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.161.4 \|\|

*sarvātmā sarvalokeśo mahādevaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*sūrya eva trilokasya mūlaṃ paramadaivatam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He is the universal soul, the lord of all the lokas, Mahadeva and Prajapati. Surya is the main cause for the building of the three lokas.

## \|\| 1.161.5 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃjāyate sarvaṃ tatraiva pravilīyate \|*  
*bhāvābhāvau hi lokanāmādityānniḥsṛtau purā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The entire universe emerging out of him gets ultimately absorbed in him. Therefore, the maintenance and absorption of the lokas by the Sungod is predestined.

## \|\| 1.161.6 \|\|

*jagajjyeṣṭho graho vipra pradīptaḥ prabhavo raviḥ \|*  
*tatra gacchaṃti nidhanaṃ jāyaṃte ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Brahmana, the best planets of the world even when resplendent, their lustre is attributed to the Sungod only. They get absorbed in him, they are also repeatedly born of him alone.

## \|\| 1.161.7-8 \|\|

*kṣaṇā muhūrtā divasā rātripakṣāśca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*māsāḥ saṃvatsarāścaiva ṛtavaśca yugāni ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sa eṣa kālaścāgniśca dvādaśātmā prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*prabhāsayati vipreṃdra trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The moments, muhurtas, nights, fortnights, the months, years, seasons, the four yugas and periods, as well as Prajapatis with twelve names, represent him. O great Brahmana, all the mobiles and immobiles of the three worlds have been illuminated by him.

## \|\| 1.161.9 \|\|

*tasmādasya dvijaśreṣṭha pūjane yatphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tanme brūhi prayatnena prasādapravaṇo bhava \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Therefore, O best of the Brahmanas, what is the extent of merits earned by a person by worshipping the Sungod? You please tell me.

## Chapter 162. The Solar religion

## \|\| 1.162.1 \|\|

*sumaṃturuvāca \|*  
*bhānuṃ pratiṣṭhāpya naraḥ sarvadevamayaṃ vibhum \|*  
*prāpnotyamaratāṃ vīra tejasā ravisannibhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — Consecrating the image of Surya, a person becomes resplendent like the Sungod and then achieves the nectar like position.

## \|\| 1.162.2 \|\|

*yo bhānuṃ dveṣṭi saṃmohātsarvadevanama skṛtam \|*  
*naro narakagāmī syāttasyasaṃbhāṣaṇādapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A person, who out of delusion becomes envious of the Sungod, such a talkative person falls in the heaven ultimately.

## \|\| 1.162.3 \|\|

*bhānumiṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sarvayatnairvidhānataḥ \|*  
*yatpuṇyaphalamāpnoti tadekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Making all the efforts in an appropriate manner, one who consecrates his family god Surya’s image, he achieves the great merit, the details of which you listen from me attentively.

## \|\| 1.162.4 \|\|

*sarvayajñatapodānatīrthadeveṣu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ sthāpya bhānuṃ labhennaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A person who achieves the merit for the performing of all the sacrifices, tapas, charities, visiting of holy places and the worship of gods, the merit equivalent to crores of times more is achieved by a person with the consecration of the Surya image.

## \|\| 1.162.5 \|\|

*yo bhānuṃ sthāpayedbhaktyā vidhipūrvaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*sarvāṃgamuditaṃ puṇyaṃ labhetkoṭiguṇaṃ naraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O great monarch, a person who consecrates the image of the Sungod in the prescribed manner, he earns crores of times more merit.

## \|\| 1.162.6 \|\|

*mātṛjānpitṛjāṃścaiva yatra codvahate striyam \|*  
*kulatrayaṃ samuddhṛtya śakraloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In case, the image is consecrated by a woman, then her mother’s, father’s and husband’s families are totally redeemed and they are honoured in the abode of Indra.

## \|\| 1.162.7-8 \|\|

*bhuktvā vipulānbhogānpralaye samupasthite \|*  
*jñānayogaṃ samāsādya tatraiva pravimucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*atha vā rājyamākāṃkṣejjāyate saṃbhavāṃtare \|*  
*saptadvīmasamudrāyāḥ kṣiteradhipatirbhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Thus, a person enjoying all the pleasures on earth, at the time of destruction, by means of jnanayoga gets absorbed in the Sungod. One who is desirous of the kingdom in future births, he becomes the ruler of the earth surrounded by the seven oceans.

## \|\| 1.162.9 \|\|

*yatkṛtvā pārthivaṃ byomni arcayetsarvadevakam \|*  
*samūlamakhilaṃ tena trailokyaṃ pūjitaṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One who worships the clay image of the vyoma form of the Sungod, he is considered to have worshipped the three worlds. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.162.10 \|\|

*ihaiva dhanavāñcchrīmā nsoṃte'rkatvamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*trisaṃdhyaṃ kīrtayedvyoma kṛtvā biṃbena pārthivam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Making the Surya image in clay and worshipping it thrice a day, singing his kirtana, he becomes quite rich in this world and ultimately achieves the Sayujya moksha of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.162.11-12 \|\|

*śataikādaśakaṃ yāvattasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*anena saha dehena bhānuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate kṣitau \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pāpahā sarvamartyānāṃ darśanātsparśanādapi \|*  
*uddhārayecca saṃsthāpya kulānāmekaviṃśatim \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Thus, by adoring a hundred and eleven forms of the Sungod in clay, one achieves great merit, the details of which are being revealed. You please listen. The sun remains on earth in the form of clay. By having a look at the image and also by touching the same, all the sins of the people are washed out. By consecrating his image, the twenty one families are redeemed.

## \|\| 1.162.13-16 \|\|

*gīrvāṇaiḥ sahito nityaṃ modate divi sūravat \|*  
*yo'pi piṣṭamayaṃ vyoma sarvagaṃdhopaśobhitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kusumaiḥ susugaṃdhaiśca phalaiśca vividhairnṛpa \|*  
*bhakṣyalehyarasaiścaiva kṛtadīpairalaṃkṛtaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nānārasamāyuktaṃ nānāgaṃdhasamanvitam \|*  
*tasya dakṣiṇapārśve tu vinyasedaguruṃ budhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dadyādvai paścime bhāge śrīkhaṃḍaṃ caṃdanaṃ śubham \|*  
*uttare caṃdanaṃ dadyādraktaṃ dadyācca pūrvataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. Ultimately, the person lives happily in the heaven with the gods. By creating a vyoma with powders of different colours and fragrance, it should be decorated with fragrant flowers, various types of fruits, eatables and tasteful food. It should be decorated with lamps of ghi. On the right side of it, various types of gems and fragrance, combined with Agaru should be placed. On its west side, the pieces of auspicious sandal paste should be placed. To the north of it, the sandal paste should be placed. On the east, the paste of red sandal should be used.

## \|\| 1.162.17-18 \|\|

*evaṃ vittānusāreṇa kṛtvā vibhavavistaram \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe tu saptamyāṃ bhāska rasya nivedayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sakṛdeva tu yaḥ kuryādvyoma bharatasattama \|*  
*yatphalaṃ hi bhavettasya tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Thus, according to one’s means, it should be richly decorated and dedicated for lord Bhaskara on the dark seventh moon day. O best of the race of Bharata, in case, this type of vyoma is created even once, the merit one earns is going to be spoken by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 1.162.19 \|\|

*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*niṣkalaḥ sarvago bhūtvā praviśetparamavyayam \|*  
*tejasā ravisaṃkāśaḥ prabhayārkasamaprabhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Getting freed from all the sins, worldly sufferings and the kalas, becoming moveable at every place, he becomes resplendent like the Sungod, and ultimately achieves the Sayujya moksha.

## \|\| 1.162.20 \|\|

*pāṃsunā krīḍamāno yaḥ kuryādvyoma hyakāryataḥ \|*  
*sa rājanbhavate rājā parvateṣu samaṃtataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A child, while playing with the particles of dust and unintentionally creates a vyoma, he becomes the ruler of the mountains.

## \|\| 1.162.21 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva pātrāṇāṃ paraṃ pātraṃ vibhāvasuḥ \|*  
*etatsaṃtārayedyasmādatīva narakārṇavāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Surya is conceived to be the best of the actors in the world, because it is through him only, the ocean of the universe is crossed by a person.

## \|\| 1.162.22 \|\|

*tasya pātrasya māhātmyaṃ dhruvamakṣayamādiśet \|*  
*tasmāttasmai sadā deyamaprameyaphalārthibhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The importance of that actor is said to be unshakable which has no decline. Therefore, a person desirous of enormous merit, should always keep or he should continue to give for the sake of the Sungod in the yajna, something or the other.

## \|\| 1.162.23 \|\|

*ravau dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ baliṃ pūjāṃ nivedayet \|*  
*anaṃtaphalamādiṣṭaṃ brahmādisurasattamaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With the charities or other offerings made for the sake of the Sungod, including homa, japam, offerings presents and the worship, one achieves enormous success. This has been revealed by the best of the gods.

## \|\| 1.162.24 \|\|

*bhaktyā vittānusāreṇa yaḥ kuryādālayaṃ raveḥ \|*  
*sogneyaṃ yānamāruhya modate saha bhānunā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person, who according to his means, builds a temple for the Sungod, then emplaning over the Agneya, he moves in the air with the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.162.25 \|\|

*mahāvibhavasāropi yaḥ kuryādbhaktivarjitam \|*  
*alpe mahati vā tulyaṃ phalamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A person, who inspite of his being immensely rich, but being devoid of the devotion of the Sungod, has built a small temple, he does not achieve any merit for the same, like a pauper.

## \|\| 1.162.26 \|\|

*vittaśāṭhyena yaḥ kuryādvittavānapi mānavaḥ \|*  
*na sa phalamavāpnoti pralobhākrāṃtamānasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Inspite of being rich, when a person out of wickedness, does not spends much on the temple of Surya, such a greedy person also does not earn any merit for building a temple.

## \|\| 1.162.27 \|\|

*tasmāttribhāgaṃ vittasya jīvanāya prakalpayet \|*  
*bhāgadvayaṃ ca dharmārthe anityaṃ jīvanaṃ yataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Therefore, a third of the earnings of one’s life should be spent by a person on his ownself, while the third of the same should be spent over the religious performance, because the life is perishable.

## \|\| 1.162.28 \|\|

*bhaktyā pracoditaṃ kuryādalpavitto'pi yo naraḥ \|*  
*mahāvibhavasāro'pi na kuryādbhaktivarjitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Even when a person is not so rich, still he should perform the religious functions with devotion. Therefore, inspite of a person being enormously rich, but devoid of devotion, he should not perform such tasks (building of temple etc.)

## \|\| 1.162.29 \|\|

*sarvasvamapi yo dadyādarke bhaktivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*na tena dharmabhāgī syādbhaktirevātra kāraṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A person who being devoid of devotion, gives everything in charity for the sake of the Sungod, he would never achieve dharma. Because it is devotion alone, which makes a person religious minded.

## \|\| 1.162.30 \|\|

*na tapobhirvibhorugrairna ca sarvairmahāmakhaiḥ \|*  
*gacchedekaṃ puraṃ divyamarke bhaktiyuto nṛpa \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In fact, the Suryaloka cannot be achieved even with the performing of terrific tapas and several types of yajnas. Only a devoted person could achieve the divine abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.162.31 \|\|

*ruciraṃ śubhaśailotthaṃ kuryāyastu ravergṛham \|*  
*trisaptakulasaṃyuktaḥ sūryalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A person who builds a Sun temple with the auspicious stone slabs, he makes his twenty one generations to achieve the place of Surya.

## \|\| 1.162.32 \|\|

*yanmayā koṭiguṇitaṃ kṛtaṃ syādiṣṭakāmyayā \|*  
*dviparārdhaguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ śailaje'pi vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I have already stated that with the control of one’s desires, one earns crores of times more merit. Therefore, the learned people should be aware of the fact that with the construction of a temple with stones, one earns double the merit.

## \|\| 1.162.33-34 \|\|

*mṛcchailena samaṃ jñeyaṃ puṇyamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ \|*  
*yatra tatra gataḥ kuryādbhaktyā puṇyaṃ bhagālayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śailotthamiṣṭakābhirvā dṛḍhaṃ dārumayaṃ śubham \|*  
*sa gacchetparamaṃ sthānaṃ bhānoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*gairikaṃ yānamāruhya yaḥ kuryāddhṛtabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The rich person who builds the temple with mud and stone, his merit earned as well as the one earned by a poor person, there would be no difference. Therefore, wherever it be possible, the Sun temple should be built in stone. Thus, the construction of the Sun temple should be made, since the Sun has invincible lustre. The one who does so, he achieves the best of the place.

## \|\| 1.162.35 \|\|

*krīḍamāno'pi yaḥ kuryādbālabhāve'rkamaṃdiram \|*  
*so'rkalokamavāpnoti vimānavaramāsthitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A child who during his childhood plays building a Sun temple, he also boarding the best plane, achieves the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.162.36-39 \|\|

*puṣpamālākulaṃ divyaṃ dhūpagaṃdhādivāsitam \|*  
*apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ sarvakāmamukhapradam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tatra rūḍho mahārāja vatsaraṃ vṛndamuttamam \|*  
*uṣitvā bhāskarapure pūjyamānastu daivataiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kramādāgatya loke'sminrājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmasaṃpanno yaśasā ca narādhipa \|\| 38 \|\|*

*paśyanpariharañjaṃtūnmārjanyā mṛdusūkṣmayā \|*  
*śanaiḥ saṃmārjanaṃ kuryāccāṃdrāyaṇaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. O great king, boarding the plane which is decorated with flower garlands, having the fragrance of incense and divine decorations, surrounded by the Apsaras, the plane fulfills all the desires. He lives in Suryaloka for long honoured by all the gods there, and ultimately returns to earth, and becomes a noble king here. O king, all his activities related to dharma, artha and kama are well performed. Finding the insects in the temple, a person who carefully brooms the temple, he earns the merit of performing Chandrayana vrata.

## \|\| 1.162.40 \|\|

*putrārthaṃ dehajīrṇāyā vandhyāyāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*rogārtānāṃ ca bhūtānāmārogyārthaṃ prapūjayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. A barren women should worship the Sungod even upto old age, similarly, the sick and ailing persons should also worship the Sungod for their recovery from the diseases.

## \|\| 1.162.41-42 \|\|

*gṛhītvā gomayaṃ svacchaṃ sthāne ca patitaṃ śubhe \|*  
*uparyupari saṃtyajya pratyagraṃ jantuvarjitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vastrapūtagomayena yaḥ kuryādupalepanam \|*  
*paśyettu sukhitāñjaṃtūṃścāṃdrāyaṇaśataṃ labhet \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The cowdung should be brought from an auspicious place, it should be filtered with the cloth and the land of the temple should be plastered with it, leaving the upper part of the temple. One who does so, achieves the merit of performing a Chandrayana vrata.

## \|\| 1.162.43 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryātsarvakāryāṇi vastrapūtena vāriṇā \|*  
*sa muniḥ sa mahāsādhuḥ sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who performs all the tasks with the water filtered with cloth, he is be treated as a Mum, a sage or a great ascetic. He surely achieves the position of mobility.

## \|\| 1.162.44-45 \|\|

*kṣaraṃti sarvadānāni yajñahomabalikriyāḥ \|*  
*akṣaraṃ tu mahādānaṃ sukhadaṃ sarvadehinām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nairaṃtaryeṇa yaḥ kuryātpakṣaṃ saṃmārjanārcanam \|*  
*varṣamekaṃ śataṃ divyaṃ suraloke mahīyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. All types of charities, yajnas, homas and offerings are said to be perishable. But for all the living beings, the akshara is non-perishable and everlasting. It is comfortable and is treated to be the great donation. A person who attends to the dusting, cleaning or brooming of a temple, he is honoured in the solar region for a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.162.46 \|\|

*tasyāṃte ca caturveda surūpaḥ priyadarśanaḥ \|*  
*ādyaḥ sarvaguṇopeto rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thereafter, he emerges as the immensely learned person, well-versed in all the four Vedas, loveable by all and becomes the foremost of the kings, leaning towards religion activities and possessing all the virtues.

## \|\| 1.162.47 \|\|

*saṃparkeṇāpi yaḥ kuryānnaraḥ karma bhagālaye \|*  
*sopi saumanasaṃ gatvā puraṃ krīḍati nityaśaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. One who works with others in the Sun temple, he also reaching the heaven, sports there.

## \|\| 1.162.48 \|\|

*tāvadbhramaṃti saṃsāre duḥkhaśokapariplutāḥ \|*  
*na bhajaṃti raviṃ bhaktyā yāvatsarve'pi dehinaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. All the living beings, having been overpowered with grief and sufferings, keep on wandering on earth, till such time they worship the Sungod with devotion.

## \|\| 1.162.49 \|\|

*samāsaktaṃ tathā cittaṃ jantorviṣayagocare \|*  
*yadyarko na bhavaddevaḥ ko muñcedeva bandhanāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The minds of the living beings always get attracted towards the worldly pleasures. Under these circumstances, how could they be redeemed without the Sungod?

## \|\| 1.162.50-52 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryātkuṭṭimāṃ bhūmiṃ darpaṇodarasannibhām \|*  
*nānāvarṇavicitrāṃ ca vicitra kusumojjvalām \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kvacitkalaśavinyastāṃ paṃkajairupaśobhitām \|*  
*ramyāṃ manoramāṃ saumyāmarkāyatanasaṃsadi \|\| 51 \|\|*

*yāvaddaṃḍā bhavedbhūmiḥ samaṃtācca suśobhanā \|*  
*tāvadyugasahasrāṇi sūraloke mahīyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. A person who make the floor of the Sun temple shining like the mirror, decorates it with various types of flowers, besides the lotus flowers and the kalashas and further beautifies it, he enjoys the stay in the heaven, a thousand times longer than the number of the length of the place in dandas. He is worshipped there.

## \|\| 1.162.53 \|\|

*kārayeccitraśāstrajñaiścitrakarmārkamaṃdire \|*  
*vicitraṃ yānamāruhya citrabhānorgṛhaṃ vrajet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. An efficient painter who makes the paintings in the Sun temple, then boarding a wonderful plane, he achieves the abode of Chitragupta.

## \|\| 1.162.54-55 \|\|

*yāvatsa devarūpāṇi graharūpāṇi lekhayet \|*  
*tāvadyugasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhavedbhūmiḥ samaṃtācca yaḥ kuryādarkamaṃdi ram \|*  
*ārāmāvasathādīnāṃ labhedāmūlyakaṃ phalam \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. For a thousand yugas, there should be a vast area around the Sun temple, where the lawns and orchards should be developed besides raising accommodation for the stay of the people. A person who does so, earns enormous merit.

## Chapter 163. Worship of flowers in solar religion

## \|\| 1.163.1 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*bhāskarasya mahābāho bhānoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*snānakāle prakurvīta jayaśabdādimaṃga lam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sumantu said — O valorous one, at the time of taking bath, one should recite the welfare mantras, besides performing the japam.

## \|\| 1.163.2-5 \|\|

*padmasvastikaśaṃkhaṃ tu śrīvatsaṃ dvijasattama \|*  
*hemarūpādipātreṣu kalpitaṃ gomayādibhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nānāvarṇakasaṃyuktairakṣataistilataṃdulaiḥ \|*  
*svacchaiśca dadhisaṃmiśrairyathāśobhaṃ prapūritaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dravyapīṭhapradīpāśca bhūtāśvatthādipallavaiḥ \|*  
*auṣadhībhiśca medhyābhiḥ sarvabījairyavādibhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saptamyādiṣu sarveṣu ṣaṣṭhyādiṣu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhabheryādibhiḥ kuryādvādyaghoṣaṃ suśobhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. One should make lotus, Svastika symbol, a conch or Shrivatsa symbol in vases of gold or silver, with cowdung etc. Thereafter, the unbroken rice, sesamum seeds, rice and fresh curd should be mixed. Then, the beautiful asanas, lamps, shoots of holy fig tree, the herbs, barley and other seeds should be made to sprout. Then, on the sixth or seventh moon day, singing accompanied with music should be arranged.

## \|\| 1.163.6-7 \|\|

*trisandhyaṃ vedanirghoṣaṃ kurvīta phalamuttamam \|*  
*kuryānnīrājanaṃ caiva śaṃkhavāditramaṃgalaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yāvannīrājanaṃ kuryātparvāṇi vidhivadravau \|*  
*tāvadyugasahasrāṇi sūraloke mahīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The Vedic hymns should be recited during all the three Sandhya times, which yield enormous merits. Blowing the conches and playing other musical instruments on the auspicious occasions, if the mere Aratis are performed for the Sungod, then a person is worshipped in the abode of the Sungod for the thousands of yugas.

## \|\| 1.163.8 \|\|

*kapilāpañcagavyena kuśavāriyutena vai \|*  
*snāpayenmantrapūtena brahmasnānaṃ hi tatsmṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The calf of a white cow should be bathed using panchagavya, kusha and water, because its known as Brahma bath.

## \|\| 1.163.9 \|\|

*yastvekamapi sarvebde brahmasnānaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*sa muktaḥ sarvapāpaistu sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A person who performs the Brahma-snana for the Sungod even once, he getting relieved of all the sins, is adored in the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.163.10 \|\|

*kapilāpañcagavyena dadhikṣīrayutena ca \|*  
*snānaṃ daśaguṇaṃ jñeyaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ narādhipa \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O king, when the calf is washed with the panchagavya of the white cow or with the curd and milk of the other cow together with water, one earns ten times more merit.

## \|\| 1.163.11 \|\|

*ṛbhavo vīramuddiśya dehaśuddhiṃ ca śāśvatīm \|*  
*kapilāmāharennityaṃ munidevāgninirmitām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. For the purification of their own bodies, the gods should serve a white cow, which was created for the purpose of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.163.12 \|\|

*kāpilaṃ yaḥ pibecchūdro devakāryārthanirmitam \|*  
*sa pacyate mahāghore suciraṃ narakārṇave \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For the purpose of the gods, the white cow was created, and when a Shudra drinks her milk, he falls in a painful heaven and continues to suffer for long.

## \|\| 1.163.13 \|\|

*varṣakoṭisahasreṇa yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*ghṛtābhyaṃgena sūryasya dahetsarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The ghi should be offered to the Sungod and by so doing, the sins accumulated during crores of years, get destroyed. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.163.14 \|\|

*kalpakoṭisahasraistu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam \|*  
*vajrasnānena tatsarvaṃ dahatyagniriveṃdhanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the Sungod is offered the vajra — snana, the sins collected during the crores of years, are burnt out as the fuel is burnt up by the fire god.

## \|\| 1.163.15 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ ca kṛtasnāno yajetsūryaṃ sakṛnnaraḥ \|*  
*kulānyuddhṛtya sapteha sūryaloke mahīyate \|*  
*vasuhemādiyuktaṃ ca kṣīrasnānasya tatsamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A person, taking a bath on the seventh moon day, even when worship the Sungod once, his seven generations get redeemed and he is honoured in the Suryaloka. A person, who bathes the image of the Sungod with milk, then he earns the merit equivalent to earning of the gems and gold.

## \|\| 1.163.16 \|\|

*sakṛdāḍhakena payasā yo bhānuṃ snāpa yennaraḥ \|*  
*rājatena vimānena so'rkaloke mahīyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. With 950 grams of milk, when a person offers bath to the Sungod, then mounting over the plane of silver, he is respected in the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.163.17 \|\|

*snāpya dadhnā sakṛdbhānuṃ sa triloke mahīyate \|*  
*madhunā snapayitvā taṃ śukraloke mahī yate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A person, who bathes the image of the Sungod even once with curd, he is respected in all the three lokas. A person who bathes the image of Surya once with the honey, he is respected in the abode of Venus.

## \|\| 1.163.18 \|\|

*uddhṛtya śālipiṣṭena vāyulokeṣu pūjyate \|*  
*snānamikṣuraseneha yaḥ sūrye sakṛdācaret \|*  
*sa gopatipuraṃ gacchetsarvakāmasamanvitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A person who bathes the image of Surya with the flour as well as the powder of rice, he is respected in the Vayu-loka or the abode of the Wind-god. When a person bathes the Sungod image with the juice of sugarcane even once, then getting all his desires fulfilled, he achieves the abode of Surya.

## \|\| 1.163.19 \|\|

*phalodakena yo bhānuṃ sakṛtsnāpayate naraḥ \|*  
*utsṛjya pāpakalilaṃ pitṛloke mahīyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person who bathes the Sungod even once with the fruit juice, he getting relieved of all the sins, is adored n the Pitri-loka.

## \|\| 1.163.20-21 \|\|

*śrīkhaṃḍavāriṇā snāpya sakṛdbhānuṃ narā dhipa \|*  
*caṃdrāṃśunirmalaḥ śrīmāṃścaredātreyamaṃdire \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vastrapūtena toyena yadyarkaṃ snāpayetsakṛt \|*  
*sa sarvakāmatṛptātmā rākādhipapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. O monarch, a person who bathes the image of the Sungod with sandalwood water, he getting relieved of all his sins, is respected in the abode of the Moon. A person who bathes the image of the Sungod with the water filtered with cloth, then getting all his desires fulfilled, he reaches the abode of Manu.

## \|\| 1.163.22 \|\|

*āpo hiṣṭheti japyena gaṃgātoyena bhārata \|*  
*gairikeṇa vimānena brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Bharata, by sprinkling Ganga water over the Surya image and uttering the hymn apohishthe, the person mounting over the gold plane, is honoured in the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.163.23 \|\|

*karpūrāgurutoyena yo'rkaṃ snāpayate sakṛt \|*  
*snāpya bhānuṃ sakṛnmantraiḥ saptamyāṃ samupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*sa kulānekaviṃśatimuttārya ravimāvrajet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person, who fasting on the seventh moon day, bathes the image of the Sungod with water mixed with camphor and agaru, he redeeming his twenty one generations, reaches the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.163.24 \|\|

*pitṛnuddiśya yo bhānuṃ snāpayecchītavāriṇā \|*  
*tṛptāḥ svarga vrajaṃtyāśu pitaro narakādapi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person, for the sake of his manes, when bathes the image of Sungod with cool water, all his names turning as kings, proceed to the heaven.

## \|\| 1.163.25 \|\|

*bhānuṃ śītāṃbunā snāpya dhāroṣṇapayasā saha \|*  
*snāpya paścādvrateneśamagniloke mahīyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. A person who bathes the Sungod with the just extracted cow milk and performs the vrata, he is honoured in the Agni-loka.

## \|\| 1.163.26 \|\|

*etatsnānatrayaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā tu bhārata \|*  
*aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Bharata, thus bathing the Sungod with three types of baths, a person achieves the merit of performing a thousand Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.163.27 \|\|

*mṛtkumbhāttāmrakumbhaistu snānaṃ śataguṇaṃ matam \|*  
*raupyaiḥ pādottaraṃ puṇyaṃ darśanātsparśanaṃ param \|*  
*sparśanādarcanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ghṛtasnānamataḥ param \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By bathing the Surya images with earthen or copper pitchers, one earns a hundred times more merits. By using the silver pitchers, he earns one fourth of the merit, or even more. To touch the image is better than simply looking at it. The worship of an image is better than the mere touch of it, but the bathing of the image with ghi is immensely meritorious.

## \|\| 1.163.28 \|\|

*ihāmutra kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ ghṛtasnānena naśyati \|*  
*saptajanma kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ purāṇaśravaṇena tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. All the worldly sins and those of the other world are at once washed out with the bathing of the image with ghi. Similarly, the sins of the seven births vanish with the listening of the Puranas.

## \|\| 1.163.29 \|\|

*daśāparādhāṃstoyena kṣīreṇa tu śataṃ kṣamet \|*  
*sahasraṃ kṣamate dadhnā ghṛtenāpyayutaṃ kṣamet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With the bathing of the image with water, one is relieved of ten sins. By bathing with water, one is relieved of a hundred sins. By washing the image with curd, one is relieved of a thousand sins. By washing the image with ghi, one is relieved of a thousand sins.

## \|\| 1.163.30 \|\|

*nairantaryeṇa yo māsaṃ ghṛtasnānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*daśaikādaśa kulānīha nayetsūryasya maṃdiram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A person who bathes the Sungod for a month continuously with ghi, he makes his twenty one generations to achieve the place of Surya.

## \|\| 1.163.31 \|\|

*snānaṃ palaśataṃ jñeyamabhyaṃgaḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*palānāṃ dvisahasreṇa mahāsnānamati śrutiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The bathing material should not be in any case less than (the quantity to be used) in a hundred moments. Similarly, the anointing of the oil over the body should not be less than the twenty five moments. The duration of the great bath has been defined to be of a thousand moment duration.

## \|\| 1.163.32-33 \|\|

*ghṛtābhyaṃgaṃ ghṛtasnāna bhānoḥ kuryyāddvijottama \|*  
*yaśca godhūmacūrṇaistu kaṣāyairdarbhasaṃmitaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*daśadhenusahasrāṇi yaddattvā labhate phalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate sarvamarkasyodvartane kṛte \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Therefore, O best of the Brahmanas, the Sungod should be given a bath in ghi. A person who washes the Sungod with the wheat flour resembling the colour of kusha grass, and then cleans the image with the same, he earns the merit comparable with the donating of ten thousand cows.

## \|\| 1.163.34 \|\|

*arghyaṃ puṣpaphalopetaṃ yastvarkāya nivedayet \|*  
*sa pūjyaḥ sarvalokeṣu arkavanmodate divi \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A person who offers arghya and fruits as oblation to the Sungod, he getting adored by all the lokas, enjoys all the comforts in the heaven like the Sungod himself.

## \|\| 1.163.35 \|\|

*gaṃdhatoyena saṃmiśramudakāddvādaśottaram \|*  
*pañcagavyasamāyuktamarghyaṃ śataguṇaṃ nṛpa \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A person, when he offers arghya with fragrant water, earns twelve times more merit. When the arghya of panchagavya is offered, the related merit is increased to hundred times.

## \|\| 1.163.36 \|\|

*yoṣṭāṃgagarbhamāpūrya bhānormūrdhni nivedayet \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi ramate cārkamaṃdire \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. When an arghya with ashtanga is offered over the head of the Surya image, he enjoys comforts in the Sun temple for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.163.37-38 \|\|

*āpaḥ kṣīraṃ kuśāgrāṇi ghṛtaṃ dadhi tathā madhu \|*  
*raktāni karavīrāṇi tathā raktaṃ ca canda nam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*aṣṭāṃga eṣa argho vai brahmaṇā parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*satataṃ prītijanano bhāskarasya narādhipa \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. The ashtanga has been described by Brahma as the combination of water, milk, shoots of kusha grass, ghi, curd, honey, flowers of red oleander, as well as paste of red sandal paste, which has always been the favourite of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.163.39 \|\|

*dāturvaiṇavapātreṇa datte'rghye yatphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tasmācchataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ mṛtpātreṇa narādhipa \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The merit one earns by offering the arghya in the bamboo vase, a hundred times more of the same is earned by offering the arghya in an earthen vase.

## \|\| 1.163.40 \|\|

*tāmrārghyapātradānena puṇyaṃ śataguṇaṃ matam \|*  
*pālāśapadmapatrābhyāṃ tāmrapātre phalaṃ labhet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By offering the arghya in a copper vase, the related merit is further increased by a hundred times. Similar merit is achieved by offering oblation in the leaves of Palasha or lotus.

## \|\| 1.163.41 \|\|

*raupyapātreṇa vijñeyaṃ lakṣārghyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇapātravinyastamarghyaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. By offering the arghya with a silver vase, the merit is increased to a lakh of times. There is no doubt about it. By offering arghya with a golden vase, the related merit is increased by a crore of times. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.163.42 \|\|

*evaṃ snānārghyanaivedyabalidhūpādiṣu kramāt \|*  
*pātrāṃtaraviśeṣeṇa tatphalaṃ tūttarottaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thus, with the offering of bath, arghya, bali and incense etc., the related merit is increased more and more.

## \|\| 1.163.43 \|\|

*raupyapātrapradānena yatpuṇyaṃ vedapārage \|*  
*tāmrapātrapradānena tasmācchataguṇaṃ ravau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By offering arghya in a silver vase, a great merit is achieved by a person, but when the offering of oblation is performed with a copper vase, the related merit is increased to hundred times.

## \|\| 1.163.44 \|\|

*phalaṃ koṭisuvarṇasya yo dadyādvedapārage \|*  
*sūryāya rūpyapātre tu bhavetpuṇyaṃ tato'dhikam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A person who offers oblation in a golden vase for Surya, he earns a crores of times more the related merit. By offering the oblation in the silver vase, the merit is further increased.

## \|\| 1.163.45 \|\|

*suvarṇapātraṃ yo dadyādbhāskarāya mahīpate \|*  
*na śakyaṃ tasya tadvaktuṃ puṇyaṃ pātraviśeṣataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. A person who offers the offerings in n golden vase for the Sungod, the extent of its related merit is so vast that it is beyond imagination.

## \|\| 1.163.46 \|\|

*tulyameva phalaṃ proktaṃ sarvamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ \|*  
*tayorabhyadhikaṃ tasya yastvarke bhāvanādhikaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus, the similarity in the earning of the merit by a rich as well as a pauper has also been defined. The merit greater than both of them is said to be achieved by a person whose devotion towards the Sungod keeps on growing.

## \|\| 1.163.47 \|\|

*vibhave sati yo mohānna kuryādvidhivistaram \|*  
*naiva tatphalamāpnoti pralobhākrāṃtamānasaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Inspite of his being quite rich, when a person out of illusion, does not perform the religious rites in an exhaustive manner, such a greedy person foils to achieve any merit.

## \|\| 1.163.48 \|\|

*tasmānmantraiḥ phalaistoyaiścandanādyaiśca yatnataḥ \|*  
*tadanaṃtaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ bhaktirevātra kāraṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, one should make all efforts to recite mantras besides presenting the fruits, water, and sandal paste etc. to the Sungod. By so doing, one earns enormous merit. The devotion alone is most important during the worship of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.163.49 \|\|

*varṣakoṭiśataṃ divyaṃ sūryaloke mahīyate \|*  
*gaṃdhānulepanaṃ puṇyaṃ dviguṇaṃ candanasya tu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A person who does so is honoured in the Suryaloka for a hundred crores of years. With the plastering of the sandal paste, he earns double the merit, which is the same for offering the flowers, which further increases to eighty times.

## \|\| 1.163.50-51 \|\|

*gaṃdhāccaturguṇaṃ jñeyaṃ puṣpamaṣṭaguṇaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*kṛṣṇāguru viśeṣeṇa dviguṇaṃ phalamādiśeta \|*  
*tasmācchataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kuṃkumasya vidhīyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

*caṃdanāgurukarpūraiḥ ślakṣṇapiṣṭaiḥ sakuṃkumaiḥ \|*  
*bhānuṃ paryāptamālipya kalpakoṭiṃ vaseddivi \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. The merit would be increased to four times or even eight times, when the offering of (lowers is made. With the offering of the black agaru, one attains double the merit. One earns a hundred times more merit with the offering of kunkum.

## \|\| 1.163.52-53 \|\|

*sa dīvyetsuravṛndena puṇyagaṃdhaiḥ pralepitaḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vīra mitrapure vaset \|\| 52 \|\|*

*bhaktyā nivedya arkāya tālavṛṃtaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vīralokaṃ mahīyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Making powder of the sandal, again and camphor, the kunkum should be mixed in the same, making a paste. The same paste should be applied over the body of the Surya image. One who does so, he lives in the heaven for a croore of kalpas. Thereafter, he lives in the Suryaloka for a further period of ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.163.54 \|\|

*māyūraṃ vyajanaṃ dattvā sūryāyātīva śobhanam \|*  
*varṣakoṭiśataṃ pūrṇaṃ prabhaṃjanapure vaset \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. One who offers foe bunch of palm tree fruits to the Sungod, he lives in foe Suryaloka for ten thousand years. Making a beautiful tan of the wings of peacock, when offered to foe Sungod, foe donor lives in foe Suryaloka for a hundred crores of years.

## \|\| 1.163.55-56 \|\|

*puṣpairaraṇyasaṃbhūtaiḥ patrairvā girisambhavaiḥ \|*  
*aparyuṣitaniśchidraiḥ proṣitairjaṃtuvarjitaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ātmārāmabhavaiścaiva puṣpaiḥ saṃpūjayedravim \|*  
*puṣpajātiviśeṣeṇa bhavetpuṇyaṃ tato'dhikam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. One should worship the Sungod with uninjured, wild flowers of mountains, without insects or with the flowers of his own orchard. Because of the good quality of the flowers, foe related merit also increases.

## \|\| 1.163.57-60 \|\|

*tapaḥśīlaguṇopeta iti hāsavidi dvije \|*  
*dattvā daśa suvarṇasya niṣkānyallabhate phalam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*karavīrasya kusumamarkāya vinivedayet \|*  
*labhate tatphalaṃ vīra yathāha bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*evaṃ puṣpaviśeṣeṇa phalaṃ tadadhikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*jñeyaṃ puṇyaṃ rasajñena yathā syāttannibodha me \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sadā puṣpasahasrebhyaḥ karavīraṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*bilvapatrasahasrebhyaḥ padmamekaṃ narādhipa \|\| 59 \|\|*

*padmapuṣpasahasrebhyo bakapuṣpaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*bakapuṣpasahasrebhyo mudgaraṃ paramucyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. By giving in charity ten nishkas (ancient gold coins) to an ascetic Brahmana, devoted to his preceptor, the related merit the donor earns would be equal to the merit one earns by offering oleander flowers to the Sungod. This has been ordained by the Sungod himself. Because of the importance of the donation, the donor achieves greater merit. The reality about it is well known by the alchemists. I am going to tell you about the same. The importance of oleander flowers is far greater than other thousand flowers. The merit of a lotus is considered to be greater than a thousand wood apple leaves which are better than a thousand Agate — grandiflora or Baka pushpa. A mudgara is more important than a thousand flowers.

## \|\| 1.163.61 \|\|

*kuśapuṣpasahasrebhyaḥ śamīpatraṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*śamīpuṣpasahasrebhyo nṛpa nīlotpalaṃ param \|*  
*sarvāsāṃ puṣpajātīnāṃ pravaraṃ nīlamutpalam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. As compared to a thousand kusha flowers, the leaves of the shami tree are better; out of a thousand shami leaves, a blue lotus is better. In fact, the blue lotus is the best of all the flowers.

## \|\| 1.163.62-63 \|\|

*raktotpalasahasreṇa nīlotpalaśatena ca \|*  
*raktaiśca karavīraiśca yastu pūjayate ravim \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi kalpakoṭiśatāni ca \|*  
*vasedarkapure śrīmānsūryatulyaparākramaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. A person who worships the Sungod with a thousand red lotus flowers, a hundred blue lotus flowers, besides the flowers of red oleander flowers, he becoming as valorous as the Sungod himself, lives in the Suryaloka for a hundred cores of kalpas.

## \|\| 1.163.64 \|\|

*śeṣāṇāṃ puṣpajātīnāṃ yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*tatphalasyānusāreṇa sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Whatever rewards for the other types of flowers have been narrated, the donor is adored in the Suryaloka accordingly.

## \|\| 1.163.65-66 \|\|

*śamīpuṣpaṃ bṛhatyāśca kusumaṃ tulyamucyate \|*  
*karavīrasamā jñeyā jātīvijayapāṭalāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*śvetamaṃdārakusumaṃ sitapuṣpaṃ ca tatsamam \|*  
*nalacaṃpakapunnāgamudgarāṇāṃ samāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Shami flowers and the Brihati (a medicinal plant) flowers are equal in merit. The jasmine flowers, besides vijaya and patala flowers equate with oleander. The flowers known as Naga, Champaka, Punnaga and Mudgara are all equal.

## \|\| 1.163.67 \|\|

*gaṃdhavaṃtyapavitrāṇi kusumāni vivarjayet \|*  
*gaṃdhahīnamapi grāhyaṃ pavitraṃ yatkuśādikam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Inspite of their possessing the fragrance, the inauspicious flowers should be discarded. But an auspicious flower inspite of having no fragrance like kusha, should also be accepted.

## \|\| 1.163.68-70 \|\|

*sāttvikaṃ taddhi kusumamapavitraṃ ca tāmasam \|*  
*mudgarāṇi kadaṃbāni rātrau deyāni sūraye \|\| 68 \|\|*

*divāśeṣāṇi puṣpāṇi tyajedupahatāni ca \|*  
*mukulairmārcayedbhānumapakvaṃ na nivedayet \|\| 69 \|\|*

*phalaṃ kvathitaviddhaṃ ca yatnātpakvamapi tyajet \|*  
*alābhe bata puṣpāṇāṃ patrāṇyapi nivedayet \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. The auspicious flowers are considered to be taken to be virtuous, while the inauspicious flowers lack virtue. The flowers of Mudgara and Kadamba trees can be offered to the Sungod even during the night. AH other flowers which fade out during the day, must be discarded. The unblossomed flowers should not be offered to the Sungod. Similarly, the unripened fruits are also prohibited from being offered to the Sungod. The fruits which are ripened by artificial means are also prohibited from being offered to the Sungod. In the absence of the fruits, even the fruit leaves also could be offered.

## \|\| 1.163.71-72 \|\|

*patrāṇāmapyalābhe tu phalānyapi nivedayet \|*  
*phalānāmapyalābhena tṛṇagulmauṣadhīrapi \|\| 71 \|\|*

*oṣadhīnāmabhāve tu bhaktyā bhavati pūjitaḥ \|*  
*pratyekaṃ muktapuṣpeṇa daśasauvarṇikaṃ phalam \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. In the absence of leaves, the fruit could be offered. When the fruits are in shortage, even the grass cluster of plants or herbs can be offered. When none of the above fruits or leaves are forthcoming, one should worship the Sungod with devotion alone. A person who worships the Sungod with the flowers which are naturally fallen from the trees, he earns the merit equivalent to the donation of ten nishkas of gold to a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.163.73 \|\|
