30\. Getting devoted when a person gives donation to an appropriate person, such a donation has been called to be the best. Therefore, those who are desirous of everlasting merit, then the donation should be given with devotion.

## \|\| 1.189.31 \|\|

*yaddānaṃ śraddhayā pātre vidhivatpratipāditam \|*  
*tadanaṃtaphalaṃ jñeya mapi vā bhāramātrakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The giving of charity with devotion in a vase has been said to be the best, because by so doing, one achieves the endless merit and those given otherwise are burden like.

## \|\| 1.189.32 \|\|

*ārteṣu dīneṣu guṇānviteṣu yaḥ śraddhayā svalpamapi pradadyāt \|*  
*sa sarvakāmānsamupaiti lokāñcchraddhaiva dānaṃ pravadaṃti tajjñāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A person who gives to the people who are suffering or are virtuous, even a little of food etc., all his desires are fulfilled. This has been ordained by the learned people.

## \|\| 1.189.33 \|\|

*śraddhā dānaṃ paraṃ jñeyaṃ śraddhā eva tapaḥ param \|*  
*śraddhāṃ yajñamuśantīha śraddhā paramupoṣitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The faith or devotion itself is the best charity, the tapas, yajna are the best fasting.

## \|\| 1.189.34 \|\|

*athāhiṃsā kṣamā satyaṃ hrīḥ śraddheṃdriyasaṃyamaḥ \|*  
*dānamiṣṭaṃ tapo dhyānaṃ daśakaṃ dharmasādhanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Non-violence, forgiveness, truth, modesty, control of sense organs, charities, yajna, tapas and meditation are the means to dharma.

## \|\| 1.189.35 \|\|

*haṃtavyastaiḥ samastairvā sūryadharmairanuṣṭhitaiḥ \|*  
*sūryaukasāṃ ca saṃprāptergatirekā prakīrtitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By patronizing any one of them or all, when the Surya rites are performed, one achieves the abode of the Sungod. Because this is the only method of achieving his lokas and is said to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.189.36 \|\|

*yathā bhūḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ śāṃtiratiśayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kuryātpuṇyaṃ mahattasmānmama lokepsayā sudhī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. As the earth has been praised for the peace of all, similarly, those who are desirous of achieving my lokas, should perform the meritorious deeds.

## \|\| 1.189.37 \|\|

*parastrīdravyasaṃkalpaṃ yaḥ sāpekṣaṃ karoti ca \|*  
*gurumārtamaśaktaṃ vā videśe prasthitaṃ tathā \|*  
*aribhiḥ paribhūtaṃ ca saṃtyajeccaiva pāpakṛt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One who owns the riches meant for some other woman, or that of his preceptor, or the one who is weak, or the one who is about to depart for the foreign land, or the one who has been humiliated by the enemies, he is said to be the grave sinner.

## \|\| 1.189.38 \|\|

*tadbhāryāmitraputreṣu yaścāvajñāṃ karoti ca \|*  
*ityetatpātakaṃ jñeyaṃ guruniṃdāsamaṃ bhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. To denounce a woman, friend or his sons, or the preceptor is said to be the grave sin.

## \|\| 1.189.39 \|\|

*brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*mahāpātakinastvete tatsaṃyogī ca pañcamaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One who kills a Brahmana, a drunkard, a thief or the one who units with the wife of the preceptor, is to be condemned. Those who keep contact with them are the great sinners.

## \|\| 1.189.40 \|\|

*krodhāddveṣādbhayāllobhādbrāhmaṇasya vadeta yaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāṃtikaṃ mahādoṣaṃ brahmahā sa udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. A person who uses painful language against a Brahmana out of anger, he commits a grave sin and is known as the killer of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.189.41 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ ca samāhūya yācamānamakiṃcanam \|*  
*yannāstīti ca yo brūyātsa cāṇḍālaṃ udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A person who calls for a poor Brahmana and then refuses to give him anything, he is known as a Chandala.

## \|\| 1.189.42 \|\|

*devadvijagavāṃ bhūmiṃ pūrvadattāṃ hareta yaḥ \|*  
*pranaṣṭāmapi kāle tu tamāhurbrahmaghātakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A person who usurps the land given for the gods, Brahmana and the cows inspite of it’s being unproductive, he is known as a killer of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 1.189.43 \|\|

*adhītya yo raverjñānaṃ parityajati maṃdadhīḥ \|*  
*surāpena samaṃ jñeyaṃ tasya pāpaṃ ca suvrata \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O noble one, a person, who after attaining the knowledge of Surya later disowns it, he becomes a fool and his sin equates with the one who drink wine.

## \|\| 1.189.44-46 \|\|

*agnihotraparityāgaḥ paṃcayajñiyakarmaṇām \|*  
*mātāpitṛparityāgaḥ kūṭasākṣyaṃ suhṛdvadhaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*apriyaṃ sūryabhaktānāmabhakṣyasya ca bhakṣaṇam \|*  
*evaṃ niraparādhānāṃ prāṇināṃ ca pramāraṇam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sarvādhipatyameteṣāṃ nāsti devapurottame \|*  
*ātmalokādhipatyaṃ tu yacchetsarvajatpatiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. By disowning of Agnihotra, the five yajnas practices, the parents, to appear as a deceitful witness, the killing of a friend, to speak harsh words to the devotees of the Sungod, to eat prohibited food, to kill the innocent people, a person never achieves a comfortable position in the heaven. But the Sungod, getting pleased with such a person, can bestow the leadership of his own loka to him.

## \|\| 1.189.47 \|\|

*kecidatraiva mucyante jñānayogaparā narāḥ \|*  
*āvartaṃte punaścānye saṃsāre bhogatatparāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Some people in this world utilize their life for achieving of jnana-yoga, while others for worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 1.189.48 \|\|

*tasmādvimokṣamanvicchanbhogāsaktiṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*viraktaḥ śāṃtacittātmā sauralokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, a person, who is desirous of salvation, should cut short his worldly pleasures, because only a peaceful and detached person can achieve the abode of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.189.49 \|\|

*yaccāpyasaktahṛdayā japantīmaṃ prasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*teṣāmapi vadatyekaḥ svānubhāvānurūpataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Those who are no more attracted towards the worldly pleasures, they only recite the name of the Sungod. For such people, because of their nature, the Sungod is always present for their protection.

## \|\| 1.189.50 \|\|

*tannārcayanti ye bhānuṃ sakṛducchiṣṭadehinaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ piśācaloke tu bhogānbhānuḥ prayacchati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Therefore, after achieving of the human body, one who does not meditate upon Surya even once, he is made to face the pleasures of Pishacha-loka.

## \|\| 1.189.51 \|\|

*dvirjapaṃti ca ye bhānuṃ krūrāḥ saṃkruddhalocanāḥ \|*  
*rakṣoloke ravisteṣāṃ mahābhāgyaṃ prayacchati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. While living in the Rakshasas loka, one who getting enraged with red eyes, recite the name of Surya twice, the Sungod makes him quite virtuous.

## \|\| 1.189.52 \|\|

*trirarcayanti ye bhānuṃ madyamāṃsaratā narāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣiloke ravisteṣāṃ bhogāndivyānprayacchati \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Those who are engaged in drinking and eating meat, but worship the Sungod thrice a day, the Sungod provides the divine pleasure for them in Rishi-loka.

## \|\| 1.189.53 \|\|

*ye nṛtyagītaṃ kurvaṃti triścaturdhā yadṛcchayā \|*  
*sūryasyāgre tu te yāṃti gaṃdharvabhavanaṃ khaga \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. A person who sings or dances three or four times before the Sungod, he achieves the abode of Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.189.54 \|\|

*lokāḥ khyātiṃ samuddiśya pūjayaṃti ca gopatim \|*  
*teṣāṃ śakrālaye bhānuḥ kāmāntsarvānprayacchati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Those who worship the Sungod for getting their own glory, the Sungod bestows on them all the desires of Indraloka.

## \|\| 1.189.55 \|\|

*kāmāsaktena cittena yaḥ ṣaḍarcayate ravim \|*  
*prājāpatye ravistasya loke bhogānprayacchati \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Getting uninterested in the passions, one who worship the Sungod half a dozen times in a day, the Sungod bestows him the pleasures of Prajapatya loka.

## \|\| 1.189.56 \|\|

*navakṛtvorcayedyastu citrabhānuṃ khagādhipa \|*  
*sa yāti viṣṇusālokyaṃ viṣṇunā saha modate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O best of the birds, a person who worships Chitrabhanu Surya nine times, he earns a place in Vishnuloka and enjoys all the pleasures with the same god.

## \|\| 1.189.57-60 \|\|

*tasmādapi paraṃ sthānaṃ yadbhūtānāṃ manoharam \|*  
*aprameyaguṇaidivyairvimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*asaṃkhyairvastubhirvyāptaṃ gairikai raktacitrakaiḥ \|*  
*nānāgṛhasamākīrṇaiḥ sūryakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tatsthānaṃ te pragacchaṃti arcayanti ca ye dvijān \|*  
*tatra loke khagaśreṣṭha vasaṃti viharaṃti ca \|*  
*tasmādapi paraṃ sthānaṃ jyotiṣkaṃ sauramucyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

*evaṃ sūryānubhāvena nikṛṣṭenāpi karmaṇā \|*  
*naraiḥ sthānānyavāpyante śraddhābhāvānurūpataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. The place, which is still better and quite pleasant for the living beings, having the lustre of crores of suns, possessing unparalleled virtues and the planes, and fulfills all the desires, filled with innumerable objects besides wonderful types of houses, is achieved by the people, who worship the Brahmana. O best of birds, such people live and roam about in that place. The Jyotishloka is still better than that and is the place of Surya. Thus, the people getting devoted to the Sungod, even with the performing of the petty deeds, because of their devotion, achieve the favourable places.

## Chapter 190. Discussion between Sungod and Aruni

## \|\| 1.190.1 \|\|

*saptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*tārārūpavimānānāmimāḥ saṃti ca koṭayaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ kuryāttu namaskāraṃ tasyaiva ca phalaṃ bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saptashvatilaka said — The planes which are in the forms of stars and are of crores in number, can be achieved by a person who offers his salutation to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.190.2 \|\|

*ityetā gatayaḥ proktā mahatyaḥ sauradharmiṇām \|*  
*tasmātsauraḥ sadā dharmaḥ kartavyaḥ sukhamicchatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Those who embrace the solar dharma, this is the only way. Therefore, the one who is desirous of comforts, should accept the solar faith.

## \|\| 1.190.3 \|\|

*idānīṃ pāpanicayāḥ sthūlā narakahetavaḥ \|*  
*te samāsena kathyante manovākkāyasādhanaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Presently, I am talking exhaustively about the solid heap of sins, which are foe cause of the hell and they are produced by foe people with their mind, speech and activities.

## \|\| 1.190.4 \|\|

*gavāṃ mārge vane cāgneḥ pure grāme samarpaṇam \|*  
*ityetānīha pāpāni surāpānasamāni ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The sins like foe destruction of foe path of cows, the forests, cities as well as foe villages, with foe fire flames are foe sins resembling the drinking of wine.

## \|\| 1.190.5-6 \|\|

*vane sarvasya haraṇaṃ narastrīgajavājinām \|*  
*gobhūsamīpajātānāmoṣadhīnāṃ ca khecara \|\| 5 \|\|*

*candanāgurukarpūrakastūrīpaṭṭavāsasām \|*  
*hastanyāsāpa haraṇaṃ rukmasteyasamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The usurping of the place of shelter in foe forest for the humans, women, elephants and horses, the herbs that are growing close to the cowpeas, besides the sandalwood, agaru, camphor, scarf, and the trust money given by hand when usurped by a person, he earns the sin of stealing gold.

## \|\| 1.190.7-8 \|\|

*kanyānāṃ varayogyānāmākarṣaṇamasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*putramitrakalatreṣu gamanaṃ bhaginīṣu ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kumārīsāhasaṃ ghoramaṃtyajastrīniṣevaṇam \|*  
*savarṇāyāśca gamanaṃ gurutalpasamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The sudden kidnapping of a girl of marriageable age or to have sex with the wives of a friend, a sister and to have forceful union with a maid girl, or uniting with a terrific Shudra woman, or with the woman of one’s own caste, or with the wife of a preceptor, earn equal types of sins.

## \|\| 1.190.9-21 \|\|

*mahāpātakatulyāni pāpānyuktāni yāni tu \|*  
*tāni pātakasaṃjñāni brūmahe copapātakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dvijāyārthaṃ pariśrutya na prayacchati yo dvija \|*  
*sadbhāryāṇāṃ ca saṃtyāgaḥ sādhubandhutapasvinām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gobhū hiraṇyavastrāṇāmapahāraḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*īśvarārpitabuddhīnāṃ pīḍanaṃ sumahatkṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yaḥ pīḍāmāśramasthāna ācaredalpikāmapi \|*  
*tadbhūtyuparibhūtasya paśudhānyadhanasya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kūpadhānyapaśusteyamayājyānāṃ ca yājanam \|*  
*yajñārāmataḍāgānāṃ dārāpatyasya vikrayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tīrtha yātropavāsānāṃ vrate ca japakarmaṇi \|*  
*strīdhanānyupakarṣaṃti ye janāḥ pāpakarmaṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*arakṣaṇaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāmapradānaṃ ca dhānyavṛddhyupasevanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*devāgnisādhusādhvīnāṃ nindā gobrāhmaṇasya ca \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ vā parokṣaṃ vā rājamāṇḍalikānapi \|\| 16 \|\|*

*utsannapitṛdevāśca svakarmatyāginaśca ye \|*  
*duḥśīlā nāstikāḥ pāpāḥ sadasacchūnyavādinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*evaṃ kāme pravṛtte tu viyonau paśuyoniṣu \|*  
*rajasvalāsvayonau tu maithunaṃ yaḥ samācaret \|\| 18 \|\|*

*strīputramitrasaṃprīte rārāmocchedakāśca ye \|*  
*janasyāpriyavaktāro janābhiprāyabhedinaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhettā taḍāgavaprāṇāṃ saṃkramāṇāṃ rasasya ca \|*  
*ekapaṃktisthitānāṃ ca paṃktibhedaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ityetaistu narāḥ pāpairupapātakinaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

9-21. All the sins which have been related above are the grave sins. Now, I shall tell you about the semi-sins. A person who cannot fulfil his words given to a Brahmana, disown a chaste wife, or usurp the cows of ascetics, besides the cows, land, gold and the costumes making all the efforts, and tortures the devotee of the lord Ishvara, or causes even the slightest pain in the ashramas of the sages, the riches, animals, wealth, cereals, wells and to steal the minds, performing of yajnas for a person unfit for the purpose, to sell the orchards of the yajna or sell the tanks, wife and the sons or while performing japam holy places and steal their belongings, not to protect the wife, to unite with a woman drinking wine, to himself consume the cereals of the Rishis instead of giving them, to denounce the gods, noble people, chaste woman, Brahmanas, the kings openly or otherwise, disowning of the manes, relinquishing of one’s own duty, besides the wicked, an unbeliever, sinful, heretic, becoming lustful uniting with barren women or the animals, or unite with a woman in period, destroyer of the love of the son or a friend, besides the orchard, to speak harsh words to all, to carry tale of one person to the other, destruction of a tank, stepwells and courageous juices, besides creating difference among the people sitting in the same line, these all are the activities which have been termed as mischievous.

## Chapter 191. Conversation between Saptashvatilaka and Aruna

## \|\| 1.191.1-8 \|\|

*saptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*ye gobrāhmaṇasasyānāṃ sādhūnāṃ tu tapasvinām \|*  
*dūṣakāścaiva vartaṃte narā narakagāminaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pariśrameṇa tapyante ye'pare tasya sūcakāḥ \|*  
*paradāraratānāṃ ca kanyāyā dūṣakāśca ye \|\| 2 \|\|*

*goṣṭhāgnijalaramyāsu tarucchāyānageṣu ca \|*  
*tyajaṃti ye purīṣāṇi ārāmā yataneṣu ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*madyapānaratā nityaṃ gītavādyaratā narāḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodhamadāviṣṭā raṃdhrānveṣaṇatatparāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pākhaṇḍamatasaṃyuktā vṛthā saṃlāpa kautukāḥ \|*  
*ye mārgānuparudhaṃti parasīmāṃ haraṃti ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kūṭaśāsanakartāraḥ kūṭakarmakṛto narāḥ \|*  
*dhanuṣaḥ śilpiśastrāṇāṃ yaḥ kartā yaśca vikrayī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nirdayotīvabhṛtyeṣu paśūnāṃ damakaśca yaḥ \|*  
*mithyā pravadato vācamākarṇayati yaḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*svāmimitragurudrohī māyāvī capalaḥ śaṭhaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ye bhāryāputramitrāṇi bālavṛddhakuśāturān \|*  
*bhṛtyānatithibandhūṃśca tyajaṃti ca bubhukṣitān \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Saptashvatilaka said — Such of the degraded people who cause pain to cows, Brahmanas and the ascetics, are found in abundance on earth. Moreover, there is also no death of the people who carry the news of the ascetics performing tapas, to others. Those who enjoy the wives of others or the denouncers of girls, besides those who drop refuse near cow’s pen, the fire place, tanks, under the shade of mountains or the shades of trees, in orchards, in the temples or in their vicinity, those who drink wine daily, the singers or those who play on the musical instruments, lustful, those full of rage, arrogance, those who search for the weaknesses of others, the wicked or those who talk uselessly with delight, those who obstruct the path spreading the thorns, those who usurp the boundaries of others, those who rule with secret intrigues, those who manufacture the bows or other weapons or those who sell them, those who are cruel over the servants, those who suppress the animals, those who listen to the false talk about others quite interestingly, those who cheat the master, preceptor and the friends, those who are cheats, unstable, wicked and falling painful because of hunger, thirst, wife, sons and friends besides children, old people and sick people, besides the servants, guests and relatives, and those who disown the guests and relatives, all of them have been considered to be the sinners.

## \|\| 1.191.9 \|\|

*yaḥ svayaṃ pakvamaśnāti viprāyānnaṃ na yacchati \|*  
*vṛthā pākaḥ sa vijñeyo brahmavādiṣu garhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A person who himself enjoys the delicious food instead of first giving it to a Brahmana, his food is of no use. Such a person is denounced among the learned people.

## \|\| 1.191.10-12 \|\|

*niyamaṃ svayamādāya ye tyajaṃtyajiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*pravrajyāvasitā ye ca rahasyānāṃ tu bhedakāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ye tāḍayaṃti gāṃ mūḍhāstrāsayaṃti muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*durbalaṃ na ca puṣṇaṃti pranaṣṭānnānviṣaṃti ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pīḍayaṃtyatibhāreṇa akṣayaṃ vāhayaṃti ca \|*  
*vṛṣāṇāṃ vṛṣaṇānanye pāpiṣṭhā gālayaṃti hi \|*  
*vāhayaṃti ca gāṃ vaṃdhyāṃ te pāpiṣṭhā narādhamāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Similarly, those who do not observe the rules properly, undisciplined, those who even after embracing sanyasa revert again as householders, those who reveal the secrets, those who cause pain to the weak and cows again and again, those who destroy the food, who load excessive weight over the bulls and make them carry it for long distance, crush the testicles of the bulls making them unfit for production, those who carry weight by the barren cows, all of them are considered to be degraded and the sinful persons.

## \|\| 1.191.13 \|\|

*anarthavikalaṃ hīnaṃ bālavṛddhakṛśānugam \|*  
*nānukaṃpaṃti ye mūḍhāste yāṃti narakaṃ narāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A pauper, a person with upset sense organs, useless, who does not show mercy for the children, old people and the ailing persons, are all fools and therefore, fall in the hell.

## \|\| 1.191.14-15 \|\|

*ajāvikā māhiṣikāḥ savitrīvṛṣalīpatiḥ \|*  
*kṣatraviṭśūdravṛddhāśca svadharmavihatāḥ sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śilpinaḥ kārukā veśyāḥ kṣemakāranṛpadhvajāḥ \|*  
*nartakyo jyotiṣi hatāḥ sarve narakagāminaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Those who rear the sheep, goats, husband of a Shudra woman, a Kshatriya who is deprived of his dharma besides a Vaishya, Shudra, old woman, a painter, mason, the harlots, the female dancers besides those who end their lives by self burning or by lightning, all of them fall in the hell.

## \|\| 1.191.16-20 \|\|

*ghṛta tailānupānāni madhumāṃsarasāsavam \|*  
*guḍekṣukṣīraśākānhi dadhimūlaphalāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tṛṇāni kāṣṭhaṃ puṣpāṇi bījauṣadhimanuttamām \|*  
*upānacchatra śakaṭamāsanaṃ śayanaṃ mṛdaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tāmraṃ sīsaṃ trapuṃ kāṃsyaṃ śaṃkhādyaṃ ca jalodbhavam \|*  
*vārkṣaṃ vā vaiṇavaṃ vāpi gṛhopakaraṇāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*aurṇakārpāsakauśeyabhaṃgapaṭṭodbhavāni ca \|*  
*sthūlasūkṣmāṇi saṃmūḍhā ye ca lokā haraṃti vai \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evamādīni cānyāni dravyāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*narakeṣu dhruvaṃ gacchedyau hareta pumānbalāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

16-20. The people who steal ghi, oil or the food items made by them, honey, meat, juice, ferments, sugarcane balls, sugarcane, payasam, vegetables, curd, roots, fruits, grass, wood, flowers, seeds, herbs, the shoes, the umbrellas, bullock carts, the seat, sleeping beds, the clay, copper, lead, tin, bronze, the conch born of the water, the sheep, bamboo fruit, the material for the building of a house, (woolen, cotton and silk) garments, lamp, stone grinders, all of them are considered to be fools. These as well as the other things when are stolen by the people, they surely fall in the hell.

## \|\| 1.191.21 \|\|

*yadvā tadvā tu pārokṣyamapi sarṣapamātrakam \|*  
*apahṛtya naro yāti narakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even the small things of a person which could be as small as the mustard seed is when stolen in the absence of the owner, the person who steals fall in the hell. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.191.22 \|\|

*evamādyairnaraḥ pāpairutkrāṃteḥ samanaṃtaram \|*  
*śarīrayātanārthaṃ tatpūrvakāyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person committing several such sins, he regains birth in order to face the reward of his evil deeds.

## \|\| 1.191.23 \|\|

*yamaloke vrajedevaṃ śarīreṇa yamājñayā \|*  
*yamadūtairmahāghorairnīyamānaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He faces painful situations with the same body, he is then carried by the horrible messengers of Yama to Yamaraja.

## \|\| 1.191.24 \|\|

*devamānuṣajīvānāmadharmaniratātmanām \|*  
*dharmarājaḥ smṛtaḥ śāstā sughorairvividhairvadhaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Dharmaraja exercises his control over the people and the gods, who indulge themselves into the sinful deeds.

## \|\| 1.191.25 \|\|

*vinayābhāvayuktānāṃ pramādā tsvalitātmanām \|*  
*prāyaścittairbahuvidhaiḥ pātakaṃ naṣṭatāmiyāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sins of arrogant people, the proud people and those with weak souls, can be removed by performing various types of repentances.

## \|\| 1.191.26-27 \|\|

*pāradārikacorāṇāmanyāyavyavahāriṇām \|*  
*śāstā kṣitipatiḥ proktaḥ pracchannānāṃ ca dharmarāṭ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmātkṛtasya pāpasya prāyaścittaṃ samācaret \|*  
*nābhuktasyānyathā nāśaḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Because those who steal the wives of others and those who conduct themselves in an illegal manner, are ruled by the king above them, while those who commit sins secretly, they have to be disciplined by Dharmaraja. Therefore, it is necessary to do repentance for a sin that has already been committed. Because otherwise, even after trying for a hundred and crores of kalpas, the sins cannot be destroyed without facing the reward of the same.

## \|\| 1.191.28 \|\|

*yaḥ karoti śubhaṃ karma kārayedanumodayet \|*  
*kāyena manasā vācā sa viṃdetottamaṃ sukham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person who performs the noble deeds using his mind, speech and activities, or gets them done by others, he achieves the best of pleasures.

## \|\| 1.191.29 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktā pāpabhedāttridhā gatiḥ \|*  
*tathānyā gatayaścitrāḥ kathyaṃte karmabhedataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In this day, the three divisions of the sins have been explained. I am now speaking about the astonishing types of results achieved from the same.

## Chapter 192. Discussion between Saptashvatilaka and Aruna

## \|\| 1.192.1-2 \|\|

*gtsaptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*saṃtrāsajananaṃ ghoraṃ pāpānāṃ pāpakāriṇām \|*  
*garbhasthairjāyamānaiśca bālaistaruṇamadhyamaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*strīpunapuṃsakairvṛddhairgaṃtavyaṃ sarvajaṃtuṣu \|*  
*śubhāśubhaphalaṃ tatra bhoktavyaṃ dehibhistathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Saptashvatilaka said — The sinful people have to undergo horrible tortures as a result of the sins committed by them, irrespective of his being a child, a youthful person, a middle aged one. eunuch or an eldery one All of them, whether in womb or taking too small or big sized bodies, have to bear the reward of their deeds the same body, whether they are good or bad.

## \|\| 1.192.3 \|\|

*citraguptādibhiḥ sarvairdharmasthaiḥ satyavādibhi \|*  
*proktaṃ vai dharmarājasya nikaṭe yacchubhāśubham \|*  
*avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ tadvicāritam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Chitragupta and others are all truthful and religious minded, who remain in close contact with Dharmaraja. whatever the good or bad decision of noble or evil deeds are taken, they are to be borne by such people definitely.

## \|\| 1.192.4-5 \|\|

*tatra ye śubhakarmāṇaḥ saumya cittā dayānvitāḥ \|*  
*te narā yāṃti saumyena yathā yamaniketanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yaḥ pradadyāddvijeṃdrāṇāmupānatkāṣṭhachatrakam \|*  
*sa ca dharmeṇa mahatā sukhaṃ yāti yamālayam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Those of them, who had performed the noble deeds, having kind hearts and are merciful, the way they proceeds to the abode of Yama, is being stated by me. A person, who gives the shoes and the umbrella with wooden rod to a Brahmana, he being a religious ended one, reaches the abode of Yamaraja quite comfortably.

## \|\| 1.192.6 \|\|

*sopānatko naro yastu devāyatanamāviśet \|*  
*viśeṣato garbhagṛhaṃ sa saṃtrāsamupāśnute \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. One who enters the temple with his shoes on, as a punishment, he has to face the sufferings.

## \|\| 1.192.7 \|\|

*sopānatkāni dānāni tathānnaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dānaviśeṣeṇa dharmarājapuraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yasmādyāti sukhenaiva tasmāddharmaṃ samācaret \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A person who donates particularly the food and the shoes, then because of that charity, he comfortably moves towards the abode of Yama Therefore, it k essential for all to follow dharma.

## \|\| 1.192.8 \|\|

*ye punaḥ krūrakarmāṇo narāḥ pāparatāḥ khaga \|*  
*te ghoreṇa tathā yāṃti dakṣiṇena yamālayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Such of the sinful people who move in cruel ways, they move over the southern and difficult path and are made to enter the city of Yama.

## \|\| 1.192.9 \|\|

*ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāmaśīti ca \|*  
*vaivasvatapuraṃ jñeyaṃ nānārūpamiti sthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The different types of cities of Yama are located at a distance of eighty six thousand yojanas.

## \|\| 1.192.10 \|\|

*samīpasthamivābhāti narāṇāṃ śubhacāriṇām \|*  
*pāpānāmatidūrasthaṃ tathā raudreṇa gacchatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those cities appear to be at a short distance for those who perform the good deeds, while for the sinners they appear to be at a very long distance which is difficult to cover, besides being painful.

## \|\| 1.192.11 \|\|

*tīkṣṇakaṃṭakayuktena śarkarānicitena ca \|*  
*kṣuradhārātinistriṃśaiḥ pāṣāṇaiściṃtitena ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The path of the sinner is infested with sharp edged thorns, stone pebbles, is narrow, complex with the surface as sharp as the barber’s razor. Besides, there are huge stones obstructing the path.

## \|\| 1.192.12-13 \|\|

*kvacidarkeṇa mahatā duraṃtaiścaiva khātakaiḥ \|*  
*lohaśaṃkubhirācchinnāstathā khaḍgaiḥ samanvitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tataḥ patadbhirvimalaiḥ parvatairvṛkṣasaṃkulaiḥ \|*  
*pretaprākārayuktena yāṃti mārgeṇa duḥkhitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. At places one has to face the extreme heat of the sun, deep and bottomless ravines, with the iron nails spread everywhere, clusters of thick trees, the mountainous regions, where walking is extremely difficult and can be covered only by falling quite a few times. Thus suffering, a sinful person has to move through the path of goblins.

## \|\| 1.192.14-15 \|\|

*kvacidviṣamagartābhiḥ kvacilloṣṭhaiḥ sapicchalaiḥ \|*  
*sutaptavālukābhiśca tathā tīkṣṇaiśca śaṃkubhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*anekaśākhāracitairvyāptairvaṃśavanaiḥ kvacit \|*  
*kaṣṭena tamasaḥ mārga anā laṃbe sudāruṇi \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. At places there are uneven pits to be crossed, at places there are swamps and slippery ground through which the path crosses. Then are hot sands, sharp nails and the bamboos forests wife several branches, which make the path inaccessible. There is complete darkness and fee path has to be crossed in a helpless manner.

## \|\| 1.192.16 \|\|

*atha śṛṃgāṭakairvyāptaiḥ kvaciddāvāgninā punaḥ \|*  
*kvacittaptaśilābhiśca kvacidvyāptaṃ himena tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At places the path is obstructed with thorny trees, while there is the forest fire at some places. There are the burning rocks at places, while there are heaps of snow at some places.

## \|\| 1.192.17-21 \|\|

*kvacidvālukayā vyāptamākaṃṭhāṃtaṃ praveśayet \|*  
*kvacidduṣṭāṃbunā vyāptaṃ kvacicca kariṣāgninā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kvacitsiṃhaiḥ kvacidvyāghrairdaṃśaiḥ kīṭaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*kvacinmahājalaukābhiḥ kvaci dvājagaraiḥ punaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*makṣikābhiśca raudrābhiḥ kvacitsapeṃrviṣolbaṇaiḥ \|*  
*mahāgajeṃdrayūnaiśca balonmattaiḥ pramāthibhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*paṃthānamullikhadbhiśca tīkṣṇa śṛṃgairmahāvṛṣaiḥ \|*  
*mahāśṛṃgaiśca mahiṣairuṣṭrairmattairmadāturaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ḍākinībhiśca raudrābhirvikarālaiśca rākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*vyādhibhiśca mahāghoraiḥ pīḍyamānā vrajaṃti hi \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. At places the heaps of sand are so high feat a person sinks in them upto the head. Some places are filled with the blemished water and at places, the cowdung cakes are burning. Some places are infested with lions, tigers, mosquitoes, terrific insects, horrible types of leeches, groups of pythons, blood sucking flies, terrific and poisonous serpents, huge tuskers who forcefully chum the water, the horrible bulls with sharp horns, or the cow buffaloes with long horns, which obstruct the path with disturbance, intoxicated camels wander in herbs. At places, there are horrible Dakinis and the groups of terrific Rakshasas. Thus, the grave sinners have to move through these paths which is difficult to be crossed and then reach fee abode of Yama.

## \|\| 1.192.22-24 \|\|

*mahāpāśavimiśreṇa mahācaṃḍena vāyunā \|*  
*mahāpāṣāṇavarṣeṇa hanyamānā nirāśrayāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kvacidvidyutprapātena dīryamāṇā vrajaṃti hi \|*  
*patadbhirvajrasaṃghātairulkāpātaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pradīptāṃgāravarṣeṇa dahyamānā vrajaṃti hi \|*  
*mahāṃdhakāraśukreṇa pīḍyamānā vrajaṃti hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. The huge boulders bound in the nooses are carried wife the force of fee wind, which strike the travellers, which one has to bear while crossing fee path alone. Even the huge cities are shattered with the fall of the lightnings. Then, there is great darkness and pain at many places in between the path.

## \|\| 1.192.25-26 \|\|

*mahāmegharavairghorairvitrāsyaṃte muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*tīkṣṇapāṣāṇayuktena pūryamāṇāḥ samantataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mahākṣurāṃbudhārābhiḥ sevyamānā vrajaṃti hi \|*  
*mahāmegharavairghorai rvitrāsyante muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. While in the journey, at time the clouds with thundering sound, repeatedly frighten the travellers. At places, sharp stones are placed. At places, the water falls as sharp as the blades are falling. The clouds with their terrific thundering sound, try to frighten a person who has to travel by the same path.

## \|\| 1.192.27-29 \|\|

*bhṛśaṃ śītena tīkṣṇena rūkṣeṇa mārutena ca \|*  
*itthaṃ mārgeṇa raudreṇa pātheyarahitena ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nirālaṃbena durgeṇa nirjanena samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*aviśrāmeṇa mahatā vigatāpāyadurdharaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nīyaṃte dehinaḥ sarve ye mūḍhāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*iti jñātvā naraḥ kuryātpuṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ca varjayet \|*  
*puṇyena yāti devatvaṃ pāpena narakaṃ vrajet \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. The season is extremely cold where the sharp and dry winds blow. One has to travel through such a path which is quite difficult, in a restless manner, without any obstruction. All the sinners and foolish people are taken by that way. Thus realizing, a person should perform meritorious deeds, because by so doing, one achieves the heaven and with the performing of evil deeds, one falls in the hell.

## \|\| 1.192.30 \|\|

*yairmanāgapi deveśo manasā pūjito raviḥ \|*  
*te kadāpi na paśyaṃti yamasya vadanaṃ khaga \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A person who with utmost devotion worships the Sungod even a little, he does not have to face the Yama.

## \|\| 1.192.31 \|\|

*kiṃ tu pāpairmahāghoraiḥ kiñcitkālaṃ tavājñayā \|*  
*bhavaṃti pretarājānastato yāṃti raveḥ puram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. But the terrific sinners, (when they perform your worship) at your command, (when they serve as your slave), then they achieve a place in the Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.192.32 \|\|

*ye punaḥ sarvabhāvena bhajante bhuvi bhāska ram \|*  
*na te limpaṃti pāpena padmapatramivāṃbhasā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Those who worship the Sungod with utmost devotion, the sins do not touch him as the water does not touch the lotus flower.

## \|\| 1.192.33 \|\|

*tasmātprakuryādbhaktiṃ vai bhāskare satataṃ naraḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā pūjayedbhānuṃ ya icchedvipulaṃ dhanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Therefore, a person should worship the Sungod regularly. Those, who are desirous of enormous riches, should worship the Sungod.

## Chapter 193. The tooth stick

## \|\| 1.193.1 \|\|

*saptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*ayane viṣuve vāre saṃkrāṃtau grahaṇe tathā \|*  
*pūjayetsatataṃ bhānuṃ saptamyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saptashvatilaka said — On the Uttarayana and Dakshinayana, the equinox day, the first day of the month, the day of eclipse, or on the seventh moon day of the month, the Sungod should be worshipped.

## \|\| 1.193.2 \|\|

*vainateya nibodha tvaṃ vidhānaṃ saptamīvrate \|*  
*etaddhi paramaṃ guhyaṃ raverārādhanaṃ param \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O son of Vinata, the process of the Saptami vrata, which is quite secret, during which the excellent worship of Surya has been prescribed (is going to be narrated by me). You please listen.

## \|\| 1.193.3-4 \|\|

*siddhārthakaistu prathamā dvitīyā cārkasaṃpuṭaiḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyā maricaiḥ kāryā caturthī tila saptamī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saptamī caudanairvīra saptamī parikīrtitā \|*  
*ityetāḥ sapta saptamyaḥ kartavyā bhūtimicchatā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The vrata of the first Saptami should be performed with due devotion, while mustard should be given on the second Saptami; the folded form of swallow wart should be given on third Saptami; the black pepper on the fourth Saptami; sesamum should be given and on the seventh Saptami boiled rice are to be given at the conclusion of the rites. Therefore, a person who is desirous of wealth, should perform all the seven Saptamis.

## \|\| 1.193.5-11 \|\|

*tathā cānukrame tāsāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kathayā myaham \|*  
*māghe vā mārgaśīrṣe vā kāryā śuklā tu saptamī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ārtasya tu na niyamaḥ pakṣamāsakṛto bhavet \|*  
*ardhapraharaśeṣe tu kuryādvai daṃtadhāva nam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pañcamyāṃ tatra ye vṛkṣāḥ kāmitāstānvadāmyaham \|*  
*madhūke putralābhaḥ syādduḥkhahā mārkavo bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*badaryā ca bṛhatyā ca kṣipraṃ rogātpramucyate \|*  
*aiśvaryaṃ ca bhavedbilvaiḥ khadireṇa ca saṃcayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śatrukṣayaḥ kadaṃbeṣu arthalābhotimuktake \|*  
*gurutāṃ yāti sarvatra āṭarūṣakasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jñātipradhānatāṃ yāti aśvattho yacchate yaśaḥ \|*  
*karavīrātparijñānamacalaṃ syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śriyaṃ prāpnoti vipulāṃ śirīṣasya nive śane \|*  
*priyaṃguṃ sevyamānasya saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

5-11. I am now revealing the symptoms and process of the vratas. During the month of the Magha or Margashirsha on the day of bright Saptami, the celebration should be made. For a distressed person, there is no binding for the fortnight or the month. Therefore, when a prahara of a day remains, the brushing of the teeth has been prescribed. For the fulfilment of the desire on the fifth moon day, I am speaking about the trees (of which a tooth stick is to be made). By using the tooth stick of Madhuka (Bassia latifolia) one gets a son, by using Bhringaraja the miseries disappear; by using Brihati (a medicinal plant) one is relieved of the disease; by using creeper one achieves riches; by using catechu stick one saves money; by using Kadamba the enemies get destroyed; with the use of the stick of a boney tree one gains profits; by use of Atarushaka one attains importance everywhere; with use of the stick of the holy fig tree one becomes prominent in the caste besides achieving glory. By using the oleander stick, one becomes firm and attains vast knowledge. There is no doubt about it. With the use of Shirsha stick, one achieves enormous wealth and with the use of Priyangu or black mustard, he gains excellent fortunes.

## \|\| 1.193.12-21 \|\|

*abhīpsitārthasiddhyarthaṃ sukhāsīnotha vāgyataḥ \|*  
*kāmaṃ yatheṣṭahṛdaye kṛtvā samabhi maṃtrya ca \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena matimānaśnīyāddantadhāvanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*varaṃ dattvābhijānāsi kāmadaṃ ca vanaspate \|*  
*siddhiṃ prayaccha me nityaṃ daṃtakāṣṭha namo'stu te \|\| 13 \|\|*

*trīnvārānparijapyaivaṃ bhakṣayeddaṃtadhāvanam \|*  
*paścātprakṣālya kāṣṭhaṃ tu śucau deśe vinikṣipet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ūrdhve nipatite siddhistathā cābhi mukhe sthite \|*  
*atonyathā tu patite ānīya punarutsṛjet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*parāṅmukhaṃ yadi bhavettrīnvārāndaṃtadhāvanam \|*  
*asiddhāṃ tu vijānīyānna grāhyā sā tu saptamī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*brahmacārī tu tāṃ rātriṃ svapyānmaṃgalasevayā \|*  
*bibhradvāsonupahataṃ śucirācārasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prāta rutthāya vai khaga \|*  
*prakṣālayenmukhaṃ dhīmānaśnīyāddantadhāvanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*upaviśya śucirbhūtvā praṇamya śirasā ravim \|*  
*japaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ kṛtvā tu juhuyācca hutāśane \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tatoparāhnasamaye snātvā mṛdgomayāṃbubhiḥ \|*  
*vidhivanniyamaṃ kṛtvā maunī śuklāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā vidhiṃ bhaktyā devadevaṃ divākaram \|*  
*svapyāddevasya purato gāyatrījapatatparaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

12-21. For getting his purpose served, one should get himself seated comfortably and recall his desire in his mind with the mantra, while using the tooth stick — “O vegetation, you are aware of my purpose, therefore, for its fulfilment, you bestow above on me. O tooth stick, bestow success on me. Salutation to you always.” Thus, the vegetation should be invoked thrice, and then the person should clean his teeth. Then, after cleaning, the same should be thrown at a neat and clean place. With its fall in upside position or downwards or with its head above, one achieves success. In case it falls otherwise, one should pick it up again and throw it once again. In case, the tooth stick falls upside down thrice, then leasing aside that Saptami, the devotee should start the performance from some other Saptami. The Brahmachari should put on some new clothes and should go to sleep with all his sense organs under control. O bird, when the night is passed, one should rise on the next morning, wash his mouth and brush his teeth using the tooth stick. Purifying himself, he should perform the required japam and then perform homa. Then, he should take bath in the forenoon with clay as well as the cowdung. Then purifying himself with water, he should wear white clothes and worship the Sungod appropriately. Then the Gayatri mantra should be recited and should sleep before the image of the Sungod.

## Chapter 194. Conversation between Sungod &amp; Aruna

## \|\| 1.194.1 \|\|

*saptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yairyairya tphalamaśnute \|*  
*svapne dṛṣṭe tu saptamyāṃ puruṣo niyatavrataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saptashvatilaka said — Thereafter, he should perform Saptami vrata controlling all his sense and the interpretation of the merits achieved by the performer, in respect of each one of the dreams, is being spoken by me.

## \|\| 1.194.2 \|\|

*samāpya vidhivatsarvāṃ japahomādikāṃ kriyām \|*  
*bhūmau śayyāṃ samāsthāya devadevaṃ vicintayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The japam, homa and other rites should be performed appropriately. One should lay down on earth in sleeping posture and should meditate upon the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.194.3 \|\|

*hanta supto yadi naraḥ paśyetsvapne divākaram \|*  
*śakradhvajaṃ vā candraṃ vā tasya sarvāḥ samṛddhayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At that point of time, in case a person finds Surya, Indra, flag, or the Moon, he achieves all types of advancements.

## \|\| 1.194.4 \|\|

*bhṛṃgāracamarādarśakanakābharaṇāni ca \|*  
*rudhirasya srutiḥ keśapātaṃ aiśvaryakārakaḥ \|*  
*svapne vṛkṣādhirohe tu kṣipramaiśvaryamāhave \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When he witnesses small pitcher, flywhisk, mirror, gold ornaments, blood bath, or fall of hair, he achieves riches and by planting of the tree he receives riches in an auspicious place.

## \|\| 1.194.5 \|\|

*dohanaṃ mahiṣīsiṃhīgodhenūnāṃ kare svake \|*  
*bandhaścāsāṃ rājyalābho nābheḥ sparśe tu durmatiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When he witnesses male buffalo, lioness, cow and cows’s milk being milked by him with his own hands, the binding of cows, he achieves the gain with the king. By touching the navel, he becomes wicked minded.

## \|\| 1.194.6-7 \|\|

*aviṃ hatvā svayaṃ khādetsiṃhamaṃbujameva ca \|*  
*svāṃgamasthi hutāśaṃ ca surāpānaṃ khagādhipa \|\| 6 \|\|*

*haime vā rājate vāpi yo bhuṃkte pāyasaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*pātre tu padmapatre vā tasyaiśvaryaṃ samaṃ bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. When he finds a lion or a sheep and then takes the meat, similar would be the case if he eats lotus, his own limbs and bones, besides the fire, drinking of wine in gold or silver vase or in the lotus leaf, he earns enormous riches or fortunes.

## \|\| 1.194.8 \|\|

*dyūte ca vātha vā yuddhe vijayo hi sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*gātrasya svasya jvalanaṃ śirobandhaśca bhūtaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By being victorious in gambling or in the war, he earns enormous pleasures. With the burning of his own body or the turban, one achieves fortunes.

## \|\| 1.194.9 \|\|

*mālyāṃbarāṇāṃ śuklānāṃ hayānāṃ paśupakṣiṇām \|*  
*sadā lābhaṃ praśaṃsaṃti viṣṭhānāṃ cānulepanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When a white horse is seen in foe dream, decorated with the flower garlands or when he finds it plastered with the dung of birds, he always gains profit

## \|\| 1.194.10 \|\|

*hayayāne bhavetkṣipraṃ rathayāne prajāgamaḥ \|*  
*nānāśirobāhutā ca gṛhasthāṃ kurute śriyam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When a person rides a vehicle driven by horses, he gets a child birth. When he finds various types of heads and arms, he attains enormous riches.

## \|\| 1.194.11-12 \|\|

*agamyāgamanaṃ dhanyaṃ vedādhyayanamuttamam \|*  
*devadvijaśreṣṭhavīraguruvṛddhatapasvinaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yadvadaṃti naraṃ svapne satyameveti tadviduḥ \|*  
*praśastaṃ darśanaṃ caiṣāmāśīrvādaḥ khagādhipa \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. By enjoying the company of a fallen woman, he earns respect and with the study of the Vedas, he gets ample reward. Whatever is spoken by a god, a Brahmana, preceptor, an old man and an ascetic in the dream, it proves out to be correct. Their sights as well as blessings are said to be quite praiseworthy.

## \|\| 1.194.13-14 \|\|

*rājyaṃ syātsvaśiraśchede dhanaṃ bahuvadhe bhavet \|*  
*rudite bhakṣyasaṃprāptī rājyaṃ nigaḍabandhane \|\| 13 \|\|*

*parvataṃ turagaṃ siṃhaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gajameva hi \|*  
*mahadaiśvaryamāpnoti yo vikramyādhirohati \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. In case one cuts off his own head in a dream, he becomes a king. By piercing holes, he attains riches; by weeping one earns eatables; by arranging of the veni one becomes a king. By witnessing mountains, horse, lion, an elephant with force or a bull, one gains enormous fortunes.

## \|\| 1.194.15 \|\|

*āgṛhṇāno grahāṃstārā marīciṃ parivartayan \|*  
*unmūlayati parvatāṃśca rājā bhavati bhūtale \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. By accepting the planets and stars, by changing of the Maharishi Marichi, and by uprooting of the mountains, he becomes the ruler of the earth.

## \|\| 1.194.16 \|\|

*dehānniṣkāṃtiraṃtrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca khagādhipa \|*  
*pānaṃ samudrasaritāmaiśvaryasukhakārakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O foremost of the birds, by taking out all the intestines or by drinking of ocean and rivers, one earns enormous comfort.

## \|\| 1.194.17 \|\|

*balaṃ cāṃbunidhiṃ vāpi tīrthapāraṃ prayāti yaḥ \|*  
*tasyāpatyaṃ bhavedvīra acalaṃ ca khagādhipa \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O foremost of the birds, one penetrating the army and the ocean and then performs the pilgrimage, he achieve the brave and stable progeny.

## \|\| 1.194.18 \|\|

*bhavatyarthāgamaḥ śīghraṃ kṛmirvā yadi bhakṣayet \|*  
*aṃgānāṃ ca surūpāṇāṃ lābho darśanameva ca \|*  
*saṃyogaścaiva māṃgalyairārogyaṃ dhanameva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In case a person is bitten by insects, then the riches arrive suddenly; by witnessing the beautiful limbs, one gains profit. By witnessing of welfare sight, he gets an excellent chance, good health and wealth.

## \|\| 1.194.19-20 \|\|

*aiśvaryaṃ rājyalābhaśca yasminsvapna udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*sapta syānnātra saṃdehaścaturbhiḥ śruta uttamaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*paṃcabhiḥ putrabāhulyaṃ ṣaḍbhirāyuḥ sutāndhanam \|*  
*saptabhirvividhānkāmānaṣṭabhirvividhaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Such of the dreams in which one is said to achieve reaches and the kingdom, the seven of them is true and there is no doubt about it; in four of them there is excellent hearing; with five, one gets a number of sons and riches; in seven of them several types of desires are fulfilled and in the eighth one, a person achieves enormous glory.

## Chapter 195. Conversation between Surya and Aruna

## \|\| 1.195.1 \|\|

*anūruruvāca \|*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi saptamīnāṃ paraṃ vidhim \|*  
*sarvāsāmanurūpāṇāṃ kathayasva mahāmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Aruna said — O lord, O great sage, I intend to know process of performing vrata for all the Saptamis. You kindly speak about them in a chronological order.

## \|\| 1.195.2 \|\|

*saptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu vīra khagaśreṣṭha saptamīnāṃ paraṃ vidhim \|*  
*kīrtayiṣyāmi te sarvaṃ yathāvatparipṛcchate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Saptashvatilaka said — O foremost of the birds, I am narrating the process of all the Saptamis at your instance, appropriately.

## \|\| 1.195.3-9 \|\|

*tulyaṃ kila khagaśreṣṭha yathākhyātaṃ vivasvatā \|*  
*śuklapakṣe ravidine pravṛtte cottarāyaṇe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*putradāradhanakṣetre gṛhṇīyātsaptamīvratam \|*  
*ṛṣibhirjñānasaṃpannaiḥ sarvakāmaphala pradaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saptamyaḥ saptaākhyātāstāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|*  
*arkasaṃpuṭakairekā dvitīyā maricaistathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tṛtīyā niṃbapatraiśca caturthī phala saptamī \|*  
*saptamī kāmikā nāmnā vidhimāsāṃ nibodha me \|\| 6 \|\|*

*paṃcamyāmekabhaktaṃ tu kuryānniyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*alpāhāraṃ na kurvīta maithunaṃ dūratastyaje t \|\| 7 \|\|*

*varjayenmadhu māṃsaṃ ca atyamlaṃ ca khagādhipa \|*  
*prabhāte caiva ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu ekaikaparṇasaṃpuṭe \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ghṛtaśālyodanaṃ kṛtvā bhakṣayettu vidhānataḥ \|*  
*anyadannamabhuṃjānaḥ saptamyāṃ bhojanaṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

3-9. This narration would be such, as has been spoken by the Sungod himself in earlier times. When the Sun is in Uttarayana on the bright Sunday, in the Dhanu or ninth sign of zodiac, then the person with a wife and son should start the religious rites. The highly enlightened Rishis possessing the divine knowledge, have mentioned about the seven Saptamis. You better listen to their names. The first one is Arka-Saptami; the second one is of black pepper; the third one is of the leaves of myrobalan; the fourth one is known as Phala Saptami. The seventh one is Kamika Saptami and their performances are being spoken by me. You please listen. Controlling all the sense organs, concentrating the mind, a devotee should take light food on the fifth moon day, while the enjoying of sex act should be discarded from a distance. O foremost of the birds, the honey, meat and extremely painful things should be totally discarded. On the morning of the sixth moon day, cups may be made of a single leaf each and Shali rice with ghi should be placed in each one of them. The rice should then be taken appropriately. No other cereal should be consumed. On the day of Saptami (or the seventh moon day), regular food should be taken.

## \|\| 1.195.10-11 \|\|

*ekaikavṛddhābhiyuktairyo vasettu khageśvara \|*  
*anyatra maricaṃ bhakṣenniṃbapatrāṇyataḥ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

*evaṃ labdhaphalānīha pakṣayorubhayorapi \|*  
*annādai rahito yatnādanodana iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. O lord of the birds, with the advancement of one, each of the process should be completed. Similarly, the conclusion of the vrata on the second Saptami should be with i black pepper, and third with the leaf of myrobalan. Thus, by performing the religious rites of Saptami-vrata of both the fortnights, the merits which are achieved by a person, have been defined. Because of the discarding of the food, it is also called annodana (or without rice).

## \|\| 1.195.12-17 \|\|

*ācaredvidhivadbhaktyā pūjayitvā vibhāvasum \|*  
*ahorātraṃ vāyubhakṣaḥ kuryādvijayasaptamīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saptadhānyahiraṇyāḍhye śaśikundeṃdusannibhe \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tāni sarvāṇi nāmāni vilekhya susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*śvetacaṃdanadigdhāṃge mālyadāmopaśobhite \|\| 14 \|\|*

*aśvatthāśokapatrāḍhye dadhyodanasamanvite \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadarthaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā taistairdṛṣṭairna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu śobhanaṃ svapnaṃ na bhūyaḥ śayanaṃ svapet \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prātaśca kī rtayetsvapne yathādṛṣṭaṃ khagādhipa \|*  
*prājñabhojakaviprebhyaḥ suhṛdbhyaśca khagādhipa \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-17. On the day of Vijaya-Saptami, worshiping the Sungod appropriately, the day and night should be spent by inhaling air alone. On each one of the Saptami, the process of vrata is required to be completed appropriately. Their names should be written on pieces of paper individually and placed before the image of the Sungod the limbs of whom should be plastered with white sandal paste and adorned with garlands of white flowers, which should be lodged in seven cereals or gold. It should have the shine of moon, gold and lotus. There should be heaps of leaves of holy fig or Ashoka trees. The cooked rice with curd should also be placed before it. The image should then be consecrated with devotion and worshipped and in case it is so done, the Sungod severally appears in the dream. There is no doubt about it. After witnessing the beautiful dream, one should not sleep again. O foremost of the birds, rising up early in the morning, the dream witnessed should be described before a Bhojaka Brahmana or friends.

## \|\| 1.195.18 \|\|

*tato madhyāhnasamaye snātaḥ prayatamānasaḥ \|*  
*taṃ caiva devaṃ vidhivatpūjayitvā divākaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thereafter, controlling all his senses, the devotee should take bath at noon and then worship the god appropriately.

## \|\| 1.195.19-25 \|\|

*samyakkṛtajapo maunī naro hutahutāśanaḥ \|*  
*niṣkramya devāyatanādbhojakāya nivedayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhavedalābho yadi bhojakānāṃ viprāstamarhaṃti purāṇavijñāḥ \|*  
*ye maṃtravedāvayaveṣu niścitā vibhuṃ samabhyarcya divaṃ vrajeyuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kṛtvaivaṃ saptamī sapta naro bhakti samanvitaḥ \|*  
*śraddadhānopi sūryasya sa kathaṃ nāpnuyātphalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ kṛtānāṃ yatphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tatphalaṃ saptamī sapta kṛtvā bhaktyā labheta nā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*duṣpāpaṃ nāsti tadvīra saptamyāṃ yanna dahyate \|*  
*na ca rogo'styasau loke ya etābhirna śāmyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kuṣṭhāni yāni raudrāṇi duśchedyāni bhiṣagjanaiḥ \|*  
*nīyante tāni sarvāṇi garuḍeneva pannagāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sakalavibudhamānyaṃ svaprakāśaṃ janānāmabhimataphaladāne dīkṣitaṃ taṃ supūjyam \|*  
*sutadhanakulabhogaiḥ saukhyapuṇyairupeto vrajati ca sutanuṃ kāṃ śāśvatā tigmaraśmeḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

19-25. Observing silence, one should perform the japam appropriately and the homa should also be performed. Then coming out of the temple, a Bhojaka should be informed about it. When the Bhojaka is not available, then the dream should be revealed to a Brahmana, well-versed in the Puranas having attained proficiency in all the six parts of the Vedas, besides being a devotee of the Sungod and desirable of achieving the heaven. Thus, a person with utmost devotion and faith, should complete the vratas of all the seven Saptamis appropriately. The merit which accrues therefrom would surely be gained by him. The merits which one earns with the performing of ten Ashvamedha sacrifices, the same merit could be achieved by a person who performs the vratas of the seven Saptamis with devotion. There is no grave sin that cannot be destroyed in the fire of the Saptami vratas. There is no ailment which cannot be cured with the performing of the Saptami vratas. All the horrible leprosy diseases which are beyond the cure of the physicians, all of them disappear like the serpents who vanish on the arrival of Garuda with the worship of the Sungod, who is the foremost of all the Devas, is self resplendent and is the bestower of the desired merits to the humans. By worshiping the same Sungod appropriately, one achieves sons, riches, all the comforts enjoyed by the people of high social order. He also achieves the best of body and the best of lokas.

## Chapter 196. Method of Nama-puja

## \|\| 1.196.1 \|\|

*saptāśvavatilaka uvāca \|*  
*atītya bhuktaṃ puruṣaḥ saptamyāṃ garuḍāgraja \|*  
*maitrīṃ vidadhyātsarvatra jīvahiṃsāṃ vivarjayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saptashvatilaka said — O elder brother of Garuda, after taking food on the day of Saptami, a person should stop killing of living beings and establish friendship everywhere.

## \|\| 1.196.2-3 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ na spṛśettailaṃ nīlaṃ vastraṃ na dhārayet \|*  
*na śayīta striyā sārdhaṃ na seveta durodaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*na rudyādaśrupātena na vā dhyāyetpiśācakān \|*  
*nākṛṣecchiraso yūkā na vṛthāvādamācaret \|*  
*parasyāniṣṭakathanamativādaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The touch of oil, wearing of blue clothes, uniting with the wife, keeping company of the wicked people, weeping and dropping of tears, thinking about the Pishachas to extract life from the head and useless talks are strictly prohibited. Similarly, one should avoid controversy even when others indulge in evil talks.

## \|\| 1.196.4 \|\|

*na kaṃcittāḍayejjaṃtuṃ na viśeta kadācana \|*  
*brahmahatyāmavāpnoti viśamāno ravergṛham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. During that period, no one should be tortured physically. He should not enter a Sun temple, because by so doing, he would earn the sin of a Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 1.196.5-6 \|\|

*ityete samayāḥ proktāḥ saurāṇāṃ garuḍāgraja \|*  
*bhojakānāṃ viśeṣeṇa purā me bhānunānagha \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhojakaḥ khagaśārdūla yo lobhāddravyamutsṛjet \|*  
*vṛddhyai tu satataṃ vīra sa gacchennarakaṃ dhuvam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O elder brother of Garuda, it is essential for the devotees of the Sungod to follow these rules and more so for the Bhojakas. O sinless one, I have been informed about the same by the Sungod himself. A Bhojaka who distributes the money on interest, he surely falls in the hell.

## \|\| 1.196.7-8 \|\|

*viśeṣe cālpakaśate kāmayāne khagādhipa \|*  
*prayujyamāno bhojakastu paṃcakena śatena vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

*prāyaścittī bhavedvīra na cārhaḥ pūjane raveḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā sāṃtapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ tatraḥ saṃpūjayedravim \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. A Bhojaka who lends five hundred (coins) with the intention of having interest of over hundred (coins), he would not be entitled to the Sun worship, without performing of repentance. He, after performing the Sentapana and Kricchra vrata, should perform the worship of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.196.9 \|\|

*nānyadevapratiṣṭhā tu kartavyā bhojakena tu \|*  
*kṛtvā tu tāṃ khagaśreṣṭha prāyaścittīyate naraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O best of birds, a Bhojaka should not consecrate any other god and in case he does so, it is necessary for him to perform repentance.

## \|\| 1.196.10 \|\|

*tasmāttu tāṃ na kuryādvai bhojakaḥ khagasattama \|*  
*muktvā tu bhāskaraṃ devaṃ nānyaṃ devaṃ nivedayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, a Bhojaka must not offer prayer to any other god, except the Sun.

## \|\| 1.196.11 \|\|

*kṛtvādhiveśaṃ devānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ khagādhipa \|*  
*bhojako na spṛśedbhānuṃ kuryātkṛcchraṃ ca śuddhaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After worshipping Brahma or any other gods, a Bhojaka becomes untouchable for the image of the Sun.

## \|\| 1.196.12 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu kṛcchraṃ vidhi vacchuddherhetuṃ khagādhipa \|*  
*tataḥ pūjayituṃ bhānumadhikārī bhavennaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For self purification, he should perform the Krichhra vrata appropriately and after so doing, he becomes entitled to the worship of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.196.13 \|\|

*na vijñātaṃ pradātavyaṃ na mlānaṃ na ca dūṣitam \|*  
*na ca paryuṣitaṃ mālyaṃ dātavyamṛddhimicchatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person who is desirous of advancement should not offer undecided, faded, blemished and old garlands to the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.196.14-15 \|\|

*devamullocayedyastu sa khalaḥ puṣpalobhataḥ \|*  
*puṣpāṇi ca sugaṃdhīni bhojako netarāṇi ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brahmahatyāmavāpnoti bhojako lobhamohitaḥ \|*  
*mahārauravamāsādya pacyate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Out of greed, if a person makes a canopy of flowers (meant for the worship of the Sungod), he should be treated as a wicked person. The Bhojakas should prepare canopies for the Sungod with fragrant flowers, and not of flowers without fragrance. Otherwise, the greedy Bhojakas shall earn the sin of Brahmahatya, as a result of which they have to boil in the Raurava hell for long.

## \|\| 1.196.16 \|\|

*haṃta te kīrtayiṣyāmi dhūpadānavidhiṃ param \|*  
*pradāne devadevasya yena dhūpena yatphalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Now, I shall speak about the offering of the type of incense to the Sungod and the type of reward he achieves, by so doing. It has been described exhaustively.

## \|\| 1.196.17 \|\|

*sadā caṃdanadhūpena sānnidhyaṃ kurute raviḥ \|*  
*pradadyānmānase caiva yadyadicchati mānavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With the offering of incense of sandal wood, the Sungod always fulfills the desires of the same person.

## \|\| 1.196.18-19 \|\|

*tathaivāgurudhūpena varaṃ dadyā dabhīpsitam \|*  
*ārogyaṃ vā striyaṃ prepsurnityadā guggulaṃ dahet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*maṃgalaṃ dhūpadānena sadā yacchati bhānumān \|*  
*ārogyaṃ ca striyaṃ dadyā tsaukhyaṃ ca paramaṃ bhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. By offering the incense of agaru, one achieves the desired thing; by offering the incense of guggulu one achieves good health and unites with his beloved; with the offering of incense the Sungod always bestows welfare, besides good health and comforts.

## \|\| 1.196.20-21 \|\|

*sadā kuṃkumadhūpena saubhāgyaṃ labhate naraḥ \|*  
*śrīvāsakasya dhūpena vāṇijyaṃ saphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*rasaṃ sarvarasopetaṃ dadatorthāgamo dhruvam \|*  
*devadāruṃ ca dahato bhavatyannamathākṣayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. By offering the incense of Kunkum, one attains fortune and with the use of Vasaka incense one achieves success in business; with the offering of all the essences, the wealth surely arrives. With the offering of the incense of the pine tree, undecaying cereals are achieved.

## \|\| 1.196.22 \|\|

*vilepanaṃ kuṃkumena sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*iha loke sukhī bhūtvā dātā svargama vāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The plaster of kunkum fulfills all the desires in this world and one achieves comforts in the next world, besides reaching in the heaven.

## \|\| 1.196.23 \|\|

*caṃdanasya pradānena śriyamāyuśca viṃdati \|*  
*raktacaṃdanadānena sarvaṃ dadyāddivākaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With the offering of the sandalwood paste one achieves long life and with the offering of the red sandal paste, the Sungod bestows everything.

## \|\| 1.196.24 \|\|

*api rogaśatairgrastaiḥ kṣiprārogyamavā pnuyāt \|*  
*vartigaṃdhaiśca saugaṃdhyaṃ paramaṃ viṃdate naraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Instead suffering from hundreds of diseases, the performer gains rapid cure of all the ailments. By providing a fragrant wick, a person gets excellent fragrance.

## \|\| 1.196.25 \|\|

*kastūrikālepanakairaiśvaryamatulaṃ labhet \|*  
*karpūrasaṃyutairgaṃdhaiḥ kṣmādhipādhipatirbhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With the plaster of musk, one achieves unprecedented fortunes. With the offering of a paste mixed with camphor, the performer becomes king of kings.

## \|\| 1.196.26 \|\|

*catuḥsamena gaṃdhena kiṃ tulyaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*devāgāraṃ tu tanmanye bhaktyā ya upalepayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By offering four types of fragrance, a person achieves merits, which is divine in nature. A person who offers the paste with devotion, it resembles the offering made to the Sungod, after building a temple.

## \|\| 1.196.27 \|\|

*sa rogānmucyate kṣipraṃ puruṣo bhogavānbhavet \|*  
*aṣṭādaśeha kuṣṭhāni ye cānye vyādhayo nṛṇām \|*  
*pralayaṃ yāṃti te sarve mṛdā yadyupalepayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The concerned person, getting free from ailments, enjoys all the comforts. The eighteen types of human leprosy diseases and other ailments also get removed, in case he pastes the clay alone.

## \|\| 1.196.28 \|\|

*pralepanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ raktacaṃdanamuttamam \|*  
*nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcidbhānostuṣṭikaraṃ param \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Of all the pastes, the paste of the red sandal paste is considered to be quite praiseworthy. So much so, that for pleasing the Sungod, there is no other paste comparable with it.

## \|\| 1.196.29 \|\|

*kiṃ tasya na bhavelloko yo hyanena pralepayet \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddho'sau sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. A person who do the smearing of the paste, he does not have to face any shortage in life. He gets all the things in plenty. Having all his desires fulfilled in this world, he is ultimately honoured in Suryaloka.

## \|\| 1.196.30 \|\|

*upalipya ravergehaṃ kuryādvai maṃḍalaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*ekenātha samāpnoti bhāgyamārogyamuttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By using the same process the plastering of Sun temple and with the making of the masala, one achieves both good fortune and excellent health.

## \|\| 1.196.31-32 \|\|

*tribhiḥ saptabhiracchinnā bālo vānyopi yo naraḥ \|*  
*tena pradāpayeddevānkuryāttānna nivārayet \|*  
*anena vidhinā kuryādyāvatīḥ sapta saptamī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*etā vai sapta saptamyo yathā proktā vivasvatā \|*  
*kurvīta yo naro bhaktyā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. All the above incense or any one of them can be offered by a boy or any other person following the same process in an appropriate manner. The vratas of seven Saptamis should also be concluded in a similar manner. A person who performs vratas for the seven Saptamis as has been told by the Sungod, he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.196.33 \|\|

*arkasaṃpuṭakairvittaṃ maricaiḥ priyasaṃgamam \|*  
*niṃbapatrai roganāśaṃ phalaiḥ putrānyathepsitān \|*  
*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca tato dadyādvivasvate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Arka Saptami bestows riches; the Maricha Saptami unites with the beloved; the Nimbapatra Saptami removes ailments and flower Saptami enables one to have a son of his own liking. Thereafter, the wealth and other cereals, gold etc. should be given in the name of the Sungod.

## \|\| 1.196.34-35 \|\|

*jayaṃ prāpnoti vipulaṃ kṛtvā sarvatra khecara \|*  
*sarvānkāmānkāmikastu prāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*naro vā yadi vā nārī yathoktaṃ saptamīvratam \|*  
*yaḥ karoti khagaśreṣṭha sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. O moon of the sky, by thus performing the vratas, the performer gets victorious everywhere and gets his desires fulfilled. There is no doubt about it. The performance of the Saptami vrata can be concluded by the men, women or any other person, because by so doing, the performer achieves the highest positions.

## \|\| 1.196.36 \|\|

*na teṣāṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcidastīti durlabham \|*  
*ye bhaktyā lokanāthasya vratinaḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A person who performs the vratas of the Sungod appropriately with devotion, for him nothing in the world is beyond his reach.

## \|\| 1.196.37 \|\|

*sarvayajñaphalaṃ teṣāṃ yathā vedoditaṃ bhavet \|*  
*brahmeṃdraviṣṇavastena pūjitā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The merits of the yajnas as revealed in the Vedas are all bestowed by Surya. Besides, Brahma, Indra and Vishnu also stand worshipped by him. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.196.38 \|\|

*nāṃdho na kuṣṭhī na klībo na vyaṃgo na ca nirdhanaḥ \|*  
*kadāpi ca bhavetkaścidyaścaretsaptamīvratam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Whosoever may perform the vratas including a blind, leper, eunuch, a joker or a pauper, he never becomes poor.

## \|\| 1.196.39 \|\|

*putrārthī śrutisaṃpannāllaṃbhetputrāścirāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcidastīti durlabham \|*  
*bhogārthī labhate bhogānvratenānena suvrata \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The people desirous of a son, they achieve the Vedic scholars with long life as sons who never have anything beyond their reach in the three worlds. With the influence of this vrata, those who are involved in worldly pleasures, achieve them in abundance.

## \|\| 1.196.40 \|\|

*krodhātpramādāllobhācca vratabhaṃgo yadā bhavet \|*  
*prāyaścittamidaṃ kṛtvā punareva vratī bhavet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Out of anger, arrogance or the pride, in case the vrata is missed, one should perform repentance and again perform the vrata.

## \|\| 1.196.41 \|\|

*saptaiva yāvatsaptamyaḥ saṃprāptā guruṇā khaga \|*  
*tāsu bhāskaramabhyarcya mālyadhūpādibhirnaraḥ \|*  
*bhojayitvā dvijāñchaktyā prāpnuyātsvargamakṣayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All the seven Saptamis indicated by the preceptors when arrive, the person should welcome the Sungod offering garlands, incense etc. After doing so, he should serve food to the Brahmanas as per his means, by which he achieves the heaven for all times to come.

## \|\| 1.196.42 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ vipramukhyebhyo yo'nnaṃ dadyātkhageśvara \|*  
*tadakṣayaṃ bhavettasya sa ca sūryagṛhaṃ vrajet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. By distributing food to the prominent Brahmanas on the days of Saptami, it becomes everlasting. Thereafter, he achieves the place of Surya.

## \|\| 1.196.43 \|\|

*iti te kīrtitaṃ vīra saptamīvratamuttamam \|*  
*bhūya evābhidhāsyāmi śṛṇu me vadatonagha \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus, I have narrated to you, O valorous one, the processing of the vrata of all the Saptamis. I am repeating the same again.

## \|\| 1.196.44 \|\|

*yena vrataprabhāveṇa kāmikaṃ phalamaśnute \|*  
*saptamīṃ khagaśārdūla śuklāṃ dvādaśanāmikām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O lion among the birds, the vratas with the performing of which the desires of all the people get fulfilled, I am revealing that particular Saptami which is known with twelve names.

## \|\| 1.196.45-46 \|\|

*gomūtragomayāhāraḥ ṣaḍvṛtāhāra eva ca \|*  
*atha vā yāvakāhāraḥ śīrṇaparṇāśanopi vā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kṣīrāśī caikabhaktaṃ vā sikthāhārotha vā punaḥ \|*  
*jalāhārotha vā vidvānpūjayeta divākaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. One should worship the Sungod consuming cow’s urine, cowdung, Shadavrita, butter milk, the dry leaves, payasam, the honey left over by the bees, besides the water. A devotee should worship the Sungod consuming the aforesaid things.

## \|\| 1.196.47-49 \|\|

*puṣpopahārairvividhaiḥ padmasaugaṃdhikotpalaiḥ \|*  
*nānāprakārairgaṃdhaiśca dhūpairguggulucaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kṛśaraiḥ pāyasānnairvā vividhaiśca vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*arcayitvā dvijaśreṣṭha bhakṣyavastrādibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sarvapakṣaphalaṃ prāpya sūryalokaṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*tapasoṃte tato vīra kule mahati jāyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. O best of the Brahmanas, with the presents of various types of flowers, red lotus flowers, fragrance of various types, incense, guggulu, sandal paste, rice mixed with pulses, payasam, several types of ornaments, eatables and costumes, the Sungod should be worshipped and when it is so done, one achieves a place in Suryaloka, besides all the merits. Soon after that, he is born in a well established race.

## \|\| 1.196.50-53 \|\|

*yathākramaṃ prayatnena nāmāni parikīrtayet \|*  
*māghe ca phālgune māsi caitre ca garuḍāgraja \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vaiśākhe tvatha jyeṣṭhe tu āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe tathā \|*  
*māsi bhādrapade vīra tathā cāśvayuje khaga \|\| 51 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣe tathā pauṣe pūjayetsatataṃ ravim \|*  
*vibhāvasuṃ vivasvaṃtaṃ bhāskaraṃ pakṣisattama \|\| 52 \|\|*

*vikartanaṃ pataṃgaṃ ca sahasrāṃśuṃ khagādhipa \|*  
*etāni devanāmāni māseṣveteṣu khecara \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-53. Several names of the months are being spoken by me. These are — Magha, Phalguna, Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashvina (Karttika), Margashirsha and Pausha, in which the sun should be worshipped. The Sungod is worshipped by the names of Vibhavasu, Vivasvan, Bhaskara, Vikartana, Patanga and Sahasramshu.

## \|\| 1.196.54 \|\|

*pūjayeddevadeveśaṃ devānāmapi durlabham \|*  
*evaṃ krameṇa tīkṣṇāṃśuṃ nāmabhiḥ paripūjayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O bird moving in the sky, Tikshamshu is also a name of Surya and with this name, worship should be performed which is beyond the reach of even the gods.

## \|\| 1.196.55 \|\|

*ityevaṃ te samākhyātaṃ mayā guhyamidaṃ khaga \|*  
*abhaktāya na dātavyaṃ nāśiṣyāya kathaṃcana \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thus, all the details have been revealed before you. The relevant details should not be made known to the unbelievers and nondisciples.

## \|\| 1.196.56-57 \|\|

*na ca pāpakṛte vīra dātavyaṃ vinatātmaja \|*  
*vyādhestu nāśanārthāya deyaṃ viprāya suvrata \|\| 56 \|\|*

*dattvā svargamavāpnoti śrutvā ca vidhivatkhaga \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. O son of Vinata, this knowledge also should not be given to a simple person. It would not be improper to reveal this information to a Brahmana from getting relieved of a disease. By passing on the same (to a suitable person), one achieves the heaven.

## Chapter 197. Description of Cowrie

## \|\| 1.197.1 \|\|

*saptāśvatilaka uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi puṣpadhūpādikāmikam \|*  
*yena yena tu dānena tattatphalamavāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saptashvatilaka said — I am now speaking about the flowers and incense, the use of which bestows different merits to the devotee.

## \|\| 1.197.2-4 \|\|

*mālatīkusumaiḥ pūjā bhavetsānnidhyakārikā \|*  
*ārogyaṃ karavīraistu bhavatyarthaśca śāśvataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aiśvaryamatulaṃ caiva yaśaśca vipulaṃ tathā \|*  
*mallikāyāśca kusumairbhagavatsammukho bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saubhāgyaṃ puṃḍarīkaistu paramaiśvaryamāpnuyāt \|*  
*kamalotpalakuṃdaistu yaśo vidyā balaṃ bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. The use of jasmine (Malati) flower for the worship of the Sungod enables a devotee to reach close to the lord. By worshipping him with oleander flower, one gets a continue flow of riches, unprecedented fortunes and enormous glory. With the use of Malika (a kind of jasmine flower) in the worship of the Sungod, one earns special grace of the lord. With the use of Pundarika (a kind of lotus), one earns fortunes, excellence and wealth. The use of red lotus, blue lotus and white lotus bestows on a person glory, education and strength.

## \|\| 1.197.5-6 \|\|

*nānāvidhaiḥ sukusumaiḥ kṣipraṃ rogātpramucyate \|*  
*bhavatyakṣayamannaṃ ca nityama rcayato ravim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*maṃdārakusumaiḥ pūjā sarvakuṣṭhanivāriṇī \|*  
*bilvasya patrakusumairmahatīṃ śriyamāpnuyāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The offering of various types of fragrant flowers relieves one of the disease. With the regular worship of the Sungod, one achieves indestructible food, while the flowers of the coral tree when used for Sun worship, relieves the devotee of all types of leprosy. With the use of wood apple leaves and their flowers, one achieves enormous wealth.

## \|\| 1.197.7 \|\|

*arkasrajā bhavatyarkaḥ sarvadā varadaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*pradadyādrūpiṇīṃ kanyāmarcito bakulasrajā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the garlands of the flowers of a coral tree are offered to the Sungod, he always bestows boons over the devotees. By worshipping the Sungod with the rosary of Bakula, the Sungod bestows a beautiful girl.

## \|\| 1.197.8 \|\|

*kiṃśukaiḥ pūjito devo na pīḍayati bhāskara \|*  
*agatsyakusumaiḥ siddhiṃ sānukūlyaṃ prayacchati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By using the flowers of kimshuka in the worship of the Sungod, the Sungod does not cause any misery. By worshipping him with the Agastya, one achieves the desired success.

## \|\| 1.197.9 \|\|

*svayaṃ rūpavatīṃ dadyātpūjitaścaṃpakasrajā \|*  
*nirudvego bhavennityaṃ pūjitaḥ puṣpamālayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. By offering the garland of Champaka flowers, one earns comforts and beautiful form.

## \|\| 1.197.10 \|\|

*aśokakusumairdevamarcayedyo divākaram \|*  
*āmrātakasya kusumaṃ nirmālyamiva dṛśyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The myrobalan flower is also considered to be auspicious like the leftover of the lord.

## \|\| 1.197.11-12 \|\|

*apratyagnaṃ bahiryasmāttasmāttatparivarjayet \|*  
*navabhistvacalāṃ kīrtiṃ daśabhiḥ sukhamuttamam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhogānekādaśeneha prāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśenācalaṃ rājyaṃ dvādaśākhyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. But its inner part is lodged in the outer surface and becomes visible. Therefore, it is to be discarded. By offering the fresh flowers, one achieves lasting glory. By offering ten flowers, one gets excellent comfort and by offering eleven flowers, one achieves pleasures. There is no doubt about it. By offering twelve flowers, one achieves stable kingdom, because he is popular with twelve names.

## \|\| 1.197.13-16 \|\|

*prathamaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā bhūrūpaṃ praṇametsadā \|*  
*bhuvarnamo dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīyaṃ svarnamennaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*maharnamaścaturthaṃ tu paṃcamaṃ tu jano namaḥ \|*  
*tapo namastathā ṣaṣṭhaṃ namaḥ satyaṃ tu saptamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*aṣṭamaṃ bhūrbhuvaśceti navamaṃ khagasattama \|*  
*daśamaṃ ṣaḍato vīra namolkāya tathā param \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dvādaśaṃ tu khaṣolketi oṃ namaḥ pūjayetkhaga \|*  
*evaṃ maṃḍalakārī tu kramādevaṃ phalaṃ labhet \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. First of all, the Sungod should be worshipped in the form of Bhu-rupa offering salutation to him. The other form is Bhuva-rupa, the third one is Svara-rupa; the fourth is Мahah-rupa; fifth is Jana-rupa; sixth is Tapah-rupa; seventh is Satya-rupa; the eighth is Bhurbhuva-rupa; ninth is Shveta-rupa. In the tenth form, all the rupas from Bhu to tapas are included. The eleventh form is Ulka, while the twelfth form is khasholka which should also he worshipped. In this way, a mandahi should he prepared. One who worships the Sungod in proper order, he achieves all the merits.

## \|\| 1.197.17 \|\|

*ghṛtadīpapradānena cakṣuṣmāñjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*kaṭutailasya dīpena śatrūṇāṃ saṃśrayo bhavet \|*  
*madhūkānāṃ tu tailena saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ labhet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The people who offer the lamps of ghi possess bright eyesight. By offering the lamp of mustard oil, his enemies are destroyed. By offering the lamp of Madhuka oil, one achieves enormous fortunes.

## \|\| 1.197.18 \|\|

*saṃpūjya vidhivaddevaṃ puṣpadhūpādibhirnaraḥ \|*  
*yathāśaktyā tataḥ paścānnaivedyaṃ tu prakalpayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus, by worshipping the Sungod m prefer manner, the food offerings should then be made to him.

## \|\| 1.197.19 \|\|

*puṣpāṇāṃ pravarā jātī dhūpānāṃ caiva candanam \|*  
*gaṃdhānāṃ kuṃkumaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ modakāśca nivedane \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Jasmine is the best of flowers, sandal is the best of incenses, kunkum is the best among the saffrons and the sweet ball is the best among the naivedyas (or food offerings).

## \|\| 1.197.20 \|\|

*etaistuṣyati deveśaḥ sānnidhyaṃ cādhigacchati \|*  
*dadāti pravarāniṣṭāndātuśca svargatiṃ tathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By offering them all, the lord Surya gets pleased and favours the devotees with his vicinity. They finally gain access to the heaven.

## \|\| 1.197.21 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivatkṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā devaṃ bhāskaraṃ timirāpaham \|*  
*āruhya suvimānaṃ sa yāti bhānoḥ salokatām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus, by worshipping the Sungod in a proper manner besides the circumambulation, offering salutations lowering the head, the Sungod who is the remover of darkness, grants the devotee’s stay in his place by means of a beautiful plane.

## \|\| 1.197.22-23 \|\|

*punaḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ japaṃ kuryādyatheṣṭakam \|*  
*hutāśane ca juhuyādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*evamekaikaśaḥ kāryāḥ saptamyaḥ sapta sarvadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*udakaprasṛtiṃ pītvā kriyate yā tu saptamī \|*  
*sā jñeyā sukhadā vīra sadaivodakasaptamī \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. After performing the puja, the japam as liked by the Sungod, should also be performed, besides performing of the homa Thus, all the Saptami vratas should be performed one after the other. Half a palm of water should be sipped and when the particular Saptami vrata gets completed, it bestows all the comforts. It is known as Udaka Saptami. It bestows all the comforts. It is well known as the Udaka-Saptami.

## \|\| 1.197.24-25 \|\|

*yā kācitsaptamī noktā tāṃ te vakṣyāmi marvadā \|*  
*varāṭikā krameṇāptaṃ yatkiṃcitpratibhakṣayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*anena deyamūlyena yallabdhaṃ tatprabhakṣayeta \|*  
*abhakṣyaṃ cāpi bhakṣyaṃ vā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The particular Saptami about which I have spoken, I am speaking about the same. Whatever one gets by the giving of a cowrie, the same should be consumed, without any consideration for permissible or unpermissible food. This has been ordained.

## Chapter 198. Talk between Vyasa and Bhishma

## \|\| 1.198.1-2 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca \|*  
*kimekaṃ daivataṃ loke kiṃ vāpyekaṃ parāyaṇam \|*  
*stuvantaḥ kaṃ kamarcataḥ prāpnuyurmānavāḥ śubham \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ko dharmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ kaśca pūjyo matastava \|*  
*brahmādayaḥ kamarcaṃti kaścādistridivaukasām \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Shatanika said — Who is the best of all the gods in the world? In whose favour, the parayana should be done? By adoring and praising whom, a human can meet with welfare? According to your view, which one of the dharma is the best? To whom the gods like Brahma and others adore? Who is the foremost of the gods?

## \|\| 1.198.3 \|\|

*sumanturuvāca \|*  
*atrāhaṃ te pravakṣyāmi saṃvādaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*bhīṣmasya naraśārdūla vyāsasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Sumantu said — In this connection, I am placing before you the talk between the sage Vyasa and Bhishma.

## \|\| 1.198.4-8 \|\|

*sukhāsīnaṃ mahāvyāsaṃ gaṃgākūle dvijottama \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sumahātejā jvalaṃtamiva pāvakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sākṣānnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ tejasādityasannibham \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā vīra sarvaśāstrālayaṃ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mahābhāratakartāraṃ vedārthanikaṣaṃ param \|*  
*ācāryaṃ paramarṣīṇāṃ rājarṣīṇāṃ ca bhārata \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kartāraṃ kuruvaṃśasya daivataṃ paramaṃ mama \|*  
*papraccha kuruśārdūlo dvijabhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*devadevasya māhātmyaṃ cittasthaṃ bhāskarasya tu \|*  
*sa mahātmā mahātejā bhīṣmaḥ pūrvaṃ muniṃ tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

4-8. O best of Brahmanas, once on the bank of the river Ganga, the great sage Vyasa was seated comfortably and was shining like the fire flames or lord Narayana himself appeared at that place, like the abode of all the excellent Shastras. Vyasa had been the composer of the epic of Mahabharata, the supreme Rishi, teacher of Rajarishis and the creator of the race of Kuru. Offering him salutation with devotion, the illustrious great soul known as Bhishma, enshring the glory of Bhaskara in his mind, questioned Vyasa — the earlier sage.

## \|\| 1.198.9-12 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*bhagavandvijaśārdūla pārāśarya mahāmate \|*  
*mamākhyātaṃ tvayā sarvaṃ vāṅmayaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhāskarasya muniśreṣṭha saṃśayodyāpi vartate \|*  
*ādau tasya namaskāramanyeṣāṃ tadanaṃtaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

*brahmādīnāṃ tu rudrādyairbrūhi tattvena hetunā \|*  
*ka eṣa bhāskaro brahmankuto jātaḥ ka ucyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kīrtayasva yathānyāyaṃ kautukaṃ hi paraṃ mama \|*  
*kuśalo hi bhavāṃlloke tasmāttvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-12. Bhishma said — O lord, O lion among the Brahmanas, the great adviser, you have revealed all the mobile and immobile scriptures to me. But I am still doubtful about Bhaskara. Offering salutation to him first, only then the other gods are adored. Because of which one of the tattvas, the Sungod is to be offered salutation first? Who is Bhaskara? Where was he born? I am quite anxious to know about all these things. You happen to be a competent orator in the world. Therefore, you kindly try to explain the truth to me in a judicious manner.

## \|\| 1.198.13-16 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*aho tava mahatkaṣṭaṃ pramūḍhosi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*stuvaṃtaśca tamarcābhiḥ siddhā brahmādayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmeva devānāmādirāditya ucyate \|*  
*sa haṃti timiraṃ sarvaṃ digvidikṣu vyavasthitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sa dharmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sa ca pūjyatamo mataḥ \|*  
*brahmādayastamarcaṃti sa cādistridivaukasām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*aditiḥ kaśyapasatī ādityastena cocyate \|*  
*ādikartātha vā yasmā ttasmādāditya ucyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. Vyasa said — You feel yourself to be in a painful situation because of these matters. This is quite surprising. There is no doubt about your being ignorant. Brahma and other gods have achieved success by the grace of Surya by adoring him. Because of this, Surya happens to be the foremost of all of them. The darkness pervading the directions and intermediate directions is removed by him alone. Of all the dharmas, he happens to be the foremost dharma. Therefore, according to my opinion, he is the most adorable one. He is adored by Brahma and other gods. He is the beginning of the gods. Because of the accepting of the water by Kashyapa and Aditi initially and because of his being the preeminent creator, he is known by the name of Aditya.

## \|\| 1.198.17-20 \|\|

*tasmādetajjagatsarvamādityātsaṃpravartate \|*  
*sadevāsuragaṃdharvaṃ sayakṣoragarākṣasam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*rudropeṃdrau tatheṃdraśca brahmā dakṣotha kaśyapaḥ \|*
